gāvaḥ—cows; mṛgāḥ—deer; khagāḥ—birds; nāryaḥ—women; puṣpiṇyaḥ—which have flowers (or desirous of sex) (or in menstruation); śaradā—due to autumn; abhavan—became; anvīyamānāḥ—being followed; sva-vṛṣaiḥ—by their males (“by their bulls”); phalaiḥ—by \[good\] results (by fruits); īśa-kriyāḥ— actions for the Lord; iva—like.

*gāvaḥ mṛgāḥ khagāḥ nāryaḥ śaradā (nimittena) sva-vṛṣaiḥ anvīyamānāḥ, phalaiḥ (anvīyamānāḥ) īśa-kriyāḥ iva (samasta-bhoga-garbhāḥ bhavanti), puṣpiṇyaḥ abhavan.*

**Перевод:**

**Because of the fall season, cows, does, female birds, and women which had flowers and were being followed by their mates were like spiritual deeds, which are followed by the fruits.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Being followed (anvīyamānāḥ = anugamyamānāḥ) forcefully by their mates (sva-vṛṣaiḥ = sva-patibhiḥ), the females became pregnant (puṣpiṇyaḥ = garbhiṇyaḥ) like actions for worshiping the Lord (īśa-kriyāḥ = īśvarārādhanārthāḥ kriyāḥ), which are being followed by results by force, become pregnant with all types of enjoyment.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Mṛgāḥ and khagāḥ are poetic license; the words should be mṛgyaḥ and khagyaḥ. The rest was explained by Śrīdhara Svāmī. Or the sense is: puṣpam ārtavaṁ tadvatyaḥ sva-vṛṣair anvīyamānā babhūvuḥ, īśvarārādhana-kriyā yathā puṣpa-sadrśam āntarīyakaṁ jñānādikaṁ darśayantyaḥ premādi-lakṣaṇaiḥ phalair anugatā bhavati, “Having menses, they were being followed by their mates, like actions for worshiping the Lord are followed by the fruit, prema, to show that jñāna-yoga and karma-yoga are external methods akin to mere flowers.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Mṛgāḥ and khagāḥ are poetic license; they should be mṛgyaḥ and khagyaḥ. The rest was explained by Śrīdhara Svāmī. Alternatively: puṣpam ṛtu-kārī dhātu-viśeṣas tadvatyaḥ satyaḥ sva-vṛṣaiḥ prasava-viśeṣa-sampādaka-sva-sva-puṁbhiḥ prārthanāṁ vināpy anvīyamānā babhūvuḥ, phalaiḥ phala-viśeṣa-sampādakair apūrvakair apūrvaiḥ, “They, having a particular bodily substance that makes a period, were being followed, even without a request, by their respective males that effect a particular procreation, like actions for the Lord are followed by unprecedented results.”

Krama-sandarbha—The explanation is: puṇpiṇyaḥ ṛtumatyaḥ tāḥ sva-vṛṣair avaśyam anvīyamānā abhavan phalair īśa-kriyā iva, “Having menses, those females were necessarily being followed by their mates, like actions for the Lord by the fruits.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Mṛgāḥ (deer) stands for mṛgyaḥ (female deer), and khagāḥ (birds) for khagyaḥ (female birds). They were being followed by their respective mates (sva-vṛṣaiḥ = sva-sva-patibhiḥ): though unwilling they were being followed for the sake of intercourse.

Īśa-kriyāḥ means: bhagavad-ārādhana-lakṣaṇāḥ kriyāḥ niṣkāmāḥ api, “actions, though devoid of material desire, characterized by worshiping the Lord.” Phalaiḥ signifies phalaiḥ sukha-bhogādibhiḥ (by fruits such as enjoying happiness, etc.).

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

(The commentary is a paraphrase of Bhāvārtha-dīpikā. In addition:) The simile is acceptable.

### 10.20.47

*udahṛṣyan vārijāni sūryotthāne kumud vinā \|*  
*rājñā tu nirbhayā lokā yathā dasyūn vinā nṛpa \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

udahṛṣyan—became delighted; vāri-jāni—lotuses (or water lilies, “born in water”); sūrya-utthāne—when there was a rising of the sun; kumud vinā—except the kumut flower (a white water lily); rājñā—because of the king; tu—only; nirbhayāḥ—fearless; lokāḥ— people; yathā—like; dasyūn vinā—save for thieves; nṛpa—O king (“protector of men”).

*nṛpa! yathā lokāḥ rājñā tu (hetunā) nirbhayāḥ (santaḥ hṛṣṭāḥ bhavanti, kintu) dasyūn vinā, (tathā) sūryotthāne (sati) vārijāni udahṛṣyan, (parantu) kumud vinā.*

**Перевод:**

**Without kumut water lilies, lotuses rejoiced upon the rise of the sun. Similarly, without thieves the population becomes fearless only because of a king, O protector of men!**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Kumud stands for kumudam. There is a similarity with thieves: kutsitā mud yasya (one whose joy is despicable).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kumud stands for kumudam. There is a similarity with thieves: kutsiteṣu mud yasya (one who has joy about despicable things).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Since lotuses that bloom in daytime are enemies, in terms of being the counterpart, of kumuda flowers, which bloom at night, by blooming without them a distinct resplendence is implied, therefore they were highly, i.e. intensely, joyful (udahṛṣyan = uccair atiśayena ahṛṣyan), in other words they bloomed happily.

Rājñā means rājñā hetunā (because of a king). It is well known that people are apprehensive of robbers (dasyu = luṇṭhaka), consequently: “like they, being fearless without robbers, are highly joyful.”

Or vinā has the sense of “except” instead of “without”, and so kumud vinā means: kumudāni ca na udahṛṣyan (the kumuda flowers did not highly rejoice) and dasyūn vinā signifies: dasyavaḥ tu sa-bhayāḥ bhavanti (but the robbers become afraid).

The gist of nṛpa (O king) is: “That takes place because of a king like you.” Or, “This is already known to you.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Here, by the word vārija, all flowers that originate in water are included, but not the lotus, because of the nonaccomplishment of the negation of the kumuda (the kumuda is a water lily, a synonym of lotus). Only a generality is meant, as in the case of the word loka (people). Because of blooming at night, there is a similarity between kumuda flowers and thieves.

Rājñā (because of the king), that is, when he rises, or when ascends for the first time on the throne, or when there is an undertaking. This is an elliptical simile (luptopamā) (in the reading āsan dasyūn). Another reading is: yathā dasyūn. Nṛpa (O king) hints at an example of the example.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Vārijāni means padmāni (lotuses, especially daytime lotuses). The deletion of the case ending after kumud is poetic license. Viśva-kośa states: kumude ’pi kumut smṛtam, “Kumut means kumuda.” The sense is: kairavāṇi vinā, “without kairava flowers (white lotuses that bloom in moonlight).” The simile is acceptable for kings.

**Annotation**

The word rājan also means “moon”, and so the pun is: “Similarly, without thieves the population becomes fearless only because of the moon.” The definition is: rājā mṛgāṅke kṣatriye nṛpe, “Rājan means moon, Kṣatriya, and king” (Amara-koṣa 3.3.111).

### 10.20.48

*pura-grāmeṣv āgrayaṇair aindriyaiś ca mahotsavaiḥ \|*  
*babhau bhūḥ pakva-sasyāḍhyā kalābhyāṁ nitarāṁ hareḥ \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

pura-grāmeṣu—in towns and in villages; āgrayaṇaiḥ—pertaining to the offering of the first grains of the harvest; aindriyaiḥ—pertaining to the senses; ca—and; mahā-utsavaiḥ—with great festivals; babhau—shone (was resplendent); bhūḥ—the Earth; pakva—ripe; sasya—with grains; āḍhyā—richly endowed; kalā—an expansion (a potency); ābhyām—because of (or with) These two; nitarām— exceedingly (“incessantly more”); hareḥ—of Hari (of Nārāyaṇa).

*pura-grāmeṣu āgrayaṇaiḥ aindriyaiḥ ca mahotsavaiḥ ābhyāṁ (ca rāma-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ) bhūḥ pakva-sasyāḍhyā hareḥ kalā nitarāṁ babhau.*

**Перевод:**

**Richly endowed with ripe grains because of These two, the Earth, a fraction of Hari’s power, was very resplendent because of big Āgrayaṇa festivals and big parties in towns and villages.**

Alternatively:

**Перевод:**

**Richly endowed with ripe grains, the Earth, especially in towns and villages, was very resplendent with grand festivals related to Vedic offerings of new grains and to Indra, and was even more so with These two amśas of Hari.**

Optionally:

**Перевод:**

**Richly endowed with ripe grains, the Earth, very resplendent because of big Āgrayaṇa festivals and big parties in towns and villages, looked like Nārāyaṇa’s Bhū potency because of These two.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The Earth was resplendent with festivals, those that were Vedic (āgrayaṇaiḥ = vaidikaiḥ), whose purpose was navānna (new grains) and prāśana (feeding, esp. the first feeding of a child), and those that were worldly, for the sake of the senses (aindriyaiś ca = indriyārthaiḥ laukikaiḥ ca).

Kalābhyām means: rāma-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ darśanādi-mahotsavābhyām, “with Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, two kalā \[expansions of Hari\] that were two festivals for the eyes.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“In towns,” such as Śrī Yadu-purī (Mathurā), or in Nandīśvara and other dwelling places of Śrī Nanda.

“The Earth shone in a special way (nitarām = viśeṣataḥ) with Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Śrī Rāma, two kalās—the forms of a topmost resplendence by the manifestation of Their entire godhood—of Lord Śrī Nārāyaṇa (hareḥ kālābhyam = bhagavataḥ śrī-nārāyaṇasya kalābhyāṁ nijākhila-bhagavattā-prakaṭanena parama-śobhā-rūpābhyāṁ śrī-kṛṣṇa-rāmābhyām).”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“In towns,” such as Śrī Mathurā. “In villages that were like villages,” such as Śrī Nanda’s dwelling place. Regarding āgrayaṇaiḥ, there is a verse:

*navānnaṁ naiva nandāyāṁ na ca supte janārdane \|*  
*na kṛṣṇa-pakṣe dhanuṣi tulāyāṁ naiva kārayet \|\|*

**“One should not do navānna on nandā (the name of three auspicious tithis: the first, the sixth, and the eleventh day of a fortnight), nor when Janārdana is asleep (the rainy season), nor in the dark fortnight, in dhanus (Sagittarius, or between November 22nd and December 21st), nor in tulā (Libra, or between September 23rd to October 22nd).”**

It should be understood to be after prabodhinī (the eleventh day in the bright fortnight of Kārttika), in vṛścika (Scorpio, or between October 23rd and November 21st). It is a custom of śarad only because of being at the end of śarad.

“With great festivals, which also consisted of a worship to Indra” (aindriyaiś ca = indra-pūjā-mayaiḥ ca), because of being said with: indram indriya-kāmas tu, “but one who desires sensory power should worship Indra” (Bhāgavatam 2.3.2). Nanda will consider that the pūjā to Indra is a worldly tradition. The pūjā to him used to take place in Vraja, and elsewhere, only in Kārttika. Govardhana-pūjā was set in motion by the Lord only after destroying the pūjā to him.

What is the Earth like? It is a potency (kalā = śaktiḥ) of Hari. Ābhyām (with These two) means rāma-kṛṣṇābhyām (with Rāma and Kṛṣṇa).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Āgrayaṇaiḥ means navānna-prāśanārthaiḥ vaidikaiḥ (with Vedic festivals for the purpose of navānna and prāśana). This citation is from Smṛti: navānnaṁ… (see above).

Indriyaiḥ \[BBT reading\] means indra-devatākaiḥ, “\[by festivals,\] whose presiding deity was Indra.” This is a description of the autumn before the disruption of the cowherds’ sacrifice to Indra.

What is the Earth like? It is a potency (kalā = śaktiḥ) of Hari. Or hari means candra (moon). The explanation is this: hareś candrasya kalābhyāṁ śukla-dvitīyā-sāyam-uditābhyām utsavaiḥ rājakīya-puruṣa-prabhṛti-kṛtair yathā saiva bhūḥ, “just as the Earth was resplendent with festivals done by royals, men, etc., for the sake of two kalās of the moon which were risen on the evening of the second day of the bright fortnight.” If the word yathā (like) is added, to avoid breaking the procedure, the simile is acceptable. Medinī-kośa states: hariś candrārka-vātāśva-śuka-bheka-yamāhiṣu, “Hari means moon, sun, wind, horse, parrot, frog, Yama, and snake.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“The Earth, a potency of Hari, completely shone with Śrī Rāma and Śrī Kṛṣṇa.” Indriyaiḥ means indriyārthaiḥ laukikaiḥ ca, “\[with great festivals\] that were for sense gratification and that were commonplace.”

Anvitārtha-prakāśikā—Nitarāṁ babhau means atiśayena aśobhata (the Earth was intensely resplendent).

**Annotation**

Viśvanātha Cakravartī writes: svarūpa-bhūtāyāḥ sākṣād bhū-śakteḥ satyabhāmāyā aṁśa-bhūtā asyā eva vibhūtiḥ pṛthivī prasiddhā, “The Earth, an aṁśa of Satyabhāmā who is Bhū-śakti, which is svarūpa-śakti, is a vibhūti of hers” (Sārārtha-darśinī 10.42.1). The designation Bhū is also used in another context: In Bhāgavat-sandarbha 22 Jīva Gosvāmī discusses three aspects, Śrī, Bhū, and Durgā, of the material energy. He adds: bhūs tat-sṛṣṭi-śaktiḥ, “Bhū is the potency of the creation of the world.” In Bhāgavat-sandarbha 98, he specifies that the Lord’s spiritual energies have material counterparts that bear the same name. In Bhāgavat-sandarbha 98.2, he elaborates upon the spiritual Śrī and the material Śrī. In the next subsection he mentions Bhū: tatra ilā bhūḥ, “Of those energies, Ilā is Bhū” (Bhāgavat-sandarbha 98.3).

### 10.20.49

*vaṇiṅ-muni-nṛpa-snātā nirgamyārthān prapedire \|*  
*varṣa-ruddhā yathā siddhāḥ sva-piṇḍān kāla āgate \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇij—merchants; muni—sages; nṛpa—kings; snātāḥ—‘bathed’ (i.e. snātakas); nirgamya—after setting out; arthān—the goals; prapedire—obtained; varṣa-ruddhāḥ—checked by the rain (or obstructed by years); yathā—like; siddhāḥ—perfected beings; sva-piṇḍān—own bodies; kāle āgate—when the time comes.

*yathā siddhāḥ (varṣa-ruddhāḥ) kāle āgate (sati) sva-piṇḍān (prāpnuvanti, tathā) vaṇiṅ-muni-nṛpa-snātāḥ varṣa-ruddhāḥ (santaḥ) nirgamya arthān prapedire (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**Merchants, sages, kings and graduate Brahmacārīs had been impeded by the rains (varṣa-ruddha). After the rainy season, they departed and achieved their goals. Likewise, perfected beings, obstructed for years (varṣa-ruddha), obtain their ideal bodies when the time comes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Merchants, renunciants (muni = yati), kings, and snātakas, impeded by the rain—because of dṛṣṭa (foreseen potential results of actions) and adṛṣṭa (fate, i.e. unforeseen potential results of action)—went out and obtained the goals—commerce, independence, conquering the world, and knowledge—like beings perfected by mantra and yoga (siddhāḥ = mantra-yogādi-siddhāḥ)— these beings too are obstructed by their life span—obtain, when the time comes, bodies,” such as gods, which are attainable by yoga and so on (sva-piṇḍān = yogādi-prāpyān devādi-dehān).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Merchants, renunciants (muni = yati), kings, and snātakas were impeded by the rain. Setting out at the end of the rainy season (nirgamya = varṣānte niṣkramya), they obtained the goals—commerce, independence, conquering the world, and knowledge—like perfected beings, obstructed by years that constituted their life span (varṣa-ruddhāḥ is carried forward) (varṣa-ruddhāḥ = svāyur-ghaṭakaiḥ vatsaraiḥ ruddhāḥ), obtain, when the time for the end comes (kāle āgate = anta-samaye āgate), bodies of transcendental associates (sva-piṇḍān = pārṣadādi-dehān). The simile is agreeable.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

The stanza was already elucidated by the venerable one. Alternatively: “… like liberated souls (siddhāḥ = jīvan-muktāḥ), who were covered (ruddhāḥ = āvṛtāḥ) by the knowledge of advaita,” which is equal to the rains since it covers the sun of bhakti. Or they were made to be submissive (ruddhāḥ = vaśī-kṛtāḥ) by the bliss of sat-saṅga that is incessant like the rains, or perhaps because of the attainment of a planet of Vaikuṇṭha by the grace of the Lord. “They obtain, when the time is reached (āgate = prāpte), bodies of pārṣadas, which are dense sat-cid-ānanda and which are suitable for them (sva-piṇḍān = svasya yogyān sac-cid-ānanda-ghana-pārṣada-dehān).”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The word varṣa (rain) is also expressive of time. The sense is āyuḥ (life span), and so the drift is: jīvanārtha-parimitaiḥ vatsaraiḥ ruddhāḥ, “\[perfected beings,\] obstructed by a limited number of years to live.” The goals of the snātakas include traveling to holy places. The perfected being are beings perfected by bhakti and so forth. They get bodies of pārṣadas that can be attained (sva-piṇḍān = prāptavya-pārṣada-dehān).

## Chapter 21 - The Song of the Flute

### 10.21.1

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*ittham sarat-svaccha-jalam padmakara-sugandhina* ***\|***  
*nyavisad vayuna vatam sa-go-gopalako ’cyutah* ***\|\|***

**Пословный перевод:**

*sri-sukah uvaca***—**Sri Suka said; *ittham***—**in this way; *sarad***—**because of autumn; *svaccha***—**is translucid; *jalam***—**whose water; *padma- akara***—**from a pond abounding in lotuses; *su-gandhina***—**which had a nice fragrance; *nyavisat***—**entered; *vayuna***—**by a wind; *vatam***—** \[the forest,\] ventilated; *sa-go-gopalakah***—**who was accompanied by cows and by cow herders; *acyutah***—**Acyuta.

*sri-sukah uvaca—acyutah sa-go-gopalakah sarat-svaccha-jalam padmakara-sugandhina vayuna vatam ittham (vanam) nyavisat.*

**Перевод:**

**Sri Suka said: Accompanied by cows and cow herders, Acyuta entered the forest where the lakes were clear because of autumn and which was ventilated by a breeze that had a nice scent from lotus ponds.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*eka-vimse sarad-ramya-vrndavana-gate harau* ***\|***  
*tad-venu-svanam akarnya gopibhir gitam iryate \|\|*

**“In the twenty-first chapter, when He went in the forest of Vrnda- vana, which was delightful because of autumn, He played the flute; hearing this, the** ***gopis*** **sang a song.”**

**10.21.1**

“He entered the forest (*vanam* is added), which was in this way *(ittham* = *evam-bhutam).”* Suka expounds: “In it, the bodies of water were translucid because of autumn (*sarat-svaccha-jalam = sarada svacchani jalani yasmin tat).* It was followed (*vatam = anugatam)* by the wind.” This means it was mostly filled by that.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

After portraying autumn in this manner, from this verse to the end of the chapter he mentions a particular amusement of the Lord at that time. At first, in one verse and a half he again talks of the forest as an assistant of that, as the abode of lovely water and wind, and as being lovely in its own right.

The water was lovely; this is clear because it was translucent, due to the manifestion of the natural quality by being devoid of impurity. And so was the wind.

*Padmakara* denotes *padmanam akarah,* in other words: *prasphuta-padma-mayah sarovaradih,* “a lake and the like which had fully bloomed lotuses.” Thus the breeze was nicely fragrant because of that, and cooling too. In point of *vatam* (ventilated), the breeze was slow, and so was everything in the forest.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The first paragraph is the same.) The sense of *ittham* is: *yathaham varnitavan, prayas tatha varnana-prakarena,* “in the manner of a description mostly like I narrated.” The word *sa-go-gopalakah* is a modifier of *madhupatih* in the next verse. Or, due to a pastime whose form, which ought to be depicted, reaches the heart, this is said because of the rise of a special emotion, as a result of which the main noun, any synonym of “Sri Krsna,” was not pronounced. The term “*sri-krsnah*” is the remainder of the sentence that is to be understood. The same applies ahead, in the verse that begins *barhapidam* (10.21.5). The reading *acyutah* meets the approval of Citsukha. Only in this one, *vanam* needs to be added.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Starting from this verse, the apex of the splendor of the forest when He entered it is illustrated.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*eka-vimse venu-gita-smararta gopika muhuh \|*  
*venu-vrndavana-mrgi-devy-adinam yaso jaguh \|\|*  
*yad yad vanam gatah krsnas caritam madhuram vyadhat \|*  
*prema-netreksitam gopyo gostha-sthas tad avarnayan \|\|*

**“This is in the twenty-first chapter: The** ***gopis,*** **pained by Cupid by means of a flute song, repeatedly sing the fame of the flute and of the does, goddesses and other inhabitants of Vrndavana. Staying in the village, the** ***gopis*** **described whichever forest Krsna, who did sweet deeds, went to. They saw with eyes of love.”**

Having depicted autumn, now, to narrate the pastime, which pertains to that season, of the song of the flute, at first he talks about Krsna’s entrance in Vrndavana, which was adorned with the sweetness of autumn.

In reference to *padmakara-sugandhina,* coolness and a nice fragrance are to be understood from a connection with *padmakara* (lake abounding in lotuses), and so is the slowness of the breeze, owing to the singular in *vayuna,* since it is not said *vayubhih* (by winds). In regard to *sa-go-gopalakah,* which means *go-gopalaka- sahitah* (accompanied by cows and by cow herders), the syntactical connection is with *madhupatih,* the word which is the main noun and is in the next verse.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

*eka-vimse venu-nada-matta gopyah smararditah \|*  
*vrndatavyam jaguh kirtim mrgy-adinam muhur muhuh \|\|*

**“In the twenty-first chapter, the** ***gopis,*** **maddened by the sound of a flute and pained by Cupid, repeatedly sang the renown of the does and of others in Vrnda’s forest.”**

**10.21.1**

“Madhupati—this is a concomitant syntactical connection with that word in the next verse—entered forest after forest (*vanam vanam),* each of which was ventilated, or followed (*vatam = anugatam*), by the wind.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

He completely (or continuously) *(ni* = *nitaram*) entered a forest.

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

The *atmanepada* in *nyavisat* is poetic license (is justified in consideration of the sages’ license to break the rules of grammar).

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Because of the *sutra: ner visah,* “\[An *atmanepada* suffix is applied\] after *vis* which is after *ni"* (*Astadhyayi* 1.3.17; HNV 722), the rule for the *atmanepada* pertains to *laukika* Sanskrit, not to *vaidika* Sanskrit (but *Bhagavatam* conforms to the rules of *laukika* Sanskrit).

### 10.21.2

*kusumita-vanaraji-susmi-bhrnga-*  
*dvija-kula-ghusta-sarah-sarin-mahidhram \|*  
*madhupatir avagahya carayan gah*  
*saha-pasupala-balas cukuja venum \|\|*  
*(puta)*  
*(with irregularities)*

**Пословный перевод:**

*kusumita—*flowering; *vana-raji*—in trees (“which make the forest resplendent”); *susmi*—vigorous (ruttish or maddened) (“that which has fire / wind (*susma,* “that which dries”)”); *bhrnga*—of bees; *dvija*—of birds; *kula*—because of multitudes; *ghusta*—were resounding; *sarah*—in which the lakes; *sarit*—rivers; *mahi-dhram*— and mountains (*mahi-dhara* “which hold the Earth”); *madhupatih*—the protector of the Madhus (or the master of honey, i.e. of sweetness); *avagahya*—going deep (entering); *carayan gah*—while tending cows; *saha-pasu-pala-balah*—accompanied by herders of animals and by Bala; *cukuja*—sounded; *venum*—a flute.

*madhupatih gah carayan saha-pasu-pala-balah (san) kusumita- vanaraji-susmi-bhrnga-dvija-kula-ghusta-sarah-sarin-mahidhram (vanam) avagahya venum cukuja.*

**Перевод:**

**The lakes, rivers and hills resounded because of energetic birds and bees in flowering trees. Accompanied by Bala and the herdsmen, Madhupati, tending cows, sounded a flute while penetrating the wilderness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Krsna played (*cukuja = avadayat)* the flute after entering (*avagahya* = *pravisya)* the forest, in which the lakes, the rivers, and the hills resounded because of multitudes of maddened bees and birds in flowering trees (*kusumita-vanaraji-susmi-bhrnga- dvija-kula-ghusta-sarah-sarin-mahidhram* = *kusumita-vana-rajisu susmino matta bhrnga dvijah khagas ca tesam kulani tair ghustah saramsi sarito mahidhras ca yasmin tad vanam).*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

(The commentary is the same. In addition:) Madhupati is Krsna. In reference to *avagahya* (after entering): He is the master of *madhu,* i.e. of *vasanta* (spring), by the entering of which the forest is resplendent. Thus an excellent resplendence is implied as a double meaning.

*Cukuja* means *kujayamasa* (He sounded). Concerning *saha- pasupala-balah,* togetherness takes place in entering the forest and in tending cows, but not in playing a flute, because of the statement “*krsnasya venu-gitam*” in the next verse.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

All this too is said as an excitant (*uddipana)* of love. As before, the fact that this sort of amusement is continual should be perceived. A continuous description of *cukuja* (He sounded) is to be inferred ahead also.

The connection is: *sa-go-gopalako madhupatih.* Or, due to a pastime whose form, which ought to be portrayed, reaches the heart, this is said by the origination of a special emotion, either because of not pronouncing the substantive or because of the inability to pronounce “*sri-krsnah,* ” which is the remainder of the sentence that is to be understood (in verse 1), and similarly ahead, in the verse beginning *barhapidam* (10.21.5). The reading *acyutah* meets the approval of Sri Citsukha.

In point of *madhupatih,* the Madhus are the Yadavas. He is their Lord *(patih = isvarah).* Although there is an impossibility of Him tending the cows, by doing so He means to signify a special Rasa (pleasure), beginning from *bhakta-vatsalya. Madhu* (liquor) is a particular intoxicating drink. He is the master *(patih = svami)* of that. As a double meaning in this way, being intoxicated at that time and being an intoxicator are implied.

*Avagahya* means *antah pravisya* (after penetrating within): Penetrating the forest everywhere hints at the transcendental fact of His entering within everything. He was accompanied by the herdsmen and by Bala (*saha-pasu-pala-balah* = *pasupalaih balena ca sahitah*): This means they also played a flute. Or, the syntactical connection is: *saha-pasu-pala-balo gas carayan* (accompanied by Bala and the herdsmen while tending cows).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

On account of being Yadavas, the cowherds too are Madhus: He is their protector (*madhu-patih* = *yadavatvad gopah ca madhavah tesam patih).* Having all the requisites for the fun is thus suggested. As a pun, He is the master of spring too, the king of seasons (*madhu-patih* = *rtu-rajasya api patih).* By His entering, the full resplendence, i.e. the apex of it, of the forest is pointed out.

*Avagahya* means *antah pravisya* (after penetrating within): By penetrating the forest everywhere, the knowledge of the truth of the matter is implied. The syntactical connection of *saha-pasupala-balah* (accompanied by the cow herders and by Bala) should only be with *gas carayan* (He grazed the cows), but not with *cukuja venum* (He sounded the flute). Moreover, the meaning of *\[n\]i* (the causative sense) is included in *cukuja.2*

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Nanda’s son is the master (*patih = svami)* of cowherds, who are Madhavas on account of being Yadavas.3

### 10.21.3

*tad vraja-striya asrutya venu-gitam smarodayam \|*  
*kascit paroksam krsnasya sva-sakhibhyo ’nvavarnayan \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tat*—that; *vraja-striyah*—the women in the cowherd village; *asrutya*—after hearing; *venu-gitam*—the song of the flute; *smara-udayam*—because of which there is a rise of Cupid (“who makes one remember”); *kascit*—some of them; *paroksam*—in the manner of being out of sight (or in private); *krsnasya*—of Krsna; sva- *sakhibhyah*—to their female friends; *anvavarnayan*—continuously described.

*kascit vraja-striyah tad krsnasya venu-gitam smarodayam asrutya sva- sakhibhyah (tad gitam) paroksam (yatha syat tatha) anvavarnayan.*

**Перевод:**

**Listening to that song of Krsna’s flute, due to which there was an upsurge of Cupid, some women of the village continuously described it to their lady friends, unperceived by others.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Hearing (*asrutya = srutva)* that song of Krsna’s flute (*tad krsnasya venu-gitam* = *tat krsna-venu-gitam),* because of which there was a rise of Cupid (*smarodayam* = *smarasya udayah yasmat tad)...” Paroksam* (out of sight; privately) is an adverb, since they were in the village.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Hearing that song of Krsna’s flute (*tad krsnasya venu-gitam)..." Paroksam* is an adverb, since those ladies were in the village.4

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

The song of Krsna’s flute there (*tat = tatra).* They narrated either after the song or continuously *(anu = gitanantaram nirantaram va).* The reason for that is: *smarodayam.* This means: *tasya eva smarena kamena gopi-smaranena va udayah yasya,* “\[The flute song\] has a rise due to His love—by seeing that kind of water and so on—or due to His remembrance of the *gopis.* ” Or: *smarasya udayah yasmat tat* (the flute song, because of which there is a rise of lust). Although He has that sort of nature at all times, being such is said due to a special playing on account of the origination of His special mood then. Consequently there also was a continuous description of it by those girls right then.

There is another explanation: *tad* (“that” flute song) optionally means that the topmost enchantment is suggestive of Krsna’s special emotion, because: *smarodayam.* The rest is the same.

“The women of the village” or “the women present in the village” (*vraja-striyah = vrajasya vraje va vartamanah yah striyah tah).* They completely heard from afar (*asrutya* = *durato’pi samyak srutva*), since they were made to stay, either by Krsna’s particular desire or simply by the influence of their emotions. Or: “after hearing a little” (*asrutya = isat srutva).5*

The girls heard *venu-gitam,* “what was sung by the flute,” or “the song of the flute” because, merely by the touch of Sri Krsna’s lips, it automatically came across as a special twist on His cooing. By the action of *kujanam* (sounding, lit., cooing) expressed by the verb *cukuja* in the previous verse, only a song is meant.6

“Some women” denotes Sri Radha Devi and others who had extraordinary feelings. Although all the women of the village heard it, those that were high in rank only experienced the rise of an increase of *vatsalya,* and so they are discarded.

*Paroksam* means: *tasam evasaksat nibhrtam,* “clandestinely only to them, without being directly present,” therefore they only spoke to their friends (*sva-sakhibhyah* = *sviyabhyah sakhibhyah = tah prati)* such as Sri Lalita. Or the dative case has the sense of *tadarthyam* (for their sake). The sense is: “for the sake of their happiness,” because of one derives joy from their joy.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“The song of Krsna’s flute there” (*tat=tatra*), or “that very song of Krsna’s flute” *(tad - tad eva).* They narrated either after the song or continuously *(anu = gitanantaram nirantaram va).* The reason for that is *smarodayam,* an adverb: “Hearing in such a way that there was a manifestation of Cupid *(smarodayam = smarasya udayah prakatyam yatra tadrsam yatha syat tatha)."* Although He always delights in playing a flute, this is said because of the display of a distinct cleverness by the manifestation of an excellent age. In addition, His emotions were ablaze also by seeing the play of the Laksmi of autumn, and He was showing off His skill in playing a flute to completely attract those girls. Their being like that occurred due to that skill. Consequently there also was a continuous description of it by those ladies right at that time.

They completely heard even from afar *(asrutya = durato ’pi samyak srutva),* because Krsna’s nature pervades all, especially when there is a melody *(kalatve ’pi sarva-vyapi-svabhavatvat).* Or: “after hearing a little” *(asrutya = isat srutva).*

(This paragraph is the same.) “Some women” denotes Sri Radha Devi and others who had special emotions. Although all the women of the village heard it, because it is going to be said: *sarva-bhuta-manoharam* (10.21.6), the mothers, etc., only had a rise of *vatsalya* and so on, but not a rise of Cupid, and so they are set aside. Therefore they only spoke for the sake of their friends *(sva- sakhibhyah* = *sviyabhyah sakhibhyah)* such as Sri Lalita.

The sense is: *nija-mano-baspodgiranaya tah api sravayitum* (for the sake of ejecting tears from their own minds, to make those ladies too listen). By the word *sva* (own), the lady friends of the lady friends are excluded; their being very well-behaved is thus shown. What is the use of saying much? Over and above that, *paroksam,* which means: *arthantarac channam savahittham yatha syat tatha,* “secretly, because of another purpose, i.e. in such a way that there was the concealment of external symptoms.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“Some women” denotes only the beloveds.

### 10.21.4

*tad varnayitum arabdhah smarantyah krsna-cestitam \|*  
*nasakan smara-vegena viksipta-manaso nrpa \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

*tat*—that; *varnayitum*—to describe; *arabdhah*—they who had begun to begin; *smarantyah*—while remembering; *krsna-cestitam*— Krsna’s style; *na asakan*—they were not able; *smara-vegena*—by the momentum of Cupid; *viksipta-manasah*—they whose minds are distraught; *nrpa*—O king.

*nrpa! (tah gopyah) tad (venu-gitam) varnayitum arabdhah (api) krsna-cestitam smarantyah smara-vegena viksipta-manasah (satyah, vamanam kartum) na asakan.*

**Перевод:**

**Although they had begun to begin describing it, they, whose hearts were overwhelmed due to an outburst of Cupid while remembering Krsna’s style, were unable to make a description, O king!**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Viksipta-manasah* means *vyakula-cittah* (they whose hearts are overwhelmed).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

*Arabdhah* means *arabdhavatyah* (they had begun). The idea is: Obviously, the conclusion of what has begun is expected. Still, they were incapable. The reason for that is: *smara,* which means: *smarasya sri-krsna-smrti-visesasya tad-visayaka- kamasya,* “\[due to an outburst\] of *smara,* a special remembrance of Sri Krsna, i.e. a love whose object is Him.” “They were remembering, that is taking interest in, the deed—either the deed that consists of playing that flute or the style (*cestitam*) described ahead—of Krsna, who attracts the hearts of all.” There is another explanation: “Some ladies did a description; some ladies, although they had begun to describe it, were incapable.”

*Nrpa* is a vocative on account of agitation by his own obtainment of a special emotion by narrating that. Or it is for the sake of addressing him after perceiving the rise of a special emotion only in him.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In this verse he talks about the sequence of the upsurge of Cupid. “Although they had begun (*arabdhah = arabdhavatyo ’pi)* to describe it, which was of that sort, in private (*tat* = *tadrsam paroksam yatha syat tatha),* they were unable,” i.e. they were unable to describe in that way *(nasakan* = *tatha varnayitum na aparayan).* The reason for that is: *smara.* Why? “They were remembering—i.e. taking interest in—the deed, consisting of that flute song, of Krsna, who attracts the hearts of all.” *Nrpa* is a vocative... (The rest is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Although they had begun *(arabdhah* = *arabdhavatyo ’pi)* to describe the flute song *(tad* = *venu-gitam),* they were unable to describe *(nasakan = varnayitum na asakan)."* The reason for that is: *smara-vegena* (due to an outburst of Cupid).

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

*Viksipta-manasah* (their minds were overwhelmed) means *vyakula-hrdayah* (their hearts were overwhelmed).

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

They had begun to describe it, i.e. either the Lord’s form or the flute song.

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

“Although they, who were remembering Krsna’s style, had begun to describe Krsna’s style *(tat = krsna- cestitam),* they were unable to make a description *(nasakan* = *vamanam kartum na asakan).” Arabdhah* means *arabdhavatyo ’pi* (although they had begun). The rule: *adi-karmani ktah kartari ca,* “When it denotes the beginning of an action, the suffix *\[k\]ta* is also used in the active voice” *(Astadhyayi* 3.4.71); (thus *arabdhah* means ‘they begun to begin’).

### 10.21.5

*barhapidam nata-vara-vapuh karnayoh karnikaram*  
*bibhrad vasah kanaka-kapisam vaijayantim ca malam \|*  
*randhran venor adhara-sudhaya purayan gopa-vrndair*  
*vrndaranyam sva-pada-ramanam pravisad gita-kirtih \|\|*  
*(mandakranta)*

**Пословный перевод:**

*barha*—is a peacock’s tail feather; *apidam*—on which the head decoration; *nata-vara*—\[like the body\] of the best of dancers (or of actors); *vapuh*—a body; *karnayoh*—on both ears; *karnikaram*—a *karnikara* flower; *bibhrat*—wearing (or having); *vasah*—a garment; *kanaka*—gold; *kapisam*—dark yellow; *vaijayantim*—\[named\] *vaijayanti; ca*—and; *malam*—a garland; *randhran*—the holes; *venoh*—of a flute; *adhara-sudhaya*—with the nectar of the lips; *purayan*—while filling; *gopa-vrndaih*—by a multitude of cow herders; *vrnda-aranyam*—Vrnda’s forest; *sva-pada*—because of His footprints; *ramanam*—in which there is a delight; *pravisat*—He entered; *gita-kirtih*—He whose fame is sung.

*(sri-krsnah) nata-vara-vapuh barhapidam karnayoh karnikaram kanaka-kapisam vasah vaijayantim malam ca bibhrad venoh randhran (svasya) adhara-sudhaya purayan gopa-vrndaih gita-kirtih (san) sva-pada-ramanam vrndaranyam pravisad (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**He had the form of the best of dancers. Wearing a peacock feather as a head ornament, a** ***kamikara*** **flower on each ear, a garment dark yellow like gold, and a** ***vaijayanti*** **garland, He, whose fame was sung by cow herders, entered Vrnda’s forest, delightful because of His footprints, while filling the holes of His flute with the nectar of His lips.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Remembrance of Krsna turned out as an agitator of those ladies’ minds. In this verse he gives the details of the remembrance. “Having a body that was excellent like a dancer’s *(nata-vara-vapuh bibhrat* = *nata-vad-varam vapuh bibhrat),* He entered Vrndavana *(vrndaranyam = vrndavanam)."* How was the forest? *sva-pada-ramanam,* “It evoked delight because of His footprints, which were marked” (= *sva-padaih ankitaih rati- janakam).* The prose order is: *gopa-vrndair gita-kirtih* (He, whose fame was sung by cow herders).

In that way, He was holding a head ornament made of peacock tail feathers (*barhapidam = barha-mayam apidam siro-bhusanam).* Or *barhapidam* is an adjective of *vapuh* (body): *barham apidah yasmin* (on which the head ornament is a peacock’s tail feather).

With *randhran venoh* (the holes of the flute) and so on, playing a flute is fancifully imagined. Therefore the drift is: “Indeed, while moving out of the filled flute, the nectar of the lips ought to diffuse like a song.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

By the origination of an outstanding mood in this way, Sri Vyasa-nandana, remembering the apparel of Sri Nanda- nandana at that time, describes it right in the middle of those ladies’ description of it: his intention was elucidated by Sridhara Svami in his preliminary.

Or, to talk about yet another reason, he describes His form; he speaks with this intention: “They were unable because of His particular forestial apparel, which overwhelms the heart by the remembrance of His style, and because their own minds were excited.”

There is another explanation: In this verse he says, “Afterward, they continuously gave a description after mustering some strength, somehow,” because in the next verse, beginning with *iti,* Sri Badarayani mentions the sound of the flute exactly that way.

Sometimes the reading *nata-vara* is seen. The compound *nata- nara-vapuh7* means: *natah ca asau narah ca iti tadvad-vicitra-vesam vapuh,* “He is a body which has an amazing attire like that of a dancing male. Or He was manifesting (*bibhrat = prakatayan)* a body because of which all living entities are dancing with joy (*nata-nara- vapuh = natanti harsa-bharena nrtyanti iti natah narah jivah sarve yasmat tad vapuh).* Another explanation is: *tad vapur yasya sah* (He has the body of a male dancer).8

Although *karnikaram* is in the singular, a pair is to be understood because of a pair of ears. The same applies to *vasah* (the garment). The *karnikara* has a yellow color. It is a flower that is the form of a water lily (*utpala*).9He was wearing it because of the affluence in autumn and specifically in spring, and since it promotes a distinct resplendence. The garland called Vaijayanti (*vaijayantim malam = vaijayanti nama mala tam)* is strung with flowers of five colors.

He was filling *(purayan)* the holes (*randhran* = *randhrani)* of a flute with the nectar of the lips; thus, He played the flute with a special emotion. In that way, it’s implied that the flute is most enchanting like that nectar.

It is Vrnda’s forest (*vrndaranyam = vrndayah aranyam).* This means it is especially embellished by her, the presiding deity of it, by intending to express a zeal for the special amusements of the Lord. Therefore it is delightful, meaning it makes her, or everyone, happy *(ramanam = tasyah sarvesam va sukha-karam),* because of His footprints—they are extraordinary—which are marked everywhere *(sva-pada-ramanam = svaih asadharanaih padaih sarvatra ankitaih ramanam).* Optionally: *sva-pada-ramanam* signifies *sva-padayoh rati-janakam,* “The forest produces delight for both feet of His,” since it consists of delightful and soft dust particles, flowers, flower pollen, leaves, and so forth.

His fame, the form of various types of beauty and cleverness, was sung (*gita-kirtih* = *gita kirtih yasya)* by a multitude of cowherds. Or, *gita-kirtih* means: *gita kirtih gopinam yasmin,* “He for whom the fame of the *gopis* is sung” by cow herders after perceiving a special *bhava* of His. Not directly mentioning those ladies is due to bashfulness.

There is no representation of ornaments such as a pearl necklace and golden armlets since that description is eternally established automatically. Or it’s because of entering in the forest just in that fashion exclusively with a forestial apparel for the purpose of a particular recreation on the first day of autumn.

Not mentioning here an accompaniment by Sri Baladeva, which was mentioned earlier and is going to be related ahead, is because he might feel out of place after seeing the elder brother with a certain emotion. Or, inasmuch as only Sri Krsna’s style, which is to be depicted, is most enchanting, he is left out because describing him does not add to the splendor of the situation. Another interpretation is that he is included by *gopa-vrndaih* (the multitudes of cowherds). In that regard, there is no clear mention of him being secondary.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Because of those various special emotions, Suka expounds upon the song. This verse and the next make one unit of two verses. *Nata-vara-vapuh* (He has the body of the best of dancers) is a *bahuvrihi,* by a figurative superimposition (*upacara)* of difference although there is no difference. The sense is He was had the attire of a dancer. By its very nature, *nata-vara-vapuh* is the very best of all His forms. It amazes even Him, in reference to this verse:

*yan martya-lilaupayikam sva-yoga-*  
*maya-balam darsayata grhitam \|*  
*vismapanam svasya ca saubhagarddheh*  
*param padam bhusana-bhusanangam \|\|*

**“Krsna’s form was suited to human pastimes. It was taken by Him to show the power of His Yogamaya. It amazes Him also. It is the utmost limit of an abundance of loveliness, and its limbs are the ornaments of its ornaments.” (*****Bhagavatam*** **3.2.12)10**

“Assuming that body” means *sasvac-chobavirbhavanena pusnan* (while enhancing it by causing the constant rise of resplendence). Sometimes the reading *nata-vara* is seen.

The *kamikara* has a yellow color. It is a flower that is the form of an *utpala* (lotus, water lily). The garland called Vaijayanti is strung with flowers of five colors. He was filling the holes (*randhran = randhrani)* of a flute with the nectar of the lips, and so the fact that the flute is most enchanting like that nectar is suggested.

It is Vrnda’s forest... (This paragraph is the same, except for this addition at the end): Although the cowherd village (*vraja*) is within Vrndavana, He goes barefoot outside of the village. (The rest of the commentary is the same, except that the last paragraph is:) Here, Baladeva is included by *gopa-vrndaih.* There is no mention of him in terms of Them being a pair. The fact that the divine cowherd ladies are solely fixed on Sri Krsna suggests that a description with his companionship is only due to being His assistant.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

What is that particular style of Krsna’s *(cestitam* in verse 4) which generates an outburst of lust and agitates their minds? In consideration of this, Sri Suka, on account of being omniscient, narrates.

He had the form of the best dancer (*nata-vara-vapur bibhrat*), on which the head ornament was a peacock’s tail feather (*barhapidam* = *barham apidah siro-bhusanam yatra).* He had a *karnikara* flower, only one, on both ears, sometimes on the left one and sometimes on the right. He had it to indicate that He is intoxicated by youthfulness. Specifically, Krsna’s style evoked an outburst of Cupid due to the supereminence of those ladies. He had a Vaijayanti garland, a garland strung with flowers of five colors.

With *randhran* and so on, playing a flute is fancifully imagined. The following is implied by that: Krsna had the desire (suspecting that the girls might find fault with the flute for having holes): “I am making My flute holeless simply with the nectar of My lips.” The nectar of the lips, however, made the flute, though lifeless, conscious by contacting it, made it alive, maddened the three worlds with it, and, afterward, knowing it as hard, as having an unconscious nature, and as unqualified, departed from its holes, made itself successful by entering the hearts of the ladies of the village through their ears, and showed all of its own prowess right there.

He entered the forest, in which there was a delight for His feet *(sva-pada-ramanam* = *sva-padayoh ramanam yatra),* by leaping and so on during the Rasa dance.11This is a distinguishing feature compared to the village. By the logical reasoning of enhancing what was said, “He entered” *(pravisat*) is not a useless repetition.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Krsna, along with the cow herders (*gopa- vrndaih = gopa-vrndaih saha),* entered Vrnda’s forest. He was wearing two garments golden like gold (*vasah kanaka-kapisam = svarna-gaura-vasasi).* He was filling the holes of the flute with the nectar of the lips. The nectar was the form of sweet tones that were high and low. It was the syllables of a mantra that was issuing out and that was bewildering. It had diverse melodies *(raga),* beats *(tala),* songs *(gana),* and modulations *(murcchana).* It had an excellence of sound. His fame was sung by gods (*gita-kirtih* = *suraih gita-kirtih).*

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

*Nata-nara-vapuh* means: *nata-vat nara-vad dvi-bhujam vapuh yasya* (He whose body is two-handed like the body of human and is like a dancer). Or *nata-nara-vapuh* is separated as *natana-ra-vapuh,* “He whose body makes one dance; literally it gives *natana* (dancing), a transformation that is the exultation of bliss” (= *natanam anandollasah vikarah tam rati iti natana-ram).* After seeing it, any living being dances, specifically the peacocks dance, either from the illusion of a cloud or from His accepting their own tail feathers. In the reading *nata-vara,* the sense is; *natebhyo 'pi varam* (better than dancers) or *nata-vat vara-vat,* “\[He whose body\] is like the body of a bridegroom who is like a dancer”: *varo vivaha- pravrttah,* “*Vara* means bridegroom.”12

Although there is only one *karnikara* on both ears, some say there is a special amusement: He puts a *karnikara* sometimes on the right ear, sometimes on the left.

He entered Vrndaranya. How was it? *sva-pada-ramanam,* which denotes: *sva-padanam sva-sthalanam vaikunthadinam api ramanam rati-pradam,* “It gives delight to Vaikuntha and other places of His.” The masculine gender in *randhran* is poetic license.

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

He had a garment yellow like gold (*kanaka- kapisam = kanaka-vat pitam).*

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

He had a garment tawny like gold (*kanaka-kapisam = kanaka-vat pisangam).*

**Annotation**

The gloss of *kapisa* either as golden or as yellow is not sourced anywhere. The word *kapisa* is also seen in *Bhagavatam* 3.33.14. Sridhara Svami glosses it as *pisahga* (tawny). The context is locks of matted hair. Hemacandra sums up the definitions of *kapisa* as follows: *kapisau sihlaka-syavau kapisa madhavi sura,* “*Kapisa* means *sihlaka* (olibanum, i.e. frankincense) and *syava* (brown). *Kapisa* means *madhavi* (*madhavi* flower) and *sura* (liquor)” (*Hema-kosa* 3.356). *Vacaspatya* and *Sabda-kalpa-druma* say *kapisa* can mean *krsna-pita-misrita-varna* (a color that is a mix of black and yellow). Similarly, commenting on: *syavah syat kapisah, “Syava* and *kapisa* are synonymous” (*Amara-kosa* 1.5.16), Bhanuji Diksita explains: *krsna-pitasya dve,* “Both of them pertain to that which is black and yellow” *(Sri Ramasrami* 1.5.16).

Furthermore, the word *kapisa* is made by *Astadhyayi* 5.2.100: The suffix *sa,* which has the sense of *mat \[up\],* is added after *kapi.* Thus *kapisa* primarily signifies *kapila-varna* (brown color) *(Svami-dayananda-vrtti* on *Unadi-sutra* 4.145). Etymologically, the word *kapi* is made by adding the suffix *i* after the verbal root *kap\[i\]* (to shake), and the *n\[um\]* of *kap\[i\]* is deleted (*Unadi-sutra* 4.145).

Moreover, Hemacandra states: *sarin kalyane sukhe,* “*Sam* means auspiciousness, and joy” (*Hema-kosa, parisista-kanda* 21). Thus *kanaka-kapi-sam* can be a *bahuvrihi* compound: “a garment that is golden and because of which there is joy that causes a thrill.” For example, commenting on *Bhagavatam* 10.1.20, the *acaryas* gloss *akapi* in ‘Vrsakapi’ as: *akampayati* (it fully causes a shake).

### 10.21.6

*iti venu-ravam rajan sarva-bhuta-manoharam \|*  
*srutva vraja-striyah sarva varnayantyo ’bhirebhire \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

*iti*—in this way (or *iti* marks the end of the quotation); *venu-ravam*— the sound of the flute; *rajan*—O king; *sarva-bhuta*—all beings; *manah-haram*—which captivates (“steals the mind”); *srutva*—after hearing; *vraja-striyah sarvah*—all the ladies of the village (or all the ladies abiding in the village); *varnayantyah*—while describing; *abhirebhire*—they embraced.

*rajan! iti venu-ravam sarva-bhuta-manoharam srutva vraja-striyah sarvah (venu-gitam) varnayantyah (parasparam) abhirebhire.*

**Перевод:**

**Hearing the sound of the flute, a sound which captivates all beings, O king, all the women of the village embraced while making a description.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

They embraced *(abhirebhire),* that is, while giving a description they embraced (*abhirebhire* = *parirabdhavatyah)* Krsna, the personification of the topmost bliss, in every word.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

*—Iti* means either *idrsam* (which was like this) or *anena prakarena* (in this manner). “All of them” *(sarvah),* that is, either those who were far or those who were near. Or *sarvah* means: *praudha-baladi-bhedena vartamanah* (all the ladies abiding as the varieties of proud women, etc.). Or: “everyone, as a group.” “They were describing” (*varnayantyah = varnayantyah satyah).* They continuously described only the sound of the flute (*venu- ravam = venu-ravam eva anvavarnayan),* since only that is the contextual topic—it was so even before (verse 3)—consequently it is to be inferred whereever this is not clear. Furthermore, ahead, the description of the form, the apparel, etc., too is because it is applicable due to their togetherness. Alternatively, *krsna-cestitam* (Krsna’s style/ deed), mentioned in verse 4, is to be carried forward here, due to the statement at the end of all: *varnayantyo mitho gopyah kridah,* “The *gopis* described the amusements to one another” (10.21.20).

“They gave a hug” (*abhirebhire*). This took place due to a contemplation on Sri Krsna, who overwhelmed the heart. Another explanation is that everyone hugged one another, owing to the nature of an upsurge of a special *bhava.* Or, possibly, they embraced only the sound of the flute. This means they made it adhere to the heart with love.

The reason in all cases is that the sound captivates all beings *(sarva-bhuta-manoharam = sarvesam eva bhutanam manoharam),* let alone those ladies. The reading *abhiremire* is only approved by Sri Citsukha. The sense is: *abhi abhitah ratim prapuh* (they had delight all around).

The vocative *rajan* is like *nrpa,* said earlier (verse 4). Or he addresses him: *bhava-visesena prakasamana* (O you shining with a special emotion). It’s understood that he got up by taking him by the hand, and hugged him.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) *Iti* means *anena prakarena* (in this manner). “All of them” *(sarvah)* means: *tasu eva praudha-baladi-bhedena vartamanah* (all the ladies who were present as the varieties of proud women, etc., among them). “They embraced” (*abhirebhire)* owing to a contemplation on Sri Krsna, who overwhelmed the heart. Or they embraced one another due to an infatuation arising from a special *bhava,* after thinking about Him. Another explanation is that everyone hugged one another owing to the nature of an upsurge of a special *bhava.*

The reason in all cases is that the sound captivates all living beings *(sarva-bhuta-manoharam* = *sarvesam eva bhutanam praninam manoharam*), let alone those ladies. The reading *abhiremire* is only approved by Citsukha. The sense is: *abhitah ratim prapuh* (they had delight all around). The vocative *rajan* is like *nrpa* mentioned previously.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In this stanza he says, “After a few moments, when there was an alleviation of the vehemence of the outburst of Cupid, who had risen by the remembrance of Krsna’s style, they were still completely unable to describe the song of the flute.”

*Iti* has the sense of *samapti* (end). The gist is: *smara-vega- viksepe samapte sati* (when the turbulence of the outburst of Cupid came to an end). *Amara-kosa* states: *iti hetu-prakarana-prakaradi-samaptisu,* *“Iti* is used in the senses of *hetu* (‘because’) *prakarana* (topic), *prakara* (manner), *adi* (beginning), and *samapti* (end)” (3.3.244).

The sound of the flute captivated all beings *(sarva-bhuta- manoharam),* but it is not that it captivated only the *gopis,* like at the time of the beginning of Rasa.

“They embraced while describing” *(varnayantyo 'bhirebhire*): *“Sakhi,* I am touched by the way you talk. Now I too want to describe it.” On account of perceiving that each girl had the same type of realization, the girls hugged one another.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“While describing the song of the flute *(varnayantyah = venu-gitam varnayantyah*), all of them embraced,” in other words, “while describing what was on their mind, they hugged one another,” or they embraced Krsna with the heart.

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

*Iti* means *vaksyamanam* (what is about to be said). Another explanation of *sarva-bhuta-manoharam* is as an adverb: “while describing in such a way that it was captivating to all beings.”

The ladies belong to many kinds of groups. For example: *vatsala* (motherly affectionate) and *anurakta* (in love). At first they are twofold. Further, the *vatsalas* are twofold: Sri Yasoda’s constant associates, and other mothers. The *anuraktas* too are twofold: *udha* (married) and *anudha* (unmarried). The married ones are twofold: *bala* (simple) and *sapatnya* (cowife). They are twofold: *pura-vadhu* (city wives) and *kevala-gopa* (only cowherd). All the married ones are twofold in another way: *sruti-rupa* (personified scriptures) and *kevala* (not so distinct). These *gopis* are threefold: *praudha, madhya,* and *mukhya.* The unmarried women are twofold: *siddha* and *sadhika.* The *siddhas* are twofold: *svabhava-siddha* (perfect by nature) and *tat-kala-bhagavat-prasada-siddha* (perfect by the grace of the Lord at that time). The *sadhikas* are threefold, by the categories of *uttama* (high), *madhyama* (mid-level), and *kanistha* (junior).

Further, these ones are twofold: *pradhana-kalpa* (almost primary) and *tat-sahacari-rupa* (their companions). Again, these ones are eightfold from the eight varieties of states. In addition, these ones are threefold on account of the varieties of *dhira* and so on. Thus there are many groups. Therefore the sense is: Those ladies who had the same disposition began a description which involved a mutual embrace with those who had a similar disposition. All of this will become clear in *rasa-vilasa* (the play of the Rasa).

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The sense of *iti* is *vaksyamana-prakarena* (in the manner about to be told).

**Annotation**

Usually *iti* either follows or precedes what it is connnected with. If *iti* is connected with the previous words, then *iti* marks the end of the quotation. But if *iti* is connected with the words that follow it, *iti* means *anena prakarena* (in this way). The *Bhagavatam* abounds in puns; the word *iti* here is paronomastic: Firstly, by connecting the words *iti venu-ravam srutva* (after hearing the sound of the flute in this manner), the verse says they heard the sound of the flute while hearing the description of Krsna stated in verse 5. And secondly, *iti* is connected with *varnayantyah* (while describing in this way), meaning verse 5 is Sukadeva’s description of what the *gopis* had begun to say, as he mentioned in verse 4, and so *iti* also marks the end of the quotation, hence *iti* is syntactically connected at the end of verse 5.

In verse 3, Sukadeva said the *gopis* continuously described (*anvarvanayan*) the song of the flute. It’s understood that the *gopis* regained their composure and began a description anew, starting from the next verse.

### 10.21.7

*gopya ucuh*  
*aksanvatam phalam idam na param vidamah*  
*sakhyah pasun anuvivesayator vayasyaih \|*  
*vaktram vrajesa-sutayor anuvenu-justam*  
*yair va nipitam anurakta-kataksa-moksam \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

*gopyah ucuh*—the *gopis* said; *aksan-vatam*—of those who have eyes; *phalam*—the prize; *idam*—this; *na*—not; *param*—another; *vidamah*—we know; *sakhyah*—O friends; *pasun anuvivesayatoh*— who are making the cows enter \[either the forest or the village\] in specific ways *(vi)* in order (*anu*)14; *vayasyaih*—with the companions (“of the same age”); *vaktram*—the face (the faces); *vraja-isa- sutayoh*—of the two sons of the chief of Vraja; *anu-venu-justam*— congenially served by a flute15; *yaih*—by which \[persons\]; *va*—or (or: perhaps); *nipitam*—continuously drunk; *anurakta*—loving; *kata-aksa*—sidelong glances; *moksam*—from which \[face\] there is a release.

*gopyah ucuh—sakhyah! (rama-krsnayoh) vayasyaih (saha) pasun anuvivesayatoh (satoh tayoh) vrajesa-sutayoh (yad) vaktram anuvenu-justam yaih (janaih drstam) nipitam va anurakta-kataksa-moksam (bhavati), idam (vaktram tesam jananam) aksanvatam phalam (bhavati. vayam atah phalat) param (utkrstam phalam) na vidamah.*

**Перевод:**

**The** ***gopis*** **said: “Girlfriends, this is the prize for those who have eyes; we don’t know another: The faces which are seen by such persons, if not continuously imbibed by them; which are served by a conformable flute; and from which there is a release of loving sidelong glances, of the two sons of the chief of Vraja when They graze the cows with Their companions.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

In thirteen verses, he talks about the continuous description. Here, the word “this” means “the sight of a dear one.” “This is the prize only for those who have eyes *(aksanvatam = caksusmatam tavat).* We don’t know *(na vidamah* = *na vidmah*) another *(param = anyat)."* The prize is the faces, which are served only by those by whom the faces are continuousy drunk *(justam yair va nipitam = yair nipitam tair eva sevitam),* of Rama and Krsna who, with Their companions, are making the animals enter a forest *(pasun anuvivesayator vayasyaih* = *sakhibhih saha pasun vanam pravesayatoh).*

How are Their faces? *anu-venu,* “They are playing a flute that continuously remains present” (= *venum anuvartamanam tam vadayat)* and *anurakta-kataksa-moksam,* “from which there is an emission of affectionate sidelong glances” (= *snigdha-kataksa- visargam).*

There is another interpretation: *yair nipitam tayor vaktram tair yaj justam idam evaksanvatam aksnoh phalam,* “This, the faces, which are served by those by whom they are continuously drunk, of both of Them, is the prize of the two eyes of those who have eyes.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Sridhara Svami’s disapproval of the verse preliminary “*sri-gopya ucuh*” is perceived, because he wrote: *anuvarnanam evaha,* “Suka talks about the continuous description.” However, that reading is seen everywhere.16

*yasam budhyate vag-artho yasam eva prasadatah \|*  
*gopih prapadye ta yabhih sa gambhirasayo jitah \|\|*

**“I take shelter of the** ***gopis,*** **by whose grace the sense of their speech is understood and by whom He, whose intentions are deep, was won over.”**

The mention of *idam* (this) at first is due to the inappropriateness of immediately revealing at the outset the meaning about to be said, the form of the topmost prize, since it is most confidential. Or it is because of the inability to point out a detail of it at once on account of helplessness due to an upsurge of profuse love for Him, who overwhelms the heart.

“We do not know *(na vidamah* = *na vidmah vayam*) another— i.e. another amazing sight such as Sri Vrndavana, or another sight of Him also, who is accompanied by others, either at another time or in another way—prize for both eyes *(aksanvatam = aksnoh)."* The sense is: *anye janas tv anyaj janantu nama,* “Let other people know anything else that they know.” This is these ladies’ sarcastic statement, and so the idea is: “Now our eyes are successful.” They can easily see Him in the village, but although the very act of imbibing His face, wherever, whenever, by any means, is the prize of the eyes, still they speak like that with an eagerness to see Him in that way during the amusements in the forests. Such is the nature of love: The thirst of intense love brings pain because it cannot be quenched. Moreover, the gist of the vocative *sakhyah* (girlfriends) is: “This is already known to all of you.”

Regarding *vrajesa-sutayoh,* Sri Baladeva and Sri Krsna are the sons of the two chiefs of Vraja: Sri Nanda and Sri Vasudeva. Sri Baladeva too is his son, in accordance with the text of *Sri Hari- vamsa: vasudeva iti khyato gosu tisthati bhu-tale,* “He, who is known as Vasudeva, abides among cows, on Earth,” or it is because he is a foster child, due to being with Sri Krsna. *Anuvivesayatoh* signifies “while the two of Them are making the cows enter (*vesayatoh* = *pravesayatoh),* by means of staying behind—or: forest after forest *(anu = pascat sthitva, vanat vanantaram va)*—in a specific way,” that is, in the manner of a special entrance *(vi = visesena = visesena pravesena*), with sweet words that are a signal, a holler, and so forth.

Although there is no use here, in the context of a description of the song of Krsna’s flute, of the elder brother, the statement is made with the intent to express Krsna’s distinct resplendence in his company. Or the mention of both of Them in a general way is for the sake of the girls’ covering, with their innate bashfulness, their feelings for Sri Krsna.

In like manner, later on too, only one face is mentioned, although both of Them are two, because here the singular automatically denotes a pair, since They are an eternal duo, and also because often the usage of the singular for a body part is in consideration of the category *(jati).* This has already been elaborated upon, in regard to: *prapibatoh sma mukham* (10.8.23).

Another rendering is as follows: “Of the two sons of the chief of Vraja *(vrajesa-sutayoh = vrajesa-sutayoh madhye)* the face which is served by the flute (*anuvenu-justam = venu-justam),* which is continuously drunk *(nipitam* = *nitaram pitam),* etc.” It’s well known that only Sri Krsna’s face is served by the flute. In reference to *nitaram pitam,* it’s implied that the face is the form of the moon, which exudes nectar. *Vai* means *prasiddham* (it is well-known). Sometimes the reading is *va.* The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami.

There is another interpretation: “The face is continuously served by a flute” *(anu venu-justam = nirantaram venuna sevitam).* Here the word is *anujustam.* It is like: *pari ye calanti* (which denotes: *ye paricalanti,* ‘they move around’), by the usage in the Vedas: *vyavahitas ca,* “\[In the Vedas, prefixes are\] also separated \[from the verbal root\]” *(Astadhyayi* 1.4.82). Or: “The face is served by a conformable flute” (*anuvenu-justam = anurupena venuna justam).* Or the word *vai* has the sense of *ukta-sammuccaya* (combining something stated), just like: *maninam anutapam vai (Bhagavatam* 10.20.12).

Alternatively: “The face is properly and deferentially seen by those persons (*yair nipitam* = *yaih sadaram samyak drstam)* and is served, seen with love, in such a way that there is a release of affectionate sidelong glances” (*anurakta-kataksa-moksam* = *snigdha-kataksa-moksam yatha syat tatha justam ca) (justam = sevitam).* Here *anuvenu-justam* is separated as *anu-venu justam.*

Or, *anurakta-kataksa-moksam* means: *anurakta-jananam yusmakam kataksa-moksah yasmin tat* (the face, toward which there is a release of sidelong glances of us loving persons). Or: *anuraktah kataksa-moksah yasya tat* (the face has a lovely realease of sidelong glances).

“We know that this, the continuous ‘drinking’, of those persons, who have senses (*aksanvatam = tesam aksanvatam* = *tesam indriyavatam),* is the prize, that is, the success of all the senses. We do not know of any other.” The success as if of all the senses is brought about by the accomplishment of the success of the actions of all the senses, inasmuch as by continuously drinking that, i.e. by the success of the eyes, meeting face to face too is the form of the topmost prize.

Optionally: “We do not know that this is the topmost—or the only *(param* = *paramam kevalam vd)*—prize.” What is that? *justam* (served): the face is seen with love. Is there another prize? In that regard they say: *yair nipitam,* which portends: *yair adhardmrta-pana- rupam phalam* (a prize that is the form of those persons’ drinking the nectar of the lips). The sense is: “We know that this is the topmost prize,” by the accomplishment of success by the organ of taste’s drinking the face—the sense of taste is the primary sense organ, by the logical reasoning in: *jitam sarvam jite rase,* “all \[the senses\] are conquered when taste is conquered” *(Bhagavatam* 11.8.21)— and specifically by the nice accomplishment, automatically, of the success of all the senses by the excellence of drinking the nectar of His lips, which is worthy of worship among all the multitude of prizes.

Or: “This, the face that is served and imbibed, is the prize for the eyes (*aksanvatam phalam = caksusmatam phalam = caksuh- phalam).”* The word *vai* has the sense of *tu* (only, specifically): *yaih tu janaih rasanendriyaih va nipitam, tesam phalam kim vaktavyam iti sesah,* “Can the prize of those persons, or the prize of the tongues, that taste the face be described at all?” This is to be added, due to the girls’ inability to speak clearly on account of having a choked voice because of tears by remembering Him; or it is because such is the nature of the unfathomability of the speech of *prema* of those ladies, whose feet should be worshiped by witty individuals.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions in this paragraph are underlined.) In reference to: *sri-gopya ucuh,* Sridhara Svami’s disapproval is perceived, because of being written: *anuvarnanam evaha* (he talks about the continuous description), since that is unsuitable due to being a useless repetition and due to the inappropriateness of the singular. However, that reading is seen everywhere.

*yasam budhyate...* (see above)

Now, in this verse, Suka illustrates the following: Even while describing Him, who was with Rama, by concealing their feelings for Him, they were incapable of doing so due to a special meaning implied by nature.

In that regard, a harmonization of Sridhara Svami's explanation is done. “We know that this is the prize only for those who have eyes. We don’t know another prize, even seeing a dear one.” What is it? The face which is drunk, i.e. experienced by the senses *(nipitam = anubhutam),* and relished *(justam = asvaditam).* In his alternative interpretation, the sense is: *yair nipitam tayor vaktram tair yaj justam tad idam eva tesam aksnoh phalam,* “The face of one of Those two which is drunk by and served by people is the prize of those people’s eyes” (*aksanvatam* = *aksnoh).* The drift is: How can others understand?

Moreover, the mention at first only as a state of being ‘*idam*’ (this), by not making a mention in a specific way, is due to the inappropriateness of immediately bringing to light what it is, since it is most confidential. Or the reason is that they were unable to point out a detail of it at once on account of helplessness due to an upsurge of profuse love for Him.

(The rest is the same. In addition:) The two chiefs of Vraja are Sri Nanda and Sri Vasudeva, since Vasudeva as well has many cows, in accordance with what is said in *Sri Hari-vamsa...* (see above). That said. Vrajesa is only Gopa-raja Sri Nanda. They are two sons of His. The usage of even Sri Baladeva’s being his son has already been seen, from Sri Vasudeva’s statement: *tatam bhavantam manvanah,* “My son is thinking that you are his father” (10.5.27). As a result, in regard to his return to Vraja it will be said: *rama ’bhivadya pitarau asirbhir abhinanditah,* “After saluting his two parents. Rama was greeted with blessings” (10.65.2).

Now. “*smarantyah krsna-cestitam''* (while remembering Krsna’s style, 10.21.4) is illustrated. The meaning is hinted at by nature. For example: “Of the two sons of the chief of Vraja (*vrajesa-sutayoh = vrajesa-sutayoh madhye)* the face which is served by a flute from behind *(anu venu-justam = pascat venu-justam),* which is continuously drunk *(nipitam = nitaram pitam),* etc.”

(The rest is the same. Moreover:) Or, *anurakta-kataksa-moksam* means: *anurakta-janesu kataksa-moksah yasya tat* (the face has a release of sidelong glances toward lovers). Thus there is a cause for the excellence of a distinct joy in serving (looking at His face with love).

The secret intention is as follows: “We do not know that this is the only *(param* = *kevalam)* prize.” What is that? *justam,* i.e. it is seen with love. Is there another prize? In that regard they say: *yair nipitam,* which connotes: *yair adharamrta-pana-dvara nipitam, tesam yan-nipana-rupam phalam idam eva,* “The prize of those by whom His face is continuously drunk by means of drinking the nectar of His lips is exactly that, the very fact of continuously drinking it.”17Or: “This, the face that is served...” (The rest of the commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*venu-nada-sudha-vrstya niskramayyokti-madhurim \|*  
*yasam nah payayamasa krsnas ta eva no gatih \|\|*

**“By inducing, with the nectar rain of the sound of His flute, the sweetness of their utterances to come out, Krsna makes us drink. Those girls are our goal.”**

*“Sakhis!* You, abiding here in your homes, which are shackles, are not giving your eyes and other senses bestowed by the Creator a chance to become successful, so today you should quickly go from here to the forest, make the real sweet thing come in the range of your senses and let your lives be a success.” This is the substance of the verse uttered by the *gopis.*

*Aksanvatam* is poetic license. The proper form is *aksimatam.* “Only this is the prize of the eyes of those who have eyes (*aksimatam* = *aksimatam aksnam);* we do not know *(na vidamah = na vidmah)* another.” “In the opinion of outsiders, there might be some other prize to be had, but we don’t think so.”

What is the prize? *vrajesa-sutayor vaktram,* “the faces of Rama and Krsna, the two sons of Vrajesa.” The faces are served by an agreeable flute (*anuvenu-justam = anukula-venu-sevitam). Yair nipitam* (drunk by which persons) is a surface meaning, only in the sense of concealing their own feelings by letting others perceive their intention: “If the mothers-in-law, the sisters-in-law and the neighbors hear what we say, why worry about it? Let them hear us. As all the residents of Vraja, whether male or female, describe the sweetness of Rama and Krsna’s faces, we too shall do so.” This is implied: “Their faces give bliss to everyone except to us who are very far away.”

The notion that Baladeva too is the son of Vrajesa is well-known in Vraja, from Vasudeva’s statement to Nanda: *tatam bhavantam manvanah...* (see above).

The intended meaning is as follows: “the face, served by the flute *(venu-justam),* of one of the two sons of Vrajesa who remains behind *(anu = pascat) (vrajesa-sutayoh pascat = vrajesa-sutayoh madhye pascad vartinah yasya).”*

Regarding *yair va,* because of the word *va* (or) this is meant: *yair drstam sprstam srutam aghratam yair va nitaram atisayena pitam,* “the face, which is seen, touched, heard, and smelled by those persons who have eyes, if not continuously, i.e. intensely (*ni = nitaram* = *atisayena),* imbibed by them.”

In the reading *vai,* the sense is: “Surely (*vai = niscitam eva),* success is the lot of the eyes and of other senses of persons who have eyes and by whom, upon giving up shyness and seriousness, Their faces are continuously drunk.” The drift is: “Therefore today let us offer our respectful farewell to etiquette, fear, bashfulness, and gravity!”

Some *gopis* might reply: “We are well-behaved, and so seeing Them and hearing the flute song are no big problem for us, but we are too shy to drink Their faces. How might we muster the courage to do so?” They respond: Each of Their faces is *anurakta-kataksa- moksam,* “that by means of which is a release of sidelong glances toward big-hearted folks” (= *anuraktesu janesu kataksasya moksah yena tat).* The idea is: “Once you make eye contact, an arrow of a sidelong glance will be released from His face, and so you will be excited by that impact, lose your bashfulness, gravity and the rest, and drink His beauty.”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

*Aksanvatam* has the sense of *caksusmatam* (of those who have eyes)—the usage pertains to the Vedas—the sense is: *aksimatam.* Although Rama is renowned as Rohini’s son, He is Sri Nanda’s son by the figurative superimposition of a sameness of affection.

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

By the rule: *chandasy api drsyate,* “It is seen even in the Vedas \[that the affix *an* replaces the *i* of *aksi* regardless of the suffix\]” (*Astadhyayi* 7.1.76), the affix *an\[an\]* is applied after *aksi* even without a case ending that starts with a vowel from the third case ending onward.18Then *n\[ut\]* is applied after *aksan,* by the rule: *ano nut,* “\[In the Vedas,\] the affix *n\[ut\]* is applied after a word ending in *an* \[when that word is followed by *mat\[up*/\]” (*Astadhyayi* 8.2.16; *Siddhanta-kaumudi* 3601).19Moreover, the nondeletion of *\[s\]a\[p\],* in *vidamah,* is poetic license.

### 10.21.8

*cuta-pravala-barha-stabakotpalabja-*  
*malanuprkta-paridhana-vicitra-vesau\|*  
*madhye virejatur alam pasu-pala-gosthyam*  
*range yatha nata-varau kvaca gayamanau \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*  
*(with one irregularity)*

**Пословный перевод:**

*cuta-pravala*—mango shoots; *barha*—peacock feathers; *stabaka*— clusters of flowers; *utpala*—water lilies; *abja*—lotuses; *mala*— with garlands; *anuprkta*—congenially in contact; *paridhana*— with garments; *vicitra-vesau*—They whose apparel is variegated (either diverse or colorful) (or amazing); *madhye*—in the middle *virejatuh*—the two of Them were resplendent in a special way; *alam*—exceedingly; *pasu-pala*—of tenders of animals; *gosthyam*—in an assembly; *range*—on a stage; *yatha*—like; *nata-varau*—two best dancers (or actors); *kvaca*—sometimes; *gayamanau*—while singing.

*(rama-krsnau) cuta-pravala-barha-stabakotpalabja-malanuprkta-paridhana-vicitra-vesau kvaca pasu-pala-gosthyam madhye gayamanau, nata-varau yatha range (gayamanau atyartham virajete), alam virejatuh.*

**Перевод:**

**“The two of Them have an amazing attire consisting of mango buds, peacock tail feathers, clusters of flowers, lilies, and garments that are congenially in contact with lotus garlands. While occasionally singing in an assembly of cow herders, in the middle, They are exceedingly resplendent like two foremost dancers on a stage.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Other ladies speak. “The two of Them, whose attire is amazing with two garments, blue and yellow, that are gently touched in various spots by colorful garlands of mango shoots and so forth” (*cuta-pravala-barha-stabakotpalabja-malanuprkta- paridhana-vicitra-vesau = cuta-pravaladinam citrabhir malabhir anuprkte isad antarantaratah samyukte paridhane nila-pitambare tabhyam vicitro veso yayos tau). Kvaca* means *kadacit* (sometimes). “Within the assembly of cowherds *(pasu-pala-gosthyam madhye* = *gopala-sabhayam madhye),* both of Them were exceedingly (*alam - atyartham)* resplendent.” The drift is: How amazing is the cowherds’ *punya!*

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

They had new mango buds (*cuta-pravala = cutasya nava-pallava)* and clusters of flowers *(stabaka = puspa- guccha).* They were in a circle of cow herders (*pasu-pala-gosthyam = pasu-palanam mandalyam),* and moreover They were in the middle *(madhye).* Therefore They were resplendent, either in a special manner, i.e. by the display of the beauty of each of those, or in various ways *(virejatuh = visesena vividham va rejatuh) (rejatuh = susubhate),* like two best dancers are resplendent on a stage *(range yatha nata-varau = yatha nata-varau range virajete).* By this example, Their dances, etc., and Their being dedicated to having pleasure at will are implied, otherwise there is no excellence of the resplendence of dancing and so on.

*Kva ca* means *kadacit* (sometimes), due to not always staying in the middle, owing to an absorption in play. *Alam* (exceedingly) is because “sometimes, near both parents, or even near us, there is no excellence of such swagger when They neither sing nor dance like that, due to inhibition in that situation.” The rest was elucidated by Sridhara Svami.

Alternatively: By not conceiving of each verse in terms of a different female speaker, the harmonization of verses is done in terms of varieties of groups. Of those, a statement of one group is made with the first six verses, otherwise, by the occurrence of the glory of goddesses, which are talked about in the sixth verse (10.21.12), what is meant does not come through in comparison to cows described in the seventh.
