Or, by not conceiving in terms of a variety of groups, the verses as a whole are one statement of all the girls. For instance, the intented meaning in the previous stanza was: “Therefore, the success of the eyes of all those cowherds occurred at that time because of seeing Their faces.” And in this verse the girls say: “ It’s not just that those cowherds see Them; in the forest they sing and dance at will in the inner circle of Those two, who have a variegated sylvan attire.”

*Gayamanau* signifies *venuna eva gayantau* (both of Them, while singing only with a flute); or *gayamanau* means: *gayena ganena manah puja yayoh tau,* “the two of Them, revering whom is done by singing,” insofar as the songs are special: nothing compares to them. Optionally the syntactical connection of *kvacit* (*kvaca*) is done right here because They did not always sing, due to the fatigue of dancing and so on.

Another explanation \[of *kvaca gaya-manau\]* is: *kadacid gaye gane manah garvah yayoh tau,* “They have pride (*mana = garva)* in singing.” The pride is of this sort: “Who among you is a singer equal to Us? Let him come here and sing!” and so forth. This too is the sweetness of mirth. Therefore, “Only the *gopas* are fortunate, but we are continually unfortunate, because we cannot get a feel for Their mojo. We cannot get rid of our shyness, due to being afraid of what common people might say.” This, the rest of the statement, is to be inferred later on too. The reason for that has already been explained.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

After pondering whether they should reveal their inner feeling by implied meanings, they conceal it in the second verse (the current one) by being very careful once more. But in the third, due to a vehement outburst of Cupid again, they are unable to conceal their love. In the fourth and so on they are somewhat able to do so. That is what he says in five verses.

They had new mango buds (*cuta-pravala* = *cutasya nava-pallava)* and clusters of flowers *(stabaka = puspa-guccha).* In that regard, new mango buds, a peacock’s tail feather, and a cluster of flowers were on the top of the head. A water lily, i.e. the inner flower cup of it, was on both ears. A lotus, i.e. a play lotus, was in the right hand. They had an amazing apparel because of these and because of many garments coming in contact with a garland.

(Additions are underlined.) They were in a circle of cow herders *(pasu-pala-gosthyam = pasu-palanam mandalyam),* and moreover They were in the middle (*madhye*). Therefore They were resplendent, either in a special manner, i.e. by the display of the beauty of each of those, or in various ways (*virejatuh = visesena vividham va rejatuh) (rejatuh* = *susubhate*), like two best dancers are resplendent on a stage (*range yatha nata-varau* = *yatha nata- varau range virajete).* By this example, Their dances, etc., and Their being dedicated to having pleasure at will are implied, and so is the cowherds’ cleverness in regard to that attire and their being dedicated to playing musical instruments, and so on. otherwise there is no excellence of the resplendence of dancing and so on.

*Kva ca* means *kadacit* (sometimes), due to not always staying in the middle, owing to an absorption in play. *Alam* (exceedingly) is because “sometimes, only within the village, there is no excellence of having such swagger when They neither sing nor dance like that, due to inhibition in that situation.” The rest was elucidated by Sridhara Svami.

Alternatively: Here, in a set of five verses, a mutual connection of all the verses is to be done from the perspective of being a statement of all those ladies. For instance, the intention in the previous stanza was: “Therefore, the success of the eyes of all those cowherds occurred at that time because of seeing Their faces.” And in this verse the girls say: “ It’s not just that those cowherds see Them; in the forest they sing and dance at will in the inner circle of Those two, who have a variegated sylvan attire.”

*Gayamanau* should read *gayantau* (while singing); or *gayamanau* means: *gayena ganena manah puja yayoh tau,* “the two of Them, revering whom is done by singing,” insofar as the songs are special: nothing compares to them. Optionally the syntactical connection of *kvacit (kvaca)* is done right here, because. Optionally the syntactical connection of *kva ca* is done right here because They did not always sing, due of an engrossment in dancing and so on.

Another explanation \[of *kvaca gaya-manau\]* is: *kadacid gaye gane manah garvah yayoh tau,* “They have pride (*maria = garva)* in singing.” The pride is of this sort: “Who among you is a singer equal to Us? Let him come here and sing!” and so forth. This too is the sweetness of mirth. Therefore, “Only the *gopas* are fortunate, but we are continually unfortunate, because in that way Their spontaneous demeanor is not brought about in our presence due to fearing the common people here.” This, the rest of the statement, is to be inferred later on too. The reason for that has already been explained.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In case one *gopi* were to say, “How would we cope with mockery toward us? Therefore we shall not go there,” another one says, “No. That will not happen because we don’t have a desire to go there when He is with Baladeva, and so we will go there and quickly return after seeing, between the leaves, the nectar of His beauty, the nectar of His singing, and the way He takes pleasure.” This is what is meant here.

“The two of Them have an amazing attire with garments— which are red, yellow, and dark blue, as is suitable for dancers— which congenially adhere to the body, and with new mango buds, a peacock’s tail feather, and a bunch of flowers on the top of the head; two water lilies, one for each ear; a play lotus in the right hand, and garlands on the neck.”

Regarding *nata-varau* (the best dancers): When the *sakhas* were the singers and the musicians, sometimes They danced and sometimes They sang (*gayamanau*): The suffix *\[s\]ana\[c\]* has the sense of *tacchilya* (habit).21Or *gaya-manau* signifies: *gaye gane mano garvo yayoh,* “the two of Them have pride in singing,” in this manner: “No singer in the three worlds is equal to Us. Who are you lowly cowherds!”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

They were resplendent in an assembly of cowherds, whose qualities are equal to Theirs, and moreover They were in middle. *Gayamanau* stands for *gayantau.* Or *gaya-manau* means: *gaye gane manah sarvaih dattah satkarah yayoh tau,* “the two of Them, unto whom respect in the matter of singing is given by all.” “They were exceedingly resplendent,” even more so than Their being resplendent in the village inasmuch as there was no such singing or dancing, owing to shyness.

### 10.21.9

*gopyah kim acarad ayam kusalam sma venur*  
*damodaradhara-sudham api gopikanam \|*  
*bhunkte svayam yad avasista-rasam hradinyo*  
*hrsyat-tvaco ’sru mumucus taravo yatharyah \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

*gopyah*—O *gopis; kim*—what; *acarat*—performed; *ayam*—this; *kusalam*—good deed; *sma*—(a verse filler); *venuh*—\[this\] flute; *damodara-adhara-sudham*—the nectar of Damodara’s lips; *api*— although; *gopikanam*—in relation to the *gopis* (it belongs to the *gopis); bhunkte*—enjoys; *svayam*—by itself (independently); *yat*— because (or by which \[flute\]); *avasista-rasam*—in such a way that juice remains (or no juice remains); *hradinyah*—the rivers (“they have lakes / pools”); *hrsyat-tvacah*—they whose skin is bristling; *asru*—tear (tears); *mumucuh*—shed; *taravah*—trees; *yatha*—like; *aryah*—venerable ones.

*gopyah! ayam venuh kim kusalam acarat, yat (yat = yasmat) gopikanam api (asmakam) damodaradhara-sudham svayam avasista-rasam (yatha syat tatha) bhunkte? yatha aryah (sva-vamse bhagavat-sevakam labdha-tat-prasadam drstva hrsyat-tvacah (santah) asru muncanti, tatha) hradinyah hrsyat-tvacah (babhuvuh), taravah (ca) asru mumucuh.*

*\[kimva: gopyah! ayam venuh kim kusalam acarat? (sah venuh) gopikanam api (asmakam) damodaradhara-sudham svayam bhuhkte. yatha aryah (bhaktah hrsyat-tvacah satyah asru muncanti, tatha) hradinyah yad-avasista-rasam (bhunjate atah) hrsyat-tvacah (bhavanti, sah venuh yesam vamse jatah, te) taravah (api) yad-avasista-rasam (bhunjate atah) asru mumucuh.}*

*{athava: gopyah! ayam venuh kim kusalam acarat, yat (yat = yasmat) (sah venuh) damodaradhara-sudham gopikanam (asmakam) avasista-rasam api svayam bhunkte? yatha aryah (bhuvah) hrsyat- tvacah (bhavanti) asru mumucuh (ca, tatha) hradinyah taravah (ca bhavanti).}*

**Перевод:**

**“Hey** ***gopis!*** **What meritorious act did this flute perform, because it enjoys by itself the nectar of Damodara’s lips, although that nectar belongs to us** ***gopikas,*** **in such a way that no juice is left? Rivers have hairs on end and trees shed tears like venerable parents do.**

**Alternatively: “Hey** ***gopis,*** **what meritorious act did this flute do, because it enjoys by itself the nectar of Damodara’s lips, although that nectar belongs to us** ***gopikas*****? The rivers enjoy the remainder of the flute’s relishment (they listen to Krsna’s flute song) and experience horripilation in the form of lotuses in bloom. The trees shed a tear like venerable elders do.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Other girls speak. “Hey *gopis!* This flute did what meritorious act *(kim sma kusalam* = *kim sma puny am*)?— why do you ask?—because *(yat = yasmat)* it enjoys independently, by its own will *(svayam = svatantryena = yathestam),* the nectar of Damodara’s lips though that nectar should be enjoyed only by the *gopis (api gopikanam = gopikanam eva bhogyam satim api).”*

How does it enjoy it? *avasista-rasam,* “in such a way that the full *rasa* remains” (= *avasista-rasam kevalam avasistam rasa-matram yatha bhavati tatha),* because: “The rivers, by whose water the flute was nourished and which are similar to mothers, seems to have goose bumps, by the tricky appearance of groves of blooming lotuses *(hrsyat-tvacah = vikasita-kamala-vana-misena romancitah laksyante);* the trees, in whose lineage *(vamsa)* the flute was born, are shedding a tear, by the tricky appearance of a flow of sap, much like family elders *(aryah = kula-vrddhah)* horripilate upon seeing a servant of the Lord in their own lineage and shed a tear.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

In this verse they say: “How amazing! What can be said about the good fortune of the cowherds who associate with Him!” “What meritorious act did this flute—made of juiceless wood—do (*kim kusalam acarat = katamat punyam krtavan*),” either in this life or in the past? “Once we know what that meritorious deed is, we’ll do the same.”

*Sma* has the sense of *vismaya* (astonishment). With *damodara* and so on they hint at that. With the name “Damodara,” they make one perceive that He is under the control of their group leader, owing to a special love inasmuch as Radha-Damodara are a couple. For this reason the nectar is to be enjoyed by the *gopikas.* By the mention of the masculine gender, in *ayam* (“this” flute), its ineligibility for that enjoyment is stated, nonetheless: *bhuhkte* (it enjoys), meaning the flute always drinks the nectar of His lips as its only enjoyment, insofar as no one sees it enjoying anything else.

Someone might wonder: “Isn’t it that even after it enjoys Damodara’s lips, those lips are seen as juicy, not dry (so perhaps the flute did not enjoy the lips at all). ” They respond with *yad avasista-rasam.* The sense is: Right after enjoying that nectar, the flute left only a trickle, some remainder.

The substance of the vocative *gopyah* is: “Because of that, there is good fortune only by a birth as a flute, not by a birth as a *gopi,* so why did you become *gopis*?” Further, saying *gopikanam* when it should be said *asmakam* (belongs “to us”) is because in that way they strengthen the idea that the nectar of His lips only belongs to them due to being *gopis;* because of their particular conceit; and because of the special *rasa* of cleverness. As a pun on the verbal root *gup,* with the same intention *gopikanam* means *dehadi-raksikanam* (us who are protecting our bodies, trying to stay alive). The rest was elucidated by Sridhara Svami.

There is another rendering. “Fine, let it forever abide in His hand, in His heart, and in His face, but it enjoys by itself, without our consent, the nectar of the lips of Damodara, who is only under the control of, or else the master of, the *gopikas.” Ava* has the sense *of hina* (lesser, wanting), like *avarata,* and so on. *Yad-avasista-rasam* signifies: *ava hinam sistam yasya rasasya tatha-bhutam yatha syat,* “\[It enjoys the nectar\] in such a way that the remainder of its *rasa* is wanting.” This means the flute does not leave any *rasa* at all.

Or: *avasistah rasah ragah yatha syat,* “in such a way that pleasure remains.” Since the flute always enjoys in that way, it never stops.

Or *yad-avasista-rasam* is a modifier of the nectar (*sudham*): “The flute also enjoys the nectar that is the leftover *rasa* meant for the *gopis."* Indeed, there is *rasa* in that. The nectar is *rasa* in the sense that it is a special sweet thing to be relished (*rasaniya*).

Or, the *gopis* talk about yet another characteristic of doing a meritorious deed *(kusalam):* Even the rivers *(hradinyah = nadyah*), such as Sri Yamuna, enjoy the leftover essence of that deed *(yad- avasista-rasam* = *yasya avasistam ucchistam eva tathapi rasah drava- matram),* but not the nectar. By the removal of the lipstick due to water games and so on, the rivers and others drink the nectar of the lips. This is well known by means of inference in poetry, for example:

*nihsesa-cyuta-candanam stana-tatam nirmrsta-rago ’dharo*  
*netre duram ananjane pulakita tanvi taveyam tanuh \|*  
*mithya-vadini duti bandhava-janasyajnata-pidagame*  
*vapim snatum ito gatasi na punas tasyadhamasyantikam \|\|*

**“\[A group leader speaks:\] The sandalwood paste has completely fallen from the slopes of your breasts. Your lipstick has washed away. Your two eyes have been without eyeliner for a long time. This thin body of yours is full of goose bumps. Messenger! You habitual liar, unaware of your friend’s upsurge of pain! You went from here to bathe in a pond; you didn’t go to meet that rake again!”** ***(Kavya-prakasa*** **1.2)** ***(Sahitya-darpana*** **2.16)22**

The sign of the rivers’ enjoyment of it is *hrsyat-tvacah* (they have horripilation, lit., “they whose skin is bristling”). The trees too, which are like sages abiding on those riverbanks, enjoy it by drinking the water of the rivers with their roots. The token of that is: *asru mumucuh,* “They shed tears.” An example is given: “like the greats *(aryah = mahantah)* quiver due to rapture by experiencing *bhakti- rasa* and shed tears.”

There is another interpretation: The rivers had horripilation, by getting what is most hard to get. The drift is: How can the glory of its *punya* be described? The trees, however, shed tears. This means they cried out of sorrow by not obtaining that either. How were they? *aryah,* which means: *chayadina jagad-upakaran mahanto ’pi,* “they are greats too because of benefiting the world with shade and so on.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In this verse they say: “This is even more amazing! What can be said about the good fortune of the cowherds, let alone the good fortune of the flute!” In this verse, conceiving a false theory due to being madly in love *(unmada),* a madness breaking forth because of *maha-bhava,* they talk about an inner longing involving jealousy.

(Additions are underlined.) “What meritorious act did this flute—made of juiceless wood—do *(kim kusalam acarat = katamat punyam krtavan),”* either in this life or in the past? “Once we know what that meritorious deed is, we’ll do the same.”

*Sma* has the sense of *vismaya* (astonishment). They hint at it: “because” *(yat = yasmat)... damodara* and so on. With the word *damodara.* they imply that Krsna and themselves have a special natural relationship, given that the girls’ emotions now are the sprouts of the feelings they had for Him starting from childhood. For this reason, “the nectar is to be enjoyed only by us *gopikas*.” By the mention of the masculine gender, in *ayam,* its ineligibility as well for that enjoyment is stated, nonetheless: *bhunkte* (it enjoys), meaning the flute always drinks the nectar of His lips as its only enjoyment, insofar as no one sees it enjoying anything else.

Someone might wonder: “Isn’t it that even after it enjoys Damodara’s lips, those lips are seen as juicy, not dry, so perhaps the flute did not enjoy the lips at all.” They respond: *avasista-rasam.* which means: *avasistah rasah rasa-matram yatra tad yatha syat,* “\[It enjoys it\] in such a way that just a little juice remains.” The sense is: Right after enjoying that nectar, the flute left only a trickle, some remainder.

The substance of the vocative *gopyah* is: “Because of that, there is good fortune only by a birth as a flute, not by a birth as a *gopi,* so why did you take birth as *gopis?”* Further, saying *gopikanam* when it should be said *asmakam* (belongs “to us”) is because the sense of “us” might mean “us residents of the village.” whereas no one but the *gopis* themselves is qualified to taste the nectar of His lips: because of their particular conceit: “The flute is not qualified for this”: and because of the special *rasa* of cleverness. As a pun on the verbal root *gup,* with the same intention *gopikanam* means *dehadi- raksikanam* (us who are protecting our bodies, trying to stay alive).

There is another idea: “The flute is always in your lover’s hand, in His heart, and on His mouth, but it enjoys by itself, without your consent, the nectar of Damodara’s lips.”

There is another explanation. How does the flute enjoy it? *avasista-rasam.* Here *avasista* is the opposite of *vasista.* which means *avasista* in the normal sense (remaining), by the rule: *vasti bhagurir al-lopam avapyor upasargayoh.* “Bhaguri prefers the deletion of the *a* of the prefixes *ava* and *api*” *(Varttika* 2.4.82). The sense is: “\[It enjoys the nectar\] in such a way that *rasa* is not a remainder.” This means the flute does not leave any *rasa* at all. Or: *avasistah rasah ragah yatra tad yatha syat,* “in such a way that pleasure remains.” Since the flute always enjoys in that way, it never stops.

Or *yad-avasista-rasam* is a modifier of the nectar *(sudham):* “The flute also enjoys the nectar that is the leftover *rasa* meant for the *gopis.”*

Or, the *gopis* talk about yet another characteristic of doing a meritorious deed *(kusalam): hradinyo hrsyat-tvacah.* The sense is: Seeing its enjoyment of that sort, even the rivers, who are most virtuous, had horripilation (*hrsyat-tvacah = jata-roma-harsah babhuvuh)* out of greed, by the tricky appearance of lotuses in bloom. Optionally, *yad-avasista-rasam* can be linked right here. The sense is: *yasya venor avasista ucchisto yo raso nada-rupas tam hradinyo ’pi bhunjate asvadayanti, yatas ca hrsyat-tvaco bhavanti,* “Even the rivers relish the *rasa,* the sound, which is the remnant of the flute, and get goose bumps.” In addition, seeing that kind of good fortune of the flute, which took birth in their own species, all immobile species shed tears, by the tricky appearance of sap.

There is an example: *yatharyah.* The gist is: *yatha pitarah sva- kula-sambhavasya tadrsam saubhagyam anubhuya asru muncanti,* “like fathers, realizing the kind of good fortune of one who took birth in their family, shed a tear.”

On the side of jealousy, this idea appears: “All flutes are full of holes, so what at all might be the fault of that one? Therefore let’s hide it somewhere and keep it hidden” (*gopyah = samgopya raksaniyah).*

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“The rivers, purifiers of the world in regard to bathing, drinking, etc., enjoy the *rasa,* the sound, that is the remnant of the flute. How amazing! After looking at them, even the trees shed tears, by the tricky appearance of sap, while horripilating, by the tricky appearance of shoots. What are the trees like? *Yatharyah,* “like sages who are well known to have such qualities” (= *yatha munayas tad-gunais tatha-bhuta api).*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Moreover, while throwing us in an ocean of mockery, this flute is committing an offense.”

“Hey cowherd girls (*gopyah)!* Why did the *murali* perform a meritorious act (*kim kusalam = kimsvit punyam)?"* Although words such as *vamsi* and *murali* are feminine, the word *venu,* whose meaning is that, is masculine, as in the case of the word *dara* (wife). This should be understood.

There is another explanation: *kim mangalam acarat,* “What auspicious act did it perform?” The drift is: “None. The flute is just part of a nonmoving species.” Still, “It enjoys the nectar of Damodara’s lips.” How? *avasista-rasam.* The purport is: “We are unable to tolerate this!” The reason for that is: *gopikanam.* “Specifically in the matter of the nectar of the lips, it belongs to us *gopis,* because we are women in the subcaste of cowherd, since Krsna too is in the subcaste of cowherd, and because, by that logic, He is being sensually enjoyed by us at night all the time. The flute, however, belongs to a different species; further, thinking of its own delight with Krsna, it has the conceit of being Krsna’s beloved; moreover, it sensually enjoys with boldness and, what’s more, after manifesting manhood; besides, it enjoys another’s wealth; in addition, it enjoys only by itself, but it doesn’t allow anyone to be an associate; on top of that, it doesn’t enjoy it by stealing, but only by letting us, the rightful owners of that wealth, know by blowing: rather it is not an instance of blowing, it is a libidinous moan arisen from its carnal enjoyment, and that too only after making us hear it; over and above that, it enjoys in such a way that not even the slightest juice remains (*avasista = na vasista = na avasista)* (*avasista- rasam = na avasisto rasah kincin matro ’pi yatra tad yatha syat tatha).”* The deletion of *a* occurs by the rule: *vasti-bhaguri-val-lopah* and so on. The drift is: “It doesn’t even save a little remainder of what it enjoyed for us, the owners of that wealth. What audacity!”

Additionally, everyone who abides in that place turns out like that. This is what they say, “because of which enjoyment of the nectar of the lips (*yat = yatah = yatah adhara-sudha-bhogat)*— the sense is: after seeing it—the rivers (*hradinyah* = *nadyah)* had horripilation (*hrsyat-tvacah = pulakavatyah babhuvuh)* due to the tricky appearance of open lotuses; the trees shed tears, by the tricky appearance of sap. Just as venerable elders have horripilation and tears by hearing about the Lord’s qualities, so did the rivers, its female friends, upon hearing the libidinous sound of the flute, and the trees, its male friends that are only messengers, respectively.” The idea is: “The flutes, the rivers, and the trees, all of them, are our enemies.” Therefore it, which should be hidden *(gopyah),* is to be secretly kept somewhere so that it does not reach Krsna’s lips. In this way the *sancari-bhava* called *asuya* (envy) is implied.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Other ladies speak. “Hey *gopis*! What auspicious act *(kim kusalam = kim mangalam)* did this flute perform—when that will be known, we will strive to do it—because *(yat = yatah hetoh)* it enjoys the nectar of Damodara’s lips, although the nectar is the wealth of the *gopikas?"* The drift is: “If it were a woman, it could possibly enjoy the nectar of the lips of a husband of other women with great passion. But it’s just a male flute! How can it enjoy that nectar?” There is derision in that, from the intention in using the word *venu.*

Additionally, it enjoys by itself *(svayam = atmana).* The idea is: Even one *gopi* did not obtain a fraction of what it got. That is astonishing. Next they say, “There’s something more all of you should hear: “The rivers, which are very pure, such as Yamuna, enjoy the leftover *rasa.* And after enjoying, they are seen to horripilate, by the tricky appearance of lotuses in bloom. Further, by observing that kind of glory of the flute, the trees, which are mostly part of its lineage, horripilate, by the tricky appearance of outgrowths of shoots, and shed tears, by the tricky appearance of flows of sap—this means they do not count any impropriety on the part of the flute— just as some venerable elders have those emotions upon seeing the glory of someone in their lineage,”” and that implies the following: There is nothing wrong on the part of the trees.

The genitive case in *gopikanam* is the suggestiveness of a *padamsa* (aspect of a word) (*Sahitya-kaumudi* 4.93). Here the genitive case is obtained by the relation of *sva-svami-bhava* (owner and owned), and so it suggests that the nectar of Krsna’s lips only belongs to the *gopis.*

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Simple ones talk with simple ones. Rivers enjoy the *rasa* that is the remnant of the flute’s repast (*yad-avasista- rasam = yad-bhojanavasista-rasam).* How is that understood? By the transformations: *hrsyat-tvacah,* which means: *hrsyat phullat kamaladi-rupah tvacah yasam,* “they whose skin, the form of lotuses, etc., is bristling, i.e. blooming.” Not just rivers, trees too enjoy it, since there is plenty of leftover *rasa.* Even the rivers cannot enjoy it all. How is it understood that the trees enjoy that leftover? “The trees release tears, meaning they cry (*asru mumucuh = krandanti)*— the past tense is used in the sense of the present—like you ladies *(aryah - bhavatyah*) are shedding tears.” Or *aryah* denotes devotees.

Or the drift is: “Consequently this flute should be stolen by cowherds so that it won’t do another thing like that.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

The name ‘Damodara’ is formed by the derivation: *dama udare yasya,* “He on whose abdomen is a rope (or a garland).” The implied idea is the Lord is under the control of the *gopikas. Aryah* means *santah* (transcendentalists, *sadhus).*

**Annotation**

In another context, the *Brahma-samhita* states: *vamsi priya-sakhi,* “The flute is a dear *sakhi."* (5.56). Moreover, the verbal root in *venu* is: *aj gatau ksepane ca* (to go, move; to throw, dispatch), and so the sense is the *venu* is so called because it emits something. The word *venu* is made by the rule: *aji-vr-ribhyo nic ca,* “The affix *nit* is applied after the verbal roots *aj, vr,* and *ri* (respectively)” (*Unadi- sutra* 3.38). The commentaries on *Unadi-sutra* explain that when *nit,* a code name for *nu,* is applied after the verbal root *aj, aj* changes to *vi* by the rule: *ajer vy aghan-apoh,* “ *Vi* is the replacement of *aj* when an *ardha-dhatuka* suffix that is neither *\[gh\]a\[n\]* nor *a\[p\]* follows” *(Astadhyayi* 2.4.56) (*ajer vi ghanam vina rama-dhatuke,* HNV 379). Then vi undergoes *guna.* Thereafter *ve* is combined with *nu* to make *venu.*

### 10.21.10

*vrndavanam sakhi bhuvo vitanoti kirtim*  
*yad devaki-suta-padambuja-labdha-laksmi \|*  
*govinda-venum anu matta-mayura-nrtyam*  
*preksyddri-sanv-avaratanya-samasta-sattvam \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

*vrndavanam*—Vrndavana; *sakhi*—O friend; *bhuvah*—of the Earth (or *sakhi-bhuvah*—of the place of the *sakhis*); *vitanoti*—expands (or expands in a special way); *kirtim*—the fame; *yat*—because (or which \[Vrndavana\]); *devaki-suta*—of Devaki’s son (or two sons); *pada- ambuja*—due to the lotus feet; *labdha-laksmi*—\[Vrndavana,\] whose beauty was obtained; *govinda-venum*—Govinda’s flute; *anu*—after (or in reference to); *matta-mayura*—of excited peacocks; *nrtyam*— the dance; *preksya*—worthy of being seen (or after eminently seeing); *adri-sanu*—on the summits of hills; *avarata*—stopped; *anya*—other; *samasta*—all; *sattvam*—where living entities.

*sakhi! vrndavanam bhuvah kirtim vitanoti yad (yad = yasmat) (vrndavanam) devaki-suta-padambuja-labdha-laksmi govinda- venum anu matta-mayura-nrtyam preksya adri-sanv-avaratanya- samasta-sattvam (bhavati).*

*yad (vrndavanam) devaki-suta-padambuja-labdha-laksmi govinda- venu-manu-matta-mayura-nrtyam preksyadri-sanu aparatanya- samasta-sattvam (bhavati, tad) vrndavanam sakhi-bhuvah kirtim vitanoti.*

**Перевод:**

***“Sakhi,*** **Vrndavana expands the fame of the Earth, since it obtained diverse types of resplendence due to the lotus feet of Devaki’s son. Eminently observing the excited peacocks dancing to the sound of Govinda’s flute, all the other living beings on hilltops become motionless.**

**Alternatively: “Vrnda’s forest, which obtained excellences because of the lotus feet of Devaki’s son, where peacocks, excited by a mantra from Govinda’s flute, are dancing, where the hilltops are worth seeing, and where all other living entities become stunned, expands the glory of the place of the** ***sakhis*** **in specific ways.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Some ladies speak. *“Sakhi,* Vrndavana expands the fame of the Earth,” in terms of being even more special than heaven. How is Vrndavana? *yad devaki-suta-padambuja-labdha- laksmi,* “by which a resplendence, an excellence, was obtained because of the lotus feet of Devaki’s son” (= *yad devaki-sutasya padambujabhyam labdha laksmih sobha sampad yena tat).*

Moreover: “Having observed the dancing of peacocks that were excited—they were thinking that He was actually a gently rumbling rain cloud—upon hearing the sound of Govinda’s flute (*govinda- venum anu = govindasya venu-ninadam srutva anantaram),* all other beings in it, which were on mountain tops here and there in groups, ceased their actions (*adri-sanv-aparatanya-samasta-sattvam = sanghasas tatra tatradri-sanusv aparatany uparata-kriyany anyani samastani sattvani yasmims tat).''* This does not exist in other worlds, so this means it expands the fame of the Earth.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“How astonishing! Can the glory of the flute, which rests on His divine hand and so on, be expressed? Can the good fortune of just Sri Vrndavana be described?” That is what they say here.

“Hey friend Radha (*sakhi = he sri-radhe)!* It expands the fame of the Earth in terms of being even more special than heaven (*vitanoti* = *visesena tanoti = svargadibhyo ’pi visesena vistarayati),* because *(yat = yasmat*): *devaki-suta-padambuja-labdha-laksmi* (Vrndavana obtained splendor because of the lotus feet of Devaki's son), which means: “Vrndavana, by which various types of splendor, in terms of having a lightning flash, an elephant goad and other such nice marks which are completely distinct from anything of the world, was obtained because of the two lotus feet of Devaki’s son.” Or *yad* is a pronoun whose antecedent is *vrndavanam.*

This happened directly, by the lotus feet, not by sandals. By this and by the touch of feet that have natural qualities, such as extreme delicateness and coolness, which are implied by a metaphor with a lotus, the supreme good fortune of the ground of Sri Vrndavana is intimated. It is also implied that the special beauty of His lotus feet is greater than that of Sri Visnu, who has sandals.

Their saying ‘*devaki-suta*’ is in accordance with Garga’s statement that begins: *prag ayam* *vasudevasya* (10.8.14). The word *suta* (son) means He is her son by birth (*prasuta*), whereas He is only Sri Yasoda’s son *(putra*). Alternatively, Devaki is Vrajesvari, from the statement in *Brhad Visnu Purana:*

*dve namni nanda-bharyaya yasoda devakity api \|*  
*atah sakhyam abhut tasya devakya sauri-jayaya \|\|*

**“Yasoda and Devaki are two names of Nanda’s wife, therefore she had a friendship with Sauri’s wife, Devaki.”**

The gist is: “Vrndavana is more fortunate than us.” How amazing! What can be said? It is more fortunate than heaven, and even more so than Sri Vaikuntha-loka.

With *govinda* they talk about a distinctive feature, mentioned with the word *vi* in *vistarayati* (i.e. *vitanoti).* He is the lord of cows *(gavam indrah iti govindah).* He is regarded as Yasoda’s son, as the crest jewel of cowherds, and as the stylish enjoyer *(rasika)* of wonderful games. He is surrounded by cows and cow herders and has sylvan ornaments.

“O *sakhi,* by the rulership of Vrndavana that was bestowed to You by Sri Krsna, luck is on Your side.” This should be understood as a consolation done by Sri Radha’s *sakhis,* such as Lalita, to Her, who had sorrow because of the good fortune, said by them in the previous verse, of the flute.

The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami. In his commentary, “the peacocks were thinking He was a gently rumbling rain cloud” is the reason for the peacocks’ excitement and dancing, otherwise they too would have become motionless like the others. In conformity with the verse that begins: *mallanam asanih,* “\[In the arena in Mathura, Krsna was\] a thunderbolt to the wrestlers” (10.43.17), the Lord, though one, appears to those ones in various ways. In this way, it’s inferred that to the cuckoos He seemed to be the personification of spring, and so forth.

Alternatively: *govinda-venum anu,* i.e. *govindasya venum anu,* which means *tan-nada-sravananantaram* (after hearing the sound of Govinda’s flute), is to be carried forward from the third line to the fourth.

Or the words in the third line are separated as follows: *govinda- venu-manu-matta-mayura-nrtyam,* “\[Vrndavana,\] in which there is a dance by excited peacocks only because of the mantra,24which is most enchanting and which consists of sound, of Govinda’s flute.” (= *govinda-venoh manuh nadatmaka-parama-mohana-mantrah tena eva mattanam mayuranam nrtyam yasmin tat).*

Moreover: *preksyadri-sanu,* “\[Vrndavana,\] where the hilltops are worth seeing specifically because of that” (= *tena eva preksyah adri-sanavah yasmin tat),* meaning they are most delightful because of that reverberation, or they are most worthy of being seen by all due to the obtainment, by the animals roving in the woodland, of proximity to the Lord for the sake of looking and so on. Further: *avaratanya-samasta-sattvam,* “\[Vrndavana,\] where all living entities other than peacocks have become stunned just because of that.” (= *tena eva avaratani stabdhatam praptani anyani mayura-vyatiriktani samastani sattvani praninah yasmin).*

Alternatively, *preksyadri-sanu* means: *preksyah parama- sundarah pritya vraja-janaih sada drsyah va adreh sri-govardhanasya sanuh sikhara-pradesah yasmin,* “\[Vrndavana,\] in which the area of the summit of Sri Govardhana is most beautiful; or it can always be seen by the people of Vraja with affection,” insofar as it was trodden by the Lord, who was eating their multiple offerings while saying: *sailo’smi,* “I am the mountain” (10.24.35), after He sat there as a special pastime during the worship of Sri Govardhana.

Additionally: *avaratanya-samasta-sattvam,* which means: *avarate nivrtte anye rajas-tamasi yasmat tatha-bhuta-samasta- sattvam visuddha-sattva-gunah yasmin tat,* “Vrndavana, in which there is pure *sattva-guna,* because of which the two others, *rajas* and *tamas,* have stopped,” inasmuch as the trees, the creepers, etc., had an eruption of *sattvika bhavas,* since this is going to be said:

*vana-latas tarava atmani visnum*  
*vyanjayantya iva puspa-phaladhyah \|*  
*pranata-bhara-vitapa madhu-dharah*  
*prema-hrsta-tanavo sasrjuh sma \|\|*

**“When Krsna calls the cows with the sound of His flute, the forestial creepers (in the female gender) and the trees (their husbands), richly endowed with flowers and fruits, stoop under the weight; their bodies are thrilled out of love; and they trickle nectarous sap as if to reveal the presence of Visnu (Rasa) in themselves.” (10.35.9)**

Further, by a similarity between what is said in texts such as: *pravartate yatra rajas tamas tayoh sattvam ca misram na ca,* “\[Vaikuntha,\] where there is no *rajas* nor *tamas,* nor *sattva* mixed with both of them” *(Bhagavatam* 2.9.10) and this, the expansion of the fame of the Earth over that of heaven and so forth is proven. Although there is no material *sattva-guna,* due to the mention right after that in the same passage, *na yatra maya kim utapare,* “where there is no Maya” (2.9.10), the mention of the activity of *suddha- sattva* is done with the intent to express the *sattva* that is the form of *sat-cid-ananda-vilasa,* which is beyond the *gunas.* And that has already been expounded upon in many places in *Sri Bhagavatamrta.* It should be inferred in that way.

Alternatively, *preksyadri* signifies: *preksyah adrayah sri- govardhanadyah yasmin tat,* “where the hills, such as Sri Govardhana, are worth seeing,” and *sanv-avaratanya-samasta-sattvam* means: *sanusu avaratani mayuretara-samasta-sattvani yasmin,* “where all living entities other than peacocks have stopped on the peaks.”

There is another rendering: “*matta-mayura-nrtyam preksya*” and “*govinda-venum*” should be linked by inverting them. The sense is: *barhavatamsasya tasya vanagamana-sandarsana-matrena pritya mattanam mayuranam nrtyam tat preksaya harsena govindasya venuh tena tad-vadanam ity arthah, tam anu adri-sanusu avaratani viratani sri-bhagavad-darsanadi-vyatiriktasesa-prayojanani yesam tatha-bhutani samasta-sattvani yasmin,* “\[Vrndavana,\] where all living beings on hilltops have all their purposes which are entirely different from seeing the Lord come to an end after Govinda’s flute—this means, when He plays the flute—, because of joy by seeing the dancing of peacocks excited out of affection merely by fully observing the arrival of Him who has a peacock’s tail feather as an ornament, in the woodland.”

The peacocks too are included by the word *samasta* (all): At first they were dancing due to being excited from the bliss of seeing the Lord, and subsequently, because of the sound of the flute, they experienced a swoon of *prema,* a swoon characterized by the cessation of everything other than hearing His flute and looking at Him, as in the case of other living entities.

This kind of thing does not even exist in Sri Vaikuntha. The distinct fame of Vrndavana over that too is proven. The drift is: “Alas! We are unfortunate. We cannot be like these living beings.” And this is just a characteristic of those ladies’ pain of nonsatisfaction, which is inherent and is a special *prema.* That characteristic is to be inferred everywhere.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) “How astonishing! Can the glory of the flute, which rests on His divine hand and so on, be expressed? Can the good fortune of Vrndavana be described even a little?” That is what they say here.

*“Sakhi,* it expands it in terms of being even more special than Vaikuntha and so on (*vitanoti = visesena tanoti = vaikunthadibhyo ’pi visesena vistarayati*), because (*yat - yasmat*): *devaki-suta- padambuja-labdha-laksmi,* which means: *devaki-sutasya sri-krsnasya padambujabhyam krtva labdhah laksmyah sarva-sobha-mahimnoh sampadah yena tat,* “Vrndavana, by which various types pf splendor were obtained because of the lotus feet of Sri Krsna. Devaki's son.” Or *yad* is a pronoun whose antecedent is *vrndavanam.* On top of that, directly by the lotus feet, but not by sandals. By this, the supreme good fortune of the ground of Sri Vrndavana is intimated.

Their saying ‘*devaki-suta'* is in accordance with Garga’s statement that begins: *prag ayam vasudevasya* (10.8.14). In that manner also, the mention is for the sake of a concealment. In this way, adhering to the opinion of a maker of a dictionary, even the word *govinda.* which is hinted at there: *gavadhyakse ’pi govindah. “Govinda* is also used in the sense of *gavadhyaksa* (superintendent of cows')” *(Amara-kosa* 3.3.91), is due to the renown in Vraja on account of that name only after the *abhiseka* of Sri Govinda.25Only in reference to *nanda-nandanam* in the next verse, it is because of the inability of a concealment. Alternatively, Devaki is Vrajesvari, from the statement in *Brhad Visnu Purana: dve namni* (see above).

With *govinda* they talk about a distinctive feature, mentioned with the word *vi.* He is the lord of cows *(gavam indrah iti govindah).* He is regarded as Yasoda’s son, the crest jewel of cowherds, the stylish enjoyer (*rasika)* of wonderful games. He is surrounded by cows and cow herders and has sylvan ornaments. Therefore the gist is: “We eagerly wish for the good fortune of Vrndavana too.”

The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami. In his commentary, “the peacocks were thinking that He was a gently rumbling rain cloud” is the reason for the peacocks’ excitement and dancing, otherwise they too would have become motionless like the others. Still, their being otherworldly is superior.

Another interpretation is as follows: Owing to the Lord’s grace toward their entire species, due to a connection with the peacocks of Sri Vrndavana, which have an intense inherent affection for Sri Krsna, even the peacocks that abide elsewhere can be understood to have affection for a rain cloud just because of a similarity with them.

In addition to that, *govinda-venum anu,* i.e. *govindasya venum anu,* which means *tan-nada-sravananantaram* (after hearing the sound of Govinda’s flute), is to be carried forward everywhere.

Or the words in the third line are separated as follows: *govinda-venu-manu-matta-mayura-nrtyam.*.. (see above).

Just as the sound of His flute is the cause of the peacocks’ dancing, it is also the cause of the motionlessness of other beings. Although such is the case, the term *preksya* (after seeing) (as a separate word) signifies that others are together in a group only for the sake of observing, that is. fancifully imagining *(utpreksitum).* the style of the dance.

Or *preksyadri-sanv-avaratanya-samasta-sattvam* means: *muhuh sri-bhagavad-asanata-praptya sarvesam paramavalokaniyah adri- sanavah ye, yadva preksam arhanti ye, tesu uccesu tad-darsana- sthanesu avaratani stabdhatam praptani anyani mayura-vyatiriktani samastani sattvani praninah yasmin,* “\[Vrndavana,\] where all living entities that are different from peacocks have become stunned on high hilltops, which are most worthy of a look by all, due to the repeated obtainment of nearness to the Lord.” Or ‘which are fit for dancing’, from the definition in *Visva-prakasa: preksya nrtyeksane vrddhau.26*and which are places for seeing Him.”

There is another rendering: “*matta-mayura-nrtyam preksya"* and “*govinda-venum*” should be linked by inverting them. The sense is: *barhavatamsasya tasya vanagamana-sandarsana-matrena pritya mattanam mayuranam nrtyam tat preksaya harsena govindasya venuh tena tad-vadanam ity arthah, tam anu adri-sanusu avaratani viratani anyani sri-bhagavad-darsanadi-vyatiriktasesa-prayojanani yesam tatha-bhutani samasta-sattvani yasmin,* “\[Vrndavana,\] where all living beings on hilltops have all their purposes which are entirely different from seeing the Lord come to an end after Govinda’s flute—this means, when He plays the flute—, because of joy by seeing the dancing of peacocks excited out of affection merely by fully observing the arrival of Him who has a peacock’s tail feather as an ornament, in the woodland.”

This kind of thing does not even exist in Sri Vaikuntha: The distinct fame of Vrndavana over that too is proven. The drift is: “Alas! We are unfortunate. We cannot be like these living beings.” And this is just a characteristic of those ladies’ pain of nonsatisfaction, which is inherent and is a special *prema.* That characteristic is to be inferred everywhere.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In this stanza, other girls say: “Now, the sweetness of Vrndavana, the abode of that sort of pastimes of His, shines more. Therefore we, desiring to see it, are going there. There’s no fault in this.”

“Vrndavana especially expands the fame of the Earth, meaning it expands it in terms of being even better than heaven and other places (*vitanoti = visesena tanoti = svargadibhyah visesena tanoti*), because (*yad = yatah*): *devaki-suta-padambuja-labdha-laksmi,* Vrndavana obtained a resplendence, an excellence, consisting of the marks of a flag, lightning flash, etc., by means of both lotus feet of Yasoda’s son.” The gist is: Even a forest of Vaikuntha cannot possibly be like this. *Brhad Visnu Purana* states: *dve namni...* (see above).

In case someone thinks, “The village of any cow herders could be like this,” they say: “Observing the dancing of peacocks excited at Govinda’s playing a flute (*govinda-venum anu = govindasya venu- vadyam laksi-krtya),* all other beings in Vrndavana, which were on mountain tops, ceased their actions (*adri-sanv-avaratanya-samasta- sattvam = adri-sanusv avaratany uparata-kriyany anyani samastani sattvani yatra tat)."*

Govinda, playing a flute, was requested by the peacocks: “Make us dance,” and so He played the flute while also dancing among them, which were dancing in a circle, in rhythm. Afterward, gratified by His musical performance, they offered Him their divine tail feathers as a reward. Joyfully taking the feathers, as the customary style of musicians, He wore one or more above the turban on His head. The deer, such as *krsna-sara,* and the birds, such as pigeons, assembled; sitting on hilltops, they relished that triad of song, dance, and music, and became numb out of bliss. The idea is: “We want to see all this.”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

The compound *devaki-suta-padambuja- labdha-laksmi* signifies: *devaki-suta-caranena hetuna ambujaih iva labdha laksmir yena,* “Vrndavana, by which beauty was obtained as if with lotuses because of the foot of Devaki’s son.” *Govinda-venu-manu* means: *govinda-venuh eva manuh dharmopadesta yatra,* “where Govinda’s flute is a teacher of duty.” In Vrndavana is a dance by excited peacocks (*matta-mayura-nrtyam = mattanam mayuranam nrtyam yatra).* Or they are mad for Govinda’s flute (*govinda-venum anu = govinda-venum laksi-krtya).*

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

The compound *devaki-suta-padambuja- labdha-laksmi* means: *devaki-sutasya padambujaih tatra tatra ankitaih labdhah laksmyah sobhah yena tat,* “\[Vrndavana,\] by which many types of resplendence were obtained because of the lotus footprints, impressed here and there, of Devaki's son.” The suffix *ka\[p\]* is not applied because in the plural *laksmi* is not an *ura-adi*,27

### 10.21.11

*dhanyah sma mudha-gatayo ’pi harinya eta*  
*ya nanda-nandanam upatta-vicitra-vesam \|*  
*akarnya venu-ranitam saha-krsna-sarah*  
*pujam dadhur viracitam pranayavalokaih \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

*dhanydh*—fortunate (or worthy of the wealth \[of love\]28); *sma*— (a verse filler); *mudha-gatayah*—their movements are indolent (or their intelligence is dull); *api*—although (or also); *harinyah*— does; *etah*—these; *yah*—which \[does\]; *nanda-nandanam*—Nanda’s son; *upatta-vicitra-vesam*—by whom an amazing attire was taken; *akarnya*—after hearing; *venu-ranitam*—the sound of the flute; *saha- krsna-sarah*—accompanied by the *krsna-sara* deer (“they for whom the best is Krsna” or “they who make one go to Krsna”); *pujam dadhuh*—they did an homage; *viracitam*—performed; *pranaya- avalokaih*—with sidelong looks of love.

*etah harinyah mudha-gatayah api dhanyah (bhavanti) sma, yah (harinyah) venu-ranitam akarnya upatta-vicitra-vesam nanda- nandanam (prati) pranayavalokaih viracitam pujam saha-krsna- sarah dadhuh.*

**Перевод:**

**“Although slow-witted, the does are fortunate. Upon hearing the sound of the flute, they, who were with their mates, the** ***krsna-sara*** **deer, paid homage, performed with sidelong looks of love, to Him, Nanda’s son, who had donned a colorful attire.**

**Alternatively: “The does too become indolent upon hearing the sound of the flute. Accompanied by the** ***krsna-sara*** **bucks, they are worthy of the wealth of love. The does showed courteous regard, with their affectionate side-looks, to Nanda-nandana. He was wearing an amazing attire.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Other ladies speak. *"Sakhi,* these does, though belonging to an animal species (*mudha-matayo ’pi* = *tiryag-jatayo ’pi),* are successful *(dhanyah* = *krtarthah).* Hearing the sound of the flute (*venu-ranitam = venu-nadam),* they did an homage (*pujam dadhuh = sammanam krtavatyah),* performed with side- looks accompanied with love *(pranayavalokaih = pranaya-sahitaih avalokanaih*), to Nanda’s son *(nanda-nandanam = nanda-nandanam prati).* In addition, they did the homage only with their mates, the *krsna-sara* deer *(saha-krsna-sarah = krsna-saraih sva-patibhih sahitah eva)."* The gist is: “However, our husbands, the cowherds, are insignificant: They cannot tolerate that.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Here they exclaim: “The glory of Sri Vrndavana is even more amazing by considering that all the souls it shelters are dear to Hari (and all the souls it shelters love Hari), not to mention the good fortune of the does. Although does are animals, can their good fortune be described?”

*Mudha-gatayah* means: *mudha viveka-hina gatih jnanam yasam tah,* “their awareness lacks good judgement,” inasmuch as they are in an animal species. In the reading *mudha-matayah,* the sense is the same. Saying *etah* (these ones) when it should be said *tah* (those ones) (the usual correlative of *yah)* is with the intent to express their being directly perceptible. *Etah* portends either *sri-vrndavana- vartinyah* (they habitually abide in Vrndavana) or *vana-caryah* (they roam in the woods).

He is the little boy of the divine king of cowherds (*nanda- nandanam = nandasya sri-vallavendrasya kumaram).* This implies that He is a stylish enjoyer who has the most beautiful attire. As a pun, ‘Nanda-nandana’ means: *nandam saksad anandam apy anandayati,* “He makes even bliss itself blissful,” and so *nanda- nandanam* signifies: *paramananda-ghana-murtim* (Him whose form is the highest dense bliss).

*Upatta-vicitra-vesam* denotes: *upattah svikrtah vicitrah vesah yena tam,* “Him, by whom an amazing (or colorful, or diverse) apparel—that is to say: sylvan garlands, decorations such as a peacock’s tail feather as a head adornment, and *gunja* earrings, all of which were offered by *sakhis* as a gift—was taken, i.e. accepted.”

“The does did a worship performed in a special way (*viracitam* *=visesena kalpitam)* only with side-looks of love toward Him,” inasmuch as there was an excellence in worshiping Him, the crest jewel of stylish enjoyers, only with those, since they didn’t have articles of formal worship. The plural in *pranayavalokaih* is used either because of high regard or because of the desire to express a series of such side-looks. *Sma* has the sense of either *vismaya* (astonishment) or in *kheda* (despair). The idea is: “Gosh, we don’t have this kind of good luck.” The rest was elucidated by Sridhara Svami.

There is another rendering. Upon hearing the sound of the flute, they became *mudha-gatayah,* meaning their inner sensory functions and outer sensory functions were confounded (= *mudha gatih bahyantarendriya-vrttih yasam).* These girls who are the most clever and know everything are like that too, on account of the glory of a birth in Vrndavana. Or *mudha-gatayah* means their standing posture was is like that of numb beings. Or their whose movements, characterized by being stunned, or by tottering here and there, were like the movements of numb beings.

“These—meaning our rivals (*etah = asmat-sapatnyah)*— does, although they always wander within a forest, did a worship performed with side-looks of love.” That is, bewildered by lust, they were unable to think properly; this means they glanced with love as if they were solely worshiping with great respect.

The word *api* is connected with the *krsna-sarah.* The significance is: *krsna-sara api saha tatha cakruh,* “The *krsna-sara* deer did so too, at once (*saha = ekada eva).”29* The etymology is: *krsnah eva sarah sresthah paramopadeyah yesam,* “they for whom the best, i.e. the one most selectable, is Krsna.” As an implied meaning, the cowherds are criticized, insofar as they cannot directly, spontaneously, do their own service to Sri Krsna.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) Here they exclaim: “This is even more wonderful! Can the glory of Sri Vrndavana, which shelters all the souls dear to Hari, let alone the good fortune of the animal species, be somewhat described?”

*Mudha-gatayo ’pi* means: *mudha viveka-hina gatih jnanam yasam tatha-bhutah api,* “although they lack good judgement...” Even in the reading *mudha-matayah,* the sense is the same. Concerning *harinyah* (does): Though they habitually roam the forests, these ones (*etah)* are as if being seen.

He is the son of the divine king of cowherds (*nanda-nandanam = nandasya sri-vallavendrasya nandanam).* By the power of the meaning of the verbal root, being the greatest as one who has all virtues is implied.30Mentioning the name of Nanda, though he is an elder, is because it was said: *viksipta-manasah.* “they whose hearts are overwhelmed” (10.21.4), owing to the helplessness of agitation.

*Upatta-vicitra-vesam* denotes: *upattah svikrtah vicitrah vesah yena tam,* “Him, by whom an amazing (or colorful, or diverse) apparel—which is the form of sylvan garlands, a peacock’s tail feather as a head adornment, and *gunja* earrings—was taken, i.e. accepted.”

In point of *venu-riphitam,* it does not culminate as a melody: A mere blowing at first is stated. This is just an imitative sound.31

The etymology of *krsna-sara* is: *krsnah eva sarah paramopadeyah yesam,* “they for whom the best, i.e. the one most selectable, is Krsna.” As a implied meaning, their own husbands are criticized.

The word *pujam* here suggests that the does’ side-looks of love attained the status of *upacara* (objects offered in a formal worship). The idea is the does enhanced *(dadhuh = pupusuh)* the worship. In other words, their worship was better than all formal worships. Consequently there is a specialty modifying the action expressed by the verb: *viracitam* signifies *visesena racitam* (performed in a special way). The reason for everything in that matter is: *pranayavalokaih* (with side-looks of love), from the excellence of worshiping Him, who merely acknowledges the mood in the worshiper, only with those. The plural is because of the desire to express a series of looks. *Sma* is used either in the sense of *vismaya* (astonishment) or in the sense of *kheda* (despair). The idea is: “What a wonder! We don’t have this kind of good fortune.” The rest is by Sridhara Svami.

(This paragraph is new.) Alternatively, *nanda-nandanam* is the object of *akarnya* (hearing) and *venu-riphitam* is a modifier of *nanda- nandanam* as follows: *veno riphitam yatra tadrsam santam akarnya sravana-dvara jhatva upatta-vesam santam pranayavalokair dadhur vasi-krtavatyah tair eva pujam priti-sevam api vidadhuh,* “Knowing by hearing that Nanda-nandana, in regard to whom there was a riff of a flute, was in the area, the does made Him submissive with side- looks of love and also served Him with love with those looks.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The girls speak this verse to illustrate the following: “How amazing! Although we are witty, we, who are not approaching our lover, are making our lives unsuccessful. The does, however, have become successful though they are slow-witted.”

*Sma* has the sense of either *vismaya* (astonishment) or *kheda* (despair).32The drift is: “We don’t have this sort of good luck.” The two readings, *venu-ranitam* and *venu-riphitam,* have a similar meaning. “Only with side-looks involving love *(pranayavalokaih* = *pranaya-purvakavalokaih eva),* the does enhanced (*dadhuh = pupusuh)* a worship to Nanda’s son (*nanda-nandanam = nanda- nandanam prati*).” The substance is: “How much more highly might Nanda-nandana, who thinks that His own worship is enhanced by their side-looks, think of a *puja* enhanced by our side-looks?”

Moreover, the does are only with the mates *(saha-krsna- sarah = patibhih sahitah eva).* The gist is as follows: “The bucks, for whom the best, in terms of being an object of affection, is only Krsna (*krsna-sarah = krsna eva priti-visayatvena saro yesam te),* are suitably named and are the mates of those does. Perceiving that their wives were emotionally attached to Krsna, they, who were thrilled, considering their own state of husbands as blessed, made them, who were following, approach Krsna (*krsna-sarah = tah krsnam abhisarayanti).* However, our husbands are hostile even to the scent of Krsna. Fie on our lives!”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Other *gopis* speak: “Although we are witty, we, who are not approaching the lover due to bashfulness and out of fear of *adharma,* are making our lives unsuccessful. However, the does, who are shameless, are making their lives successful although they are slow-witted *(mudha-matayo ’pi).”*

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Married *gopis* speak this verse and the next.

### 10.21.12

*krsnam niriksya vanitotsava-rupa-silam*  
*srutva ca tat-kvanita-venu-vivikta-gitam \|*  
*devyo vimana-gatayah smara-nunna-sara*  
*bhrasyat-prasuna-kabara mumuhur vinivyah \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

*krsnam niriksya*—observing Krsna; *vanita*—for women; *utsava*— produce a festival; *rupa-silam*—whose beauty and character; *srutva ca*—and hearing; *tat-kvanita*—sounded by Him; *venu*—of the flute; *vivikta*—distinct (clear); *gitam*—the song; *devyah*—the goddesses; *vimana-gatayah*—they whose movements occur by means of aircrafts; *smara*—by Cupid; *nunna*—was driven away; *sarah*— they whose essence (solemnity); *bhrasyat*—are falling; *prasuna- kabarah*—they the flowers from whose braids; *mumuhuh*—they became bewildered; *vinivyah*—they whose girdles have gone.

*devyah vimana-gatayah vanitotsava-rupa-silam krsnam niriksya tat- kvanita-venu-vivikta-gitam ca srutva smara-nunna-sarah mumuhuh. (tah devyah) bhrasyat-prasuna-kabarah vinivyah (ca abhavan).*

**Перевод:**

**“Gazing at Krsna, whose beauty and character bring about a festival for women, and listening to the distinct song of the flute that He played, the goddesses, who were going in aircrafts and whose gravity was shaken off by Cupid, became bewildered. Flowers fell from their braids, and their girdles loosened.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Other ladies speak. “Hey *gopis*! Listen to another wonder. Observing Krsna, whose form and nature create a festival for women (*vanitotsava-rupa-silam = vanitanam utsavah yasmat tad rupam silam ca yasya tam),* and hearing the nondisorderly song of the flute played by Him (*tat-kvanita-venu-vivikta-gitam srutva ca = tena vadita-venoh asankirnam gitam ca srutva),* the goddesses, going by means of aircrafts (*vimana-gatayah = vimanaih gacchantyah),* and whose gravity was thrown off by Cupid (*smara-nunna-sarah* = *smarena pariksipta-dhairyah)*—although they were on the gods’ laps—became bewildered.”

They mention the signs of the bewilderment: “flowers are falling from their topknot” (*bhrasyat-prasuna-kabarah = bhrasyat- prasunah kabaras cuda yasam tah)* and “their girdles have loosened” *(vinivyah = vigatah nivyah yasam tah).*

Because of a variety of speakers in these verses, an excessive harmonization should not be attempted.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

In this verse they say, “How astonishing is the glory of those females that abide in Vrndavana and go in proximity to Sri Krsna owing to a compatibility with cows! Can even the good fortune of the high-flying goddesses be described?”

Krsna is the one who attracts the heart (*krsnam* = *cittakarsakam).* His nature *(sila = svabhava),* such as being dedicated to wonderful amusements, and His body create a festival for clever women, else for any woman (*vanita = vidagdhah, sarvah stri-jatayah va).* Sometimes the reading is *vesam* instead of *silam.* They heard a song of a flute played by Him. The song was *vivikta* (clear), which means either *suddha* (pure), *manojna* (charming), or *srngaradi-rasa- labdha-vibhaga* (a portion obtained from *srngara-rasa,* etc.).

*Vimana-gatayah* connotes their being with their husbands. Thus an arrival all of a sudden, since they were dwelling in an aerial vehicle, and the unsuitability of seeking Sri Krsna’s company are implied. Still, “They, whose seriousness was struck by love (*smara- nunna-sarah = kama-hata-dhairyah satyah),* became bewildered.”

Here, the mention of seeing the form, etc., is because He was unseen by them. Consequently, by seeing Him, and specifically by hearing a song of a flute, that sort of bewilderment is fitting. Or: Bewilderment occurs whenever there is a sensory perception of His form and so on. There is no mention of this elsewhere due to being obvious. Just because of the bewilderment they were unable to alight from the aircraft and go near Sri Krsna.

“Wow! Shame on us, who are not getting even a sight of Him, the enchanter even of beautiful heavenly women. He is such a nectar ocean of all good fortune.” Or the gist is, “Since we are not seeing Him who sports in the woodland in that way there, we are simply unfortunate, but those ladies are fortunate.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In this verse they say, “How astonishing is the glory of these women who abide in Sri Vrndavana and are going in proximity to Sri Krsna. Can the good fortune even of those that go in the sky be described?”

Krsna attracts the heart (*krsnam = cittakarsakam). Vanita* denotes *tad-anuraga-yogyah stri-jatayah* (women qualified for deeply loving Him). *Sila* signifies *susvabhava* (nice nature). They heard a song of a flute sounded by Him. The song was pure (*vivikta* = *suddha*): it wasn’t mixed with an adverse melody, or it was a portion obtained from *srngara-rasa,* etc. *(vivikta = srngaradi-rasa-labdha-vibhaga).*

(This paragraph is the same.) *Vimana-gatayah* connotes their being with their husbands. Thus an arrival all of a sudden, since they were dwelling in an aerial vehicle, and the unsuitability of seeking Sri Krsna’s company are implied. Still, “They, whose seriousness was struck by love (*smara-nunna-sarah = kama-hata-dhairyah satyah*), became bewildered.” Here, the mention of seeing the form, etc., is because He was unseen by them. Consequently, by seeing Him, and specifically by hearing a song of a flute, that sort of bewilderment is fitting. Or: Bewilderment occurs whenever there is a sensory perception of His form and so on.

Having mentioned that both of them: *niriksya srutva ca* (after seeing and hearing), are the causes of the stupefaction, even the contrariness of those two are a fact of life, only when it is obtained in sequence, so the drift is: Just by a bewilderment, they are unable to alight from an aircraft and go near Sri Krsna. This is the *anubhava* called *mottayita* (indication of longing). For instance:

*kanta-smarana-varttadau hrdi tad-bhava-bhavatah \|*  
*prakatyam abhilasasya mottayitam udiryate \|\|*

**“When there is talk, or remembrance, etc., of the lover, the manifestation of an inner longing because of a contemplation, in the heart, focused on love for him is called** ***mottayita*****.” (*****Ujjvala-nilamani*** **11.47)**

(Additions are underlined.) “Wow! Shame on us, who are not getting even a sight of Him. He enchants does, which are most foolish, and even beautiful heavenly women, who are most witty. He is such a nectar ocean of all good fortune.” Or the gist is, “Since we are not seeing Him who sports in the woodland in that way there, we are simply unfortunate, but those ladies are fortunate.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Here they say: “Moreover, the love of us *gopis* for a cowherd, Krsna, is not totally unsuitable because even the goddesses, who have love for a man, a mere cowherd, Krsna, are making their godhood successful. That is mind-boggling.” His form and nature create a festival for all passionate women. The drift is: “The gods, who are extremely smart, do not become hostile to their wives even after knowing about it. Rather, considering their own good fortune, they make them mount an aircraft and drive them to induce them to constantly see Krsna, but our husbands are just hostile. Therefore the lowly does are eminent, the goddesses too are fortunate, but we, humans in between, are unfortunate.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“The goddesses, unchecked by their husbands, deeply love Krsna. If the goddesses, like the does, belong to another category *(jati),* how is it that our love is not as deep as theirs although we and He are in the same classification?” Enthusiasm is intimated in this fashion.

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Here they say, “O *sakhi,* the does and even the goddesses above are fortunate, yet we are not.”

Amara states: *vanita janitatyarthdnuragayam ca yositi,* “ *Vanita* is a woman in general or a woman who has developed intense passion” *(Amara-kosa* 3.3.73). Krsna’s form and nature are like a festival for them *(vanitotsava-rupa-silam = tasam utsava-vat rupa-silam ca yasya).* The flute song was unmixed with another melody *(vivikta = ragantarena amisrita*), or it was separated by intervals *(vivikta = virala*), or it had many subtle hints *(vivikta = sanketa-bahula):* “It is understood only by us, not by others.”

*Vimana-gatayah* implies that they were with their husbands. “They, who have braids, from which flowers fall (*bhrasyat-prasuna- kabarah* = *bhrasyanti prasunani yebhyah tatha-vidhah kabarah yasam),* became bewildered. Nevertheless, their husbands didn’t show indignation. However, even after hearing a song of the flute, which is done because of us, we are not listening to it out of fear of our husbands. Alas!” In this way there is *dainya* (meekness) and *glani* (dejection).

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Vinivyah* means: “they whose garments have loosened, or they the knots of whose garments have loosened” (= *vigatah srastah nivyah vastrani vastra-granthayah va yasam tah).* Yadava states: *nivi vastramsuka-granthayoh,* *“Nivi* means *vastra* (garment, i.e. a skirt, petticoat) and *amsuka-grantha* (the knot of a fine cloth, i.e. on the waist)” (*Yadava-kosa*).

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

The omission of the suffix *ka\[p\],* in *vinivyah,* is poetic license.

### 10.21.13

*gavas ca krsna-mukha-nirgata-venu-gita-*  
*piyusam uttabhita-karna-putaih pibantyah \|*  
*savah snuta-stana-payah-kavalah sma tasthur*  
*govindam atmani drsasru-kalah sprsantyah \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

*gavah*—the cows; *ca*—and; *krsna-mukha*—from Krsna’s mouth; *nirgata*—gone out; *venu-gita-piyusam*—the nectar that is the song of the flute; *uttabhita*—erect (“made to be stiff upward”); *karna- putaih*—with the ears, which were cups; *pibantyah*—while drinking; *savah*—the young (the calves); *snuta*—oozing; *stana*—from the udders; *payah-kavalah*—they who have mouthfuls of milk; *sma*—(a verse filler); *tasthuh*—stood (stood still); *govindam*—Govinda (“the lord of cows”); *atmani*—in their hearts; *drsa*—with the eye (or by seeing); *asru-kalah*—they who have fractions of tears; *sprsantyah*— while feeling.

*gavah ca krsna-mukha-nirgata-venu-gita-piyusam uttabhita-karna-putaih pibantyah govindam drsa atmani sprsantyah asru-kalah (tasthuh. tatha) savah (ca stanya-pane pravrttah tad gita-piyusam uttambhita-karna-putaih pibantah) snuta-stana-payah-kavalah tasthuh.*

**Перевод:**

**“The cows as well stood still. While drinking, with cupped ears, the nectarlike flute song emanating from Krsna’s mouth, they, who had teardrops, were feeling Govinda in their hearts by having a vision. Their young remained morionless, their mouths full of milk from flowing udders.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The cows were drinking with the upraised cups of their ears *(uttabhita = uttambhita= unnamitaih)33...* as if because of fearing a spill. Similarly, the calves too *(savah = savas ca = vatsas ca),* which had begun to suck the udder and were drinking, with the upraised cups of their ears, that same nectar by hearing the song, remained in place. Mouthfuls of milk were just trickling from the udders unto their mouths (*snuta-stana-payah-kavalah = kevalam stanebhyah ksarita-ksira-grasah mukhesu yesam te).* This means they forgot what they were doing. The reason for that is: The cows were feeling, i.e. embracing *(sprsantyah* = *alingantyah),* Govinda in the mind *(atmani = manasi)* through the eye, a path *(drsa = margena).* Therefore both the cows and the calves were *asru-kalah,* “they had fragments of tears in their eyes” (= *asrunam kala lesa locanayoh yasam ta gavas te ca savah).*

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Now, in four verses Suka relates the speech of another *gopi.* Or, they say, “So be it, the goddesses, who are extremely smart, are lucky, but can the good luck of the cows, which are animals, be described?”

*Ca* has the sense of *tu,* to make a distinction from before. Owing to the metaphor with nectar, the face is a moon. By the word *krsna-mukha,* the specialty of the nectar is implied. Krsna is *paramananda-ghana-murti* (the form of dense high bliss). Thus the flute song, which emanated from His moon face, was nectar. *Sma* has the sense of either *vismaya* (astonishment) or *niscaya* (certainty). *Tasthuh* means: *stabdhata-laksanam sattvika-vikaram praptah,* “They got *sattvika* transformations characterized by being stunned.” *Govindam* portends *nija-prabhum* (own master): this makes one aware of their feeling with *priti* (affection; bliss). The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami.

Alternatively: Some calves, the young ones, had mother’s milk oozing from the mouth, and some others, who were grazing grass, had a mouthful of grass.

They were raining tears (*asru-kalah = asruni kalayanti varsayanti iti tatha tah).* The sense is: Due to covering the eyes with a flow of tears, they were seeing only with the mind.34The singular in *atmani,* which means *manasi* (in the mind), is used in the sense of *jati* (category).

“We are unfortunate only because of not touching Him.” The word *ca* (and) in *gavas ca* (the cows too) connotes a nondifference compared to the does and the heavenly ladies: It was said that the does and the goddesses saw His form and heard the flute, and here it is said that the cows had that sort of feeling just by hearing the song of the flute.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Now, in three verses he mentions the speech of another *gopi.* In that regard, at first, a depiction of cows, which have a motherly mood incompatible with their own mood, is for the purpose of concealing emotions as before and, by a nonincompatibility as regards an aspect of the generality of *priti,* for the sake of the appropriateness of what is meant.

*Ca* has the sense of *api: loke sarasara-viveka-hinatvena khyata gavo ’pi,* “Even the cows, known to lack discrimination between what is the essence and what is not.”

Owing to the metaphor with nectar, the face is a moon. By the word *krsna-mukha,* the specialty of the nectar is implied. Indeed, Krsna is said to be *paramananda-ghana-murti* (the form of dense high bliss). *Sma* signifies astonishment. *Tasthuh* means: *stabdhata-laksanam sattvika-vikaram praptah,* “They got *sattvika* transformations characterized by being stunned.” *Govindam* portends *nija-prabhum* (own master): this makes one aware of feeling with *priti.* The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami.

In the reading *snuta-stana-payah,* which he does not approve,35the significance is: *snutam kesancid abhinavanam mukhat ksaritam stana-payah matr-stana-ksiram kesancid tu trna-caranam purita- kanthady-asrunam ata eva sa-dravataya ksaritah kavalah ca trna- grasah yesam te,* “the calves, some of whom, the very young ones, had mother’s milk oozing from the mouth, but some, grazing grass and their throats chocked with tears, had, therefore, a mouthful of grass, a mouthful oozing due to being semiliquid.” *Atmani* means *manasi* (in the mind). *Drsa* means *netrena* (with the eye). *Asru-kalah* means: *asruni kalayanti varsayanti iti tatha tah* (they are raining tears). The sense is: Due to covering the eyes with a flow of tears, they were seeing only with the mind. “We are unfortunate only because of not touching Him.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In this verse they say, “It cannot be said that the bewilderment is the yawn of lust of all women, because all of you should see the bewilderment of the cows too, which have motherly affection.” “They stood only while drinking with the upraised cups of the ears, just because of fearing a spill (*uttabhita-karna-putaih = ksarana-sankaya eva uttabhitaih karna-putaih) (uttabhitaih = unnamitaih).* Nor can it be said that they remained only with *vatsalya-bhava,* nor can it be said that *vatsalya-bhava* is the cause of the bewilderment, because all of you should see the bewilderment of their calves, though they are devoid of *bhava.”* They speak thus, “The calves (*savah = vatsah*), which had begun to suck the udder and were drinking with the upraised cups of the ears that same nectar immediately by hearing the song, remained standing. Each had a mouthful of milk, trickling from the udders, in the mouth, due to the inability to suck the udder, but not in the manner of swallowing it (*snuta-stana-payah-kavalah = stana-panasamarthyat stanebhyah snutanam payasam kavala eva mukhe na tu nigilanam yesam te).”* This means they became stunned by a rise of numbness.

After that, their mothers stood while feeling, i.e. placing, Govinda in their minds (*atmani* = *sva-manasi)*—out of *vatsalya* they placed Him on the lap of their minds—with the eye, i.e. they attracted Him, brought Him, only with the eyes, that is, they made Him enter within as if through the holes of the eyes. In that way they caused tears to flow, out of bliss (*asru-kalah = asruny anandat kalayanti dharayanti iti tah*).36

In this way also, the love of all living entities for Krsna is unconditional. However, “the calves are fortunate because of a close connection, but we are unfortunate because of separation. Only this much is the difference.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Some other *gopis* say: “This *anuraga* is not caused by lust, but by the *svarupa* (inherent nature).”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

The *madhya gopis* speak. “Drinking (*pibantyah = pibantyah pibantah ca)* the nectar emanating from Krsna’s mouth and feeling (*sprsantyah* = *sprsantyah sprsantah ca)* Govinda in themselves (*atmani*) with the eye, the cows and their calves (*gavas ca savah* = *gavah tad-vatsah ca)* became transfixed *(tasthuh = nispandah eva babhuvuh)."*

“However, we are less fortunate than the animals because although we are drinking it we are not forgetting our homes.” Thus they express *dainya* (meekness).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“The cows, though animals, are forgetting their own bodies, but we cannot even forget our homes. Fie on us.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

*Atmani* means *hrdi* (in the heart).

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

Because of *ca,* the cows too turned out like that. Moreover, *snuta-stana-payah-kavalah* means: *snutam stanat payah kavala-rupam yesam,* “the calves, who have milk—in the form of a mouthful—flowing from the udder.” The milk didn’t go in. Both the cows and the calves stood still.

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

On account of *ca,* these two modifiers: “*krsna-mukha-nirgata-venu-gita-piyusam uttabhita-karna-putaih pibantyah"* and “*asru-kalah*”, also apply to the calves, with a modification of gender.

### 10.21.14

*prayo batamba vihaga munayo vane ’smin*  
*krsneksitam tad-uditam kala-venu-gitam \|*  
*aruhya ye druma-bhujan rucira-pravalan*  
*srnvanti milita-drso vigatanya-vacah \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

*prayah*—for the most part; *bata*—(a word expressive of amazement); *amba*—O mother; *viha-gah*—the birds (“which go in the sky”); *munayah*—sages; *vane asmin*—in this forest; *krsna-iksitam*—in such a way that there is a sight of Krsna; *tad-uditam*—arisen from Him; *kala*—melodious (sweet, soft); *venu-gitam*—the song pertaining to a flute; *aruhya*—after ascending; *ye*—which \[birds\]; *druma-bhujan*— to branches of trees; *rucira-pravalan*—whose shoots are splendid; *srnvanti*—they hear; *milita-drsah*—they whose eyes are closed; *vigata-anya-vacah*—they whose talk about other \[subject matters\] has ceased.

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*bata! amba! asmin vane ye vihagah krsneksitam (yatha bhavati tatha) rucira-pravalan druma-bhujan aruhya tad-uditam kala-venu- gitam milita-drsah vigatanya-vacah (ca santah) srnvanti, (te) prayah munayah (bhavitum arhanti).*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*bata! amba! asmin vane ye vihagah druma-bhujan rucira-pravalan aruhya krsneksitam tad-uditam kala-venu-gitam srnvanti, (atah eva milita-drsah vigatanya-vacah bhavanti, te) prayah munayah (bhaveyuh).*

**“How amazing, mother! The birds in this forest must be sages, for the most part. Having ascended to branches, which have splendid burgeons, in such a way that they see Krsna, the birds, hearing the melodious flute song arisen from Him, close their eyes and do not utter unrelated sounds.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Mother! (*amba* = *bho amba = bho matah).* The birds (*vihagah* = *paksinah)* in this forest must be sages *(ye vihagah, te munayah bhavitum arhanti),* for the most part *(prayah = prayena)."* Why? “After ascending to branches of trees (*druma- bhujan = vrksanam sakhah),* which branches have splendid shoots *(rucira-pravalan = rucirah pravalah yesam tan),* in such a way that there is a vision of Krsna, without the obstruction of a flower or a fruit (*krsneksitam = krsna-darsanam puspa-phalady-antaram vina yatha bhavati tatha),* they, whose eyes are closed—because of a certain joy—and by whom other talks are given up *(vigatanya- vacah* = *tyaktanya-vacah),* hear the melodious flute song, which is manifested by Him, Sri Krsna (*tad-uditam = tena sri-krsnena prakatitam)."*

For example, sages, who have ascended to branches of the tree of the Vedas by rejecting the fruits of karma mentioned in the Vedas, in such a way that there is a vision of Sri Krsna, and who are happy, accepting only actions, represented by splendid shoots, only listen to Sri Krsna’s song. Therefore the birds must be sages.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Here they say: “How much more amazing this is! The cows tended by Sri Krsna are fortunate, fine, but can the good fortune of the birds in the forest be described?”

*Prayah* has the sense of *bahulyam* (for the most part), insofar as some peacocks have a similarity with devotees due to dancing with *prema,* and so on. *Bata* (how amazing) has the sense of *vismaya* (astonishment). *Amba* (mother) is said due to the helplessness of *prema.* It is a vocative, in terms of being a mother, directed to an own lady friend. Or it is directed at some elderly lady. Another explanation is that this is the nature of the talk between young women engrossed in *bhava,* because the mention *amba,* which means *matar* (O mother), is suggestive of astonishment.
