“Having ascended to the branches of trees—this means: once situated above a branch—in such a way that they were seeing Krsna...” or in such a way that Krsna was seeing them (*krsneksitam* = *sva-kartrkam krsnasya darsanam, tat-kartrkam va sva-darsanam, yatha syat tatha).* In point of *rucira-pravalan* (whose offshoots are splendid): An obstruction in seeing Him and the means of achieving material enjoyment are pointed out. Still: *krsneksitam yatha syat tatha srnvanti* (they hear in such a way that they see Krsna).

“Their eyes are half-closed” (*milita-drsah* = *ardha-mudrita- drsah).* The sense is their sight is indolent owing to the excellence of great love. They were *vigatanya-vacah,* “their vocal expressions different from “Krsna, Krsna” have ceased” (= *vigatah anyah krsna krsna iti vyatiriktah vacah yesam).* Therefore they are fortunate. The rest was elucidated by Sridhara Svami. In his commentary, his idea in the analogy with the shoots is that the actions are for the Lord, on account of the word *rucira* (splendid), and the purpose is *bhava.*

There is another rendering: “Perhaps *(prayah = vitarke)* the sages, Sri Sanaka and other *atmaramas,* have become birds in this forest.” The girls mention the sages’ purpose: The flute playing is fancifully imagined by Krsna (*krsneksitam = krsnena iksitam svayam eva utpreksitam)*—inasmuch as it wasn’t like that before—, is indescribable, and appeared by itself (*tad uditam) (tad* = *anirvacaniyam)* (*uditam* = s*vayam eva avirbhutam).* What is meant here is that the flute song is *sat-cid-ananda* (spiritual). Or, *tad- uditam* means *sa krsna uditah prakato bhavati yasmat,* “\[the song,\] from which He, Krsna, is manifest.”

The song of the flute agitates the minds of all (*kala-venu-gitam = kalayati jagat cittam ksobhayati iti kalam venu-gitam).* “After ascending to branches, which had splendid shoots...” The shoots were soft and acted like ropes for the birds so they avoid a fall due to the helplessness of *prema.*

“The birds, their knowledge of the truth about the soul covered (*milita-drsah = milita mudrita acchanna drk atma-tattvadi-jnanam37* *yesam tatha-bhutah santah*), were *vigatanya-vacah,* “they to whom the speech, let alone any consideration, of those completely disconnected from Krsna has ceased” (= *vigata anyesam krsna- vyatiriktanam vak tathapi kim punar vicaradikam yebhyah*). Or the previous explanation of *vigatanya-vacah* applies here too.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) Here they say: “How much more amazing this is! The cows tended by Sri Krsna are fortunate, fine, but can the good fortune of the birds in the forest be described?”

*Prayah* has the sense of *bahulyam* (for the most part), insofar as some peacocks have a similarity with topmost devotees due to dancing with *prema,* and so on. *Bata* has the sense of *vismaya* (astonishment). Regarding *amba:* This is the nature of the talk of young women engrossed in *bhava.* Obviously, it is a vocative even when there is no mother, since it was said: *sva-sakhibhyo ’nvavarnayan,* “\[some women of the village\] continuously described it to their lady friends” (10.21.3).

“Having ascended to the branches of trees in such a way that they were seeing Krsna...” or in such a way that Krsna was seeing them *(krsneksitam* = *sva-kartrkam krsnasya darsanam, tat-kartrkam va sva-darsanam, yatra tat yatha syat tatha).* In point of *rucira-pravalan* (whose offshoots are splendid): Their transformations, such as burgeons, are meant to be expressed, and the birds’ obstruction in seeing Him and their means of achieving material enjoyment are pointed out. Still: *krsneksitam yatha syat tatha srnvanti* (they hear in such a way that they see Krsna).

“Their eyes are half-closed” (*milita-drsah = ardha-mudrita- drsah).* The sense is their sight is indolent owing to the excellence of great love. They were *vigatanya-vacah,* “their vocal expressions which are entirely different from vocal expressions about the *murali* flute, have ceased, i.e. have completely left their minds, ears, and voices.” Therefore they are fortunate. The rest is by Sridhara Svami. In his commentary, In his commentary, his idea in the analogy with the shoots is that the actions are for the Lord, on account of the word *rucira* (splendid), and the purpose is *bhava.*

There is another rendering: “Perhaps *(prayah* = *vitarke)* the sages, Sri Sanaka and other *atmaramas,* have become birds in this forest.” The girls mention the sages’ purpose: The flute playing is fancifully imagined by Krsna (*krsneksitam = krsnena iksitam svayam eva utpreksitam)* (*utpreksitam = kalpitam)*—inasmuch as it wasn’t like that before—and is accentuated by Him, meaning He manifests the qualities of the flute playing as a crescendo (*tad-uditam = tena eva uditam) (uditam = uttarottara-prakatita-gunam).* This shows that the flute song attracts the sages even more than trance in Brahman does. The song of the flute attracts the minds of all (*kala-venu-gitam* = *kalayati jagat cittam akarsati iti kalam venu-gitam).*

Next, they mention signs which reveal that the birds truly are sages. The branches consist of variegated subbranches (*rucira- pravalan* = *vicitropasakha-mayan)* and symbolize the branches of the Vedas. After ascending the branches, i.e. after going beyond them in the sense that they reject an engrossment in such branches. they, by whom their bodily perception is covered over (*milita-drsah = milita mudrita acchanna drk dehadi-jnanam yaih tatha-bhutah api santah),* were *vigatanya-vacah,* “they to whom the speech, let alone any consideration, of those completely disconnected from Krsna has ceased.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

At first, the flute song was seen, i.e. figured out, by Krsna (*krsneksitam = tena eva prathamam avagatam)* and was manifested from Him (*tad-uditam* = *tasmad vyaktam ca).* Regarding *rucira-pravalan,* the shoots symbolize a *sattvika-bhava* of the trees.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Calves too are only aware of external things. This is just the materialistic *rasa.* There is an *upadhi* (material characteristic) in that. It is not spiritual. The sages, however, are *atmaramas,* and so they reject all things by means of *jnana* and do not change: They cannot be moved by Krsna.” This cannot be said either, because He attracts even them with His sweetness and enchants them. This is what they say here.

*Bata* is in the sense of *vismaya* (astonishment). *Amba* is a vocative directed at a *sakhi.* This is the nature of young women engrossed in *bhava.*

“The birds must only be sages (*vihaga munayah = vihagah munayah eva bhaveyuh*),” from seeing uncommon attributes, such as residing in a forest, closing the eyes, being silent, and not moving. The syntactical connection is: *ye druma-bhujan aruhya venu-gitam srnvanti,* “The birds who, ascending to branches of a tree, hear the song of the flute...” Concerning *rucira-pravalan* (which have splendid offshoots), a transformation, such as burgeons, of the branches too is pointed out because of the bliss of a song of the flute and because of the bliss of the touch of sages.

The song of the flute agitates the minds of all (*kalayati jagat cittam ksobhayati iti kala-venu-gitam).* How is *venu-gitam? krsneksitam,* “seen only in Krsna” (= *krsne eva iksitam),* meaning it is not seen in Sakra, Paramesthi, Rudra, nor Visnu although they create songs. This is said because these sages are very ancient; because their movements are unimpeded everywhere; because those various songs are composed in many ways; and because of they know the textbooks on music.

“This song cannot possibly have been invented by anyone else.” This is exactly what they say with *tad-uditam,* “the song originated only from Him, Krsna” (= *tasmat krsnad eva uditam avirbhutam).* Only Krsna is the creator of it. The implied meaning is the song is unknown to others. As a result, it’s understood that, just because there is no taker, Krsna, unlike Brahma, Rudra, and others, did not write His own textbook on music. Consequently, on account of being subjugated by relishing a totally unprecedented song, the birds were *milita-drsah* (their eyes are closed) and *vigatanya-vacah,* “their mutual talk about other things, even about the realization of the bliss of Brahman, has ceased.” The drift is: At this time, rejecting even that, those ones became intoxicated by *krsnananda.*

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

*Vigatanya-vacah* means: *vigatah anya- vacah yesam te,* “they whose other words have ceased.” The sense is: *tusnim stutva* (silently praising).

The sages have ascended the branches of the tree of the Vedas by rejecting the fruits of actions mentioned in the Vedas. They, who have accepted, in one way or another, only nonmaterially motivated actions (*niskama-karma*), which are mentioned in the Vedas and are symbolized by splendid offshoots, only listen to Sri Krsna’s song. They are sages because they went beyond that characteristic. The Sruti states: *tam evaikam janatha atmanam anya vaco vimuncatha amrtasyaisa setuh,* “All of you should know that the Soul is one. Avoid other talks. The Soul is the bridge to immortality” (*Mundaka Upanisad* 2.2.5). Thus their *prema* is caused by the *svarupa.*

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Innocent girls (*mugdha)* speak. *Bata* (alas) has the sense of *kheda* (despair): “We cannot become like this.” There is a mix of longing (*abhilasa*), astonishment (*smaya*), and dejection (*visada).*

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“This is a wonder (*bata* = *ascaryam idam),* mother!” It is said like that because birds and sages have a similarity in terms of being silent.

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

The song of the flute was indistinctly sweet *(kala = kalam = avyakta-madhuram). Vigatanya-vacah* signifies: “they from whom words about other subject matters have departed in a special way” (= *visesena gatah anya-visayakah vacah yebhyah).*

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The song of the flute is softly sweet *(kala = madhura). Pravala* means *pallava* (shoot or bud).

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

“The birds in this forest must be sages: Their eyes are closed in such a way that they see Krsna *(krsneksitam milita-drsah = krsneksitam yatha syat tatha milita-drsah*).”

### 10.21.15

*nadyas tada tad upadharya mukunda-gitam*  
*avarta-laksita-manobhava-bhagna-vegah \|*  
*alingana-sthagitam urmi-bhujair murarer*  
*grhnanti pada-yugalam kamalopaharah \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

*nadyah*—the rivers; *tada*—at that time; *tat*—that; *upadharya*— attentively hearing; *mukunda-gitam*—song of Mukunda; *avarta*— by eddies; *laksita*—recognized; *manobhava*—by love (“that which exists in the heart”); *bhagna-vegah*—they whose flow is broken; *alingana-sthagitam*—covered by an embrace; *urmi-bhujaih*—with waves (*urmi),* which are arms; *murareh*—Murari’s; *grhnanti*—they hold; *pada-yugalam*—pair of feet; *kamala-upaharah*—they whose offering is lotuses (as a symbol of the heart).

*nadyah tada tad mukunda-gitam upadharya avarta-laksita- manobhava-bhagna-vegah kamalopaharah urmi-bhujaih alingana- sthagitam (kula-sthitasya) murareh pada-yugalam grhnanti.*

**Перевод:**

**“Attentively hearing that song of Mukunda, the rivers, whose flow is interrupted by their love, recognized by eddies on that occasion, hold Murari’s feet covered by an embrace with the arms of their waves and offer lotuses.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Let us talk about conscious beings. “Even the rivers (*nadyah = nadyo ’pi),* the flow of whom was broken by love, hinted at by whirlpools (*avarta-laksita-manobhava-bhagna- vegah = avartaih paribhramaih laksitena sucitena manobhavena kamena bhagnah vegah, yasam tah),* and who are offering lotuses *(kamalopaharah* = *kamalani upaharantyah)* with their waves, which are arms *(urmi-bhujaih = urmayah eva bhujah taih),* in such a way that there is a covering with an embrace *(alingana-sthagitam = alinganena sthagitam yatha bhavati tatha) (sthagitam* = *acchaditam),* are holding *(grhnanti = dharayanti)* Murari’s two feet.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

How more amazing is the glory of conscious beings! Can the good fortune of rivers, though they consist of nonconscious water, be described?

“Attentively hearing *(upadharya* = *savadhanam srutva)* it, which is most fascinating, Sri Kalindi, Sri Manasa-Ganga, and other rivers hold the lotus feet of Murari—in order to offer lotuses *(kamalopaharah = kamalani upaharantyah).”* This means: “to offer, as an official tribute, flowers dear to Him.”

Regarding Murari: There was a big demon named Mura. Owing to a boon from Sri Siva, he would take away the whole life force just by placing the hand on the chest. He terrified the gods. He is famous in regard to *Sri Vamana Purana.* Murari is Narayana, by the derivation: *murasya ari* (Mura’s foe). This is because of Garga’s statement: *tasman nandatmajo ’yam te narayana-samo gunaih,* “Therefore, Nanda, this son of yours is similar to Narayana in terms of attributes” *(Bhagavatam* 10.8.19); because Krsna was being designated in Vraja with his names; and because of a similarity of attributes. ‘Murari’ is said with this intention: “Just as Mura was playfully killed by him before, Death too (*mara,* or Cupid), which is killing us right now, should be cast away by You.”

The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami. Alternatively, *kamalopaharah* means: *kamalaya laksmya api upaharah baly- arpanam yasu,* “the rivers, on whom there is an offering of tribute by Laksmi.” Or, as a pun on *upahara,* the following is implied: Hearing the bewildering flute song, the rivers abandoned a natural quickness in going toward their husband, the ocean, became embodied, turned out as ladies who have divine presentations such as gems and pearls and, being adorned with the presentations, which were placed above lotuses (*kamalopaharah = kamalanam upa haraih bhusitah satyah)* (*upa = upari vinyastaih),* did a full embrace by holding Murari’s feet in place (*alingana-sthagitam = susthiri-krtya samyag alinganti)* with the long arms of their waves.

“Therefore only they are the most fortunate. We are unlucky; listening to that flute song does not evoke any such response in us. There is no hiatus in the flow of our household chores such as serving one’s husband, we are not wearing ornaments for His satisfaction in a manifest way, nor do we have many arms with which we could hug one of His feet by placing it firmly on our breasts.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Unable even to conceal their emotions like before, due to the immenseness of *raga* (love; melody) they fancifully imagine their own lot even in comparison to a nonconscious entity while continuously giving a description only in conformity with their own taste.

The syntactical connection is: *nadyah tada tad mukunda-gitam upadharya urmi-bhujaih kamalopaharah satyah alingana-sthagitam taih eva murareh pada-yugalam grhnanti,* “At that very moment (*tada = tat-ksane eva),* i.e. when the soundwaves of the song came, the rivers, attentively hearing (*upadharya = savadhanam srutva)* that song...” i.e. that topmost enchanting tune, a song whose melody was produced from the highest bliss; the ardent agitation in reference to *avarta* (eddy) is shown thus.

“... of Mukunda...” by the derivation: *muktim dadati,* “He gives liberation” from all sorrow, by means of His association, which is the crest jewel of all bliss.38

While holding offerings of lotuses with the waves of their arms, the rivers, including Sri Kalindi and Sri Manasa-Ganga, take hold of Murari’s two feet with those arms in such a way that the feet are covered by an embrace (*alingana-sthagitam = taih eva alinganena avrtam yatha syat tatha).*

Further in that regard, this is the sequence: Right at first, they offer lotuses cut by whirlpools. Afterward they take hold of both feet. Then they embrace both feet.

This is being said: Hearing the bewildering flute song, the rivers, abandoning a natural quickness in going toward their husband, the ocean, and having offerings of lotuses (*kamalopaharah = kamalani eva harah yasam tatha-bhutah satyah)* *(upa* = *upari vinyastaih),* made Murari’s two feet very firm on themselves by holding and embracing with waves that were many long arms. Lotuses are dear to Sri Krsna, just because of the species, and specifically because they originated in Sri Vrndavana.

Murari is the killer of Mura (*murari = murasya hanta),* a particular ancient demon mentioned in *Vamana Purana.* In reference to: *narayana-samah,* which means *narayanena samo ’yam,* “He is similar to Narayana” (10.8.19), the rivers also think: “By doing *bhajana* to Him, there is no deviation from being dedicated to one’s husband.”

“Therefore only they are the most fortunate...” (The rest is the same. Moreover:) The truth in this matter is as follows: When the Krsna moon performs that kind of flute song, burgeons on dry branches come about, stones melt, streams solidify, and so on. Therefore the rivers, whose water has increased by the solidification of water and whose waves have lotuses, rise up to Him, though He is on elevated ground, and touch His lotus feet. From this perspective, the rivers look like conscious beings.39

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Moreover, they say: “Although Krsna enchants everyone, the fact that He enchants all females is much more pronounced.”

The rivers' momentum was broken by their lust indicated by whirlpools (*dvarta-laksita-manobhava-bhagna-vegah = avartaih paribhramaih laksitena manobhavena kamena bhagnah vegah yasam tah).* Therefore the rivers, having lost their patience and bashfulness, did not proceed to meet their husband, the ocean. The water level rose, hence they hold on their limbs (*grhnanti = svangesu dharayanti)* both feet of Murari—who is on the shore. His feet are covered, meaning they are made to stay in place, by an embrace with the arms of their waves (*urmi-bhujaih* = *urmayah eva bhujah taih).*

They do so while offering a lotus (*kamalopaharah* = *padmam upaharantyah).* Or they are offering very cool and fragrant water *(kamalopaharah = susitalam sugandham jalam upaharantyah). Amara-kosa* states: *salilam kamalam jalam,* “*Salilam, kamalam,* and *jalam* \[are synonymous\]” (1.10.3). The drift is they are as if proffering an offering of *padya* for washing the feet with their water. Or they are offering all their wealth (*kamalopaharah = kamala sva-sarva- sampattih tam arpayantyah).40* The idea is: *sva-ramanam prinayitum* (to please their lover). The drift is: “Their husband, though he is the ocean, never despised the rivers like our husbands despise us. Alas! Only we are unfortunate.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Other ladies speak. *Nadyah* (rivers) denotes *ambu-pravahatmanah* (those whose nature is to flow water; or those whose body is a stream of water). *Upadharya* means *srutva* (after hearing). *Kamalopaharah* signifies: *kamalani upaharah yasam,* “the rivers, whose offering consists of lotuses.” This means the rivers were offering those gifts.

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

*Praudha gopis* speak: “Hey *sakhi,* the river flow has momentum by nature, yet the rivers solidify even their own flow. They change their nature. Why can we not give up our patience and shyness too?” Moreover, *manobhava* means either *manoratha* (inner longing) or *kama* (love, passion).

### 10.21.16

*drstvatape vraja-pasun saha rama-gopaih*  
*sancarayantam anu venum udirayantam \|*  
*prema-pravrddha uditah kusumavalibhih*  
*sakhyur vyadhat sva-vapusambuda atapatram \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

*drstva*—after seeing; *atape*—in the heat; *vraja-pasun*—animals in the pastures; *saha rama-gopaih*—with Rama and with the cow herders; *sancarayantam*—\[Him\] who was herding; *anu*—after (being at the back); *venum*—a flute (or *anuvenum*—a congenial flute); *udirayantam*—who was sounding; *prema-pravrddhah*—increased out of love; *uditah*—went above; *kusuma-avalibhih*—because of a series of flowers; *sakhyuh*—for its friend; *vyadhat*—it made; *sva- vapusa*—with its body; *ambu-dah*—a cloud (“which gives water”); *atapa-tram*—a parasol (“that which protects from the heat”).

*ambudah (tam sri-krsnam) atape rama-gopaih saha vraja-pasun sancarayantam anu venum udirayantam drstva prema-pravrddhah (sri-krsnasya upari) uditah (ca san svasya) sakhyuh (sri-krsnasya) kusumavalibhih sva-vapusa atapatram vyadhat.*

**Перевод:**

**“Noticing that He, along with Rama and the cowherds, was grazing animals in the heat and was playing a flute while being at the back, a cloud went above Him, increased out of love and, for its friend Krsna, made a parasol with its own body, because of series of flowers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

By the similarity of being one who habitually takes away the pain of people, Krsna is a friend *(sakhyuh = sri- krsnasya).* “Having risen above Him, and having increased out of love *(prema-pravrddha uditah* = *tad-upary-uditah punah premna pravrddhah san),* a cloud made a parasol *(atapatram vyadhat = chatram vihitavan)* with its body with a multitude of flowers,” or with snowflakes, which are similar to that *(kusumavalibhih = puspa- samuhaih saha, tat-tulyaih tusaraih saha va).*

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Here they say, “So be it. Sri Kalindi and Sri Manasa-Ganga, who abide in Sri Vrndavana and have obtained Sri Krsna’s wonderful amusements, and other rivers too due to fellowship with them, have that kind of good luck. Can even the good fortune of a simple cloud, which abides in the sky, is mostly unconscious and is formed of vapor, be described?”

“A cloud saw Sri Krsna.” The word sri-krsnam needs to be added. Because of the meter, the absence of it is not faulty. Krsna was loudly playing (udirayantam = uccaih irayantam = uccaih vadayantam) a flute time and time again (anu = varam-varam). He did so to gladden and assemble all the animals that had gone to faraway places. Accompanied by the cow herders, He was grazing here and there the cows, buffalos and other animals of Vraja (vraja- pasun = vrajasya pasun) in the heat, even at the time of autumn. This implies exertion.

Or anu venum signifies venum anu “after playing the flute” (= tad-vadananantaram). Optionally, the syntactical connection of udirayantam anu venum is done right here. This means: venu-nadena eva udirayantam (while shouting only with the sound of a flute).

Having increased out of love (prema-pravrddhah = premna pravrddhah san), the cloud made a parasol with its body, which has water—since the word used is ambuda (cloud, lit., ‘giver of water’). The body of the cloud is accompanied with a multitude of droplets of water (kusumavalibhih = kusumam megha-puspam jalam tasya avalibhih = jalasya bindu-nikaraih sahitena), by the definition: megha-puspam ghana-rasah, “Megha-puspam and ghana-rasa \[are synonymous and mean “water”\]” (Amara-kosa 1.10.5). The purpose was to also mitigate the heat of the companions.

Or, the instrumental case has the sense of visesana (modifier): the parasol is characterized by water droplets (kusumavalibhih = tabhih visistam). The overall idea is: “It made a parasol, which is its body.” The parasol has a kusumavali. Thus its own body and wealth were offered out of friendship. The rest was elucidated by Sri Svami.

There is another interpretation: pravrddhe atape asmakam sakhyuh priyasya sva-vapusa atapatram vyadhat, kusumavalibhih ca prema vyadhat,41“When the heat greatly increased, the cloud made a parasol with its body for our friend, our lover, and showed affection *(prema = pritim)* with a series of flowers.”42In this way, the displeasure of rain, obtained due to the existence of a cloud, is repudiated. Therefore the gist is: “The cloud is very fortunate, but we are out of luck because we don’t see Him then.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Now, even while imagining an emotion in an unconscious entity as before, with a description of the *rasa* of friendship they speak as if to cover their own *rasa.* They do this in the next verse as well.

“A cloud saw...” with eyes made of lightning; this needs to be added. The word *atapa* denotes a heat greater than *tapa* (heat).43Concerning *vraja-pasun* (the animals of the cowherd village; or the animals in the pastures): They need to stay in the pastures because much grass is required.

Krsna is accompanied by Rama and the cow herders: This means much shade is needed. Krsna was loudly sounding (*udirayantam = uccaih irayantam)* a flute at the back of the pack (*anu = pascat)...* to attract clouds. Right after that, a cloud arose, in the name of love, and greatly increased *(prema-pravrddha uditah = premanam vyapya uditah pravrddhah ca):* Its body swelled. For the friend (*sakhyuh*), in terms of a similarity of color, etc., the cloud made a parasol *(atapatram vyadhat = chatram krtavan)* with its body—which has water, since it is said: *ambuda* (cloud, lit., ‘giver of water’). The body of the cloud is accompanied with a multitude of droplets of water *(kusumavalibhih = kusumam megha-puspam jalam tasya avalibhih = jalasya bindu-nikaraih sahitena),”* by the definition: *megha- puspam...* (see above). Even the parasol has a *kusumavali.* Thus its own body and wealth were offered out of friendship. Therefore the gist is: “The cloud is most fortunate, but we are out of luck because we don’t see Him then.”

The truth of the matter is this: When His companions are exhausted while tending cows in the heat and when cows go astray, He plays the *mallara raga* with the names of those ones to attract cows and clouds. By a vision of that sort of pastime, some girls fancifully imagine the situation in that way.

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

*Kusumavalibhih* means *kusuma-prayaih sikaraih,* “with drizzles, which are almost flowers,” because water is *megha-puspa.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

They say, “Darn, even the things that are in *sakhya-bhava* make themselves successful.” The cloud enlarged only out of love *(prema-pravrddhah = premna eva pravrddhah).* This means it increased to alleviate the heat of Him who was with cows and cow herders.

The cloud made a parasol with its body with a series of water drops (*kusumavalibhih = jala-kanavalibhih saha),* by the definition: *megha-puspam...* (see above).

*Sakhyuh* means *sri-krsnasya* (for Krsna, a friend). Krsna is a friend in terms habitually dispelling the *tapa* (heat or affliction) with a rain of Rasa; in terms of having the same color; and also by looking at the similarity of a yellow garment and the sound of the flute with its lightning flashes and its rumbling. The cloud, thinking from the viewpoint of friendship, made a parasol that rained snow *(atapatram = tusara-varsi-cchatram).* The drift is: “Even a cloud, situated in the sky, makes Him happy, but only we cannot get to make Him happy. Fie on us!”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

How was the parasol? It was characterized by fine water drops (*kusumavalibhih = suksmabhih ambu-kanabhih visistam).*

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

*Kusumavalibhih* means *suksma-sva-kanikabhih* (with its fine droplets), because a dictionary states: *megha-puspam ghana-rasah.*

**Annotation**

The third case ending in *kusumavalibhih* can also be explained along the lines of the *sahokti* ornament (conjoined statement): “The cloud made (*vyadhat*) a parasol and made a series of flowers.” This is the *utpreksa* ornament (fanciful imagination). Flowers were showered by goddesses. Moreover, a white parasol is a symbol of royalty. Girls love a prince.

Regarding *sahokti,* in his elaboration on his *sutra: saharthair apradhane trtiya* (*Hari-namamrta-vyakarana* 676), Jiva Gosvami writes: *evam karma-sahabhave ’pi, yatha, ganena saha nrtyam karotity-adi,* “Likewise, it occurs even when the accompaniment is with the object of the action, for instance: *ganena saha nrtyam karoti krsnah* (Krsna does a dance along with a song)” (HNV 676 *vrtti).*

### 10.21.17

*purnah pulindya urugaya-padabja-raga-*  
*sri-kunkumena dayita-stana-manditena \|*  
*tad-darsana-smara-rujas trna-rusitena*  
*limpantya anana-kucesu jahus tad-adhim \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

*purnah*—complete (or filled);*pulindyah*—the women of the Pulinda tribe; *urugaya*—of Urugaya; *pada-abja*—on the lotus feet; *raga*— which was a red color; *sri-kunkumena*—with saffron paste, endowed with splendor; *dayita-stana-manditena*—which was an adornment on the breasts of a beloved; *tat-darsana*—by seeing that \[saffron\]; *smara-rujah*—they who have the pain of Cupid; *trna*—grass; *rusitena*—adorned (smeared on, i.e. adhering to); *limpantyah*— while smearing; *anana*—on \[their\] faces; *kucesu*—and breasts; *jahuh*—they gave up; *tat-adhim*—their mental torment.

*pulindyah dayita-stana-manditena trna-rusitena urugaya-padabja- raga-sri-kunkumena purnah (babhuvuh. tah) anana-kucesu (tat trna- rusita-kunkumam) limpantyah tad-darsana-smara-rujah (satyah) tad-adhim jahuh.*

**Перевод:**

**“The Pulinda women are complete. Smearing their faces and breasts with splendorous saffron which had adorned a beloved’s breast, which then became a red color on Urugaya’s lotus feet, and which was adhering to grass, they, who had felt the torment of Eros by seeing the saffron, gave up that mental pain.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Here the *gopis* speak in a self-conceited way. The Pulindis are the women of tribal people *(pulindyah* = *sabaranganah).* They are complete, meaning they are successful *(purnah = krtarthah).* How did this occur? In answer to this, the *gopis* say: “At first the *kunkuma* (saffron paste) was smeared (*manditena = anuliptena*) on the breasts of His girlfriends. Later, at the time of conjugal sports, the *kunkuma* acquired splendor by the redness (*raga-sri = ragena arunyena srih kantir yasya tena kunkumena)* on the lotus feet of Urugaya, Sri Krsna. Afterward, by His wandering about in the various places of the forest, the *kunkuma* adhered (*rusitena = lagnena)* to blades of grass. By seeing that *kunkuma,* the aborigine women experienced the distress created by Cupid, and so they smeared it on their faces and breasts, which were pained by lust. Thus they became successful, but to hell with us who are unable to find such means of eradicating the same distress.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Now, in three verses Suka relates the statement of other *gopis.* Or, as before, an explanation is done as one statement. For instance: “So be it. The cloud, who does that kind of service and who won His friendship by rendering assistance to all has good fortune. Can even just the good fortune of the women of the lowest stratum of society, who are to be rejected from afar due to being untouchable, be described?” Along with the Pulindis, all the women belonging to the lowest stratum, such as the Bhillas, who roam the woodlands, are worthy of being included here, due to fellowship.

‘Urugaya’ is derived as: *urudha giyate gopaih svayam va gayati venuna ity urugayah,* “He is sung in many ways by cow herders—or He Himself sings in many ways, with a flute—and so He is Urugaya.”

The saffron was adorned, that is, was taken as an adornment, on the breasts of some particular beloveds (*dayita-stana-manditena = dayitanam kasancit stanesu bhusanataya grhitena).* It was adorned (*rusitena)44* on grass—the pebbles too are meant by this, as a partial indication. Further, the manners of those various women are not clearly stated on account of bashfulness. The verse was elucidated by Sri Svamipada.

They gave up the pain of lust (*tad-adhim = kama-vyatham).* Or they gave up, right at that time, the mental anguish already done by Cupid (*tadadhim = tada adhim)* (*tada = tasmin eva ksane)* (*manovyatham smara-krtam eva).* Alternatively, they gave up an indescribable pain, i.e. the mental displeasure of not attaining Sri Krsna (*tad-adhim = anirvacaniyam sri-krsnaprapti-manoduhkham).* The rest was elucidated by Sridhara Svami.

Alternatively, the saffron belonged to Sri, who has love for Urugaya’s lotus feet (*urugaya-padabja-raga-sri-kunkumena = urugaya-padabjayoh anuragah yasyah tasyah sriyah kunkumena),* therefore “it was smeared, as an adornment (*manditena = mandanataya anuliptena),* on the breasts of beloveds, persons like us, just for personal satisfaction.” Or the saffron had a splendor that was reddish like the redness of Urugaya’s lotus feet (*urugaya- padabja-raga-sri-kunkumena = urugaya-padabja-raga-vad aruna srih yasya kunkumasya tena):* Out of love, which is similar to the red color of His lotus feet, the women put it on their breasts as an adornment (*manditena = mandanataya grhitena).*

Venerable Sri Vallabha says: The women gave up their anguish by a special favor of the Lord because of an entrance (*avesa*) in those women by Maha-Laksmi on account of a connection with that saffron.

Another explanation is that the saffron had a splendor like the splendor of a ruby45(*abja-raga-sri-kunkumena* = *padma-ragah tasya srih iva srih kantih yasya tena kunkumena).* Or *sri-kunkuma* had a red color like the redness of a lotus (*abja-raga-sri-kunkumena* = *abjasya ragah iva ragah yasya tena sri-kunkumena).*

As a double meaning, this could be said: “By seeing the saffron, the Pulinda women remembered Him and felt great pain, which involved an upsurge of infinite sadness due to not attaining Him. And by touching that saffron, a certain happiness was produced, culminating in the sweetness of the excellence of sheer bliss. They thus gave up their unbearable anguish and became complete, successful, by a connection with the Lord, or with those girlfriends that had a connection with Him. In this way their mental pain was mitigated, yet ours remains, and so we are more unfortunate than all living beings in every way, due to being inferior even to those women.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Now, a description of their own *rasa,* with a verse suggestive of their own *bhava.* However, the harmonization is as follows: “So be it: A cloud, His friend, has good fortune; can even just the good fortune of ladies of the lowest stratum of society be described?”

Insofar as *purnah* (complete) is concerned, the *gopis* mean to say: “We too are able to become like that by a connection with it somehow or other, but actually that sort of good luck doesn’t exist.” As for *pulindyah* (the Pulindis): “We are more lamentable than them.”

‘Urugaya’ is by the derivation: *urudha venuna gayati iti urugayah,* “He sings in many ways, with a flute, and so He is Urugaya.” This is the reason why the *gopis* are losing patience. *Urugaya-padabja-raga- sri-kunkumena* means: *urugaya-padabjayoh raga-rupam yat tatah eva hetoh asmadrsaika-gamya-kanty-amodadi-sri-visesa-yuktam ca yat tena kunkumena,* “with saffron, which is the color of the redness of Urugaya’s lotus feet and, because of that, which has a special beauty *(sri),* such as a sheen and fragrance, that should only belong to us.” With this, they say their hearts have the desire to touch that kind of lotus feet.

With *dayita-stana-manditena* (adorned on the breasts of a beloved), they say a lover like Him cannot possibly be without a girlfriend. “The saffron brought a special resplendence from both breasts of some secret beloved” (= *ya kacit preyasi nigudham vidyate, tasyah stanabhyam manditam sobha-visesam anita-caram yat tena).* The *gopis* imply: “Only She has that sort of good fortune, the fact of engaging in the sport of love with Him, but ours is much farther than very far.”

Regarding *tad-darsana,* which signifies *tad-darsanena* (“by seeing that” saffron): Even that which has a connection with Him immediately has the power of enchanting like He does, either only by nature or by making one take interest in His pastimes, to say nothing of seeing Him. As regards *trna-rusitena* (adhering on grass): “Let us have a birth of that sort.” As for *limpantyah* (while smearing) and the rest: “It’s unbelievable. How happy must they be!”

“At first each Pulinda woman took the saffron and brought it to her face to smell it and to look at it, given that this kind of saffron evokes greed for itself. Afterward, she smeared it on her face, and then on her breast due to an outburst of Cupid. Because of seeing a thing that had the touch of Krsna’s limb, there should be an occasion merely to touch that thing. The pain of Cupid was launched, but by getting that thing, the lust was somewhat alleviated. That happened to them, but in our case, there is not even a fraction of alleviation of it, therefore even those women are better off than we are.”

Here, this idea is being conveyed: The entire statement of the *gopis,* though suitably understood merely as an emotional response, is related because that type of deep emotion is the cause of directly coming in contact with the object of the emotion, even from afar. For example, it is said: *yasyasti bhaktir bhagavaty akincanah,* “The gods assemble along with all their virtues in one who has unselfish *bhakti* to the Lord” (*Bhagavatam* 5.18.12). Therefore the above and more will be reiterated by the turbaned queens:

*kamayamaha etasya srimat-pada-rajah sriyah \|*  
*kuca-kunkuma-gandhadhyam murdhna vodhum gadabhrtah \|\|*  
*vraja-striyo yad vanchanti pulindyas trna-virudhah \|*

**“We desire to carry with the head His resplendent foot dust which is enhanced with the scent of saffron on Sri’s bosom. We long for the touch, which the ladies of Vraja, the Pulinda women, grass, and creepers, crave, of the great Soul’s feet.” (*****Bhagavatam*** **10.83.42-43)**

Such being the case, it’s understood from the words “*urugaya- padabja-raga*” and “*dayita-stana-manditena"* that the saffron which adhered to His feet came from His beloved’s breasts. That beloved is mentioned with the word *sri.* She is distinguished even among those girls making the descriptions. Only Sri Radha is obtained, by the renown from *Matsya Purana: rukmini dvaravatyam tu radha vrndavane vane,* “Rukmini is in Dvaraka, but Radha is in Vrndavana forest.” Given that all the Vraja-devis are Sris, by looking at *Brahma- samhita: sriyah kantah kantah parama-purusah,* “The ladyloves are Sris, the lover is the topmost Purusa” (5.56), Her superiority is seen specifically in *Brhad-gautamiya:*

*devi krsna-mayi prokta radhika para-devata \|*  
*sarva-laksmi-mayi sarva-kantih sammohini para \|\|*

**“Radhika, the topmost deity, is said to be a goddess filled by Krsna. She has the nature of all the Laksmis. She has all kinds of splendor, and is the topmost enchantress.”**

The other Sri, referred to in the verse that begins: *kasyanubhavo ’sya na deva vidmahe,* **“The influence of what does he have, as a result of which he has the qualification to touch the dust of Your feet? We don’t know, Lord. With a desire for it, Sri, a lady, relinquished enjoyments and performed austerities for a long time, maintaining her vow”** (*Bhagavatam* 10.16.36), is rejected. Nor is there any connection with Rukmini here, and so the following makes sense: This is a meeting that took place on that very day, insofar as the Pulindis were roaming right there. It’s understood, from the act of smearing, that the saffron was moist.

This connection between the Two is not the form of a certain kind of *sambhoga,* because, on the occasion of Rasa, Their meeting felt like a new meeting, by considering this text: *bhagavan api ta ratrih saradotphulla-mallikah, viksya rantum manas cakre,* **“Seeing those nights, during which the jasmines were in bloom because of autumn, Krsna, relying on Yogamaya, made up His mind to enjoy amorous pleasure even though He is God”** (10.29.1); and because otherwise a statement of disregard by Him once more (10.29.27), for the sake of testing the *gopis,* would appear incongruent.

The following is understood: This happened only because of a connection with the flute, given that the event is told in the context of flute playing. The connection with the flute is implied with the name Urugaya. Therefore this idea is obtained: On a certain occasion, Krsna played the flute. Radha was attracted and fell in a swoon. For the purpose of abating it, out of respect Krsna touched Her on the chest, which had saffron and was perspiring, with the blossom which is the antidote of His foot. Then, because even at that time His shyness had not completely dissipated, He quickly went away from there, and so it was said: *kascit paroksam krsnasya,* “Listening to that song of Krsna’s flute, some women of the village continuously described it to their lady friends, unperceived by others” (10.21.3). The *gopis* who spoke verse 3 also spoke the current verse. Since these girls, most of whom had *purva anuraga* (love before ever meeting Him), had no opportunity to be jealous, even the idea that another girl met Him doubled their passion. However, there is the text:

***yarhy ambujaksa tava pada-talam ramaya***  
***datta-ksanam kvacid aranya-jana-priyasya*** **\|**  
***aspraksma tat-prabhrti nanya-samaksam anga***  
***sthatums tvayabhiramita bata parayamah*** **\|\|**

**“Hey lotus-eyed, since the time when we touched the base of Your foot, which provides Rama with a festival if she gets a chance to touch it, we, delighted by You who like the people in the forest, have been unable to remain in front of another man. Isn’t this amazing, sweetheart! (10.29.36)**

Here the notion that the virgin *gopis* were accepted by Him by His touch refers to the idea that they identify with Her, who was touched by Him, as told in the current verse.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The word *dayita* is in the plural. The beloveds are some women who were attracted by the flute and who fainted. A mere touch was done by His blossomlike feet to alleviate their swoon.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Now, paying no attention to either His form, such as beauty, or to His qualities, such as the flute song, the ***gopis*** who are the splendor of Sri Vrsabhanu-kumari’s lotus feet hint at the aspect of *mahabhava* which is the great essence known as *madana* while expounding the fact that even something connected with Him enchants women as much as He does. *Mahabhava* is the seventh stage of *prema.*

“The Pulindis, women of tribal people, are successful, but we are not, therefore we want to know what austerity they did so we can do that.” Their *anuraga* is implied thus.

Someone might ask, “By what are they complete?” In that regard they say: *urugaya-padabja-raga-sri-kunkumena,* which signifies: *urugaya-padabjasya ragah ranjanam yatra tena sri-kunkumena,* “by *sri-kunkuma,46* on which is the color of Urugaya’s lotus feet.”

Where did that saffron on His lotus feet come from? *dayita- stana-manditena* (adorned on a beloved’s breast). The sense is the saffron was there because of contact with the beloved’s breast as a result of sensual enjoyment. The gist is: “Therefore let us only praise the Pulindis, because we could not tolerate praising and desiring Her supreme good luck.”

Although here the beloved is only Sri Vrsabhanu-kumari, not honoring Her is only due to an upsurge of passion. “Do the Pulindis atribute any significance to that saffron paste?” In that matter, they say: *trna-rusitena,* “the saffrom adhered on grass” (= *trnesu lagnena),* owing to the forestial amusement of Krsna after His sensual enjoyment with the beloved.

Next: *tad-darsana-smara-rujah,* “The Pulindis had the pain of Cupid by seeing that, the saffron that adhered on grass.” The gist is: “We don’t know what would have happened to them had they seen Krsna.”

Afterward, while smearing it—meaning they thought they were being sensually enjoyed by Krsna—on the face, with the desire to smell the fragrance on Krsna’s limbs, and on the breasts, with the intent to experience the sensual enjoyment that She got, they gave up the pain of Cupid (*tad-adhim = kandarpa-pidam).* “How amazing! This is some special power of Her saffron! We, however, are not getting even a whiff of it.”

In *Ujjvala-nilamani,* the current verse is given as an example of *madana,* specifically on the topic of praising someone who had a mere connection with Krsna: *sadabhoge ’pi tad-gandha-matradhara- stutir yatha* (14.223). Only because *madana* is the aggregate of emotions (*bhava-samasti*), all sensual enjoyments (*sambhoga*) and all amusements (*vihara)* exist in *madana.*

Here, it is to be understood that a *sambhoga* (sensual enjoyment; meeting) even in *vihara* took place because Krsna suddenly made His appearance at that time. Thus, in this regard they say (or a respectable scholar says) that this: *sahasaivavirbhutam krsnam alingitavatyah,* “They embraced Krsna, who appeared at once,” is the sense of that: *varnayantyo ’bhirebhire,* “They embraced while describing” (10.21.6).47

*sarva-bhavodgamollasi madano ’yam paratparah \|*  
*rajate hladini-saro radhayam eva yah sada \|\|*

**“*****Madana,*** **whose nature is to eminently shine in such a way that it goes above all emotions, is higher than the highest,48is the essence of Hladini, and always shines only in Radha.” (*****Ujjvala-nilamani*** **14.219)**

Because of this text, the explanation is not that the speaker is some other.49

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Srimatl’s *sakhis* speak to one another while hinting at the *mahabhava* known as *madana.* “Hey *sakhis,* the Pulindis, the tribal women, are complete, but we are incomplete.” Where does the saffron that was on His lotus feet come from? In that regard they say: *dayita.* “Therefore let us only praise the Pulindis.”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Again, *mugdha gopis* speak. “Even the Pulindis are more fortunate and complete than us. We are lower than them.” The beloved is Radha. The saffron was an adornment *(manditena = mandanena)* of Her breasts; The suffix *\[k\]ta* in *manditena* is in the passive impersonal. “Considering themselves embraced by Sri Krsna, the Pulindis became successful, but we are unable to do like they did because we lack independence, so fie on us.” There is *nirveda* (self-deprecation), *glani* (dejection), *sanka* (fear of having done wrong), and *dainya* (meekness).

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

The Pulindis are the wives of the Pulindas, a meager category of people who reside in woodlands. In this verse, the *gopis* say even those women developed *bhakti,* on account of proximity to the Lord. The Pulindis are complete, meaning their direct connection with the dust of the lotus feet of the Lord remains intact. ‘Urugaya’ means: *urubhir giyate ity urugayah,* “He is sung by many, and so He is Urugaya.”

The saffron belonged to Sri, Laksmi. She chose the Lord. She is a devotee of the Lord’s lotus feet. Applying the saffron on their faces and breasts to relieve themselves of lust, even the Pulindis were enjoyed because of the entrance *(pravesa*) of Laksmi through the saffron, and so they gave up their mental pain and hence became successful. In truth, lust is the only form of mental pain. This *bhagavat-katha* is extraordinary, and so it is said: *urugaya.*

### 10.21.18

*hantayam adrir abala hari-dasa-varyo*  
*yad rama-krsna-carana-sparasa-pramodah \|*  
*manam tanoti saha-go-ganayos tayor yat*  
*paniya-suyavasa-kandara-kanda-mulaih \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

*hanta*—(a word used for expressing joy / astonishment); *ayam*—this; *adrih*—hill; *abalah*—O women; *hari-dasa-varyah*—the best among Hari’s servants; *yat*—because; *rama-krsna-carana*—of Rama’s feet and of Krsna’s feet; *sparasa* (i.e. *sparsa*)—by the touch; *pramodah*— who has rapture; *manam tanoti*—honors (“extends honor”); *saha- go-ganayoh*—who are with cows and with the group; *tayoh*—unto both of Them; *yat*—because; *paniya*—with drinkable substances; *suyavasa* (i.e. *su-yavasa*)—nice grass; *kandara*—caves; *kanda- mulaih*—and with bulbous roots (or *kanda*—with bulbs; *mulaih*— with roots).

*hanta! abalah! ayam adrih hari-dasa-varyah (bhavati,) yad (yad = yasmat) (sah adrih) rama-krsna-carana-sparasa-pramodah (bhavati), yat (ca sah) saha-go-ganayoh tayoh (rama-krsnayoh) paniya-suyavasa-kandara-kanda-mulaih manam tanoti.*

**Перевод:**

**“How astonishing! This hill, girls, is Hari’s best servant because it has rapture by the touch of Rama’s and Krsna’s feet and because it honors both of Them, who are accompanied by both the group and the cows and are supplied with drinkable substances, nice grass, caves, bulbs, and roots.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*Hanta* has the sense of *harsa* (joy). “Hey *sakhis,* this hill, Govardhana, is obviously the best of Hari’s servants *(hari- dasa-varyah = dhruvam hari-dasesu sresthah*).” Why? “Because *(yat = yasmat)* it has rapture due to the touch of Rama’s and Krsna’s feet *(rama-krsna-carana-sparasa-pramodah = rama-krsnayoh carana- sparsena pramodah yasya sah)..."* in terms of seeing a bristling of hairs by the tricky appearance of a growth of grass and the like.

“…and because *(yat = yasmat)* it gives honor to both of Them *(tayoh),* who are with cows and with a multitude of friends *(saha- go-ganayoh = saha gobhih ganena ca vartamanayoh) (ganena = sakhi-samuhena),* —with what?—with drinking water, nice grass, caves, and bulbous roots *(paniya-suyavasa-kandara-kanda-mulaih* = *paniyaih suyavasaih sobhana-trnaih kandaraih ca kanda-mulaih ca),"* according to the occasion. Therefore it is extremely fortunate. *Sparasa* stands for *sparsa.*

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“*Aho!* Fine, let the good fortune of these Pulindis, who have the ability to go wherever Krsna travels, be far away from us. Govardhana, though immobile, has the topmost good fortune.”

*Ayam* (this) is said because of directly pointing to it with the index finger, due to their residing in the vicinity of Sri Govardhana. Or it is because of their impression of it as one dearest to Sri Krsna. Alternatively, the reason is that in this way they avoid mentioning the mountain’s name, out of great respect.

He takes away (*harati*) unlimited sins and sorrows of the world, and the hearts of all, as is appropriate, and so He is called Hari. This hill is the best (*varyah* = *sresthah)* of His servants who have His nature. *Pramoda* means ‘eminent joy’ *(pramodah* = *prakrstah modah = prakrstah harsah).* It is characterized by a growth of grass, the condition of melting, a flow of water drops, etc., which are the natures of horripilation, perspiration, tears of bliss, and so on.

Regarding *tanoti* (it spreads, expands), the sense is: “It expands the honor being shown by everyone else.” By the word *go* (cow), other animals are included, as a partial indication. *Paniya,* in the plural, signifies beverages such as water, and honey. *Suyavasa* are soft grasses that promote nourishment and cause the production of milk. The long vowel in *suyavasa* is poetic license, owing to a conformity with the meter.

Alternatively, the word is *paniyasu-yavasa. Paniya-su* means: *paniyamsuvate ksaranti paniya-sunimrduni yavasani,* “They produce drinkable liquid, that is, they give forth drinkable liquid, and so they are *paniya-su,50* soft grasses.” Or *su* stands for *sava,* which denotes *prasava:* flowers, fruits, and so on. Sometimes the reading is *bhu.* The sense of *bhu* (ground) is a beautiful place for sitting. *Kandara* means *guhah* (caves). The following, which are there, are partially indicated: jewels, beds, seats, lamps, mirrors, and so forth. The varieties of *kanda* (bulb) and *mula* (root) are respectively different. This was written earlier (BVT 10.20.28).51

Govardhana gives respect to animals, always with water, soft grass, and caves, and sometimes with bulbous roots too, which can be eaten by them on occasion, and to the cow herders, always with everything. In that regard, soft grass is for the sake of sitting for a picnic, and so forth.

The idea in the vocative *abalah* (girls; weak) is: “By our inability to do what the hill does, we are not even qualified for *dasya!* Talk about bad luck!” The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami.

Alternatively, *rama* denotes Krsna, by the derivation: *ramate sada kridayati iti ramah,* “He takes pleasure, meaning He always plays” or *ramayati sukhayati iti ramah,* “He makes one delight, i.e. He gives happiness.”52

Or Govardhana eminently gives pleasure *(pramodah = prakarsena modayati iti tatha sah)* to Krsna’s feet, which are *rama* in the same way, by its own touch. Govardhana is very soft: Its stones turn into butter balls at once when His lotus feet step on them. In that regard, it eminently gives pleasure in many ways: by warmth in the cold season, by coolness in the hot season, and so on. Moreover, *gana* signifies “the group of companions such as Sri Balarama and Sridama.”

Another interpretation of *rama-krsna-carana-sparasa-pramodah* is: “Govardhana has rapture by giving a deed, an amusement, to Krsna” (= *ramam jagan-manoramam yat krsnasya caranam acaranam viharah tasya sparsena sparsanena danena pramodah yasya sah).* Amara states: *visrananam vitaranam sparsanam,* “*Visranana, vitarana, sparsana,* \[and other words are synonyms of *dana* (giving)\]” (*Amara-kosa* 2.7.29). This means Govardhana is always enthusiastic to bring about His fun, in every way. Or it eminently gives pleasure by that touch. Or it delights Him, or it delights us, or it delights the whole world, on account of the effectuation of profuse bliss to all because, by facilitating His entertainment, Govardhana dispels all unhappiness, given that everyone can hear about them, and because of expanding the *seva.*

Another rendering of *rama-krsna-carana-sparasa-pramodah* is: “Govardhana, the great pleasure of whose touch is like the great pleasure of the touch of Krsna’s feet, which are *rama”* (= ramayoh krsna-caranayoh iva sparsa-pramodah yasya). By touching Govardhana, one accomplishes the bliss of touching Krsna’s feet because, since Govardhana is hari-dasa-varya, the excellence in it is like the excellence consisting of touching His feet, inasmuch as He constantly performs various pastimes of love here.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Though the talk is within a fellowship (gosthi), it is covered by another rasa in the same way, since they speak in this manner in two verses.

(Additions are underlined.) Ayam (this) is said because of directly pointing to it with the index finger, due to their residing in the vicinity of Sri Govardhana. He takes away (harati) unlimited sins and sorrows of the world, and the hearts of all, as is appropriate, and so He is Hari. He is renowned in the scriptures and in the world as its presiding deity. This hill is the best (varyah = sresthah) of His servants who have His nature.

Next by indicating the result they illustrate that Govardhana is the best: Pramoda means ‘eminent joy’ (pramodah = prakrstah modah = prakrstah harsah). It is characterized by a growth of grass, the condition of melting, a flow of water drops, etc., which are the natures of horripilation, perspiration, tears of bliss, and so on.

Regarding tanoti (it spreads, expands), the sense is: “It expands the honor being shown by everyone else.” By the word go (cow), other animals are included, as a partial indication. Paniya, in the plural, signifies beverages such as water, and honey. Suyavasa are soft grasses that promote nourishment and cause the production of milk. The long vowel in suyavasa is poetic license, owing to a conformity with the meter.

Alternatively, paniyasu-yavasa, which means: paniyam suvate ksaranti paniya-suvo nirjharah, ‘“cascades’, by the derivation: “they produce drinkable water, and so they are paniya-su.” Sometimes the reading is bhu. The sense of bhu is a beautiful place for sitting. Kandara means guhah (caves). The following, which are there, are partially indicated: jewels, beds, seats, lamps, mirrors, and so forth.

The idea in the vocative abalah is: “By our inability to do what the hill does, the good fortune of this kind of service cannot take place. Gosh, what bad luck!” The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami.

(From here, additions are not underlined.) Here also, there is the manifestation of another meaning, even when there is a concealment of their emotions, like before, in reference to: aksanvatam (10.21.7). For instance: Govardhana has pleasure by touching both feet of Krsna, who is lovely (rama-krsna-carana-sparasa-pramodah = ramah ramaniyah yah krsnah tasya caranayoh sparsena pramodah yasya sah), from the definition in Amara-kosa: ramo nila-caru-site trisu, “In all three genders, rama means nila (a dark color), caru (beautiful), and sita (white)” (Amara-kosa 3.3.140). It gives honor to both lotus feet (tayoh = tayoh caranayoh).

Alternatively: rama-krsna-carana-sparasa-pramodah means: tadrsa-krsna-caranayoh sparsa-pramodah yasmat, “Govardhana causes the great pleasure of the touch of both feet of Krsna, who is lovely,” inasmuch as it imparts coolness, etc., to its stones, in accordance with the season.

(Additions are underlined.) Or: ramam krida-rupam yat krsnasya caranam acaranam, tasya sparsena sparsanena danena pramodah yasya sah, “Govardhana, which has rapture by giving a deed, the form of an amusement, to Krsna.” Amara states: visrananam... (see above). This means Govardhana is always enthusiastic to bring about His fun.

Optionally: “By that, it makes Him, us and everyone enjoy.” Another rendering is: tadrsa-krsna-caranayoh iva sparsa-pramodah yasya, “Govardhana, the great pleasure of whose touch is like that of the touch of the feet of lovely Krsna.” By touching Govardhana, one accomplishes the bliss of touching Krsna’s feet because, since the excellence in it is like the excellence consisting of touching His feet, inasmuch as He constantly performs various pastimes of love here.

Given that it should be said: tasya. “\[It does an honor\] to Him,” tayoh. which means tayoh caranayoh (those two feet). is used because of high regard.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

On the side of the inability to conceal the nature, rama-krsna-carana-sparasa-pramodah connotes: ramanam ramah krida tad-yuktasya krsnasya caranayoh sparsena pramodah yasya, “Govardhana has rapture because of the touch of both feet of Krsna, who has an amusement (rama = ramana = krida) (“that by means of which there is pleasure”).”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Alas, sakhis! It was heard from Gargi’s mouth: “Without taking shelter of one of the greats, an inner longing never fructifies. Only Hari’s devotees are great, and of them, Sri Govardhana, the king of hills, is foremost,” so today let’s go see its presiding deity, Narayana, named Sri Hari-deva, after bathing in Manasa-Ganga, which is in that area. Certainly our elders will not object to this, and Krsna plays right there.” Deciding upon this arrangement, the girls, desiring to go forward to meet Him, their beloved, offer praise to Govardhana for the purpose of fulfilling their own desires, given that it fulfills the desires of Krsna and of His companions.

Hanta (alas) has the sense of vismaya (astonishment). “Of Hari’s servants, such as Narada, these three: Yudhisthira, Uddhava, and Govardhana, are the foremost Haridasas. Of them, only this hill is hari-dasa-varya—from the usage of the word hari-dasa in relation to Yudhisthira: hari-dasasya rajarse rajasuyam mahodayam, “while praising the Rajasuya, a grand success of Rajarsi, a servant of Hari” (10.75.27), in relation to Uddhava: krsnam samsmarayan reme hari- daso vrajaukasam, “Causing the remembrance of the Vrajavasis’ Krsna, the servant of Hari took pleasure” (10.47.56)—because (yat = yasmat) it has rapture, indicated by melting stones, etc., due to the touch of Rama’s and Krsna’s feet (rama-krsna-carana-sparasa- pramodah = rama-krsnayoh carana-sparsena pramodah yasya sah).”

Symbols on the feet—such as a flag, a lightning flash, and a elephant goad, by the stones’ obtainment of a similarity of attributes with mud when there is a touch of the feet—and tears, horripilation, etc., which correspond to waterfalls, a growth of grass, etc., can be understood as signs of rapture. Here the usage of the word rama is for the sake of concealing the mood. As a double meaning, from Amara-kosa: ramo nila-caru-site trisu, “In all three genders, rama means nila (a dark color), caru (beautiful), and sita (white)” (Amara-kosa 3.3.140), rama means ramaniya (lovely), which applies to Krsna. The gist of the vocative abalah (women, lit., ‘weak’) is: “for you who are under the control of your husbands, the only strength is to take shelter of it.”

“Because of this rapture (yat = yatah = yatah pramodad eva hetoh), it expands a worship, which gladdens Him (manam tanoti = tat-prasadanim pujam tanoti), unto both of Them (tayoh), who are with cows and with a multitude of friends (saha-go-ganayoh = saha gobhih ganena ca vartamanayoh) (ganena = sakhi-samuhena)—with what?—with drinking water, i.e. the water of cascades, which is nicely cool and fragrant, for padya, for acamaniya, and for drinking, and beverages, such as honey, mango juice, and pilu juice, which are for naivedya; with durva grass, for arghya, and grass (yavasa = trna), for the cows’ grazing.

The grass, the main ingredient in the production of milk, is nicely fragrant and very soft (su = sugandha, sukomala)—the long vowel in suyavasa is poetic license; or else the sense is “cascades”.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Other ladies speak with this mood: “Sakhis! Without taking shelter of a sattama (the highest transcendentalist), He, Nanda’s son, who is dear to the sats (transcendentalists, sadhus), is not obtained. He is Giriraja, so let’s go see him. We shall attain Him right there.”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Hanta has the sense of harsa (joy): “Wow, sakhis, Govardhana’s favor is the cause of Krsna’s favor. We should seek its blessing.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

How is it that the Pulindis turned out like this? Being in that way occurred because of the association of a devotee of the Lord. Here the gopis talk about the fact that Govardhana is a devotee of the Lord.

“This hill, Govardhana, is the best among Hari’s servants because it has intense joy in touching both lotus feet of Rama and of Krsna (rama-krsna-carana-sparasa-pramodah = rama-krsna-caranaravinda-sparse prakrstah modah yasya).” One who becomes endowed with bliss even in touching the path of bhakti is the best among those who belong to the Lord. Govardhana shows hospitality (manam tanoti = atithyam karoti) to both of Them with water and so on. Abalah is a vocative; this is being said: “All of us are unable to go there.”

**Annotation**

On the side of srngara-rasa, the implied meaning is Govardhana increases Krsna’s renown with paniya-su yavasa (wet grass), kandara (caves), and kanda-mula (the main things, which are like two bulbs). This is understood from the analogy: trnaih kupam ivavrtam, “like a well covered by grass” (Bhagavatam 3.31.40).

### 10.21.19

*ga gopakair anu-vanam nayator udara-*  
*venu-svanaih kala-padais tanu-bhrtsu sakhyah \|*  
*aspandanam gatimatam pulakas tarunam*  
*niryoga-pasa-krta-laksanayor vicitram \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

gah—cows; gopakaih—with cowherd boys (“with little cowherds”); anu-vanam—forest after forest; nayatoh—who are driving; udara— exalted; venu-svanaih—sounds of the flute; kala-padaih—which are sweet tones; tanu-bhrtsu—among those that have a body; sakhyah—O sakhis; aspandanam—immobility; gati-matam—of those who have mobility; pulakah—horripilation; tarunam—of trees; niryoga-pasa—by the ropes called niryoga; krta-laksanayoh—\[when both of Them,\] whose characteristic is done; vicitram—amazing.

*sakhyah! gopakaih (saha) anu-vanam gah nayatoh niryoga-pasa- krta-laksanayoh (rama-krsnayoh satoh, idam) vicitram (bhavati). kala-padaih udara-venu-svanaih (hetubhih) tanu-bhrtsu gatimatam (jantunam) aspandanam tarunam pulakah (ca bhavati iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Sakhis, when both of Them, recognized by niryoga ropes, are driving the cows with the cowherd boys from one forest to the next, there is a marvel: Because of the sounds, which are sweet tones, of the exalted flute, mobile beings become immobile and trees have goose bumps.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Hey sakhis! This, however, is utterly amazing (vicitram = idam tu aticitram). Of embodied beings (tanu-bhrtsu = saririsu), those that have locomotion (gatimatam = ye gatimantah, tesam) acquire immobility, an attribute of immobile things, and trees have horripilation, an attribute of mobile beings—because of the sounds, which are sweet notes (kala-padaih = madhura-padaih), of the great flutes (udara-venu-svanaih = maha-venu-nadaih) of Those two, Rama and Krsna, who are grazing (nayatoh = sancarayatoh) the cows in every forest (anu-vanam = vane vane) in the company of cow herders (gopakaih - gopaih saha)."

With niryoga-pasa and so on, the gopis characterize Rama and Krsna: niryoga-pasa-krta-laksanayoh, “Their trademark is done with niryogas, which are ropes for binding the feet—by the derivation: niryujyante gavah abhih, “Cows are ‘tied’53with these”— and with ropes for attracting cows that cannot be subjugated.”” (= niryujyante gavah abhih iti niryogah pada-bandha-rajjavah, adhrsya- gavam karsanarthah pasah ca, taih krtam laksanam cihnam yayoh).

This means They were resplendent with the beauty of loops of cowboys: the winding of a niryoga on the head and a rope positioned on a shoulder.54

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

In this verse they say, “Can the glory of Govardhana, fittingly called hari-dasa-varya, really be described? Even all moving beings and nonmoving things that abide in Vraja-bhumi, Vrndavana, are most fortunate.”

The suffix ka in gopakaih is expressive of affection. As a pun, the sense is “They protect.” Or ka means sukha (joy) and gopa-kaih modifies svanaih: “with sounds of the flute, because of which the cow herders have joy (= gopanam kam sukham yebhyah taih venu- svanaih)."

Anu-vanam means prati-vanam (each forest): All the forests in the region of Mathura are included. The sounds of the flute are great, i.e. loud, or they bestow bliss to all (udara = udaraih = mahadbhih uccaih sarvananda-pradaih va). Kala-padaih means: kalani madhura-svarani padam gitangani yesu, “\[the sounds of the flute,\] in which the aspects of the song are sweet tones.”

Or the respective natures of mobile beings and trees completely change also because of Their lotus feet, which have sweet indistinct sounds (kala-padaih = madhurasphuta-dhvani-yuktaih padaih ca padabjaih). The sweet indistinct sounds (kala) come from Their anklebells.

Mobile beings reach the state of being stunned (aspandanam = stabdhata): This is an attribute of immobile things. As a partial indication, the mention trees encompasses all immobile beings: They experience horripilation: this too is a partial indication; kampa (shaking) and other manifestations are to be understood. Thus, immobile beings acquire an attribute of mobile beings. That is a reversal, therefore it is amazing (vicitram = adbhutam). Or vicitram is an adjective of aspandanam. The sense is the immobility is quite distinct from anything seen the world. Vicitram can be inferred as an adjective of pulakah also, by carrying forward the word Vicitra and by changing its gender from neuter to masculine. Thus, the rise of everyone’s special prema is implied. The sight of that astonishing lovely attire of Theirs, also by the niryoga, should be inferred as yet another cause of becoming stunned and so on. Trees have a subtle vision. This is understood from Mahabharata: tasmat pasyanti padapah, “Therefore trees see.”

There is another rendering. In this verse they clearly say: “In addition to immobility and mobility, there are many kinds of transformations of spiritual love.” The term niryoga can be explained in various ways, and so niryoga-pasa-krta-laksanayoh means: nihsesena yogah sangamo yasmat, kimva nirgato yogah prema-sampad-virodhi nirvikalpa-samadhir yasmat, sa casau pasas ca prema-laksanah, saksat tad-anuktir duhkha-visesat, tasya krtam laksanam mohadina nipatadikam rodanadikam ca yabhyam.

“Mobile beings become stunned and trees have goose bumps due to the sweet flute sounds of Rama and Krsna, because of whom there are characteristics occasioned by the rope of love, a rope which is niryoga in the sense of either “incessant union occurs because of it” or “complete trance, obstructive to the wealth of prema, is gone because of it.”” The characteristics are: anubhavas such as falling and sattvika-bhavas such as crying, because of bewilderment and the like.

The substance is: “Alas (hanta), these mobile beings and immobile things are lucky. They see Him, whose attire, such as niryoga-pasa, is sweet. But in our case, even just seeing Him is very hard to come by. What a misfortune.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In this verse they say, “Can the glory of Govardhana, fittingly called hari-dasa-varya, really be described? Even all moving beings and nonmoving things that abide here are most fortunate.”

gah (cows): By this, being a bestower of joy to living entities that are in faraway locations is meant, in terms of being one who goes far, since those cows are innumerable. (But He does not care for us.)

anu-vanam (forest after forest): In addition to going far, He goes to various locations because of a difference of groves. Because of the cheating that goes on there, the participants lose their punya.

gopakaih (with cow herders): The suffix ka\[n\] is used in the sense of daya (compassion) on account of being objects of affection as His parivara (entourage; distant relatives). Consequently there is a pun: “They protect Sri Krsna... from a miserable, fearful place” (gopayanti = duhkha-bhaya-sthanat sri-krsnam raksanti). The drift is: “Only we do not have the qualification for that sort of prema- seva.”

nayatoh (of both of Them, who are leading): “In going to various areas, Their freedom can come about... but not in proximity to us. Darn.”

udara, which means udaraih (\[because of flute sounds,\] which are grand): He gives the highest bliss only to beings in those various areas.

venu (the flute): Its sounds are special: kala-padaih (in which the notes are sweet): The flute enchants by sweetness. Another reason is that the sound is indistinct. A listener thinks: “What is this signal?” By overwhelming the listeners with diverse moods in this fashion, a supereminence occurs. The definition is: dhvanau tu madhurasphute kale, “Only in regard to sound, kala means madhura (sweet) and asphuta (indistinct)” (Amara-kosa 1.7.2). Alternatively: kala-padaih means: nupura-kala-sabda-yuktaih padaih pada-viksepaih, “\[Mobile beings become stunned and trees have goose bumps\] because of footsteps that have the sweet, indistinct sound of anklebells.” This evokes the remembrance of His pastimes.

tanu-bhrtsu (of those who have bodies): Which embodied soul might not fall for that subjugation?

sakhyah (hey sakhis): “All of you too know this!”

aspandanam (immobility) signifies the absence of even a little motion.

gatimatam (of those who have movement), i.e. of those who have locomotion; or even of rivers, which always move by nature, “so what could be said about us if we were to travel so far?”

pulakas tarunam (the horripilation of trees) although they have no hair. Both the hairs and the horripilation are simultaneously understood by the tricky appearance of an outgrowth of burgeons. Therefore, kampa (shaking) too is somewhat indicated. As a result, there is also a reversal between the attributes of immobile things and those of mobile beings.

niryoga-pasa-krta-laksanayoh: Since any other rope is useless, given that all the cows behave nicely, niryoga-pasa means a rope called niryoga. It is a rope for binding the legs so that the calf which has a fickle nature clings to the left shank of a cow at the time of milking. The two of Them were krta-laksana, “They whose characteristic is done” by that rope. That is, They were recognized (krta-laksana = pratita) by the quality of topmost beauty, from Amara’s statement: gunaih pratite tu krta-laksanahata-laksanau, “Krta-laksana and ahata-laksana refer to an appearance by qualities” (Amara-kosa 3.1.10). Moreover, this implies that it is made of patta (fine cloth; silk; ligature), both ends of which are furnished with clusters of pearls. The rope too has resplendence above a turban and so on. Although the attire of a cowherd attracts the hearts of all, it is specifically understood only by those beautiful divine cowherd ladies. The attire, etc., which has a similarity with His area, subcaste, and age, greatly appeals to all.

vicitram (amazing): There is the bewilderment, out of aston¬ishment, of those who are His own, here and there. This word is to be syntactically linked in many clauses, in accordance with the suitability.

There is also an indicator of a feeling focused only on Krsna, as before. The sense is as follows. In this verse they say, “Aho, sakhis! Clearly, under the pretext of tending cows, He, while wandering in a forest with the group and with His brother, is perceived as if He were a cheat.” “Because of the sounds of the flute of the one who, between the two of Them (nayatoh = nayatoh tayoh madhye), is the best of all (udara = yah sarva-variyan, tasya), mobile beings (gatimatam = jangamanam) have become immobile and immobile beings (tarunam = sthavaranam ca) have goose bumps. The two of Them are driving the cows from one forest to the next (anu-vanam = vanad vanam) with the keepers (gopakaih = raksakaih saha), those who keep His yogurt, milk, and stolen articles; these persons are called prstha-pala (those who watch His back). Each of the two is distinguished by a rope called niryoga. Everyone knows that ropes are used by rogues for tying up the feet.”

What are the sounds of the flute like? kala-padaih, “their tones are indistinct and are captivating like an enchanting mantra.” “Therefore only the great flute player is the main cheat here. Others, however, are just His followers. Consequently you, like us, should not hear His flute, which has a bewitching spell, otherwise it is certain that your minds will be caught by those niryoga ropes.” In this way, the girls only mean to express the sad state of their own bewilderment.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Only Sri Krsna’s flute is understood from the modifier udara (great).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Here they say, “In addition, there should be no delay in going to that area, insofar as He, who follows cows, could vanish in another forest.” Regarding gopakaih, the suffix ka\[n\] has the sense of anukampa (compassion, endearment, pity),55therefore there is also a double meaning: they protect Krsna out of affection (gopayanti = krsnam snehat palayanti),56since every morning Sri Yasoda asks this of the boys.

The syntactical connection is: anu-vanam gas tayor nayatoh sator idam vicitram bhavati, “While both of Them are driving the cows forest after forest (anu-vanam = vane vane), this becomes amazing.” What is it? “Hey sakhis! Of embodied beings (tanu-bhrtsu = saririsu madhye), those that have locomotion (gatimatam = ye gatimantah, tesam) have immobility, an attribute of immobile entities, and trees have horripilation, an attribute of mobile beings—due to the sounds of the flute.”

Niryoga-pasa is a rope called niryoga. It is a rope for binding the neck of calves so that the calves which have a fickle nature cling to the left shank of a cow at the time of milking.

The two of Them were krta-laksana, “They whose characteristic is done” by that rope. This means They were renowned (krta- laksana = khyata), due to acquiring such a special beauty. Amara states: gunaih pratite... (see above).

Moreover, the rope is made of yellow patta (fine cloth; silk; ligature). Both ends of the rope are furnished with clusters of pearls. It is like a special ornament that clings to the turban. It is an indicator of being a cow herder. It is understood as an object that stupefies the minds of onlookers.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Niryoga-pasa is a rope called niryoga, by the derivation: niryujyante gavah anena iti niryogah, “Cows are ‘bound’ with this, and so it is called niryoga.” Both of Them had a characteristic done by that (niryoga-pasa-krta-laksanayoh = niryoga-pasena krtam cihnam yayoh).

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Anu-vanam means vanam vanam (to every forest): Sometimes They went to Vrndavana and sometimes They went to Bhandlravana, and so forth. The suffix ka in gopakaih has the sense of anukampa.

“Because of the sounds of the flute of the one who, out of Rama and Krsna, is udara... ” It is well-known that the sound of the flute is Sri Krsna’s. Niryoga-pasa means go-cchandana-rajju (a rope for covering cows). Although there is a similarity of attire, this is the attractiveness only of Krsna because He is paripurna.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“Because of great flute sounds (udara-venu-svanaih = maha-venu-ravaih hetubhih), in which the tones are indistinctly sweet (kala-padaih = kalani padam yesu taih = avyakta-madhura- sabdah yesu taih), of Rama and Krsna...”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Niryoga-pasa is called ksepana (sling; lasso).

**Annotation**

In this regard, in Hari-vamsa, in the context of diverse new pastimes, it is stated: vane sa viro gas caiva jagraha graha-vad vibhuh, “In the woodland, the Lord, who is a hero, also caught cows and treated them as capture” (Hari-vamsa 2.20.17). This is what cowboys do.

Moreover, by taking the definition of krta-laksana as gunaih pratita (recognized by qualities) (Amara-kosa), niryoga-pasa-krta- laksanayoh can mean: “\[of Those two,\] who are recognized by the rope of love, because of which yoga (nirvikalpa-samadhi) is gone (nir = nirgata).”

### 10.21.20

*evam-vidha bhagavato ya vrndavana-carinah \|*  
*varnayantyo mitho gopyah kridas tan-mayatam yayuh \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam-vidhah—which are of such kinds; bhagavatah—of the Lord; yah—which \[pastimes\]; vrndavana-carinah—who habitually wanders in Vrnda’s forest; varnayantyah—while describing; mithah—mutually; gopyah—the cowherd ladies; kriddh—the pastimes; tat-mayatam yayuh—attained the state of being imbued with Him.

*yah evam-vidhah vrndavana-carinah bhagavatah kridah (bhavanti), gopyah (tah ca) mithah varnayantyah tan-mayatam yayuh (iti).*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*gopyah vrndavana-carinah bhagavatah evam-vidhah (anyah api) yah kridah varnayantyah (babhuvuh), tan-mayatam yayuh.*

**While describing to one another such pastimes of the Lord, who wanders in Vrndavana, the gopis imbibed His nature.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*gopinam kamatah krsne nihsima-prema-sangamah \|*  
*katyayany-arcanodbhuta-tat- prasada-mahodayah \|\|*

**“Owing to the gopis’ love for Krsna, a meeting of boundless love took place. There was a great rise of His grace, evoked by the worship of Katyayani.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Here Sukadeva concludes by intending to signify this: “The ladies described more pastimes of this sort and of other kinds. How many of those can I narrate?”

The pastimes the girls described to one another were like this, meaning they enchant the world (evam-vidhah = idrsyah = jagan- mohinyah).
