The reason for that is: bhagavatah, “\[the pastimes\] of the Lord, who is revealing His infinite godly might in specific ways.” In addition: vrndavana-carinah (He roams Vrndavana), which portends: “He has fun at will” (= svacchanda-viharinah). Or, in reference to vrnddvana-carinah, they described only the amusements which pertain to that place, not His amusements when He wanders within the village, because of the occurrence of their good fortune by seeing the Lord there. In the other reading, viharinah, the sense is the same.

“While depicting all the amusements, they reached the state of being imbued with the Lord (tan-mayatam = bhagavan-mayatam)." This means they forever became dedicated to glorifying Him, hearing about Him, and so forth. Or they constantly had the bliss of feeling Him. Or they reached the condition of being involved in the fun (tan-mayatam = krida-mayatam), that is, they forever sported with Him.

In regard to the pronoun tat (in tan-mayatam): As before there is no direct mention of His name, on account of a special heartache by the burning of the fire of love. The sense is they became greatly pained by the continuous increase of a mass of prema. As regards gopyah (gopis), that is their very nature. Thus by the increase of the wealth of their prema, their good fortune, which exceeds all, is implied.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

He concludes in this fashion: “They described many pastimes (kridah = lilah) in this way, yet how many can I tell?” The pastimes were like this, i.e. they enchant the world (evam-vidhah = idrsyah = jagan-mohinyah). The reason for that is: bhagavatah, “of the Lord, who is revealing His infinite sweetness.” Here, it is clearly implied that He has that sort of eternal pastimes, by the sense of tacchilya (habit) in vrnddvana-carinah, and that those ladies always have those types of emotion. However, in the reading vrndavana- viharinah (Of Him, who habitually has fun in Vrndavana), the sense is this is His special quality.

The prose order is: tasya tah sarva eva krida varnayantyah satyas tan-mayatam yayuh, “While describing all His pastimes, they reached the state of being possessed by pastimes (tan-mayatam = krida-mayatam = tad-avistatam).”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Tan-mayatam means “being possessed by His pastimes” (= tasya tan-mayatam = tasya krida-mayatam).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He concludes. “The gopis got (yayuh = prapuh) a profuseness of pastimes (tan-mayatam = tat-pracuratam = krida-pracuryam), which were of such kinds, and other pastimes too, of the Lord, who wanders in Vrndavana, and which they were describing.” This means they went to meet their beloved and had such pastimes.

Or bhagavato yah signifies bhagavato ’yah, where ayah modifies the girls: “The gopis are going to a rendezvous,” by the derivation: ayante abhisaranti iti ayah, “They are going, i.e. going to a rendezvous, and so they are aya." The gist is: “The gopis, going to a rendezvous, got (yayuh = prapuh) the Lord’s amusements of this kind, that is, amusements in which He is the doer and those in which He is the object, in a secret place (mithah = rahasi)." The sense is they had fun and made Him have fun.” Amara states: mitho ’nyonyam rahasy api, “Mithas means anyonyam (mutually) and rahas (secret place)” (Amara-kosa 3.3.255). After that, “they reached the state of oneness with the love games and got the bewilderment of transcendental ecstasy (tan-mayatam = krida-tadatmyam ananda-mohanam ca prapuh)." This explanation must be accepted, for in an upcoming section it is said tvayabhiramitah (we were sexually enjoyed by You), in the verse that begins yarhy ambujaksa (10.29.36)

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

The syntactical connection is: vrndavana- carino bhagavato ya evam-vidha kridas ta varnayantyo gopyas tan- mayatam yayuh, “While describing such kinds of pastimes of the Lord, who wanders in Vrndavana, the gopis attained a mental absorption in that (or they became possessed by Him) (tan-mayatam = tad-avesam).”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Bhagavatah denotes “of Sri Krsna,” but not “of both of Them.” Mithah means either rahasi (privately; in a private place) or anyonyam (mutually). “They attained the state of being imbued with Him” means they had a very blissful meeting by a inner vision right then.

## Chapter 22 - Krsna Steals the Gopis’ Clothes

### 10.22.1

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*hemante prathame masi nanda-vraja-kumarikah \|*  
*cerur havisyam bhunjanah katyayany-arcana-vratam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah uvaca—Sri Suka said; hemante—in winter; prathame masi—in the first month; nanda-vraja—of Nanda's village; kumarikah—virgin girls (young unmarried women); ceruh— performed; havisyam—food fit for offering in a fire sacrifice (“fit for an oblation”); bhunjanah—while eating; Katyayani-arcana-vratam— the vow of worshiping Katyayani.

*sri-sukah uvaca—hemante prathame masi nanda-vraja-kumarikah havisyam bhunjanah katyayany-arcana-vratam ceruh.*

**Перевод:**

**Sri Suka said: In winter, in the first month, while eating havisya the virgins girls of Nanda’s village performed the vow of worshiping Katyayani.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*dvavimse gopa-kanyanam vastraharana-lilaya \|*  
*varam dattva gatah krsno yajna-salam itiryate \|\|*

**“In the twenty-second chapter, it is said that after giving a boon, as the pastime of stealing the garments of virgin gopis, Krsna went to the sacrificial grounds.”**

**10.22.1**

“In the first month” means “in Margasirsa” (mid-November to mid- December).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

After mentioning the amusements in the rains and in autumn, now, from this verse to the one that ends with vrajam (10.22.28) he talks about an amusement, obtained in sequence, at the time of winter.

They are girls in the village of Nanda the king of cowherds (nanda-vraja-kumarikah = nandasya gopa-rajasya vraje kumarikah). This means they are qualified in every way for marrying the Lord. For the most part, the suffix ka has the sense of alpa (little) with the intent to express childhood. Or the suffix ka is used without changing the meaning.

Havisyam means: haimantika-sita-dhanyadi-sahitam gavya- dadhi-dugdhadikam, “cow’s yogurt, milk, etc., accompanied with white grains, etc., existing in winter.”57

Katyayani is Parvati, Siva’s sweetheart, the topmost Vaisnavi. The girls performed an observance related to her, or they performed a vow that was the form of a worship of her (katyayany-arcana- vratam = tasyah arcana-vratam niyamam, arcana-rupam va vratam).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Having described, on the occasion of autumn, the purva anuraga of married women, on the occasion of winter he talks about a procedure which relates to the purva anuraga of virgin girls, from this verse to the one that ends with vrajam (10.22.28).58

These two groups of women are mentioned in Sri Hari-vamsa: yuvatir gopa-kanyas ca ratrau sankalya kala-vit, **“Thinking highly of His fresh youth, He who knows when it’s time invited both the young women and the virgin girls and took pleasure in being with them”** (Hari-vamsa 2.20.18).

Someone might object: “In the verse that begins: tata arabhya nandasya, **“Since then, O king, Nanda’s Vraja, endowed with all types of excellence due to qualities of its own in terms of being Hari’s abode, became a place for Rama’s pastimes”** (10.5.18), it was established that Sri Radhika and others are the foremost Ramas. Also with yad-vanchaya srir lalanacarat tapah, “With a desire for it, Sri, a lady, performed austerities” (10.16.36), it was shown that Sri Vrajendra-nandana is their sole lover. It will also be illustrated with: nayam sriyo ’nga, **“While dancing in the Rasa festival, the cowherd girls got their wish when their throats were held by His pole-like arms. This favor was never bestowed on Laksmi, though she is exceedingly fond of Him, nor on the women of heaven, whose radiance has the scent of lotuses, so how could it possibly be bestowed on other women?”** (10.47.60). The same point was strenghtened with: damodaradhara-sudham api gopikanam, “The flute enjoys the nectar of Damodara’s lips although that nectar belongs to us gopikas” (10.21.9). It will also be said: krsna-vadhvah, “Krsna’s wives” (10.33.7) in the context of the Rasa. In the Agama scriptures, the method of revering Him, who is with His eternal beloveds, who are untouched by others, is enjoined. In Gautamiya, in the explanation of His name in relation to ten-syllable mantra, the conclusion was made by Narada: He is the only husband of the gopikas. In Brahma-samhita, the conclusion is ascertained in the same way, with: sriyah kantah kantah parama-purusah, “The ladyloves are Sris, the lover is the topmost Purusa” (5.56). And in Tapani sruti, the same is directly heard: sa vo hi svami bhavati, “He is the husband of all of you” (Gopala-tapani Upanisad 2.22). In that way, with yad-dhamartha-suhrt-priyatma-tanaya, “these cowherd village residents, whose homes, wealth, friends, beloveds, children, life force, and thoughts are for Your sake” (10.14.35), their fathers do not believe in giving them, who are solely fit for Sri Krsna, to a man other than Him. Should such a gift occur, even living, which rests only on Him, is inconceivable, as in the case of Sri Rukmini’s statement beginning from: jahyam asun vrata-krsan sata-janmabhih syat, “I shall relinquish my life airs, which will have become weakened by vows throughout one hundred lifetimes” (10.52.43). Therefore how do you justify your statement that some gopis were married to men other than Krsna?”

The reconciliation is this: By the proof of arthapatti (presumption: the presumption of a fact that is otherwise inexplicable) of the meanings in those various texts, which cannot be explained otherwise, the marriage of those gopis was false and, by means of Maya, took place by the lila-sakti. Everyone, including the brides, their fathers, and all other residents of the village, were confounded. Still, the brides too decided to stay alive, by hoping to have only Krsna as a husband. This hope was a subconscious tendency inherent in the nature.

Further, this is obtained: The wives’ bodily connection with any man other than Krsna was prevented by the same Maya by her making forms similar to theirs. For example, it will be made into a partial indication: nasuyan khalu krsnaya mohitas tasya mayaya, manyamanah sva-parsva-sthan svan svan daran vrajaukasah, **“The cowherd men did not resent Krsna: Bewildered by His power of illusion, they thought that their respective wives were at their sides”** (10.33.38). This and that were just for the sake of increasing the longing of those ladies, as in: yathadhano labdha-dhane vinaste tac-cintayanyan nibhrto na veda, **““But I, My dear friends, do not even reciprocate with people who are kind to Me, because My intent is to see what they are really made of. Their engrossment becomes like that of a man who has lost his wealth and is so absorbed in thought of it that he is not interested in anything else”** (10.32.20). In this regard also, the twofold classification as the varieties of married women and virgin women is for the purpose of enhancing the wonderment of the fun of love. This is the general idea. It will be specifically proven on the occasion of the Rasa.

Now we are following the subject matter. They are girls in Nanda’s village (nanda-vraja-kumarikah = sri-nandasya vraje kumarikah). Due to such a mention with indifference, the girls which are not part of His family are meant. In the other reading, nanda-gopa-kumarikah, the sense is the same: sriman-nandasya ye gopah tesam kumarikah, “the girls of the cowherds of Nanda.” That was stated as follows: yuvatir gopa-kanyas ca, “He invited both the young women and the virgin girls” (Hari-vamsa 2.20.18) (also quoted above). The suffix ka\[n\] either has the sense of alpa (little) or suggests the sense of alpa. Katyayani is Vaisnavi, Sakti. The girls performed a vow which was the worship of her (katyayany-arcana- vratam = tasyah arcana-rupam vratam).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*dvavimse candika-puja gopibhir vasasam hrtih \|*  
*samlapo vara-danam tu stutih krsnena kirtyate \|\|*

**“In the twenty-second chapter, there is the worship of Candika by gopis, the theft of clothes, a friendly conversation, the bestowal of a boon, and a praise eminently verbalized by Krsna.”**

**10.22.1**

Having described the passion (anuraga) of married ladies for Krsna in autumn, now, to reiterate that, although the girls in this context are not married, Suka talks about the worship they did to Devi in the winter only by a popular custom, with the desire to attain Krsna. In the case of these gorls too, the mood of being a lover of Krsna is eternally established.

“In the first month” means “in Margasirsa.” This twofold variety of Krsna’s ladyloves is seen in Sri Hari-vamsa, Sri Visnu Purdna, Sri Brahma Purdna, and so on, such as: yuvatir gopa-kanyas ca ratrau sankalpa-kala-vit... (see above) (Hari-vamsa 2.20.18).

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

*dvavimse ’bhyarcita durga kanyabhir vasasam hrtih \|*  
*krsnena vara-danam ca taru-stotram ca kathyate \|\|*

**“In the twenty-second chapter, this is told: Durga was worshiped by virgin girls, and a theft of garments, the bestowal of a boon and a eulogy in a tree were done by Krsna.**

**10.22.1**

Although these girls are His eternal ladyloves, there was a worship of Katyayani only by a worldly tradition. She who is mentioned as para sakti in Narada Pancaratra, beginning from: janaty eka para kantam, should be understood as Katyayani.59

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Having described the passion of married girls, he talks about the passion of unmarried girls. It happened in Margasirsa. Just because of this pastime, this month became His favorite, therefore He will say: masanam margasirso ’ham, “Of months, I am Margasirsa” (Bhagavatam 11.16.27) (Gita 10.35).

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

Havisyam means havisyannam, “boiled rice (or boiled barley) fit for a sacrificial offering” (with ghee and without spice).

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Having mentioned some of the Lord’s autumnal deeds which were reiterated by gopis to one another, now, in seven chapters he, who wanted to narrate some, minutely describes some winter deeds of the Lord, who is in the age of pauganda, by the logic of a lion’s glance (taking a look back at them). Havisyam bhunjanah (while eating havisya) portends niyataharah (their food is regulated).

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

Havisyam means havisyannam, i.e. nivaran (wild rice).

### 10.22.2-3

*aplutyambhasi kalindya jalante codite ’rune \|*  
*krtva pratikrtim devim anarcur nrpa saikatim \|\|*  
*gandhair malyaih surabhibhir balibhir dhupa-dipakaih \|*  
*uccavacais copaharaih pravala-phala-tandulaih \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

aplutya—after plunging; ambhasi—in the water; kalindyah—of the Kalindi; jala-ante—at the edge of the water; ca—and; udite arune— when dawn was rising; krtva—after making; pratikrtim—a replica; devim—Devi (“the goddess”); anarcuh—they worshiped; nrpa—O king; saikatim—made of sand;

gandhaih—with fragrant substances; malyaih—with flowers (or with garlands); surabhibhih—fragrant; balibhih—with propitiatory offerings; dhiipa-dipakaih—with incense and lamps; ucca-avacaih— great and small (diverse) (“high and lower”); ca—and; upaharaih— with presents (food); pravala—with new leaves (or shoot, sprouts); phala—fruits; tandulaih—and rice (unbroken).

*nrpa! arune udite (sati, tah gopyah) kalindyah ambhasi aplutya (kalindyah) jalante saikatim pratikrtim krtva ca (tarn) devim gandhair malyaih surabhibhih balibhih dhupa-dipakaih uccavacaih upaharaih pyavala-phala-tandulaih ca anarcuh.*

**Перевод:**

**When dawn was approaching, O king, they immersed themselves in the water of the Kalindi, made a sandy idol at the brink of the water, and worshiped Devi with aromatic substances, fragrant flowers, propitiatory offerings, incense, lamps, diverse esculent presentations, new leaves, fruits, and rice.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

In three and a half verses, he talks about the method of it. Ambhasy aplutya means they immersed, i.e. bathed, in terms of being clotheless in the water, which was most purifying and cool. With this, and with jalante (at the brink of the water) and so on, the hardhip in executing the vow is shown. The word kalindyah (of Kalindi) is connected both with the previous word (ambhasi) and with the next one (jalante).

“When the sun’s charioteer—or when the sun—was rising” (arune udite = surya-sarathau, surye va, udite sati). With regard to the vow, it’s understood that the immersion occurred just before sunrise. “They made an idol (pratikrtim = pratimam) made of sand (saikatim = baluka-mayim),” for the complete fulfilment of a special wish before long.

The gist of the vocative nrpa (O king) is: “For the sake of Sri Krsna, even she was worshiped in that way by those ladies, though they are worthy of being worshiped in the world. Lo, behold the greatness of determination!”

**10.22.3**

Surabhih (fragrant) can be linked with everything, according to the suitability. The plural is because of the multiplicity of gandha and so on. Balibhih (with propitiatory offerings) means vastra-bhusana-naivedyady-upacaraih (with articles for a formal worship, such as garments, ornaments, and food): He mentions them, beginning from pravala (new leaves; sprouts). Here the broken order is due to those ladies’ forgetfulness of the order since their hearts were stolen by Sri Krsna. Or Badarayani transgressed the order, owing to a high enthusiasm for narrating their vow.

Another explanation is as follows. Balibhih means pujopakaranaih (with subsidiary articles of formal worship). In regard to gandhaih and so on: The quality of the refinement, etc., of those various ones is intended to be expressed. And after that, upaharaih means naivedyadibhih (with edible offerings, etc.). In the end, the rest, starting from pravala, is for the purpose of nirajana (waving a lamp before a deity). Uccavacaih (great and small, ‘high and low’) (diverse) is an adjective of everything.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

While illustrating the way their passion for Him took shape, to also enlighten people who want to do it he talks about the method of it, in three and a half verses. Of those verses, this text is one unit of two verses. With ambhasi and so forth, hardhip in executing a vow in winter is shown. It was at the brink of the water of Kalindi, that is, at a ghat of Vraja famous even today by the name ghatta-vasini devi.

Arune means surya-sarathau (when the sun’s charioteer). ‘Devi’ is Katyayani. Saikatim pratikrtim krtva (after making a sandy idol) denotes: tad-abhinnatvena pratisthapya, “after consecrating it as nondifferent from her.” Saikatim (sandy) is because it was the means of accomplishing the goal before long.

The gist of the vocative nrpa (O king) is: “Although they hadn’t yet reached yauvana (youth), they worshiped with this sort of raga. Ponder over their condition of being bewildered by Sri Krsna.”

**10.22.3**

Surabhih (fragrant) can be linked with everything, according to the suitability. The plural is because of the multiplicity of each one. Balibhih (with propitiatory offerings) means vastra-bhusana-naivedyady-upacaraih (with articles for a formal worship, such as garments, ornaments, and food). They were great and small (uccavacaih), and there were others too, of diverse kinds: He mentions them, beginning from pravala. Here the broken order is due to the ladies’ forgetfulness of the order since their hearts were stolen by Krsna. Or it is because of Sri Badarayani’s confusion in narrating that event.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Balibhih means vastra-bhusana- naivedyady-upacaraih.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Uccavacaih means nana-vidhaih vastradibhih (with garments, etc., of diverse kinds). Upaharaih means naivedyaih (with edible offerings). Pravalaih signifies: vidrumaih pallavaih ca (with corals and with shoots). Medini states: pravalo ’stri kisalaye vina-dande ca vidrume, “Pravala, which is not feminine, means kisalaya (shoot, bud), vina-danda (the neck of a lute), and vidruma (coral)” (Medini-kosa, la-trikam 107).

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Arune udite stands for arune udite sati and signifies “at the time of dawn.” Malyaih means puspaih (with flowers). Balibhih means puja-sadhanaih (with means of accomplishing a formal worship). Upaharaih means naivedyaih.

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

Gandhaih (with aromatic substances) means “with sandalwood paste and so on.” Malyaih means puspaih (with flowers). Balibhih denotes: yan agre vidhuya pranamah kriyate taih nalikeradibhih, “with items such as a coconut, etc. Offering obeisance is done after placing such items in front.”

**Annotation**

Regarding the order of a formal worship, as a guideline the following is the sequence of the sixteen offerings in a formal worship (sodasopacara): asanam (seat), svagatam (welcome), padya (for rinsing the feet), arghya (water mixed with specific items, used as a greeting), acamanam (water for sipping), madhuparka (a mix of ghee, honey, and sugar, and sometimes also yogurt and milk), punar-acamanam (again, water for sipping), snanam (bath), vastram (cloth), alankara (ornaments), gandha (scents, i.e. candana, karpura, aguru), puspa (flowers), dhupa (incense), dipam (lamp), naivedyam (succulent food offering), pranama (offering obeisances, including vandana, prayers).

Some devotees offer malya (a garland) before vandana. Dvadasopacara consists of: asanam, svagatam, padya, arghya, acamanam, madhuparka, punar-acamanam, gandha, puspa, dhupa, dipam, and naivedyam. Dasopacara is: asanam, svagatam, padya, arghya, acamanam, gandha, puspa, dhupa, dipam, and naivedyam. Pancopacara is: gandha, puspa, dhupa, dipam, and naivedyam. For more details, consult Hari-bhakti-vilasa 11.127-140.

### 10.22.4

*katyayani maha-maye maha-yoginy adhisvari \|*  
*nanda-gopa-sutam devi patim me kuru te namah \|*  
*iti mantram japantyas tah pujam cakruh kumarikah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

Katyayani—O Katyayani; maha-maye—O Maha-maya (or O you whose magic is great); maha-yogini—O you who have great mystic powers; adhisvari—O overlord; nanda-gopa-sutam—the son of the cowherd named Nanda; devi—O goddess; patim—husband; me— my; kuru—make; te namah—obeisances to you; iti—(marks the end of the quotation); mantram japantyah—while muttering the mantra; tah—those; pujam cakruh—did a formal worship; kumarikah— virgin girls.

*“katyayani! maha-maye! maha-yogini! adhisvari! devi! (tvam) nanda-gopa-sutam me patim kuru. te namah” iti (etam) mantram japantyah tah kumarikah pujam cakruh.*

**Перевод:**

**“Those virgin girls did a formal worship while uttering this mantra at a low voice: “O Katyayani, O Maha-maya, O great yogini, O lady overlord, O Devi, kindly make the son of the cowherd named Nanda my husband. I offer my respects to you.””**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Each girl requested her while implying the following with the vocatives beginning from Maha-maya: “Nothing is impossible to you.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“O Maha-maya!” means “O you who are a form of the Lord’s potency of sat-cid-ananda!” The sense is: “You are able to give all powers to us too. We are qualified for attaining Sri Krsna.” “But He doesn’t require any wife here.” To that they say, “O great yogini!” This means: “Although it is hard to come by, you can easily make it happen.” "But I fear Maha-Laksmi.”

They respond: adhisvari. “On account of being fully endowed with unlimited aisvarya, you are much more fearless than that.” In case she were to retort, “Then all of you should worship only Him,” they say: devi. The sense is: “O you who are shining with exclusive devotional service to Him.” The substance is: Only worshiping those who are dearest to Him is better than directly worshiping Him, in a formal way. The purport is: “Our inner longing can be completely fulfilled by you in every way.”

Nanda-gopa-sutam means: nandah ca asau gopah ca iti tasya sutam kumaram, “the son, i.e. the little boy, of he who is Nanda and is a cowherd.” This is implied: “We, virgin girls of cowherds, are fit for being His wives.” Alternatively, go-pa means bhu-pa (king): This means: asmakam raja (our king). The implied meaning is Krsna is hard to get. Still, “Make Him our husband (patim = svaminam).” The capability in that regard was already pointed out. Or, nanda- gopa-sutam is the cause of requesting Him as a husband, since the amusements, etc., in the attire of a cowherd steal the heart. Thus, the gopis want Krsna to always remain that way.

Me means mama (my): It’s inferred that, due to fearing the possibility that He might have cowives, all the girls, one by one, requested within their hearts that this situation be avoided.

There is another interpretation: This ancient mantra, which already existed that way, was seen by the great sage Sri Narada and others, so enough of a special imagination for that sake. This mantra had been seen by those same girls; Some say so; because, in accordance with a text in Padma Purdna, in a previous life, during the descent of Sri Raghunatha, those girls were Rsis.

Mantram denotes etam mantram (this mantra). Since there was no other mantra then, by the reiteration of pujam cakruh (they did a formal worship) the idea that they had another desire is repudiated.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

This is one verse of six lines. Regarding Katyayani: Because of having a prakasa in a lineage of that sage, being one who bestows a great dharma is implied.60

“O Maha-maya!” means “O you who are a form of a great potency of the Lord!” The sense is: “You are able to give us too a power adequate for fulfilling our desire. In case she were to reply, “There is some difficulty in this,” they say: maha-yogini, “O you who have the ability to make the impossible possible” (= durghata-ghatana-samarthe). “All of you should worship some other presiding deity.” They respond to her, who is testing their dedication to herself: adhisvari. The idea is: “There is no deity above you.”

Nanda-gopa-sutam means: sriman-nanda-raja-kumaram. This is a specification whose foundation is a conformity with their own mood. The implication is that He comes across as the only one worthy of being chosen as the husband. Here, nanda is the direct mention of the name of a very honorable person. The modifier gopa is due to suspecting that otherwise those words could mean something else.

“To obtain Sri Krsna, all of you should worship only Him.” They respond: “O you who are familiar with the mojo of good fun!” (devi = krida-rasabhijne). The sense is: “Requesting Him directly for the sake of Him is not conducive to Rasa. You already know this.”

The singular in me (my) is because each girl did a separate low utterance. Mantram denotes etam mantram (this mantra). Therefore this mantra, which bestows Sri Krsna as a husband, already existed.

Moreover, it should be thought that this Devi is svarupa-sakti— she is not the external potency, the cause of the world—because the former is one with the Lord, for instance: na visnuna vina devi na harih padmajam vina, “Devi is not without Visnu. Hari is not without Laksmi” (Hayasirsa Pancaratra, quoted in Bhagavat- Sandarbha 99.2), and because the latter is insignificant, due to depending on her, on account of texts such as: yasyarhsamsamsa- bhagena visvotpatti-layodayah, “The origination, development, and merging of the universe occur on account of a portion of a portion of a portion of a portion of Yours” (Bhdgavatam 10.85.31), due to the obtainment of that sort of differentiation in these two verses of Visnu Purdna:

*yatita-gocara vacam manasam cavisesana \|*  
*jnani-jnana-paricchedya vande tam isvarim param \|\|*  
*sarva-bhutesu sarvatman ya saktir apara tava \|*  
*gunasraya namas tasyai sasvatayai suresvara \|\|*

**“O Soul of all, O God of gods, obeisances to that potency, the inferior one, of Yours, which is the shelter of the gunas and is perpetual. I praise her, Para, the scope of whom is beyond words and minds, who cannot be materially described, who is to be accurately determined through the knowledge of knowledgeable persons, and who belongs to the Lord.” (Visnu Purdna 1.19.76-77)**

For example, in Sri Narada Pancaratra, in the conversation between Sruti and Vidya:

*janaty eka para kantam saiva durga tad-atmika \|*  
*ya para parama saktir maha-visnu-svarupini \|\|*  
*yasya vijnana-matrena paranam paramatmanah \|*  
*muhurtad deva-devasya praptir bhavati nanyatha \|\|*  
*ekeyam prema-sarvasva-svabhava gokulesvari \|*  
*anaya sulabho jneya adi-devo ’khilesvarah \|\|*  
*asya avarika saktir maha-mayakhilesvari \|*  
*yaya mugdham jagat sarvam sarve dehabhimaninah \|\|*

**“She who is the highest supreme potency and has the nature of Maha-Visnu is Durga. She, unique and transcendental, knows the lover and is of His nature. Obtaining the Paramatma of transcendental entities, the god of gods, after a moment occurs merely by understanding her, not otherwise. She, Gokulesvari, is unparalleled. She has the nature of those for whom prema is all in all. The primeval God, the Lord of all, is understood by and is easily attainable by her. Maha-maya, the goddess of all, due to whom the whole world is bewildered and everyone has the conceit of being a material body, is her covering potency.”**

Consequently, only the first one is known as the presiding deity of the eighteen-syllable mantra, and so on. Confusion takes place by a similarity of names such as Durga and Maha-maya. Alternatively, the mode can be as follows: The third line of this mantra (nanda- gopa-sutam devi) is linked with a name of their dear one (devi patim can mean devi-patim). Because of that, since Vraja has pastimes that are like worldly pastimes, only the worship of Maya is obtained, and so is the play of the merriness of their prema, the highest. Likewise, the upasana as well is done only with love. In that way, obtaining Him is not secured by a worship in that manner. It should be discerned thus.

In this regard, some scholars who consider themselves wholly devoted and think differently on this topic do not have a whiff of the scent of a connection with the scent of the prema of those who belong to Him. In every instance, only pure love for the Lord is the goal of human life. Only all the upasanas related to no other deity but Him are the very means to attain Him. Such is the philosophical conclusion in Srimad Bhdgavatam. And that is proven in relation to those girls and is the most prominent of all. What is the use of considering a sadhana? That prema, the love which is the topmost achievement, induces the experience of exclusive sweetness, by causing ananya-bhakti to be set in motion. By the experience of supreme godhood, however, it is only mixed, out of reverence. And only by prema is the Lord made submissive, not by that. For example, in nemam virincah and so on (10.9.20), in ittham satam and so on (10.12.11), and in nayam sriyo ’nga and so forth (10.47.60), only the divine Vrajavasis are praised as being above all. In the same way, here it is said: nanda-gopa-sutam, but not sri-bhagavantam (Krsna, God). Consequently, this indeed is those girls’ play of pure sweet love. It is not something else. This is established as being above all.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Katyayani is the potency called Vaisnavi. The mantra is in this manner, meaning it already existed. In that regard, if the mode is that there should be a link of the name of the desired one (patim) with the third line of the verse (nanda-gopa-sutam devi), then it is only a worship of Maya as a pastime like a worldly pastime, but if that too was established earlier, then this is only a worship of svarupa-sakti.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“O Katyayani! Make the son of Nanda- gopa my husband.” Katyayani might argue: “With the verb kuru (make), why do you attribute independence in that matter to me? I can only inspire your parents for that sake. Therefore you should say either karaya (cause to make) or dehi (give).” Suspecting this, in the manner an option, a girl says: “Great yogini! Union with Him can be quickly brought about by you, but not with the commotion of the intervention of parents, because we, who have an intense longing, cannot tolarate a delay and because Krsna is not eligible for marriage since He still has not been initiated by a guru.” The sense of “O Devi” is: “Make Him my husband only and exclusively by the Gandharva style of marriage, without a foremost marriage.” The gist of adhisvari (O lady overlord) is: “Nothing is impossible to you in that regard.”

“But how will the touch of Krsna’s body, which you desire, be nicely accomplished, given that your parents don’t know that you think of Krsna as your husband?” Therefore the girl says: “O Maha¬maya! By Maya, bewilder my parents so that my marriage with another cowherd will never be arranged by them and so that the secret of my union with Krsna’s limb cannot be known.”

Or devi patim denotes devi-patim, which means: divyati kridati devayati kridayati iti va devi sa ca asau patih ca iti tam, tadrsa- patitvam vivaham vind eva siddhyati, “Make the son of Nanda-gopa a husband who has fun (devi = devi = divyati = kridati), or a husband who is causing fun (devi = devi = devayati = kridayati),61that is, bring about that sort of husbandhood, but only without a marriage.” The drift is: “When I will be married to another cowherd, I will not be at a loss.” Thus each girl uttered the mantra after severally considering each meaning of the mantra.

She who was venerated by them is only Yogamaya, who is a function of cit-sakti and is the svarupa, but not the external Maya. That is said in Narada Pancaratra, in the conversation between Sruti and Vidya: janaty eka para... (see above). Therefore, in the Agama: sarvesu krsna-mantresu durgadhisthatr-devata, “In all mantras about Krsna, Durga is the presiding deity.” Only Yogamaya, whose svarupa is transcendental existence (suddha-sattva); who is a function of cit-sakti; who is Krsna’s sister; and whose designation is ekanamsa, is the presiding deity of the mantra. Indeed, only she was venerated by these girls. It is to be understood that the confusion of people takes place by a similarity of names such as Durga and Maha-maya. Since Vraja has pastimes that are like worldly pastimes, there is no fault in revering Maya. In this regard, some persons who consider themselves wholly devoted and who think differently on this topic, do not even have a whiff of a scent of a connection of a scent of the prema of those who belong to Him. This is from Sri Vaisnava-tosani.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“O Katyayani!” That is, “O you who became manifest in the lineage of that sage! O you who bestow the topmost dharma!” (Katyayani = tan-muni-vamsa-prakasike = parama-dharma-datri). “Make the son of the king named Nanda (nanda-gopa-sutam = nanda-namnah rajnah sutam) my husband (me patim = me pani-grahakam)." \[...\] The vocative devi portends: iyam eka krida sampadyatam, “This one amusement should be brought about.”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

The name Maha-maya means: mahati maya yasyah sa, “she whose magic is great.”

### 10.22.5

*evam masam vratam ceruh kumaryah krsna-cetasah \|*  
*bhadrakalim samanarcur bhuyan nanda-sutah patih \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam—in this way; masam—for a month; vratam—the vow; ceruh— performed; kumaryah—the virgin girls; krsna-cetasah—whose hearts are for Krsna (or whose minds are on Krsna); bhadrakalim samanarcuh—they properly worshiped Bhadrakali; bhuyat nanda- sutah—May Nanda’s son become; patih—the husband.

*kumaryah krsna-cetasah evam masam vratam ceruh. nanda-sutah (asmakam) patih bhuyat (iti sankalpya tah) bhadrakalim samanarcuh.*

**Перевод:**

**The virgin girls, whose hearts were for Krsna, performed the vow for one month in this way. They worshiped Bhadrakali: “May Nanda’s son become the husband.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Suka expounds on their being krsna-cetas (their hearts are for Krsna): bhuyan nanda-sutah patir ity anarcuh, “They worshiped (samanarcuh = anarcuh) in this way: “May Nanda’s son become the husband.””

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Suka speaks the verse with the following intention: “The result of their endeavor was nicely accomplished in a very short time.” Masam signifies: ekam margasirsam vyapya, “for the duration of one Margasirsa.” Owing to being a vibhuti of the Lord: masanam margasirso ’ham, “Of months, I am Margasirsa” (Bhagavatam 11.16.27) (Bhagavad-gita 10.35), the sense is that the time during the vow had eminent qualities.

“They properly worshiped—according to the injunctions (samanarcuh = samyag anarcuh) (samyag = yatha-vidhi)— Bhadrakali.” She is the same Katyayani, who is well known as Mangala-Candi. As a double meaning, bhadrakalim means: bhadram uttamam kam sukham tasya alih panktih yasyah sakasat, “her, because of whom there is a series of the highest joy.” The eminent quality of the deity to be worshiped is illustrated thus.

Krsna-cetasah means: krsne saksat sarvesvare cetah yasam, “They whose minds are on Krsna, who is God in person.” Even in properly worshiping her, only the worship of Krsna is meant to be expressed. Therefore, later he will describe the arrival only of Sri Krsna for the sake of giving a boon.

Or, by mentioning that the mind, in terms of being krsna-cetas, is most pure, what is meant is the complete result will manifest before long.

There is another rendering: Someone might think: “Isn’t it that an intense longing for a goal like this, which is utterly hard to get, is improper for very intelligent girls?” He responds with krsna-cetasah, which means: krsne sarva-cittakarsake cetah buddhih yasam, “they whose intellect is on Krsna, who attracts all hearts.” The gist is: Their hearts already belong to Him, and so they had no opportunity to think.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The gist of masam is: The result was accomplished in a very short time. Krsna-cetasah means: krsne cetah yasam, “They whose minds are on Krsna.” Although she is worshiped, only the worship of Krsna is meant to be expressed. Therefore, later Suka will describe the arrival only of Sri Krsna for the sake of giving a boon. Bhuyat etc. (may He be the husband) is the Sankalpa (desire; declaration of purpose) at the beginning of the puja.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The connection is: nanda-sutah patir bhuyad iti sankalpya, “after stating the purpose—sahkalpya is to be added—as follows: “May Nanda’s son become the husband.””

### 10.22.6

*usasy utthaya gotraih svair anyonyabaddha-bahavah \|*  
*krsnam uccair jagur yantyah. kalindyam snatum anv-aham \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

usasi—at dawn; utthaya—after rising; gotraih svaih—by their own names; anyonya—mutually; abaddha—are joined; bahavah—they whose forearms (or they by whom the forearms); krsnam uccaih jaguh—they loudly sang (glorified) Krsna; yantyah—while going; kalindyam—in the Kalindi; snatum—to bathe; anu-aham—every day.

*(tah kumarikah) anv-aham usasi utthaya (anyonyam) svaih (svaih) gotraih (ahuya) anyonyabaddha-bahavah kalindyam snatum yantyah krsnam uccaih jaguh.*

**Перевод:**

**Daily rising at dawn, they called one another by their names, joined hands, and loudly sang about Krsna while going to bathe in the Kalindi.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He talks about a previous aspect of the vow. Gotraih means namabhih (with the names). Anyonyabaddha- bahavah means parasparam grhita-panayah, “they whose hands are taken by one another.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

They are not only krsna-cetas, they are also dedicated to a sankirtana of Him. Thus he says their worship involved the topmost qualities.

Or: When the whole method of that worship is understood, that vow can also be undertaken by other people: By his mercy in this way, and after perceiving Sri Pariksit’s intention, he talks about the main aspect of that vow.

“Getting up at dawn every day (usasi = pratyusa eva)—for the sake of bathing far in the Yamuna just before sunrise—and calling one another by their respective names (svair gotraih = anyonyam tat-tan-namabhih ahuya), they, by whom the arms were firmly held by one another (anyonyabaddha-bahavah = anyonyam abaddhah. bahavah yabhih tah) (abaddhah = samyak baddhah = drdham grhitah)...” out of fear of tripping on the path in the darkness at the end of night, or it was due to being afraid of falling on account of the bewilderment of prema in a sankirtana of Krsna, or it was because of a special mutual affection. By a mutual affection in this way, only the completeness of the vow is demonstrated.

Uccaih (loudly) is so that all the girls would come together in one place; or it was because of a special absorption in singing. Regarding nityam kalindyam snatum (to always bathe in the Kalindi) (anv- aham = nityam): This was said in verse 2. The repetition is for the sake of making one aware of the excellence of bathing there.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Remembering a previous aspect of the vow, an aspect which he forgot out of prema and which was part of the sequence in the manifestation of their anuraga, Suka speaks the verse.

In regard to usasy utthaya62(after rising at dawn), the drift is those girls have a great inner longing. They called one another by their names (gotraih = namabhih). They held each other’s hands because what they had in common is love for Krsna. Concerning krsnam: Their words, like their minds, are only focused on Him. In addition: uccaih (loudly): this signifies an absorption in Him. Regarding kalindyam snatum anv-aham (to bathe daily in the Kalindi): Going far and always thinking of Him as their sole object of affection are shown. Thus, only the specialty of their anuraga is described in every way.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

It was said: aplutyambhasi, “after immersing themselves in the water” (10.22.2). Here Suka speaks upon recalling the sequence before that. Svair gotraih signifies: svaih svaih gotraih; the sense is they were called also by their respective names (svaih gotraih = svaih svaih namabhih apiahutah) in this way: “Hey Dhanya! Where are you? Why are you delaying?”

### 10.22.7

*nadyam kadacid agatya tire niksipya purva-vat \|*  
*vasamsi krsnam gayantyo vijahruh salile muda \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

nadyam—to the river; kadacit—at some point in time; agatya— after arriving; tire—on the shore; niksipya—after throwing; purva-vat—like before; vasamsi—the garments; krsnam gayantyah—while singing (praising) Krsna; vijahruh—they sported; salile—in water; muda—with joy.

*(tah) kadacit purva-vat nadyam agatya tire vasamsi niksipya krsnam gayantyah salile muda vijahruh.*

**Перевод:**

**At some point in time, they came to the river as before, threw their garments on the shore, and joyfully sported in the water while singing about Krsna.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Nadyam (to the river) means kalindyam eva (to the Kalindi). A flow is meant to be expressed by the word nadi (river). Kadacit signifies either “on the dvadasi at the end of Margasirsa” or “on the full moon at the end of Margasirsa.” With purva-vat (as before), a continual bathing in terms of being naked is made to be perceived.

“They sported with joy.” The reason for that is: krsnam gayantyah, “while singing—inasmuch as by singing there was no hindrance from the cold in the very cold water in the middle of winter, even in Sri Kalindi’s flow—about Krsna,” Him whose form is the topmost, dense bliss, or Him who attracts the heart the most.

Or the gist is this: Muda (with joy) is said because of executing the vow without impediments for a whole month’ therefore: krsnam gayantyo vijahruh (they sported while singing about Krsna).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kadacit denotes “on the full moon at the end of the month.” With purva-vat (as before), a continual bathing in terms of being naked is made to be perceived. And this is only due to a childish mood.

The reason for sporting with joy is: krsnam gayantyah (while singing about Krsna) since by the bliss of that singing there was no perception of cold even in the water in the winter.

Or, muda (with joy) is said because the vow was completed on that day, consequently: krsnam gayantyo vijahruh (they sported while singing about Krsna).

Moreover, by not taking interest in the body, being krsna-cetas is pointed out. In this way it is shown that the respective actions of mind, body, and speech are in unison.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kadacit (at some point in time) means: “when it was the full moon, on the day of the completion of the vow,” because this is implied as follows: evam masam vratam ceruh, “They performed the vow for a month in this way” (10.22.5). Therefore, Vrsabhanu-nandini and others, who had become an abode of close friendship due to having similar inclinations, were brought, after being invited, by those virgin girls for the sake of a festival. This is to be understood as a good fun in the water, which was almost like an avabhrtha bath (the bath that marks the end of a sacrifice), with those girls after the completion of the formal worship.

### 10.22.8

*bhagavams tad abhipretya krsno yogesvaresvarah \|*  
*vayasyair avrtas tatra gatas tat-karma-siddhaye \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

bhagavan—the Lord; tat—that (the water (salilam): ‘salile’ is in the previous verse); abhipretya—aiming for; krsnah—Krsna; yoga-isvara-isvarah—the master of the masters of mystic yoga; vayasyaih—by the companions (“of the same age”); avrtah— surrounded; tatra—there; gatah—went; tat-karma-siddhaye—for the accomplishment of the ritualistic act of those girls.

*bhagavan krsnah yogesvaresvarah tad abhipretya vayasyaih avrtah tat-karma-siddhaye tatra gatah.*

**Перевод:**

**With that in mind, Lord Krsna, the master of the masters of Yoga, went there, surrounded by His companions, for the accomplishment of the girls’ ritualistic act.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He is the master of the masters of yoga (yogesvaresvarah = yogesvaranam isvarah): In that way Suka shows His ability to fulfill each girl’s desire. “He went there for the accomplishment, i.e. to give the result, of their ritualistic act (tat- karma-siddhaye = tasam karmanah siddhaye) (siddhaye = phala- danaya)."

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Tad abhipretya (with that in mind) denotes: “knowing the vow” (tat - tad vratam) (abhipretya = jnatva). The sense is He inferred, somehow, by means of the results, since there was no direct manifestation of the mindset of those girls, whose feet ought to be worshiped by the most clever persons, the vow of worshiping Katyatani to get Him as a husband. The reason for that understanding of what is hard to know is: bhagavan, which connotes either sarvajnah (omniscient) or sarvaisvarya-yuktah (He has all godly might).

“He arrived right there” (tatra gatah = tatra eva agatah) because: krsnah, He the crest jewel of stylish enjoyers (rasika-siromani), He whose pastimes attract the hearts of all. He was surrounded by His companions. It was for the purpose of quickly and simultaneously stealing the many clothes of those numerous girls. The companions are different from those who had a sister or a cousin in that group of girls.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

He is to be revered by those who have acquired mystic perfections such as omniscience (yogesvaresvarah = yogesvaranam isvarah = labdha-sarvajnadi-siddhinam aradhyah). Therefore: bhagavan, meaning He too has powers, such as omniscience, which are eternal and inherent.

Tad abhipretya means: “after inferring (abhipretya = anumiya eva), by the specific style of their singing, etc., that the sole purpose of their vow was to obtain Him.” His engrossment in a pastime saturated with that kind of love for Him is shown in this way. Still, the ability to give the result by Himself, even to worshipers of another deity, and to steal all the clothes simultaneously is demonstrated. The reason for that is: krsnah. The sense is He is notoriously known to be that way.

Inasmuch as it is going to be said balaih, vayasyaih denotes balakaih eva sakhibhih (by friends who were just little boys). “Being surrounded (avrtah = avrtah, san) by them, He arrived (gatah = agatah)." Further, they should be understood as Dama, Sudama, Vasudama and Kinkini, who are in His inner circle of friends. For instance, it is said in Gautamiya Tantra:

*dama-vasudama-sudama-kinkiningandha-puspakaih \|*  
*antahkarana-rupas te krsnasya parikirtitah \|*  
*atmabhedena te pujya yatha krsnas tathaiva te \|\|*

**“With aromatic substances and with flowers, one should worship Dama, Sudama, Vasudama and Kinkini. They are the form of Krsna’s antahkarana. They are not different from Him. They should be worshiped like Krsna is.’’**

Antahkarana-rupah means: kramena buddhy-ahankara-citta-mano- rupah, “Those companions the forms of the intelligence, the ego, the subconscious, and the mind, respectively.” He was surrounded by them: It’s understood that it was for the sake of good fun, such as laughter.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He is the master even of the masters of yoga (yogesvaresvarah = yogesvaranam api isvarah). Because of this, it’s implied that He has omniscience; the ability to fulfill each girl’s desire; the ability to steal all the clothes placed by those girls right before their eyes; the ability to make those well-bred virgin girls make them bow to Him upon getting out of the water, when they came to the conclusion that giving up their embrrassment is better than giving up their lives; and the ability to refrain from sexually enjoying them, all of whose limbs were seen and who had been obtained in a lonely place, though they were submissive to Him.64

Regarding vayasyaih (by the companions): Since it’s going to be said balaih (‘with children’, in the next verse), they are to be understood as little children of two or three years old, whose clothes were the cardinal directions, who didn’t know the difference between male and female, who were thought of as friends, and who had not given up Krsna’s company even in tending the cows and so forth. That is said in Krama-dipika:

*jahghanta-pivara-katira-tati-nibaddha-*  
*vyalola-kihkini-ghataghatitairatadbhih \|*  
*mugdhais taraksu-nakha-kalpita-kantha-bhusair*  
*avyakta-manju-vacanaih prthukaih paritam \|\|*

**“\[One should contemplate on Mukunda,\] who is surrounded by little children, who are going around with sounds of a tinkling small bells tied on the declination of fat hips, who are innocent, whose ornaments on the neck are fashioned with nails of hyenas, and whose utterances are indistinct and charming.” (Krama-dipika 3.22)**

In Vaisnava-tosani, it is said: They are Dama, Sudama, Vasudama and Kinkini,66who are the forms of Krsna’s antahkarana and are seen in Gautamiya Tantra.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Bhagavan denotes He who is characterized by the six bhagas in full from aisvarya to Vairagya. The suffix mat \[up\] in bhagavan is used in the sense of nitya-yoga (eternal connection). Tad abhipretya signifies: sva-phalakam tasam vratacaranam vijnaya, “understanding their execution of the vow, whose result is He.”

### 10.22.9

*tasam vasamsy upadaya nipam aruhya satvarah \|*  
*hasadbhih prahasan balaih parihasam uvaca ha \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tasam—of those girls; vasamsi—the clothes; upadaya—taking; nipam—a kadamba tree; aruhya—climbing; satvarah—He who is quick; hasadbhih—who were laughing; prahasan—while laughing; balaih—with children; parihasam—a joke (or in a manner of jesting); uvaca—He uttered; ha—(a verse filler).

*(sah bhagavan krsnah) satvarah tasam vasamsi upadaya nipam aruhya hasadbhih balaih (saha) prahasan parihasam uvaca.*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna quickly took the girls’ clothes and climbed a Kadamba tree. While guffawing with the little boys, who were laughing, He spoke in jest.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

A nipa tree is a kadamba tree. Balaih signifies balaih saha (with the boys).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

After taking the clothes nearby, He, endowed with speed (tvaraya anvitah san) and accompanied by the little boys (balaih = balaih saha), who were loudly laughing on account of that gesture, climbed a nipa tree out of fear of those girls due to stealing from them.

Regarding balaih: For the sake of that jest, right at first He abandoned those who were bold, and so it’s understood that at this time He was surrounded by companions who were just little boys (balakaih eva vayasyaih vrtah). Alternatively, because of narrating this pastime before the holding of Sri Govardhana, which was done at the end of the seventh year of age, all of them were just little boys, insofar as the Lord, whose age was the same as theirs, had manifested six years of age. Still, this pastime is as if bold, since it is possible that the Lord was like that even in childhood. That too is well-known everywhere, It was already mentioned before. Similarly ahead as well, the pastime of showing favor to the divine yajna-patnis can be understood in like manner. Therefore, in the childhood of those boys, everything is uncensurable.

There is another rendering. These two pastimes occurred only in kaisora. The mention of this is before the holding of Sri Govardhana because this pastime, in the context of a special bhava of divine gopis which was revealed in the description of the song of the flute at the time of autumn, and even the pastime of showing favor to the divine yajha-patnis, in that context, are concomitant. Moreover, the sequence of the pastimes is for the most part disregarded by Sri Badarayani, sometimes because of following the context, sometimes because of an upsurge of a special bhava. This was obvious before, and will be obvious ahead.

“He only cracked a joke (parihasam =narma eva)” to attract the girls. Therefore He was eminently laughing (prahasan = prakarsena hasan). Ha has the sense of either harsa (joy) or sphutam (clearly).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

He, having speed (satvaram67= tvara-yuktah) with the little boys (balaih = balaih saha) in a stealthy way as if He were afraid, told the boys to keep quiet and took the girls’ clothes, thinking that His deed was acceptable for the sake of a special purpose, and climbed a nipa tree. At leisure, He laughed with those boys, and they laughed too. He clearly (ha = sphutam eva) uttered a humorous statement (parihasam = sa-narma-vakyam). The sense is this. The girls wondered why He was laughing. Knowing that their indignation was filled with love, but pretending not to know, He cracked a joke at them, who were dumbfounded: “Gosh! You are shivering. Why do you remain in the cold water? Get out, dry yourselves up and put on dry clothes.” It was an act in this manner, and so it was not improper, by the logic in: bhavan eva bhavan iva, “Only you are like you” (Krsna is Krsna) (Gopala-campu 1.22.31).

Regarding balaih: For the sake of that jest, right at first he abandoned those who were bold and had a close connection with the girls, and so He was with friends who were just little boys (balaih = balakaih eva sakhibhih). Therefore it was not censurable.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“While eminently laughing (prahasan = prakarsena hasan), that is, to draw the girls’ attention, along with the little boys—the boys were laughing for no good reason, just because of being in early childhood—, He spoke in jest:

—“Hey little girls of Vraja! Who placed so many clothes here on the branches of the kadamba tree? Do you know? Seeing them from afar while grazing cows, I quickly came here, joyful at beholding a wonder: “Is this our kadamba tree? Today it has colorful clothes for flowers and fruits.” I’m climbing it.

—Hey! Don’t do that! The clothes belong to us.

—Then how did they get so high on the branches of such a lofty kadamba tree? 67 —Only you put them there after stealing them.

—Okay, okay. You have the nerve to accuse Me, the son of King Nanda, of theft, so it’s inferred that today you want to go to King Kamsa, who stays in Mathura.

—Don’t be angry. Look at the clothes and consider this: Are they ladies’ clothes or men’s clothes?

—All right, smart gals! These garments are only ladies’ clothes. Are you the only ladies in this world? Aren’t there other ladies?

—There are indeed, but which other ladies except us village girls come in this desolate woodland?

—Dear girls who habitually wander in lonely places! Do only you, and no other, play in a solitary place?

—It’s not like that, wise guy! We didn’t come here to play, but to worship Durga, the deity of the kadamba tree.

—Are you the only lady worshipers of Durga? There is no other worshiper?

—That’s right.

—Come on, simple girls! Every night, goddesses on aircrafts come here and worship Durga Devi.

—Fine. Let them worship Devi. Why would they leave their clothes behind and go?

—Young girls, you don’t know the truth of the matter. They keep their clothes here so that they will wear them again tonight, after bathing, for the puja of Devi.

—Krsna, You don’t know the truth. The clothes are kept on high branches by the forestial deity so they will be worn only by us; we have just bathed, and now we are about to worship her.”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Regarding vasamsi (clothes): There is a plurality of clothes for each one, by the varieties of antariya (undergarment), kurpasaka (bodice), and uttariya (outer garment). He was quick (satvarah) in taking everything. Parihasam is an adverb.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

The nipa tree is a particular kind of kadamba tree.

### 10.22.10

*atragatyabalah kamam svam svam vasah pragrhyatam \|*  
*satyam bravani no narma yad yuyam vrata-karsitah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

atra—here; agatya—after coming; abalah—Hey girls; kamam— freely; svam svam—one’s respective; vasah—clothing; pragrhyatam—should be taken; satyam—the truth; bravani—I should speak (I speak); no—not; narma—a joke; yat—because; yuyam—all of you; vrata-karsitah—emaciated because of the vow.

*abalah! (yusmabhih) kamam atra agatya svam svam vasah (paricitya) pragrhyatam. (aham) satyam bravani. (idam) narma no (bhavati), yad yuyam vrata-karsitah (bhavatha).*

**Перевод:**

**“Hey girls! You may come here at your discretion and take your respective clothes. I tell you the truth. I’m not joking, because you are emaciated due to following the vow.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Hey girls! This is not a joke (no narma = na parihasah), because (yad = yasmat) you are fatigued on account of the vow (vrata-karsitah = vrata-srantah)."

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

In two verses, he relates the joke. “Here” means “near Me, at the base of the nipa tree.” “The clothes can be eminently taken (pragrhyatam = prakarsena grhyatam) at your discretion (kamam = yathestam),” that is, “I will not make any further impediment.”

Concerning svam svam (respective ones): “All the girls should come together; then each girl can take her own clothes (svam svam = nijam nijam). Who knows? Maybe one of you girls will snatch somebody else’s clothes.”

The girls might think: “You are faultless, but then again You have the habit of joking, and so we cannot tell whether you are deceiving us.” To that He says satyam and so on. Bruvani (‘I must speak’, the BBT reading) is poetic license. The sense is bravani (‘I must speak’, Sridhara Svami’s reading). Sometimes the reading is karavani (I should make). “This is not a joke.” It can be suspected, so He elaborates on that. The gist is: “Because a joke on you ascetics, thin on account of the vow (vrata-karsita = vrata-krsa), is inappropriate.” This is only the topmost jestful utterance by the nature of a special bhakti, since it is not seen in any text that those ladies, who are always completely enraptured, became thin because of a vow, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In two verses, he only talks about the joke. In point of atragatya (after coming here): He points to the place, the object of His intense sight, intending to say, “There is enough room right there, next to the clothes.” “They can be eminently taken (pragrhyatam = prakarsena grhyatam) at will (kamam - yathestam).” He enthuses them for the sake of a speedy arrival. His nonchalance in stealing suggests the following: “I saw these clothes from afar. Obviously, they were stolen by some thief, who hid them here in this kadamba tree.”

Concerning svam svam: “One’s own clothes may be taken after all the ladies have come, but not after only one, two, three, or several have come. One’s clothing might be taken by any of you. There might also be an exchange by you tricky ladies among yourselves at some point in time.”

The hidden mood is only another, which is to be inferred. “We don’t clearly grasp Your speech.” To that He says satyam and so on. Bruvani is poetic license. The sense is bravani (I must speak); sometimes that reading is seen. “You could be lying as a joke.” He responds: no narma (not a joke). “But this too is another one of Your jokes.” Suspecting that, He says: “Hey girls! Because you...” The gist is: “Because a joke on you ascetics, who are women (abala), who have not attained fortitude (bala) due to not reaching adolescense, and who are thin on account of the vow (vrata-karsita = vrata-krsa), would be totally wrong.” With this too He agitates the minds of those girls with a witticism that hints at a renewed indifference after implying: “Now what are you going to do?”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In this verse He clearly, as expressed by the word ha, utters the joke. “If it’s true that these clothes are yours, you may come here by your own will (kamam = yathestam eva), find out which ones are yours (svam svam = svam svam paricitya), and take them (pragrhyatam = grhyatam)—but only after giving Me, the protector of your wealth (svam), a necklace as payment.”

Concerning svam svam (respective ones): After all the ladies have come (agatya = sarvabhih eva agatya), but not after only one, two, or three have come, because women, who are greedy for clothing, might take more.

“We cannot go.” He responds to that, with laughter: “Hey girls!” (abalah) (lit. ‘weak ones’). The drift is: “I think you are unable to come here just because of emaciation on account of the vow.” Or: “If you don’t come, I will not give you your clothes. What can you do to Me? I am very strong.”

“We don’t clearly grasp what You say. You are deceitful at times.” He responds: “I must speak (bruvani)—this is poetic license; sometimes the reading is bravani—only the truth (satyam = tathyam eva)." Or: “I swear”, literally “I speak (bruvani = bravimi), having made an oath (satyam = sapatham krtva),” Amara states: satyam sapatha-tathyayoh, “Satyam means sapatha (curse; oath, vow) and tathyam (truth)” (Amara-kosa).

“This is no joke, because (yad = yatah) you were made thin by the vow (vrata-karsitah = vratena krsi-krtah)." The idea is: “My daya-bhakti (compassionate devotion) and dharma-bhaya (fear of breaching moral duty) in regard to you ascetics are rising.”

### 10.22.11

*na mayodita-purvam va anrtam tad ime viduh \|*  
*ekaikasah praticchadhvam sahaivotasumadhyamah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—not; maya—by Me; udita—said; purvam—before; vai—indeed (or a verse filler); anrtam—a lie; tat—that; ime—these ones; viduh— know; eka-ekasah—one by one; praticchadhvam—all of you should receive; saha eva—only together; uta—or; su-madhyamah—O you whose waists are nice.

*sumadhyamah! vai maya anrtam na udita-purvam (bhavati). ime (gopah) tad (anrtasya anukta-purvatvam) viduh. (yuyam) ekaikasah, uta saha eva, (atra agatya sva-sva-vasamsi) praticchadhvam (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Indeed, I have not told a lie before. These boys know that. Hey slender-waisted girls, come here one by one, or together, and get your clothes.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The syntactical connection is: ekaikaso va agatya svi-kuruta sahaiva va, “Indeed, receive (praticchadhvam = svi- kuruta) your clothes after coming one by one, or (uta = va) after arriving together.” The gist is: “We have no interest in them.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Isn’t it that only dishonesty is understood from a jestful utterance?” He responds to that here. Udita-purvam means: purvam purvam uktam yat, tad anrtam mithya naiva bhavati, “Whatever was spoken at various times previously has never been false.” Or: “A lie was not spoken before at any time” (anrtam na maya udita-purvam = kadapi anrtam purvam na uditam).

Vai (indeed) has the sense of prasiddhi (renown). “These ones, My comrades, know this too, inasmuch as only these ones are knowledgeable of all events related to Me, since they always go wherever I go.” In case they were to retort, “But Your companions are just like You,” He says: ekaikasah praticchadhvam, in other words: ekaikasa agatya svakiya-vastram grhnita, “After coming one by one, all of you may take your clothes.” “If the girl who comes does not get her clothes, then my word shall be false. Think of it that way.”

“How amazing! Whether in this manner or by procrastinating, is My word true? Is there any foulness in My heart?” To make them aware of this, He mentions the other option: saha (together). Uta means va (or).

“Hey girls whose waist is resplendent!” This is the secret intention: “Only the beauty of your middle portion is desired to be seen. These clothes are useless to Me.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) “Isn’t it that only dishonesty is understood from a jestful utterance?” He responds to that here. Udita-purvam means: purva-purvam uktam yat, tad anrtam mithya naiva bhavati, “What was spoken at various times previously is never false.” Alternatively: anrtam na maya udita- purvam signifies: kadacid api anrtam purvam na uditam, “A lie was not said before at any time.”

Vai has the sense of prasiddhi (renown). “These ones, My comrades, know this too, inasmuch as only these ones are knowledgeable of all events related to Me.” In case they were to opine, “But Your companions are just like You,” He says: ekaikasah praticchadhvam, in other words: ekaikasa agatya sviyam vastram grhnita, “By coming one by one, all of you may take your clothes.” “If things don’t happen that way, then the next girl, thinking that My word is a lie, should not come.”

“How amazing! At first, there is no consensus among the girls. Then, when some girl gets out of the water, the others do not automatically follow. What is this? Whether in this manner or by procrastinating, there is no crookedness at all in My words or in My mind.” To make them aware of this, He mentions the other option: saha. Uta means va (or).

“Hey girls whose waist is resplendent!” The gist is: “You of slender waists have been in cold water for a long time. This makes Me weak. Only the beauty of your middle portion is desired to be seen, but it is not that I have a purpose with these clothes.” This is the secret mood.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“We don’t believe even in this oath of Yours. You are a habitual liar.” In response, with tongue in cheek He utters this verse. Regarding udita-purvam: The compound was made in reference to: sup supa, “\[A word that has\] a case ending \[is compounded\] with \[a word ending in\] a case ending.”69This means: anrtam na purvam uditam, “A lie was not said before.” “In this life, up to this age, I have not told a lie. What is the proof of this, you ask? It is these little boys.” The drift is: “Because little boys have the nature of perceiving things as they are seen and because they are honest.”

—Then, from afar the clothes should be thrown here in the water, or, they may be given through the little boys.

—Alas, alas! How can I give them? I am unable to know whether these clothes belong to you or to someone else. By rule, the belongings of others are not touched, even with the tips of the nails, by persons of our kind, who follow moral codes. Therefore, come here, find your respective clothes and take them (praticchadhvam = praticchata = svam svam paricitya grhnita), because I neither take, give, or touch a thing that belongs to another. I live by principles.

—We, well-bred virgins, will not go near You, just because You are an audacious impostor.”

In that regard, He says: ekaikasah (one by one): “At first, some younger girl among you should come here. If she is not deceived, another should come, and then another.” As for sahaivota (or just together), the sense is it is impossible to mock women when many women come together.

“Hey slender-waisted girls!” (sumadhyamah). The drift is: “You are already showing Me your heads. Show Me the rest. You have no reason to be ashamed.”

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

The atmanepada in praticchadhvam is poetic license.

### 10.22.12

*tasya tat ksvelitam drstva gopyah prema-pariplutah \|*  
*vriditah preksya canyonyam jata-hasa na niryayuh \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tasya—of His; tat ksvelitam—that jest; drstva—seeing; gopyah— the cowherd girls; prema-pariplutah—plunged in love; vriditah— embarrassed; preksya—seeing; ca—and; anyonyam jata-hasah— they whose mutual laughter occurred; na niryayuh—did not go out.

*gopyah tasya tat ksvelitam drstva prema-pariplutah anyonyam preksya vriditah (anyonyam) jata-hasah (eva) ca (tasthuh, jalad bahir) na (tu) niryayuh.*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing that prank of His, the gopis became immersed in love. They looked at one another and felt embarrassed. They joked among themselves, but did not get out of the water.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Ksvelitam (prank) means parihasah (jest). Prema-pariplutah (flooded by love) means prema-rasa-nimagnah (immersed in the mojo of love).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Ksvelitam means parihasoktim (jestful utterance). Regarding prema-pariplutah (immersed in love): Naturally, as gopis, they have love for Him, and specifically after hearing His humor they became immersed in the Rasa of love to a higher degree. “While beginning to laugh (jata-hasah ca = jata- hasah ca satyah), they did not get out,” because: anyonyam preksya vriditah (they were embarrassed after looking at one another).

Or, only because of being immersed in love, they became embarrassed and started to smile (jata-hasah ca = jata-smitah ca). “After seeing one another (anyonyam preksya)” for the sake of being unanimous in not getting out. Or: Although they wanted to get out, upon seeing one another they became embarrassed due to being naked. Just because of that, they, laughing by seeing one another, did not get out.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Regarding prema-pariplutah: Naturally, as particular gopis, they have a special love, but at this time, understanding that jestful utterance (tat ksvelitam drstva = tat parihasoktim jnatva), they became immersed in an ever-increasing Rasa of love. In addition, they were embarrassed just by the nature of their gender. Seeing one another with embarrassment and with joy, while also having started to laugh (jata-hasah ca = jata-hasah ca satyah) they did not get out.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Seeing the subtle joke (ksvelitam = rahasya-parihasam), they became flooded by love, “We wonder: To please Him, our lover, how much self-respect do we have to lose?” The sense is they became submerged by the bliss of mental anulapa (chatter). Outwardly, however, they were not embarrassed after seeing one another: “Hey lotus-eyed girl, He is calling you.” Likewise: “You go first, nectar-faced girl. Let Him have it!” They were girls whose mutual laughter took place (anyonyam jata-hasah) in this way. That is, they were only joking; they did not get out.

### 10.22.13

*evam bruvati govinde narmanaksipta-cetasah \|*  
*a-kantha-magnah sitode vepamanas tam abruvan \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam—in this manner; bruvati govinde—while Govinda was talking; narmana—by the humor; aksipta-cetasah—they whose minds are transported; a-kantha—up to the neck (or including the neck); magnah—immersed; sita-ude—in cold water; vepamanah— trembling; tam—Him; abruvan—they addressed.

*govinde evam (narma) bruvati (sati, tah gopyah anena) narmana aksipta-cetasah sitode a-kantha-magnah vepamanah tam abruvan.*

**Перевод:**

**The girls’ minds were transported by humor when Govinda talked like that. Submerged in cold water up to the neck, the gopis, shivering, spoke to Him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Evam bruvati means: punah punah tatha eva vadati, “when He was repeatedly talking in that same manner.” The name Govinda signifies: “He finds words in terms of being under His control” (govinde = gah vacah nija-vasyataya vindati iti govindah tasmin). The fact that His speech is calculated and topnotch is meant to be understood by this.

The girls’ minds were attracted (aksipta-cetasah = aksiptani akrstani cetamsi yasam tah) by the humor, therefore they spoke, otherwise they would have said nothing, out of embarrassment. Moreover, they were shivering. The reason for that is: sitode a-kantha-magnah,which means: “By virtue of bashfulness, they entered in the cold water for a long time up to the neck in order to cover their chests” (= sitala-jale lajjaya vaksah-sthalacchadanaya kantha-paryantam ciram pravistah).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

'‘When Govinda, so called because He finds words that are humorous and sweet (govinde = gah vindati iti tasmin = narma-madhura-vacah vindati iti tasmin), was joking in various ways (evam bruvati = nana-prakaram narma bruvati sati)..." The humor took place as follows:

—“Hey wagtail-eyed girls, if you don’t come here, I’ll fashion a hammock and a pillow with these clothes that are on the branches and rest. Sleep is coming to Me now. I stayed awake all night.

—Hey Gopala! Out of greed for grass Your cows entered a dense thicket, so quickly go from here to make them turn around.

—Hey, hey, little girls of cowherds, you should swiftly return to the village for household chores. Don’t make your parents anxious about your whereabouts.

—Peacock-feather-crested guy! From now we are not going home for a month. By our parents’ order, after concluding our vow for Katyayani we will do the vow of fasting on water for a whole month. —Dear girls who are ascetics too! By the power of seeing you, I too feel dispassionate about living at home. I think I will do the vow of staying up in the air right here for an entire month. If you allow, I will alight from here and do the vow of staying in water with you.”

“..., the girls, whose minds were carried away by this jesting, became immersed in water up to the neck even more due to apprehension and shivered” because of the cold and also on account of sanka (apprehension), harsa (joy) and autsukyam (eager impatience).

### 10.22.14

*manayam bhoh krthas tvam tu nanda-gopa-sutam priyam \|*  
*janimo 'nga vraja-slaghyam dehi vasamsi vepitah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

ma—not; anayam—a bad conduct (a-naya, or an-aya,70“misfortune”); bhoh—(a vocative term); krthah—do; tvam—You; tu—specifically; nanda-gopa-sutam—the son of the cowherd named 70 Nanda; priyam—beloved (likable); janimah—we know; anga— (a vocative used for expressing endearment); vraja-slaghyam— praiseworthy in Vraja; dehi—give; vasamsi—the clothes; vepitah— \[we,\] who are shivering.

*anga! bhoh (krsna! tvam) anayam ma krthah. (vayam) tvam tu nanda- gopa-sutam vraja-slaghyam priyam janimah. (tvam asmabhyam asmakam) vasamsi dehi. (vayam sitena) vepitah (smah).*

**Перевод:**

**“Oh, don’t be unjust! We know You, dear. You are the son of Nanda the cowherd, are praiseworthy in Vraja, and are likable. Give us our clothes. We are shivering.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

At that time, the simple girls (mugdha) spoke: “Dear one (ahga)! Oh, Krsna (bhoh = bhoh krsna)! Do not do an injustice (anayam = anyayyam).”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

At first, they speak by means of conciliation (sama). The mention of the word ma (not) at the outset is for the sake of emphasis. Bhoh and anga are two vocatives of love; that explains the double utterance. “We know You, the son of Nanda the cowherd: You are the little boy of a cowherd, and we are little girls of cowherds, so You shouldn’t do that sort of impropriety (anayam - anyayyam) to us.”

Or, He is the son of the king of Vraja, Nanda, who delights Vraja (nandayati vrajam iti nandah): “Only Your kindness to us citizens is appropriate—You are the crown prince—but not a sorrowful act; that would be in opposition to what Your father stands for.”

Or, the gist of ‘the son of Nanda the cowherd’ is: “A misdeed of You who are the protector of the livelihood of all the people of Vraja would be unbecoming.”

Further: priyam priya iti janimah, ““We know that what we want is You as the husband,”71so carrying out what is unpleasant to us is improper.” Additionally: “We know that You are also praiseworthy in Vraja—or within Vraja, or by Vraja (vraja = vraje, vraja-madhye, vrajena va)—consequently doing this deed, censurable in Vraja, is not right, since we are shivering (vepitah = vayam vepitah)." Optionally: vepitah prati, “to girls who are shivering.” Thus they evoke His kindness.

There is another rendering: tvam priyam vraja-slaghyam ca janimah, ““We know You, who are dear and are praiseworthy in Vraja, because the girls are shaking due to being immersed in cold water up to the neck because of You, on account of stealing clothes.” This is a humorous statement with irony.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The commentary is the same. In addition:) Bhoh and anga are two vocatives endowed with the pain of love. As a pun, He is the son of the king of Vraja, Nanda, who delights Vraja (nandayati vrajam iti nandah), hence: “Only Your justice to us citizens is appropriate.” However, the mention of His name here is for the sake of hinting at anger and indifference. That too is because of bashfulness, given that there is a manifestation of their womanly nature.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

At first, they speak by means of conciliation (sama): “Do not do an impropriety (anayam = anyayyam)." “Hey simple girls! You don’t know Me, because you have no fear in accusing Me of unethical conduct.” They respond with tvam tu and so forth. “We don’t know other persons who stay in Vraja. We only know You, who are very well-known (tu = atiprasiddham) and are the son of King Nanda (nanda-gopa-sutam = nanda-rajasya sutam),” from the definition: gopo bhupe ’pi drsyate, “Gopa also means bhupa (king).”72“Moreover, You are worthy of a praise by anyone who stays in Vraja (vraja-slaghyam = vraja-stha-matrasya api slaghyam). Over and above that, You are a beloved.”

“Hey unintelligent girls! If I’m the king’s son, then how can there be any lack of ethics on My part? If you think, “Sometimes a prince becomes immoral,” how is it that I am praiseworthy in Vraja and dear to boot?
