Immoral people are neither praiseworthy nor dear in the eyes of good people.” “It’s true. We ladies are foolish to speak our minds, therefore be kind, forgive our offense and give us our clothes. We are shivering (vepitah = vayam vepitah).”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Anayam means anitim (an injustice).

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

At first they speak by means of conciliation. “We know You,” but not: “Now Your true self is coming out.” The word anga is a respectful vocative. Or anga is part of the compound: anga-vraja-slaghyam, which means sarvahga-sundaram (beautiful on all the limbs).73Priyam means either priyakaram (a beloved) or prinati iti pritam, “a pleasant person.”

### 10.22.15

*syamasundara te dasyah karavama tavoditam \|*  
*dehi vasamsi dharma-jna no ced rajne bruvamahe \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

syamasundara—O Syamasundara; te—Your; dasyah—servants; karavama—we shall do; tava uditam—Your utterance; dehi—give; vasamsi—the garments; dharma-jha—O knower of moral duty; no— not; cet—if; rajhe—unto the king; bruvamahe—we tell (see below).

*syamasundara! (vayam) te dasyah (smah. vayam) tava uditam karavama. dharma-jna! (tvam) vasamsi dehi. he (krsna! tvam vasamsi) no (dasyasi iti) cet, (tarhi vayam) rajne (idam vrttam) bruvama (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Syamasundara! We, Your servants, shall do as You say. Knower of moral duty, give us our clothes. If not, we'll tell the king.’’**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The mature girls (praudha) speak. Bruvamahe is two words: bruvama and he, “Otherwise, Krsna (he = he krsna), we’ll tell (bruvama = bravama) the king,” either Nanda or Kamsa.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Now they expound the intended act of giving. The name Syamasundara means: syamah ca asau sundarah ca, “He is dark blue and is beautiful.” Alternatively: syamesu sundarah, “Of dark persons, He is beautiful.” Therefore: “We are Your servants (te dasyah = vayam tava dasyah), and specifically, from now on we shall do what You say (tava uditam = tvad-uktam)." Or: “We will proclaim (karavama = khyapayama) Your rise, that is, Your eminence (uditam = udayam = utkarsam)." Optionally, dasyah satyah (being Your servants) is syntactically connected here. “We will become (syama = bhavama)” (syama sundara instead of Syama¬sundara) meets Citsukha’s approval. By servanthood in this way, a gift, consisting of offering oneself (atma-samarpanam), etc., is inferred.

Now, with dharma-jna and soon they make use of bheda (creating dissension). The drift is: Otherwise, by disregarding dharma, fear of unrighteousness is produced by looking at naked women and by stealing another’s belongings. Not perceiving His fear of adrsta (fate; unforeseen potential results of an action), with no cet and the rest they produce drsta-bhaya (fear of foreseen potential results of an action). Thus, twofold bheda is used. The theory in this regard was expounded before, in reference to slaghaniya-gunah (10.1.37) (BVT 10.1.36).

“Otherwise we’ll tell King Nanda” (rajne = gopa-rajaya). As an implied meaning (the following is in reference to the previous verse): nanda-gopasya sutam priyam, “We know You, the son of Nanda,” has the sense of “We know You are dear to him. Therefore, due to being dear to him, You were not taught by force.” On the side of being a crown prince: “This lewd act of Yours is fitting.” On the side of being a cowherd’s son: “You are like that due to associating with cows, due to being a cowherd.” Likewise: anga-vraja-slaghyam, “You are praiseworthy in terms of bodily limbs, not in qualities.” Dharma-jna too is a sarcastic statement, in the sense of a relinquishent of moral duty.

In truth, this is the secret intention: “You would make a good fit as our husband, given that You are nanda-gopa-suta (Nanda’s son), priya (likable), and vraja-slaghya (praised in the community), not to mention that You are beautiful.” This is the significance of the vocative “Syamasundara.” The gist of dasyah (servants) is: “We are qualified to be Your wives.” On top of that, there is a special bhakti, with karavama tava uditam (we shall do what You say). The sense of dharma-jna is: “Disregarding us who are such is inappropriate.” In another way, the sense of rajne is: “We will tell Dharma-raja” (rajne = dharma-rajaya), that is to say: “We will die.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The commentary is the same as the first two paragraphs above (in BVT). In addition:) The anubhava called kila- kincita took place from tasya tat ksvelitam (10.22.12) to here. The definition is:

*garvabhilasa-rudita-smitasuya-bhaya-krudham \|*  
*sankari-karanam harsad ucyate kila-kincitam \|\|*

**“That which, because of joy, makes a combination of garva (overweening pride), abhilasa (longing), ruditam (weeping), smitam (smiling) asuya (indignation), bhayam (fear), and krut (anger), is called kila-kihcitam (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.44)**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Yet again, they speak by way of conciliation. The reading syama is approved by Citsukha. “We shall become (syama = bhavama) servants.” In the reading syama, the sense is: dasyah satyas tavoktam karavama, “Being servants, we shall do what You say (uditam = uktam)." The gist is: “When You will be king, the servanthood of us citizens will be fully proper.” In truth, however, they offered themselves only by that duplicity. The sense is: sundarasya tava asmabhih yad dasyam sambhavet tatra tava uktam karavama, “We shall do what you say in the matter of our possibly becoming servants of You who are beautiful.”

Some harsh ladies make use of bheda (crushing an opponent’s viewpoint, specifically by inducing fear): “Knower of moral duty!” (dharma-jna). The drift is: “Because of stealing the property of women and because of looking at naked women, You will be the recipient of adharma (unrighteousness).” Not perceiving that He has fear of unrighteousness, with no ced rajne they illustrate a foreseeable fear. Thus there is twofold bheda.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

If the clothes are not given, then we are telling (bruvamahe)74the king, Nanda, Your father.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

Rajhe bruvamahe signifies: nandam jnapayisyamah, “We will inform Nanda.”

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

“If You do not give the clothes, we shall tell (bruvama = kathayama) this occurrence to the king (rajne = rajne idam vrttam)." Bruvama should read bravama.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

In case someone were to argue: “From the statement of Smrti: nagnam nekset para-striyam75(one should not look at the naked woman of another), why did the Lord do a wrong?” Listen, those women do not belong to any other, since their bodies were offered to the Lord76and since He had given a promise in that way in previous descents.

### 10.22.16

*sri-bhagavan uvaca*  
*bhavatyo yadi me dasyo mayoktam vd karisyatha \|*  
*atragatya sva-vasamsi praticchata suci-smitah \|*  
*no cen naham pradasye kim kruddho raja karisyati \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-bhagavan uvaca—the Lord said; bhavatyah—you; yadi—if; me— My; dasyah—maidservants; maya—by Me; uktam—what is said; va—and; karisyatha—you do; atra—here; agatya—after coming; sva- vasamsi—your clothes; praticchata—receive; suci-smitah—\[you,\] whose smiles are bright; no—not; cet—if; na aham pradasye—I will not give; kim—what; kruddhah—\[being\] angry; raja—the king; karisyati—will do.

*sri-bhagavan uvaca—yadi bhavatyah me dasyah (stha, yadi) va (bhavatyah) maya uktam karisyatha, (tada yuyam) suci-smitah (satyah) atra agatya sva-vasamsi praticchata. (yuyam sva-vasamsi) no (praticchatha iti) cet, aham na pradasye. raja kruddhah (api san) kim karisyati (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**The glorious Lord said: “If you are My maidservants and if you do what I say, then come here, get your clothes and put a bright smile on your faces. If not, I will not bestow them to you. What will an angry king do?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Bhavatyah (‘all of you’, in the honorific) at first is because of great respect in consideration of bhakti and so on. “After coming here” (atragatya), but not: “Let Me throw them to you in the water so you can take them.”

Suci-smitah (you whose smiles are bright) is a vocative. By this kind of pure (suci = suddha) smiling, it’s understood that there was no discomfort due to cold and so on, and that the shivering was just because of deceit. Moreover, “After agreeing to what I say and coming here, you make take these clothes.” With a special cleverness in this manner, He attracts them from the water.

Or: suci-smitah satyah praticchata, “You should receive them while having bright smiles.” The drift is: “If I see any melancholy in your faces, I will not give.” This is a special state of being a stylish enjoyer.

“If not, I will not give eminently” (na pradasye = prakarsena na dasye). This is implied by the prefix pra (eminently): “Or, if I were to give, for some reason, then I would give only a little something, only to some girl, maybe, after tearing it to pieces.”

“What will the king of cowherds (raja = gopa-rajah) do, even if he gets angry (kruddhah = kruddho 'pi san)? Nothing, because he has a special affection for Me, his son.” Here also, this is an implied meaning to be understood as a reply. By the splendid utterance ‘suci- smitah', their being qualified for marrying Him is intimated. Having said that. He made some of their clothes into a seat, fashioned some as a bed, fixed some on the upper branches of the nipa tree as flags, as banners, as a canopy, etc., made some into a hammock and swung

Himself in it, and again threw some here and there on the tree. This is to be inferred because of the text: skandhe nidhaya, “after placing on a bough” (10.22.18).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In this verse of six lines, He brings about their defeat simply by their acceptance in that way. The word bhavat (bhavatyah, you), which is expressive of respect, is used to entice them to come forward. The half verse that begins no cet is sometimes seen.77Suci- smitah is a vocative... (The rest of the commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Having defeated them with their words. He speaks to make them speechless. The gist is: “You say you are My servants? Let Me test your honesty. Obviously, I will not give anything to any dishonest girl.”

“While having bright smiles” (suci-smitah = suci-smitah satyah). The drift is: “If, in this test of dharma, there is melancholy in your faces, in this case too I won’t give you anything.” In truth, however, suci means srngara (romance, eroticism); suci-smitah signifies srngara-maya-smitah (you have smiles of love). Thus He makes them know about an emotion arisen in Him. Moreover, with no cet (if not) and the rest He lets them know: “Given that I am powerful, only sama (conciliation), not bheda (creating dissension), is your means of accomplishing the effect.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

In truth, suci-smitah signifies srngara-maya-smitah (you have smiles of love), from the definition: srngarah sucir ujjvalah, “Srhgara, suci, and ujjvala are synonymous” (Amara- kosa 1.7.17).

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

Va means ca (and).

### 10.22.17

*tato jalasayat sarva darikah sita-vepitah \|*  
*panibhyam yonim acchadya protteruh sita-karsitah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatah—after that; jala-asayat—from the body of water; sarvah darikah—all the little girls; sita-vepitah—shivering with cold; panibhyam—with both hands; yonim—the pubic area; acchadya— covering; protteruh—emerged; sita-karsitah—indolent and emaciated (or emaciated by the cold).

*tatah sarvah darikah sita-vepitah sita-karsitah panibhyam yonim acchadya jalasayat protteruh.*

**Перевод:**

**Afterward, all the girls, shivering with cold, covered their pubic area with both hands and emerged from the body of water. They were indolent and emaciated.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Protteruh means nirgatah (they went out).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“After that” (tatah = tad-anantaram) means “after seeing His zeal.” The girls were little girls (darikah = balah): For the most part, their age was the same as Sri Krsna’s.

“Shivering only due to cold (sita-vepitah = sitena eva vepitah), they covered their pubic area with both hands,” although their bodies were trembling: Shivering too is a sattvika-bhava that originates from the nature of prema, “and eminently went out (protteruh = prakarsena utteruh = prakarsena nihsrtah) from within the water (jalasayat - jala-madhyatah).,' The reason they went out is: sita-karsitah, “they were emaciated, i.e. pervaded inside out, by cold (sita-karsitah = sitena karsitah - sitena bahir antas ca vyaptah).”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) Afterward, i.e. seeing that zeal of His, the girls (darikah = balah), shivering with cold, covered \[that\] with both hands, though their bodies were trembling. Shivering too is a sattvika-bhava that originates from the nature of prema. The reason they emerged is: sita-karsitah, which means: sitena krsi-krtah hina-balatvam apaditah, “they were made emaciated by the cold, that is. they became weak.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

After that, “Hey sakhis, we have been defeated by our own words. If we procrastinate any longer and if in the meantime some other man comes, we will fall in a huge ocean of ridicule, even more than this. Further, our desire to touch His body has become very strong and is hard to resist. It does not even allow us to drown ourselves right here. All this was written on our foreheads by the Creator, otherwise those things would not happen, so let us honor the obstinacy of our priyatama, send our obstinacy to Rasatala, close our eyes after making a respectful offering of water to bashfulness, cover our respective bodies only with the darkness obtained by closing our eyes, and go to the shore.” They motivated one another in this way and went close to Krsna.

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

They were trembling with cold (sita-vepitah = sitena kampitah). They were indolent, and therefore they had become thin (sita-karsitah = sitah atah eva karsitah = alasah atah eva tanu-bhutah). This means they were indolent owing to a special bhava engendered from bliss and were emaciated. Sita and alasa are synonymous.78

### 10.22.18

*bhagavan ahata viksya suddha-bhava-prasaditah \|*  
*skandhe nidhaya vasamsi pritah provaca sa-smitam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

bhagavan—the Lord; ahatah—dumbstruck; viksya—after seeing; suddha-bhava-prasaditah—satisfied by pure love; skandhe—on the shoulder (or on a bough); nidhaya—after placing; vasamsi—the clothes; pritah—pleased; provaca—eminently spoke; sa-smitam—in the manner of having a smile.

*bhagavan (tasam) suddha-bhava-prasaditah (tah) ahatah viksya (tasam) vasamsi (kadambad adaya svasya) skandhe nidhaya pritah (san) sa-smitam provaca.*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing them, who were dumbstricken, the Lord, satisfied by their pure love, placed their garments on a bough. Being pleased, He eminently spoke with a smile.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Seeing them, who were slightly unblemished virgins (ahatah = isad-aksata-yonih)...”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Satisfied, already before, and now also, by pure love, or by the pure desire for Him becoming their husband (suddha-bhava-prasaditah = suddhena premna patitva-kamanaya va prasaditah), He, being pleased (pritah = pritah san) after seeing them who had arrived (ahatah = agatah)—since the verbal root han has the sense of gati (motion)—placed the clothes, after piling up all of them, on His shoulder (skandhe = sva-skandhe) for the sake of the excellence of each girl’s good mood, and eminently spoke (provaca = prakarsena uvaca), that is, He spoke by demonstrating a logic just to give a lesson.” The word sa-smitam (in the manner of having a smile) is used because what is about to be said is borderline humourous.

There is another rendering. The reason for placing the clothes on the shoulder is: suddha (pure). The reason for eminently speaking with a smile is: pritah (pleased): A humorous utterance is obviously implied by this, by considering the inevitable rise of it only by priti. By virtue of placing so many clothes on one shoulder in that way, a godly might (aisvarya) in a worldly pastime is illustrated as before. For this reason at first it was said yogesvaresvarah (10.22.8).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions in this paragraph are underlined.) “Satisfied, already before, and now also, by pure love (bhava = prema). He, being pleased (pritah = pritah san) after seeing them who had arrived (ahatah = agatah)—since the verbal root han has the sense of gati (motion)—placed the clothes, after piling up all of them, on a large branch of the tree (skandhe = vrksasya skandhe) and eminently spoke (provaca = prakarsena uvaca), that is, He spoke by demonstrating a logic as if to give a lesson.” Sa-smitam (with a smile) is used because these two facts are borderline humourous: the girls stayed in that manner for a long time, and what is about to be said.

Someone might argue: “The meaning of ahatah as agatah is wrong because the verbal root han is not in usage (aprayukta) that way.” This is the opinion of those who abide in the pit of poetry, not of those who abide in the great ocean of words such as the Veda. For example, Patanjali says in Maha-bhasya: sapta-dvipa vasumati trayo lokas catvaro vedah sangah sa-rahasya anekadha bhinna ekasatam adhvaryu-sakhah sahasra-vartma sama-veda ekavimsatir bahvrcyam navadhatharvano veda vakovakyam itihasa-puranani vaidyakam ity etavantam sabda-prayogam anisamyaprayuktah sabdah, “The Earth has seven islands. There are three worlds. There are four Vedas, along with their limbs and their manifold different secrets. There are one hundred and one branches of Adhvaryu priests. The Sama- Veda has a thousand paths. There are twenty-one traditions of Rg-Veda. There are nine types of Atharva priests. There are the Vedas, the Vako-vakyam, the Itihasas, the Puranas, and works on medicine. Not having heard such a usage of words, words are not used.”

The whole statement is inconsiderate. Even in the opinion of the makers of dictionaries, another meaning of ahata occurs. In Visva- prakasa for instance: ahatam gunite ’pi syat tadite ’py anake ’pi ca, “Ahatam means gunitam (multiplied), taditam (struck), and anaka (a large drum).” In the explanation of the word ahata, Ksirasvami enounced: ahatam udghositam, “Ahatam means udghositam (proclaimed).” Here also it’s understood that those girls are renowned, and this suggests a supereminence of the astonishment in seeing those girls in that way. Enough of this hypothesis.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Ahatah signifies agatah (them, who have come). Or ahatah sita-piditah (struck... by the cold). For instance, Visva states: ahatam gunite ’pi syat tadite ’py anake ’pi ca.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Seeing them, who were as if dead in a complete way (ahatah = samyak prakarena eva hatah) (hatah = mrtah iva), He, satisfied by their unconditional love (suddha- bhava-prasaditah = yah suddhah nirupadhih bhdvah prema tena prasaditah), which He understood as follows: “For well-mannered girls, this kind of relinquishment of bashfulness is even worse than death, but they did it on My insistence,” placed their clothes on the shoulder—only out of greed for getting the fragrance of the girls’ limbs, and moreover His tender love for those girls and His respect for them are proven: “I am even holding your undergarments on My shoulder”—and eminently spoke,” i.e. He spoke thoughtfully (provaca = prakarsena uvaca = sa-paramarsam uvaca).

He thought: “The girls did what had to be done, although it is hard for any woman to do, with respect for My love (or with the impediment of My love) (mat-premoparodhena). Yet another thing has to be done. This one is even harder to do. Whether they can do it or not remains to be seen. Let Me behold this situation. I want to see the power of love for Me.”

He spoke with a smile (sa-smitam): “Girls! Servanthood to Me was accepted merely with your mouths. Now I will put this declaration of yours to the test: karavama tavoditam, “We shall do as You say” (10.22.15). Thus, if you are willing to emerge, I will give you your clothes, once they become imbued with My soul, mind, body, and life force.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“Seeing them, who had come (ahatah =agatah tah)—or: “Seeing them, who were completely struck” (ahatah = samyak taditah) due to giving up shame—, the Lord, satisfied by a pure mood, a bhava whose end result is only He, placed the garments on the shoulder” to enlighten them about the nonduality of His limbs with theirs. “Being pleased, by getting the aroma of their limbs and by understanding: “For these girls, I am their life,” He spoke with a smile, thinking, “To those who emerge from the water, I will give the clothes along with My heart.”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

The girls were completely struck (ahatah = samyak hatah) by the rush of bliss, or by the cold, or by dejection, or by shame. Alternatively, ahatah means agatah, because of the sense of gati in the root han himsa-gatyoh (to hurt, to go). Satisfied by their unconditional (suddha = upadhi-sunya) bhava, He spoke. Sa- smitam is an adverb. After doing what? After placing the garments on His shoulder (skandhe = svamse). The intention is this: “Now, a direct touch is not taking place. Let there not be a mutual touch.” Placing garments on the shoulder is easily suggestive of an embrace.

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

He placed the garments on the branch of a tree.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Ahatah means agatah. The fault of nonusage is only in regard to poetry and so on,79not in this statement of a sage. Or ahatah signifies trapaya apahatah (devastated by shame). He eminently spoke... what is about to be said: vaksyamanam is to be added.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“Seeing those girls, who were slightly unblemished virgins, meaning they were between childhood and youth (ahatah = isad-aksata-yonih tah = balya-yauvana-sandhi-sthah tah kumarikah)...” He was satisfied, because of a pure, i.e. guileless, mood, a nature that does not go beyond what was said. Having mercy (prasaditah = anugraha-yuktah) in that way, He placed the garments on the branch of a tree (skandhe = vrksa-sakhayam).

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Aksata-yonih signifies krtalpa- nidhuvanah (the girls, by whom a little amorous play was done).

### 10.22.19

*yuyam vivastra yad apo dhrta-vrata*  
*vyagahataitat tad u deva-helanam \|*  
*baddhvahjalim murdhny apanuttaye ’mhasah*  
*krtva namo ’dho-vasanam pragrhyatam \|\|*  
*upajati (12)*

**Пословный перевод:**

yuyam—all of you; vivastrah—who were without clothes; yat—which; apah—the water; dhrta-vratah—by whom the vow is maintained; vyagahata—she penetrated (or bathed, or splashed); etat—this (it is well-known); tad—that; u—assuredly; deva-helanam—an offense to the god; baddhva anjalim—after prayerfully joining both hand palms murdhni—on the head; apanuttaye—for the expiation; amhasah—the wrong; krtva namah adhah—after doing a low bow (or adhah-vasanam, lower garments); vasanam—garment (garments); pragrhyatam—may be taken.

*dhrta-vratah (satyah api) yuyam vivastrah (bhavatha. abala evam- bhuta) apah vyagahata (iti) yad (bhavati), tad etat deva-helanam u (bhavati, atah asya) amhasah apanuttaye (yusmabhih) murdhni anjalim baddhva namah krtva (ca yusmakam) adho-vasanam pragrhyatdm (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Although you were observing the vow, you entered the waters naked. That is surely an offense to the gods. You may take your garments once you join both palms on the head and do a low bow to atone for the sin.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The syntactical connection is: dhrta-vratah satyo vivastra apo vyagahatapsu snata iti yat tad etat u eva deva-helanam, “While maintaining your vow, you, who didn’t have clothes, bathed in the waters (apo vyagahata = apsu snatah). That is disrespect to the gods.” The sense is: “It is an offense.”

He mentions their means of atonement; He talks to the girls, who fear a defectiveness in their vow: “having joined cupped hands on the head, and bowed low—that is, having done an obeisance (adho namah krtva = pranamam krtva)—to nullify this sin (amhasah apanuttaye = asya papasya nivrttaye)...”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“But there is no fault in childhood.” He responds to that with dhrta-vratah (you were following a vow). Regarding yad etat, the gist is: “Since I directly perceive it, there is no chance that I am going to overlook it.” Concerning deva, the mention in the masculine, though there is a worship of Devi, is with the intent to express the generality of that disrespect to all other gods too, to strengthen His point. Or the sense is: It is disrespect (helanam = avajna) to Varuna, the presiding deity of water. Or, only an offense (helanam = aparadhah), the form of a hole in the vow, due to being a technicality, is signified with the word deva-helanam.

Anjalim baddhva (after joining the palms): That was on the head, not elsewhere, to fulfil the special desire of Him who is the crest jewel of stylish enjoyers. The expression anjalim baddhva is added because the wording: namah krtva (after doing an obeisance) could signify the endeavor to do an obeisance with one hand. This is technically allowable, because of the reading of the text: eka-hasta- pranamas ca, “one-handed obeisance also” (Visnu-smrti, quoted in Hari-bhakti-vilasa 8.406). On top of that, it’s inferred that He thought the girls might do an anjali at a normal height, and so He said: murdhni (on the head).

The word adhah is connected with namah krtva (doing a low obeisance). Or adhah forms a compound: adho-vasanam, which means paridhana-vastram (undergarment), and so the idea is: “However, you cannot take your outer garments.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Here He says, “Alas, alas! This hidden offense of yours has become blatant.” The syntactical connection is: yuyam vivastra satyo yad apo vyagahata, tad etat u evarthe devasya jaladhisthatur varunasya narayanasya va helanam, “That all of you, being without clothes, penetrated (vyagahata = vyagahadhvam) the waters is indeed an offense (helanam = aparadhah) to the presiding deity of water,” either Varuna or Narayana. Here, u has the sense of eva (certainly, indeed).

“This is the local custom. It is not an offense on the part of young girls.” He responds to that with dhrta-vratah. He made them afraid: “Only the nonfruition of this vow that was executed will inevitably take place.” Seeing that they, all of whose limbs had slackened while making their minds repent: “Alas, alas! This sort of disgrace happened, and the intended result of the vow will not occur, therefore we are as good as dead, so enough of delaying the relinquishment of our life force,” had become pale and greatly worried, He immediately thought, “Gee, their life airs should not leave!”, told them the atonement of it with baddhva and so on, and pacified them, “Emaciated girls! Don’t fear. Because of the scriptural statement: striyo hi yasya dasyo bhavanti sa eva tasam sarva-deva- mayo narayanah, “Narayana, who is all the gods, belongs to those ladies who are His servants,” and because of Garga’s statement: narayana-samo gunaih (10.8.19), at this time, I am your Narayana, therefore you are face to face with Me.”

“The undergarments should be taken (adho-vasanam pragrhyatam = antariya-vastram grhyatam) after doing an obeisance to nullify the offense (amhasah apanuttaye = aparadhasya nivrttaye).” The idea is: “Since I, a man, have no use for ladies’ undergarments, I will only give them. As far as the outer garments are concerned, I will make them into My own outer garments.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

U has the sense of niscaya (certainly).

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

U is a vocative. Or u has the sense of eva, “This is simply an offense to a god (u deva-helanam etat = deva-helanam eva etat),80therefore (tat = tasmat)...” The idea is: “I will only give the undergarments, not the outer garments.” This is a practical joke. In truth, however, there was an offense only to Varuna, the presiding deity of water. “Once I am pleased, after you do your obeisance, the offense will be nullified.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

“Although you were maintaining your vow (dhrta- vratah = dhrta-vratah api), that you naked girls agitated the waters (apah vyagahata)—literally “you specifically caused an agitation” (vyagahata = visesena viloditavatyah81= visesena ksobham utpaditavatyah)—is a disturbance (etat = etad alodanam). That is certainly (u = niscaye) an offense to a god. This is well-known (tat = prasiddham eva).”

### 10.22.20

*ity acyutenabhihitam vrajabala*  
*matva vivastraplavanam vrata-cyutim \|*  
*tat-purti-kamas tad-asesa-karmanam*  
*saksat krtam nemur avadya-mrg yatah \|\|*  
*(indra-vamsa)*

**Пословный перевод:**

iti—in this manner; acyutena—by Acyuta; abhihitam—called \[ a fault\]; vraja-abalah—the village girls; matva—thinking; vivastra—in the manner of having no clothing; aplavanam—a plunge (or a bath); vraja-cyutim—a violation of the vow (“a fall in regard to the vow”); tat-purti-kamah—they who have the desire for the fulfilment of that; tat-asesa-karmanam—of that and of all rites; saksat krtam—\[to Him,\] the direct result; nemuh—they bowed; avadya—of imperfections ("what is blamable”); mrk—the purification; yatah—because of whom.

*iti (dosatvena) acyutena abhihitam vivastraplavanam vrata-cyutim matva (tah) vrajabalah tat-purti-kamah tad-asesa-karmanam saksat krtam (sri-krsnam) nemuh, yatah avadya-mrg (bhavati).*

**Перевод:**

**Realizing that taking a dip while being naked, designated as a fault by Acyuta in this way, was an infraction of the observance, those girls of Vraja, desiring the fulfillment of the vow, bowed to Him, who was the direct result of that vow and of all other rites. Owing to that obeisance, the purification of the imperfection occurred.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Thinking that nakedly plunging, designated by Acyuta as a fault in this manner, was a cause of the degradation of the vow, they, desiring the fulfillment of it, bowed to Him, who is the direct result (saksat krtam = phala-bhutam tam eva) of that vow and of all other rites. Only He is the cleanser of sinful reactions (avadya- mrk = papa-marjakah).'"

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Concerning acyutena (by Acyuta), their intention is implied: “There is no fall at any time in any way of Your words from the real meaning.” They are females. In addition to that, with the word abala (woman; weak) the sense is they are unable to transgress His words.

“Thinking that the observance had a deviation, i.e. a hole (vrata- cyutim = vratasya chidram)—though there was no deviation—after hearing—srutva is to be added—what was said (abhihitam = uktam) by Acyuta...”

There was no deviation because, truthfully, in terms of being naked in childhood there is no fault in the case of those who are following a vow. And this is elucidated ahead by Sri Svamipada: drdham atyartham pralabdha vancitah “yuyam vivastrah’’ ity-adina, ‘‘The girls were utterly cheated, with yuyam vivastrah and so on (10.22.19).” (Bhavartha-dipika 10.22.22). The rest was explained by him.

Here is another interpretation: “Being desirous of fulfilling all those actions (tad-asesa-karmanam), characterized by the worship of Devi, they bowed, because He is the one who fills the holes of all rites (asesa-karmanam avadya-mrk = asesa-karmanam sah eva chidra-purti-karakah).”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Concerning acyutena: “There is no fall at any time in any way of Your words from the real meaning.” Their intention is implied in this way, since they are women of the village (vrajabalah = vrajasya striyah). In addition to that, with the word abala (woman; weak) the sense is they are unable to transgress His words—on account of being under the control of prema.

In point of matva (after thinking): In truth it is because there is no fault, due to being obtained as a local custom, a conduct of childhood. For this reason it will be said: pralabdhah, “The girls were cheated” (10.22.22). Saksat krtam means saksat pati-rupam phalam (the direct result, the form of a husband).82Because He is that, it is said: avadya-mrk. This specifically is their intention.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The girls reached this conclusion: “Let our bashfulness, moral duties pertaining to subcaste and family, and all the rest come to nil, fine, but there should not be a defectiveness in our vow,” and did exactly what their beloved said.

“Thinking that nakedly plunging, designated as a fault by Acyuta in this manner, was a cause of the degradation of the vow, they, desiring the fulfilment of that vow, bowed to Him, who is the form of the result to be achieved (saksat-krtam = sadhya-phala- svarupam tam) of that vow and of all other rites.” The drift is: When He, the embodiment of all prizes, is satisfied, what other prize might there be?

“Because of Him (yatah = acyutad eva), all defects disappear (avadya-mrk = sarva-dosa-nivrttih)." Mrg is poetic license. The substance is: Those who have become the object of His grace have no defect characterized by an infringement.

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

"... because (yatah = yasmat) there is the purification of all faults (avadya-mrg = sarva-dosa-marjanam bhavati).” The suffix \[k\]vi\[p\] is applied in the passive impersonal. The fact that mrj has no s is poetic license. Or: “because only He is the cleanser of faults (avadya-mrg = sah eva dosa-marjakah),” where the suffix \[k\]vi\[p\] is applied in the active voice.83

### 10.22.21

*tas tathavanata drstva bhagavan devaki-sutah \|*  
*vasamsi tabhyah prayacchat karunas tena tositah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tah—those girls; tatha—in that way; avanatah—who had bowed; drstva—after seeing; bhagavan—the Lord; devaki-sutah—Devaki’s son; vasamsi—the clothes; tabhyah—to those girls; prayacchat—He gave; karunah—compassionate; tena—by that \[obeisance\]; tositah— pleased.

*bhagavan devaki-sutah tatha avanatah tah (kumarikah) drstva karunah tena (pranamena) tositah tabhyah vasamsi prayacchat.*

**Перевод:**

**Observing them, who had bowed in that way, the Lord, Devaki’s son, who is compassionate and was gratified by that, gave the garments to the girls.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Seeing them, who had bowed, in terms of having done an anjali (avanatah = krtanjalitvena pranatah), in that way, i.e. in the manner that He said (tatha = tena svoktena prakarena), He eminently gave (prayacchat = prakarsena ayacchat) the clothes.” He gave them “eminently”, that is, according to the suitability, by means of loving vocatives, or with joviality, i.e. with the mirth of exchanging one another’s clothes for the sake of the girls’ priti (love, bliss). It’s understood that at first He came down from the nipa tree.

He gave all the clothes: the undergarments, the outer garments, and so on, because: karunah, He is compassionate, meaning He is inherently satisfied (= svatah eva pritah). In addition: bhagavan, He is dedicated to manifesting His unlimited qualities and so forth, because: devaki-sutah, He is Devaki’s son, that is, He took birth from her for that purpose. The sense of the word Devaki was already explained. And specifically, He was gratified by that vow (tena = tena vratena), or by their honoring His words.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The first paragraph above is the same. Moreover:) The reason He gave all the clothes is: karunah, He is inherently compassionate in every situation (= svatah eva sarvatra dayaluh). And specifically, He was gratified by that. The sense is as follows: Because of the girls’ great longing to see Him, this mood of His, which was like the fickleness of a little materialistic boy, came about although there was also the manifestation of feelings suitable on the part of an experienced gallant. His wish was fulfilled because of that special state of the girls; that state had ripped to shreds the girls’ self- conceit and bashfulness, had originated from their pttrva anuraga, and involved excrutiating pain.

Devaki-sutah is Sukadeva’s statement to Pariksit. This statement is proper here because it evokes Pariksit’s joy, given that he looks up to Him in that way, considering that he is the great-grandson of Kunti and the grandson of Subhadra. Sukadeva’s statement: bhavatam prapitamahi, “your great-grandmother” (10.49.14) was said for the same reasons. At the beginning of the tenth canto (10.1.5-11), Pariksit asked about Him in that way. Therefore here the gist is that Sukadeva means to say: “The one whom you look up to lost His mind out of love for those girls. Think about how glorious these gopis are.” Referring to Krsna as the son of Devaki should be explained in this way in other texts too.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He gave all the clothes, since He was pleased by that obeisance (tena = tena pranamena), the means of accomplishing what He wanted.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Devaki-sutah means yasodatmajah (Yasoda’s son). Seeing them shivering with cold, He was compassionate. He was gratified by their absolute love (tena = pranayena aikantikena).

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Or, karunas tena tositah is one word: karuna- stena-tositah, which means: karunah ca stenah ca tositah ca, “He is a compassionate (karuna = karunavan) thief (stena = caura) who is gratified.”

### 10.22.22

*drdham pralabdhas trapaya ca hapitah*  
*prastobhitah kridana-vac ca karitah \|*  
*vastrani caivapahrtany athapy annum*  
*ta nabhyasuyan priya-sanga-nirvrtah \|\|*  
*upajati (12)*

**Пословный перевод:**

drdham—utterly; pralabdhah—cheated; trapaya ca hapitah—and they were caused to abandon shame; prastobhitah—ridiculed; kridana-vat—like toys; ca—and; karitah—made to do; vastrani—the garments; ca—and; eva—certainly; apahrtani—were stolen; atha api—nonetheless; amum—to Him; tah na abhyasuyan—they did not show indignation84; priya-sahga-nirvrtah—happy in the company of the beloved.

*(yadyapi tah kumarikah) drdham pralabdhah, trapaya hapitah ca, prastobhitah (ca), kridana-vat karitah ca, vastrani ca apahrtani, athapi tah priya-sanga-nirvrtah amum (krsnam) na abhyasuyan.*

**Перевод:**

**They were utterly cheated, were induced to give up embarrassment, were ridiculed, and were made to act like toys, and their clothes were stolen. Still, blissful in the company of the beloved, they did not hold a grudge against Him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

They were utterly cheated (drdham pralabdhah = atyartham vancitah), with the words beginning from: yuyam vivastrah, “You, who were naked, took a dip” (10.22.19). They were induced to give up shame too (hapitah = avahapitah = tyajitah), by the whim: atragatya sva-vasamsi, “If you are My servants and if you do as I say, come here and get your clothes” (10.22.16). They were ridiculed (prastobhitah = upahasitah), with: satyam bravani no narma, “I speak the truth, not a joke” (10.22.10). And they were made to do like toys, with the pretext of an atonement, beginning from: baddhvanjalim, “once you join both palms” (10.22.19). They did not hold a grudge, meaning they did not see any fault in what He did to them.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“How amazing, king! Behold the glory of deep love,” or: “Behold how Sri Krsna is a charmer!” To signify this, he utters the verse, as if he were envious of them. Kridanam means: kridopakaranam yantra-putrikadi, “a puppet, or any such implement for playing.” They were happy by associating with Him, their sweetheart.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Here Suka only expounds upon tena in the previous verse (He was gratified “by that”). (The rest of the commentary is the same as the above.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Out of amazement, since it is hard for others to do, he praises what the girls did, which was agreeable to their beloved although He was treating them disrespectfully. (The rest is the same as Bhavartha-dipika. Moreover:) They were happy by being with their sweetheart, despite the way He treated them. The sense is: Just because He is the beloved, the girls were experiencing what He did, though it was a gift of trouble, only as a reason to be happy.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Karitah means krtah (made). The affix \[n\]i\[c\] in karitah is used without changing the meaning. Athapi means tathapi (nevertheless).

Here, those of shallow intellects might have a doubt: “The idea that Hari, whose bliss is complete, derives bliss from woman like the jivas do is impossible.” Since those women are His svarupa- sakti, they are transcendental. The body of Vidhu can be with the kalas (expansions), from the statement in Brahma-samhita: ananda- cinmaya-rasa-pratibhavitabhis tabhir ya eva nija-rupataya kalabhih, “He resides in Goloka with those ladies, who are expansions, in terms of being His forms, and who correspond to the transcendental, blissful Rasa” (5.37).

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Kridana-vac ca karitah signifies: kridanam daru-putrikadih, daru-putrikah sutra-grathitah yatha nartyante, tatha karitah, “They were made to act like wooden dolls strung on strings dance,” because: priya-sanga-nirvrtah, which connotes: “their cause of happiness is merely the association of the beloved” (= priya- sanga-matram nirvrti-hetuh yasam tah).

### 10.22.23

*paridhaya sva-vasamsi prestha-sangama-sajjitah \|*  
*grhita-citta no celus tasmin lajjayiteksanah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

paridhaya—after donning; sva-vasamsi—their clothes; prestha- sahgama—the association of the dearest one; sajjitah—caused to be attached to (or moved85by); grhita-cittah—they whose minds were seized; no celuh—they did not move; tasmin—toward Him; lajja ayita—attained shyness; iksanah—they whose glances.

*(tah kumarikah sva-)sva-vasamsi paridhaya prestha-sahgama- sajjitah grhita-cittah tasmin lajjayiteksanah no celuh.*

**Перевод:**

**After donning their clothes, the girls, who were moved by meeting their lover and whose hearts were stolen, did not budge. Their glances toward Him gained shyness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“They were made submissive by the association of the dearest one (prestha-sahgama-sajjitah = prestha-sangamena vasi- krtah), therefore they, whose minds were taken away (grhita-cittah = grhita-cittah satyah), did not move.” Next, he talks about the state of having the mind taken away: tasmin lajjayiteksanah, “the girls, whose glance toward Krsna is the play of bashfulness” (= tasmin krsne lajjayiteksanah, lajja-vilasitam iksanam yasam tah).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“After donning their respectives clothes (sva- vasamsi = nija-nija-vastrani)" although the clothes, which had been piled up, had been returned by Him. The rest is by Sridhara Svami.

There is another explanation. By associating with the dearest one, Sri Krsna, the girls were made to be greatly attached only to Him (prestha-sahgama-sajjitah = presthasya sri-krsnasya sangamena asajjitah) (asajjitah = tasmin eva dsakti-krtah), therefore they were grhita-cittah, “they by whom the Lord’s mind is attracted” (= akrsta- bhagavac-cittah). Consequently, while having glances endowed with shyness (lajjayiteksanah = sa-lajja-drstayah satyah)—either by the rise of a special mutual love or by obtaining the graciousness of consoling words—, they, who were steady in that place, or who were steady in regard to Krsna (tasmin = tasmin sthane, krsne va, avasthitah) did not move...” from there. Optionally, the locative case (tasmin) has the sense of the ablative (“from there”).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The commentary is the same. In addition:) There is another interpretation. When, after they put on their clothes, the disappearance of excessive shyness occurred, their emotions arose (grhita-cittah = udita-bhavah), therefore they were remaining as if ready (sajjitah = sajjah iva vartamanah) for secretly getting married right then (prestha-sangama = prestha-sangamaya = tada eva pani- grahanaya)—consequently—while having glances toward Him that were acting as though they were shy (tasmin lajjayiteksanah = tasmin lajjayiteksanah satyah) they did not move.”

Lajjayita is a form that ends in pac-adi a\[c\] (called “pac-ader at" in HNV), by the derivation: lajjate lajjah, “Lajja is one who is shy,”86when there is the nistha (the suffix \[k\]ta) after the affix \[k\]ya\[n\]. This is the anubhava called vikrtam (implying by a gesture). This is the definition:

*hri-manersyadibhir yatra nocyate sva-vivaksitam \|*  
*vyajyate cestayaivedam vikrtam tad vidur budhah \|\|*

**“The learned know: What is meant by oneself but is not expressed by either shyness, covert anger, or jealousy, etc., and is implied only by a gesture is vikrtam.” (Ujjvala-nilamani 11.58)87**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

They were made to be greatly attracted to Him, the boyfriend (prestha-sangama-sajjitah = prestha-sangamena sajjitah = tasmin eva atyadhikam asakti-krtah). Their clothes were stolen by Krsna; in that way they stole His heart: this is the significance of grhita-cittah, “they by whom His heart was taken away” (= grhitam tasya api cittam yabhih tah). A mutual love is implied in this way. The girls thought: “Krsna knows that we are emotionally attached to Him, and we know that He is emotionally attached to us on account of Katyayani’s grace.”

“The girls, whose glance toward Sri Krsna attained bashfulness (tasmin lajjayiteksanah = sri-krsne lajja ayitam praptam iksanam yasam tatha-bhutah satyah), did not move (no celuh = na celuh),” only due to numbness arisen from love.

The following utpreksa (fanciful imagination) is implied: Bashfulness, banished by Krsna and even by those girls, departed from their limbs and went far way. But it turned around, came back, went near Krsna, obtained an excellent graciousness from Him, returned in the girls’ limbs and became even better than before.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“The girls, whose glances toward Him, the lover, gained shyness (tasmin lajjayiteksanah = presthe lajjam praptam iksanani yasam tadrsyah satyah), did not move.” This means they could not move, owing to the rise of stambha (being stunned), because the girls came to this conclusion: “Hari loves us.” Hence their shyness, which had gone away, reentered their limbs and became very potent.

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

“They became fixated on the union of the lover (prestha-sangama-sajjitah = presthasya sangame sajjitah jatah)," in the sense of the third purusartha (kama). This means the girls became forms of Rasa.

“Their minds were taken away by Him.” Or “they by whom His mind was taken away,” because this was implied with: tositah (gratified) (10.22.21).

Their glances to Him attained shyness (tasmin lajjayiteksanah = tasmin lajjam praptam iksanani yasam). Or their glances were offered with shyness to the Lord (tasmin lajjayiteksanah = bhagavati lajjaya arpitani iksanani yasam). This was a glance of love.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“They did not go away (nocceluh88= na ucceluh)" from that spot; sthita-pradesat is to be added.

### 10.22.24

*tasam vijnaya bhagavan sva-pada-sparsa-kamyaya \|*  
*dhrta-vratanam sankalpam aha damodaro ’balah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tasam—of those girls; vijnaya—understanding; bhagavan—the Lord; sva-pada—of His feet; sparsa—for the touch; kamyaya—with the desire; dhrta-vratanam—by whom the observance was maintained; sahkalpam—the resolve; aha—says (spoke); damodarah— Damodara; abalah—to the girls.

*bhagavan damodarah sva-pada-sparsa-kamyaya dhrta-vratanam tasam sankalpam vijnaya (tah) abalah (prati) aha (sma).*

**Перевод:**

**Understanding the resolve of the girls, who had observed the vow with the desire to touch His feet, the Lord, Damodara, addressed the girls.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The name Damodara is used to imply His bhakta- vatsalya. Abalah means abalah prati (to the girls).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Understanding the resolve.” This means He directly realizing it by seeing their special mindset. Next, Suka illustrates the resolve of the girls, by whom the observance was maintained... by the rules. Or the sense is the girls observed the vow with effort (dhrta-vratanam = dhrtam niyamena yatnatah anusthitam va vratam yabhih tasam). They did so with the desire for the touch of His feet, that is, with the desire for extreme closeness, with bhakti, as a wife. Or they desired the bestowal of His feet in terms of Him being a husband. In short, they wanted Him to belong to them (sva-pada- sparsa-kamyaya = sva-padayoh sparsam tasya kamyaya) (sparsam = sparsanam = patitvena tasu samarpanam = tat-svatvopapadanam). This means their resolve was to touch His feet. A special state of being a husband with a special love is implied by the word pada- sparsa (the touch of the feet).

Abalah (girls) signifies that they do not have independence due to being little girls. The idea is: That sort of mercy to them is just right, in reference to pritah (pleased) (10.22.18). Another explanation of abalah is like that of words such as anuttama. That is: na balam anyesam yabhyah tah, “those because of whom others have no power,” meaning the gopis are the most powerful women, on account of making the Lord submissive.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The first paragraph is the same. Moreover:) The sense of ‘Damodara’ is He had love for them from the very beginning of being Damodara. As for abalah (girls), which denotes abalah prati (to the girls), it signifies that they do not have independence due to being little girls. The idea is: Their desire was to be fulfilled only by Him, and so that sort of mercy to them is just right.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“O best Rasika! We have already attained a result of the vow, since an uncommon mockery was done by You. Despite that, our life force did not depart. On the contrary, our life force was made to be fully satisfied by a conformity with You. Moreover, having made us get out of the water and seen all our limbs, You said several things while giving us our clothes after putting them on Your shoulder, along with the jewel of Your heart, although we should have been wearing them in the first place. We only give You a shy glance as an answer to that too. You, cognizant of the proper time, place, and persons involved, should tell us, who do not know whether by glancing we are offending You or pleasing You, what you mean to say. Only after hearing that will we go home.”

In that regard, with this verse he talks about the full cognizance of the Lord, who wants to reply, and after that in three verses he mentions His reply.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

The connection is: sva-pada-sparsa-kamyaya sankalpam vijnaya, “Understanding a resolve with the desire to touch His feet,” that is, with the desire for the mood of being wives. Concerning ‘Damodara’, the sense is He had love for them from the beginning of that pastime.

### 10.22.25

*sankalpo viditah sadhvyo bhavatinam mad-arcanam \|*  
*mayanumoditah so ’sau satyo bhavitum arhati \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sahkalpah—the resolve (desire); viditah—known; sadhvyah—O virtuous girls; bhavatinam—your; mat-arcanam—worship of Me; maya—by Me; anumoditah—approved; sah asau—that very (or that well-known) \[resolve\]; satyah—true; bhavitum—to become; arhati—deserves.

*sadhvyah! bhavatinam sankalpah (yusmabhih) mad-arcanam maya viditah anumoditah (ca). sah asau (sankalpah) satyah bhavitum arhati.*

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

*sadhvyah! mad-arcanam bhavatinam sankalpah (yusmabhih lajjaya akathitah api) maya viditah (maya) anumoditah (ca, atah) sah asau (sankalpah) satyah bhavitum arhati.*

**“Virtuous girls, your resolve is known to Me. It is your worship of Me, and I approve it. That resolve deserves to come true.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Virtuous girls, your worship of Me is your longing. It was known to Me, though you didn’t say it out of bashfulness. It is approved by Me, therefore it deserves to become true.” By the mention of the sense of sambhavana (possibility) in the verb arhati (deserves), the implied sense is: atyantiko na bhavisyati, “It will not be absolute (perpetual).”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

The vocative sadhvyah (virtuous ladies) is used because the resolve was better than anything. As a pun: sarvatha rupa-gunadina sadhutvena yutah mad-apeksyah eva, “Due to being good, in terms of form, qualities, etc., in every way, you are certainly to be looked after by Me.”89

He talks about the resolve: mad-arcanam, “the worship of Me in terms of serving Me by being a wife, with bhakti.” The resolve is exactly that. Satyah (true) means susiddha-phalah (a nicely accomplished result).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Here Suka substantiates the fact that His mercy to them is just right. In that way also, a distinctiveness from other things is meant. The vocative sadhvyah portends: parama-prema- vyavasaya-guna-rupavatyah, “O you who have the topmost love, determination, qualities, and forms!” Because of that too, the sense is: mad-ekapeksitah, “O you who are solely required by Me.” Or sadhvyah means: mad-ekapeksikah, “O you who only depend on Me.”

“Your worshiping Me is the resolve, which consists of love for Me as a husband. That resolve was known (viditah = jnatah) to Me. It is the goal of all. And it was approved because you have no other desire. That very resolve certainly deserves (arhati = yujyate eva) to be forever unvariable (satyah = sada api avyabhicari eva)."

Regarding the verb arhati, the difference between the two sutras: sambhavane lam iti cet siddhaprayoge, “\[A lin suffix is used after a verbal root\] when the sense is sambhavana (assumption; possibility) if there is no established usage of alam ” (Astadhyayi 3.3.154) (vidhih, sakti-sambhavane calam-sabdaprayoge tatha, HNV 713) and arhe krtya-trcas ca, “A krtya suffix (which makes a potential participle), the suffix tr\[c\], and \[a lin suffix are used after a verbal root\] when the sense is arha (being worthy)” (Astadhyayi 3.3.169) (arha-saktyor vidhi-visnukrtya-trlah, HNV 716) has been discerned in Kasika: (1) sambhavanam yogyatadhyavasanam, “Sambhavanam means the ascertainment (or superimposition) of worthyness (ability) \[in regard to the action denoted by the verb\]”90and (2) arhatvam yogyatvam, “Arha denotes worthiness \[in the subject of the verb\].”91Adhyavasanam signifies aropanam (superimposition, attribution), as is well known in regard to the rupaka ornament (metaphor). And when the state of being sambhavana is conceived, it is explained in that way: mahatam sambhavitam satyam eva, “What is possible for the greats is true.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Virtuous ladies, your longing is your worship of Me, which evokes My joy. Moreover, though you didn’t say it out of bashfulness it was known by and approved of by Me. And it is true, due to being guileless. Therefore it deserves to be.” The drift is: “What indeed is impossible for you ladies in this regard, given that even I am under the control of love, because the intended purport is My happiness.”

Here, only the potency of mercy (krpa-sakti) made the Lord, who had come forth to the next level, give a flash of His aisvarya to the girls, though He is under the control of their love and though He was engrossed in those pastimes, and made Him understand the difficulty in their worshiping Katyayani for the goal of attaining Him. It also made Him bestow its result. The girls thought: “He thinks of Himself as Narayana, due to Garga’s statement: narayana- samah, “equal to Narayana” (10.8.19).”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Anumoditah (approved) signifies svi-krtah (accepted).

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

“Therefore that very resolve (so 'sau = so ’sau sankalpah) deserves to become fruitful (satyah = saphalah).”

### 10.22.26

*na mayy avesita-dhiyam kamah kamaya kalpate \|*  
*bharjita kvathita dhana prayo bijaya nesate \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—not; mayi—in Me; avesita—engrossed; dhiyam—of those whose minds; kamah—a desire (or a material desire, or lust, or love); kamaya kalpate—does not produce a material desire (“is fit for a material desire”); bharjita—roasted (or fried); kvathita—boiled; dhana—a grain; prayah—generally; bijaya—\[to be\] a seed (to be the source of a sprout); na isate—are not able (is not able).

*mayi avesita-dhiyam kamah prayah kamaya na kalpate. bharjita kvathita dhana bijaya na isate (i.e. iste).*

**Перевод:**

**“Generally, the lust of those whose minds are engrossed in Me is not conducive to lust. A roasted boiled grain cannot sprout.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Why?” (Why is there a possibility that it will not be perpetual?) Therefore He speaks this verse. “It is not conducive to repeated material sense gratification (kamaya = punah kama- bhogaya),” because this kind of kama (desire; lust) is the cause of the quieting of itself, by the greatness of the object (Krsna). An example of the nonsprouting of kama is given: “A scorched (bharjita = dagdha) cooked (kvathita = pakva) grain, such as barley (dhana = yavadi), is unable to effect the origination of a sprout (bijaya = ankurodgamaya)."

Prayah (generally) implies that a sprouting might occur, by one’s own desire, since it is seen in that way in the case of Dhruva and others (they had material desires even after meeting the Lord.)92

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

The stanza was explained by Sridhara Svami. In that regard, the following, the remainder of the statement, is to be understood in conformity with what is going to be said: yadyapy evam, tathapi bhavatinam asau satyo bhavisyati, tad-atita-phalam ca bhavy eva vrata-visesat, “Although it is so, still this desire of yours will come true. The result, which exceeds that, will also occur, owing to a special vow.”

In point of mayy avesita-dhiyam (of those whose minds are engrossed in Me),93any idea that this also applies to another scope is repudiated, and so is the desire for another rasa in relation to Him.

“The desire of those whose minds are engrossed in Me is not suited (na kalpate = na yogyah bhavati) to the joy of mundane sex (kamaya = grama-kama-sukhaya)” because it is the crest jewel of all goals of life due to being the nature of the topmost love.

Or, kamaya means sambhogaya, by the derivation: kamyate iti kamah (that which is desired): sambhogaya na kalpate, “The desire is not conducive to sexual union?” With a modulation of the voice (kaku), the sense is: kalpate eva (it certainly is conducive). The reason for that is only: mayy avesita-dhiyam, inasmuch as that desire as well is the form of the play of the maturity of the topmost prema. And that has already been explained in many ways in Sri Bhagavatamrta. Alternatively: “Any material desire (kamah = prakrtah kamah api) is not fit for kama."

There is another explanation: “The entire intended result takes place. Moreover, a desire for Me also gives a superior result.” That is what He says, “The desire is not merely conducive to the intended result (kamaya = kamita-phala-matraya)..." rather it is also conducive to a result that totally exceeds it, insofar as it bestows a result beyond the wish, therefore the gist is, “You will attain Me along with the joy of paramourship, which is even superior to husbandhood.”

“... because: For the most part (prayah = bahulyena), grains that are scorched and cooked (bharjitah kvathitah = dagdhah randhitah ca eva) are unable to become a seed.”

However, dried by the heat of the sun and later made to be moist with water at the time of sowing, grains obviously become able to produce a sprout. “Given that love in a relationship with a paramour is better than love for the husband, You will attain Me only in that way.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In this verse, He talks about being worthy (yuktatvam). “In the case of those who serve Me in that way, or even mentally, a desire for a kingdom, sovereignty and so on does not produce a material desire (kamaya = kamatvaya), rather it culminates only as unselfish bhakti to Me, so what need be said about the desire of you for whom the goal of life is only prema-seva to Me?”

An example is Sri Kardama, regarding the upasana of Sri Visnu, in reference to this text:

*satyam disaty arthitam arthito nrnam*  
*naivarthado yat punar arthita yatah \|*  
*svayam vidhatte bhajatam anicchatam*  
*iccha-pidhanam nija-pada-pallavam \|\|*

**“True, He, being requested, gives to men what is requested, but He does not give a thing so that requests occur again. To those who revere without selfish motive, He brings about the attainment of His budlike feet, which overshadow material desires.” (5.19.27)**

With bharjitah and so on there is an example of not becoming a material desire. Prayah (generally) has the sense of vitarka (conjecture). Dhanah means bhrasta-yavah (roasted barleycorns). Visva states: dhana bhrasta-yave94prokta dhanyake ’bhinavankure, “Dhana means “roasted barleycorn”, “coriander” and “new sprout”.” By constitution, they are roasted (bharjitah), and later they are cooked (kvathitah = randhitah ca). This is with the intent to express excessiveness. “They are not fit (nesate = na kalpante) for being a seed (bijaya = bijatvaya)."

There is another explanation. “In the case of all those whose sole goal in life is I (mayy avesita-dhiyam = mad-eka-purusartha-matranam), the desire only for loving service to Me (kamah = kamah mat-prema-sevaika-visayah) is not conducive to another desire (kamaya = kamantaraya), but it becomes relishable in itself. This applies to you girls to a higher degree.” An appropriate example is given. The grains are roasted by nature. Later, “fried (bharjitah) by using ghee, etc., for the sake of a special taste and well cooked by using cane sugar (guda) and so forth, they become unable to cause an effect for the sake of generating another result (bijaya nesate = phalantarotpadanaya na sampadaniyah bhavanti), but they become relishable by themselves. Your desire for prema-seva to Me, which is embellished by special emotions devoid of another wish, is in that way.”

The substance is: “This is some sort of sweetness of Mine!” For instance, after realizing it they will say: surata-vardhanam soka-nasanam, **“Your lips are a nectar that heightens amorous pleasure, terminates sorrow, and is nicely kissed by the flute which is made to sound in such a way that it makes people forget about other ragas. O hero, give us the nectar of Your lips”** (10.31.14). The fact that the bhava of these girls is the crest jewel of the topmost goal of life was expounded upon in that way in Sri Bhagavatamrta and in Sri Bhagavata-sandarbha (the six Sandarbhas).

Moreover, by the logical reasoning in: vanchanti yad bhava-bhiyo munayo vayam ca, **“These cowherd women who have an elevated love for Govinda, the Soul of all, are the foremost embodied beings on Earth because sages, we devotees and those who fear material life want that type of love”** (10.47.58), what other kind of santi directed at Him, the object of their desire, might be useful at all to those sages, who are most peaceful? Therefore: satyo bhavitum arhati eva” (“It certainly deserves to come true,” in the previous verse).

This desire, which consists of the proclamation of His qualities and which is bewildering, is to be understood only as transcendental due to having a connection with the Lord, although it involves His behavior as a gallant. Citsukha’s reading is dhana prayo bijaya nesyate. The meaning is clear.95

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Furthermore, an occasional worship of Me which is untrue, that is, not genuine, due to being endowed with deceit, deserves to become true owing to its good qualities focused on Me, so what can be said of your desire to worship Me with the greatest love?” This is the substance of the verse.

“Deceit, characterized by having a material desire (kamah = sa-kamatva-laksanam kaitavam), is not conducive to material sense gratification, which is the result of a material desire and is not in accordance with the truth (kamaya = tat-phalaya ayatharthaya kama-bhogaya)" but is conducive to the cessation of the material desire by the greatness of the object, Krsna.

An example is given in the second half of the verse. Here the nominal base dhana indicates grains such as barleycorns. Those grains, sown in a muddy soil, sprout. The same ones, exposed on a stony ground, become scorched (bharjitah) by the heat. Later they become moistened by rain. “They, exposed to heat (kvathitah = randhitah), are unable (nesate = na samarthah syuh) to originate a sprout (bijaya = ankurodgamaya).”

The sense of prayah is yatha (like). For instance, Visva-prakasa says:prayas canasane mrtyau prayo bahulya-tulyayoh, “Praya means anasanam (fasting) mrtyu (death), bahulyam (for the most part), and tulya (similar),” and Medini states: prayo bahulya-tulyayoh, “Praya means bahulya and tulya."

The reading nesyate is approved by Citsukha. In that one, the singular is poetic license.96

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“The desire, whose scope is only loving service to Me (kamah = kamah mat-prema-sevaika-visayah), of those by whom the mind is completely attached to Me (avesita-dhiyam = prasajjita dhih yaih tesam), having understood that I am the goal of life, is not conducive to a longing for another result (kamaya = phalantarabhildsaya),” but it becomes relishable in itself.

At first, barleycorns are roasted. Later, fried with ghee, and well-cooked by boiling them in sugar (kvathitah = sita-kvathena nispakvah), they are not meant for generating another result (bijaya = phalantarotpadanaya). The singular in nesyate is poetic license. Prayah means yatha (like). Visva states: prayo bahulya-tulyayoh.

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

“In the case of those whose minds are engrossed in Me, a resolve (kamah = sankalpah) is not conducive to a material desire.” There is an example, with bharjita and so on. Prayah means bahulyena (generally). Bijaya means bijatvaya (for being a seed).

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“It is not conducive to the germination of the desire for sense objects (kamaya = visayeccha-prarohaya)."

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

The word kvathitah is used because the grains go in boiling water: This is a partial indication (of simple syrup: sugary water). “Generally (bhuyah), such grains are unable to become a seed (bijaya nesate = bijaya na samarthah bhavanti)." Therefore: “A material desire offered to Me will not generate another material desire again.” Even more than that, it will not cause the attainment of a previous condition.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“Grains that are fried, i.e. thrown in a frying pan, and well cooked (kvathitah = nispakvah) are not desired (nesyate = nesyante) for the origination of a sprout (bijaya = ankurodgamaya).”

In nesyate, the discrepancy in number is poetic license. Prayah (for the most part) is connected to bharjitah (fried) and kvathitah (cooked).

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

“A barleycorn, or the like (dhana = yavadi- rupa), that is either roasted or boiled is not taken (nesyate = na angi-kriyate) for the sake of generating a sprout (bijaya = punar ankurotpadanaya),” but is only taken for the purpose of being relished.

**Annotation**

Regarding Visvanatha Cakravarti ?s explanation of praya: In usage, however, praya has the sense of like (“almost like”) only when it is the last word in a compound.

Still, according to Visvanatha Kaviraja, the word praya can be used to signify the utpreksa ornament (fanciful assumption): atra janimahe ity utpreksa-vacakam. evam, manye sanke dhruvam prayo nunam ity evam-adayah, “The words janimahe (we know, we surmise), manye (I think), sanke (I suspect), dhruvam (indeed), praya (perhaps), nunam (surely) and so on are expressive of a fanciful imagination” (Sahitya-darpana 10.45) (Bhakti-rasamrta- sesa 4.154).

In India, the idea of “grains fried and boiled” often refers to a sweet that is the form of a ball (gulabjamun). The wording in the verse constitutes the paryayokta ornament (circumlocution). In the context of madhura-rasa, the utpreksa is as follows, with a modulation of the voice: “The love of the girls whose minds are engrossed in Me is not conducive to making love? Sweet balls are unable to make a seed.”

### 10.22.27

*yatabala vrajam siddha mayema ramsyatha ksapah \|*  
*yad uddisya vratam idam cerur dryarcanam satih \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

yata—all of you should go; abalah—O girls; vrajam—to the cowherd village; siddhah—perfect; maya—with Me; imah—these; ramsyatha—you will enjoy; ksapah—nights; yat uddisya—after aiming for which \[enjoyment\]; vratam—vow; idam—this; ceruh— they performed (you performed); arya-arcanam—which was the worship of Durga; satih—saintly ladies.

*abalah! satih! (yuyam) vrajam yata. (yuyam) siddhah (bhavatha. yuyam) imah ksapah maya (saha) ramsyatha, yad (ramanam) uddisya (bhavatyah) idam vratam aryarcanam ceruh (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Girls, return to the village. You are successful. You will enjoy these nights with Me. Aiming for that enjoyment, you performed this vow, the worship of Arya.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Siddhah (successful) means purna-manorathah (the girls, whose longing is fulfilled, i.e. is about to be fulfilled). He talks about it: “You will enjoy these upcoming nights (imah ksapah = imah agaminih ratrih) with Me.” Arya is Katyayani. Satih stands for satyah (being).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Therefore (i.e. “Because I implied that I will bestow to you girls a result that is beyond what you wished for”) (in his previous commentary) He says this.

“You will have fun in the games of Rasa (ramsyatha = rasa- kridadina kridayisyatha), or “You will get a special happiness” for many nights (ksapah = ksapah vyapya)." By obtaining such a grace, their superiority over Laksmi is shown, as evidenced from Uddhava’s statement that begins: nayam sriyo ’nga, “This favor was never bestowed on Laksmi...” (10.47.60). In addition: imah ksapah (these nights). The accomplishment of that before long is meant.

“Hey girls (abalah)! ” In this way He suggests that they are utterly childish, so the drift is: Now, sensual enjoyment is inappropriate. Or, by an aforementioned logic, the sense is they have more power than everyone, by having the distinction of making Him submissive in a special fashion. The reason for that is: siddhah, “their wish has come true and its result is more than expected” (= sampanna-kamita-tad- atita-phalah). Imah (these) signifies upcoming nights, the nights of upcoming autumn. Though they are far away, imah is an utterance for the purpose of a consolation, due to being forthcoming. Possibly, imah ksapah denotes upcoming nights that will enhance the months after winter.

The girls might say: “The happiness of a marriage with You, which was our resolve, should be accomplished. As a result, let the joy of the games of Rasa also take place.” He responds to that in the second half of the verse. The sense is: “That aiming for which you performed (ceruh = bhavatyah ceruh) the vow, the worship of Arya, is this (idam), i.e. what I said, the joy of the games of Rasa with Me as a paramour. Should there be husbandhood, by a marriage, the special happiness of the games of Rasa would not be successful.”

Satih means he satyah (hey virtuous women). The idea is: “Although there is paramourship, you are already virtuous (satyah = sadhvyah eva) in every way—in truth it is because there is no paramourship—due to being dearer than married ladies.” Alternatively, satih is an adjective of ksapah. The sense is those nights were the best (satih = uttamah): they caused the appearance of the bliss of Rasa, were autumnal, meaning they were devoid of cold and heat, and were lighted by the moon.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

With yata (you should go), He starts the process leading to the effectuation of the desire. The sense is: “Your desire is accepted. And only I can fulfill it.” With this intention He says: he abalah (Hey girls): It is like before.

“Fine. But where should we go now?” In consideration of this He says vrajam (to the village). “If so, where is Your kindness to us little girls?” Expecting this, with siddhah He clearly reveals the fruition of it. The gist is: “I have already accepted you in principle, in accordance with the resolve.” Having brought about a marriage consisting of an acceptance in this manner, with maya and so forth He also brings about a special result: His limbs. Imah denotes sannihitah eva (forthcoming).

For the sake of a return, which is inevitable by that sort of attainment, He concludes only with an utterance for sadhana-sadhus: yad ceruh. Here bhavatyah (you ladies) is to be added: “You ladies implemented the status of being My wives (yat = mat-patnitvam)."

Satih means he satyah (hey saintly women). Therefore this is understood: (1) They did not eagerly accept another husband, and (2) Still, as girls who were covertly married, they despised the secret like any cheating wife would. Only the girls other than these ones acted as parakiya ladyloves. It was said in that way: yuvatir gopa- kanyas ca, “He who knows when it’s time invited both the young women and the virgin girls and took pleasure in being with them” (Hari-vamsa 2.20.18).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He speaks this verse with the following intention: “The auspicious time for the first romantic enjoyment is only nighttime.” “You are already successful (siddhah = siddhah eva yuyam)." The sense is the conceit of being sadhakas occured only on account of His mood of having human pastimes, a mood that enhances sweetness. “You will enjoy (ramsyatha = ramsyadhve) these forthcoming (imah = sannihitah) nights.” Yat means yad ramanam (aiming for “which enjoyment” you performed this vow). Arya is Durga. Satih stands for satyah, i.e. bhavatyah (you ladies).

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Satih means he satyah. This is perceived: The marriage of these girls occurred by the Gandharva rite.

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Why didn’t the effectuation of the resolve take place right at that time? He speaks in that regard. The little girls are twofold: purva-siddha (perfect before) and vrata-siddha (perfected by the vow). Even the purva-siddhas performed (ceruh) the vow with the others due to being under the spell of joviality. “Hey girls (abalah)! Perfect girls! (siddhah = he siddhah). Go to the village.” “How will we go without the accomplishment of the resolve?” Understanding their minds, He says mayemah and so on. The sense is: “You will enjoy as many nights as there will be after this one. For the time being, the only bodily contact has been My contact with your clothes.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Or satih (enduring, etc.) is an adjective of ksapah (nights), insofar as it is impossible that a case ending used by the Lord be in another way.

### 10.22.28

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*ity adista bhagavata labdha-kamah kumarikah \|*  
*dhyayantyas tat-padambhojam krcchran nirvivisur vrajam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah uvaca—Sri Suka said; iti—in this way; adistah—ordered; bhagavata—by the Lord; labdha-kamah—they whose desire was obtained (fulfilled); kumarikah—the young girls; dhyayantyah— while meditating; tat-pada-ambhojam—His lotuslike feet; krcchrat— with difficulty; nirvivisuh vrajam—they set out for the cowherd village.

*sri-sukah uvaca—iti bhagavata adistah labdha-kamah kumarikah tat-padambhojam dhyayantyah vrajam krcchrat nirvivisuh.*

**Перевод:**

**Sri Suka said: Ordered by the Lord in this way, the girls, whose desire was fulfilled, set out for the village with difficulty, while meditating on His lotus feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“They were ordered: “Go to the village” (iti = vrajam yata iti).” Bhagavata (by the Lord) is because of the manifestation of the all in all of the essence of godhood by the foreshadowing of the excellence of the games of Rasa.

Labdha-kamah signifies “they by whom their desire was achieved,” mostly because they had that sort of bhava, and on top of that because of getting the order in that way of Him whose promise comes true. Nonetheless, they entered (nirvivisuh = pravisam) the village, only with difficulty (krcchrat = duhkhena eva). Why? tat- padambhojam dhyayantyah, “They were only meditating on His lotus feet,” but not directly seeing them. This means: On account of separation from Him.

Although they might think that the condition of the accomplishment of their wish occurred just by the boon of Katyayani, the reconciliation is that the vow was successful only due to the supereminence of worshiping a person dear to Him. This points the direction.

There is another rendering, by a coalescence of the vowel a, the words bhagavatalabdha-kamah stand for bhagavata alabdha-kamah: “they by whom the desire, a special fun with Him immediately, was not achieved” (= na labdhah kamah sadyah eva tena saha krida- visesah yabhih), therefore: krcchrat (they went “with difficulty”). The reason for not getting what they wanted is kumarikah (little girls). This means they were not qualified for His entertainment then, due to extreme childhood. By the power of the favor done by the Lord and due to the nature of the women of the village, in only a little time they will become qualified for that.

Someone might wonder: “Then why did they leave?” He answers: dhyayantyah (while meditating). The sense is: Because of the pacification of the torment of the heart, simply by a meditation on His divine feet, from which flows the Rasa of the topmost bliss, the mitigator of all distress. Or, they were contemplating (dhyayantyah = cintayantyah) upon His lotus feet, i.e. on the fun that they were going to have with them.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The commentary is the same as the second paragraph above. In addition:) Padambhoja (lotus feet) is the special mention of a detail because of high regard in terms of having the concept of being wives, or else because they, who had become submissive with shyness at that time, set out by looking only at His feet and proceeded further by constantly remembering Him on the way.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Krcchrat (with difficulty) is because He had stolen their hearts, their eyes, and so on.

### 10.22.29

*atha gopaih parivrto bhagavan devaki-sutah \|*  
*vrndavanad gato duram carayan gah sahagrajah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

atha—afterward; gopaih parivrtah—surrounded by cow herders; bhagavan—the Lord; devaki-sutah—Devaki’s son; vrndavanat— from Vrndavana; gatah—went; duram—far; carayan gah—while grazing cows; saha-agrajah—who was with the elder brother.
