*atha bhagavan devaki-sutah gopaih parivrtah sahagrajah gah carayan vrndavanad duram gatah.*

**Перевод:**

**Later on, surrounded by cow herders and accompanied by His elder brother, the Lord, Devaki’s son, went far from Vrndavana while grazing cows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*bhaktyanukampya kanyas tas tad-vivarjita-yajvanam \|*  
*patny-anugrahatas tesam ahan karma-maha-madam \|\|*

**“Having shown compassion to those virgins with bhakti, by a favor to the wives of performers of Vedic sacrifices who were devoid of that He put an end to those men’s great overweening pride in regard to rites.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Now, on the occasion, in order to talk about the grace to the wives of ritualistic Brahmanas, which was like the grace to the divine cowherd virgins, he begins the narration of an incidental occurrence related to that event. Atha means kalantare (at another time), that is, “at some point in summertime,” since it is going to be said: nidagharkatape tigme, “in the torrid heat of the summer sun” (in the next verse). Therefore: sahagrajah, “accompanied by Baladeva,” inasmuch as Baladeva was not with Him on the day that the garments of the virgin cowherd girls were stolen.

He was surrounded by cow herders on all sides (parivrtah = paritah vrtah). The mention of them at first is in consideration of the special requirement of them in the pastime about to be told. He is Devaki’s son: This term is used because He is perceived only in that way by the yajna-patnis, who stay in Mathura, and so the significance is: After attracting them by means of a bhava, He went far from Vrndavana to go near their homes, because: bhagavan, “He is most compassionate” (= parama-dayaluh).

There is another interpretation. ‘Devaki’ denotes ‘Yasoda’. This has already been explained, and so going far from there was just to show favor to the divine yajha-patnis. Further, in reference to the course of thought in Sri Svamipada’s explanation (Bhavartha- dipika 10.22.38): At first it was because of the inappropriateness of Baladeva’s arrival there at that time; afterward he came and was met, so the following is to be understood: It occurred in Pausa (mid December to mid January).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Now, having mentioned the grace to the divine cowherd virgins, by virtue of a similarity with that context he begins to describe the grace to the wives of ritualistic Brahmanas.

(Additions are underlined.) Atha signifies lilantarambhe (at the outset of another pastime): that should be understood as: “in summertime,” since it is going to be said: nidagharkatape tigme, “in the torrid heat of the summer sun” (in the next verse). Therefore: sahagrajah, “accompanied by Baladeva,” inasmuch as Baladeva was not with Him on the day that the garments of the virgin cowherd girls were stolen. He was surrounded by cow herders on all sides (parivrtah = paritah vrtah). The mention of them at first is due to the special requirement of them in the pastime about to be told. He is Devaki’s son: That is said because of a previous reason. Regarding vrndavanad gato duram (He went far from Vrndavana): Right at first. He went to Kamvakavana. where there are many hills.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*gopa-kanya-prasadasya prastutyarohitah smrtau \|*  
*yajna-patni-prasado ’tas tam vivaksur abhun munih \|\|*

**“By an eminent praise of the grace to virgin cowherd girls, the grace to the wives of ritualistic Brahmanas rose in the memory, therefore the sage became desirous of narrating it.”**

Atha (later on) is suggestive of another time. The sense is: “at some point in time in the summer season.”

### 10.22.30

*nidagharkatape tigme chayabhih svabhir atmanah \|*  
*atapatrayitan viksya druman aha vrajaukasah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

nidagha—summer; arka—of the sun; atape—in the heat; tigme— torrid; chayabhih svabhih—with their multiple shade; atmanah—for Himself; atapatrayitan—which were acting like parasols; viksya— looking at; druman—trees; aha—He says (He spoke); vraja- okasah—to them whose residence is Vraja.

*nidagharkatape tigme, svabhih chayabhih atmanah atapatrayitan druman viksya (bhagavan) vrajaukasah (prati) aha (sma).*

**Перевод:**

**Observing the trees that were acting like parasols for Him in the torrid heat of the summer sun with their shade, He addressed the residents of Vraja.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Why did He go far? Suka talks about it, in seven verses. Atmanah (for Himself) signifies sri-bhagavatah (for the Lord). He spoke to the residents of Vraja, that is, to the cow herders, mostly because the cow herders who were in the forest were benefited by trees, and because, on account of friendship, the occurrence of what is dear to them and what is not dear to them should be described.

Or, the trees were acting like parasols toward His residents of Vraja, i.e. toward the cow herders, the cows, and so forth (atmano vrajaukasah = gopa-gavadayah tan prati). Or: atmanah prati (toward His own). The plural is because the cow herders, who are acknowledged to have a nondifferent mood on account of being most dear, are forms of Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In that regard, in seven verses he talks about the manner of walking in Vrndavana. Atmanah is a partial indication: “Looking at trees that were in the forest of Vraja (vrajaukasah =vraja-vana-vartinah) and that were acting like parasols for Him and for those who belong to Him (atmanah = svasya svesam ca), he spoke (aha = vakti = vakti sma).”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“He spoke to the homeboys” (vrajaukasah = nija-saha-vasinah).

### 10.22.31-32

*he stokakrsna he amso sridaman subalarjuna \|*  
*visala vrsabhaujasvin devaprastha varuthapa \|\|*  
*pasyataitan maha-bhagan pararthaikanta-jivitan \|*  
*vata-varsatapa-himan sahanto varayanti nah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

he stoka-krsna—O Stokakrsna (“little Krsna”); he amso—O Amsu (“ray”); sri-ddman—O Sridama (“one who gives resplendence”); su-bala—O Subala (“he who has good strength”); arjuna—O Arjuna (“white”); visala—O Visala (“colossal”); Vrsabha—O Vrsabha (“bull,” “best”); ojasvin—O Ojasvi (“he whose has vigor”); deva- prastha—O Devaprastha (“he who has a mountain top (a white parasol) for God"); varutha-pa—O Varuthapa (“the protector of a multitude”);

*pasyata—you should see; etan—these ones; maha-bhagan—whose good fortune is great; para-artha—for the sake of others; ekanta— solely; jivitan—whose life; vata—the wind; varsa—rain; atapa— sunshine; himan—and snow; sahantah—tolerating; varayanti—they block \[them\]; nah—for us.*

*he stokakrsna! he amso! sridaman! subala! arjuna! visala! vrsabha! ojasvin! devaprastha! varuthapa! (yuyam) etan maha-bhagan pararthaikanta-jivitan (druman) pasyata, (ete drumah) vata- varsatapa-himan sahantah nah (vatadin) varayanti.*

**Перевод:**

**“Hey Stokakrsna! Hey Amsu, Sridama, Subala, Arjuna, Visala, Vrsabha, Ojasvi, Devaprastha, Varuthapa! Look at these ones. They are very fortunate: Their lives are solely for the sake of others. Tolerating the wind, the rain, the sunshine, and the snow, they block them for us.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

While going to the enclosed location for fire sacrifices to show favor to the wives of Brahmanas, in four verses He praises them: “Trees are even better than those men,” intending to say: Brahmanas are hardhearted.

“Hey Stokakrsna and other cow herders! See these trees (etan = etan druman) whose lives are solely for the sake of others (pararthaikanta-jivitan = parartham eva ekantena jivitam yesam tan)." That is what He expounds: “Themselves tolerating (sahantah = svayam sahamanah) the wind, the rain, etc., they block them for us (nah = asmakam)."

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

He calls the very foremost boys one by one with priti. Although Sridama is foremost, calling Stokakrsna at first is because he is a friend as one who has a similar name and because he was abiding right in front.

These ten were appointed by Queen Yasoda for the purpose of looking after Krsna in the eight directions. They are to be understood in conformity with what is said in the uttara-khanda in Sri Bhagavatamrta. Of those boys, Stokakrsna and others are in the four cardinal directions sequentially, starting from the east. Arjuna and others are in the intermediate directions, beginning from the northeast. Devaprastha and Varuthapa hold the parasol and clear the paths: They are situated above and below. The eleventh, Bhadrasena, is the boss of cow herders. He takes care of everything. It is indicated that he was far at that time. He takes care of things, close-by and far away.

Maha-bhagan signifies: “them who have great good fortune” (= mahan bhagah bhagyam yesam tan). He talks about that characteristic, with para and so on. Nah means asmakam (for us), that is, “for us cowherds” or “for all living entities.” Some block the wind and so forth.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The sequence in calling is to be understood according to who was in sight. These ten abide with prema in the eight directions, for the object of looking after Krsna. Some opine so, due to being ten in number. Of those boys, the eight beginning from Stokakrsna are in the eight directions. Devaprastha and Varuthapa hold the parasol and clear the paths: They are situated above and below. The eleventh, Bhadrasena, is the boss of cow herders, and Rama takes care of everything. It is indicated that he was far at that time. Maha-bhagan signifies... (The rest of the commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In four verses, This is told: After calling the sakhas, He praises the trees to let one understand this meaning: The boon of a birth in the species of exalted trees, not a birth in the category of Brahmanas who are miserable karmis, is worthy of being requested by sadhus.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

The masculine gender in vata-varsatapa-himan is poetic license.97

### 10.22.33

*aho esam varam janma sarva-prany-upajivanam \|*  
*sujanasyeva yesam vai vimukha yanti narthinah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

aho—(a word used to express astonishment); esam—of these \[trees\]; varam—better; janma—the birth (the life); sarva-prani—of all living entities; upajivinam—because of which there is the means of subsistence; su-janasya—of a good person; iva—like; yesam—of which \[trees\]; vai—indeed; vimukhah—disappointed; yanti—they go; na—do not; arthinah—askers (“those who have a motive”).

*aho! sarva-prany-upajivanam esam (drumanam) janma varam (bhavati), yesam (drumanam sthane agatah janah), sujanasya (grhe agatah) arthinah (janah) iva (vimukhah na yanti), vimukhah vai na yanti.*

**Перевод:**

**“How amazing! The life of these trees, because of which all living entities have subsistence, is better. Indeed, those who go near them do not leave disappointed, like persons who ask a good fellow do not become disgruntled.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Like those who ask (arthina iva) a compassionate person (sujanasya = krpaloh).”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

These trees do not only dispel the inconvenience of the wind and so forth, they facilitate the accomplishment of all objectives. This is what He says in two verses. Aho has the sense of either vismaya (astonishment) or harsa (joy). Varam (better) signifies: sarvatah srestham (best of all). Why? sarva-prany-upajivanam, “The birth of these trees is the cause of the subsistence of all living entities” (= sarvesam praninam jivika-hetuh). In the reading jivinam, the sense is the same: The suffix \[n\] in\[i\] is added after the word, which ends in the causative \[n\]i. That is just what He talks about: “Persons (janah is added) do not leave disappointed from them (yesam = yebhyah). Vai (indeed) has the sense of prasiddhi (renown).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Sujanasya means atitheyasya (of a hospi¬table person). Arthinah means yacakah (askers).

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Yesam should read yebhyah.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“The birth of these trees is better than a birth as a human (varam = manusya-janmanah srestham).” Moreover, "Those who ask them (yesam arthinah), who are like a munificent person (sujanasya iva = vadanyasya iva), do not leave disappointed.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“Like those who ask a good person (sujanasya arthinah iva), those who ask them (yesam = yesam arthinah) never leave disappointed.”

### 10.22.34

*patra-puspa-phala-cchaya-mula-valkala-darubhih \|*  
*gandha-niryasa-bhasmasthi-tokmaih kaman vitanvate \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

patra—with leaves; puspa—flowers; phala—fruits; chaya—shade; mula—roots; valkala—bark; darubhih—and wood; gandha—with the aroma; niryasa—sap (“exudation”); bhasma—ashes; asthi—logs (“bone”); tokmaih—and shoots; kaman—desires; vitanvate—they expand (they expansively fulfill).

*(ete drumah) patra-puspa-phala-cchaya-mula-valkala-darubhih gandha-niryasa-bhasmasthi-tokmaih (karanena arthinam jananam) kaman vitanvate.*

**Перевод:**

**“With their leaves, flowers, fruits, shade, roots, bark, and pieces of wood, and with their aroma, sap, ashes, logs, and shoots, they expansively fulfill one’s desires.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Niryasa means ghana-rasah (‘thick liquid’, i.e. sap). In tokmaih, tokmah (shoots) means pallavady-ankurah (sprouts such as buds).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Here He says the trees also fulfill the desires of those who are not asking. “They completely and expansively fulfill (vitanvate = vistarena paripurayanti) desires (kaman = icchah).”

Mula denotes the jada plant, for medicine and so on. It does not denote the support of a tree, for without it the trees would perish. The aroma originates from sap and so on (gandha = rasadi-bhava). Bhasma (ashes) connotes: darv-adi-jam angaradi (charcoal, etc., originating from wooden pieces). Asthi (bone) signifies saramsa (the aspect that is the core: logs). Alternatively, daru means fuel (indhanam) that is external and that originates from minor branches, etc., which are drying by themselves, and asthi is internal wood that is to be split, or it denotes huge branches, for the purpose of posts and so on. The trees fulfill all desires with one or more of those. A greatness like that of a wish-fulfilling tree is suggested.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(This is the same.) Here He says the trees also fulfill the desires of those who are not asking. The aroma originates from sap, etc. (gandha = rasadi-bhava). Asthi means saramsa.

### 10.22.35

*etavaj janma-saphalyam dehinam iha dehisu \|*  
*pranair arthair dhiya vaca sreya-acaranam sada \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

etavat—this much; janma-saphalyam—the fruitfulness of a birth (the success of life); dehinam—of embodied beings; iha—here (in this world); dehisu—to embodied beings; pranaih—with the life airs; arthaih—with multiple wealth; dhiya—with the intelligence; vaca—with speech; sreyah—of the highest good; acaranam—the performance; sada—always.

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

*(yat) sada iha (samsare) pranaih arthaih dhiya vaca (ca) dehisu sreya-acaranam (bhavati), etavad (eva) dehinam janma-saphalyam (bhavati).*

**“In this world, the success of the life of embodied beings is this: To always do the highest good to other living beings, with one’s vitality, wealth, intelligence, and words.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

He talks about the resultant meaning. “To always do the highest good to living beings (dehisu sreya-acaranam sada = jivesu sada sreyasah acaranam yat)." Dhiya (with the intelligence) means sad-upaya-cintanadina (by contemplating on the genuine means of success, etc.). Vaca (with speech) denotes upadesadi-rupaya (with advice, etc.).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The connection is: janmanah saphalyam etavad eva, “The success of taking birth is exactly this.”

### 10.22.36

*iti pravala-stabaka-phala-puspa-dalotkaraih \|*  
*tarunam namra-sakhanam madhyena yamunam gatah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

iti—(marks the end of the quotation); pravala—of buds; stabaka— clusters of flowers; phala—fruits; puspa—flowers; dala—and leaves; utkaraih—by multitudes; tarunam—of trees; namra-sakhanam— whose branches were bowed; madhyena—through the midst; yamunam—to the Yamuna; gatah—He went.

*iti (druman abhinandan bhagavan) pravala-stabaka-phala-puspa-dalotkaraih namra-sakhanam tarunam madhyena yamunam gatah.*

**Перевод:**

**Saying so, He went to the Yamuna by meandering through the woods, where the boughs bowed because of multitudes of buds, flower clusters, fruits, blossoms, and leaves.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Having done a praise in this way (iti = iti abhinandan), He reached (gatah = praptah) the Yamuna by going in between trees whose branches were bowing (namra-sakhanam = nata-sakhanam) because of multitudes of shoots and so on (pravala-stabaka-phala-puspa-dalotkaraih = pravaladi-samuhaih)."

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Stabaka (cluster of flowers) is in the plural and means puspanam patranam ca gucchah (bunches of flowers and of leaves). The flowers (puspa) and the leaves (dala) mentioned were not mixed. He went in between trees, that is, by the path in the midst of trees (madhyena = madhya-varti-vartmana). Not getting the torrid heat in this way and going far from a multitude of such trees are implied, therefore he will say: ksudhartah (‘pained by hunger’, 10.22.38), for otherwise it would be possible to appease the hunger only with their fruits and so forth, therefore the path was adorned by asoka trees, whose fruits are unfit for eating.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Stabaka is in the plural and means puspanam gucchakah (bunches of flowers). Madhyena portends: madhya-varti-vartmana (by the path in the midst). In this way they did not feel the torrid heat.

### 10.22.37

*tatra gah payayitvapah sumrstah sitalah sivah \|*  
*tato nrpa svayam gopah kamam svadu papur jalam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatra—there; gah payayitva—making the cows drink; apah—the water; su-mrstah—very clear; sitalah—cool; sivah—beneficial; tatah—after that; nrpa—O king; svayam—themselves; gopah—the cow herders; kamam—at will; svadu—tasty; papuh—drank; jalam— the water.

*nrpa! gopah tatra sumrstah sitalah sivah apah gah payayitva tatah svayam svadu jalam kamam papuh.*

**Перевод:**

**The cow herders induced the cows to drink the clear, cool, and beneficial water there, O king, and then they themselves freely drank the tasty water.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

By nature, the water of the Yamuna is sweet. By a connection with Vrndavana it is even sweeter. The water was pleasurable (sivah = sukha-karih). Or the sense is it was auspicious (sivah = mangala-rupah).

Tatah means tad-anantaram eva (immediately after that) because: gopah svayam (the cow herders themselves), since they considered that the cows’ happiness is superior to theirs. Or: svayam bhagavan gopas ca, “Himself, i.e. the Lord, and the cowherds.” Or the sense is the boys drank by themselves (svayam), with cupped hands, without the need for a container. Someone might argue: “Isn’t there an injunction that one should not drink water from the hand?” He responds: gopah. The gist is it is fitting for them, because they don’t have to follow injunctions and prohibitions.

The drift of the vocative nrpa is: “As protecting citizens is primordial for you, so protecting cows is primary for them: Drinking it afterward by not considering one’s own well-being is certainly appropriate.”

Although all qualities such as tastiness are suggested by saying sumrstah (very clear) and so on, the repeated mention svadu jalam (tasty water) is due to being the reason for kamam papuh: “They drank at will (kamam = yathestam).” Or, it might be suspected that the good qualities of the water changed because so many cows went to the bank to drink, therefore the reiteration is said to repudiate that. “They drank the water, which was still tasty (svadu = svadu eva)." The glory of the water is stated thus.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) They made the cows drink the water of the Yamuna (tatra = tasyah). The water was very clear (sumrstah = atisvacchah). By virtue of not bringing about a disease and by being a bestower of punya, it effected auspiciousness (sivah = mangala-karah). Tatah means tad-anantaram eva (immediately after that) because: gopah. Such is their occupation. The drift of the vocative nrpa is: “Protecting cows is their dharma, just like you protect citizens.” The sense of svadu (tasty) is the water had qualities such as great clearness although hosts of animals were agitating it: The glory of the water is said in this way. Thus they drank at will (kamam = yathestam). Consequently the repetition in using the word jalam (water) is meaningful.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Sivah signifies sreyas-karah, “\[water,\] which makes for the highest benefit.”

### 10.22.38

*tasya upavane kamam carayantah pasun nrpa \|*  
*krsna-ramav upagamya ksudharta idam abruvan \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tasyah—of her (of the Yamuna); upavane—in a subforest; kamam— at will; carayantah pasun—while grazing the animals; nrpa—O king; krsna-ramau upagamya—after going near Krsna and Rama; ksudha—by hunger; artah—pained; idam—this; abruvan—they said.

*nrpa! (gopah) tasyah upavane pasun kamam carayantah ksudha artah (santah) krsna-ramau upagamya idam abruvan.*

**Перевод:**

**Incommodated by hunger while tending the animals at will in a woodland near the Yamuna, O king, they approached Krsna and Rama, and spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

It is said ksudhartah (pained by hunger) because they had left before the virgin girls did. The boys had not taken lunch due to being overwhelmed by His humor.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

It was in a subforest mostly adorned by asoka trees. It is to be known in this way, for it is told like that later on (10.23.21). They were tending the animals at will, i.e. in accordance with the animals’ desire. Hence, while awakening hunger by wandering around, hunger arose also by drinking water in the Yamuna and because there was no fruit in that woodland.

They were being pained, that is, either troubled or distracted (artah = duhkhitah vyagrah va santah), by the desire to eat (ksudha = bubhuksaya). Although it is impossible that they could be pained by that, let alone by the Lord, it’s understood that this occurred because Krsna wanted to do a favor to the wives of ritualistic Brahmanas by begging for food. In truth, however, the boys inferred that the Lord had hunger.

Arriving near Them (upagamya = samipe agatya)—owing to the occurrence of self-restraint in talking from afar; or due to the importance of the meaning about to be told—they spoke this, what is going to be said (idam = vaksyamanam).”

The chapter comes to an end here. That way, the episode is unexpectedly cut in half. As before, Badarayani was stunned for a moment by remembering a special pastime that he is about to narrate. Or it is because of holding silence for an instant to enlighten the listeners about its underlying mystery. It should be inferred in like manner elsewhere as well.

The vocative nrpa is used by Badarayani to get the king’s utmost attention in listening to an astonishing pastime. Or, the reason for calling him again and again was explained earlier.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In point of ksudhartah, a particular pain, by inferring the hunger of Sri Krsna and of Sri Rama as well, is to be understood. His mention of that is the arrangement of prema. However, the boys will say to the Brahmanas who perform Vedic sacrifices: ramacyutau vo lasato bubhuksitau, “Rama and Acyuta are tending cows not too far away. Both are hungry and want your food.” (10.23.7).

Unlike what they did on other days, the boys did not bring yogurt and rice on that day because Krsna wanted to do a favor to the wives of sacrificial Brahmanas under some pretext. The degradation of the sacrificial performers will be illustrated just to show those ladies’ eminence. It’s understood that the trees were extolled only to point out how those men are. “Arriving near Them...” (The rest of the commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

They were grazing the animals in a woodland in proximity to the Yamuna (tasya upa vane = yamunayah samipe vane). Though they had eaten in the early morning, the cow herders were pained by hunger (ksudhartah = ksudha piditah).

## Chapter 23 - Krsna is Merciful to the Wives of Ritualistic Brahmanas

### 10.23.1

*gopa ucuh*  
*rama rama maha-baho krsna dusta-nibarhana \|*  
*esa vai badhate ksun nas tac-chantim kartum arhathah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

gopah ucuh—the cow herders said; rama—O Rama; rama—O Rama; maha-baho—O You whose arms are great; krsna—O Krsna; dusta-nibarhana—O killer of rogues; esa—this (the well-known); vai—indeed; badhate—is bothering; ksut—hunger; nah—us; tat-santim—the appeasement of it; kartum arhathah—both of You ought to do.

*gopah ucuh—rama! rama! maha-baho! krsna! dusta-nibarhana! esa ksut nah badhate, (atah yuvam) tac-chantim kartum arhathah (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**The cow herders said: “Rama, Rama! O You of mighty arms! O Krsna, slayer of rogues! Hunger is bothering us. You should appease it.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*travovimse tato gopair anna-yacnapadesatah \|*  
*tat-patny-anugrahat krsno diksitan anvatapayat \|\|*

**“In the twenty-third chapter, Krsna made initiated Brahmanas repent by doing a favor to their wives on the pretext of asking for food by the intermediary of the cow herders.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Rama is a vocative. The derivation is: ramayati, sarvan eva sukhayati iti ramah, “He makes everyone happy, and so he is named Rama.” The gist is: “he makes us happy too.” The repetition is due to the pang of hunger. With the vocative maha-baho, they hint at his special ability in that regard. In the reading maha-virya, the sense is the same.

The significance of ‘Krsna’ is: paramananda-ghana-murte, “O You whose body is the topmost dense bliss,” and so the drift is: “In the case of those who are Yours, the trouble of hunger is inappropriate.” And specifically: dusta-nibarhana (O killer of villains). The idea is: “Put an end to our hunger, which gives us trouble and is also an enemy.” This is from Sruti: ksut khalu vai manusyasya bhratrvya-satruh, “Indeed, hunger is the enemy of a man.” Esa, “this \[hunger\],” means adhuna saksat (now, manifestly). Or it is directly perceptible (esa = pratyaksa) by signs such as a dry mouth. Vai means niscitam (indeed). By an expression of humility: arhatah (‘the two of You should’, a polite expression in Sanskrit), it is made to be understood that it must be done. Or arhatah denotes: yogyau bhavatah, “Both of You are suited \[for that\].” This suitability too is implied by the vocatives, which are conformable to this meaning. Asking both of Them with a special fondness is due to the nondifference of Those two. In that regard, addressing the elder first is in consideration of a worldly custom; or it is because of the nonexcellence of showing affection to Krsna by slighting Rama. For this reason there is also a pair of vocatives directed at Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Though they were pained by hunger, the boys, not considering that trees are fulfillers of desires, a fact praised by Him based upon a special humor from the nature of friendship, give up the ways of men and request Him who had brought them to a faraway woodland.

The sense of rama is: asman api ramayati, “He delights us too.” The repetition is due to the pang of hunger. In point of the vocative maha-baho, the capability is mentioned... (The rest is the same. Moreover:) Asking both of Them with a special affection is due to the nondifference of Those two. In that regard, a vocative for Rama at first and the repetition in the same place are on account of Sri Krsna’s happiness by thus showing deference, a form of customary etiquette, to him. He Himself will say: kirtayantah and so on: “while proclaiming the names of the Lord, of My elder brother, and of Mine” (10.23.4).

Esa (“this” hunger) signifies: duhsahatvena anubhuyamana, “being experienced as difficult to bear.” Arhatah means yogyau bhavatah, “Both of You are suited \[for that\],” hence it’s implied that They must do so. In truth, this too is simply one type of fun.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*trayovimse ’nna-yacnana-drtair gopaih punas ca sa \|*  
*patninam prema vipranam anutapas ca varnyate \|\|*

**“In the twenty-third, this is described: The request for food by cow herders, who were disregarded; that request once more; the prema of the wives; and the repentance of the Brahmanas.”**

**10.23.1**

Regarding ksun nah (hunger is bothering us): “If now both of You are able to end our hunger, our big enemy—from the statement of Sruti: ksut...—, only then will Your respective epithets as maha-bahu (strong-armed) and krsna dusta-nibarhana (killer of villains) be meaningful.” Humor is implied in this way.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

*trayovimse tv anna-yacna gopair vipran prati prabhoh \|*  
*tat-patninam para bhaktis tesam tapas ca varnyate \|\|*

**“In the twenty-third chapter, a request of food by cow herders to Brahmanas from the Almighty, the topmost bhakti of their wives, and the repentance of those men are described.”**

### 10.23.2

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*iti vijnapito gopair bhagavan devaki-sutah \|*  
*bhaktaya vipra-bharyayah prasidann idam abravit \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah uvaca—Sri Suka said; iti—in this way; vijnapitah— entreated; gopaih—by cow herders; bhagavan—the Lord; devaki-sutah—Devaki’s son; bhaktayah—who is a devotee (who are devotees); vipra-bharyayah—toward the wife of a Brahmana (to wives of Brahmanas); prasidan—to be gracious; idam—this; abravit—said.

*sri-sukah uvaca—iti gopaih vijnapitah (san) bhagavan devaki-sutah bhaktayah vipra-bharyayah prasidan idam abravit.*

**Перевод:**

**Sri Suka said: Entreated by cow herders in this way, the Lord, Devaki’s son, spoke as follows to be gracious toward Brahmanas’ wives who were devotees.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The singular in bhaktayah is used with the intent to express sayujya at once.99

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Being informed in a special manner ( vijnapitah = visesena jnapitah san)—with a polite request and by hinting at the pang of hunger—in this way (iti = anena prakarena), the master of the universe (jagad-isvarah),100meaning He has all powers, spoke the following (idam = vaksyamanam).” Why? “He wanted to do a favor to the Brahmanas’ wives (vipra-bharyayah prasidan = tah prati anugraham kartum icchan).” The singular in bharyayah has the sense of jati (category).

The reason for that is: bhaktayah, which signifies either that they had done bhajana to the Lord for a long time or that they had faith in and reverence for the Lord for a long time. Still, asking Brahmanas at first was done to demonstrate the greatness only of those ladies. This will become clear ahead.

Someone might wonder: “How did they become devotees?” He responds: bhagavan. The idea is: by His revealing His special godhood. Or the sense is: bhakta-vatsalah. This is the reason for a special grace by means of repeatedly begging. Therefore even though boys requested both of Them, only He gave a reply, since only He is qualified in every way in that matter.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) “The Lord (bhagavan), He who has all powers, spoke the following (idam = vaksyamanam)— why?—to show favor to Brahmanas’ wives (vipra-bharyayah prasidan = tah prati anugraham kartum).” The singular is used in the sense of jati (category), to make all those ladies, indistinctly, reach a certain condition. The reason for doing them a favor is: bhaktayah, which signifies that they had love (rati) for the Lord for a long time. Still, asking the Brahmanas at first was done to demonstrate the greatness only of those ladies. This will become clear ahead.

Someone might wonder: “How did they become devotees.” He responds: jagad-isvarah. At that time He was revealing both sweetness and godly might in the world. The drift is: How can it possibly be conceived that those women whose hearts are extremely super soft did not perform bhakti to Him? Sometimes the reading is devaki-sutah.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The ladies were devotees (bhaktayah); He was pleased (prasidan) at once by remembering those ladies’ bhakti. Additionally, remembering that only one lady (bhaktayah = ekasyah tu) among them was going to have the tenth state (prema), He was also intensely lamenting (prasidan = prakarsena sidan ca) (sidan = socamanah). Some say the singular is for the purpose of obtaining these two meanings.101

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

He is the Lord, meaning He can do anything. He is Devaki’s son; this means He is most compassionate: He is more merciful to women. He fosters the path of bhakti.

### 10.23.3

*prayata deva-yajanam brahmana brahma-vadinah \|*  
*satram angirasam nama hy asate svarga-kamyaya \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

prayata—all of you should go; deva-yajanam—to the sacrificial grounds (“where there are sacrifices to gods”); brahmanah— Brahmanas; brahma-vadinah—who are Brahmavadis (those who expose the Vedas; or those for whom the concept of Brahman is topmost); satram—a sacrifice (“where people are sitting”); angirasam nama—called Angirasa; hi—obviously; asate—are sitting (are doing) (see the Commentary); svarga-kamyaya—with a desire for Svarga.

*(yuyam) deva-yajanam prayata, (yatra) brahmanah brahma-vadinah satram angirasam nama svarga-kamyaya asate.*

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

*(gopah! yatra) brahma-vadinah brahmanah svarga-kamyaya angirasam nama satram asate, (tad) deva-yajanam prayata.*

**“All of you should go the sacrificial grounds where Brahmanas who are Brahmavadis are sitting for the session called Angirasa with a desire to attain Svarga.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Deva-yajanam means yajna-vatam (the sacrificial grounds). Brahma-vadinah signifies: veda-ghosana-silah, “those whose habit is to proclaim the Vedas,” but not: vedartha-vidah (those whose know the goal of the Vedas): This is the secret intention. Therefore: “They are performing a sacrifice (satram asate = yajnam anutisthanti) with a desire for Svarga.” Hi means niscitam (surely).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Since there is no bhakti in the Brahmanas though they have tapas (the practice of austerity), vidya (knowledge, skill), and dharma (the sense of duty), I do not have a kind disposition (prasada) to them, but since their wives have bhakti though they are devoid of tapas and so on, I am kindly disposed toward those ladies.” To make one aware of these two meanings related to the category of Brahmana, at first He tells the cow herders to send a message to the Brahmanas.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Prasada does not occur merely due to attributes such as upavita-samskara (investiture with a sacred thread), but only due to bhakti. Brahma-vadinah means veda-vadinah, “they habitually talk about the Vedas (Vedic rites).”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Satram denotes bahu-kartrkam (a sacrifice where many priests are involved). In regard to Angirasa, Angirasa means Jupiter. Asate means kurvate (they are doing). The word hi has the sense of hetu (‘because’): yasmat satre annam deyam tasmat prayata, “Because food is to be given in a sacrifice, you should go.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

The angirasa satra goes on for twenty-four days and nights.

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

Svarga-kamyaya (with a desire for Svarga) signifies: svarga-prapticchaya (with the desire to attain heaven).

**Annotation**

There is a grammatically technical discussion by Sridhara Svami on the topic of satram asate (“they sat a sacrifice” i.e. “they did a sacrifice”). He explains the words satram asata in Bhagavatam 1.1.4 as follows: satra-samjnakam karmoddisya asata upavivisuh. yad va asatakurvatety arthah, alabheta nirvapati upayantity-adi-vat-pratyayoccarana-matrarthatvenaster dhatv-arthasyavivaksitatvat, ““They sat down (asata = upavivisuh), aiming at the rite called Satra.” Or, asata (they sit) means akurvata (they did), inasmuch as the meaning of the verbal root as (2A) (to sit) is not meant to be expressed, since the intention is merely to voice the verbal suffix, as in the case of alabheta, nirvapati, upayanti, and so on” (Bhavartha- dipika 1.1.4).

The underlying idea here is that a verbal suffix merely conveys the sense of the verbal root \[du\]kr\[n\] karane (to do), and the meaning of the verbal root itself is not taken into account, like in the examples: (1) agnistomiya-pasor alabhanam alabhate (he does the prescribed killing of a sacrificial animal), where alabhate means kurute (he does), (2) amavasyayam pitrbhyah sraddham nirvapati (on the newmoon day he performs the sraddha ceremony for the ancestors), where nirvapati means karoti (he does), and (3) asta-varsayah parinayanam upayanti (they carry out the marriage of an eight-year old girl), where upayanti means kurvanti (they do). These examples are taken from Bhavartha-dipika-prakasa 1.1.4.

Further, the word satra is made by applying the Unadi suffix tra after the verbal root sad\[l\], mentioned in a footnote above, by gu-dhr-vi-paci-vaci-yami-sadi-ksadibhyas trah (Unadi-sutra 4.168). The derivation is: sidanti yatreti satra, yajno va satah sat-purusan trayate tat satram ity vyutpatty-antaram, “A satra is that where persons sit. Or it means a sacrifice. Another derivation is: “It delivers eminent men”” (Svami-dayananda-vrtti 4.168). Vamsidhara Pandita adds that the proper spelling is sattra: satah sujanan trayata iti sattram, “It delivers good persons, and so it is sattram” (Bhavartha-dipika- prakasa 1.1.4). In usage, sattra became satra because the sound is the same.

### 10.23.4

*tatra gatvaudanam gopa yacatasmad-visarjitah \|*  
*kirtayanto bhagavata aryasya mama cabhidham \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatra—there; gatva—having gone; odanam—food (“boiled rice”); gopah—O cow herders; yacata—you should beg; asmat-visarjitah— sent by Us; kirtayantah—while mentioning (or while glorifying); bhagavatah—of the Lord; aryasya—of the venerable one (of the elder brother); mama—of Mine; ca—and; abhidham—the name.

*gopah! (yuyam) asmad-visarjitah (santah) tatra gatva bhagavatah aryasya mama ca abhidham kirtayantah odanam yacata (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Cow herders! When you, sent by Us, go there, beg food while proclaiming the names of the Lord, of My elder brother, and of Mine.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Being dispatched by both of Us (asmad-visarjitah = avabhyam prahitah santah), you should beg (yacata = yacadhvam). What’s embarrassing about this?” In case they reply: “Why would they give to us, since we are not worthy recipients?”, He says kirtayantah and the rest.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

The boys might respond: “We Vaisnavas don’t need to beg their food.” He replies: asmad-visarjitah (sent by Us). The sense is: “Since We are the dispatchers, that fault will not stick to you.” “But a fault sticks even to those who are following.” To that He says: kirtayantah. The drift is: “By a kirtana of Our names, that fault will become nil.” Why? bhagavatah, “\[the name\] of He who has all powers” (= sarva-saktimatah). The manner of begging too, by means of a kirtana of the Lord’s names, is taught to beggars in this way.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

He says asmad-visarjitah with this intention: “Should you think highly of your timidity, announce yourselves as Our order carriers, but not with the names of your fathers and so on.” In addition to that, with kirtayantah He mentions a particularity. Bhagavatah signifies maha-prabhavasya (of He who has great might). The reasoning as well in that regard is expressed: mama ca (and Mine). The sense is: “Beg in terms of having a connection with Me.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Yacata stands for yacadhvam (all of you should beg).102Kirtayantah (while mentioning) is said to communicate this: “They cannot even be woken up by calling out with Our names, and even by Us. Such is the dormant state of those learned men.” “While first mentioning the name of Baladeva (aryasya = baladevasya)...” It is with this intention: “If they, who see outwardly, give little to you, considering that he, a Ksatriya, is a fitter recipient of alms than I, a Vaisya, due to being slightly more venerable, that too is okay.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“Being sent by both of Us (asmad-visarjitah = avabhyam presitah santah), you should beg (yacata = yacadhvam).” “Why would Brahmanas give to Us. And if they give, why should we take, since we are not worthy recipients of pratigraha (alms to Brahmanas)?” He answers: “while mentioning the name of Baladeva and of Mine—since both of Us are worthy recipients,” from the passage of Smrti:

*atah patra-parah ko ’nyas trisu lokesu vidyate \|*  
*krsnat kamala-patraksad devadevaj janardanat \|\|*

**“Therefore who in the three worlds is another, better recipient than Krsna, whose eyes are expanded like lotus petals, who is the god of gods, and who is Janardana?” (also quoted by Baladeva Vidyabhusana in his commentary on Visnu-sahasra-nama 67)**

### 10.23.5

*ity adista bhagavata gatvayacanta te tatha \|*  
*krtanjali-puta vipran danda-vat patita bhuvi \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

iti—in this way (and marks the end of the quotation); adistah— ordered; bhagavata—by the Lord; gatva—after going; ayacanta te— they begged; tatha—in that way; krta-anjali-putah—they by whom the hollow of cupped hands was done; vipran—to the Brahmanas; danda-vat—like sticks; patitah—fallen; bhuvi—on the ground.

*iti bhagavata adistah te (gopah tatra) gatva tatha vipran ayacanta. (te gopah) krtanjali-putah (bhutva) danda-vat bhuvi patitah.*

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

*iti bhagavata adistah te (gopah tatra) gatva krtanjali-putah (bhutva) danda-vat bhuvi patitah tatha vipran ayacanta.*

**Thus ordered by the Lord, they went, and begged the Brahmanas in that way. They prayerfully cupped their hands and fell on the ground like rods.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Ordered by the Lord in this way,” because carrying out His order is a must. Tatha (in that way) means: “in the same manner He instructed.” This makes one aware of the following: Perceiving the cow herders’ irreverence toward them, He also instructed them to offer obeisance with devotion to the Brahmanas.

Or, they, the topmost Vaisnavas, naturally have bhakti toward Brahmanas: Also because of that, they begged in that way, i.e. in the manner of a nama-kirtana and so forth.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Ity adistah signifies: tad-adesa-gauravena eva (only with high regard for His order). To detail the bad nature of the sacrificial performers, with krta and so on he talks about the good nature of the boys.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Prayerfully cupping their hands was for the sake of implying their own good nature. And this was just to get alms at that time. “They fell like rods,” thinking that those Brahmanas had much more fiery energy than the ones in their village.

### 10.23.6

*he bhumi-devah srnuta krsnasyadesa-karinah \|*  
*praptan janita bhadram vo gopan no rama-coditan \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

he bhumi-devah—O Brahmanas (“gods on Earth”); srnuta—listen; krsnasya adesa-karinah—the doers of Krsna’s order; praptan—who have reached (arrived); janita—you should know; bhadram—good; vah—unto you; gopan—cow herders; nah—us; rama-coditan— impelled by Rama.

*he bhumi-devah! (yuyam) srnuta. bhadram vah (bhuyat. yuyam) nah gopan krsnasya adesa-karinah rama-coditan (yusmat-sannidhau) praptan janita.*

**Перевод:**

**“O Brahmanas, listen! May good betide you. Know that we cowherds, who have arrived, are carrying out Krsna’s orders and were sent by Rama.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Bhumi-devah is a vocative for Brahmanas with bhakti. Although “aryasya” (of the elder brother) was enjoined by Sri Krsna at first (10.23.4), the mention at the outset of krsnasya adesa-karinah, which means krsnasya sevakan (Krsna’s servants), is by virtue of their special bhakti for Krsna, by nature.

Praptan means agatan (who have arrived). Not perceiving an interest in listening to them and thinking that a huge offense would be done to them, they hope for tolerance with mercy: bhadram vah, which means: vo bhadram astu, “May good betide you.” Or this is the very nature of an utterance of bhakti, possibly due to a conformity with the ways of beggars.

They might ask: “Why did you, Krsna’s servants, come here?” In that regard they say: rama-coditan (inspired by Rama). The sense is: “Because of an incitement by Rama by Krsna’s order.” In this way the following is made to be understood: They are followers of Sri Krsna and Sri Rama, they have more bhakti toward Krsna, and Krsna’s glory is greater than Rama’s.

Or, in reference to krsnasyadesa-karinah, they were sent by Rama by Krsna’s order. The sense is: rama-preranaya ca praptan, “us, who arrived also by Rama’s incitement.” An incitement by both of Them is made to be known in that way. Still, the transgression of the sequence enunciated by Krsna is only due to the nature of their bhakti to Krsna, insofar as the two names of Krsna and Rama are accordant in meaning. The aisvarya of both of Them is implied due to a renown everywhere with a profuse glory just by Their respective names. Thus the gist is: “We, His servants, have arrived only by His order, but not at our leisure.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Bhumi-devah is a vocative with bhakti. They say krsnasya since Krsna is foremost in their hearts. They say rama after dramatically acting the forgetfulness of the sequence of Sri Krsna’s words. This means only Rama’s order is primary in being dispatched there. Consequently, in the middle, to cover that, bhadram vah is an utterance of respect with reverence.103

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

They are Krsna’s order carriers because He has more sway than Rama, since He is the son of King Nanda. Rama-coditan (impelled by Rama) is said with this idea: “Through us, only Rama is begging food at first.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“O Brahmanas (he bhumi-devah = viprah), you should know that we are Krsna’s order carriers (krsnasyadesa-karinah nah = krsnasya ajna-vahan asman) dispatched by Rama (rama-coditan = ramena presitan).”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“O earthly gods! Listen.” “Why?” “Acknowledge us, whose habit is the execution of Krsna’s order (krsnasyadesa-karinah = krsnasya ajna-karana-silan); who were impelled by Rama; who just got here (praptan = iha praptan); and who are cow herders. May prosperity befall you (bhadram vah = yusmabhyam bhadram astu).”

### 10.23.7

*gas carayantav avidura odanam*  
*ramacyutau vo lasato bubhuksitau \|*  
*tayor dvija odanam arthinor yadi*  
*sraddha ca vo yacchata dharma-vittamah \|\|*  
*upajati (12)*

**Пословный перевод:**

gah carayantau—who are tending cows; avidure—not too far; odanam—food (“boiled rice”); rama-acyutau—Rama and Acyuta; vah—your; lasatah—want; bubhuksitau—who are hungry (“desirous of eating”); tayoh—in Them; dvijah—O twice-born persons; odanam—food (“boiled rice”); arthinoh—who are asking; yadi— if; sraddha ca—and faith; vah—your; yacchata—give; dharma-vit-tamah—O foremost knowers of ethics.

*dharma-vittamah! dvijah! ramacyutau bubhuksitau avidure (vartamanau santau) gah carayantau vah odanam lasatah. yadi vah odanam sraddha ca (asti, tarhi yuyam) tayoh arthinoh yacchata.*

**Перевод:**

**“Rama and Acyuta are tending cows not too far away. Both are hungry and want your food. If, O twice-borns, you have food and if you have faith in Them, who are asking, then give, O foremost knowers of ethics!**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“While not being too far (avidure = avidure vartamanau santau), both of Them want your food (odanam vo lasatah = vah yad annam, tad abhilasatah). If you have food and faith, then give (odanam yadi sraddha ca vo yacchata = vah odanam sraddha ca yady asti, tarhi yacchata).”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Now that you have arrived, why are you staying?” They respond with gah and so on. They might ask: “How is it that They are not too far away?” They reply: gas carayantau, “They are tending cows.” Thus, to safeguard honor, an arrival there just for the sake of begging food is repudiated. Sometimes the reading odanam is in place of annam. Still, even Sridhara Svami’s explanation: yad annam, can certainly be harmonized. Owing to a conformity only with annam, for the most part only bhaktam (cooked) is said with the word odana, since He happily eats that.

Or, “Why are They hungry (bubhuksitau)?” They answer: gas carayantau. The sense is: “Because of exertion by grazing cows and on top of that by going far.” Although only they are hungry, since it wasn’t said that They were pained by hunger, they say bubhuksitau (Those two are hungry) because they will get food only by Their desire to eat. Or it is by virtue of inferring Their hunger by their own hunger, due to a special deep affection.

There is another interpretation. "Why didn’t They come here?” They respond with gah and so forth. The idea is: The cows cannot be left alone. “Where are They now?” They answer: avidure. The sense is: prayah nikate eva (almost already nearby).

Out of fear of Brahmanas, with the dual compound ramacyutau He is pointed out in the manner of a sequence with the elder brother. Baladeva is ‘Rama’ because of delighting the world (loka-ramana); He is ‘Acyuta’ since He is devoid of a fall (cyuti-rahita) from any virtue; a greatness is thus implied in order to get food. “Only your food (vah annam = yusmakam eva annam)": In that way any other food is rejected. “Nevertheless, we cannot relinquish the sacrifice and leave.” The boys respond: yacchata (give), that is: “Entrust it only to us.” “Isn’t it that the proper recipient of charity is only a Brahmana, no other?” To that they say: “Dharma, or the texts on dharma, such as: annasya ksudhitah patram, “One who is hungry for rice is a proper recipient,” is already entirely known to you; otherwise, not giving anything would simply be adharma." In dharma-vittamah (O greatest knowers of dharma), the suffix tama\[p\] (greatest) is only used for the sake of a praise, but it is not truly so, because those Brahmanas do not know the truth about dharma. The same idea applies in the next verse: sattamah (greatest sadhus).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“Now that you have arrived, for what purpose are you staying?” They respond with gah and so on. They might ask: “How is it that They are not too far away?” They reply: gas carayantau, “They are tending cows.” To safeguard honor, an arrival there only for the sake of begging food is repudiated. Annam is Svami’s reading.104Amara states: bhissa stri bhaktam andho’nnam odano ’stri sa didivih, “Bhissa, in the feminine; bhaktam, andhas, and annam, in the neuter; odana, in the masculine and in the neuter; and didivi, in the masculine \[are synonymous and mean food\]” (Amara-kosa 2.9.48).

Or, “Why are They hungry (bubhuksitau)?” They answer: gas carayantau... (The rest of the commentary is the same.).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Both of Them are begging you (vo lasatah = yusman bhiksete).” The two readings, odanam and annam, have a similar meaning.105They might reply: “They are not Brahmanas. How can we give before Brahmanas eat?” They respond: bubhuksitau (Those two are hungry). The gist is: “You must already know the authoritative statement: annasya ksudhitah patram, “One who is hungry for rice is a proper recipient.” Noticing that they were not saying anything in reply, they speak once more: “O twice-borns! If you have faith in those Two, who are asking, then give.” The idea is: “If not, say: ‘No’. We shall turn around and leave.” Regarding dharma-vittamah, “Indeed, dharma and adharma exist in relation to conformity (anvaya) and contrariety (vyatireka). What more should we say?”

As a pun: “Because all of you are silent after hearing that Rama and Krsna, with only one name of whom the whole world melts with love and who are very much pained by hunger, are asking, you are dvijas simply in the sense of being “born from two” (dvijah = pitr-dvaya-jatah eva, “born from two parents”).” This is also a revilement. Dharma-vittamah is said by viparita-laksana (irony: the real meaning is the opposite).

### 10.23.8

*diksayah pasu-samsthayah sautramanyas ca sattamah \|*  
*anyatra diksitasyapi nannam asnan hi dusyati \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

diksayah—from the initiation; pasu-samsthayah—\[up to\] the killing of the sacrificial animal (“\[before\] the complete fixity of a animal”); sautramanyah—than the Sautramani;106ca—and; sat-tamah—O topmost righteous persons; anyatra—at another time; diksitasya api—even of one who is initiated; na—not; annam—food; asnan— while eating; hi—indeed; dusyati—is at fault.

*sattamah! diksayah (anantaram) pasu-samsthayah (purvam janah diksitasya annam asnan dusyati. anyatra janah diksitasya annam asnan na dusyati. evam) sautramanyah ca anyatra (janah) diksitasya api annam asnan hi na dusyati iti.*

**Перевод:**

**“O topmost righteous persons! From the initiation for a sacrifice to the killing of a sacrificial animal, one who eats the food of an initiated person is at fault, just like someone who eats during the Sautramani. But not at any other time.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

They speak, suspecting that the Brahmanas might say: “We are initiated and have not yet eaten.” There is a fault before the prescribed killing of a sacrificial animal (pasu-samsthayah = agnisomiya-pasv-alambanat purvam), beginning from the initiation (diksayah = diksayah arabhya): not at any other time.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

The discourse here is only because of their inherent erudition. They say hi (indeed) to signify that they know this from the renown of the scriptures.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The utterance beginning from diksayah reveals their natural erudition. Therefore the killing of a sacrificial animal too had occurred: This is determined by the particularity of the performance. In point of hi (indeed): They determined this by the renown of the scriptures.

One is at fault beginning from the initiation (diksayah = diksam arabhya), before killing of a sacrificial animal (pasu-samsthayah = pasu-samsthatah purvam). Other than that (anyatra = tatah anyatra = tatah param), one is not at fault. And at a time other than the Sautramani, one is not at fault. This means one who eats during the Sautramani is at fault. The tenor is: “We are begging, knowing the considerations such as the proper time.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

They speak, suspecting that those ones would say: “We initiated persons have not eaten the food,” because of the statement: diksitannam na bhunjita, “One should not eat the food set aside for initiated persons.” There is a fault after the initiation (diksayah = diksanantaram) and before the prescribed killing of the sacrificial animal.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Although the boys did not study the scriptures, it’s implied that their own correct notions were in conformity with scriptural knowledge because they are the Lord’s associates.

### 10.23.9

*iti te bhagavad-yacnam srnvanto ‘pi na susruvuh \|*  
*ksudrasa bhuri-karmano balisa vrddha-maninah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

iti—(marks the end of the quotation); te—they; bhagavat-yacnam— the request of the Lord; srnvantah api—even while hearing; na susruvuh—did not listen; ksudra-asah—they whose wishes are insignificant; bhuri-karmanah—they who have many rituals; balisah—childish (or ignorant); vrddha-maninah—they who have the false conceit of being mature (or of being learned108).

*te ksudrasah bhuri-karmanah balisah vrddha-maninah bhagavad-yacnam srnvantah api na susruvuh.*

**Перевод:**

**Though they heard the Lord’s request, they did not listen. Their objectives were insignificant; they were involved in numerous rituals; they were ignorant; and they had the false pride of being learned.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Ksudrasah signifies: ksudre svargadau asa-matram yesam, “all their ambitions regard heaven and other insignificant things.” Bhuri-karmanah connotes: bhurini klesadhikani karmani yesam, “their activities are numerous, meaning their deeds are more trouble.” Therefore they were ignorant (balisah = ajnah) and useless: they had the false pride that they were mature in knowledge (vrddha-maninah = jnana-vrddhah iti manavantah).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) Here Suka speaks. “The Brahmanas did not listen—this means: with a huge self-conceit they did not have respect for that request since they were sent by Him for the sake of food—to the request of the Lord,” that is, although He is completely full of all aisvarya and although He was doing a favor that way.”

In that regard, in two and a half verses, Suka angrily rebukes those Brahmanas because of a disrespect to the Lord. Although they are ksudrasa, (their objectives were insignificant), they are bhuri-karman (they engage in many rites) because they have little intelligence (balisah = alpa-buddhayah). Still: vrddha-maninah (proud of being learned).

Another rendering is as follows: A great goal is accomplished by bhakti to the Lord, even with very little effort; because of not understanding that, they are simply balisa (childish). Someone might wonder: “Why don’t they pursue the Truth?" He responds: vrddha-maninah, “they think themselves mature in knowledge” (= atmanam jnana-vrddham manyante).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Someone might wonder: “They too knew the scriptures. Why didn’t they listen?” In two verses and a half, he angrily scoffs at them: They did not really know the scriptures; on the contrary, having studied and taught the scriptures, they were just fools. They were vrddha-manin (having the conceit of being mature), not jnana-vrddha (mature in knowledge).

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Balisah (childish) means murkhah (foolish), from the definition: baliso bala-murkhayoh, “Balisa means bala (child, childish) and murkha (fool).”109

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

Ksudra has the sense of alpa (‘little’, as contrasted with bhuri-karmanah). Vrddha-maninah means they thought: “Only we are learned in the three Vedas, and only we know the goal of the Vedas.”

### 10.23.10-11

*desah kalah prthag dravyam mantra-tantrartvijo ’gnayah \|*  
*devata yajamanas ca kratur dharmas ca yan-mayah \|\|*  
*tam brahma paramam saksad bhagavantam adhoksajam \|*  
*manusya-drstya dusprajna martyatmano na menire \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

desah—the location; kalah—the time; prthak dravyam—the separate items; mantra—the mantras (mystic verbal formulas); tantra—the procedure; rtvijah—the priests; agnayah—the fires; devatah—the divinities; yajamanah—the sponsor (“the one who is sacrificing / worshiping”); ca—and; kratuh—the sacrifice (as a whole) (or the resolve); dharmah—the merit; ca—and; yat-mayah—have the nature of whom;

tam—Him; brahma—Brahman; paramam—the Supreme; saksat— directly (in person); bhagavantam—the Lord; adhoksajam— Adhoksaja (“beyond sense perception”); manusya-drstya—with the notion of manhood; dusprajnah—they whose wisdom is bad; martya-atmanah—they for whom the self is mortal; na menire—did not esteem (or did not understand).

*desah kalah prthag dravyam mantra-tantrartvijah agnayah devatah yajamanah ca (pratyekam yan-mayah bhavanti), kratuh dharmah ca yan-mayah (ca bhavati, ete viprah) dusprajnah martyatmanah tarn saksat paramam brahma bhagavantam adhoksajam manusya-drstya na menire.*

**Перевод:**

**By perceiving Him as a human, the Brahmanas, who were stubborn and for whom the body is the self, did not understand that He is the supreme Brahman, God in person, Adhoksaja, although the place, the time, the manifold items, the mantras, the procedure, the priests, the fires, the divinities, the sponsor, the purpose, and the unforeseen merit are made of Him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The Brahmanas might think: “Why would food for the sake of another be given by transgressing the sequence of the ritual?” He speaks the verse in response. Prthag dravyam means caru-purodasadi dravyam, “items such as caru (an oblation of rice, barley, and pulse cooked with ghee and milk) and purodasa (a mass of ground rice rounded into cakelike forms).” Tantra means prayoga (procedure). Dharma means apurvam (unforeseen result). Manusya-drstya signifies: manusyo ’yam iti drstya (with the notion: He is a man). Martyatmanah portends: brahmanah vayam mahantah iti manyamanah (while thinking: we Brahmanas are great).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

In two verses, to illustrate, as if while teaching the true meaning, that they are ignorant, Suka speaks as if he were lamenting them. Prthak means bahu-vidham (manifold). The reason the place and other aspects are infused by the Lord is: paramam brahma (He is the supreme Brahman). Therefore: bhagavantam, “He is complete with all godly might” (= sarvaisvarya-purnam), consequently: adhoksajam, “He is out of the scope of the senses (= indriyagocaram). In addition, out of mercy He was directly present (saksat = saksad bhutam).

There is another explanation. The infusement in the place, etc., is shown only with brahma. Further, paramam denotes Sri Narayana, whose form is dense sac-cid-ananda. Moreover: saksat, i.e. svayam eva (in person), but not as the form of an Avatara. In addition: bhagavantam, He is dedicated to revealing His own infinite godhood; “Bhagavan” denotes Sri Mathura-natha. Over and above that, adhoksajam: He was as if born again under a cart, since a cart had collapsed. An elaborate etymology of this has already been enunciated in the fourteenth chapter, in a description of Him in regard to garbha-gatasya (10.14.12). The sense of adhoksajam is “the festival of Sri Gokula.”

“With the notion of manhood, they did not respect (na menire = na adrtavantah) Him either (tam = tam api).” Why? dusprajnah, “they lacked a cogitation” (= vicara-hinah). Why? martyatmanah. It was already explained by Sridhara Svami. Another interpretation is: martyah anubhavisyamana-marana-laksana-samsarakah atma svarupam yesam te, “they whose identity pertains to transmigration, characterized by death, which is going to be experienced.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) Now, with this unit of two verses, by looking at the truth he speaks to inform about the fact that they are ignorant. Prthak means bahu-vidham (manifold). The reason for the Lord’s infusement in the place and so on is: paramam brahma. Therefore: bhagavantam, i.e. sarvaisvarya-paripurnam (fully complete with all godly might), consequently: adhoksajam, which means: indriyagocaram (out of sensory range). Still, out of mercy He was directly present (saksat = saksad bhutam).

“With the notion of mortality (manusya-drstya = martya-buddhya), they did not respect (na menire = na adrtavantah) Him either (tam = tam api).” Why? dusprajnah, which means vicara-hinah (lacking a cogitation). That too is for what reason? martyatmanah.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“The place and other aspects are the forms of the grandeurs of an aspect of an aspect of whom (yan-mayah = yad-amsamsa-vibhuti-rupah).”

With the notion: “He is a special soul” (manusya-drstya = jiva-viseso ’yam iti drstya) the Brahmanas, who had the conceit of being their respective material bodies (martyatmanah = dehabhimaninah), did not esteem Him, the Supreme, Brahman, Adhoksaja, that is, He who had become directly perceptible out of mercy though He is out of sensory range.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

The reason for the Lord’s infusement in the place and so on is: paramam brahma, insofar as He, who has potencies, is those various forms.110Or it is because the place, the time, etc., have functions that are dependent on Him and are pervaded by Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Adhoksajam means: adhah krtam aksa-jam indriya-jnanam yatra, “Him, in regard to whom sensory knowledge is made low.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The place is the scope of the roaming of krsna-sara deer. The time denotes spring and so forth. The mantras are Om, etc., which cause the manifestation of the divinities’ grace. Tantra means anusthana-vidhi (the rules of the performance). The priests are the Adhvaryu and others. The fires are the ahavaniya and so forth.111The divinities are Indra and others, as denoted by the words. Kratu means sankalpa (resolve, purpose).112Yajamana means adhikara (i.e. the adhikari, the sponsor). Yan-mayah denotes yat-pradhana-pratipadyah, “The aspects are to be explained as things whose chief element is Him.” They did not understand Him (na menire = na jnatavantah).113

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Their concept of identity relates to the body, whose nature is to perish (martyatmanah = marana-sile dehe atma atma-buddhih yesam te).

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

All of these are Brahman, and in addition: paramam. Four things are said by the word brahma: The Vedas, the category of Brahmana, Brahma, and Para-Brahman, therefore the word paramam is said to exclude the other ones. The fires are manifold, such as ahavaniya. The mantras are Rk and so on. The derivation of Adhoksaja is: adho ‘ksa-jam jnanam yasmat, “He from whom knowledge is low (below radar).” They did not accept Him (na menire = na angi-krtavantah).

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“Those Brahmanas, whose conceit about the self was in relation to the body, which has attributes of mortality (martyatmanah = martye marana-dharmake dehe atmabhimanah yesam te brahmanah), did not esteem Him (na menire = na adrtavantah)."

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

There are sixteen priests: Brahma, Udgata, Hota, Adhvaryu, Brahmanacchamsi, Prastota, Maitravaruna, Pratiprasthata, Pratiharta, Pota, Acchavaka, Nesta, Agnidhra, Subrahmanya, Gravastota, and Unneta.114

### 10.23.12

*na te yad om iti procur na neti ca parantapa \|*  
*gopa nirasah pratyetya tathocuh krsna-ramayoh \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—not; te—they; yat—when; Om—yes; iti—(end of citation); procuh—they said; na—not; na—no; iti— (end of citation); ca—and; parantapa—O chastiser of enemies (“scorchers of others”); gopah— the cow herders; nirasah—discouraged (“whose hopes have gone away”); pratyetya—after going back; tatha—in that way; ucuh—told; krsna-ramayoh—to Krsna and Rama.

*parantapa! yad te (viprah) “om (vayam dasyamah)” iti na procuh, “(vayam) na (dasyamah)” iti ca na (procuh, tada) gopah (annalabhe) nirasah krsna-ramayoh (samipe) pratyetya (tau) tatha (tad vrttam) ucuh.*

**Перевод:**

**The Brahmanas said neither ‘yes’ or ‘no’, and so the cow herders, discouraged, came back and told the news to Krsna and Rama, O scorcher of enemies.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

The Brahmanas did not reply. Here Om (yes) has the sense of svikara (acceptance115). “They did not say: “Yes, we will give,” nor did they say: “We will not give,”” owing to a colossal disrespect on account of being possessed by a wicked self-conceit.

“O scorcher of enemies! (parantapa).” The drift is: “Only a person of your kind is able to subdue the enemy which is arrogant pride (paran = param = mada-laksanam satrum).” “They told in that way (tatha ucuh),” i.e. they told what they said and what the Brahmanas did.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“They did not say: om.” The gist is: “How can we give to the cowherd boys now, before we Brahmanas have completed the meal?” “Nor did they say: No.” “If there will be leftover food after Brahmanas have completed the meal, then we’ll be able to give.” At that time, noticing that the anger of the king was rising, he addresses him: parantapa. “Had you been the king then, you, though the crest jewel of all persons favorable to Brahmanas, would surely have punished those Brahmanas as if they were enemies.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Om has the sense of svikara (acceptance). Visva states: om ity anumatau proktam, “ Om signifies an approbation.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

“They turned back, assembled (pratyetya = vyaghutya = samagatya), and spoke in that way in front of Krsna and Rama (krsna-ramayoh = krsna-ramayoh puratah).”

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

Yad means yada (when). “They came back and told Krsna and Rama.” The genitive case in krsna-ramayoh is a sese sasthi: it has the sense of the accusative (the object of the verb).

### 10.23.13

*tad upakarnya bhagavan prahasya jagad-isvarah \|*  
*vyajahara punar gopan darsayan laukikim gatim \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tat—that; upakarnya—after hearing close-by; bhagavan—the Lord; prahasya—after laughing; jagat-isvarah—the controller of the world; vyajahara—spoke; punah—again; gopan—to the cow herders; darsayan—in order to show; laukikim gatim—the worldly ways.

*bhagavan jagad-isvarah tad upakarnya prahasya (ca) laukikim gatim darsayan gopan punar vyajahara.*

**Перевод:**

**Giving an ear to that, the Lord, the master of the universe, laughed. To illustrate the ways of the world, He addressed the cowherds once more.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“He spoke to show the universally accepted principle” (laukikim gatim = loka-sthitim): “Those who expect a result should not be dejected: Who is the beggar who hasn’t been turned down?”, and the like.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Although the cow herders spoke to both of Them, Sri Rama did not speak at all, either because of anger caused by the disregard of Sri Krsna’s order or because of knowing Sri Krsna’s intention. Only Sri Krsna replied. “After hearing close-by (upakarnya = upa akarnya = samipe eva akarnya)—inasmuch as the cow herders spoke slowly on account of the gloom of that disregard—and loudly laughing (prahasya = uccair hasitva)...” The reasons for that are: He is the controller of all (jagad-isvarah = sarva-niyanta) and is full of all godly might (bhagavan = sarvaisvarya-purnah), therefore begging in that way was merely for the sake of joviality. The gist is: When disappointment might be the end result, only laughing was appropriate. Or the sense is, as the master of the universe. He is also the controller of those Brahmanas. This means He did not consider the offense, because: bhagavan, He is omniscient: “What is their fault? They are bewildered by My Maya.” Or bhagavan denotes parama-daya-guna-yuktah, “He has the quality of topmost compassion.” The rest was explained by the venerable one.

There is another rendering: Whenever the act of begging a man doesn’t work, one should beg his wife. The sense is: “to teach beggars.” Or: “To teach people: “For the accomplishment of My devotee’s desire, one should not become despondent in any way and must strive.””

This too is just a pastime consisting of joviality. In truth, however, given that it was made to be known that those men are worse than trees, by the style of what He said earlier, there is also a particularity here. Intending to signify this, He spoke to illustrate to the world, through the behavior of those Brahmanas and of their wives, the following: “The nondevotees’ sole dedication to reciting the Vedas, performing fire sacrifices, etc., is conducive to faults such as a wicked self-conceit and to unhappiness, not to true welfare, consequently only My devotees, though they are devoid of that, are topmost.”

There is another interpretation. He spoke to show a truth about the world (laukikim gatim darsayan = laukika-tattvam darsayitum): “For the most part, toward Me the mindset of women and of those who have that sort of bhava is quite different from the mindset of men.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“He spoke to show the universally accepted principle” (laukikim gatim = loka-sthitim): Those who expect a result are not dejected: Who is the beggar who hasn’t been turned down? He laughed because anger toward ignorant Brahmanas is inappropriate.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Laukikim gatim means: loka-siddham ritim (the ways of the world).

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“Once again, He spoke (vyajahara = uvaca) to the cow herders, as if to show a worldly method (laukikim gatim darsayan = loka-paripatim darsayan iva), which is as follows: trnad api laghus tulas tulad api ca yacakah, “Cotton is lighter than grass, and a beggar is even lighter than cotton.””

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Hearing (upakarnya = srutva) about those Brahmanas’ offense to Him, He again spoke to show the ways of the world, such as:

*apamanam puraskrtya krtva manam tu prsthatah \|*  
*sva-karyam sadhayed dhiman karya-nase tu murkhata \|\|*

**“Putting disrespect aside and respect at the back, an intelligent person should accomplish his or her objective. There is foolishness only in the loss of the objective.”**

### 10.23.14

*mam jnapayata patnibhyah sa-sankarsanam agatam \|*  
*dasyanti kamam annam vah snigdha mayy usita dhiya \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

mam—about Me; jnapayata—inform; patnibhyah—to the wives (“for the wives’ sake”); sa-sankarsanam—accompanied by Sankarsana; agatam—who have come; dasyanti—they will give; kamam—as desired; annam—food; vah—to you; snigdhah—who are affectionate; mayi—to Me (and in Me); usitah—who resided (who reside); dhiya—with the intelligence (or mind).

*(yuyam atra) agatam sa-sankarsanam mam (vipranam) patnibhyah jnapayata. (tah) mayi snigdhah (mayi sva-sva-)dhiya usitah kamam annam vah dasyanti (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Inform the wives, for their sake, that I, along with Sankarsana, have come. They will give you food at will. They are affectionate to Me: They live with their intelligence in Me.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“They reside at home only with the body; with the mind they reside in Me. Since those ladies like Me, they will give.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Inform them about Me, who have just arrived (agatam = agatam eva); there is no need to disclose the hunger or the request for food, because they will give only by being informed of My arrival.” It is not specified tesam patnibhyah (to their wives) nor yajnasya patnibhyah (to the wives related to the sacrifice), since those men are not worthy of being so related.

Moreover, by their special bhava for Sri Krsna, it is said that He was accompanied by Sankarsana (sa-sankarsanam = sankarsana-sahitam) inasmuch as Sri Baladeva is secondary in that regard. For the sake of those ladies’ bhakti to Him, even His separate mood with him is implied by the word Sankarsana.

Someone might wonder: “How might they give without the approval of the husbands? Even while giving, somehow, they could be stopped by the husbands.” He responds: snigdhah (affectionate). The idea is: “In consideration of Me, the ladies will not have high regard for them. And specifically, by their bad behavior then, they will disregard them and come together to Me. Concerning snigdhah: Although it is proper for yajna-patnis to have a sweet rati, the mention is in the manner of being a generality because He did not have that sort of bhava toward those ladies.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) “Inform them about Me, who have just arrived (agatam = agatam eva); there is no need to disclose the hunger or the request for food, because they will give only by being informed of My arrival.”

Patnibhyah means: yajna-sambandhinibhvah bharyabhyah. “to the wives, who have a connection with the sacrifice.” from remembering: patyur no yajna-samyoge. “After the word pati (husband), there is an addition of n in the sense of a connection with a sacrifice” (Astadhyayi 4.1.33).116Because of this, it is only a connection of dharma that is unspecific in relation to those ladies. but it was not a connection of lust, “because the ladies have deep feelings for Me.” This is how He thought.

Moreover, by their special bhava for Sri Krsna, it is said that He was accompanied by Sankarsana inasmuch as Sri Baladeva is secondary in that regard. In point of ‘Sankarsana’. since his name has greatness it is mentioned directly.

Someone might wonder: “How might they give without the approval of the husbands? Even while giving, somehow, they could be stopped by the husbands.” He responds: snigdhah (affectionate). The idea is: “In consideration of Me, the ladies will not have high regard for them.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Inform them that I have just arrived (agatam = agatam eva), but don’t tell them I’m hungry, because, should they hear about My discomfort, the hunger, they would be in anguish.

—How will they give food without being informed of Your hunger?

—They will give to you (vah = yusmabhyam) just by perceiving your hunger, only by a connection with Me.

—Won’t their husbands stop them?

—They have affection (snigdhah = snehavatyah) for Me. They won’t think much of a hindrance by the husbands, since they live with the intelligence only in Me (usita dhiya = mayi eva dhiya usitah). They stay in their husbands’ homes only with the body.”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

In mam jnapayata (inform about Me), He points Himself out as primary, since those ladies are enamored of Him only.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

What is the proof they will give? snigdha mayi (they are affectionate to Me). How so? dhiya usita mayi (with the intelligence, they live in Me). The word mayi is used twice, by the logical reasoning called a crow’s eye (kakaksi-nyaya).

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Dvijanam is to be added to patnibhyah (to the Brahmanas’ wives).

### 10.23.15

*gatvatha patni-salayam drstvasinah svalankrtah \|*  
*natva dvija-satir gopah prasrita idam abruvan \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

gatva—after going; atha—afterward; patni-salayam—in the hall for wives \[of priests etc.\]; drstva—after seeing; asinah—who were sitting; su-alankrtah—who were nicely adorned; natva—after bowing; dvija-satih—\[seeing\] the chaste women who were Brahmanis; gopah—the cow herders; prasritah—\[being\] courteous (or humble); idam—this; abruvan—said.

*atha gopah patni-salayam gatva (tatra) asinah svalankrtah dvija-satih drstva natva (ca) prasritah (santah) idam abruvan.*

**Перевод:**

**Afterward, the cow herders went to the hall reserved for wives, saw those virtuous Brahmanis, who were sitting and were nicely adorned, bowed to them and, being courteous, spoke as follows.**
