**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Atha signifies: “right after the Lord’s speech.” In point of asinah (sitting): They were not busy with activities like the husbands were, but were abiding comfortably and happily on account of bhakti to the Lord. Concerning sv-alankrtah, the characteristic of being yajna-patnis (wives for a fire sacrifice) is implied.

“Seeing the wives of those Brahmanas (dvija-satih = vipranam tesam patnih)...” Although the ladies are the wives of those men, because of bhakti to the Lord by the word sati implies that the ladies were virtuous (sadhvi). Or the sense is the ladies are even more virtuous than those Brahmanas, in every way.

The boys are humble (vinitah) by nature, or they were humble by hearing about the ladies’ special affection for Sri Krsna. In the reading prasritah, the sense is the same.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Atha signifies: “right after the Lord’s speech” and also refers to snigdhah (affectionate) and mayy usita dhiya (they live with their intelligence in Me) in the previous verse, otherwise a trip for the purpose of begging anew would be improper.

With asinah (sitting), he says their going occurred only on a good occasion in relation to those ladies. Indeed, being ready for a conversation the sake of joy is threefold: as one whose mind is undisturbed, as one who has a nice attire, and as one who has good behavior. The sense of asinah, meaning tatra asinah (sitting there), is that they were already sitting at their leisure, by being immobile due to a mutual absorption in topics about the Lord, after getting out of the hustle of cooking, etc., which is necessary due to being under the control of a husband, and after bathing, etc.

Svalankrtah means they were already adorned just because of a behavior fitting for a wife and were excellently (su = susthu) adorned specifically with pulaka (horripilation); this suggests an engrossment in prema for the Lord.

“Seeing the saintly women, who are in the category of the twice-born, which is the very best (dvija-satih = parama-sattamayam dvija-jatau api satih)...” The sense is: By the rise of all virtues, which took place on account of bhakti to the Lord, they were also endowed with qualities of the topmost good behavior.

The cow herders are prasrita (courteous) by nature, or else they were so because of hearing about the ladies’ special affection for Sri Krsna.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Prasritah means vinitah (well-mannered).

### 10.23.16

*namo vo vipra-patnibhyo nibodhata vacamsi nah \|*  
*ito ’vidure carata krsnenehesita vayam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

namah—obeisances; vah—to you; vipra-patnibhyah—who are wives of Brahmanas; nibodhata—hear; vacamsi—words; nah—our; itah— from here; avidure—not very far; carata—who is going; krsnena—by Krsna; iha—here; isitah—dispatched; vayam—we.

*vah vipra-patnibhyah namah (astu. yuyam) nah vacamsi nibodhata. vayam itah avidure carata krsnena iha isitah.*

**Перевод:**

**“Please accept our respects to you, wives of Brahmanas! Heed our words. We were sent here by Krsna, who is going around not too far from here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Isitah means presitah (sent).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Our respects to you (vah = yusmabhyam).” This is a pranama with the voice, either to examine those ladies’ mood or to make the ladies face them so they listen to their speech.

Concerning vipra-patnibhyah (to you, wives of Brahmanas): The qualification for an obeisance is mentioned. The repeated obeisance is because of the intensity of bhakti, or it is for the purpose of the announcement.

The plural in vacamsi (words) is due to high regard. Nibodhata (heed) means srnuta (hear), owing to the nature of profuse humility; or it is for the sake of listening with attention, possibly on account of the rapture of hearing news of the dear one. “We were sent by Krsna—the one who is attracting your hearts (yusmac- cittakarsaka)—who is already nearby (avidure = nikate eva).”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Beholding that the ladies were exactly like Sri Krsna said they are: snigdha mayy usita dhiya, “They are affectionate to Me: They live with their intelligence in Me” (10.23.14), they make those ladies fully pay attention: “Obeisances to you (vah = yusmabhyam).” Concerning vipra-patnibhyah (to you, wives of Brahmanas): The qualification for an obeisance is mentioned. Next they say to them, who were still not so much in external consciousness as before: nibodhata (hear). The plural in vacamsi (words) is due to high regard for the meanings. “We were sent by Krsna—the one who is attracting your hearts (yusmac-cittakarsaka)—who is already nearby (avidure = nikate eva).”

### 10.23.17

*gas carayan sa gopalaih sa-ramo duram agatah \|*  
*bubhuksitasya tasyannam sanugasya pradiyatam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

gah carayan—while grazing cows; sah—He; gopalaih—with cow herders; sa-ramah—who is with Rama; duram—far; agatah—has come; bubhuksitasya—who is hungry (“who desires to eat”); tasya— to Him; annam—food; sa-anugasya—who is with the followers; pradiyatam—should be given.

*sah (krsnah) sa-ramah gopalaih (saha) gah carayan (grhat) duram agatah. sanugasya bubhuksitasya tasya (krsnasya) annam pradiyatam (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“He, accompanied by Rama, has come far while grazing cows along with the cow herders. Food should be given to Him: He is hungry and is with His followers.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Sah denotes sa krsnah (He, Krsna). Gopalaih means gopalaih saha (with cow herders).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

He always delights (sada ramayati) Krsna, hence his name is Rama. As a result the boys lost their inhibition, and so they discarded the formality. “He has come far—from home,” so the idea is: Food could not be brought from there. Alternatively, the word is aduram (not far) (sa-ramo duram = sa-ramo ’duram). The repetition is for the purpose of the ladies’ arrival very close-by.

“Food should be eminently given (pradiyatam = prakarsena diyatam)—that is, by means of containers for carrying tasty sweet food and drink—to Him, who is accompanied by Sri Rama and by the group of cow herders (sanugasya = sri-rama-gopa-varga- sahitasya).”

At first there was only Their request for food, and now: sanugasya (accompanied by the retinue), and on top of that, prakarsena (eminently), by virtue of hearing about the ladies’ special bhakti to the Lord. Asking for food though it was not ordered by the Lord was due to their pang of hunger—or the reason is so that they too, His retinue, would get something to eat, or it was just to get food—for otherwise there would be the possibility that merely by hearing about His arrival the ladies would have come, even by quickly leaving the food behind.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

He always delights Sri Krsna, thus he is Rama. As a result, their inhibition is discarded. At first, Krsna used the name Sankarsana to proclaim his glory, but at this time it was appropriate for these fellows to proclaim Baladeva’s inclination toward Him with this name because although previously only an increased high regard was suitable, they saw how the wives felt about Krsna, and so the formality was no longer necessary.

(Additions are underlined.) “He has come not far (aduram)— from here.” The repetition is for the purpose of the ladies’ arrival very close-by. “Food should be eminently given (pradiyatam = prakarsena diyatam)—by means of containers for carrying tasty sweet food and drink—to Him, who is accompanied by Sri Rama and by the group of cow herders (sanugasya = sri-rama-gopa-varga-sahitasya).” At first there was only Their request for food, and now: sanugasya, even without His order, and on top of that, prakarsena (eminently), by virtue of hearing about the ladies’ special bhakti to the Lord. It was said with humor, also by considering the possibility that merely by hearing about His arrival the ladies would have come quickly, leaving the food behind.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Alas, how amazing! The ladies fainted out of bliss just because of Krsna’s name. Therefore, to arouse them, although they had already stated their motive, they mention it more loudly with some more details.

“He has come nearby (aduram agatah = nikatam eva ayatah)." In addition to that, in the second half of the verse he says: Perceiving that they were totally awake, they made them hear about His expectation of food and agitated them, who had intense, deep affection.

### 10.23.18

*srutvacyutam upayatam nityam tad-darsanotsukah \|*  
*tat-kathaksipta-manaso babhuvur jata-sambhramah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

srutva—hearing about; acyutam—Acyuta; upayatam—who had arrived nearby; nityam—constantly; tat-darsana-utsukah—eager to see Him; tat-katha-akspita-manasah—they whose hearts are overwhelmed by topics about Him (or they by whom their minds are reviled on account of news about Him); babhuvuh—they became; jata-sambhramah—they whose bustle occurred.

*(tah vipra-patnyah) acyutam upayatam srutva nityam tad-darsanotsukah tat-kathaksipta-manasah (satyah) jata-sambhramah babhuvuh.*

**Перевод:**

**Hearing that Acyuta had arrived nearby, the ladies, who were always eager to see Him and whose hearts were transported by news of Him, stood up and created a flurry of activity.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

They were tad-darsanotsuka (eager to see Him) because they were tat-kathakspita-manas (their hearts are overwhelmed by topics about Him). Therefore, hearing that He had arrived nearby (upayatam = upagatam), they became jata-sambhrama (their bustle occurred).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Acyuta is He who nevers falls from the heart. Upayatam means: samipe eva saksad agatam, “Him, who has come in person very close-by.” The rest was elucidated by Sridhara Svami. There is another explanation: “And specifically, their minds are disturbed by news of His hunger” (tat-kathaksipta-manasah = tat-kathaya tad-bubhuksa-vartaya aksipta-manasah).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“The wives reviled (aksipta = tiraskrta) their own minds, on account of the news... of His hunger,” in this way: “Are, stupid mind! Why don’t you wake up from swoon even by hearing that the dearest one is hungry? Fie on you.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Their minds are taken away (aksipta = ahrta) by a discourse about Him, Krsna.

### 10.23.19-20

*catur-vidham bahu-gunam annam adaya bhajanaih \|*  
*abhisasruh priyam sarvah samudram iva nimnagah \|\|*  
*nisidhyamanah patibhir bhratrbhir bandhubhih sutaih \|*  
*bhagavaty uttamasloke dirgha-sruta-dhrtasayah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

catuh-vidham—of four kinds; bahu-gunam—which had many good qualities; annam—food; adaya—taking; bhajanaih—by means of containers; abhisasruh—went to meet (went for an abhisara); priyam—to the dear one; sarvah—all the ladies; samudram—to the ocean; iva—like; nimna-gah—rivers (“which go downward”); nisidhyamanah—forbidden; patibhih—by the husbands; bhratrbhih—by the brothers; bandhubhih—by relatives; sutaih—by the sons; bhagavati—on the Lord; uttama-sloke—who is extolled by the best (or for whom there are the best verses); dirgha—for a long time; sruta—by hearing; dhrta-asayah—they whose minds were fixed.

*sarvah (tah vipra-patnyah svasam) patibhih bhratrbhih bandhubhih sutaih nisidhyamanah (api) bhagavati uttamasloke dirgha-sruta-dhrtasayah catur-vidham bahu-gunam annam bhajanaih adaya, nimnagah samudram iva (abhisaranti), priyam abhisasruh.*

**Перевод:**

**Bringing, by means of receptacles, the four kinds of food, which had many excellent qualities, all those ladies, whose minds were focused on Lord Uttamasloka due to hearing about Him for a long time, went to meet their dear one like rivers go to the sea, although they were forbidden by their husbands, brothers, relatives, and sons.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The food was of four kinds, by the varieties of bhaksya (to be chewed), bhojya (to be swallowed: pudding, porridge, etc.), lehya (to be licked: yogurt, chutney), and cosya (to be sucked: raw sugarcane, pieces of orange, fibrous stalks of greens). Bahu-gunam means the food had many qualities, such as taste and aroma, due to special preparations. Bhajanaih means either amatraih (with large vessels) or bhandaih (with containers).

“Although they were blocked (nisidhyamanah = varyamanah api) by the husbands and others, they approached (abhisasruh = abhijagmuh) the dear one, Sri Krsna.” The example is in point of the absence of impediment: samudram nimnaga iva, “like rivers (nimnagah = nadyah) go to the ocean.” The reason for that is bhagavati and so on (He is God). Dirgha-sruta-dhrtasayah means: “they by whom the mind was focused \[on the Lord\] because of hearing for a long time” (= dirgham bahu-kalam srutena sravanena dhrtah asayah yabhih tah).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Bhajanaih means either they put the food in containers, or they put it with containers for eating, or they left the cooked food in the pots because of being in a hurry and for the sake of keeping the food warm.

At first, they were forbidden by their husbands, since they are under their control. Afterward, on account of the disrespecting the husbands’ order, the ladies were forbidden by the fathers out of fear of being rejected, then by the brothers, since they have more affection than them, and then by the sons, who require even more affection than them. The nonmention of the mothers is because they are included among the fathers due to companionship; or it is because they did not prevent them, by reason of that sort of bhava toward the Lord. The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami.

Another rendering is as follows. Dirgha-sruta is a vocative for Sri Pariksit: dirgham bahu-kalam srutam sravanam sastram va yasya, ‘“O you who have been hearing for a long time’ or ‘O you for whom the scripture is long’.” The sense is: Only this behavior is proper for one who is dirgha-sruta. Alternatively, the idea is: “You have heard about many things in the world, but have you ever heard about anything like this sort of bhakti before?” The sense is: Certainly not.

Dhrtasayah means nyasta-cittah (they whose minds are fixed). Or: bhava-visesena sada krta-drdha-manorathah (they by whom firm desires were always kept with a special mood).117

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions in this paragraph are underlined.) This is one unit of two verses. Bhajanaih means either they put the food in containers or they left the cooked food in the pots because of being in a hurry and for the sake of keeping the food warm.

In Sridhara Svami’s commentary, bhaksya means carvya (to be chewed), and cosya means cusya (to be sucked). Nisidhyamanah (forbidden) means that only they, not the food, were prevented from going: “If food should be given to Him, let it be delivered, but you yourselves should not go.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The food was of four kinds, by the varieties of bhaksya (to be swallowed), carvya (to be chewed), cusya (to be sucked), and lehya (to be licked).

Abhisasruh (they approached, or they went to a tryst) is said after beholding the ladies’ conceit of being lovers (nayika) of Krsna at that time. The reason for that is: bhagavati dirgha-sruta-dhrtasayah, which means: bhagavati dirgham bahu-kalam srutena sravanena dhrtah asayah yabhih tah, “they by whom the mind was fixed on the Lord because of hearing for a long time.”118

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The ladies, by whom an intention (asaya = abhipraya)—“When will we see Him?”—toward the Lord was maintained by hearing for a long time, set out to met Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

The four kinds of food are bhaksya (to be chewed), peya (to be drunk), cosya (to be sucked), and lehya (to be licked). Bhaksya involves the use of teeth. The rest is secondary. Bhajanaih signifies that the food did not spill. ‘Uttamasloka’ means: uttamaih slokyate, “He is praised by the best.” The rivers do not think that mountains, etc., are obstacles. The gods are not their husbands, rather only the ocean is. Asaya means citta (mind).

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

Bhojya is food for which using the teeth is not required.

### 10.23.21

*yamunopavane ‘soka-nava-pallava-mandite \|*  
*vicarantam vrtam gopaih sagrajam dadrsuh striyah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

yamuna-upavane—in a subforest of the Yamuna; asoka-nava-pallava-mandite—adorned by new buds of asoka; vicarantam— who was going around; vrtam—surrounded; gopaih—by the cow herders; sa-agrajam—who was with the elder brother; dadrsuh— saw; striyah—the women.

*(tah) striyah (tatha agatah satyah) yamunopavane asoka-nava-pallava-mandite vicarantam gopaih vrtam sagrajam (tam sri-krsnam) dadrsuh.*

**Перевод:**

**The ladies caught sight of Him, who was sauntering in a grove near the Yamuna, which was beautified by new buds on Asoka trees. He was surrounded by cow herders and accompanied by His elder brother.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Once they arrived in that manner, they saw.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“And after that, they saw... Krsna—krsnam is to be added—in a subforest of the Yamuna.” As a pun, after seeing the asoka trees the ladies’ sorrow of separation from Him went away; the word asoka is formed by the derivation: na tisthati soko yasmat, “that because of which no sorrow remains.”

He was in the company of cow herders; the sense is: “They saw Him although He was with them,” since He radiates more than anyone by His unique resplendence, just as the moon is surrounded by stars.

Sagrajam (accompanied by the elder brother) is on account of the increase of a profuse resplendence by His association. Or it is because, by the ladies’ arrival, he is secondary. Striyah (ladies) hints at their seeing with emotion.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Sagrajam informs about Krsna’s distinct beauty, which is superior to anything beautiful, inasmuch as in the separation of the constituent words: agrajena saha (with the elder brother), the instrumental case, in connection with the meaning of saha, is ordained in the meaning of being secondary.

### 10.23.22

*syamam hiranya-paridhim vana-malya-barha-*  
*dhatu-pravala-nata-vesam anuvratamse \|*  
*vinyasta-hastam itarena dhunanam abjam*  
*karnotpalalaka-kapola-mukhabja-hasam \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

syamam—who is dark blue; hiranya—is golden; paridhim—whose garment; vana-malya—with a sylvan garland; barha—a peacock’s tail feather; dhatu—mineral pigments; pravala—and buds (or shoots, or soft leaves); nata-vesam—Him, whose attire is like \[the attire of\] an actor; anuvrata—of a follower; amse—on the shoulder; vinyasta-hastam—by whom a hand is placed; itarena—with the other one; dhunanam—who is twirling; abjam—a lotus; karna-utpala— who has lilies on the ears; alaka-kapola—on whose cheeks are curls; mukha-abja-hasam—who has a smile on the lotus face.

*(tah striyah sri-krsnam) syamam hiranya-paridhim vana-malya-barha-dhatu-pravala-nata-vesam anuvratamse vinyasta-hastam itarena (hastena) abjam dhunanam karnotpalalaka-kapola-mukhabja-hasam (dadrsuh).*

**Перевод:**

**He was dark blue and His garment golden. With sylvan garlands, peacock tail feathers, mineral pigments, and flower buds, His attire resembled the costume of a theatrical actor. He had placed one hand on the shoulder of a friend, and with the other He was twirling a lotus. He had lilies on the ears, curly hair on His cheeks, and a smile on His lotus face.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Hiranya-paridhim means pitambaram (His clothes are yellow). The analysis is: hiranya-vat paridhih paridhanam yasya tam, “Him, whose garment is as if golden.’’ With sylvan garlands, peacock tail feathers, pigments, and buds, He had an attire that was like the attire of a theatrical actor (vanamalya-barha-dhatu-pravala-nata-vesam = vana-malyair barhair dhatubhih pravalais ca nata-vad-veso yasya tam).

anuvratamse vinyasta-hastam means: anuvratasya sakhyur amse vinyasto nihito hasto yena tam, “Him, by whom a hand is placed on the shoulder of a friend.”

itarena dhunanam abjam signifies: itarena hastena lilaya abjam dhunanam bhramayantam, “Him, who, with the other hand, was rotating a lotus as a pastime.”

karnotpalalaka-kapola-mukhabja-hasam means: karnayor utpale yasya, alakah kapolayor yasya, mukhabje haso yasya, tam ca tam ca tam ca, “Him, who has one lily on each ear, on whose cheeks are locks of hair, and who has a smile on His lotus face.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

By the word hiranya (golden), a silken garment that is slightly red and yellow is meant. In addition, because of the covering of the uttariya (upper garment or outer garment) of the paridhana, since the word paridhi is expressive of acchadana (a covering; clothes), the paridhana (garment) is one.119

The arrangement of the sylvan garland and so on is to be inferred according to the resplendence. In that regard, the sylvan garland (vana-malya = vana-mala) is on the chest; the peacock feather is either in a tuft of hair or above a golden crown studded with jewels; or a crown made of peacock feathers is on the head; mineral pigments such as gairika are on the tilaka and so on120; buds are either at the forefront of a tuft of hair or at the tip of the crown.

Alternatively, in accordance with this verse in Sri Hari-vamsa: ekenamala-patrena kantha-sutravalambina, raraja barhi-patrena manda-maruta-kampina, **“He shone with one spotless pinion, a peacock feather, that was hanging from a thread on the neck and was shaking in the gentle breeze”** (Hari-vamsa 2.11.10), it’s understood that the peacock feather was below the neck, and that there is always a crown made of that.121Thus there is an outfit like an theatrical actor’s.

Krsna put one hand on a follower’s shoulder is because of a natural condition due to a special pastime. Or it is on account of the abundance of His extreme affection for the cow herders. With the other one, the right hand, He was rotating a play lotus (abjam dhunanam = lila-kamalam bhramayantam), owing to the nature of a distinct cleverness. Possibly, it makes one aware of the removal of those ladies’ endless burning. In terms of beauty, the sequentially increasing superiority of these adjectives is to be inferred. It is presumed that He did not take the flute since it is not suited to Brahmanis, insofar as a flute brings about the topmost bewilderment.

The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami. In his commentary, alaka-kapola (on whose cheeks are curls) is because although the curls were above the forehead they fell on both cheeks, either due to some intention; due to some pastime; or because of the exertion of play.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Because it is said nata-vesam, in the second line, hiranya-paridhim means: His garment surrounds the waist, is curved, has lines of demarcation, has the color of liquid gold, and is obviously suitable for a dramatic actor.

Vana-malya means a garland fashioned with various forestial flowers; the sense is He had two vaikaksikas (garland worn like a sacred thread), over the left shoulder and under the right arm, and vice versa.” Peacock tail feathers (barha = barhani) and buds are ornaments on the head. Mineral pigments are called saugandhika (fragrant) and are obtained from a particular mountain in Kamyakavana; the limbs are colored with them. The sense is: taih nata-vesa-dharam, “Him, who, with those things, has the attire of a theatrical actor.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Hiranya-paridhim means His garment is tinged with the essence of gold. With a sylvan garland, made of leaves and flowers and hanging down to His feet, with a peacock’s tail feather atop His head, with mineral pigments fashioned as colors on the limbs, and with buds in the gap above each ear, His attire looked like the costume of a theatrical actor.

Moreover, Suka says the wives also realized His intent: “With the other one, the right hand, He was twirling a play lotus.” By bestowing this darsana, He was implying the following: “You should know that after letting the lotus of the hearts of you emotional women reach My hand, I am twirling it with eagerness.” Or He was hinting at this: “Now that I see you emotional ladies, the lotus of My heart is spinning out of eagerness, and so with the pretext of twirling a play lotus I am only showing you the whirl of My heart.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Pravala signifies nava-pallava (new buds). They were on the ears.

### 10.23.23

*prayah-sruta-priyatamodaya-karna-purair*  
*yasmin nimagna-manasas tam athaksi-randraih \|*  
*antah pravesya suciram parirabhya tapam*  
*prajnam yathabhimatayo vijahur narendra \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

prayah—often; sruta—heard; priyatama—of the dearest one; udaya—by means of the excellences (“rise, development, success”); karna-puraih—which are ornaments for the ears (“which fill the ears”); yasmin—in whom; nimagna-manasah—they whose minds are immersed; tam—Him; atha—afterward (after seeing Him); aksi-randhraih—through the orifices of the eyes; antah—within; pravesya—after causing \[Him\] to enter; su-ciram—for a very long time; parirabhya—after embracing; tapam—distress; prajnam— deep sleep (or a learned person); yatha—like; abhimatayah—the egos (functions of ego: mind, intellect and subfunctions thereof); vijahuh—especially gave up (in addition to their husbands, etc.); nara-indra—O best of men.

*narendra! prayah-sruta-priyatamodaya-karna-puraih yasmin (sri-krsne) nimagna-manasah (vipra-patnyah abhuvan, etah patnyah) abhimatayah atha tam (sri-krsnam svasam) aksi-randraih antah pravesya (tam) suciram parirabhya, (janah) yatha prajnam (jahati, tadvat) tapam vijahuh.*

*{athava: narendra! Prayah-sruta-priyatamodaya-karna-puraih yasmin (sri-krsne) nimagna-manasah (vipra-patnyah etavad-dina-paryantam asan, etah patnyah) atha tam (sri-krsnam) aksi-randraih antah pravesya (tam) suciram parirabhya, abhimatayah yatha prajnam (vijahati), tapam vijahuh.}*

**Перевод:**

**Their minds had been immersed in Krsna because of His various types of excellence. The wives had often heard about them and were ornaments for their ears. The ladies made Him enter their hearts through the apertures of their eyes, embraced Him for a very long time, and gave up their distress like the functions of ego give up deep sleep, O king.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Suka speaks the verse in the manner of expressing, by the quiescence of their external sensory functions, that the ladies sought to interact with Krsna in the mood of love that He was known to have.

“The ladies, whose minds were engrossed in Krsna because of His manifold excellence, which was often heard and which fill the ears, i.e. which make both ears successful—or karnapura means the excellences are ear ornaments—, made Him enter within through the eyes, mentally hugged Him for a very long time, and gave up distress, like the functions of ego give up the distress of material life by embracing the witness (the soul) in deep sleep, that is, after attaining a mergence in the witness (prajnam yathabhimatayah = aham-vrttayah susupti-saksinam parirabhya yatha = aham-vrttayah tasmin layam prapya yatha).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Atha means anantaram (afterward), that is, sadyah eva (immediately). “After making Him enter within via the holes of the eyes, i.e. directly beholding Him with great attachment, and embracing Him for a very long time, that is, merging (parirabhya = niliya) in Him out of prema—or embracing (parirabhya = alingya) Him as if directly, only with the mind—they especially, completely, gave up (vijahuh = visesena jahuh = samyaktaya jahuh) the distress... of material life, or the distress engendered by separation from Him (tapam = tapam samsarikam tad-vihara-jam va).” The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami.

Or the sense of the example is this: abhimatayah murtimad-abhimanah vidyadina maha-garvavantah te yatha prajnam parama-bhagavatam tat-krpaya parirabhya eva tapam sarvam vijahati, “like persons who are embodied self-conceits (abhimatayah), meaning they have a huge overweening pride because of knowledge and so on, give up all distress upon embracing, by his mercy, a topmost devotee of the Lord (prajnam).”

The gist of narendra is: “Since you are the best of men (indra = srestha), this is already known to you.” Or he makes him pay attention after noticing that his mind was agitated by prema on account of that topic.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“Immediately afterward (atha = anantaram = sadyah eva), they, making Him enter within, in the mind, through the holes of the eyes, embraced Him for a very long time with the mind, meaning they merged (parirabhya = niliya) in Him voluntarily while covering those eyes, which were like doors, out of bashfulness, and gave up distress, the affliction engendered by not touching Him.” A renewed occurrence of that is rejected with the word vi (in vijahuh), because of the termination of this aspect: “Alas! He is not touched.”

Alternatively: abhimukhi matir yesam te yatha prajnam parama-bhagavatam parirabhya netradibhir aslisya tapam sarvam jahati tadvat, “like men whose thoughts are conformable give up all distress after embracing, with the eyes and the mind, a topmost devotee of the Lord.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Up to this day, the ladies’ minds were immersed in Sri Krsna by means of His excellences, which were often heard and which are ornaments of the ears. This means they fill the ears, and so they make the ears successful.

At this time the ladies made Him enter inside, on the lotus bed of the inner consciousness, through the eyes, embraced Him for a very long time, firmly, and, when they felt one with Him, they, who had fainted out of bliss only by the firmness of the embrace, gave up distress, the affliction generated by not touching His body.

An example is given: abhimatayo ’ham-vrttayah prajnam susupti-saksinam parirabhya tasmin layam prapya yatha, “like the functions of ego give up distress after embracing the witness in deep sleep, that is, after attaining a mergence in the witness.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“The ladies, whose minds were immersed in Him by means of the various kinds of His supereminence, which were heard in many ways and which are ear ornaments, made Him enter the lotus of the heart (antah = hrt-kamale), at this time (atha = samprati), through the holes of the eyes, embraced Him for a very long time, i.e. very intensely, and gave up (vijahuh = jahuh) distress produced by separation from Him.”

There is an example: yatha abhimatayah deha-gehadisu aham-mamety abhimanah susuptau prajnam paramatmanam prapya jagara-tapam jahati tadvat, “like conceits of ‘I’ and ‘mine’ in regard to the body, the house, and so on, shake off their distress of the waking state by obtaining Paramatma in deep sleep.”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Prajnam means sarva-jnam (omniscient) and modifies tam (Him). The sense is He knew: “I am being embraced by these ones with the mind.” He cognized the joy of their embrace at that time.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The ladies’ eyes remained unhappy after perceiving the good fortune of their ears by hearing again and again. To remove the eyes’ sorrow, the ladies made Him enter through the eyes. Although the Lord is one, He entered through the apertures of the eyes of all the ladies and became manifest in their hearts.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Atha means darsananantaram (after seeing Him). The example is: abhimatayah bhagavad-bhaktanam tad-didrksatmikah buddhayah prajnam paramatmanam \[...\] tam drstva yatha tad-darsanabhava-jam jahuh tapam adhyatmikadikam va jahati tadvat, “Just as, after seeing Him, Paramatma, the intelligence, of the nature of the desire to see the Lord,122of the Lord’s devotees shakes off distress...” born of not seeing Him, or bodily distress, or mental distress.

Paramatma is Prajna, by looking at the texts of Sruti: (1) prajnenatmana samparisvaktah, “\[In liberation, the soul is\] completely embraced by the Soul, Prajna” (Brhad-aranyaka Upanisad 4.3.21) and (2) prajnenatmananvarudhah, “\[The soul in the body,\] ‘mounted’ by the Soul, Prajna, \[gives up the body and departs\]” (Brhad-aranyaka Upanisad 4.3.35)

In the reading atimatayah, the sense is: jnanadhikah (very knowledgeable ladies).

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

“Just as the functions of ego (abhimatayah = ahankara-vrttayah), having attained the witness in deep sleep, i.e. its own self, a form of the Lord (prajnam = susupti-saksinam = svatmanam = bhagavad-rupam), become merged in that, so these ladies attained sayujya in the Lord.” Subsequently, they, who had a remainder of samskara, came out, otherwise it would just be sayujya.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“The ladies let go of their distress like the functions of a living entity’s intelligence (abhimatayah = jiva-buddhi-vrttayah) shake off distress after attaining the Lord,” who is well-known as Prajna in the Sruti: prajnenatmana samparisvaktah, and prajnenatmananvarudhah.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Or abhi-matayah signifies: abhitah matih yesam te abhimatayah nipunah, “like men who are expert, meaning their thoughts are on all sides, endorse a learned person (prajnam = vidvamsam)123and give up their anguish.”

**Annotation**

The word prajna has many meanings. Prajna (deep sleep) is one of the four states: visva (the soul that enjoys coarse matter) (waking state), taijasa (the soul that enjoys subtle matter) (dream state), prajna (the soul that enjoys the causal matter: ego) (deep sleep), and turiya (the soul as the witness of these states) (trance) (Bhagavatam 7.15.54) (12.11.22).

The state of being the witness is one in all four states: sthula- suksma-karana-rupair visva-taijasa-prajnesvaraih sarvavasthasu saksi tv eka evavatisthate, “Only one witness abides in all conditions characterized by visva, taijasa, prajna, and isvara, which are the forms of the coarse (matter), the subtle (the life force, etc.), the causal sheath (karana-kosa), \[and transcendence respectively\]”(Narada-parivrajaka Upanisad 6).

References for equating prajna with the causal sheath include:

(1) visvo hi sthula-bhun nityam, taijasah pravivikta-bhuk, ananda-bhuk tatha prajnas tridha bhogam nibodhata, “Know the threefold enjoyment: visva is always the enjoyer of the coarse, taijasa is the enjoyer of the subtle, and prajna is the enjoyer of bliss” (Mandukya Upanisad 1.3);

(2) eki-bhutah susupta-sthah prajnana-ghanavan sukhi. nityananda-mayo ’py atma sarva-jivantara-sthitah. tathapy ananda-bhuk ceto-mukhah sarva-gato ’vyayah. catur-atmesvarah prajnah, “The soul, situated in deep sleep, has become one, has dense transcendental consciousness, and is happy. The Soul, also made of eternal bliss, is situated within all jivas. Nonetheless He enjoys bliss, His chief elements is mind, He pervades all, and is imperishable. The controller, caturatma, is Prajna” (Narada-parivrajaka Upanisad 8.12-13).

Moreover, Vira-Raghava writes: samhrti-sakty-adhisthata susupti-nirvahakah sankarsanah prajnah, “Sankarsana, the presider of the power of annihilation, the accomplisher of deep sleep, is Prajna” (Bhagavata-candra-candrika 7.15.54). Visvanatha Cakravarti says Pradyumna is the presiding deity of prajna (Sarartha- darsini 12.11.22).

God is designated as Prajna in this sutra: vadatiti cen na prajno hi prakaranat, “If \[the contention is: “The text of Katha Upanisad 1.3.11\] says \[avyakta, pradhana, is to be known,” the answer is:\] No, because Prajna \[is understood\] from the context” (Vedanta-sutra 1.4.5). Baladeva Vidyabhusana says prajna denotes Paramatma: hi yasmat tatra prajnah paramatmaivocyate, “because only Paramatma is said there” (Govinda-bhasya 1.4.5).

The word prajna can also denote a soul: prajno vedanta-vid yogi nirmamo nirahankrtih, “Prajna is a yogi who knows Vedanta (the Upanisads) and is devoid of both possessiveness and false ego” (Narada-parivrajaka Upanisad 6.24).

### 10.23.24

*tas tatha tyakta-sarvasah prapta atma-didrksaya \|*  
*vijnayakhila-drg-drasta praha prahasitananah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tah—them; tatha—in that way; tyakta-sarva-asah—they by whom all hopes are abandoned; praptah—obtained (arrived); atma-didrksaya—with the desire to see Him; vijnaya—understanding; akhila-drk—of the consciousness of all; drasta—the seer; praha— He spoke; prahasita-ananah—in whose face there is laughter.

*akhila-drg-drasta (bhagavan) tah (striyah) tatha(-bhutah) tyakta-sarvasah atma-didrksaya praptah vijnaya prahasitananah (san) praha (sma).*

**Перевод:**

**Understanding that those ladies were in that way, had abandoned all hopes of going back home and had arrived with the desire to see Him, Krsna, the observer of everyone’s consciousness, spoke. There was glee on His face.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Akhila-drg-drasta means sarva-buddhi-saksi (the witness of everyone’s intelligence).124“Even after understanding that they had arrived in that way (tas tatha prapta vijnayapi)...” Next he expounds upon tatha (in that way). Tyakta-sarvasah means: tyaktah sarvah asah yabhih tah, “them, by whom all hopes were abandoned.” Atma-didrksaya signifies: kevalam atmanah svasya eva didrksaya (exclusively with the desire to see Him).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

He is the witness of everyone’s intelligence (akhila-drg-drasta = sarva-buddhinam saksi): That is the reason for understanding. Alternatively: Even after understanding, He eminently spoke (praha = prakarsena aha)... by illustrating a logical reasoning. In this He is well versed in all knowledge. This means He spoke while pondering: “It is not appropriate for Me to do as they want.” Therefore He was prahasitananah (in His face is laughter); the laughter was only in His face, by the apprehension of their sorrow within if He were to abandon them. Or, in the manner that is about to be said, the sense is: “while pondering, “These ladies and their husbands might have peace of mind.”” And because of that, having laughter in His face was just natural, because it usually happens on His divine face.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Atma-didrksaya (with the desire to see Him) is because, at first, of the longing for Him only. He is the witness of everyone’s intelligence (akhila-drg-drasta = sarva-buddhinam saksi): That is the reason for understanding. Alternatively, akhila-drg-drasta signifies: akhila-drsam buddhy-adi-drastrnam jivanam api drasta, “the observer of all souls, who witness the intelligence and so on.” In point of prahasitananah (He in whose face is laughter), there is a cleverness of deception which involves sweetness.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Seeing (vijnaya = drstva) them in that way, meaning He saw how they were (tatha = tatha-bhutah): they had placed their presents of food in front and were starting to faint, He, the witness of the intellects of everyone (akhila-drg-drasta = akhilanam api drsam buddhinam drasta), spoke.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“Then, the Lord, noticing that they had come with the desire to see Him, and understanding that they abandoned all hopes related to their respective families (tyakta-sarvasah = tyaktah sarvah asah paty-adi-visayah yabhih tah), spoke.” Prahasitananah means: prahasitam ananam yasya, “He whose face is laughing.”

### 10.23.25

*svagatam vo maha-bhaga asyatam karavama kim \|*  
*yan no didrksaya prapta upapannam idam hi vah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

su-agatam—welcome (“nice arrival”); vah—to you; maha-bhagah—O greatly fortunate ladies; asyatam—sitting should be done; karavama kim—what should we do (the royal ‘we’); yat— which; nah—Us; didrksaya—with the desire to see; praptah—\[you,\] who have arrived; upapannam—appropriate; idam—this; hi— because; vah—on your part.

*maha-bhagah! vah svagatam (astu. yusmabhih atra) asyatam. (vayam vah) kim karavama, hi nah didrksaya praptah (iti yad asti, tad) idam vah upapannam (bhavati).*

**Перевод:**

**“Welcome, greatly fortunate ladies! Be seated. What can We do for you? That you have come with the desire to see Us is appropriate on your part.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Hey greatly fortunate ladies! Your splendid arrival (vah svagatam = vah subham agamanam) has occurred.” That is just what He talks about: “because (yat = yasmat) this, i.e. you came with the desire to see Us by removing the impediments, is excellent on your part,” or “is appropriate on your part” (upapannam = sampannam, yuktam va).”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Take rest near Me (asyatam = mad-antike visramyatam),” and consequently: kim karavama, “What shall We do?” The sense is: “It should be specified.” And this is only because of the state of being merciful. It is to be understood in that way. Similarly, the mention of plurality in karavama and in nah, which means asmakam (us), is, by His bringing about a generality, for the purpose of covering, out of shyness, the state of being solely fixed on Him; or it is for the purpose of indifference. Although the ladies came just for the sake of servanthood—that will become clear ahead—nevertheless, He says didrksaya (“with a desire to see” Us) for the purpose of covering, out of good manners in a gathering, the Brahmanis’ special emotions.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) Exactly in that way (a cleverness of deception involving sweetness), He speaks with respect. “Take rest (asyatam = visramyatam),” and consequently: kim karavama, “What shall We do?” The sense is: “It should be specified.” The explanation is this: The mention of plurality in karavama and in nah, which means asmakam (us), is, by bringing about a generality, for the purpose of covering the state of being solely fixed on Him and for the purpose of indifference.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He talks to them, who had great love, like He will talk to gopis who are going to a rendezvous at the time of Rasa. “Let You arrival be splendid (vah svagatam = vah subham eva agamanam), because (yat = yasmat) this, “you came with the desire to see Us while removing millions of impediments,” was accomplished by you (vah upapannam = vah upapadyate sma eva).”

The gist is: “Owing to My inability to reciprocate, I did nothing.” Therefore, “What can We do for you?” The sense is: “I am indebted to you.” Hence, “O you who are even more greatly fortunate than I (maha-bhagah = matto ’pi maha-bhagyavatyah)! Be seated here for a moment (asyatam = ksanam iha upavisyatam)... just for the sake of looking at Me.”

### 10.23.26

*nanv addha mayi kurvanti kusalah svartha-darsinah \|*  
*ahaituky-avyavahitam bhaktim atma-priye yatha \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

nanu—indeed; addha—truly; mayi—unto Me; kurvanti—they do; kusalah—clever persons; sva-artha—one’s benefit; darsinah— they who see (or they who make others see); ahaituki—unselfish (“without a reason”); avyavahitam—uninterrupted; bhaktim— devotional service; atma-priye—\[to Me,\] who am the Soul and who am dear (or who am dearer than themselves); yatha—suitably.

**Комментарий. Автор :**

*nanu (ye) atma-priye mayi kusalah (atah eva) svartha-darsinah (bhavanti, te) addha yatha ahaituky-avyavahitam bhaktim kurvanti.*

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*yatha (raginah) atma-priye (pritim kurvanti, tadvad) nanu kusalah (atah eva) svartha-darsinah mayi addha ahaituky-avyavahitam bhaktim kurvanti.*

**“Indeed, clever persons who see their benefit suitably perform true devotional service, unselfish and uninterrupted, unto Me. I am dearer to them than they are to themselves.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Here He talks about the aforesaid state of being appropriate: “Those who have good discrimination (kusalah = vivekinah) regarding Me, who am the Soul and am dear to them (atma-priye = atma ca priyas ca tasmin), and therefore they are svartha-darsin, meaning they see their own true benefit (svartha = svasya purusartha), suitably (yatha = yathavat) do devotional service.”

Next He talks about the suitability: addha means saksat (direct). The reason for this is: ahaituky-avyavahitam. This means: phalabhisandhi-rahitam atah eva avyavahitam nirantaram, “They do bhakti which is devoid of an aim for a selfish result and hence is continuous.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“O Brahmanis (nanu = nanu bhu-devyah).” Or nanu means niscitam (certainly).125

Addha means saksad eva (only direct), i.e. visuddham, “pure bhakti,” because: ahaituki (unselfish). Or addha mayi means: saksan mayi, “bhakti directly to Me,” but not to a Guna Avatara and the like.

He talks about the fact that bhakti is appropriate (yatha =yathavat): ahaituki. Atma-priye means: atmanah sakasad api priye, “to Me, who am even dearer than oneself,” on account of being Paramatma. Or, svartha-darsin is a guru, who habitually shows one’s true benefit, and so svartha-darsinah means: unselfish bhakti “because of the guru,” that is, because of his instructions.

Or svartha-darsinah is in the nominative plural and yatha means “like”: svartha-darsinah janah yatha kusalah pativratah striyah atma-priye, “People who see their benefit perform exclusive bhakti to Me like women who are clever, that is, dedicated to their respective husband, are devoted to someone dear to them.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

He speaks to cheat, at this time, the ladies’ desire to attain His association. Addha means saksad eva, i.e. visuddham (pure), because: ahaituki and so on. In that regard, He talks about the fact that bhakti is appropriate (yatha = yathavat): ahaituki. Atma-priye means: atmanah sakasad api priye, “to Me, who am even dearer than oneself,” on account of being Paramatma. The idea is: “Since I continuously have your association, due to being Paramatma also, an obstinacy for associating in a manner of being perceived by everyone should not be implemented.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Although the ladies had the topmost prema, at that time the fulfillment of their inner longing would not bring the nourishment of Rasa, and without the nourishment of Rasa a pastime does not make for astonishment, therefore the Lord’s aisvarya, made to suddenly appear in His mind only by lila- sakti, became the cause of those ladies’ going back to their homes.

Although for the most part aisvarya is unable to make its appearance in the proximity of persons who have prema, still, for the sake of the excellence of the pastime, it certainly could make its appearance to increase those ladies’ prema by increasing an intense longing in separation, and so it pacified the Lord’s bhava known as rati and caused the rise of His good jusdgement. Therefore in two verses the Lord speaks only in a manner favorable to that.

“Not only you ladies are greatly attracted to Me. Many other persons perform bhakti, i.e. priti (affection), to Me, Paramesvara.” Who are they? They are clever persons (kusalah = caturah). He talks about that cleverness: svartha-darsinah.The drift is: Obviously, in this world only those who cause the accomplishment of their goals are said to be clever.

Ahaituky-avyavahitam means the bhakti is devoid of a selfish desire and is unobstructed, meaning there is no jnana-yoga or occupation which would effect the obstruction of affection. An example is given: atma-priye yatha, “like a person is devoted to something dear to oneself, such as the body or a child (atma-priye = dehapatyadau).”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

He clarifies the appropriateness: “Those who have good discrimination (kusalah = vivekinah)—therefore they know their own benefit (svartha-darsinah = svartha-jnah)— perform direct (addha = saksat) bhakti to Me like passionate people are affectionate to someone who loves them.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

He expounds upon the appropriateness. “O wives of Brahmanas (nanu = nanu dvija-patnyah)! Persons who rightly discriminate between what is beneficial to them and what is not (kusalah = atma-hitahita-vivekinah janah) and who know their purpose (svartha-darsanah126= sva-prayojanabhijnah) perform bhakti only to Me (mayi addha = mayi eva), who am even dearer to them than they are to themselves (atma-priye = svasmad api priye).”

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

Nanu has the sense of a soft vocative. “They perform direct (addha = saksat) bhakti," but it is not that they perform bhakti for the sake of the fulfillment of a material desire.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“O chaste ladies (nanu = nanu satyah)! Only they who appropriately (yatha = yathavat) perform bhakti to Me, who am dear to them (atma-priye = atmanam priye), are kusala and svartha-darsin." He talks about the appropriateness: addha means sphutam (clearly).127

### 10.23.27

*prana-buddhi-manah-svatma-darapatya-dhanadayah \|*  
*yat-samparkat priya asams tatah ko nv aparah priyah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

prana—life force; buddhi—intelligence; manah—mind; sva—body (or relatives); atma—soul (or body); dara—wife; apatya—offsprings; dhana—wealth; adayah—and so on; yat-samparkat—because of the connection with whom (Paramatma); priyah—dear; asan—were (are); tatah—than Him (than Paramatma); kah—who; nu—indeed; aparah—other; priyah—dear.

*prana-buddhi-manah-svatma-darapatya-dhanadayah yat-samparkat priyah asan, tatah aparah kah nu priyah (syat).*

**Перевод:**

**“One’s vitality, intelligence, mind, relatives, body, wife, offsprings, wealth, and so on are dear because of a connection with the self. Who at all is dearer than one’s self?**

**Alternatively: “The life force, the intelligence, the mind, the body, the soul, the wife, the offsprings, wealth, and so on are dear because of a connection with Paramatma. Who at all, other than Him, might be dear?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He expounds upon the notion that one’s self is dearer than all. Sva, in the plural, means jnatayah (relatives), atman means deha (body). Yat-samparkat means: yasya adhyasena upakaranatvena va, “because of the connection of the self, either by a wrongful superimposition or in terms of being helpful.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

To prove that He is the most dear, as Paramatma, at first He says only the soul is dear. The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami. Alternatively, in this verse He establishes that Paramatma is dearer than the soul. “They are (asan = bhavanti) dear only by a connection, such as an entrustment, with Me (yat-samparkat = yasya mama samarpanadi-sambandhena eva).”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

He establishes that Paramatma is dearer than the soul. Here, atman means jiva. Yat-samparkat means: yasya mama paramatmanah samparkad, atmanah api mad-amsatvena eva tathathvat, “because of a connection with Me, Paramatma, that is, because the soul too is like that simply on account of being a spark of Me.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

An example was shown only for the sake of making the general idea enter the intelligence. In truth, however, the supporting example, from the example of the body and so on, is: “Paramatma, I, am very dear.” In this verse, He enlightens them with this logical reasoning.

Sva means svam, i.e. deha (body); atman means jiva. Thus, all of those are dear because of the connection of Paramatma (yat-samparkat = yasya paramatmanah sambandhat). Is there anything dearer than Paramatma? (tatah = paramatmanah).

### 10.23.28

*tad yata deva-yajanam patayo vo dvi-jatayah \|*  
*sva-satram parayisyanti yusmabhir grha-medhinah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tat—therefore; yata—all of you should go; deva-yajanam—to the sacrificial grounds; patayah—husbands; vah—your; dvi-jatayah—twice-born persons; sva-satram—their sacrificial session; parayisyanti—will bring to completion; yusmabhih—with you; grha-medhinah—householders (“they have a sacrifice for the house,” i.e. householders who do domestic sacrifices).

*tad (yuyam) deva-yajanam yata. vah patayah dvi-jatayah grha-medhinah yusmabhih (saha) sva-satram parayisyanti (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Therefore go to the sacrificial grounds. Your husbands, twice-born domestic sacrificers, will complete their sacrifice with you.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Therefore (tat = tasmat) you, who are successful, should go to the sacrificial grounds (deva-yajanam yata = krtarthah yuyam yajna-vatam gacchata). In case they argue, “Why should we go if we’re successful?”, He says patayah (husbands) and so on. Parayisyanti means samapayisyanti (they will complete). The sense is: for the sake of your husbands’ blessings.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“They will complete their sacrifice (sva-satram = svakiyam yajnam).” They are grha-medhin (they are householders), meaning they cannot complete it without their wives.

For this reason, in consideration of the Brahmanas it is said: deva-yajanam yata, “Go to the sacrificial grounds,” but not: “Go home.”

The ladies might argue, “They should be disregarded since they disrespected You.” To that He says: dvi-jatayah, which means they are Brahmanas. The sense is: “On account of bhakti to Me, they must be honored.” Consequently He Himself will say, in the story of Nrga:

*vipram krtagasam api naiva druhyata mamakah \|*  
*ghnantam bahu sapantam va namas-kuruta nityasah \|\|*

**“My dear kinsmen, do not harm a Brahmana, even if he committed an offense. Even if he assaults you or repeatedly curses you, always salute him.” (10.64.41)**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Sridhara Svami’s approval of the reading: tad yata deva-yajanam is perceived, inasmuch as he quotes the reading, yet the reading: tad yata sadhvyo yajanam is almost everywhere.

The word sva (own) in sva-satram signifies that the Brahmanas need to conclude the sacrifice because it is their own.

Here too Krsna’s ordering the wives to go back to their husbands, who were averse to Him, is because He is everyone’s well-wisher, He is beneficial to cows and to Brahmanas, and He wanted to do a favor through the connection of those ladies.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Since you heard from Garga’s mouth that Paramatma too is I, go to the sacrificial grounds.” They might reply, “Still, why should we abandon You, who are Paramatma in person and go home?” He responds: “They will conclude it with you.”

The idea is: “Rites such as a satra were enounced only by Me, whose form is the Vedas, and so you should go just because of a compliance with what is to be done in relation to Me. You will see Me there. I will be sparkling (visible) and embodied.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“They will conclude the sacrifice only with you, who will have become assistants, since a husband and his wife have an eligibility together.”

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

“Without you, your husbands have no eligibility (adhikara).”

### 10.23.29

*patnya ucuh*  
*maivam vibho ’rhati bhavan gaditum nrsamsam*  
*satyam kurusva nigamam tava pada-mulam \|*  
*prapta vayam tulasi-dama padavasrstam*  
*kesair nivodhum atilanghya samasta-bandhun \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

patnyah ucuh—the wives said; ma—not; evam—such; vibho—O omnipresent Lord; arhati—ought; bhavan—You; gaditum—to speak; nr-samsam—harsh (or harshly); satyam—true; kurusva— make; nigamam—word; tava—Your; pada-mulam—the soles of the feet; praptah—attained; vayam—we; tulasi-dama—the garland of tulasi \[sprigs\]; pada—with the foot; avasrstam—let loose below (discarded); kesaih—with the hairs; nivodhum—to continuously carry; atilanghya—after disobeying; samasta-bandhun—all relatives.

*patnyah ucuh—vibho! bhavan evam nrsamsam (vacah) gaditum ma arhati. (tvam tava) nigamam satyam kurusva. vayam samasta-bandhun atilanghya tulasi-dama padavasrstam (svasam) kesaih nivodhum tava pada-mulam praptah.*

**Перевод:**

**The wives said: “O pervader! You should not speak so harshly. Make Your word come true. We disobeyed all our family relatives and have attained the soles of Your feet to continuously carry in our hair a tulasi garland discarded by Your foot.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Do not speak such harsh words (nrsamsam = parusam). Make your promise (nigamam = pratijnam) come true: na me bhaktah pranasyati, “My devotee does not perish” (Bhagavad-gita 9.31). Or “Make the Veda (nigamam = vedam) come true: na sa punar avartate, “One does not return again” (Chandogya Upanisad 8.15.1).”

Padavasrstam signifies: avajnaya api dattam, “given even with contempt.” Kesair nivodhum means: bahu-manena kesair nivodhum dasi-bhavitum, “to carry with great reverence, with the hair,” that is, “to become maidservants.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

The mention of the word ma (not) at first is from a forbiddance in terms of being disturbed to the utmost. Evam means idrsim, “this kind \[of speech\],” which refers to: patinam samapanartham yajna-sthanam yata, “Go to the sacrificial grounds so that your husbands to complete their sacrifice.” The vocative vibho denotes: bahir-antar-vyapaka, “O you who pervade outside and inside.” The drift is: “Our outside and our inside, everything, are already known to You.” The reading vacah (speech) is easy to understand.

The honorific bhavan (You) connotes this idea: “You who usually speak sweetly should not speak so harshly.” Or the sense of bhavan is: rasarnava-candrah (the moon from the ocean of Rasa). The sense is: “You shouldn’t speak hard words devoid of Rasa.”

“Your words are not just cruel, they’re also lies.” With this in mind they say: satyam and so on. At first: bhavan (You), for the sake of an entreaty with bhakti, then: kurusva (You should do), hence they only spoke with prema.

Although the truthfulness of the Vedas might not be accomplished from a transgression of etiquette by accepting those ladies, still, owing to the statement of Sruti that begins: na sa punar avartate (Chandogya Upanisad 8.15.1) and from the text of Smrti that starts: devarsi-bhutapta-nrnam, “O king, one who completely abandons work and goes to Mukunda, who should be resorted to, for shelter with all one’s heart remains neither a servant of nor a debtor to gods, Rsis, other beings, honorable men, or forefathers” (Bhagavatam 11.5.41), and since devotees are beyond injunctions and prohibitions, that truthfulness can certainly be accomplished simply because He is the Lord in person.

“On account of bringing you within Gokula, the gopis will treat Me with contempt and will as if exhibit rivalry toward you.” They respond with tava and so on. The short i in tulasi is poetic license (because of the meter). It is a garland of tulasi. “To continuously carry (nivodhum = nitaram vodhum), that is, to always carry with a special devotion, a garland of tulasi, because Your lotus feet are always coming in contact with it, since it is dear, and because it is worthy of being highly regarded by Laksmi and others, with rivalry (or due to being a cowife).”

The gist is: “By the servanthood of merely continuously carrying only that, the gopis will not treat You with contempt nor will they exhibit rivalry toward us.” Or the gist is: “By our servanthood to You, we will occasion those ladies’ servanthood.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The first three paragraphs above are the same here. Moreover:) His promise (nigamam) is to be understood only as: karavama kim, “What can We do for you” (Bhagavatam 10.23.25). Here it should be known that because of their longing, the ladies did not point out the fact that the Lord does not go against the wish of a Brahmana.

Krsna might say, “It is not right for you Brahmanis to completely abandon your husbands and others.” They answer: “We have attained the soles of Your feet.” This means “We have abandoned everything and have accepted servanthood (dasyam) to You.” This meaning of “tava pada-mulam prapta vayam” is an atyanta-tiraskrta-vacya-dhvani, an implied meaning in regard to which the literal meaning is discarded.

Not only that, the ladies want to hold on their heads the tulasi garland discarded by His foot, having determined that His feet have great aisvarya. Thus, their fault in meeting Him is repudiated by the style of His statements of this sort: sarva-dharman parityajya, “Totally rejecting all moral duties, only take shelter of Me” (Bhagavad-gita 18.66).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He talks as if they were gopis who have great love at the beginning of Rasa. “Make the Vedic statement: na ca punar avartate, “One does not return again” (Chandogya Upanisad 8.15.1) and Your own statement, the form of a sacred precept: ye yatha mam prapadyate tams tathaiva bhajamy aham, “I serve them in the same way they devote themselves to Me” (Bhagavad-gita 4.11) (nigamam = veda-vakyam, nigama-rupam sva-vakyam ca) come true.” A conversation ensued:

—It is hard for you ladies to give up the conceit of being in the Brahmana caste.

—For the sake of servanthood we attained the soles of Your feet although You are a cowherd. If we had a conceit of being in the Brahmana caste, no one could speak like this, therefore it should be deduced simply by our speech. We don’t have the conceit of belonging to a caste.

—Only gopis are suitably maidservants of Mine and beloveds of Mine, a cowherd. There are many of them.

—That’s true. Fine, let them be, let them shine. We would remain only in Vrndavana like presiding deities of a forest. We would become successful just by the scent of a connection with You. We don’t have a desire for the mood of a lover nor for the mood of a maidservant, both of which are hard to get.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

By hinting, with padavasrstam tulasi-dama, at the topmost godhood in Him, this is implied: “We only want dasya unto you. Moreover, the svarupa of a jiva already has dasya unto You.” The Padma Purana states: dasa-bhuto harer eva, “A soul is a servant only of Hari” (quoted in Govinda-bhasya 2.3.43, Prameya-ratnavali 5.2, and Paramatma-sandarbha 19).

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Alternatively, nigamam denotes this promise: sakrd eva prapanno yas tavasmiti ca yacate, abhayam sarvada tasmai dadamy etad vratam mama, **“I bestow constant fearlessness to him who, even just once, surrenders, and beseeches Me by saying: “I am Yours.” This is My oath.”** (Ramayana, yuddha-kanda 12.20)

### 10.23.30

*grhnanti no na patayah pitarau suta va*  
*na bhratr-bandhu-suhrdah kuta eva canye \|*  
*tasmad bhavat-prapadayoh patitatmanam no*  
*nanya bhaved gatir arindama tad vidhehi \|\|*  
*(vasanta-tilaka)*

**Пословный перевод:**

grhnanti—they take (they will accept); nah—us (or our); na—not; patayah—husbands; pitarau—two parents; sutah—sons; va—or; na—nor; bhratr—brothers; bandhu—relatives; suhrdah—friends; kutah—why; eva—indeed; ca—and; anye—others; tasmat— therefore; bhavat—Your; prapadayoh—at the two front parts of the feet; patita-atmanam—whose bodies are fallen; nah—our; na—not; anya—another; bhavet—can be; gatih—recourse; arindama—O subduer of enemies129; tat—that (servanthood: dasyam); vidhehi— make (bestow).

*arindama! nah patayah pitarau sutah va (asman) na grhnanti, (tatha nah) bhratr-bandhu-suhrdah ca na (grhnanti). anye (janah asman) kutah eva (grhniyuh). tasmad bhavat-prapadayoh patitatmanam nah (tvattah) anya gatih na bhavet, (atah tvam asman) tad (sva-dasyam) vidhehi (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Neither our husbands, parents, nor sons will take us, nor will our brothers, relatives, and friends, so why would others accept us? Therefore we, whose bodies are fallen in front of Your feet, have no other recourse. O subduer of enemies, make it happen!”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Moreover, they will not take us (nah = asman).” The vocative arindama (subduer of enemies) denotes: kama-lobha-papadi-damana, “O You who subdue lust, greed, sinful reactions, and so on.” “Let us, whose bodies are fallen in front of Your feet (bhavat-prapadayoh patitatmanam = bhavatah padagrayoh patita-dehanam), not have another destination such as Svarga (nanya bhaved gatih = anya svargadi-gatih api ma bhut). Therefore (tat = tasmat) bestow servanthood to us (vidhehi = dasyam vidhehi iti).”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Krsna might think about saying, in reference to: sadhavo dina-vatsalah, “Saintly persons care for wretched people” (11.2.6): “Go for their sake,” or “By My order, even something that should not be done should still be done.” They counter that here. The gist is: “Even if we return there, they will certainly not accept us (grhnanti nah = asman na svi-karisyanti).” Or the sense is: “On account of noticing our mood toward You, they already spurned us right at first.”

Concerning pitarau (two parents): Although the mothers of the wives did not forbid them to go, they would not be willing to take them back out of fear of their own husbands. Or the sense is the wives exaggerated to make Him aware of their condition of not having any recourse but Him. In that regard, the proper discernment is this: In consideration of dharma, etc., they went to their husbands, but were not accepted by them. Owing to affection, they went to their respective parents’ homes; even they did not take them. Out of fear of people, etc., they went to their sons out of affection for them, which was greater than their affection for their parents, but still their sons did not take them. Hence why might others, neighbors and so forth, take them?

“Therefore (tasmat), that is, because of the nonacceptance by the husbands and others, we, whose bodies are fallen in front of both lotus feet, in other words, not far away, out of the topmost meekness, meaning we take exclusive shelter of You because You are our last resort, ...” The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami.

There is another rendering: Patitatmanam denotes: patitanam iva atma svabhavah yasam tasam, “our nature is like the nature of fallen people.” This is expressive of humility. “Bring about that which relates to the forefront of Your feet (bhavat-prapadayos tat),” which means: “Bring about our action of continuously carrying one of Your discarded tulasi garland with our hair, as mentioned before (tat = purvoktam kesaih tulasi-dama-nivahanam).” Not clearly specifying it is because it is very hard to get and because it is most confidential.

There is another interpretation. Tat means tatha (in that way). From the constant connection between yat and tat, the word yatha is added, and so the idea is: yatha anya tvad-dasyetara gatih phalam na bhavet, tatha vidhehi, “Make our servitude to You happen in such a way that there will be no other result.”

“Still, I fear the rivalry of the divine gopikas.” They respond: arindama (O subduer of enemies). This means: “Only You will obliterate the enemy which is their jealousy.”

There is another explanation: patitatmanam mrtanam satinam, tayoh agre mryamahe, gatih ca anya na bhaved iti vidhehi, “Given that our bodies have fallen dead at Your feet, ensure that this will remain our sole destination.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) He might add, in reference to: sadhavo dina-vatsalah, “Saintly persons care for wretched people” (11.2.6): “Go for their sake,” or He might say: “By My order, even something that should not be done should still be done.” They respond here. The gist is: Even if we return there, they will certainly not accept us (grhnanti nah = asman na svi-karisyanti), on account of transgressing their interdiction. As for the others, neighbors and so on, they will not even utter a word. Therefore, that is, because of the nonacceptance by the husbands and others, we, whose bodies are fallen near the tip of both feet of Yours (prapadayoh = padagra-samipe), meaning we have taken shelter only of You due to not having another recourse...”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Moreover, from that day, beginning from puberty, when we heard about Your form, virtues, and sweetness from the mouths of the womenfolk, such as the garlandmaker and the seller of betel nuts, in Your town, our husbands, not engaging in close contact after seeing us, who were emotional, were indifferent to household chores too and were as if deviating, never had any dealing with us.” This is the substance of the verse.

Sutah means sapatni-putrah (sons of cowives). Anye (others) means prativesyadayah (neighbors et al.). With tasmat (therefore) and so on, the ladies, bowing in front of His feet while weeping with great agitation, speak with a choked voice: asmakam anya gatir yatha na bhavet tatha vidhehi, “Make it happen in such a way that we cannot have any other course of action.”

“O arindama!” The sense is: “You should subdue, out of mercy, the enemies, such as grave difficulties, that have become impediments in attaining You.”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Alternatively, the present tense in grhnanti has the sense of the future, and no and na are two negative words that cancel each other: “It is not that they won’t take us.” In like manner, no is carried forward in conjunction with na bhratr-bandhu-suhrdah (It is not that the brothers, relatives, and friends will not take us). The drift is: “They will accept us. Because we like You, they will show more respect to us (since You are the Soul of all souls).”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“Make it happen (tad vidhehi)” means: “Bring about what was just said: tulasi-dama padavasrstam kesair nivodhum, “to continuously carry with our hair a tulasi garland discarded by Your foot” (10.23.29).”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Vidhehi means sampadaya (bring about).

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“Without Your help, they will never accept us, therefore shelter us (tad vidhehi = saranam kuru).”

### 10.23.31

*sri-bhagavan uvaca*  
*patayo nabhyasuyeran pitr-bhratr-sutadayah \|*  
*lokas ca vo mayopeta deva apy anumanvate \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-bhagavan uvaca—the Lord said; patayah—the husbands; na abhyasuyeran—cannot resent; pitr-bhratr-suta-adayah—fathers (or parents), brothers, sons, and so on; lokah—people; ca—and; vah— you; maya upetah—associated with Me; devah—the gods; api— even; anumanvate—approve.

*sri-bhagavan uvaca—patayah pitr-bhratr-sutadayah lokah ca vah na abhyasuyeran. maya upetah (yusman) devah api anumanvate.*

**Перевод:**

**The glorious Lord said: “No one, not even your husbands, parents, brothers, or sons, can despise you. Even the gods approve of you, who are associated with Me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Mayopetah means maya anujnatah (directed by Me). He says deva api (even the gods) after showing the gods in a directly perceptible way.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“They cannot have resentment, meaning they will not even see a fault, so why would they not accept you? Everyone of them, as well as the general population, cannot have resentment. By the influence of devotional service to Me, they are directed by Me (upetah = anujnatah),” or else “They are directly ordered (upetah = saksad adistah) by Me in My form as the inner controller, as we speak.”

“The gods, who are in the mode of goodness and are devoted to Me, cannot possibly resent you, My devotees. And specifically, the gods directly extol exclusive devotional service to Me, not to mention that they are under My control.” The rest was explained by the venerable one.

Alternatively, the sense is: “Neither the husbands or the gods can reject you, because you are needed to complete the fire sacrifice. The gods take a share of the sacrifice. Thereafter, your parents and others will accept you and show respect.”

Or mayopetah modifies vah in the accusative plural: “Even the gods approve of you (vah = yusman), who are associated with Me (mayopetah = maya sangatah), so why would the husbands and others despise you?”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“They cannot resent you, meaning they will not even see a fault, so why would they not take you? No one will resent you, and neither will the gods, who are affectionate.”

Mayopetah is an adjective of the ladies: “directed by Me” (mayopetah = maya anujnatah). The sense is: “The gods do not resent you simply because I give you permission to leave.”

The rest was explained by the venerable one. In his commentary, the gist of anujnatah is that the Lord takes the fault of being with the wives, because only that sort of meaning is proper. Regarding pratyaksam (in a directly perceptible way), the sense is: pratyaksam iva (as if in a directly perceptible way), on account of the usage of lat, the present tense (in anumanvate), by abandoning lin, the tense used in the context (in abhyasuyeran), which consists of sambhavana (assumption).

There is another interpretation: “The husbands and the others cannot resent you (vah = yusman), who are closely associated with Me (mayopetah = maya saha samipam sangatah), since it is known to them too that I am God,” because: “Even the gods, made to be directly perceptible by your husbands in the act of carrying out a fire sacrifice, approve.” In other words, “Once asked, the gods say they think of Me as God.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“All of you have prema for Me and are only dedicated to making Me happy, so you should not do what I don’t want. Don’t be stubborn. Go home.” “O crest jewel of smart persons! We, well-mannered ladies who cannot be touched by the sun, made light of them because of transgressing their words and came to You, who are famous in Vraja as a debauchee and are this far out of your village, and so our husbands will not even allow us to get back in town and will kill us today out of anger. We know this.” He responds: “The husbands cannot envy you (vah = yusmabhyam), meaning they won’t even see a fault. Why do you suspect that something undesirable will happen?”

Mayopetah modifies the ladies: “The gods respect you even though You are with Me (= maya saha sangatah api)... because it is known to them too that I am God,” because: “Even the gods, made to be directly perceptible by your husbands in acts related to the fire sacrifice and asked about this matter, will only approve of you (anumanvate = bhavatih anumanvate = bhavatih anumamsyante eva).”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“The husbands cannot have resentment, meaning they cannot superimpose a fault on qualities that are the sight of Me, a conversation with Me, and an offering of food to Me. The gods too, made to be directly perceptible by them in the fire sacrifice, respect you (vah = yusman), whom I gave permission to leave (upetah = anujnatah). This means the gods will approve (anvamanvate = anumodisyante) of you: “They did well.””

### 10.23.32

*na pritaye ’nuragaya hy anga-sango nrnam iha \|*  
*tan mano mayi yunjana aciran mam avapsyatha \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—not; pritaye—for the satisfaction; anuragaya—for the affection; hi—because; anga-sangah—bodily association; nrnam—of people; iha—here (in this world); tat—therefore; manah—the mind (or tan-manah—their minds); mayi—in Me; yunjanah—while linking; acirat—before long; mam—Me; avapsyatha—you will attain.

*hi iha (jagati) anga-sangah nrnam pritaye anuragaya (ca) na (bhavet), tad (yuyam) mayi manah yunjanah mam acirad avapsyatha (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Intimate bodily contact neither makes the populace happy nor makes them affectionate. Therefore, while linking yours minds in Me you will attain Me before long.”**

*hi iha (jagati) anga-sangah nrnam pritaye anuragaya (ca) na (bhavet), tad (yuyam) mayi manah yunjanah mam acirad avapsyatha (iti).*

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He speaks in case the ladies were to respond, “Still, we cannot abandon You.” Pritaye means sukhaya (for their joy). Anuragaya means sneha-vrddhaye (for their increase of affection). Anga-sangah denotes: angabhyam sangah (contact between two bodies).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Because (hi = yasmat) My bodily association with you as Brahmanis would be conducive neither to the joy of people, including the gopas and the gopis, nor to their affection for Me or you, therefore (tat = tasmat) you, while associating with Me only with the mind (mano yunjanah = manasa eva maya saha sangam kurvanah), will attain, in some other body, Me.” Or: “You will attain Me in the end, at the termination of the body (avapsyatha = ava prapsyatha) (ava = avasane = dehante).” Not mentioning it clearly in that way is for the sake of not generating their sorrow. For this reason it is said: acirat (before long), and that is only to console them.

Anga-sangah (bodily association) denotes either maithuna-laksanah (sex) or sada ekatra avasthitih (always abiding in the same place).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Suspecting that they might say, “So what about our request?”, He reconciles the matter: “In this life as Brahmanis (iha = brahmani-janmani), My bodily association with you (anga-sangah = yusmabhih mama anga-sangah), that is, a proximity consisting of the type of servanthood that you specified, would only be for the sake of affection (anuragaya), and so it would not be conducive to the joy of the population (na pritaye = sukha-matraya na bhavet) (nrnam = jiva-matranam). Therefore (tat = tasmat), that is, on account of being especially despised in the world, while linking your mind in Me, with your bhava, you will attain Me before long, at the termination of the body (acirat = dehante eva).”

In this context, the following should be understood. Sri Krsna’s devotees are of two kinds: tata-sthah (marginal) and lilantah-patinah (in the pastimes). Whether or nor they understand the truth about the Lord, the marginal ones, the Brahmanas and others, serve one of the eight representations of Godhead (wooden deity, etc., Bhagavatam 11.27.12) and please Him by their bhakti in the form of serving the deity’s feet, taking its foot water, and so on.

The devotees included in the pastimes are twofold: The first category consists of gods and others: They interact with Him, knowing His supreme godhood. The second category includes humans such as the Brahmanas and such as Nanda: Although they know He is God, their experience is based on nara-lila, His pastimes as a human; Krsna follows the rules of human society, and so He did not want to immediately reciprocate with the wives of Brahmanas, though they wanted to serve Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The ladies might say, “Let us be with You.” He responds: “In this life as Brahmanis (iha = brahmani-janmani), your bodily association with Me (anga-sangah = bhavatinam maya anga-sangah) is not conducive to people’s happiness (na pritaye nrnam = nrnam sukhaya na bhavati), much less to their deep affection (anuragaya = anuragaya tu sutaram na).”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In this verse He says: “Hear the answer to what you are asking with tearful sidelong glances: “Will our heart’s desire be accomplished at some point in time or not?”’’ Pritaye means pritim sampadayitum (to bring about affection). Anuragaya signifies: anuragam ca samvardhayitum (or to greatly increase love). The drift is: “Only a deep longing in separation from Me intensely increases love.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**
