He talks about the bodily association implied with tava pada-mulam praptah, “We attained the soles of Your feet” (10.23.29). “The bodily association of people is conducive neither to My pleasure (na pritaye = mama pritaye na bhavati) nor to My love (anuragaya = mama anuragaya ca na bhavati), therefore, while linking the mind in Me you will swiftly achieve Me.” The following is implied by this, “I am satisfied only by bhakti, not by anything else.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

“While linking the mind in Me you will quickly achieve Me.” The crooked sadhana of one whose goal is perfection through a straight path is improper.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

He instructs them: “Once you go back home, do not be too attached to the body. Rather, meditate on Me.” “People should get together for the sake of loving Me (anuragaya = mayi anuragaya), not for the sake of worldly happiness (na pritaye = deha-gehadi-ksudra-sukhaya na bhavati), therefore...”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

Owing to the statements: dharma- samsthapanarthaya sambhavami yuge yuge (4.8) and bramanyo loka-matarah, “Brahmanis are mothers of the world,” “In your case, an anuraga like the motherly love of Yasoda is appropriate.”

### 10.23.33

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*ity ukta dvija-patnyas ta yajna-vatam punar gatah \|*  
*te canasuyavah svabhih stribhihsatram aparayan \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah uvaca—Sri Suka said; iti—in this way; uktah—told; dvija- patnyah—the wives of Brahmanas; tah—those ladies; yajna-vatam—to the sacrificial grounds; punah gatah—returned; te—those men; ca—and; anasuyavah—unspiteful; svabhih stribhih—with their women; satram—the sacrificial session; aparayan—they completed.

*sri-sukah uvaca—iti uktah tah dvija-patnyah yajna-vatam punar gatah. te (dvijah) ca anasuyavah svabhih stribhih satram aparayan.*

**Перевод:**

**Sri Suka said: Addressed in this way, those wives of Brahmanas returned to the sacrificial grounds. The husbands, unresentful, completed the sacrifice with them.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Anasuyavah (unresentful) means adosa-drstayah (not seeing any fault).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Tabhih (“with those” women) signifies: “them who were favored by the Lord.” The fault of the Lord’s neglect of the sacrificial session is repudiated thus. The great value of that sacrifice is also suggested. In the reading svabhih, the sense is nijabhih (“own” women), otherwise the fire sacrifice would not have been completed. The men were not resentful (anasuyavah) by the mercy of the Lord’s words: na abhyasuyeran (10.23.31).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Addressed in this way, i.e. knowing Krsna’s intention, they went.” The gopis, however, stayed at the beginning of Rasa upon knowing His intention, and so it is to be understood that there was no decrease in love at any time.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“They went to the place of the sacrifice (yajna-vatam = yajna-sthalam).” Medini-kosa states: vato marga-vrti-sthane, “Vata means marga (path, road), vrti (fence), and sthanam (place)” (Medini-kosa, ta-dvikam 27).

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

“Let us be close to You. What is the use of going back home?” He responds: “In the land of sadhana, the sadhana for attaining Me, bhakti, ought to be done. Bhakti occurs by smarana and so forth.” That is what He says with the verse that begins: smaranat.

### 10.23.34

*tatraika vidhrta bhartra bhagavantam yatha-srutam \|*  
*hrdopaguhya vijahau deham karmanubandhanam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatra—there; eka—one woman; vidhrta—held back; bhartra—by the husband; bhagavantam—the Lord; yatha-srutam—in accordance with what was heard; hrda—with the heart; upaguhya—after embracing; vijahau—she gave up; deham—the body; karma-anubandhanam—because of which there is a binding of karma (or which is the consequence of karma).

*tatra (yajna-vate) eka (brahmani) bhartra vidhrta (sati) yatha-srutam bhagavantam hrda upaguhya (svam) deham karmanubandhanam vijahau.*

**Перевод:**

**There, one lady held back by her husband embraced the Lord, in accordance with what she heard, with her heart and gave up her body created by karma.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Upon giving up her body, she attained the Lord as caitanya (absolute consciousness).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

It was said: aciran mam avapsyatha, “You will attain Me before long” (10.23.32); that also was not just for the sake of a pacification: it was even said truthfully, due to such a perfection directly obtained by one lady. That is what he says here.

Tatra means either yajna-vate (in the sacrificial grounds) or tasu madhye (of those ladies). “Being especially held back (vidhrta = visesena dhrta sati)—i.e. by force, with a zeal such as taking her hand and doing a praise at her feet—she gave up the body in a special way (vijahau = visesena jahau),” that is, in such a way that there would not be another birth of that sort. Why? karmanubandhanam, “the body was bound by past actions (= karmabhih anubadhyate iti tatha tat),” insofar as no one attains the Lord with a body dependent on karma. Therefore the sense is: Right then, she got a spiritual body in Gokula. The verse was explained by Sridhara Svami only with that intention.

Regarding bhaktayah (of one female devotee, 10.23.2), the singular was said with the intent to express sayujya at once. Sayujya is a constant close connection (nitya-samyoga) with a transcendental body along with the Lord.

In Sridhara Svami’s commentary, the sense of caitanyena (“as absolute consciousness”) is cid-ru??na (as a transcendental form). The particular bhakti of those ladies is implied thus.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Krsna said: aciran mam avapsyatha, “You will attain Me before long” (10.23.32). He did not say this just to pacify them, rather it was for the purpose of accepting the sacrificial grounds, and so here He gives an example.

There, in the sacrificial grounds, one lady, situated far behind all other ladies, was held back in a special way, i.e. by force; she embraced the Lord.” This word, bhagavantam, suggests that the qualities, the form, etc., are more eminent than all, and that this form of Bhagavan was the form of Sri Krsna. She embraced Him with the heart, that is, with another body that was perfect because of the desire for prema. This means: When she was held back by her husband, she yelled: “Save me, save me. I implore You to give me shelter,” owing to a complete relinquishment of inhibitions due to being pained by fear. Her body was perfect because, by the perfection of having a relationship with the Lord, it was imbued with love for the Lord. Afterward she gave up this body that was only karmanubandhana (based on karma),” but she did not give up her body that was premanubandhana (based on divine love) and that was the means of embracing Him. The word vi (in vijahau) negates a renewed return.

Consequently, the following is meant to be communicated: Possibly after giving up the body related to the husband only to the husband, the lady attained Him with a body perfected by love for the Lord, in view of these two statements in Sri Gita, (1) yam yam vapi smaran bhavam and so on, “Or, O son of Kunti, a person attains only whatever state of being he, whose mind was always infused by that state, is remembering while giving up the body at death” (8.6), and (2) ye yatha mam prapadyante and so on, “I serve them in the same way they devote themselves to Me” (4.11).

Further, this attainment is understood to have occurred in a particular manifestation of Gokula known as Sri Goloka. This was described in the context of Putana’s liberation and should also be described ahead.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

There, in the sacrificial grounds, one lady was far behind all the other ones, therefore she was held back in a particular way, by force (vidhrta = visesena balat dhrta). She gave up the bondage of karma, the body (vijahau deham karmanubandhanam = karmanubandhanam eva deham jahau), but she did not give up the body that is premanubandhana. Right then, it was caused to originate by an innermost desire greatly augmented by an intense longing in separation and was embraced by the Lord who was attained as a inner vision. Afterward, while having that transcendental body, unnoticed by all the people, she speedily left that place and attained the glorious Lord. It is explained in this way on account of the uselessness of the word karmanubandhanam.

To subtly inform about the power of love, the Lord’s mercy made that one lady give up, at the time of the rendezvous, the body that had a connection with karma (karmanubandha) and made her take a body that has a connection with prema, that is, a transcendental body. Then it, by the model of a touchstone, turned the karmanubandha bodies only of all these ladies into premanubandha bodies, that is, transcendental bodies. From that day, those ladies never had intimate contact with their respective husbands.

What is impossible for the Lord’s mercy? With one fraction of it there was an eminence in her, and with another fraction there was an eminence in the other ladies also. Yet the gradation of those ladies cannot be done inasmuch as it is not described in the scriptures on bhakti. They were perfected by the Lord’s mercy to all of them. That was stated as follows: krpa-siddha yajna-patni- vairocani-sukadayah, “Those who were perfected by mercy are the wives of the sacrificial Brahmanas; Bali; Suka, and others” (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 2.1.289).

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

She gave up the body, which was burned by the fire of separation from Him and whose cause was prarabdha-karma. She immediately became a youthful gopi, and attained Him, on account of His statement: ye yatha mam (4.11).

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Karmanubandhanam (dependent on karma) means karmanugam (which follows karma).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

With the heart, she embraced the Lord in accordance with what she heard from people (yatha-srutam = loka-mukhena yathakarnitam). She gave up the body whose binding is karma, prarabdha-karma, which is both auspicious karma and inauspicious karma.

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

In this verse he says the foremost lady (eka = mukhya) had not left. “One lady among them (tatra = tasu madhye), held by her husband (bhartra = sva-bhartra), gave up her body.” The reason for relinquishing the body is: karmanubandhanam. The body is karmanubandhanam in the sense that it is the reason there is the binding of karma (= karmanubandhanam yasmat).

### 10.23.35

*bhagavan api govindas tenaivannena gopakan \|*  
*catur-vidhenasayitva svayam ca bubhuje prabhuh \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

bhagavan—the Lord; api—even; govindah—Govinda; tena eva annena—only with that food; gopakan—the cowherd boys; catuh-vidhena—\[food\] of four kinds; asayitva—after feeding (or while feeding); svayam—He Himself; ca—and; bubhuje—ate; prabhuh— the Almighty.

*bhagavan api govindah prabhuh tena eva annena catur-vidhena gopakan asayitva svayam ca (tad eva) bubhuje.*

**Перевод:**

**Govinda, though the Lord, fed the cowherd boys only with that food, of four varieties. He Himself, the Almighty, partook of the meal.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Suka talks about the Lord’s special favor to those ladies too. Bhagavan api denotes: “although He is replete with all godly might.” Still: tenaiva, which means: tena yajna-patny-anitena eva, “with the food only brought by the wives of the ritualistic Brahmanas.” An abundance of it is mentioned thus.

The suffix ka in gopakan is said with the intent to express sneha (affection). “Himself feeding them by distributing it, He ate it afterward (bubhuje = pascat tad bubhuje),” because: govindah, He has the topmost vatsala for the cowherds. The word ca includes Balarama. Or he is included by the mention of cow herders.

Ca has the sense of api: Even He Himself (svayam ca = svayam api), ate, as a special favor to those ladies, although He is the Almighty, meaning He is complete in every way (prabhuh = sarvatha paripurno ‘pi). Or, someone might wonder, “How can only one individual feed many persons simultaneously in a short time?” Suka responds: prabhuh, i.e. sarva-saktiman (He has all powers). Therefore He ate aplenty out of mercy for those ladies.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The ladies’ special bhakti was brought to light in this manner. Here Suka also talks about the Lord’s special favor to those women. The sense of the word api is: “Even though He is God, He behaved in that way.” ‘Govinda’ denotes Sri Gokulendra, and so it is appropriate for Him to protect the cowherds.

Tenaiva (only with that) implies that there was little food in consideration of all the cow herders. Still, everyone felt that their bellies became full, because: bhagavan, He is the reservoir of all kinds of excellence (= sarva-sampatty-asrayah). Gopakan suggests that He showed tender feelings (anukampa) to them. Sri Rama is included in them because it is possible that he was eager for it just like they were, because: prabhuh, “Krsna’s will is not transgressed” (= alanghyecchah).

“Himself waiting upon them, He too ate (asayitva svayam ca = svayam ca tan prati parivesya svayam api).” In point of svayam (Himself): Sukadeva, the divine king of sages, was astonished at how He felt satisfied with those ladies. The word api in bhagavan api (although He is God) is used because: prabhuh, “His mercy has no obstacle” (= niragalanugrahah).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Because of api in bhagavan api, this is the explanation in reference to the previous verse: sa deham jahau, bhagavan api govindah tasya gah sarvendriyani ramanartham alaksitam tadaiva vindati sma, ““She gave up the body. Although He is God, He was Govinda,” as derived in the sense of “Right then, without being perceived He obtained all her senses for the sake of an undisclosed intimate enjoyment.””

Further, this meaning is obtained from ca (and): svayam bhoktum anicchann api bubhuje, “Himself unwilling to eat, He ate nonetheless.” The absence of a desire was because of the rise in Him of remorse because He broke the resolve of those ladies who had prema.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“Though He is the Lord, He Himself ate.” How amazing is the good fortune of those ladies!

### 10.23.36

*evam lila-nara-vapur nr-lokam anusilayan \|*  
*reme go-gopa-gopinam ramayan rupa-vak-krtaih \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

evam—in this manner; lila-nara-vapuh—He who has a human body for the sake of pastimes; nr-lokam—people who are human; anusilayan—while practicing (imitating); reme—He took pleasure; go—the cows; gopa—the cow herders; gopinam—the cowherd ladies; ramayan—while delighting; rupa—with His beauty; vak— speech; krtaih—and deeds.

*lila-nara-vapuh (sri-krsnah) evam nr-lokam anusilayan (svasya) rupa-vak-krtaih go-gopa-gopinam ramayan reme.*

**Перевод:**

**While following the ways of humans in this manner, He, who has a human form for pastimes, had fun while delighting the cows, the gopas and the gopis with His beauty, words and deeds.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Krsna was imitating (anusilayan = anukurvan) human society. The genitive case in go-gopa-gopinam has the sense of the accusative. “He took pleasure to delight them (ramayan = ramayitum), also by means of His form, His words, and His deeds (rupa-vak-krtaih = rupena vaca caritraih ca).”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Not only this favor to the yajna-patnis, all His deeds, and His beauty, etc., were only for the sake of the great delight of the people of Vraja: Suka concludes in this manner, with evam and so on. The following is implied: There are many other pastimes of this sort.

Lila-nara-vapuh means lila-maya-narakara-vapuh (He whose body, a human form, has the nature of play). Krsna was teaching (anusilayan = anusiksayan) human society. The sense is: “He had fun in order to foster devotional service to Him in the world of men.”

Another interpretation of nr-lokam anusilayan is: nr-loka-vyavaharam anu nirantaram silayan svabhavikatvena acaran, “While naturally behaving like humans continuously,” given that for the most part the excellence of prema for Him occurs only by means of a worldly pastime.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The first two paragraphs above are reiterated. In addition:) Another interpretation of nr-lokam anusilayan is: “While always behaving like humans” (= nr-loka-vyavaharam sada acaran).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

With evam (in this way) and so on he says: “In this way He did not sensually enjoy the wives whose existence was based on fire sacrifices, yet He sensually enjoyed the wives of cowherds.” Lila-nara-vapuh means lila-maya-nara-vapuh (He whose human body of the nature of play). The gist is: Since lila-sakti is the most venerable of all potencies, including satya-sankalpata (making His resolve come true), only the nonexcellence of a pastime of sensually enjoying the Brahmanis is the reason for not sensually enjoying them.

Krsna was following (anusilayan = anusaran) the ways of humans. Here, since the cowherd ladies who have vatsala are not contextual, the mention of “gopis” only refers to young cowherd girls. “He took pleasure while delighting them with the form, words, and deeds (rupa-vak-krtaih = rupena vaca cestitaih ca)," and so any idea that Krsna did not sensually take pleasure with the vraja-devis before the Rasa is rejected. The drift is: There are many other such pastimes in Vraja that I did not mention.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Lila-nara-vapuh denotes: lila-pradhano narakara-vapuh (He whose body, a human form, is mostly for the purpose of play).

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Lilana-ra-vapuh means: lilanam anah prananam tam rati iti ana-rah prana-pradah tatha-vidham vapur yasya, “He whose body gives life to pastimes.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“While imitating (anusilayan =anukurvan) humans, He took pleasure while enjoying Himself— atmanam should be added to ramayan—by means of the forms, words, and deeds of the cows, cowherd boys, and cowherd girls.” This means: by means of the forms of the cows, the words of the gopas, and the deeds of the gopis.”

Lila-nara-vapuh denotes: lila-pradhanam nara-vad vapur yasya (He whose body is humanlike and is mostly for the sake of play). Another explanation is lilana-ra-vapuh, which means: lilayah anah pranah iti yavat, lilanam rati iti lilana-ram vapur yasya, “He whose body gives breath, i.e. life, to a pastime.” The verbal root is an pranane (to breathe).131

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Lila-nara-vapuh denotes: lilaya na tu karmana narasya iva vapuh yasya sah bhagavan, “the Lord, who has a human¬like body as a pastime, not by karma.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

Lila-nara-vapuh means: lilartham eva nara-vapuh (He who has a human body only for the sake of pastimes).

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Lilanara-vapuh means: lilasv api anara-vapuh, “He whose body is not human, even in pastimes.” This means His form is inconceivable, unlimited, blissful, and His own.

### 10.23.37

*athanusmrtya vipras te anvatapyan krtagasah \|*  
*yad visvesvarayor yacnam ahanma nr-vidambayoh \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

atha—afterward; anusmrtya—after continuously remembering; viprah te—those Brahmanas; anvatapyan—repented; krta-agasah— they by whom a sin was done; yat—because; visva-isvarayoh—of the two Lords of the universe; yacnam—the request; ahanma—we were struck; nr-vidambayoh—cheaters (or imitators) of humans.

*atha te viprah nr-vidambayoh visvesvarayoh yacnam anusmrtya “yad (vayam) ahanma, (tasmad vayam) krtagasah (bhavamah” iti) anvatapyan.*

**Перевод:**

**Afterward, those Brahmanas, remembering the request of the two overlords of the universe, who were imitating humans, repented: “Since we were struck, we made a mistake.”**

**Or: Later on, the Brahmanas repented while remembering: “Since we killed the request of the two controllers of the universe, deriders of humans, we are offenders.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He mentions the manner of the remembrance: naranukaranavator visvesvarayor yacnam yad ahanma hatavantas tat krtagaso vayam ity anusmrtya, “remembering the request of the two Lords of the world, who had an imitation of humans, “Because we were struck, we made a mistake.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

By the influence of the association of the wives, who had obtained that kind of mercy of the Lord: patayo nabhyasuyeran and so on, “The husbands cannot resent you” (10.23.31), even their husbands turned out to be properly intelligent, and so from this verse to the end of the chapter Suka speaks to illustrate those ladies’ glory.

“After that incident, those men, that is, although they had a bad self-conceit (te = durabhimana-grastah api), repented.” Someone might wonder, “Why did Those two beg?” In that regard he says: nr- vidambayoh, “of those two, who were expanding a worldly pastime” (= laukika-lilam vistarayatoh).

Another explanation is: nrn asman tad-bhakti-hinan vidambayata upahasata iti tatha tayoh, “Those two are deriding men like us who have no bhakti to Them.” The pronoun asmat (us) should have been used, and so the usage of nr instead is by reason of the continuation of the scent of a bad self-conceit even at that time; or it is due to shyness.

Alternatively, atha means “after the completion of the fire sacrifice,” because of the excellence of the purity of mind by the origination of a genuine result of the fire sacrifice after its completion due to a remnant of what was eaten by the Lord.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The remembrance is to be understood as having occurred by the influence of the ladies, who got the Lord’s mercy with the words beginning from: patayo nabhyasuyeran (10.23.31).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In point of athanusmrtya (afterward, remembering...), it is to be understood that the men’s remembrance, self-deprecation, and so on, occurred because of the good fortune of seeing those ladies. Suka mentions the manner of their remorse: yad yasmad visvesvarayor api yacnam ahanma hatavanto vayam, tasmat krtagaso ’bhumah, “Because we killed Their request, we are offenders.”

How were the two Lords of the universe? nr-vidambayoh, which means: nrn asman vidambete iti tayoh, anna-prarthanena eva asman vancitavatoh, ““of the two of Them, who are cheating men, i.e. us,” in other words: “Those two were deceiving us by requesting food.””

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Here he says the Brahmanas had self-deprecation: “Because we killed Their request, we are offenders (krtagasah = aparadhinah).” Remembering in this way, they repented, that is, they experienced subsequent affliction (anvatapyan = pascat tapam abhajat).

### 10.23.38

*drstva strinam bhagavati krsne bhaktim alaukikim \|*  
*atmanam ca taya hinam anutapta vyagarhayan \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

drstva—seeing; strinam—of the women; bhagavati krsne—to Lord Krsna; bhaktim—devotional service; alaukikim—not of this world; atmanam—themselves; ca—and; taya hinam—devoid of that \[bhakti\]: anutaptah—repentant; vyagarhayan—they condemned.

*(te viprah) strinam bhagavati krsne bhaktim alaukikim drstva atmanam ca taya (bhaktya) hinam (drstva) anutaptah (santah atmanam) vyagarhayan.*

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

(Visvanatha Cakravarti had provided the same comment)

*strinam bhagavati krsne bhaktim alaukikim drstva (te) anutaptah taya hinam atmanam vyagarhayan.*

**Seeing the women’s extraordinary devotion to Lord Krsna, the Brahmanas, repentant, condemned themselves, being devoid of it.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

At that time, thinking that their wives were like gurus, they reproached themselves (atmanam vyagarhayan = atmanam vyanindan). Those men had no devotion to the Lord (taya hinam = bhagavad-bhakti-rahitam). The bhakti of their wives was out of this world (alaukikim = lokatitam).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Seeing the ladies’ bhakti to God in person (bhagavati = saksat paramesvarah), and on top of that, to Sri Krsna, He who attracts the hearts of all by manifesting His infinite godly might, they did not just repent, they also reproached themselves in a special way (vyagarhayan = visesena agarhayan ca): by giving up their own endless conceits.

The wives’ bhakti is called alaukikim because it was not based on desires in this world or on the desire to attain heaven and because of the instance of giving up the body at once, due to not attaining Krsna.

Or it is called alaukikim on account of signs of the excellence of a love beyond anything in the world, like those mentioned in: hasaty atho roditi, “One who is dedicated in this way develops anuraga by glorifying names that are dear to oneself. One’s heart melts. Being indifferent to the world, one laughs aloud, cries, shouts, sings and dances, as if intoxicated” (Bhagavatam 11.2.40).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The commentary is the same as the first two para¬graphs above.)

### 10.23.39

*dhig janma nas tri-vrd vidyamdhig vratam dhig bahu-jnatam \|*  
*dhik kulam dhik kriya-daksyam vimukha ye tv adhoksaje \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

dhik—fie on; janma—birth; nah—our; tri-vrt—of three modes; vidyam—knowledge (education); dhik—fie on; vratam—vow; dhik—fie on; bahu-jnatam—being knowers of much; dhik—fie on; kulam—community (or lineage); dhik—fie on; kriya-daksyam— expertise in rites; vimukhah—averse; ye—\[we\] who; tu—only (or specifically); adhoksaje—to Adhoksaja.

*adhoksaje ye (vayam) tu vimukhah (santi, tesam) nah janma tri-vrd dhig (astu, tesam asmakam) vidyam (dhig astu, tesam asmakam) vratam dhig (astu, tesam asmakam) bahu-jnatam dhig (astu, tesam asmakam) kulam dhig (astu, tesam asmakam) kriya-daksyam dhig (astu).*

**Перевод:**

**“Fie on us. We are averse to Adhoksaja. Fie on our threefold birth, fie on our education, fie on our vows, fie on being greatly learned, fie on our lineage, and to hell with our expertise in rites.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Tri-vrd janma denotes: sauklam savitram daiksam iti tri-gunitam janma, “a birth three times: by semen, by the sacred thread, and by initiation for expertise in rites.” Vratam (vow) connotes brahmacaryam (continence). Kriya daksyam means: kriya daksyam ca, “rites (kriyah = karmani) and expertise.” Or kriya-daksyam is one word. Dhik (fie on) has the sense of adhiksepa (revilement). The sense is: ye vayam tv adhoksaje vimukhas tesam janmadi tat sarvam dhig iti vyagarhan, “They rebuked themselves: “We are averse to Adhoksaja, and so fie on our birth and all the rest.””

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

They censure with an order, intending to express the sequentially increasing importance in the sequence. “Fie on our birth.” On that topic, sauklyam means a birth from a pure mother and a pure father; savitram is the birth known as upanayana (investiture with a sacred thread); daiksyam means yajnadi-diksa-sambandhi (initiation for the qualification to do fire sacrifices).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The syntactical connection is: ye adhoksaje pratyavrttau pradurbhavini paramatmany api vimukhah, tesam janmadini dhik, “Fie on the birth and on everything else of those who are averse to Adhoksaja, Paramatma,” because of censuring:

(1) the seminal birth (saukra), though it is most suitable for devotional service to Him, by the logic in: kim punar brahmanah punya bhakta rajarsayas tatha, “\[Even women, Vaisyas, and Sudras attain the topmost destination,\] not to mention pious Brahmanas, devotees, and Rajarsis” (Bhagavad-gita 9.33);

(2) the birth related to the sacred thread, on account of not understanding Gayatri, due to being expressive of Him, and the fact that Gayatri is based on Him because Srimad Bhagavatam, an elaboration of that meaning, is chiefly based on Him, in view of the fact that in Agni Purana the following is stated after mentioning that Gayati should be explained as a mantra whose chief element is Him: yatradhikrtya gayatrim kirtyate dharma-vistarah,133“The Bhagavatam is that wherein, by referring to Gayatri, an elaboration of dharma is proclaimed,” and so on (Matsya Purana);

(3) their knowledge (vidya), because of not knowing the truth: aham hi sarva-yajnanam bhokta ca prabhur eva ca, na tu mam abhijananti tattvenatas cyavanti te, “Only I am the enjoyer of and the overlord of all fire sacrifices, but they do not know Me in truth, and so they fall down” (Bhagavad-gita 9.24), and in this way:

(4) even their vows and so on.

Kulam means vamsa-paramparam (the family line).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Fie on whatever is related to us (nah yat tat = asmakam yat tad dhik). We are averse to Sri Krsna” (vimukha ye tv adhoksaje = ye vayam sri-krsne tu vimukhah eva).

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

The gist is: Only that by which Hari is pleased is fruitful. The rest is useless.

### 10.23.40

*nunam bhagavato maya yoginam api mohini \|*  
*yad vayam guravo nrnam svarthe muhyama he dvijah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

nunam—certainly; bhagavatah—of the Lord; maya—the potency of material illusion; yoginam—of yogis; api—even; mohini—a bewilderer; yat—because; vayam—we; guravah—gurus (teachers); nrnam—of men; sva-arthe—in the matter of our self interest; amuhyama—we were bewildered (svarthe muhyama = svarthe muhyama); he dvijah—O Brahmanas.

*he dvijah! nunam bhagavatah maya yoginam api mohini (bhavati), yad vayam nrnam guravah svarthe (mayaya) amuhyama.*

**Перевод:**

**“Indeed, dear Brahmanas, the Lord’s Maya even bewilders the yogis, since we, gurus of men, were bewildered about our real interest.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Here they say, “We’re in trouble! We’re bewildered by Maya. That’s for sure (nunam = niscitam).” The yogis are those who practice jnana-yoga: they think they are true yogis. Or the sense is: “His Maya even bewilders the yogis, so what hope is there for us karmis!”

“We are gurus” signifies “although we are the best,” or else “although we are teachers,” by the axiom: varnanam brahmanah guruh, “A Brahmana is the teacher of those in the caste system.”

Muhyama means: moham prapnuma (we got bewildered). “Dear Brahmanas!” (he dvijah): They address one another, on account of repentance. Another interpretation is: dvija vayam muhyamahe, “We Brahmanas are bewildered,” where the atmanepada is poetic license.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The rest of the commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Although we instruct other men about the goal, we are bewildered by Maya regarding our goal.”

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

Muhyama should read muhyamah (we are bewildered).

### 10.23.41

*aho pasyata narinam api krsne jagad-gurau \|*  
*duranta-bhavam yo ’vidhyan mrtyu-pasan grhabhidhan \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

aho—(used for expressing astonishment); pasyata—see; narinam— of the women; api—although; krsne—for Krsna; jagat-gurau— the guru of the universe; dur-anta—endless (“whose end is far”); bhavam—the love; yah—which \[love\]; avidhyat—pierced (cut); mrtyu-pasan—the ropes of death; grha-abhidhan—\[ropes,\] whose designation is home.

*aho! (yuyam asam) narinam api krsne jagad-gurau duranta-bhavam pasyata, yah (bhavah) mrtyu-pasan grhabhidhan avidhyat.*

**Перевод:**

**“What a wonder! Look at these women: They have an endless love for Krsna, the universal guru. That love severed the rope of death, the rope called “home”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“See their endless devotion (bhavam = bhaktim): It severed (avidhyat = acchinat) the ropes of death.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Darn! We men are more base than women.” They lament in this way in three verses. Aho has the sense of kheda (despair).

“Isn’t it that a woman’s love for someone other than her husband is improper?” In that regard they say jagad-gurau (the guru of the universe). The gist is He is most needed, more so than the husbands. Duranta-bhavam connotes: sarva-badhakam prema (love that annuls every obstacle). Or bhava means rati (affection), and duranta means it had no limit, or else it did not decrease.

The mention of the past tense in avidhyat (pierced, i.e. cut) is said with the intent to express the immediate disappearance of those ladies’ attachment to home and so on. In that way, the manner of the ladies’ abiding at home is also shown.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“What a wonder! We men are more base than women.” They lament in this way in three verses. Aho has the sense of ascarya (wonder). (The rest of the commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Here they mean to say, “We, the gurus, as the husbands or fathers-in-law of those women who have become successful, fell in a dark pit.”

“See their love: Its nature is such that it is hard to understand, i.e. we cannot experience it (duranta-bhavam = durgamah asmabhih anubhavitum asakyah antah iyatta134yasya tatha-bhutam bhavam) (bhavam = premanam).”

In other words: “See their love for Krsna. It revealed itself by anubhavas such as kampa (trembling), asru (tears), pulaka (horripilation), vaivarnya (paleness), while saying this in a faltering voice: “Ah, Krsna! Prana-ramana! (delighter of the life force).”

“Isn’t it that a woman’s love for a man who is not her husband is improper?” In that regard they say: jagad-gurau. The drift is: They love Him, because of the superimposition of whom in the husband is the latter a guru for his wife. Moreover, He was directly present, so what were the men thinking?

“Their love at once severed (yo ’vidhyan = yah bhavah sadyah ciccheda) the ropes of death.” In point of grhabhidhan (called ‘home’): “Not even the scent of an attachment of these ladies to the husband, the home, a child, and the rest is perceived. Hence from now, only they are our gurus.” From that day, the ladies, who had anuraga for Krsna, were highly respected by their husbands; they were not only considered as wives.

### 10.23.42-43

*nasam dvijati-samskaro na nivaso gurav api \|*  
*na tapo natma-mimamsa na saucam na kriyah subhah \|\|*  
*athapihy uttamahsloke krsne yogesvaresvare \|*  
*bhaktir drdha na casmakam samskaradimatam api \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—not; asam—of these women; dvi-jati-samskarah—the ceremonial rite of a twice-born person; na—not; nivasah—residing; gurau—in a guru (near a guru); api na—nor; tapah—austerity; na— not; atma-mimamsa—examination of the soul; na—not; saucam— cleanliness; na—not; kriyah—ritualistic activities; subhah—splendid (or auspicious);

atha api—nonetheless; hi—certainly (or a verse filler); uttamah¬sloke—to Uttamasloka; krsne—Krsna; yoga-isvara-isvare—the controller of the grandmasters of yoga; bhaktih—devotional service; drdha—firm; na ca—nor (a fickle bhakti); asmakam—of us; samskara-adi-matam—who have the samskara etc.; api—although.

*(yadyapi) asam (strinam) dvijati-samskarah na (bhavati), na api gurau nivasah (abhavat), na (ca) tapah (abhuvan), na (ca) atma-mimamsa (syat), na(ca) saucam (vidyate), na (ca asam) kriyah subhah (santi), athapi (asam strinam) uttamahsloke krsne yogesvaresvare drdha bhaktih (jata). samskaradimatam api asmakam (bhaktih) na (bhavati).*

**Перевод:**

**“Although these ladies do not have the milestone of the twice-born, did not reside near a spiritual master, did not undergo austerity, do not look into the self, do not have cleanliness and do not have splendid ritualistic activities, they have firm bhakti to Uttamasloka, Krsna, the controller of the grandmasters of yoga. We, though endowed with all that, do not even have bhakti.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The milestone of the twice-born is the investiture with a sacred thread (dvijati-samskarah = upanayanam). Kriyah denotes sandhyopasanadayah (activities such as worship at the three junctures of the day).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Here they expound upon their idea that the ladies were less evolved than them, as implied with the word api in the previous verse: narinam api (their love, “although they are women”).

Dvijati-samskarah signifies: upanayanadih tad-dharma-dvarah, “the investiture with the sacred thread and other such milestones which are the door to the above attributes.” Cleanliness (saucam) is a common attribute. Further, guru-nivasa and the rest are attributes of Brahmacaris, Vanaprasthas, Sannyasis, and Grhastas, sequentially. In that regard the transgression of the order is by reason of an absorption in lamentation. Or the subsequent mention of the attribute related to householders is because of thinking much of it, therefore it is said: subhah (“splendid” ritualistic activities).

Other explanations are as follows. Dvijati-samskara signifies a special milestone of the twice-born, such as visnu-diksa. Tapas means sri-visnu-smrtih (the remembrance of Visnu), from the statement: tat tapo yad dharih smrtih, “Austerity is the remembrance of Hari.” Saucam means visuddha-cittata (mental purity). Kriyah subhah signifies: “Reverence for Yajnesvara in a fire sacrifice, or the formal worship of Hari in the open, etc.” Atma-mimamsa means: atmanah hareh vicarah (a deliberation regarding the Soul, Hari).

**10.23.43**

“Nevertheless, the ladies have firm bhakti, that is, it cannot even be impeded by us.” Next, they characterize Him in order to also evoke the understanding of the greatness of bhakti to Him, on account of His glory. They are devoted to Uttamasloka, He whose renown (sloka = kirti) is greater than all, because He is the Avatari and because He reveals His unlimited godhood.

Or the name Uttamasloka is derived as: udgatam tamo ajnanam samsara-laksanam va yasmat sah slokah yasya, “He whose renown is that because of which darkness (tamas),136or the ignorance which is material life, is gone (ut = udgata),” because: krsne.

Therefore: yogesvaresvare, which means “He deserves to be served by Sanaka and other grandmasters of yoga, even more so by us” (= yogesvaranam sanakadinam api kimuta asmakam isvare sevye). They imply this: asmakam capala api bhaktih na asti, “We don’t even have a fickle bhakti.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

In this set of two verses they expound upon the wonderment. (The rest is the same as the second paragraph above.)

**10.23.43** (Additions in this paragraph are underlined.)

“Nevertheless, the ladies have firm bhakti, that is, it cannot even be impeded by us.” Next, they characterize Him in order to also evoke the understanding of the greatness of bhakti to Him, on account of His glory. They are devoted to Uttamasloka, He who has the topmost renown (uttama-sloke = parama-sat-khyatimati) because He gives liberation, even to enemies: He is the controller of the grandmasters of yogas, meaning He can be attained as one who should be served by those who have bhakti-yoga. ”

Next, with na ca and so on they again add to the wonderment, as a contrast. Those things, dvijati-samskara, etc., are certainly not causes of bhakti by themselves. The ladies’ sat-sanga (good association), which had that quality, could not be inferred by these men as the cause of it. This was Sukadeva’s intention.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“But it is not that the reason of their anuraga for Krsna is known to us.” Regarding yogesvaresvare, the gist is: “Only He, no other, knows the reason for the devotional service to Him and brings about its accomplishment.” Consequently the main reason, the sat-sanga of the womenfolk, such as a garland maker, who stay in Vraja, was not said, even after proclaiming Krsna’s form and qualities, on account of being unknown to those men. This was Sukadeva’s intention.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Gurau nivasah portends tat-seva (service to a spiritual master). Tapah denotes sastralocanam (looking at scriptures). Atma-mimamsa means: atma-yathatmya-vicarah (considering the soul as it truly is). Saucam signifies: tri-savana-snanadi (bathing thrice, etc.).

The reason for the ladies’ bhakti is only the eminent association (prasanga) of women, such as a garland maker, who were traveling to Mathura from Nandisvara and were glorifying Krsna’s qualities while resting in areas outside their homes, owing to the statement: dirgha-sruta, “by hearing for a long time” (10.23.20). That reason is not said since it is unknown to those men.

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

The previous verse and these two verses have a purport: Women attain Him in that manner only and merely with a bhava right at that time, but it is not so for sages, who habitually practice mental control, sensory control, etc., and for other such discerning persons. It is seen in this way in many places.137

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Atma-mimamsa means brahma-vicarah (deliberation about Brahman). Splendid rites (subhah kriyah) are fire sacrifices, etc.

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

Gaurau nivasah signifies vedadhyayanam (studying the Vedas). The name Uttamasloka means: uttamaih api slokyate, “He is glorified (slokyate = kirtyate) by the best too,” such as Vyasa, Valmiki, and Parasara.

The ladies have firm bhakti. That is, their bhakti is uninterrupted, like a flow of oil, and is better than all. They have bhakti to Him, the controller of even the grandmasters of yoga (yogesvaresvare = yogesvaranam api niyantari). Samskaradivatam api means: asta-catvarimsat-samskaravatam api (although we have the forty-eight samskaras).

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

“But (ca = tu) we do not have bhakti (na = bhaktih na asti) although we have that samskara and the rest.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

The locative case in gurau has the sense of samipikadhara (it exists in proximity), like: vate gavah, “The cows are near the Banyan tree.” Gurau nivasah gurukula for the sake of obtaining knowledge.

**Annotation**

A famous example that illustrates the figurative usage of the locative case in gurau (in the guru) is: gangayam ghosah, “The cowherd village is on the Ganges (is near the Ganges).”

### 10.23.44

*namu svartha-vimudhanam pramattanam grhehaya \|*  
*aho nah smarayamasa gopa-vakyaih satam gatih \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

nanu—(used for expressing a question); sva-artha-vimudhanam—who were bewildered about our goal; pramattanam—inattentive; grha-ihaya—because of household tasks (or because of a desire related to home); aho—(used for expressing astonishment); nah smarayamasa—He made us remember; gopa-vakyaih—through the words of cowherds; satam-gatih—the shelter of the righteous.

*aho! nanu (bhagavan) satam gatih svartha-vimudhanam grhehaya pramattanam nah (atmanam) gopa-vakyaih smarayamasa.*

**Перевод:**

**“We were bewildered about our real interest and inattentive because of household tasks, and He, the shelter of the righteous, made us remember through the words of cow herders? Wow!**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

They shed light on His name Uttamasloka: “Indeed (nanu = niscitam), we were utterly ignorant about our real interest, which is devotional service to Him, and hence were not paying attention because of household duties (grhehaya pramattanam = grha-krtyena anavahitanam)." Or else, “although we had arrogant pride on account of being householders” (grhehaya pramattanam - garhasthyena prakarsena mattanam maha-garvavatam api).

“He made us (nah = asman) remember Him (smarayamasa = atmanam smarayamasa)," because: satam gatih, He is the destination of the righteous (satam = dharmikanam). Aho has the sense of ascarya (wonderment). The gist is: “Though He induced us to understand Him since He is Uttamasloka, we did not understand owing to a lack of discernment.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

They illustrate being Uttamasloka: “Indeed (nanu = niscitam), He made us, who were utterly ignorant about our real interest—insofar as no true goal of life is accomplished without bhakti to Him, by the axiom: sarvasam api siddhinam mulam tac-caranarcanam, “worshiping His feet is the root of all perfections” (10.81.19)—and hence were not paying attention owing to household duties, remember Him (smarayamasa = atmanam smarayamasa),” because: satam gatih, He is the destination of the righteous, those for whom the highest thing is what is said in the Vedas and who have obtained their respective qualifications.

Or, satam gatih means: bhaktanam gatih api (though He is the destination of devotees). The substance is: “He did so only and exclusively because of compassion.” Or satam gatih means: santah eva tavat parama-dayalavah, sah tu tesam api gatih asrayah, “Only He is only the shelter of saintly persons, the ones who are most merciful.” Aho means ascaryam (what a wonder). The gist is: “Though He induced us to understand Him since He is Uttamasloka, we did not understand, owing to a lack of discernment.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Here they say: “Where on the one hand is the Lord’s compassion, and where on the other is our bad attitude?”138

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“Through the words of cowherds He made us remember who He really is.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

Nanu has the sense of a soft vocative. “True, He made us remember our condition in a previous life. We belong to the Lord. He made us remember with the deceit of the words of cowherds, otherwise why would He beg food?”

### 10.23.45

*anyatha purna-kamasya kaivalyady-asisam pateh \|*  
*isitavyaih kim asmabhir isasyaitad vidambanam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

anyatha—otherwise; purna-kamasya—of Him, whose desires are filled (fulfilled) (or anyatha purna-kamasya—whose desire was fulfilled in another way); kaivalya-adi-asisam—of blessings such as liberation; pateh—the master; isitavyaih—who are to be controlled; kim—what; asmabhih—through us; isasya—of God; etat—this; vidambanam—an imitation.

*etad (anna-prarthanam) isasya vidambanam (abhavat). anyatha (sri-krsnasya) purna-kamasya kaivalyady-asisam pateh isitavyaih asmabhih kim (prayojanam asti)?*

**Перевод:**

**“His desires are automatically fulfilled and He is the master of blessings such as liberation. This was a worldly imitation on His part, otherwise what might He want to accomplish through us, who are meant to be controlled?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Why did He ask for food? They respond; “This, the fact that He asked, was a showing of a worldly amusement (vidambanam = laukika-lila-pradarsanam).” Or, “It was a mockery of us” (vidambanam = asmakam vidambanam = asmakam upahasanam).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“What might be His purpose other than causing a remembrance of Himself, who consists of mercy?” (anyatha = anugraha-mayatma-smaranam antarena).

(Additions are underlined.) Someone might think, “He has no need for food, since He is purna-kama. The reason must be that the cow herders were pained by hunger.” They respond with kaivalya and so forth: “What might be His motive (kim = kim prayojanam) to be accomplished through us, who are to be controlled (isitavyaih = niyamyaih), meaning we cannot do anything at all? He is in charge of blessings such as liberation or prema.” This means He is able to bestow those things. Here prema is called kaivalya in the sense that it is a pure mindset, by virtue of the absence of a desire for another kind of result.139There is no motive. “Rather, this is just an imitation on the part of the Lord.” only because of compassion.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Otherwise, that is, except an unconditional compassion, what might be His purpose to be fulfilled through us?” The sense is: Nothing at all.

“This, the request for food, was obviously just a lighthearted joke (vidambanam = khalu laghavam eva) on the part of the Lord.” Alternatively: “This was His rebuke of us (vidambanam = tiraskarah).”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“Otherwise, i.e. if it is not compassion, what is His motive through us? He is purna-kama. There is no motive, consequently this, the request for food, was just the Lord’s deriding us (vidambanam = asmat-tiraskaranam eva).”

**Комментарий. Автор Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur:**

Anyatha (otherwise) means: purvoktam karanam vina (if not the aforementioned reason).

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

Pateh should read patyuh.

### 10.23.46

*hitvanyan bhajate yam srih pada-sparsasayasakrt \|*  
*atma-dosapavargenatad-yacna jana-mohini \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

hitva—giving up; anyan—others; bhajate—serves; yam—whom; srih—Laksmi; pada-sparsa-asaya—with the hope of the touch of the feet; asakrt—continually; atma-dosa—of her fault; apavargena—by the liberation (the rejection); tat-yacna—His begging (or asking); jana-mohini—a bewilderer of people.

*srih anyan hitva svatma-dosapavargena (sthira sati yasya) pada-sparsasaya asakrt yam bhajate, tad-yacna jana-mohini (bhavati).*

**Перевод:**

**“With the hope of continually touching His feet, Laksmi, rejecting others and setting aside her own fault, serves Him, whose begging bewilders people.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Atma-dosapavargena (by eliminating her fault) means: atmano dosapavargena cancalya-garvadi-tyagena, “by rejecting her fickleness, pride, and so on.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Someone might wonder, “Why did He beg as if He were not God? He is able to make everyone cross material life at will.” They respond here. “She serves (bhajate = sevate) Him with the hope of touching both feet at once (sakrt), or with the hope of touching only one foot at once.” Or: “She continually (asakrt) serves Him.” Thus, it is made clear that He cannot possibly beg in truth, and so the fact that He begs bewilders people, all jivas, meaning it gives rise to bewilderment. The drift is: Who at all is able to understand His deed? Perhaps the purpose is to bewilder nondevotees and to increase the bhakti of devotees. In that sense, ‘people’ means nondevotees. Or, by a coalescence of the vowel a, tad-yacnajana-mohini signifies tad-yacna ajana-mohini, meaning He bewilders ajana, those who are not His people, i.e. those who are not devotees. It bewilders them. However, devotees do not have a bewilderment by that begging of His. On the contrary, bhakti simply increases, from the origination of a special bhakti by a worldly pastime of Paramesvara. Another explanation is that His begging bewilders people, i.e. His servants, that is to say it attracts their hearts. Therefore Uddhava said to Vidura:

*mam khedayaty etad ajasya janma-*  
*vidambanam yad vasudeva-gehe \|*  
*vraje ca vaso ’ri-bhayad iva svayam*  
*purad vyavatsid yad ananta-viryah \|\|*

**“That He, unborn, pretended to take birth in Vasudeva’s quarters and that He, who has infinite prowess, lived in Vraja as if in fear of a foe and fled out of town make me depressed.” (3.2.16)**

The sense of this citation is as follows. “The acceptance of a birth in Vasudeva’s prison cell and residing in Vraja as if out of fear of Kamsa by Him who fled from Mathura though He has unlimited prowess make me depressed,” that is to say, “Owing to the increase of a special bhakti only by a worldly pastime of this sort, they generate pain in the heart of persons like me. Otherwise, by the absence of the rise of a special bhakti by a direct demonstration of His godly might, as in the case of Sri Nrsimha and others, persons like me would not have this kind of sadness.” The following texts should be understood in that way:

dunoti cetah smarato mamaitad, and so on, “That He said this, bowing at His parents’ feet: “Dear father, dear mother, be pleased with Us. Greatly afraid of Kamsa, We did not repay Our debt to you,” scorches my heart as I reminisce” (Bhagavatam 3.2.17);

tat tasya kainkaryam alam bhrtan no viglapayaty anga yad ugrasenam, “Vidura, the servanthood of He who, while standing, would inform Ugrasena, sitting on his throne: “Kindly consider, lord,” makes us, His servitors, utterly despondent” (Bhagavatam 3.2.22).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“If He caused a remembrance, why didn’t you remember?” They speak in response to that. Anyan hitva (rejecting others) is eminently said, by looking at the imitation of the pastime of her svayamvara, when she made her appearance, as if in a new way, at the end of the churning of the Milk Ocean (Bhagavatam 8.8.8). “She continually (asakrt) serves (bhajate = sevate) by not touching the faults of she whose self is herself, i.e. the faults of the worldly Laksmi, who is a semblance of her amsa (svatma-dosapavargena = svam svayam eva atma yasyah tasyah tad-amsabhasa-bhutayah jagal-laksmyah ye dosah tad-asparsena)” Thus it is made to be understood that His begging cannot occur in any way. Still, His begging bewilders people, those of our kind, i.e. all jivas: It makes one perceive, “He’s not God.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Someone might think, “This request for food was just because of being pained by hunger, but it was not compassion. It cannot be said that He is purna-kama and so forth, otherwise why would He tend cows?” They respond to that. Asakrt means muhuh (repeatedly) “Rejecting her own fault, a specific fickleness, the goddess of fortune serves Him. His begging bewilders people like us: it makes one perceive: “He's not God.””

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“Being unwavering by giving up her own fault, fickleness (svatma-dosapavargena = svatma-dosah capalyam tasya tyagena sthira sati), and having rejecting Indra and others, Sri, the form of opulence (srih = sampad-rupa) always (asakrt = sarvada) serves Him.”

### 10.23.47-48

*desah kalah prthag dravyam mantra-tantrartvijo ’gnayah \|*  
*devata yajamanas ca kratur dharmas ca yan-mayah \|\|*  
*sa esabhagavan saksad visnur yogesvaresvarah \|*  
*jato yadusv ity asrnmahy api mudha na vidmahe \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

desah—the location; kalah—the time;prthak dravyam—the separate items; mantra—the mantras (mystic verbal formulas); tantra—the procedure; rtvijah—the priests; agnayah—the fires; devatah—the divinities; yajamanah—the sponsor (“the one who is sacrificing /worshiping”); ca—and; kratuh—the sacrifice (as a whole) (or the resolve); dharmah—the merit; ca—and; yat-mayah—have the nature of whom;

sah eva—the same one; bhagavan—the Lord; saksat—directly (in person); visnuh—Visnu; yoga-isvara-isvarah—the master of grandmasters of yoga; jatah—has taken birth; yadusu—among the Yadus; iti—(end of the quotation); asrnma—we heard; hi—indeed (or a verse filler); api—although; mudhah—foolish; na vidmahe—we do not understand.

*desah kalah prthag dravyam mantra-tantrartvijah agnayah devatah yajamanah ca (pratyekam yan-mayah bhavanti), kratuh dharmah ca yan-mayah (ca bhavati), sah eva bhagavan saksad visnuh yogesvaresvarah yadusu jatah iti (vayam) hi asrnma api, (vayam) mudhah na vidmahe.*

**Перевод:**

**“Though we heard: “The place, the time, the manifold items, the mantras, the procedure, the priests, the fires, the divinities, the sponsor, the purpose, and the unforeseen merit are made of Him, Visnu in person, who is the master of the grandmasters of yoga and has taken birth among the Yadus,” we fools did not understand.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“We have hearing in this way everywhere (ity asrnma hi = evam sarvatra srutavantah vayam hi). Nevertheless (api = tathapi)..."

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

In two stanzas, they illustrate being a bewilderer of people. Sa eva saksat bhagavan means: “the same one, the Lord in person: Sri Narayana.” The reason the Lord is infused in the place and so on is: visnuh, He pervades all (= sarva-vyapakah). Next they say He should be worshiped by all: yogesvaresvarah, “He is the master of liberated souls too” (= yogesvaranam muktanam api isvarah), and so the drift is: “Only He (sa eva) should be served by us, through a fire sacrifice.”

Or sa eva signifies: sa saksad bhutah (He is directly present), and bhagavan means sarvaisvarya-yuktah (He has all types of godly might). Mudhah connotes: sastrarthanabhijnah (not knowledgeable of scriptural meanings).

In the reading esa (this), the sense is: esa pratyaksatam praptah, “He who has become directly perceptible.” Saksat means svayam (in person). Alternatively: esah adhuna eva jatah, “He who has taken birth recently.”

Another interpretation is as follows. Why did He take birth? They respond: yogesvaresvarah, which portends: “He is the master of those by whom bhakti-yoga is nicely accomplished.” The sense is He made His descent to please His devotees. With the word hi (indeed) they hint at scriptural evidence in that matter, already famous from texts such as mad-bhaktanam vinodartham:

*muhurtenapi samhartum sakto yadyapi danavan \|*  
*mad-bhaktanam vinodartham karomi vividhah kriyah \|\|*  
*darsana-dhyana-samsparsair matsya-kurma-vihangamah \|*  
*svany apatyani pusnanti tathaham api padmaja\|\|*

**“Though able to annihilate the demons in about forty-five minutes, I do diverse actions to delight My devotees. Just as fish, turtles, and birds nourish their offsprings by watching, meditating, and touching, so do I, Brahma!” (Padma Purana)**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

With this one unit of two verses, they themselves illustrate the bewilderment. (The rest of the commentary, except for the explanation of the variant reading esa, is the same. In addition:) Sukadeva’s intention with these two clauses is this: “They came to the conclusion in the same way that I did.”143

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

They expound upon the bewilderment.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Na vidmahe (we do not understand) signifies: na jnatavantah (we did not understand).

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

Vidmahe is poetic license (for vidmah).

### 10.23.49

*aho vayam dhanyatama yesam nas tadrsih striyah \|*  
*bhaktya yasarm matir jata asmakam niscala harau \|\|*

*aho! yesam nah tadrsih striyah (santi, te) vayam dhanyatamah (bhavanti), yasam (strinam) bhaktya (hetuna) asmakam (api) matih harau niscala jata.*

**Перевод:**

**“Wow! We, who have that kind of women, are the most fortunate. Owing to their bhakti, our thoughts have become fixed on Hari.**

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

This verse is vigita (not seen everywhere; dubbed dubious by some).144It too is explained: Aho has the sense of ascaryam (astonishment). “We, who have that kind (tadrsih = tadrsyah) of women, are successful (dhanyatamah = krtarthah). Their bhakti, occurring near us, serves as a reminder, and so our thoughts are steadily on Hari.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

They speak while praising themselves, on account of the greatness of the ladies’ good fortune. Tadrsih should read tadrsyah, meaning the ladies have anuraga for Sri Krsna.

### 10.23.50

*namas tubhyam bhagavatekrsnay akuntha-medhase \|*  
*yan-maya-mohita-dhiyo bhramamah karma-vartmasu \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

namah—obeisance; tubhyam—to You; bhagavate krsnaya—who are Lord Krsna; akuntha-medhase—whose intelligence is unimpeded; yat-maya—by whose Maya; mohita-dhiyah—\[we\] whose minds were bewildered; bhramamah—we are wandering; karma-vartmasu—on the paths of rites.

*tubhyam bhagavate krsnaya akuntha-medhase namah (astu), yan-maya-mohita-dhiyah (vayam) karma-vartmasu bhramamah.*

**Перевод:**

**“Obeisances to You, Lord Krsna, whose intellect is unimpeded. Our minds bewildered by Your Maya, we are wandering on the paths of sacrificial rites.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

While elaborating on the foolishness, the Brahmanas, amazed by the power of Maya, the cause of it, bow to their Lord with devotion for the sake of dispelling Maya. The verse begins with namah. “Obeisances to You, Bhagavan, i.e. You whose aisvarya is infinite and inconceivable.” The following is meant: It is hard to fathom Him. Or Bhagavan denotes; “to You who are intent on revealing Your own unlimited godhood.” The name Krsna is used with the desire to express the fact that He attracts the hearts of their wives.

“We offer respects to You because of whom memory is unbroken” (akuntha-medhase = akuntha anavacchinna medha smrtih yasmat tasmai), in the sense that their wives always remembered Him, even in household chores. Or akuntha-medhase means: alupta-jnanaya, “to You whose awareness is undiminished,” and so the idea is: “He already knows the might of His Maya and the greatness of His compassion to us, etc.”

“We are wandering on the paths of rites, that is, we are engrossed in them, meaning we are unable to get out of that frame of mind, as though it is a whirlpool.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) While elaborating on the foolishness, the Brahmanas, amazed by the power of Maya, the cause of it, bow to their Lord with devotion for the sake of dispelling Maya. The verse begins with namah. “Obeisances to You, Bhagavan, i.e. You whose aisvarya is infinite and inconceivable.” The following is meant: It is hard to fathom Him. Or Bhagavan denotes: “to You who are intent on revealing Your own unlimited godhood.” Akuntha-medhase means: alupta-jnanaya (to You whose awareness is undiminished).

In the second half of the verse, they talk about them being opposed to Him. “We are wandering on the paths of rites, that is, we are engrossed in them, meaning we are unable to get out of that frame of mind, as though it is a whirlpool.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Very disturbed on account of an offense, they give respects.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Akuntha-medhase means: apratihata medha dhisana yasya tasmai, “to You whose intelligence is unimpeded.” The suffix as\[ic\] takes place after medha by the rule: nityam asic praja-medhayoh, “The suffix as\[ic\] is always applied for praja and medha \[when they are preceded by either na\[n\], su, or dur, in a bahuvrihi compound\]” (Astadhyayi 5.4.122) (nan-su-durbhyah prajaya asir alpac ca medhayah, HNV 1077).

### 10.23.51

*sa vai na adyah pumsah sva-maya-mohitatmanam \|*  
*avijnatanubhavanam ksantum arhaty atikramam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sah—He; vai—obviously; nah—our; adyah—first (the origin of all); pumsah—person (the personal aspect of the Absolute); sva-maya-mohita-atmanam—whose minds are bewildered by His Maya; avijnata-anubhavanam—by whom His power was not understood; ksantum—to forgive; arhati—ought (used for expressing a polite command); atikramam—the transgression.

*sah vai adyah pumsah sva-maya-mohitatmanam avijnatanubhavanam nah atikramam ksantum arhati (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“May He, the origin of all, the personal aspect of the Absolute, kindly forgive our transgression. Our minds were bewildered by His Maya, and we did not understand His might.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

The Brahmanas, who had gotten very meek in this manner, induce the glorious Lord to forgive them. “He, Sri Krsna, is qualified (arhati = yogyah bhavati) to forgive our offense (nah atikramam = asmakam aparadham).” Two reasons for that are given: sva-maya-mohitatmanam, “us whose minds were bewildered by Maya, which belongs only to Him (sva-maya-mohitatmanam = tasya eva mayaya mohita-cittanam)—and therefore—by whom His glory was not understood (avijnatanubhavanam = na vijnatah anubhavah mahatmyam yaih tesam).”

Someone might think, “This huge offense cannot be forgiven.” In that regard, they say: adyah pumsah, “the first Purusa,” whose form has thousands of heads and so forth (= sahasra-sirsadi-rupah). The drift is the forgiveness of an offense of Brahmanas, who originated from His head, is fitting, like a father’s forgiveness of his son.

Or, adyah means sresthah (the best), hence “He should forgive our offense; in comparison to Him, we are vile.” And pumsah means: puri sayanat pumsah antaryami, "the inner controller, who rests in the city \[of nine gates\],” therefore: “We were driven in that way by Him.” Alternatively, the sense of adyah pumsah is Purusottama, and so He ought to forgive because of His inherent glory, such as being affectionate to wretched persons (dina-vatsalya), being favorable to Brahmanas (brahmanya), and being God.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Possessed by utter meekness, they make the Lord forgive. Atikramam (trangression) means aparadham (offense).

### 10.23.52

*iti svagham anusmrtya krsne te krta-helanah \|*  
*didrksavo ’py acyutayahkamsad bhita na cacalan \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

iti—in this way (or used as a last quotation mark); sva-agham—their sin; anusmrtya—after constantly remembering; krsne—toward Krsna; te—they; krta-helanah—by whom contempt was done; didrksavah api—although desiring to see; acyutayoh—the two Acyutas; kamsat bhitah—afraid of Kamsa; na—not; ca—but (na ca = na tu); acalan—they went.

*te (viprah) krsne krta-helanah iti svagham anusmrtya (acyutau) didrksavah api kamsad bhitah (santah) acyutayoh (samipe) na acalan. (tesam patnyah) ca (na acalan). kimva: (tau acyutau) ca (sva-sthanad na acalatam).*

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

*krsne krta-helanah te (brahmanah) iti svagham anusmrtya acyutayoh didrksavah api kamsad bhitah na acalan.*

**The Brahmanas, who had shown contempt to Krsna, continuously recalled their mistake in this fashion. Although they desired to see the two Acyutas, they did not go, out of fear of Kamsa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“They did not go... to see Them.” (na cacalan =tayor darsanaya na jagmuh).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The Brahmanas had committed an offense, an uncommon one (svagham = svam asadharanam agham aparadham). Suka expounds on it: krta-helanah, “they by whom a contempt was done, from the viewpoint of men” (= krtam helanam manusya-drstya avajna yaih te). Therefore, “Although they wanted to see (didrksavah = didrksavo ’pi), that is, although they desired to meet Them in order to obtain Their forgiveness of their mistake, they did not go to the cowherd village (vrajam = vrajam prati),” meaning they did not walk in that direction. The reason for that is they were completely (atha = kartsnyena) afraid of Kamsa, due to fearing that something undesirable would happen to Him, inasmuch as they had no firm faith in the glorious Lord.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Someone might think, “Why didn’t they take shelter of the Lord, either by going there in Asokavana right at that time or by going to the cowherd village after some time?” He responds in the second half of the verse. They did not go to Asokavana because they were feeling guilty and because they were not unanimous. Later, at dusk, they went to the cowherd village. Or, when there was unanimity, they did not go... all the way—because of ca (and). In this way they are reviled.

The reason they did not go is that He arose at once in their minds; this is the significance of kamsad bhitah (afraid of Kamsa). The sense is they were perturbed by fear: “If Kamsa gets to know about this incident, through his spies, he will destroy our livelihood.” The ladies, however, never had fear, including the fear of being killed by their husbands and the fear of being abandonned by them, in the matter of seeing Krsna. Only prema is the reason for this. The men, however, were hampered in that regard because of a semblance of fear imagined in their minds. Only the Lord’s Maya is the reason for it.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“Those Brahmanas who had shown contempt to Krsna did not go (na cacalan = na agacchan) although they wanted to see the two Acyutas.” The reason they didn’t go is they were afraid of Kamsa. This means they worshiped Krsna while staying at home. Because the wives had prema, those ladies went to Him straightaway, but at this time too the husbands stayed back because they lacked prema.

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

“Although they wanted to see (didrksavah = didrksavo ’pi), in the manner of a new beginning (atha = bhinnopakramena) they did not go to Vraja.” The reason is that they were afraid of Kamsa for His sake.

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

The genitive case in acyutayoh is loose (sese sasthi).

## Chapter 24 - Krsna Stops a Sacrifice to Indra and Inaugurates the Worship of Govardhana Hill

### 10.24.1

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*bhagavan api tatraiva baladevena samyutah \|*  
*apasyan nivasan gopan indra-yaga-krtodyaman \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah uvaca—Sri Suka said; bhagavan—the Lord; api—although; tatra eva—only there (or right there); baladevena—by Baladeva; samyutah—accompanied; apasyat—saw; nivasan—while residing; gopan—the cowherd men; indra-yaga—for a fire sacrifice to Indra; krta—were done; udyaman—by whom great efforts.

*sri-sukah uvaca—(sri-krsnah) baladevena samyutah tatra (vraje) eva nivasan bhagavan api indra-yaga-krtodyaman gopan apasyat.*

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

*(sabhayam bhratradibhih saha upavistah nanda-rajah indra-puja-sambhara-siddhaye gopan adisat.) tatra eva nivasan bhagavan api gopan indra-yaga-krtodyaman apasyat.*

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

*baladevena samyutah bhagavan (krsnah) tatra eva (gokule) nivasan indra-yaga-krtodyaman gopan apasyat.*

**Sri Suka said: Krsna was only residing there although He is the Lord. Accompanied by Baladeva, He noticed that the cowherd men were actively making arrangements for a sacrifice to Indra.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*caturvimse mahendrasya makham vyavartya hetubhih \|*  
*krsnah pravartayamasa govardhana-makhotsavam \|\|*  
*bhu-suranam kriya-garvam nirasya svah-suresu ca \|*  
*maghavan-mada-bhangaya tan-makham samavarayat \|\|*

**“In the twenty-fourth chapter, this is told: Krsna stopped a sacrifice to Indra for various reasons. Then He caused the inauguration of a festival: a sacrifice to Govardhana. Having dispelling the Brahmanas’ pride of performing rites, Krsna interrupted the sacrifice to Indra, who is one of the gods, to break his arrogance.”**

**10.24.1**

The Brahmanas, afraid of Kamsa (10.23.52), stayed on their respective properties. They were worshiping the Lord. The prose order is: bhagavan api tatraiva nivasann indra-yaga-krtodyaman gopan apasyat.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

After mentioning pastimes that were done mostly in the sixth and seventh years of age, from the beginnings of cow herding, now Suka continues in order to talk about that pastime at the outset of the eighth year with four chapters starting from the twenty-fourth.

“While continuously living, with great attachment, only in Vraja (tatraiva nivasan = vraje eva nitaram asakti-purvakam vasan)...” This suggests that He is dedicated to having fun in Vraja and that those who live there are the most fortunate.

The sense of the word api is this: viprah sva-sthanat nacalan, bhagavan api tesam santvanartham nayayau, kintu vraja eva nivasan, "The Brahmanas did not go from their place. The Lord too did not come to console them. While residing only in Vraja..."

He was accompanied by Baladeva (baladevena samyutah): The gist is He didn't send him either to console them.

The sense of indra-yaga-krtodyaman apasyat is He saw the cowherds' endeavors: they gathered various ingredients for the purpose of worshiping Indra, raised a flag for Indra, etc., at the pond called Indra-dhvaja, located east of Govardhana.

Although the cowherd men were performing a sacrifice for Indra and exerting themselves for him every year, and even though it had already been seen by the Lord, still, the mention of a detail now, with apasyat (He saw) and so forth, is because of an indifference to that previously in consideration of waiting for a suitable time either for the amusement of lifting Govardhana or for the pastime of breaking the sacrifice to Indra. Thus, previously Krsna was not interested in breaking a sacrifice to Indra or lifting Govardhana Hill. Moreover, this pastime occurred when the autumn season had begun, at the end of the rainy season, on account of the statement in Hari-vamsa:

*tam sarat-kusumapidah parivarya pradaksinam*  
*gavo giri-varam sarvas tato yantu punar vrajam*  
*prapta kileyam hi gavam svadu-toya-trnair gunaih*  
*sarat pramudita ramya gata-megha-jalasaya*

**“All the cows, decorated with chaplets of autumal flowers, should circumambulate the best of mountains, keeping it to their right, and then return to the cow shed. Indeed, the charming autumn season has arrived. It is delightful because it provides the cows with palatable grass and water. At this time, the lakes do not reflect any cloud” (Hari-vamsa 2.16.13-14), and on account of the upcoming text: apartv atyulbanam varsam, “The rain was out of season and vehement” (Bhagavatam 10.25.15).**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Krsna once said to the young girls of Vraja: yatabala vrajam siddha mayema ramsyatha ksapah, “Girls, go to the village. You are successful. You will enjoy these nights with Me” (Bhagavatam 10.22.27). The Lord enjoyed with the gopis during autumn nights, which He had talked about in the winter. Of course, those nights were in the autumn after that winter, not in any other year. The beginning of that enjoyment will be mentioned only in regard to the full moon of autumn (Bhagavatam 10.29.1-3). That full moon is the full moon night of Asvina, which occurs within autumn.

This worship of Govardhana took place on the first day of the bright fortnight during the month of Kartika and was imitated by the vraja-devis during Rasa-lila. The pastime of going to Varuna’s kingdom happened only after the worship of Govardhana. Therefore, from the previous autumn to the next, the worship of Govardhana, the going to Varuna’s kingdom, the theft of gopis' garments, the acceptance of the offerings of the sacrificial Brahmanas’ wives, and the games of Rasa are to be understood in that sequence. The analysis of the various years will be done at the end of the occurrence of the killing of Kamsa. The mention out of order by Sukadeva is due to the helplessness of prema and also because pastimes pertain to the same category.

Now, the meaning of bhagavan api tatraiva is this: “Accompanied by Baladeva, the Lord too, residing right there—a special place near the cowherd village, suitable for a sacrifice to him, and where cowherds were living, after setting out together, and were busy—, saw the cowherds, by whom efforts were made for a sacrifice to Indra.” The sense is He only kept looking with the desire to see the means of accomplishing another sacrifice with those articles. He did not say anything at first. In Sri Visnu Purana: vimalambara-naksatre kale cabhyagate vraje, dadarsendra-maharambha-yodyatams tan vrajaukasah, **“In Vraja, at a time when the constellations in the sky were bright, Krsna saw that the residents of Vraja were laboring diligently for the purpose of a great undertaking for Indra”** (Visnu Purana 5.10.16), and in Sri Hari-vamsa: vrajam ajagmatus tau tu vraje susruvatus tada, praptam sakram maha-virau gopams cotsava-lalasan, **“When the two great heros arrived at the cowherd village, They heard that the time for a sacrifice to Indra was near and that the cowherd men were eager for a festival”147** (Hari-vamsa 2.15.2), the narration is done in a general way, whereas here details are given. That is the difference.

This amusement occurred only on the first day of the bright fortnight during the month of Kartika because this event is a regular occurrence in Kartika: it is the traditional conduct of the people of central India. Another reason is this: apartv atyulbanam varsam, “The rain was out of season and vehement” (Bhagavatam 10.25.15). For instance, it is said in that way in Padma Purana, at the end of activities performed during the new moon in Kartika linked to offerings of lamps: pratipady-udite ravau pratar govardhanah pujyo ratrau dyutam samacaret, “When the sun has risen on the first day of the fortnight, Govardhana should be worshiped. At night, one should play dice games” (Padma Purana 6.122.29).148

Therefore the description in Hari-vamsa that the event occurred at the junction of the monsoon and autumn is like the description of the shore of an ocean: Sometimes in central India, the rains continue during the month of Asvina (the first of the two months of autumn).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*sva-pitra saha samlapya makham vyadhuya vajrinah \|*  
*caturvimse girindrasya makham pravartayad dharih \|\|*

**“In the twenty-fourth chapter, Hari conversed with His father, terminated the sacrifice to Indra, and inaugurated a sacrifice for Govardhana.”**

**10.24.1**

Nanda Maharaja was staying with his brothers in an assembly of cowherd men: he directed the cowherds to complete the preparations for a sacrifice to Indra.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

*caturvimse vinirdhuya pujam indrasya hetubhih \|*  
*pravartayat sva-bhaktasya giri-rajasya tam harih \|\|*

**“In the twenty-fourth chapter, after repudiating the formal worship of Indra with logical arguments, Hari set in motion a formal worship of Giri-raja, His devotee.”**

**10.24.1**

Seated with his brothers in an assembly, King Nanda ordered the cowherds for the sake of accomplishing the preparations for a formal worship of Indra. Residing right there, although He is the Lord, He saw the cowherds, who were busy for a sacrifice to Indra.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

In the twenty-fourth chapter, he describes the Govardhana festival, inaugurated by the Lord, which was preceded by a refutation of a sacrifice to Indra. Afraid of Kamsa, the Brahmanas did not go from their respective properties (na cacalan = svasranebhyah na ca acalan, 10.23.52); they stayed in them and worshiped the Lord. The syntactical connection is: bhagavan api tatra eva vrndavane nivasan indra-yaga-krtodyaman gopan apasyat, “The Lord as well, residing in the same place, in Vrndavana, saw the cowherds, by whom an effort was done for the sake of a sacrifice to Indra (indra-yaga-krtodyaman = indra-yagaya krtah udyamah yaih tan).'’

### 10.24.2

*tad-abhijno ’pi bhagavan sarvatma sarva-darsanah \|*  
*prasrayavanato ’prcchad vrddhan nanda-purogaman \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tat-abhijnah—He knows that; api—although; bhagavan—the Lord; sarva-atma—the soul of everyone; sarva-darsanah—who sees everything; prasraya—reverentially; avanatah—bowed; aprcchat— asked; vrddhan—the elders; nanda—is Nanda; purah-gaman— whose leader (“who goes in front”).

*bhagavan tad-abhijnah api sarvatma sarva-darsanah pras ray avanatah (san) nanda-purogaman vrddhan aprcchat.*

**Перевод:**

**Though the Lord, the Soul of everyone and the seer of all, was aware of the cowherds’ intentions, He bowed reverentially and inquired from the elder cowherds, whose leader is Nanda.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Although He was aware of that effort (tad-abhijno ’pi - tasya udyamasya abhijnah api), He inquired” to refute the validity of it by means of their answers. The reason for being aware of it is: sarvatma, “He pervades everything” (= sarva-vyapakah).
