Or sarvatma signifies sarvesam atma cetayita, “the Soul of everyone, the one who gives consciousness.” Therefore: sarva-darsanah, “He makes one see everything” (= sarvam darsayan iti tatha sah) because: bhagavan, He has all aisvarya. Or the Lord inquired because He is Bhagavan in the sense that He has amazing pastimes.

There is another interpretation. The reason for asking is: sarvatma, which means sarvasya atma pravartakah, “the Soul of all, the one who incites all to action.” That was for the purpose of inaugurating a sacrifice to Sri Govardhana by stopping a sacrifice to Sakra. Why? sarva-darsanah, “He sees, perceives, everything: the service to Govardhana, the best servant of Hari.” That too is for what reason? bhagavan, He has infinite virtues, such as caring for devotees. Or bhagavan means He is dedicated to manifesting all His special godly might. This is another reason.

“While reverentially bowing...” (prasrayavanatah = prasrayavanatah san), due to being an ocean of all virtues. Or He did so to make them grasp what He was going to say, so that they understand His wisdom. They are worthy of reverence. He asked the elders since only they have that understanding and because when they will be enlightened in this matter, everyone else will be so too.

Further in that regard: nanda-purogamah, “them, among whom the foremost is Nanda” (= nandah purogamah mukhyah yesam), inasmuch as when he will be enlightened, automatically all the elders will become enlightened. And specifically, the hidden meaning is this: “My father has a very simple nature. He is extremely caring, and his heart is overwhelmed by deep affection for Me. He never transgresses My desire. Everyone else is subordinate to him. Therefore, the main thing for Me is to direct My inquiries to him.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“He inquired although He was aware of that,” i.e. the sacrifice to Indra, seen each previous year. In addition: “Although He is the Lord (bhagavan = bhagavan api), due to being an ocean of all virtues, He inquired only while bowing with humility (prasrayavanatah = vinayavanamrah eva san).” The reason for being aware is He is Paramatma (sarvatma = Paramatma). The reason for asking is: sarva-darsanah, “He shows everything, meaning He impels everyone for His own purpose” (= sarvan darsayan svarthe pravartayati iti tatha sah).

“My ancestors, who were not immediately related to Me, performed the worship of gods who were averse to Me. Fine, that was then, but now the worship of these cowherds who are close to Me makes Me happy only if I am its essential aspect, and so the worship of Indra performed by My father and others gives Me sorrow.”

Indra is extremely insignificant on account of the grand glory of Vraja. The sign of that glory was: tad bhuri-bhagyam, etc., “May I have profuse good fortune by which I will have some birth in this forest” (10.14.34), and moreover he is very proud.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Tad-abhijno ’pi signifies: “although He knows about that sacrifice in every way: the method of the philosophical conclusion, the manner of the performance, and so forth.” He already knew about each previous one. Still, it’s understood that He is inquiring with disrespect for Indra.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Although He was aware of that (tad-abhijno ’pi = tasya abhijnah api)...” insofar as it was seen in each previous year. The sense of sarvatma (the Soul of everyone) is: Though in the form of Paramatma He impels the cowherds to perform a sacrifice to Indra, it was for the sake of the joviality of a pastime. Sarva-darsanah denotes: sarvam udarkam pasyati iti sah, “He sees all the consequences—His shattering Indra’s pride and His fun of staying with His kin for seven days and nights.”

### 10.24.3

*kathyatam me pitah ko ’yam sambhramo va upagatah \|*  
*kim phalam kasya voddesah kena va sadhyate makhah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

kathyatam—it should be told; me—to Me; pitah—O father; kah—what?; ayam—is this; sambhramah—bustle; vah—of all of you; upagatah—which has come about; kim—what?; phalam—the result; kasya—of whom?; va—and; uddesah—the mention; kena—by what means? (or by whom?); va—and; sadhyate—is being accomplished; makhah—the sacrifice.

*pitah! ayam vah sambhramah kah upagatah? (sah) me kathyatam. (ayam) makhah (bhavati iti cet), kim (atra) phalam (sadhyam asti? atra) kasya va uddesah (bhavati? sah makhah) kena (sadhanena adhikarina) va sadhyate?*

**Перевод:**

**“Father, what is this bustle that has come about? Kindly explain it to Me. If this is a sacrifice, what will be the result? And who is the presiding deity? It is being accomplished by whom and by what means?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“This is not a useless bustle: it’s a sacrifice. If so, what is the result to be had? Who is the presiding deity (kasya uddesah = ka devata)? It is being accomplished by which qualified person and by what means?” (kena va sadhyate = kena adhikarina kena va sadhanena sadhyate).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“It should be told to Me (me = mahyam).” The sense is: “Everybody else knows; only I don’t know. Inform Me alone.” To please His father, this is only a playfulness that is almost naive, in order to hear about it, which He must.

Vah means yusmakam. The sense is: “the bustle of all of you,” but not “of some of you.” Sambhramah (bustle) denotes either tvara-visesah (a specific haste) or vaiyagryam (busyness). As a pun, the sense of sambhramah is: samyag bhramah eva (only a complete mistake). Upagatah (it has come about) means either dure sthatum yogyo ’pi samipam praptah (though it should remain far, it has come about) or upary-apatitah (befallen from above). With the word kena, the question relates both to the karta (the doer of the sacrifice) and to the karana (the means of accomplishing it).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The words starting from kathyatam form one half verse. (The rest of the commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“A sacrifice will take place (makhah -makhah bhavisyati). If this bustle is for the sake of accomplishing it, what is the result in it? And (va = ca) there is a mention of whom? In other words: “Who is the deity referred to as worthy of being worshiped? It is being accomplished by which doer and by what means? (kena va = kena kartra karanena va).”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“The upcoming sacrifice (makhah = bhavi makhah).”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“What result is to be accomplished (kim phalam = kim phalam sodhyam)? If it is a sacrifice (makhah = makhah iti cet), it is characterized by an offering of things by mentioning which deity (kasya uddesah = kam devatam uddisya dravya-tyaga-laksanah)? It is being accomplished by which qualified person (kena = kena adhikarina)?” Or: “Why is it being accomplished (kena = kena hetuna)?”

### 10.24.4-5

*etad bruhi mahan kamo mahyam susrusave pitah \|*  
*nahi gopyam hi sadhunam krtyam sarvatmanam iha \|\|*  
*asty asva-para-drstinam amitrodasta-vidvisam \|*  
*udasino ’ri-vad varjya atma-vat suhrd ucyate \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

etat—this; bruhi—tell; mahan—great; kamah—desire; mahyam—to Me; susrusave—desirous of hearing; pitah—O father; nahi—no; gopyam—that should be kept secret; hi—indeed; sadhunam— by saintly persons; krtyam—activity; sarva-atmanam—for whom everyone is the self; iha—here;

asti—there is; asva-para-drstinam—who do not have the vision (the conception) of one’s own or another’s; amitra-udasta-vidvisam—for whom there is no friend, neutral party, or enemy; udasinah—one who is indifferent; ari-vat—like an enemy; varjyah—can be shunned; atma-vat—like one’s own self; suhrt—a friend; ucyate—is said to be.

*pitah! (tvam) susrusave mahyam etad bruhi. mahan kamah (bhavati), hi iha sarvatmanam asva-para-drstinam amitrodasta-vidvisam sadhunam krtyam gopyam nahi asti. udasinah ari-vad varjyah (bhavati), suhrt (tu) atma-vad ucyate.*

**Перевод:**

**“Tell Me about it, father. It’s a great desire. I want to hear. Indeed, no deed should be kept secret by saintly persons, for whom everyone is similar to oneself, who do not see in terms of “This is mine and that is another’s,” and for whom no one is a friend, a neutral party or an enemy. A neutral person, similar to an enemy, may be shunned, but a friend is like one’s self.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Say it. I have a great desire to hear (mahan kamah = mahan kamah mama sravane vartate).” Or: tava mahan kamo drsyate, “I see that you have a great desire.”

With na and so on, Krsna continues talking to him, who was remaining silent. Sarvatmanam means: sarvatra atma-drstinam, “\[of saintly persons\] who see the soul everywhere.” Therefore they are asva-para-drstinam, “they for whom ideas of ‘mine’ and ‘another’s’ do not exist” (= na vidyate svah parah iti drstih yesam tesam). Consequently: amitrodasta-vidvisam, “for whom there is no friend, neutral person, or enemy” (= na mitram udastah udasinah vidvid yesam tesam).

“Any deed (krtyam = sarvam karma) should not in the least be kept secret. A neutral person, similar to an enemy, can be shunned, but in the matter of taking advice, a friend should not be rejected because he is like one’s self” (atma-vat suhrt = atma-tulyatvat suhrn mantresu na varjaniyah).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The repetition etad bruhi (tell it) is for the purpose of letting him know about His intense desire to hear. “Tell it to please Me (mahyam = mam prinayitum)."

There is another interpretation: “What is the use of explaining this to You, a little boy?” He responds: susrusave. The drift is: “A son’s desire should be fulfilled.” As a pun, by the axiom: susrusam dharmam abruyat, “To a person who wants to hear, one should talk about moral codes,” the necessity of a reply is expressed.149The vocative pitah (father) was used in the previous verse; the repetition here is for the sake of evoking a special deep affection.

The words from nahi are one verse and the words from udasinah make one verse of two lines. He continues talking to him, who was remaining silent; Nanda was hesitating: “He already knows what happened in previous years. It’s understood that He is inquiring, especially with a sarcastic undertone, as a form of disrespect to Indra again, since His qualities are the same as Narayana's and because He killed many devils who defeated him.”

In point of sadhunam (of saintly persons), they are given as an example because they have nothing to hide since they don’t engage in forbidden acts. The exclusive characteristics of sadhus are mentioned with three adjectives, beginning with sarvatmanam. Asva-para-drstinam portends: Paramatma tad-drstinam, “(of sadhus,\] who have the vision of Paramatma.” Iha means jagad kutrapi (anywhere in the world). Therefore the gist is: “It is not right for you all, who have those qualities, to conceal anything from Me.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“What is the use of Your question? You’re just a child.” “My desire on this matter remains strong. Tell it to please Me, who want to hear (mahyam susrusave = susrusum mam prinayitum)." In case he replies, “Since it is confidential, I should not divulge this to children and others who are not very intelligent,” with nahi and so forth He speaks to suggest, only with astounding words, that He is very smart. Sarvatmanam means: sarve eva atmanah atma-tulyah yesam tesam, “\[of sadhus,\] for whom everyone is like one’s self.” Therefore: asva-para-drstinam, “who do not have the outlook: ‘this is related to me’, ‘this is external to me’” (= ayam sah antarangah ayam parah bahirahgah iti na vidyate drstih yesam tesam). Hence those varieties—friends, neutral persons, and enemies—do not exist: That is what He talks about with amitrodasta-vidvisam.

“We are householders. We cannot become sadhus.” With udasino ’ri-vat and the rest He replies: “Still, it is not appropriate to conceal it from Me.” The sense is: “A neutral person, similar to an enemy (ari-vat = arina tulyah)—owing to the suffix vat\[i\] being used in the sense of tulya (same, similar)—can be rejected.” Moreover, this should be known: The sameness of attribute with an enemy is said with because of the intent to do wrong since he or she is an enemy’s friend, but not because he or she did wrong. For that reason, the definition of a neutral person is seen in Ujjvala-nilamani: yo vipaksa-suhrt-paksah sa tata-stho nigadyate, “One who is a friend of the enemy is called neutral” (9.7). However, a neutral person is not the same as an enemy nor is he or she the same as a friend: A neutral person should neither be rejected in nor accepted in one’s activities, yet this definition is never put in writing.150

The sense of atma-vat suhrd is: suhrd atma-mitratvad atma-vad visvasyah, “A well-wisher is as trustworthy as one’s self on account of being one’s friend.” The idea is: “I, however, am your son, and a son is more intimately related than a friend.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

The words beginning from etad form one verse of six lines. He speaks in case Nanda were to say, “You’re a little boy. Go play with Your friends. Why do You care to ask?”

“Although we are saintly persons,151we cannot divulge secrets because we are householders.” He responds with udasino ’ri-vat and so on: These words form one verse of two lines. The sense is: udasinas ced ari-vad varjyah, “If a person is neutral, he or she can be rejected like one rejects an enemy.”152

### 10.24.6

*jnatvajnatva ca karmani jano ’yam anutisthati \|*  
*vidusah karma-siddhih syad yatha naviduso bhavet \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

jhatva—knowing; ajnatva—not knowing; ca—and; karmani—activities; janah—person; ayam—this; anutisthati—performs; vidusah—for one who knows; karma-siddhih—the perfection of the activity; syat—occurs; yatha—suitably; na—not; avidusah—for one who doesn’t know; bhavet—might occur.

*ayam (kascid) janah jhatva karmani anutisthati, (kascid janah) ca ajnatva (karmani anutisthati). yatha vidusah karma-siddhih syat, avidusah (kvacid api tatha phalam) na bhavet.*

**Перевод:**

**“This person acts with some understanding, and another does so without any understanding. Fittingly, the fruition of the deed only occurs to the one who knows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Moreover, a deed should be done only after pondering over it with friends and after having an understanding in the matter, but not merely because everybody does it.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“True, I hold You in higher esteen than I do my own life, but You’re too young to be a consultant.” He responds to that. Ajnatva ca signifies: ajnatva ca drsta-paramparaya, “not understanding and only following what others are seen to do.” Yatha means either yathavat (suitably) or yadrsi (of that kind).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Karmani (activities) signifies both agriculture, etc., and fire sacrifices and so on: The results of these activities are both drsta (seen) and adrsta (unseen: occurring in the next life). Yatha means yathavat (in conformity with what is meant to be).

### 10.24.7

*tatra tavat kriya-yogo bhavatam kim vicaritah \|*  
*athava laukikas tan me prcchatah sadhu bhanyatam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatra tavat—case in point; kriya-yogah—the ritualistic activity; bhavatam—done by all of you; kim—is it?; vicaritah—considered; athava—or; laukikah—worldly; tat—that; me—to Me; prcchatah— who am inquiring; sadhu—properly; bhanyatam—should be told.

*tatra (visaye, yah ayam) bhavatam kriya-yogah (bhavati, sah) kim (sastra-praptatvena) vicaritah (pravrttah, kim) athava laukikah (asti iti yad bhavati), tat prcchatah me sadhu bhanyatam (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Case in point, was your ritualistic activity thoroughly considered or is it simply a custom? I, who am inquiring, should be decidedly told.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Was this rite of yours set forth upon consideration, perhaps even from scriptural knowledge, or it is obtained as a worldly custom? It should be told with a logical reasoning (sadhu bhanyatam = sopapattikam kathyatam)."

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Tatra denotes tasyam, that is, tasyam karma-siddhau (in regard to the fruition of an activity). Vicaritah means sastra-vicara-siddhah (substantiated by scriptural consideration).

The drift is: If this sacrifice is sanctioned by the scriptures, it is to be refuted only by scriptural logic. If it is based on a custom, it is to be refuted with a worldly logic.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“Among rites (tatra = tesu karmasu), was this rite of yours whose result is unforeseen (kriya-yogah = idam adrsta-phalam karma) obtained from a scriptural consideration because of being evidenced only in the scriptures (vicaritah = sastraika-pramanatvat tad-vicara-praptah) or is it obtained only by a worldly tradition (athava laukikah = kim athava loka-paramparaya eva praptah)?"

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He speaks in case he were to reply, “It is being done after having thought about it and only after understanding the matter.” (The rest is the same as Laghu-vaisnava-tosani.)

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Kim laukikah means kim kulacara-praptah, “Is it obtained by family tradition?”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

“Among rites meant for gods (tatra = devata-karmanam madhye), at first (tavat = prathamam) was the method of the performance of the rite (kriya-yogah = karmanusthana-prakarah)..."

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

Kriya-yogah means: kriya-rupah yogah upayah, “a means, the form of a ceremonial rite.”153

### 10.24.8

*nanda uvaca*  
*parjanyo bhagavan indro meghas tasyatma-murtayah \|*  
*te ’bhivarsanti bhutanam prinanam jivanam payah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

nandah uvaca—Nanda said; parjanyah—Indra; bhagavan—his lordship; indrah—Indra; meghah—clouds; tasya—his; atma-murtayah—embodiments of himself; te abhivarsanti—they rain; bhutanam—of beings; prinanam—which causes the pleasure; jivanam—by means of which there is life; payah—water.

*nandah uvaca—parjanyah bhagavan indrah (bhavati), meghah tasya atma-murtayah (bhavanti), te bhutanam prinanam jivanam (ca) payah abhivarsanti.*

**Перевод:**

**Nanda said: “His lordship Indra is the god of rain. Clouds are dear forms of his. They rain water, which pleases beings and sustains life.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Nanda means to say: “It is only obtained as a custom.” He gives reasons. Atma-murtayah means priya-murtayah (dear forms).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Parjanyo bhagavan means: vrsti-dvara isvarah, “He is a controller by means of rain.” This is said with a special devotion. Prinanam means santarpakam (it makes one refreshed). Jivanam signifies: mrta-prayanam trnadinam prana-dam, “It gives life to grasses, etc., that are almost dead.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Parjanyah is made from the verbal root prs\[u\] secane (to sprinkle).155Atma-murtayah means: atma-tulyah murtayah yesam te, “\[clouds,\] whose forms are similar to himself (as Parjanya).”

### 10.24.9

*tam tata vayam anye ca varmucam patim isvaram \|*  
*dravyais tad-retasa siddhair yajante kratubhir narah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tam—him; tata—(an affectionate vocative term addressed to a junior); vayam—we; anye—others; ca—and; var-mucam—of clouds (“which release water”); patim—the master; isvaram—the controller; dravyaih—with ingredients; tat-retasa—by his semen (water); siddhaih—which are effected; yajante—they worship; kratubhih—with fire sacrifices; narah—men.

*tata, vayam (vaisyah) tam (indram) isvaram varmucam patim tad-retasa siddhaih dravyaih kratubhih (ca yajamah). anye ca narah (brahmanadyah tam evam) yajante.*

**Перевод:**

**“My dear son, we and other men worship him, the master of clouds and the controller, with ingredients brought about by means of his rainwater and with fire sacrifices.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“We and others revere Indra (tam = indram), the master of clouds (varmucam patim = meghanam svaminam), and the controller (isvaram = niyantaram)." Tad-retasa means tad-vrsti-payasa (by his rainfall).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Tata (dear boy) is an affectionate vocative to evoke faith in his words and to make Him understand the goal. “We cowherds—but not: ‘only we, for the sake of cow protection’—and all other men (anye ca narah = anye ca narah sarve) worship him.” Krsna might say: “The sun evaporates water. Isn’t it well-known that rain occurs on account of the sun?” He responds: varmucam patim, “Indra is the master of clouds (varmucam = meghanam)." This means only he is the controller (isvara) of the forms of clouds and even of sunrays. For instance, in Sri Visnu Purana: bhaumam etat payo dugdham gobhih suryasya varidaih, parjanyah sarva-lokasya bhavaya bhuvi varsati, **“Water on Earth is evaporated by sunrays. With clouds, Parjanya rains on Earth for everyone’s welfare”** (Visnu Purana 5.10.23). How is it so? He is the controller, on account of being the king of gods, otherwise he would make us afraid by his anger.

An additional interpretation is as follows: “It is not appropriate that you cowherds, the best Vaisnavas, worship another god.” To that he says: isvaram. The sense is: “We revere him by having Paramatma in mind.”

In point of tad-retasa siddhaih, the drift is: “In truth, our worship of Indra at first with those substances is proper because we have no ownership over them, otherwise ungratefulness and other faults would accrue.” The third person in yajante is poetic license; it should be yajamah, and likewise regarding upajivanti in the next verse. Or, the third person is used with the desire to express the predominance of others in order to repel his faults, out of fear of transgressing His statement (cowherds shouldn’t worship other gods), on account of knowing his son’s intention (topmost Vaisnavas should only worship Bhagavan).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

This is implied by the affectionate vocative tata (dear junior): “You, my son, are virtuous and were obtained only by the favor of such praiseworthy gods, therefore You, handsome and auspicious, should not speak against their worship.”

“As a matter of fact, even the conceit of being the doer in that fire sacrifice is inappropriate.” That is what he says with tad-retasa siddhaih, which means tad-vrsta-payasa siddhaih, “\[with ingredients\] brought about by his rain water.”

### 10.24.10

*tac-chesenopajivanti tri-varga-phala-hetave \|*  
*pumsam purusa-karanam parjanyah phala-bhavanah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tat-sesena—with the remnants of that \[sacrifice\]; upajivanti—they sustain their lives; tri-varga—\[consisting of\] the group of three (dharma, artha, and kama); phala-hetave—for a purpose, which is the result; pumsam—of men; purusa-karanam—of the human efforts; parjanyah—Indra; phala-bhavanah—who causes the manifestation of results.

*(narah) tac-chesena tri-varga-phala-hetave upajivanti, (yatah) pumsam purusa-karanam parjanyah phala-bhavanah (bhavati).*

**Перевод:**

**“To achieve dharma, artha, and kama, people sustain their lives with the remnants of that fire sacrifice. Parjanya engenders the results of human endeavors.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“They arrange for their sustenance (upajivanti =upajivikam kalpayanti) in order to accomplish religiosity, economic development, and sense gratification” (tri-varga-phala-hetave = dharmartha-kama-siddhaye)."

“Well, people live by means of agriculture and so on. What is the need of Indra?” He responds with pumsam and so on. Phala-bhavanah means phala-sadhakah, “he who brings about the result,” given that without Parjanya, agriculture and other endeavors are fruitless.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“Is there any benefit at all by offering those things?” Nanda answers here. The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami. Or: “Isn’t it that dharma, artha and kama are accomplished by human efforts?” He replies in the second sentence: That accomplishment occurs only by the grace of the devatas, and Parjanya is the king of gods. Purusa-karanam means udyamanam (of endeavors).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“They get sustenance (upajivanti = jivikam upakalpayanti) with the leftover food of that fire sacrifice (tac-chesena = tad-yajna-sistena annena),” but it is not that the sustenance too is for the sake of unrestrained material sense gratification: That is what he talks about with tri-varga-phala-hetave.

He is the one who brings about the result—the result is dharma, artha and kama—of endeavors which are for the sake of dharma, artha and kama (purusa-karanam = tri-vargartham udyamanam) (phala-bhavanah = phalam yat tri-vargah eva tasya bhavanah sadhakah), since in truth only Parjanya is the root cause of the group of three. This means there is rain because of Parjanya, there is food because of rain, there is sustenance because of food, there is dharma because of sustenance, and there is an endeavor because of dharma. Therefore only he is worshiped.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“Men make a living (upajivanti = narah jivikam kurvanti) with the leftover food of that fire sacrifice (tac-chesena = tad-yajna-sistena annena)."

### 10.24.11

*ya enam visrjed dharmam paramparyagatam narah \|*  
*kamal lobhad bhayad dvesat sa vai napnoti sobhanam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

yah—who; enam—this; visrjet—rejects; dharmam—religious practice;paramparya—from the tradition; agatam—which has come; narah—a person; kamat—because of lust; lobhat—because of greed; bhayat—because of fear; dvesat—because of enmity; sah—he; vai—certainly; na apnoti—does not achieve; sobhanam—auspiciousness.

*(atah) yah narah enam paramparyagatam dharmam kamad lobhad bhayad dvesad (va) visrjet, sah vai sobhanam na apnoti (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“A person who, out of lust, greed, fear, or enmity, rejects this moral duty, which has come from the tradition, certainly does not achieve auspiciousness.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Kamat means either “out of a desire to protect wealth” or “out of a desire to gain another result with another activity.” Dvesat means either “because of disrespecting Indra as a result of a drought and so on” or “on account of a rising of hatred for Indra’s devotees.” Bhayat signifies either “due to fearing a decline in vaisnava-dharma by worshiping another devata” or “due to fearing a decrease of wealth.” Lobhat means either “out of greed for things” or “out of a desire for fame and so on.” The word va (or) should be added.

The meaning of sobhanam napnoti is: iha amutra ca tasya ksemam na syat, “Whether in this world or in the next, he has no peace of mind.” The reason for that is: parasparyagatam (which has come from the tradition). The idea is: On account of transgressing proper conduct (sad-acara).

Vai has the sense of either prasiddhi (it is well-known) or niscaya (certainly); in this way he makes his firmness in that matter known.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Here he says: “There is a fault in the opposite scenario.” Kamat means kamad adrsta-visayat (out of a desire whose scope is unseen, i.e. future benefits). Dvesat signifies either “because of hating the gods” or “because of hating the worshipers of gods.” Bhayat means “out of fear caused by people who have an opposite point of view.” Lobhai means lobhad drsta-visayat (out of greed whose object is seen). The word va should be added.

The sense of sobhanam napnoti is: iha amutra ca tasya ksemam na syat, “Whether in this world or in the next, he has no peace of mind.” Here the matter should be discerned as follows: The desire of these Vrajavasis to get dharma, artha, and kama and the will to remove that fault only originate from Sri Krsna. Only that is being expounded.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kamat means svecchatah (because of one’s desire). Lobhai means lobhad dravya-vyayabhava-visayat (out of greed whose focus is the absence of the loss of objects). Bhayat means bhayad bhisanaloka-hetukat (out of fear caused by seeing something frightening). Dvesat signifies dvesad devata-visayakat (because of hating the gods).

### 10.24.12

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*vaco nisamya nandasya tathanyesam vrajaukasam \|*  
*indrdya manyum janayan pitaram praha kesavah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah uvaca—Sri Suka said; vacah—the speech; nisamya—after hearing; nandasya—of Nanda; tatha—and; anyesam—of others; vraja-okasam—of the residents of Vraja (“of those whose abode is Vraja”); indrdya—for Indra’s sake; manyum—anger; janayan—in order to produce; pitaram—to His father; praha—speaks (spoke); kesavah—Kesava.

*sri-sukah uvaca—kesavah nandasya vacah nisamya, tatha anyesam vrajaukasam (gopanam ca vacah nisamya), indrdya (indrasya) manyum janayan pitaram praha (sma).*

**Перевод:**

**Sri Suka said: Hearing the discourse of Nanda and of other residents of Vraja, Kesava addressed His father to arouse anger for Indra's sake.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The clause indraya manyum janayan signifies: kopa-janana-dvara garva-parvatad indrani avatarayitum, “to make Indra come down from a mountain of false pride by means of arousing his anger.” This is a rejection of the devata, but it is not the only aim.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

The word tatha has the sense of ca (and), and so tathanyesam means anyesam ca (and of others), insofar as the other Vrajavasis shared Nanda’s opinion. Or tatha means “in that way,” inasmuch as they reiterated the answers that Nanda said.

Thus, in the evening the Lord, who had arrived to the cowherd village, saw the cowherds endeavoring for the sacrifice and inquired from them. It should be known in this way in accordance with the texts in Visnu Purana and Hari-vamsa:

*vimalambara-naksatre kale cabhyagate vraje \|*  
*dadarsendra-maharambha-yodyatams tan vrajaukasah \|\|*

**“In Vraja, at a time when the constellations in the sky were bright, He saw that the residents of the village were laboring diligently for the beginning of a festival in Indra’s honor.” (Visnu Purana 5.10.16)**

*vrajam ajagmatus tau tu vraje susruvatus tada \|*  
*praptam sakram maha-virau gopams cotsava-lalasan \|\|*

**“When the two great heroes arrived at the cowherd village, They heard that the time for a sacrifice to Indra was near and that the cowherd men were eager for a festival.” (Hari-vamsa 2.15.2).**

The words indraya manyum janayan (to arouse Indra’s anger) are said either because of the doctrine of karma (karma-vada), which rejects the devata, or because of the disruption of the fire sacrifice. The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami.

Krsna speaks eminently (praha = prakarsena aha): by demonstrating a firm logic in many ways, and so forth.

The name Kesava means: kah brahma isah rudrah tau vati, “He derides Brahma (ka) and Rudra (isa).” The verbal root is va gati-gandhanayoh (to go, to deride). Or the verbal root is ve\[n\] tantu-santane (to weave): kesau vayate nija-mahimna vyapnoti, “He weaves Brahma and Siva, that is, He encompasses them by His glory.” Or va has the sense of asti (existence): tau prakrsta-sevakataya yasya sthah, “He for whom Brahma and Siva exist as excellent servants,” and so the idea is: He, to whom unlimited gods are subordinate, is rejecting the devata only due to His jovial nature. Or the reason is He intends to crush Indra’s arrogant pride of Indra. Or the drift is Kesava is the presiding deity of Mathura, and so He is rejecting the devata to expand the glory of Govardhana, which is in the district of Mathura.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Regarding tathanyesam vrajaukasam vaco nisamya (hearing the words of other residents of Vraja in that way): The cowherds spoke just like Nanda did either of their own accord or with his expressed approval.

In point of indraya manyum janayan, the gist is he is an outsider and deserves to be disrespected. The implication of pitaram (father) is that Nanda is the highest insider and is most deserving of respect. The name Kesava is derived as: kah brahma isah rudrah tau vayate nija-mahimna vyapnoti, “He pervades (vayate = vyapnoti) Brahma and Siva by His glory.” Sukadeva implies this: Who is miserable Indra compared to Him?

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Indraya manyum stands for indrasya manyum (Indra’s anger). The purpose of arousing Indra’s anger is to break his false pride, to inaugurate a yearly festival in Govardhana, to lift Govardhana, to enjoy the pastime of staying with all His dear ones, and so on. This will be understood later.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

The clause indraya manyum janayan denotes: indram nirgarvayitum tasya manyum janayan (to arouse Indra’s anger in order to make him devoid of overweening pride).

### 10.24.13

*sri-bhagavan uvaca*  
*karmana jayate jantuh karmanaiva niliyate \|*  
*sukham duhkham bhayam ksemam karmanaivabhipadyate \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-bhagavan uvaca—the glorious Lord said; karmana—by karma (the total effect of a person’s actions and conduct); jayate—is born; jantuh—a living entity; karmana—by karma; eva—only; niliyate— dies; sukham—happiness; duhkham—unhappiness; bhayam—fear; ksemam—security; karmana—because of karma; eva—only; abhipadyate—come about.

*sri-bhagavan uvaca—jantuh karmana jayate, karmana eva niliyate (ca), sukham duhkham bhayam ksemam (ca) karmana eva abhipadyate.*

**Перевод:**

**The glorious Lord said: A living entity takes birth by karma and comes to an end only by karma. Happiness, unhappiness, fear and well-being arise only because of karma.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

At the outset He uses the doctrine of karma to reject the gods. If someone were to argue, “How can the results of actions be effected merely by karma, which is inert?”, His response would be, “Ah, the fluttering faith of those who didn’t study Karma-mimamsa philosophy! Given that it’s understood from the texts in that system that karma is the cause of all results, is there anything not brought about by karma?”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Since the doctrine of karma is very well-known everywhere, at first He repudiates His father’s discourse by taking support of it. Karmana chiefly denotes prarabdha karma (karma that has begun to manifest in this life) insofar as only that gives a fixed result. Jantuh means sarvo ’pi jivah (any living entity).

Ksemam (well-being) signifies abhayam (fearlessness). The repeated repetition of karmana (by karma) strengthens the idea that karma is the sole cause. The same idea is reinforced with the two words eva (only).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“Who the heck is Indra to accept the worship of My father and other eternal associates of Mine?” Although dispelling Indra’s pride remains on His mind, still, to enhance the human pastime, at first He, not revealing this motive, repudiates His father’s discourse by referring to the doctrine of karma since it is very well-known everywhere. Ksemam... (The rest is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

While establishing a logical reasoning, given that stopping Indra’s sacrifice should be done only as a human pastime, He rejects the devata by using the doctrine of karma although it is dubbed dubious by sadhus.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

The Karmavadis repudiate the aspect of the devata. This concept is referred to here, because of the statement of Sruti: yatha karo yathacaro tatha bhavati, “As is the doer and as is the conduct, so it becomes.”

It shouldn’t be said, “How can karma, which is inert, be the doer of birth, death, and the rest?”, because doership, although inert, is seen in calati jalam (the water goes), phalati taruh (the tree bears fruit), and so on.

### 10.24.14

*asti ced isvarah kascit phala-rupy anya-karmanam \|*  
*kartaram bhajate so ’pi nahy akartuh prabhur hi sah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

asti—there is; cet—if; isvarah—who is a god; kascit—some \[living entity\]; phala—the results; rupi—who fashions (gives); anya—\[done\] by others (done by anyone except himself); karmanam—of actions (or of sacrificial rites); kartaram—the doer \[of an action\]; bhajate—serves (follows); sah—he; api—even; nahi—not (never); akartuh prabhuh—the master of one who is not a doer (or one who is able as regards one who is not a doer); hi—because; sah—he.

*kascid (jivah) anya-karmanam phala-rupi isvarah asti cet, (tarhi) sah api (isvarah karmapeksah san) kartaram (eva) bhajate, hi sah (isvarah) akartuh (janasya phala-dane) prabhuh nahi (bhavet).*

**Перевод:**

**If there is some supreme ruler who gives the results of others’ actions, he too rewards or punishes only the doer. Indeed, he has no authority over him who does nothing.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Some persons, alarmed by the excessive boldness of Karmavadis, posit a god dependent on karma. After explaining their opinion, with asti cet:, “Himself unsmeared by actions, the giver of the results (phala-rupi = phala-data) of the actions of other beings serves the doer by giving the results,” He repudiates it.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Phala-rupi denotes: phalam rupayitum darsayitum datum silam asya iti phala-rupi, “His natural propensity is to show, that is, to give, the result.” Bhajate means anusarati (he follows), on account of giving a result only in accordance with the action. He strengthens that with a contrast. The sense is: “because (hi = yatah) if there is no action, he is unable to give a result.” The second hi means niscitam (indeed).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“How can the results of actions be effected merely by karma, which is inert? A god who awards the results of actions is necessarily required.” He responds to that with asti cet and so on: “If there is a giver of the results of actions done by others (anya-karmanam phala-rupi = anya-krt-karmanam phala-data), even he follows (bhajate = anusarati) the doer—on account of giving a result only in accordance with the action; He strengthens that with a contrast—because (hi = yatah) if there is no action, he is unable to give the intended result (nahy akartuh prabhuh sah = karmabhave phalam datum na saktah).”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Those who follow the custom, thinking that Indra and others are independent in the matter of giving the result of an action, worship them with karmas (sacrificial rites). In two verses, while saying, to teach those persons, that Indra and others cannot be the givers of the result of karma by a complete disregard of the Lord, He implies that the Lord is the giver of the result of a rite: “If some soul (kascid = kascid jivah) is the god that gives the result of actions of others... ”

### 10.24.15

*kim indreneha bhutanam sva-sva-karmanuvartinam \|*  
*anisenanyatha kartum svabhava-vihitam nrnam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

kim indrena—what is the use of Indra?; iha—here; bhutanam—of living entities; sva-sva-karma—their respective karma; anuvartinam—who are following; amsena—\[Indra\] who is not able (or who is not God); anyatha—another way; kartum—to make; svabhava—by the natures (by conditioned propensities); vihitam— \[karma\] which is determined; nrnam—of men.

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

*sva-sva-karmanuvartinam bhutanam iha nrnam svabhava-vihitam (karma tad-adhinam sukha-duhkhadikam ca) anyatha kartum amsena indrena kim (prayojanam siddhyati? na kim api).*

**What is the use of Indra in this matter? The karma, determined by the nature, of human beings, who follow their respective karma, cannot be changed by him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Therefore, since only karma effects the result and since the devata is like the nipples on a goat’s neck given that he is dependent on karma, a result cannot be effected by a devata.

Someone might argue: “The flow of karma depends only on Paramatma.157How can there be no use of a devata in every way?” Expecting this He says: anisenanyatha kartum svabhava-vihitam, which means: svabhavena praktana-samskarenaiva vihitam yat karma tad anyathakartum amsena, “Karma, determined by the nature, i.e. only by previous samskaras (subconscious tendencies), cannot be changed by one who is not God (or by Indra, who is incapable).”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“of beings, who follow their respective karma.” This is said by the axiom: nabhuktam ksiyate karma, “Karma that is not experienced does not go away,” and because prarabdha karma must necessarily be experienced. The significance of nrnam (of humans) is: “although they are able to surpass the nature by thinking deeply,” so what need be said about other beings?

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“What is the use of Indra to living beings, since only karma is the cause of experiencing happiness, unhappiness, and the rest? In the case of humans too, who are among them (nrnam = tesu nrnam ca), what is the use of him? He is unable (anisena =amsena tena kim) to change their respective karma, determined by the nature (svam svam svabhava-vihitam),”158inasmuch as only the nature is the cause of giving the impulse to those various karmas.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

A result cannot be effected by a devata. Someone might argue: “The flow of karma depends only on Paramatma. How can there be no use of a devata in every way?” Expecting this He says: anisenanyatha kartum svabhava-vihitam. The sense is: “Paramatma, no other, impels a soul to do only that work which is determined by previous samskaras, meaning the work is established as one’s duty, hence what good result is to be achieved by means of praiseworthy Indra, who is unable to change karma? No good result at all.”

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

“Therefore what purpose is accomplished by Indra, who is unable (nisena = asamarthena) to change (anyatha kartum = viparivartayitum) the karma, caused to be done only by past experiences (svabhava-vihitam = purva-samskarena eva karitam), of humans in this world (iha = loke), who are beings that follow their respective karma?”

### 10.24.16

*svabhava-tantro hi janah svabhavam anuvartate \|*  
*svabhava-stham idam sarvam sa-devasura-manusam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

svabhava—of the nature; tantrah—under the control; hi—indeed (or only); janah—a person; svabhavam—his nature; anuvartate—he follows; svabhava-stham—is based on Svabhava; idam—this world; sarvam—whole; sa—along with; deva—gods; asura—demons; manusam—and humans.

*janah (svasya) svabhava-tantrah hi (bhavati), (atah janah) svabhavam anuvartate, (atah) sa-devasura-manusam idam sarvam svabhava- stham (bhavati).*

**Перевод:**

**Indeed, every individual is under the control of the nature and hence follows his or her nature. This entire universe, with all its gods, devils, and humans, is based on Svabhava.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He expounds. The sense is: pravrtteh samskaradhinatvat kim antaryamina, “Because the flow of karma is under the control of samskara (subconscious impressions),159what is the use of Paramatma?”160

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

The separate mention of the gods, demons, and humans, who are already included by the word sarvam, is like the separate mention of nrnam in the previous verse.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The separate mention of the gods, demons, and humans, who are already included by the word sarvam, occurs because they are unable to surpass their nature, even when there is an introspection and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“A person is under the control of previous samskaras (svabhava-tantrah = praktana-samskaradhinah). Therefore a person has a life based on his or her nature (svabhavam anu = svabhavam laksi-krtya)." This means people impel themselves in various activities corresponding to their nature. The gist is: What good result is to be achieved by means of Paramatma even? Nothing at all.

**Annotation**

In reference to the cosmos, the term Svabhava (nature) has two meanings: (1) The nature of things, and (2) A certain instrumental cause of Maya: At the beginning of Creation, time agitates the three gunas, which are transformed by Svabhava. Then, mahat-tattva arises, impelled by Karma (Bhagavatam 2.5.22). Jiva Gosvami says Time, fate, Karma, and Svabhava are instrumental causes (nimitta) of Maya (Paramatma-sandarbha 53).

### 10.24.17

*dehan uccavacan jantuh prapyotsrjati karmana \|*  
*satrur mitram udasinah karmaiva gurur isvarah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

dehan—bodies; ucca-avacan—high and low; jantuh—a living entity; prapya—after obtaining; utsrjati—gives up; karmana—by karma; satruh—an enemy; mitram—a friend; udasinah—an indifferent person; karma—karma; eva—only; guruh—a teacher; isvarah—a god (or a god).

*jantuh karmana uccavacan dehan prapya (karma-samaptau tan dehan) utsrjati. (tatha) satruh mitram udasinah (iti tray am) karma eva (bhavati, evam) guruh isvarah (ca karma eva bhavati).*

**Перевод:**

**A living entity obtains and gives up high-quality bodies and low-quality bodies only because of karma. Foes, friends, neutrals, teachers and gods are just karma.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The words beginning from dehan make one verse of six lines.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Prapyotsrjati denotes: prapnoti tyajati ca, “One obtains and one rejects.” “Even an enemy, as well as a friend and so on, is only karma,” because the same person sometimes shows enmity, sometimes shows friendship, and sometimes shows indifference. Such a lack of fixity is only caused by diverse karma. The sense is: Owing to the nondifference between a cause and its effect, they are only karma (they are caused to be such by karma). Someone might argue: “Given that without knowledge there is no question of engaging in actions, a teacher is necessarily required for the sake of imparting knowledge.” He responds: guruh (teacher), insofar as there is no instruction without merit (adrsta) and also because, even when there is a gain of knowledge, of the noneffectuation of its fruit without it.161

“Since karma is inert, a capable giver of the result of an action is required.” In that regard He says: isvarah (a god), since even an Isvara follows karma; it is that powerful.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

Jantuh means jivah (soul). “Enemies and so on are only karma” means they were made by karma. Isvarah signifies Indra and others: The idea is even the state of being Isvara was done by karma.

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

The word isvara is said on account of a connection with aisvarya (godly might).

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

Foes, friends, and indifferent persons are just karma because they are involved with one’s bad karma, good karma, and mixed karma. Teachers and gods are only karma since their mercy depends on merit (punya-karma).

### 10.24.18

*tasmat sampujayet karma svabhava-sthah sva-karma-krt \|*  
*anjasa yena varteta tad evasya hi daivatam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tasmat—therefore; sampujayet—one should revere; karma—work; svabhava—in one’s nature \[as a brahmana and so on\]; sthah— \[being\] situated; sva-karma—his own work; krt—\[while\] performing; ahjasa—truly (happily); yena—by which; varteta—one can remain (one can live); tat—that; eva—only; asya—of this \[individual\]; hi—because; daivatam—is a deity.

*tasmad (janah svasya) karma (eva) sampujayet. (janah svasya) svabhava-sthah (san) sva-karma-krt (bhavet), hi yena (karmana yah janah) anjasa varteta, tad eva (karma) asya (janasya) daivatam (sevyam asti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Therefore, abiding in one’s nature and doing one’s work, a person should revere work, since only that by means of which one lives happily is one’s deity.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Therefore (tasmat), that is, because karma, which is effected from the nature, is the cause of all, only work (karma) should be worshiped.” Pujayet (one should worship) means sammanayet (one should revere).

Someone could argue: “How can there be the accomplishment of a rite (karma) without a devata, since a rite consists of relinquishing objects in the fire by mentioning the name of a devata?" Expecting this, with anjasa and so on He, as if summarizing the proposition: “A devata is merely an aspect of a rite,” refers to the theory of causality (hetu-vada) and makes another kind of deity worthy.162

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“Given that only the nature impels another work and only work gives a result, therefore one should revere work, because (hi = yatah) that by which one happily (anjasa = sukha-purvakam) subsists is the deity of this person.”

Or the reason for sampujayet (one should revere) is: svabhava-sthah, “one is under the control of subconscious tendencies” (=samskaradhinah).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Although work in general is worthy of being revered, in the matter of doing a specific work only the scriptures are the authority. That is what He says, “Situated in a caste such as the Brahmana caste (svabhava-sthah - brahmanadi-varna-sthah), one does the work ordained in that (sva-karma-krt =sva-sva-vihitam karma karoti iti sah)." (The rest of the commentary is the same as Bhavartha-dipika.)

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

“Therefore, situated in a caste such as Brahmana and habitually performing the work respectively ordained (sva-karma-krt = sva-sva-karmanusthayi), one should accept (sampujayet = svikuryat) work,” but one should not also accept a devata.

“That by means of which work (yena = yena karmana)—such as begging, conquering, agriculture, service—one easily lives (anjasa varteta = anayasena jiveta) is one’s deity.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“Because only karma is the cause of happiness, unhappiness, and so forth, therefore (tasmat) a man, abiding in his nature and doing his work, that is, having the habit of doing a work in conformity with his nature, should highly esteem (sampujayet = bahu manyeta) work.

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

Yena means yena eva upayena prakarena, “only that by means of which.”

**Annotation**

As shown above, yena signifies either yena karmana (by means of which work) or yena upayena (by means of which), but in light of the rest of the chapter, starting from verse 25, where Krsna favors the worship of Govardhana, not the worship of their occupation as Vaisyas, yena means yena daivatena (because of which deity) and the verse means: “Only that deity because of whom one can live happily is one’s deity.”

### 10.24.19

*ajivyaikataram bhdvam yas tv anyam upajivati \|*  
*na tasmad vindate ksemam jaramnary asati yatha \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

ajivya—while subsisting; ekataram—on one (out of two or out of many); bhdvam—thing (or activity: see the footnote below); yah—who; tu—but; anyam—another; upajivati—resorts to; na— not; tasmat—from that \[other thing\]; vindate—\[a person\] obtains; ksemam—peace of mind; jaram—\[after meeting\] a paramour (“because of whom one grows old”); nari—a woman; asati— unchaste; yatha—just as.

*yatha asati nari jaram (upasevya sukham na apnoti, tatha) yah tu (janah) ekataram bhdvam ajivya anyam upajivati, (sah) tasmat ksemam na vindate.*

**Перевод:**

**“A person who adopts one livelihood but then takes to another does not attain peace of mind, like an unchaste woman who consorts with her paramour.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He mentions the fault in the other scenario simply on the strength on logical reasoning. Upajivati means sevate (one serves, takes to).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

(The commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Having made one thing the means of living, one who enjoys happiness from another means does not gain happiness, or auspiciousness (ksemam = sukham mangalam va), because of that,” or else “from that other means”.

The substance is: “Consequently, our worship of cows, our means of living, and of Sri Govardhana, on which they depend, should be carried out.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Tasmat means “from that other means.” In the example, the ablative case in jarat (from a paramour) matches tasmat. Sometimes the reading is jaram. The purport is the same.

His very great impudence toward His father and others should be understood only as anger which originates from their worship of a low person.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Resorting to the notion, from the power of logical reasoning, that only the means of living is the devata, He mentions the fault in the counterproposition. “One who, depending on one thing for a living, takes support of another such as Indra does not get well-being from it,” because of being ungrateful.

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

“One who takes support (ajivya =asritya) of a primary (ekataram = mukhyam) god (bhavam – bhdvam devadi-rupam)164but serves another, a secondary one (anyam = gaunam), does not achieve well-being from that secondary one (tasmat = gaunat)."

### 10.24.20

*varteta brahmana vipro rajanyo raksaya bhuvah \|*  
*vaisyas tu vartaya jivec chudras tu dvija-sevaya \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

varteta—should abide; brahmana—by means of the Veda; viprah—a Brahmana; rajanyah—a Ksatriya (“a member of the royal order”); raksaya—by means of the protection; bhuvah—of the Earth; vaisyah—a Vaisya; tu—however; vartaya—by means of a vocation (in one sense the word varta is specifically related to the occupations of Vaisyas); jivet—should live; sudrah—a Sudra; tu—but (or and); dvija-sevaya—by serving twice-born persons.

*viprah brahmana varteta. (evam) rajanyah bhuvah raksaya (varteta). vaisyah tu vartaya jivet. sudrah tu dvija-sevaya (jivet).*

**Перевод:**

**“A Brahmana should live by means of the Vedas, a Ksatriya by protecting the Earth, a Vaisya by varta, and a Sudra by serving the twice-born.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He talks about the varieties of occupations of castes as an example in order to mention the cowherds’ own occupation in the next verse. Brahmana means vedadhyapanadina (by teaching the Vedas, and so on).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Now, to refute Nanda’s words: “To achieve dharma, artha, and kama, people sustain their lives with the remnants of that fire sacrifice. Parjanya engenders the results of human endeavors” (Bhagavatam 10.24.10), at first, to nicely establish only the worship of their own livelihood, in two verses He mentions their own occupation of tending cows.

Although the word dvija refers to those in the three higher castes, it primarily denotes Brahmanas because they are the most important. Or dvija means those in the three higher castes.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Now, to establish only the worship of their own livelihood that is a work, at first He mentions their own occupation of tending cows.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In order to say: “Therefore our livelihood is our deity,” He talks about the livelihood of others too as an example.

Only the Vedic scriptures are a Brahmana’s deities. In reference to raksaya bhuvah (by protecting the Earth), only the Earth is a Ksatriya’s only deity. In point of vartaya (with a vocation), only varta is a Vaisya’s deity. Dvija-sevaya means dvija-susrusaya (with a desire to serve the twice-born), and so only the twice-born are a Sudra’s deities.

### 10.24.21

*krsi-vanijya-go-raksa kusidam turyam ucyate \|*  
*varta catur-vidha tatra vayam go-vrttayo ’nisam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

krsi—agriculture; vanijya—commerce; go-raksa—maintaining cows; kusidam—usury (lending money, animals, or things); turyam—the fourth; ucyate—is said; vdrtd—occupation; catur-vidha—fourfold; tatra—among those; vayam—we; go-vrttayah—whose occupation is cow \[protection\]; anisam—always.

*krsi-vanijya-go-raksa (iti trayam bhavati), kusidam turyam (bhavati, evam) varta catur-vidha ucyate, tatra vayam go-vrttayah anisam (bhavamah).*

**Перевод:**

**“The vocation for Vaisyas is said to be fourfold: agriculture, business, cow protection, and usury. Of these, cow protection has always been our occupation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He says the occupations of Vaisyas are fourfold. Krsi-vanijya-go-raksa signifies: krsi-vanijya-sahita go-raksa, “cow protection, along with agriculture and business,” thus there are three. Kusidam, which means vrddhi-jivanam (“living on an increase”; charges for loans), is the fourth.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Though usury (kusidam) is forbidden, by the statement: varddhyusir narakam yati, “A usurer goes to hell,” still, because it is ordained for Vaisyas, that statement is for those who charge an interest rate that is more than customary. Or this statement relates to Brahmanas who engage in the occupations of Vaisyas out of emergency.

Concerning anisam (always): “Because we never had another occupation, only cows are forever our livelihood. By tending cows, dharma, artha, and kama will automatically be accomplished.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The gist of anisam is this: “Because, although we are Vaisyas, we do not resort to agriculture, business or usury.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Go-vrttayah means: go-raksana-vrttayah (we whose occupation is cow protection). Regarding anisam (always): “Even in hard times, we never engaged in agriculture and so on, thus only cows should be worshiped, on account of being our deities.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Varta means vrttih (occupation). Tatra signifies tasu (of those occupations).

### 10.24.22

*sattvam rajas tama iti sthity-utpatty-anta-hetavah \|*  
*rajasotpadyate visvam anyonyam vividham jagat \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sattvam—the mode of goodness; rajas—the mode of action / passion; tamas—the mode of ignorance; iti—as such; sthiti—of maintenance; utpatti—creation; anta—and destruction; hetavah—the causes; rajasa—by the agency of rajo-guna; utpadyate—is generated; visvam—the universe; anyonyam—through mutual \[interaction\]; vividham—multifarious; jagat—the universe.

*sattvam rajah tamah iti (trayah gunah yatha-kramam jagatah) sthity-utpatty-anta-hetavah (bhavanti), visvam rajasa (gunena) utpadyate, jagad anyonyam vividham (bhavati).*

**Перевод:**

**“Sattva, rajas, and tamas are the causes of continuation, creation, and destruction. The universe arises by the agency of rajas. Through mutual interactions the world becomes multifarious.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Even the occupation of tending cows is dependent on the great Indra.” Expecting this argument, with two verses He rejects it by taking support of the opinion of Sankhya philosophers, who are atheistic. Anyonyam (mutual) means stri-purusa-yogena (by the union of male and female).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

(The commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

With two verses He refutes te 'bhivarsanti and so on: “His lordship Indra is the god of rain. Clouds are dear forms of his. They rain water, which pleases beings and sustains life” (10.24.8).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

It should be understood that sattva is the cause of sthiti, etc., only because of Svabhava (Bhagavatam 2.5.22-23).

### 10.24.23

*rajasa codita megha varsanty ambuni sarvatah \|*  
*prajas tair eva sidhyantimahendrah kim karisyati \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

rajasa—by rajo-guna; coditah—impelled; meghah—clouds; varsanti—rain; ambuni—water; sarvatah—everywhere; prajdh—living beings; taih—because of them; eva—only; sidhyanti—succeed (live); maha-indrah—the great Indra; kim—what?; karisyati—will do.

*meghah rajasa coditah (santah) sarvatah ambuni varsanti. prajdh taih eva (meghaih) sidhyanti. (evam sati) mahendrah kim karisyati?*

**Перевод:**

**“Impelled by rajas, clouds rain water everywhere. Living beings flourish only because of them. What can the great Indra do?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Sarvatah (everywhere) is said on account of seeing rain go even on oceans, rocks, and salty barren land. The idea is: If rain were made by Indra by using his intelligence, rain would fall on the lands of his worshipers, not just everywhere. “Living beings live only because of clouds (tair eva sidhyanti = meghaih eva jivanti).”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

(The commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

He says mahendrah (great Indra) deridingly since clouds and Indra are under the control of rajas.

### 10.24.24

*na nah puro janapada na grama na grha vayam \|*  
*vanaukasas tata nityam vana-saila-nivasinah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—not; nah—our; purah—towns; janapadah—lands; na—not; gramah—villages; na—not; grhah—houses; vayam—we; vana-okasah—forest dwellers (“they whose domicile is the forest”); tata—(used for expressing a tender vocative); nityam—constantly; vana—in forests; saila—and in hills; nivasinah—they who live.

*tata! nah purah na (santi, na ca nah) janapadah (santi), na (ca nah) gramah (santi), na (api nah) grhah (santi, yatah) vayam vanaukasah vana-saila-nivasinah (smah).*

**Перевод:**

**“Father, we have neither towns, territories, villages, or houses. We forest dwellers always reside in the woodland and on hills.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

In case Nanda were to respond: “Still, a devata is required for the sake of gain and preservation,” He speaks the above. Purah means pattanam (towns). Janapadah means desah (territories). The idea is: “Our cause of gain and preservation is only woodland, hills, and the like.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Vayam vanaukasah signifies: vanani eva okamsi grhah yesam tatha-bhutah jatya eva vayam, “we whose homes are only the forests, only by caste—therefore we are not going anywhere.” That is what He says with nityam. With the vocative tata, He makes him melt. Thus, it’s implied that He also resides near Govardhana.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The derivation of Govardhana is being perceived: gah vardhayati iti govardhanah (It makes cows increase, and so it is called Govardhana). The occupation of tending cows is dependent on Govardhana, hence Govardhana should be worshiped. He says this in two verses. They are forest dwellers insofar as they graze cows.

### 10.24.25

*tasmad gavam brahmananam adres carabhyatam makhah \|*  
*ya indra-yaga-sambharas tair ayam sadhyatam makhah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tasmat—therefore; gavam—for cows; brahmananam—for Brahmanas; adreh—for the mountain (Govardhana); ca—and; arabhyatam makhah—may the sacrifice begin; ye—which \[ingredients\]; indra-yaga—for the sacrifice to Indra; sambharah—ingredients (paraphernalia); taih—with them; ayam—this; sadhyatam—should be accomplished; makhah—sacrifice.

*tasmad gavam brahmananam adreh ca makhah arabhyatam. ye indra-yaga-sambharah (santi), ayam makhah taih (sambharaih) sadhyatam.*

**Перевод:**

**“Therefore let a fire sacrifice for cows, for Brahmanas, and for the hill begin! This sacrifice should be accomplished with the paraphernalia for Indra’s worship.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Sambharah signifies sadhanani (means of accomplishing).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

He includes the Brahmanas because He is brahmanya-deva (God favorable to Brahmanas, otherwise there might be the hypothesis that even they, like the gods, do not deserve to be worshiped. Another reason is that a fire sacrifice cannot be done without them.

The hill is Sri Govardhana. Not stating its name is because only it is very well-known in that matter. Or, only Govardhana is to understood due to being very close-by.

“The fire sacrifice should be accomplished with those same things.” He says this also to arouse Indra’s anger even more.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Tasmat (therefore) denotes ajivyatvat (because of being a means of living). Of the three, not mentioning the Brahmanas at first is because they, like the cows, are a means of living for everyone in a general way. For instance, Manu said:

*uttamangodbhavaj jyesthyad brahmanas caiva dharanat \|*  
*sarvasyaivasya sargasya dharmato brahmanah prabhuh \|\|*

**“Because of dharma, because of being senior, because of originating from a higher limb of the Universal Form, and because of upholding the Vedas, a Brahmana is the master of this entire Creation.” (Manu-samhita 1.93)**

This one sacrifice consists of the worship of three devatas. A forest is not in the enumeration, though it was being expressed as a means of living, because there is no renown of it being a devata. Optionally, it is because here only the hill is foremost. For example, in Skanda Purana: aho vrndavanam ramyam yatra govardhano girih, “How wonderful, charming Vrndavana is where the great Govardhana is.” Moreover, He will reveal its glory, with: krsnas tv anyatamam rupam, “Krsna, however, assumed another form” etc. (10.24.35), by showing a nondifference between Govardhana and Himself.

Although there are many hills in the land of Sri Vrndavana, such as Nandisvara, Astakuta, Varasanu, Dhavalagiri, and Saugandhika, nonetheless here the hill is only Sri Govardhana for these reasons:

The etymology of its name;

By counting it in the fifth among the chief mountain ranges,166only it is primary among those hills, the svarupas of His feet;

The renown, in the world and in the scriptures, of the worship only of it;

Later He will lift only it, which was worshiped, and

The renown of anna-kuta.

Not stating its name is because it is very close-by and because it is a principal place in Vraja.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“The blessings of Brahmanas are our directly perceptible results, and so Brahmanas too should be worshiped.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Sambharah means samagryah (multiple paraphernalia).

### 10.24.26

*pacyantam vividhah pakah supantah payasadayah \|*  
*samyavapupa-saskulyah sarva-dohas ca grhyatam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

pacyantam—should be cooked (prepared); vividhah—manifold; pakah—cooked foods; supa-antah—at whose end there are soups; payasa-adayah—at whose beginning there is sweet rice (or products made with milk); samyava—cakes (or cream of wheat); apupa— cakes (malpuwa)167; saskulyah—and cakes (saskuli: round cakes made from rice flour, sesame and sugar, and fried); sarva—of all \[the cows\]; dohah—the milk; ca—and; grhyatam—should be collected.

*vividhah pakah payasadayah supantah pacyantam. samyavapupa-saskulyah (pacyantam). sarva-dohah ca grhyatam.*

**Перевод:**

**“Different kinds of food should be cooked, from sweet rice to soups. Samyava, apupa, saskuli, and other fried cakes should be prepared. All the milk should be brought.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Supa signifies bean soup. Payasa is rice cooked only in milk. Samvaya and other foods are variations of wheat.168

Sweet rice should be cooked first and soups should be cooked last. The sense is: Once the desired quantity of milk is on the heat to make sweet rice, the remaining milk can be used for other things.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“This sacrifice should be even more special than a sacrifice for Indra.” With this in mind, in four verses He dictates the details of its procedure. Pakah means pacaniyah (foods to be cooked): This denotes rice, vegetables, and so forth. The separate mention of samyava, apupa, and saskuli, though they are included by the word adi in payasadayah (sweet rice and so on), is because an abundance of those preparations is required.

By the derivation duhyate (it is milked), dohah means dugdham (milk). Sarva-dohah means either all the milk, the milk of all the animals, or the milk of the entire cowherd village.” For example:

*tatra hatva pasun medhyan vitatyayatane subhe \|*  
*sarva-ghosasya sandohah kriyatam kim vicaryate \|\|*

**“Krsna addressed the cowherds: There, after killing animals fit for sacrifice, and when the altar will be splendid, once expanded, the milk of the entire village should be collected. What do you think?” (Hari-vamsa 2.16.12)**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The first paragraph is the same.) “This sacrifice should be even more special than a sacrifice for Indra.” With this in mind, in four verses He dictates the details of its procedure. Pakah means pacaniyah (foods that are to be cooked): This denotes rice, vegetables, and so forth.

Supa means supah (soups), that is, vyanjanani (vegetables; veg stew). The separate mention of samyava, apupa, and saskuli, though they are included by the word adi in payasadayah (sweet rice and so on), is because an abundance of those preparations is required. That is why He says “all the milk.” For instance, in Hari-vamsa (2.17.14): tri-ratram caiva sandohah sarva-ghosasya grhyatam, “Also, the milk of the entire village should be accumulated for three nights.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Pakah (cooked foods) denotes rice, vegetables, and so on. The sense of “Sweet rice should be cooked first and soups last” is: soups should be served warm and sweet rice cool.

### 10.24.27

*huyantam agnayah samyag-brahmanair brahma-vadibhih \|*  
*annam bahu-gunam tebhyo deyam vo dhenu-daksinah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

huyantam—should be offered oblations; agnayah—the fires; samyak—proper (or properly); brahmanaih—by Brahmanas; brahma-vadibhih—who have the habit of expounding the Vedas; annam—food; bahu-gunam—which has many good qualities; tebhyah—to them; deyam—should be offered; vah—by all of you; dhenu-daksinah—cows and other gifts as remuneration.

*agnayah samyag-brahma-vadibhih brahmanaih huyantam. (tatah) vah tebhyah (brahmanebhyah) bahu-gunam annam deyam (asti. vah) dhenu-daksinah (ca deyah bhavanti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Suitable Brahmanas, learned in Vedic mantras, shall offer oblations into the sacrificial fires. Afterward all of you should provide them with high-quality food and remunerate them with cows and other gifts.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He speaks for the sake of the splendor of the sacrifice and to increase faith. Dhenu-daksinah means either dhenu-sahitah daksinah (charity, along with cows) or dhenavah eva daksinah (cows as charity). Vah signifies yusmabhih (by all of you).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

The Brahmanas are devoted to reciting the Vedas (brahma-vadibhih = vedabhyasa-paraih). Or samyag-brahmanaih is one word (by proper Brahmanas). The sense is: “by Vaisnava Brahmanas.” The pluralilty of fires is in consideration of the three fires, beginning with garhapatya.169Or the plural is used out of high regard due to a multitude of acts of oblations.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions in this paragraph are underlined.) In this verse He gives directions for the sequence. The Brahmanas are devoted to reciting the Vedas (brahma-vadibhih = vedabhyasa-paraih)." Or samyag-brahmanaih (by proper Brahmanas) is one word. The sense is: “by Vaisnava Brahmanas.”

The plurality of in agnayah (fires) is used in consideration of the two fires, beginning with garhapatya, and because of the daksina fire, in consideration of killing Raksasas, etc., there. Regarding bahu-gunam (food of many qualities), optionally the reading is bahu-vidham (‘of many varieties’, Sridhara Svami’s reading).

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Bahu-gunam means sad-rasopetam (food that has the six tastes).

### 10.24.28

*anyebhyas ca sva-candala-patitebhyo yatharhatah \|*  
*yavasam ca gavam dattva giraye diyatam balih \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

anyebhyah—to the others; ca—and; a170sva-candala—including dogs and outcastes; patitebhyah—to fallen living entities; yatha-arhatah—as is proper (“according to who is deserving”); yavasam—grass; ca—and; gavam—to the cows; dattva—having given; giraye—to the mountain; diyatam—should be offered; balih—offerings.

*(annadikam) anyebhyah ca a sva-candala-patitebhyah (ca) yatharhatah (deyam asti. tatah yusmabhih) gavam yavasam ca dattva balih giraye diyatam.*

**Перевод:**

**“Food and drink should also be given to everyone else and to fallen living entities, such as dogs and outcastes, as deemed proper. After also giving grass to cows, you should present the offerings to the mountain.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Yavasam means trnam (grass).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The words annadikam deyam need to be added: “Food and so on should be given to others,” that is, to Brahmanas who were not the priests, to Vaisnavas, to the poor, and to beggars. What is the use of mentioning them at all? Everyone is meant, including the dogs (a sva-candala-patitebhyah =svadin abhivyapya eva). The sense of yatharhatah is yatha-yogyam deyam (it should be given according to the suitability). The idea is: only Indra is excluded. Gavam should read gobhyah (to cows). Balih means gandha-puspady-upacarah (articles for a formal worship, such as scents and flowers).

### 10.24.29

*svalankrta bhuktavantah svanuliptah suvasasah \|*  
*pradaksinam ca kuruta go-vipranala-parvatan \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

su-alankrtah—beautifully adorned; bhuktavantah—who have eaten; su-anuliptah—nicely anointed; su-vasasah—nicely dressed; pradaksinam—circumambulation; ca—and; kuruta—all of you should perform; go—of the cows; vipra—the Brahmanas; anala—the sacrificial fires; parvatan—and the mountain.

*(yuyam) svalankrtah bhuktavantah svanuliptah suvasasah ca (santah) go-vipranala-parvatan pradaksinam kuruta.*

**Перевод:**

**“Nicely adorned after eating, artistically anointed, and decently dressed, you should circumambulate the cows, the Brahmanas, the sacrificial fires and the mountain, keeping them to your right.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Afterward, being nicely adorned (svalahkrtah = susthu alankrtah) and having eaten their leftovers (bhuktavantah = tac-chesam bhuktavantah ca santah)..." There is another explanation: “It is not that this is to be brought about with difficulty, as in the case of other things that have to be done, rather only a blissful festival should take place,” and so with svalahkrtah and so forth He emphasizes a special priti (bliss; love). Not mentioning the word su in bhuktavantah, unlike in the words before and after, is due to the existence of that niceness automatically given that they mostly consume cow’s milk at other times too.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

By rule, circumambulating the cows and so forth is only done one time. A circumambulation should be done at the end of a worship. Consequently the circumambulation of the mountain will be mentioned separately: go-dhanani puraskrtya girim cakruh pradaksinam, “They circumambulated the mountain after placing the cows in front” (10.24.33).

Regarding svalankrtah and so on: This is not something special. Even in the absence of a circumambulation they are nicely adorned and so on, even though they don’t desire it. Therefore the circumambulation of cows, etc., happened before eating. However, the circumambulation of the mountain occurred after that.

Morever, there was a worship of cows, but not a worship of all the cows, since they are innumerable. Only the puja of the main ones was done. Thus, there was also only a small circumambulation of those cows.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The circumambulation of Sri Govardhana occurred after the worship and circumambulation of those ones and after eating, on account of the separate statement: go-dhanani puraskrtya (10.24.33).

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

Bhuktavantah means krta-bhojanah (they who have eaten).

### 10.24.30

*etau mama matam tato kriyatam yadi rocate \|*  
*ayam go-brahmanadrinam mahyam ca dayito makhah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

etat—this; mama—My; matam—idea; tata—(a vocative used for expressing endearment); kriyatam—may it be done; yadi—if; rocate—it is pleasing; ayam—this; go-brahmana-adrinam—for the cows, the Brahmanas, and the mountain; mahyam—to Me; ca—and; dayitah—is dear; makhah—sacrifice.

*tata! etad mama matam (bhavati, atah) yadi (etad bhavadbhyah) rocate, (tarhi) ayam go-brahmanadrinam makhah kriyatam. (ayam makhah) mahyam ca dayitah (abhavisyad iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Such is My idea, father. This sacrifice for cows, Brahmanas, and the hill can be done if you like. It would be pleasing to Me too.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He says go-brahmanadrinam (for cows, Brahmanas, and the hill) to make everyone approve by nodding the head. Mahyam ca means mama ca (to Me too).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

The hidden intention in the vocative tata is: “If you have affection for Me, your son, then it should be done.” Yadi rocate (if you like) is said because that is the way to talk to venerable persons. With that special humility He implies: It must be done.

Additionally: “This sacrifice for cows, Brahmanas and the hill is pleasing for Me too (mahyam ca dayitah = mama ca priyah)."

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) The hidden intention in the vocative tata is: “If you have affection for Me, your son, then it should be done.” Yadi rocate (if you like) is said because that is the way to talk to venerable persons. With that special humility He ensures that the sacrifice will be performed.

Additionally: “This sacrifice for cows, Brahmanas and the hill is beneficial (dayitah = hitah) for Me too.” The dative case in mahvam is used only in the sense of a connection with the meaning of hita.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Mahyam stands for mama (to Me). Dayitah means hitah (beneficial).

### 10.24.31

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*kalatmana bhagavata sakra-darpa-jighamsaya \|*  
*proktam nisamya nandadyah sadhv agrhnanta tad vacah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah uvaca—Sri Suka said; kala-atmana—who is the soul of Time; bhagavata—by the Lord; sakra—of Indra (“the mighty one”); darpa—the pride; jighamsaya—out of a desire to destroy; proktani— \[the speech\] that was said; nisamya—after hearing; nanda-adyah—Nanda and so on; Sadhu—correctly (respectfully); agrhnanta—accepted; tat vacah—that speech (or tad-vacah—His speech).

*sri-sukah uvaca—nandadyah sakra-darpa-jighamsaya kalatmana bhagavata proktani (vacah) nisamya tad vacah sadhu agrhnanta.*

**Перевод:**

**Sri Suka said: The Lord, the soul of Time, had spoken with the intent to crush Sakra’s pride. Having heard the details, Nanda and the others acknowledged that good discourse.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Kalatmana means: “by Him, who impels Time too” (= kalasya api atmana pravartakena). The fact that everyone is subject to it is implied. This is the reason for accepting His speech. Or the idea that He has the topmost power is implied, and so the idea is: Removing Indra’s pride is a petty deed for Him.
