Or, the gist is: When a sacrifice for Indra was begun, it was only begun, and now only this is taking place, hence everything happens by His desire, so who is able to transgress His will?

Another interpretation of kalatmana is: kalah syamalah atma dehah yasya, “by Him, whose body is dark blue.” This means: “by Syamasundara.” The tenor is: Everyone was made submissive by His beauty, not to mention that they were charmed by His words. Alternatively: kalayati jagac-cittam akarsati iti kalah atma svabhavah yasya, “by Him, whose nature attracts the hearts of all.” The idea is: This acceptance of His statements is not surprising.

He had spoken with the desire to crush Indra’s pride. That pride consisted of being disrespectful by viewing Nanda and others as material cowherds and Krsna as a mortal. His pride will be described in the next chapter:

*aho sri-mada-mahatmyam gopanam kananaukasam \|*  
*krsnam martyam upasritya ye cakrur deva-helanam \|\|*

**“Ha! The cowherds, who live in the woodland, have such a huge false pride due to opulence. Taking shelter of Krsna, a mortal, they showed contempt to a god.” (10.25.3)**

Indra’s pride was known to Him, therefore it was said: manyum janayan, “to arouse his anger” (10.24.12), otherwise he would have had only fear, not anger. His arousal of Indra’s anger was done with the intent to make his rage boil over.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Kalatmana (by Him, the soul of Time) connotes: indra-makha-samharakena, “the terminator of the sacrifice meant for Indra.”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Kalatmana means kalasya niyantra prerakena, “by the controller, i.e. the impeller, of Time.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Kalatmana means kalasya niyamakena (by Him, the controller of Time). This is the time for breaking Indra’s arrogant pride. The idea is: He set forth the time of that sort. “Hearing the speech that was said (proktam = proktani vacanam), they accepted His words in a good way, that is, without arguing (Sadhu = avitarkam yatha syat tatha).”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Kalatmana means kala-saktina (by Him, whose power is Time).

### 10.24.32-34

*tatha ca vyadadhuh sarvam yathaha madhusudanah \|*  
*vacayitva svasty-ayanam tad-dravyena giri-dvijan \|\|*  
*upahrtya balin sarvan adrta yavasam gavam \|*  
*go-dhanani puraskrtya girim cakruh pradaksinam \|\|*  
*anamsy anadud-yuktani te caruhya svalankrtah \|*  
*gopyas ca krsna-viryani gayantyah sa-dvijasisah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatha—in that way; ca—and; vyadadhuh—they did; sarvam—everything;yatha—just as;aha—He says (He said); madhusudanah—Madhusudana; vacayitva—after making \[Brahmanas\] recite; sv-asti-ayanam—the svasti-ayana mantras (“that which leads to a superb existence”); tat-dravyena—with those objects; giri-dvijan—to the mountain and to Brahmanas;

upahrtya—after offering; balin—offerings; sarvan—all; adrtah—they who were shown respect; yavasam—grass; gavani—to cows; go-dhanani—the cows; puraskrtya—after placing in front; girim cakruh pradaksinam—they made the mountain on the right (they did a clockwise circumambulation);

anamsi—carts; anadut-yuktani—yoked with bulls; te—they; ca—and; aruhya—mounting; su-alankrtah—nicely adorned; gopyah—the cowherd women; ca—and; krsna-viryani—Krsna’s exploits; gayantyah—while singing; sa-dvija-asisah—they who have Brahmanas’ blessings.

*(tatah) ca yatha madhusudanah aha (sma), tatha (te gopah) sarvam vyadadhuh. (te) svasty-ayanam (brahmanan) vacayitva tad-dravyena giri-dvijan (prati) sarvan balin (tatha) gavam yavasam (ca) upahrtya adrtah (abhavan), sa-dvijasisah te (gopah tatha) svalankrtah gopyah ca krsna-viryani gayantyah go-dhanani puraskrtya anadud-yuktani anamsi aruhya ca girihi pradaksinam cakruh.*

**Перевод:**

**They did everything exactly like Madhusudana said. After prompting Brahmanas to recite mantras for prosperity, they presented all the offerings, along with objects for Indra’s sacrifice, to the mountain and to Brahmanas. The cowherds, who had also given grass to cows, were shown respect: They received the Brahmanas’ blessings. Placing the cattle in front and mounting the wagons yoked to oxen, the cowherd men and women, nicely adorned, circumambulated Govardhana Mountain while the women sang Krsna’s exploits.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“After giving (upahrtya = dattva) the offerings along with those objects for the sacrifice of the great Indra (tad-dravyena = tena mahendra-makha-dravyena) to the hill and to Brahmanas” (giri-dvijan = giri-dvijan prati). Adrtah means sadarah (respectful).

Anadud-yuktani signifies uttamanadudbhir yuktani (yoked with the best oxen). Sa-dvijasisah means dvijasirbhih sahitah (they who had the Brahmanas’ blessings).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The words beginning from tatha ca make one verse of two lines. The details of it are told in Hari-vamsa:

*ananda-janano ghoso mahan mudita-gokulah \|*  
*turya-pranada-ghosais ca vrsabhanam ca garjitaih \|\|*  
*hamba-ravaisca vatsanam gopanam harsa-vardhanah \|*  
*dadhno hradah saravartahpayah-kulya-samakulah \|\|*  
*mamsa-rasi-prakrstaughah prakasaudana-parvatah \|*  
*sampravartata yajno ’sya girer gobhih samakulah \|\|*

**“The village was a generator of bliss. Gokula was very joyful. With the beats and other sounds of drums, with the bellowing of bulls, and with the lowing of calves, it increased the cowherds’ delight. There was a pond of yogurt and a pool of ghee. It was abounding in canals of milk. There was an eminent flow of heaps of pulp. There was a conspicuous mountain of cooked rice. The sacrifice of Gokula for the mountain had begun. It was crowded with cows.” (HV 2.17.16-18)**

Suka uses the name ‘Madhusudana’ to make Pariksit understand that the cowherds had no fear of Indra. As a pun, ‘Madhusudana’ means He takes the essence, like a bee, and He especially enjoys sweet Rasa, and so it is fitting that He should inaugurate a sacrifice for His best servant, and that He should enjoy those offerings. This will be stated just ahead.

In the words starting from vacayitva, which constitute one unit of two and a half verses, the sequence is to be known only in accordance with the directives enounced by Sri Krsna.

**10.24.33**

In adrtah, the active voice (if the meaning is taken as ‘respectful’) is poetic license.

**10.24.34**

How did they do the circumambulation? He talks about it with anamsi and so forth. The details of it are mentioned in Hari-vamsa:

*tato nirajanartham hi vrndaso go-kulani vai \|*  
*parivavrur giri-varam sa-vrsani samantatah \|\|*  
*tah gavah pradrutah hrstah sapida-kanakangadah \|*  
*sa-srag-apida-srngagrah sataso ’tha sahasrasah \|\|*  
*anujagmus ca gopalah kalayantodhanani ca \|*  
*bhakti-cchedanuliptanga rakta-pitasitambarah \|\|*  
*mayura-citrangadino bhujaih praharanavrtaih \|*  
*mayura-patra-citrais cakesa-bandhaih suyojitaih \|\|*  
*babhrajur adhikam gopah samavaye tada tu te \|*  
*anye vrsan aruruhur nrtyanti sma pare muda \|\|*  
*gopalas tv apare gas ca jagrhur vega-gaminah \|*

**“Then, only for the sake of an offering of dipa, the village residents, in groups, along with the best of them all around, surrounded that best of mountains. The cows were speedy and jubilant. They had golden bandlets, like clamps. They had garlands, and the tips of their horns had wreaths. They numbered in the hundreds. Then, by the thousands, the cowherds, while also protecting their wealth, followed. They were wearing tilaka and their garments were red, yellow, and white. They had amazing armlets made of peacock feathers. The cowherds were more resplendent because of their arms, covered with weapons and colorful with those feathers, and because of nicely worn hair bands. However, when they assembled, some cowherds mounted bulls, others danced with joy, and yet other, swift goers, caught cows.” (Hari-vamsa 2.17.32-37)**

In this citation, the meaning of go-kulani is gokula-sthah janah (people of the village). The sense of sa-vrsani (with the best ones, lit. “with bulls”) is the people of the village were accompanied by their dearest ones.

The cowherd women too mounted the carts and did a circumambulation. Having mentioned a nondifferentiation in the matter of doing a circumambulation, Suka gives a detail about the divine cowherd women: They were singing Krsna’s exploits; this ended with His inauguration of a yajna for Sri Govardhana. With sa-dvijasisah (they who had the Brahmanas’ blessings), it is implied that the Brahmanas also, accompanied by their wives, did a circumambulation.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Having given the offerings, along with the objects for Indra’s sacrifice (tad-dravyena = indra-makha-dravyena), to the hill and to Brahmanas (giri-dvijan - giraye dvijebhyah ca)…"

They were respected by Krsna (adrtah = krsnena adrtah). Gavani should read gobhyah (to cows). The carts were yoked with bulls (anadud-yuktani - ano-vahakair vrsair yuktani). The cowherd men (te = gopah) and the cowherd women did a circumambulation.

Sa-dvijasisah means: giyamanabhir dvijasirbhih sahitah (they who had the blessings of Brahmanas, who were singing). The sense is: dvija-kartrkasiso ’pi gayantyah, “The ladies were singing even while the Brahmanas gave blessings.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

They circumambulated by eminently keeping the mountain to the right (pradaksinam cakruh = prakarsena daksinah yatha bhavati tatha cakruh).

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

They made Brahmanas recite (vacayitva = brahmanaih vacayitva) a svasty-ayana. The offerings were the edibles (balin = naivedyani).

### 10.24.35

*krsnas tv anyatamam rupam gopa-visrambhanam gatah \|*  
*sailo ’smiti bruvan bhuri-balim adad brhad-vapuh \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

krsnah—Krsna; tu—however; anyatamam—another one of many; rupam—a form; gopa-visrambhanam—in such a way as to make the cowherds believe; gatah—attained (assumed); sailah asmi—\[I\] am the mountain; iti—(marks the end of the quotation); bruvan—while saying; bhuri—plentiful; balim—the offering; adat—He ate; brhat-vapuh—He whose body is huge.

*krsnah tu gopa-visrambhanam anyatamam rupam gatah, (sah) brhad-vapuh (san) “sailo ’smi” iti bruvan bhuri-balim adat.*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna, however, also assumed another form to make the cowherds believe. He became a gigantic body, exclaimed “The mountain is I” and ate the ample offerings.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Having assumed (gatah = praptah san) a form that evokes the cowherds’ belief (gopa-visrambhanam = gopanam visvasa-janakam), He ate the offering (balim adat = upaharam abhaksayat).”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

To show that this sacrifice which He inaugurated is by far superior to the sacrifice for Indra and to continuously generate trust in Him, under the guise of being Sri Govardhana He Himself appeared separately on top of It and, right after the gift of offerings, directly ate those offerings to give bliss to all. Thus, the word tu in krsnas tu has the sense of purvato visesah (a particularity compared to before).

In anyatamam, the suffix tama\[p\] is used with the intent to communicate an utter difference. That form made the cowherds believe (gopa-visrambhanam = gopan visrambhayati visvasayati iti tatha tat), therefore: brhad-vapuh, which means: “\[the form,\] whose body is huge,” consequently He ate (adat = abhunkta) all that offering, though it was more than profuse (bhuri-balim = bhurim pracurataram api balim tam sarvam). That is said in Hari-vamsa:

*tam gopah parvatakaram divya-srag-anulepanam \|*  
*giri-murdhni sthitam drstva hrstajagmuh pradhanatah \|\|*

**“Seeing Him, who had the shape of a mountain, who had a divine garland, who was anointed, and who was atop the mountain, most of the cowherds, enraptured, went to Krsna.” (Hari-vamsa 2.17.24)**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The commentary is the same, except that he derives brhad-vapuh as a bahuvrihi in the masculine: “He whose form is huge.”)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

To illustrate the extraordinary eminence of the sacrifice that He inaugurated, while making everyone believe in that matter He Himself became manifest as the form of a devata.

He assumed (gatah = praptah) an identity, which had all the senses (rupam = sarvendriya-vat svarupam): It was anyatama, meaning it was as if a second mountain above Govardhana Hill. Gopa-visrambhanam signifies: gopanam visrambhanam parvatah eva ayam iti visvasah yatra tat, “a form about which the cowherds have the belief: “The mountain is He.”

“While saying sailo ’smi (the mountain is I)...” This means He followed that up with this: “I, the sole overlord of this place, have appeared, being gracious because of your bhakti. Each of you can choose a boon.”

“... He ate the edibles (balim adat = naivedyam bhunkte sma),” which were being offered either visibly, by residents of Vraja that were far or near, possibly by those who abide in Nandagrama, or invisibly, by meditation. He, who had thousands of millions of hands, took humongous offerings from those various places with His hands, extremely long, and ate the food to give bliss to all those persons.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Brhad-vapuh is an adjective of rupam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

He ate the offerings. At that time the cowherds asked Him, “Who are You?” While saying sailo 'smi—the word iti is expressive of a method (prakara) (in this way); to some He said govardhano 'smi, to some He said: sailo 'smi, and to others He uttered, parvato 'smi—He ate the abundant offering.

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

“Krsna, however, assumed another form, supereminent among other forms of the Lord (anyatamam rupam = anyesu bhagavad-rupesu atisayitam rupantaram), to make the cowherds believe that Govardhana was a devata of sorts (gopa-visrambhanam = gopanam govardhane daivatatva-visvasa-karam). Therefore, He, being a huge form (brhad-vapuh = brhad-vapuh san) located atop the hill, ate the offerings, presented by cowherds, while saying sailo 'smi, which means: sailabhimani devo ’smi (the divinity who has the conceit of being the mountain is I).”

### 10.24.36-37

*tasmai namo vraja-janaih saha cakre ’tmanatmane \|\|*  
*aho pasyata sailo ’sau rupi no ’nugraham vyadhat \|*  
*eso ’vajanato martyan kama-rupi vanaukasah \|*  
*hanti hy asmai namasyamah sarmane atmano gavam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tasmai—to It; namah—an obeisance; vraja-janaih saha—with the people of Vraja; cakre—He did; atmana—by Himself (personally); dtmane—which is Himself; aho—(used for expressing astonishment); pasyata—see; sailah—hill; asau—this; rupi—having a form; nah— to us; anugraham—a favor; vyadhat—did; esah—this; avajanatah martyan—mortals who are disrespectful; kama-rupi—which has a form at will; vana-okasah—whose abode is the forest; hanti—kills; hi—because; asmai—to It; namasyamah—we will give obeisance; sarmane—for the happiness; atmanah—our; gavam—of cows.

*“aho! (yuyam) pasyata. asau sailah rupi (san) nah anugraham vyadhat, vanaukasah! hi esah (girih) kama-rupi (svam svakiyam va) avajanatah martyan (simha-vyaghra-sarpadi-rupena) hand, (tasmad vayam) atmanah gavam (ca) sarmane asmai namasyamah” (iti vadan) vraja-janaih saha (sri-krsnah) atmana tasmai atmane namah cakre.*

**Перевод:**

**Krsna Himself, along with the people of Vraja, showed respect to It, His self. “Residents of the forest! Wow! Look at this! By becoming embodied, the mountain did us a favor. Because this mountain, which assumes a form at will, kills disrespectful mortals, let us offer our respects to It for our well-being and for the cows’ well-being.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“With the people of Vraja, He Himself offered obeisance to It, Himself,” while reciting the verse of six lines that starts from aho.

Kama-rupi connotes sarpadi-rupah, “\[the hill,\] which has the form of a snake, and so forth.”178“We offer obeisance to the hill (asmai = adraye) for well-being (sarmane = ksemaya).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

In cakre ’tmana, the deletion of a is poetic license. Atmana means svayam eva (by Himself).

**10.24.37**

Why did they offer obeisance? The reason is mentioned in the verse of six lines, beginning from aho. “Being directly perceptible (rupi =pratyaksah san)—or being most beautiful (rupi = parama-sundarah san)" due to the inability to fully cover His topmost natural beauty. Moreover, suspecting the rise of the cowherds’ cognizance, to conceal it He did a favor, said in that way, by being embodied and by directly consuming the offerings.

It kills nondevotees too. “It kills those who show contempt (avajanatah = avajnam kurvatah)” that is, those who show contempt upon seeing It directly eat the unlimited offerings of all. Or It kills those who show disrespect by not doing the sacrifice (avajanatah = yagakaranena anada ram kurvatah). In this way that sacrifice is repeatedly emphasized.

It kills mortals, those in whose nature is the attribute of dying (martyan = marana-dharma-silah), and those who abide in the forest (vanaukasah), meaning those who do not have a gateway or any such thing on their property. Or vanaukasah is a vocative.

“Because (hi = yasmat) It kills, we should offer obeisance for our well-being and for the cows’,” or “for our cows’ well-being,” given that the Vrajavasis’ well-being depends on the cows’. Additionally, this is to be understood: He disappeared after giving some boon, a directly perceived result, to someone.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The words starting from tasmai make one verse of two lines. The word krsnah from the previous verse is carried forward. The wording vraja-janaih saha (with the people of Vraja) suggests the secondariness of the people of Vraja: This further implies that Krsna had a grand bhakti and revealed it. In cakre atmana, the word cakre is poetic license. Atmana means svayam eva (by Himself).

**10.24.37**

(Additions are underlined.) In the verse of six lines that begins from aho is the statement of diverse persons. “Being directly perceptible (rupi = pratyaksah san), It did us a favor,” by being embodied and by directly consuming the offerings.

It kills nondevotees too. “It kills those who show contempt (avajanatah = avajnam kurvatah)," that is, those who show contempt upon seeing It directly eat the unlimited offerings of all. Or It kills those who show disrespect by not doing the sacrifice (avajanatah = yagakaranena anadaram kurvatah). In this way that sacrifice is repeatedly emphasized.

It kills mortals, those in whose nature is the attribute of dying (martyan - marana-dharma-silah), and those who abide in the forest (vanaukasah), meaning those who do not have a gateway or any such thing on their property. Or vanaukasah is a vocative.

“Because (hi = yasmat) It kills, we should offer obeisance for our well-being and for the cows’,” or “for our cows’ well-being,” given that the Vrajavasis’ well-being depends on the cows’.

Here, inciting the father and others to give obeisance is not contradictory because, with regard to that other form, yet another Avatara. He is not a son. Besides, everyone already behaves that way toward Narayana. What happened after this, the direct order of that huge form of His, is described in Hari-vamsa:

*adya-prabhrti cejyo ’ham gosu ced asti vo daya \|\|*  
*aham vah prathamo devah sarva-kama-karah subhah \|*  
*mama prabhavac ca gavam amrtany eva bhoksyatha \|\|*  
*sivas ca vo bhavisyami mad-bhaktanam vane vane \|*  
*ramsye 'ham saha yusmabhir yatha divi gatas tatha \|\|*  
*ye ceme prathita gopa nanda-gopa-purogamah \|*  
*esam pritah prayacchami gopanam vipulam dhanam \|\|*  
*paryapnuvantu vipra mam gavo vatsa-samakulah \|*  
*evam mama para pritir bhavisyati na samsayah \|\|*

**“From today I should be worshiped, if you have compassion for cows. I am your first god, the splendid deity who fulfills all desires. And by My power you will consume the nectar of the cows. For you, My devotees, I will also become Siva (or auspicious). I will take pleasure with you in every forest, as if I were in heaven. Pleased with these celebrated cowherds, among whom the leader is Nanda, I am bestowing ample wealth to all of you cowherds. The cows, accompanied with calves, and Brahmanas should circumambulate Me. In this way I will have the topmost bliss. There is no doubt about it.” (Hari-vamsa 2.17.27-31)**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Afterward He Himself, with the body (atmana = dehena svayam), offered obeisance to It, Himself, and so did the people of Vraja, while reciting the verse of six lines that starts from aho. The deletion of the letter a (in cakre ’tmana) is poetic license.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Rupi (embodied) signifies: prakasita-devata-rupah (the hill, by whom the form of a divinity was manifested). “Having a form at will, i.e. being one who assumes the form of a snake, etc. (kama-rupi = sarpadi-rupa-dharah san), It will kill (hanti = hanisyati). Because \[it is so\], therefore (hi = hi tasmat) we will offer obeisance for the well-being of ours and of cows.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

Kama-rupi means: kamam yathestham rupavan, “It has a form at will,” and so It becomes armed, It becomes a tiger, It becomes a lion, and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Sarmane (for well-being) means sukhaya (for happiness).

**Annotation**

By definition, sarman means ‘happiness’, since it is in the list of such synonyms: mut pritih pramado harsah pramodamoda-sammadah, syad anandathur anandah sarma-sata-sukhani ca (Amara-kosa 1.4.24-25). The word sarman is also the title of a Brahmana (Sarma). Bhanuji Diksita gives the derivation: srnaty asubham. sr himsayam. sarva-dhatubhyo manin. bhave va, “Sarman is one who ends what is inauspicious. The verbal root is sr himsayam (9P) (to kill, destroy). The suffix man\[in\] is applied by sarva-dhatubhyo manin (Unadi-sutra 4.146). Or the derivation is in the passive impersonal voice (“happiness”)” (Ramasrami 1.4.25).

### 10.24.38

*ity adri-go-dvija-makham vasudeva-pracoditah \|*  
*yatha vidhaya te gopa saha-krsna vrajam yayuh \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

iti—in this way (or used to signify the end of the quotation); adri-go-dvija-makham—the sacrifice to the hill, to cows and to Brahmanas; vasudeva-pracoditah—impelled by Vasudeva; yatha—properly; vidhaya—after doing; te—they; gopah—the cowherds; saha-krsnah—accompanied by Krsna; vrajam—to the cowherd village; yayuh—went.

*te gopah vasudeva-pracoditah adri-go-dvija-makham yatha vidhaya saha-krsnah (santah) vrajam yayuh (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**Having appropriately performed the sacrifice to the hill, to cows and to Brahmanas in that way under the guidance of Vasudeva, the cowherds, accompanied by Krsna, went to the village.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*karmaivalam prak-svabhavo guno va*  
*karmangam va tad-vaso va mahesah \|*  
*varta-kartri devatetiyam ukta*  
*deva-ksobhe san-mati na tv abhista \|\|*  
*(salini)*

**“In regard to agitating the god, these six opinions were stated, but were not meant: (1) Karma alone is able (is the cause of the origination of happiness etc.), (2) One’s primordial nature (subconscious tendencies) is able, (3) The gunas are able, (4) A great controller is an aspect of karma, (5) The great controller is subject to karma, and (6) The maker of one’s occupation is one’s deity.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Iti means either anena prakarena (urged by Vasudeva “in this manner”) or idrsam (a sacrifice “of this sort”). Here the hill is mentioned first (compared to verse 30) because Sri Govardhana was foremost in that sacrifice and because It is the best Hari-dasa.

The cowherds were urged by Vasudeva, the presiding deity of all. He is the presiding deity of the subconscious (citta); that explains why they did as He instructed. A special happy oneness of opinion with the Soul of all has also been shown.

Or the sense is the name Vasudeva is used because, as Vasudeva-nandana, He is dedicated to revealing His infinite aisvarya, and so the drift is: Inaugurating the worship of Sri Govardhana, the best Hari-dasa, by disrupting the sacrifice to Indra, who was maddened by arrogant pride on account of aisvarya, was proper.

“Fittingly (yatha = yathavat), they were accompanied by Krsna (saha-krsnah = krsnena sahitah).” The sense is: Owing to an upsurge of a special affection, they were unable to abandon Him. Right after meeting Him, they went to their abode (vrajam = nija-vasam), near Sri Nandisvara Hill. Their village was located more than one krosa from Sri Radha-kunda, in the north-eastern direction of Govardhana.

In this way, by the appearance of karma-vada, which rejects a devata, the predominance of actions is established. In addition, the flow of karma (action) takes place just because of the control of samskara; in that way, given that samskara is the root of karma, the idea that one should be resolute about karma is meant. Therefore any power of actions that is not occurring by this axiom is rejected: antaryamina yatha preryate tathanusthiyate, “An action is done just as it is impelled by Paramatma.”

Over and above that, the livelihood must necessarily be brought about only by the nature of a guna, such as sattva-guna, and so the idea that at some point in time karma will cease to exist by the absence of an effort to make a living is repudiated, because of the mention of the necessary worship of one’s livelihood, the maker of gain and preservation. Thus in every way the primordialness of actions is strengthened. And that is just for the sake of being dedicated to one’s bhakti, the main thing of all actions.

Further, the essential characteristic of being dedicated to bhakti is the worship of His devotees, hence the worship of Sri Govardhana, Hari-dasa, is emphasized. Such is the philosophical conclusion.

In this regard, Sri Krsna’s hidden intention was this: “I am the fullness, Paramesvara, and am their son, their cousin, and so on, therefore who else might be in charge of these cowherds? Who at all is another divinity? Their moving force is only their nature, which is full of pure love. Moreover, there should be an acceptance of a devata, as a human pastime; only those who have a close connection with Me are suitable participants. Nonetheless I do not strive to suggest it, in order to safeguard the nature of humanlike pastimes. Consequently I will give an impetus in this way by enlightening them about those things only by teaching the atheistic doctrines of Sankhya and Mimamsa.” It is to be inferred in like manner elsewhere also, everywhere.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The acceptance of the atheistic doctrines of Sankhya and Mimamsa was for the sake of canceling the sacrifice to Indra, but they are not agreed upon by sadhus. For instance, honorable Sri Svami wrote: karmaivalam prak... (see above).

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

They went to the capital, Nandisvara (vrajam = nandisvara-rajadhanim).

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

“Eminently inspired by Vasudeva (Vasudeva-pranoditah = vasudevena eva prakarsena noditah), they had appropriately (yatha = yathavat) carried out the sacrifice.”

## Chapter 25 - Rasika-sekhara Strikes a Pose Under Govardhana

### 10.25.1

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*indras tadatmanah pujam vijnaya vihatam nrpa \|*  
*gopebhyah krsna-nathebhyo nandadibhyas cukopa sah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah uvaca—Sri Suka said; indrah—Indra; tada—at that time; atmanah—to him; pujam—the formal worship; vijnaya— after understanding; vihatam—was discontinued; nrpa—O king; gopebhyah—at the cowherds; krsna-nathebhyah—whose master is Krsna; nanda-adibhyah—among whom the first is Nanda; cukopa— became angry; sah—he.

*sri-sukah uvaca—nrpa! tada sah indrah atmanah pujam (gopaih) vihatam vijnaya (tebhyah) gopebhyah krsna-nathebhyah nandadibhyah cukopa.*

**Перевод:**

**Sri Suka said: Then, understanding that the formal worship to him was discontinued, O king, Indra became enraged at Nanda and the other cowherds, whose master is Krsna.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*panca-vimse rusa sakre vraja-nasaya varsati \|*  
*uddhrtya girim asarad araksad gokulam prabhuh \|\|*

**“In the twenty-fifth chapter: When Sakra was showering rain out of anger in order to destroy Vraja, by lifting the mountain the Almighty protected the herd of cows from the downpour.”**

**10.25.1**

Krsna-nathebhyah means: krsno natho yesam tebhyah (they whose master is Krsna).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Indra understood, that is, he directly perceived it, because he had secretly arrived in the sky at that time on the occasion of that big festival. Or the reason is the goods for the fire sacrifice to him were not in the vicinity. His puja had been halted in a particular way (vihatam = visesena hatam) inasmuch as they used the things meant for him for another purpose.

In point of krsna-nathebhyah: Indra was wrong to get enraged at them, and so his stupidity and his folly of arrogant pride are implied. The gist of the vocative nrpa is: “It’s already known to you that false pride due to luxury is the cause of faults of character.” By the word adi, in nandadibhyah, other cowherds, such as Upananda, and the priests are included. Ha means sphutam (clearly), on account of a behavior that was fitting in his case.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) He understood, directly perceived, that his puja was discontinued inasmuch as they used the things meant for him for another purpose. By getting angry at them, whose master is Krsna, who are cowherds that live in Vraja, and who are none else than Nanda and his friends, stupidity and the folly of arrogant pride are implied.

Ha means sphutam (clearly), on account of a behavior that was fitting in his case. Sometimes the reading is sah (he). The sense is: parama-durbuddhih (he is the most stupid).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*panca-vimse sa-kopoktav indre nasaya varsati \|*  
*vrajasya raksam akarod uddhrtyacalam acyutah \|\|*

**“In the twenty-fifth chapter: While Indra, with words of fury, was showering rain to destroy, Acyuta protected Vraja by lifting the mountain.”**

**10.25.1**

He was angry at them although their master is Krsna.” Indra’s foolishness and the uselessness of his anger are thus shown at the outset.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

*panca-vimse ’tikopena sakre nasaya varsati \|*  
*gokulasyakarod raksam girim uddhrtya kesavah \|\|*

**“In the twenty fifth chapter While Sakra, out of fury, was showering rain for destruction, Kesava saved Gokula by lifting the hill.”**

### 10.25.2

*ganam samvartakamnama meghanam canta-karinam \|*  
*indrah pracodayatkruddho vakyam cahesa-many uta \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

ganam samvartakam nama—the group named Samvartaka; meghanam—of clouds; ca—(a verse filler); anta-karinam—which do the end; indrah—Indra; pracodayat—impelled (sent); kruddhah— angry; vakyam—a sentence (a statement); ca—and; aha—speaks (spoke); isa-mani—he who has the conceit of being God; uta—also.

*indrah kruddhah (san) samvartakam nama anta-karinam meghanam ganam pracodayat, isa-mani uta (san idam vaksyamanam) vakyam aha (sma) ca.*

**Перевод:**

**Enraged, and thinking himself to be God, Indra summoned the Samvartaka group of clouds, which bring about ultimate annihilation, and uttered a statement as follows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Angry, Indra urged (pracodayat = presayamasa) the well-known group of clouds named Samvartaka, so-called because they bring about universal dissolution (samvartakam = samvartah pralavah tat-kartaram)."

Someone might think: “Why were the clouds ordered to kill those whose master is Krsna?” Expecting that, and with the following in mind, “Indra’s discernment was cast aside by his own imagination,” Suka relates Indra’s words in the next five verses. Indra had the overweening pride: “I am God” (isa-mani = aham eva isvarah iti garvavan).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

The word ca has the sense of api (also). “He eminently—by enthusing them with his words expressive of arrogant pride—dispatched (pracodayat-prakarsena prerayamasa) that group of clouds which also bring about universal dissolution (anta-karinam ca = antah pralayah tat-karinam api),” or he eminently impelled that group and—because of ca—the group of winds such Avaha and Pravaha.” Uta has the sense of either kheda (lamentation) or vismaya (astonishment), insofar as Devendra used those clouds at the wrong time.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) They bring about universal dissolution (anta-karinam ca - antah pralayah tat-karinam) therefore they are called Samvartaka. The word ca has the sense of api. Alternatively, “He eminently—by increasing their enthusiasm and so on with words of arrogant pride— impelled (pracodayat = prakarsena prerayamasa) that group and—because of ca—the group of winds such Avaha and Pravaha.” Uta has the sense of api (even), in the form of a reproach, insofar as even Devendra used them at the wrong time.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In this verse, Suka expounds the anger. “He urged (pracodayat = presayamasa) the group of clouds that brings about universal dissolution (samvartakam = samvartah pralayah tat-kartaram) and—because of ca—the group of Samvartaka winds such as Avaha and Pravaha” (verse 9).

### 10.25.3

*aho sri-mada-mahatmyam gopanam kananaukasam \|*  
*krsnam martyam upasritya ye cakrur deva-helanam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

aho—how amazing; sri-mada—of false pride because of wealth; mahatmyam—the hugeness; gopanam—of the cowherds; kanana-okasam—whose abode is the forest; krsnam—Krsna; martyam—a mortal; upasritya—taking shelter of close-by; ye—who; cakruh—did; deva—to God; helanam—contempt.

*aho! gopanam kananaukasam sri-mada-mahatmyam (bhavati), ye (gopah) krsnam martyam upasritya deva-helanam cakruh.*

**Перевод:**

**“Ha! The cowherds, who live in the woodland, have such a huge false pride due to opulence. Taking shelter of Krsna, a mortal, they showed contempt to a god.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“They slighted a god, me.” (deva-helanam =devasya mama avajnam)

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“What a wonder (aho = ascaryam)! They, whose abode is the woodland—being base and being ignorant are meant to be implied—showed contempt to a god by closely taking shelter of a human (martyam = manusyam).” The gist is: saying this is not possible without having a huge false pride due to opulence.

Deva (god) is said because, due to being a god, his glory is greater than the glory of a mortal, but it is not said mama (to me), also for the sake of bringing to light the inappropriateness of taking shelter of a mortal by rejecting a god.

Here also, by virtue of being cowherds and forest dwellers, it is stated that they are the most sattvika.

Though He is Para-Brahman, Krsna has a human form: Such is His bhakta-vatsalya, so for that purpose, slighting a god is fitting. That is the real meaning.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) “What a wonder (aho = ascaryam)!" Regarding kananaukasam (they whose abode is the woodland): Being base and being ignorant are meant to be implied.

Here the prefix upa has a negative undertone, as in the difference between pati and upapati: An asraya is obtained by a reputable family, attributes, and so forth, whereas an upasrava happens as a result of falling from that, and so upasritya suggests that in Indra’s mind they fell by taking shelter of Krsna. Deva is said because, due to being a god, his glory is greater than the glory of a mortal, but it is not said mama (to me), also for the sake of bringing to light the inappropriateness of taking shelter of a mortal by rejecting a god. The drift is: “They don’t think of me as a deva. much less as deva-deva."

Here also, by virtue of being cowherds and forest dwellers, it is stated that they are the most sattvika. Though He is Para-Brahman, Krsna has a human form: Such is His bhakta-vatsalya, so for that purpose, slighting a god is fitting. That is the real meaning implied by Sarasvati.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The true meanings of Sarasvati are as follows. Sri-mada-mahatmyam is a dvandva compound in the singular: “How amazing are the cowherds’ splendor, joy and glory (sri-mada-mahatmyam = srih ca madah harsah ca mahatmyam ca). They showed contempt to wicked me (deva-helanam – devasya mama dustasya helanam): such contempt is beneficial for mortals (martyam = martyebhyo hitam).”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

“Slighting a god is fit for death (martyam =maranarham).” Martyam is an adjective of deva-helanam. In other words death occurs because of it. “What a wonder! They have such a huge false pride of opulence by taking support of Krsna (krsnam upasritya - krsnopastambena).”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

They took shelter of Krsna by thinking: “He is the best support” (upasritya - sarvasmad adhikasrayo ’yam iti krtva).183

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“The magnitude of the cowherds’ false pride occasioned by the affluence of wealth makes for wonderment (sri-mada-mahatmyam - sri-madasya dhana-sampatti-krtasya madasya vaibhavam) (aho = ascarya-karam).” Indra expounds: “Taking shelter of Krsna, a mortal, those cowherds did an offense (helanam = aparadham) to a god, me,” in other words: “They broke my fire sacrifice.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

“How amazing is the hugeness of the cowherds’ false pride of opulence! (aho sri-mada-mahatmyam – sri-madasya mahatmyam ascaryam). They took shelter of Krsna close-by (upa =samipam) and slighted me.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sukadeva Maharaja:**

Here the nature of common people is made to be perceived: Ordinary people superimpose their own faults on another person; and like Indra, they reject the authority of praiseworthy individuals. It’s understood from “krsnam martyam upasritya” that Indra, who knew the truth because Brahma told the gods: gam paurusim me srnutamarah, “Immortals, immediately hear from me the statement of the Purusa” and so on (10.1.21), was possessed by anger and was jealous that Krsna, who is praiseworthy, was getting all the attention.

### 10.25.4-5

*yathadrdhaih karma-mayaih kratubhir nama-nau-nibhaih \|*  
*vidyam anviksikim hitva titirsanti bhavarnavam \|\|*  
*vacalam balisam stabdham ajnam pandita-maninam \|*  
*krsnam martyam upasritya gopa me cakrur apriyam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

yatha—just as; adrdhaih—which are not solid; karma-mayaih—which consist of rites; kratubhih—by means of fire sacrifices; nama—in name only; nau-nibhaih—which resemble a boat; vidyam anviksikim—the knowledge related to inquiry; hitva—rejecting; titirsanti—they want to cross; bhava-arnavam—the ocean in the form of material existence;

vacalam—talkative; balisam—childish; stabdham—puffed up; ajham—ignorant; pandita-maninam—thinks Himself learned; krsnam—Krsna; martyam—mortal; upasritya—by taking shelter of; gopah—the cowherds; me—to me; cakruh—did; apriyam—what is unpleasant.

*yatha (kecit) anviksikim vidyam hitva adrdhaih karma-mayaih nama-nau-nibhaih kratubhih bhavarnavam titirsanti, (tatha te) gopah vacalam balisam stabdham ajnam pandita-maninam martyam krsnam upasritya me apriyam cakruh.*

**Перевод:**

**“Krsna is talkative, childish, puffed up, ignorant, and mortal. The cowherds snubbed me by taking shelter of Him, who thinks he is learned. In like manner, those obsessed with rituals seek to cross the ocean of material existence by rejecting the science of self-introspection and by undertaking sacrifices, the rites, which are boats in name only and hence unreliable.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“As people desire to cross with fire sacrifices, which are unfit (adrdhaih = asamarthaih), which are brought about by rites (karma-mayaih = kriya-nirvartyaih) and hence which resemble a boat in name only, having rejected knowledge that is the form of a constant remembrance of the soul (anviksikim = atmanusmrti-rupam), so the cowherds did an act disagreeable to me by taking shelter of Krsna, who is talkative (vacalam = bahu-bhasinam), is a child (balisam = sisum), thinks Himself a scholar (pandita-maninam = panditam manyam) and—therefore—is not modest (stabdham =avinitam)."

Although expressive of criticism, Indra’s bharati (words; Sarasvati) extols Krsna: He is the source of the scriptures (vacalam = sastra-yonim). Though childish in this way He is not pretentious, like a child (balisam evam api sisu-van nirabhimaninam). He does not bow (stabdham = anamram), since no other person is worthy of a praise. No one is ignorant because of Him, i.e. He is omniscient (ajnam = na asti jnah yasmat tam = sarvajnam). He deserves high respect by those who know Brahman (pandita-maninam = brahma-vidam bahu-mananiyam). He is Para-Brahman, the form of constant bliss (krsnam = sadananda-rupam param brahma). Still, due to caring for His devotees He looks human (martyam = tathapi bhakta-vatsalyena manusyataya pratiyamanam).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“As fools desire to cross the ocean of material existence by means of fire sacrifices, whose results are perishable (adrdhaih = ksayisnu-phalakaih) because: karma-mayaih, they consist of rites, in other words they do not want to cross by the best means, of which the prominent ones are meditation and kirtana, so by taking shelter of Krsna the cowherds did what is unpleasant to me (me - mama)." This is merely an example of an unsuitable behavior owing to a lack of discernment.

Alternatively: tatha mam hitva krsnasrayena gopa matto bhaya-duhkhadikam titirsanti, “... so by taking shelter of Krsna after rejecting me the cowherds want to cross their fear of me, as well as trouble caused by me, and so forth.” Due to Indra’s absorption in anger, it’s understood that his sentence is incomplete.

Vacalam is said with the intent to express the exposition of karma-vada, which is harsh and is accompanied with dry logic. On account of arrogant pride, being base is implied by gopah, and being supereminent is implied by me, which denotes the master of the three worlds.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The commentary is the same. Moreover:) The real meaning is this: yatha vaisnavah karmabhih sahanviksikim hitva kevala-krsnasrayena bhavarnavam titirsanti, “\[Taking shelter of Krsna, the cowherds showed contempt to the gods,\] just like Vaisnavas desire to cross the ocean of material existence by taking shelter only of Krsna after rejecting the knowledge of inquiry about the self, along with rites.”

The rest is by Sridhara Svami. In his commentary, in the explanation suggestive of praise, vacalam literally means: vaca hetuna alam samartha ity eva, “He is able because of Vak.” In addition: balisam means “He was like innocent like a child,” by the definition: in Visva-prakasa: balisah savake murkhe, “Balisa means a young, and a fool.” Regarding brahma-vidam mananiyam (worthy of respect by those who know Brahman), the sense is: tat-kartrko mano vidyate yatra (He to whom respect is given by them).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“They desire to cross the ocean of material existence by means of fire sacrifices, which are incapable of achieving the intended result (adrdhaih = asamarthaih), which are only a bunch of rites (karma-mayaih = kevala-karma-pracuraih) and—therefore—which are like a boat in name alone, after rejecting knowledge in the form of taking interest in the soul (anviksikim = atmanusandhana-rupam).”

The real meaning is: karma-mayaih kratubhih saha anviksikim hitva avajnaya tyaktva krsnam asrityaiva Vaisnava yatha bhavarnavam titirsanti, "\[Taking shelter of Krsna, the cowherds showed contempt to the gods (deva-helanam),\] like the Vaisnavas, having contemptibly rejected, by taking shelter of Krsna, that knowledge (the desire for trance in Brahman) along with fire sacrifices, which consist of rites, desire to cross the ocean of material existence.” When the ocean of material life has turned out as a calf’s hoofprint, merely by taking shelter of Krsna, they just have the desire to cross, inasmuch as no effort is needed to cross it.

**10.25.5**

“By taking shelter of Him, they did what is unpleasant to me, though I am a god. He talks much: He has the habit of saying many disagreeable and inconsistent statements regarding the philosophies of Karma-mimamsa and Sankhya (vacalam = mimamsa-sankhyanabhimata-viruddha-bahu-bhasinam). He is a fool (balisam = murkham) because He did not study those scriptures. He behaves badly (stabdham - durvinitam) since He showed audacity even in front of His father. He doesn’t know anything (ajnam - kim apy ajananta) on account of grazing cows all the time. He considers Himself learned, and is a human (martyam = manusyam).”

The real meaning is this: Because of Him even a fool becomes adorned by Sarasvati (vacalam-balisam = vacayasarasvatya alankrtah baliso murkho ’pi yasmat tam): Here the noun is vaca: It ends in the suffix \[t\]a\[p\].184He does not bow (stabdham = anamram), since no other person is worthy of praise. No one is ignorant because of Him (ajnam = na asti jnah yasmat tam), and scholars keep giving Him respect (pandita-maninam = pandita-kartrko mana adaro vartate yasya tam).

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Anviksa means: anuksanam upanisac-cinta (thinking about the Upanisads at every moment). Anviksiki vidya means: anviksa tasyam bhava anviksiki brahmatma-vidya, "the knowledge existing in regard to such thoughts, that is, the knowledge that the soul is Brahman.”

Gir-devi hints at this: “He because of whom even a child, such as Dhruva, is adorned with Sarasvati (vacalam-balisam = vacaya sarasvatya alankrto baliso ’pi dhruvadir yasmat tam).”

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

He is an ornament in terms of speech: He speaks pleasantly (vacalam = vaca vacanatvena alam bhusanam priyam-vadam).185Prosperity, whose nature is to revolve, comes from Him (bali-sam = valitum silam yasya tad vali tatha-bhutam sam kalyanam yasmat).

### 10.25.6

*esam sriy avaliptanam krsnenddhmapitatmanam \|*  
*dhunuta sri-mada-stambham pasun navata sanksayam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

esam—of these ones; sriya—by opulence; avaliptanam—who are cocky; krsnena—by Krsna; adhmapita—made to be inflated; atmanam—whose minds; dhunuta—shake (take away); sri-mada— on account of the false pride of wealth; stambham—the arrogance; pasun—the animals; nayata—bring; sahksayam—to destruction.

*(yuyam) esam sriya avaliptanam krsnena adhmapitatmanam sri-mada-stambham dhunuta, pasun sanksayam nayata (ca).*

**Перевод:**

**“They are cocky because of wealth, and were rendered puffed-up by Krsna. You should dispel their arrogance occasioned by the false pride of wealth. Bring their animals to destruction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Dispel (dhunuta - apanayata) the arrogance that occurred because of the false pride (stambha = garva) of these ones, who are cocky (avaliptanam = mattanam) and whose bodies are fat (adhmayitatmanam - brmhita-dehanam) because of Krsna.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Having made the clouds understand the cowherds’ fault and, because of that, his rage toward them, now he orders what has to be done.

They were cocky due to wealth—either the affluence of various types of wealth or the wealth of having many animals—and their bodies were enlarged (brmhita-dehanam): An inner happiness and an outer happiness are thus implied. In addition: krsnena (because of Krsna), by the excellence of the enjoyment of sweet rice, etc., given that He tends the cows.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(The commentary is the same. Moreover:) The rest is by Sridhara Svami. In regard to his commentary: Puffing them up means making them have fiery energy, and the purport of that is an enlargement.

“How shall we dispel their arrogance?” In consideration of this he says: “Bring their animals to complete destruction (sanksayam = samyak ksayam),” since those very animals are the reason for the false pride of wealth. “Make all of them die with a massive rainfall.” The real meaning is: “Bring their animals to a proper dwelling, that is, to a state of well-being (sanksayam = samyan nivasah svasthyam).187

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

They are cocky (avaliptanam = mattanam) because their minds were made to have fiery energy by Krsna (krsnena dhmapitah satejaski-krta atma mano yesam). The real meaning is: sriya candana-carcayeva avaliptanam liptanganam sriman yah khalv astambhah jadyabhavas tam dhunuta duri-kuruta. tena tatha varsatha yatha tesam sita-janita-stambha ausnya-nivartako bhaved ity arthah, tatha pasun dhunuta sitena kampayata. tatas ca krsnena govardhane uddhrte sati sanksayam samyak nivasam tat-talam nayata. atisukhada-govardhana-tala-nivasam prati nayane yuyam eva karani-bhavatety arthah.

"Make the resplendent lack of inactivity of them (sri-mada-stambham = srimad-astambham) whose limbs are anointed as if with sandalwood paste,188go far away: Shower rain so that their immobility occasioned by chilliness will dispel their heat. And make their animals shake with a chill. Afterward, when Govardhana will be lifted by Krsna, lead the animals to the proper place, the base of it. That is, all of you should become the causes of leading the animals to the place which is the base of Govardhana, the bestower of intense joy.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

Their minds were enlarged (adhmayitatmanam = vardhita-manasam).

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

The reading adhmapitatmanam is proper.

### 10.25.7

*aham cairavatam nagam aruhyanuvraje vrajam \|*  
*marud-ganair maha-vegair nanda-gostha-jighamsaya \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

aham ca—and I; airavatam—Airavata; nagam—the elephant; aruhya—after mounting; anuvraje—I am going afterward; vrajam—to Vraja; marut-ganaih—with the multitudes of winds; maha-vegaih—who have great speed; nanda-gostha-jighamsaya—with the desire to strike Nanda’s cowherd village.

*aham ca airavatam (nama) nagam aruhya marud-ganaih maha- vegaih (saha) nanda-gostha-jighamsaya vrajam anuvraje (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Intending to strike Nanda’s village with the winds that have tremendous velocity, I, riding my elephant Airavata, will follow.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He addresses the clouds, who were afraid: “I will arrive right afterward (anuvraje - anantaram eva agamisyami).” Marud-ganaih means deva-ganaih saha (with the groups of gods).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“There is only a few of us. What power do we have in that matter?” Suspecting this he says: “I am coming right after you (anuvraje = yusmat-pascad eva agacchami), while riding on Airavata with the intent to strike, with the group of forty-nine winds, the cowherd village of Nanda.” The idea is: When you will run out of water, Airavata will provide assistance by drawing water with his trunk. Or, on account of bhakti to the Lord, the cowherd village is nanda: it delights the world, that is, it brings contentment to the world.

“It should rain only on the cowherd village, not on Madhu Puri.” This too is implied, otherwise there would be fear from Kamsa, who is puissant.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) The idea in “while riding on Airavata” is: “When you will run out of water, he will provide assistance by drawing water with his trunk.” The winds are the forty-nine winds.

“It should rain only on the cowherd village, not on Madhu Puri.” This too is implied, and so is the desire to make friends with Kamsa. The real meaning of jighamsaya is jigamisaya (“with the intent to go” to Vraja) (by taking the meaning of gati of the verbal root han himsa-gatyoh, to hurt, to go).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He addresses the clouds, who were afraid: “And I am following (anuvraje - anuvrajami) with the intent to strike (jighamsaya).” The true meaning is: jigamisaya.

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

The atmanepada in anuvraje is poetic license.

### 10.25.8

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*ittham maghavatajnapta megha nirmukta-bandhanah \|*  
*nanda-gokulam asaraih pidayamasur ojasa \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah uvaca—Sri Suka said; ittham—in this way; maghavata—by Indra; ajhaptah—ordered; meghah—the clouds; nirmukta-bandhanah—whose bondage was released; nanda-gokulam—Nanda’s cowherd community; asaraih—with hard showers; pidayamasuh—they pained; ojasa—with power.

*sri-sukah uvaca—ittham maghavata ajnaptah meghah nirmukta-bandhanah (santah) asaraih nanda-gokulam ojasa pidayamasuh.*

**Перевод:**

**Sri Suka said: Ordered by Maghavan in this way, the clouds, released from their bonds, violently tormented Nanda’s cowherd community with torrents.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“The clouds, whose bond was released by Indra... ” This is said with the intent to signify universal dissolution. At that time, being released, they tormented the community with heavy torrents of rain (asaraih = dhara-sampataih).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“With impetuosity—or with their own force (ojasa = vegena nija-balena va)—they tormented Nanda’s herd of cows, i.e. the cowherd village, that is to say they pained all those who live there (gokulam = gavam kulam = vrajam = tatratyan sarvan eva).'’

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Ojasa means balena (with force).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Those clouds, able to make one monumental ocean, are released only at universal dissolution. At this time those clouds were freed by Indra without foreseeing the consequence, since he was out of his mind due to anger.

### 10.25.9

*vidyotamana vidyudbhih stanantah stanayitnubhih \|*  
*tivrair marud-ganair nunna vavrsur jala-sarkarah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

vidyotamanah—illuminating; vidyudbhih—with lightning flashes; stanantah—rumbling; stanayitnubhih—with thunderclaps; tivraih—fierce; marut-ganaih—by the multitudes of winds; nunnah—driven; vavrsuh—they rained; jala-sarkarah—pebbles of water.

*(meghah) vidyotamanah vidyudbhih tivraih stanayitnubhih stanantah (tivraih) marud-ganaih nunnah (santah) jala-sarkarah vavrsuh.*

**Перевод:**

**Shedding light by the lightning flashes and roaring with vehement thunderclaps, the clouds, driven by fierce winds, rained hailstones.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Rumbling with thunderclaps and propelled by winds such as Avaha and Pravaha, the clouds rained hailstones.” (stanayitnubhih stananto marud-ganair nunna jala-sarkarah =asanibhih garjantah avaha-pravahadi-vayu-samuhaih preritah jalopalan)

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

In two verses he talks about the manner they tormented them. The clouds were shining in a special way (vidyotamanah = visesena dyotamanah): With this and the rest, an infinity of lightning flashes and fearsomeness are implied. The thunderclaps too were fierce (tivraih). They rained water and hailstones.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Rumbling with thunderclaps and made to move along with the winds such as Avaha and Pravaha, the clouds rained hailstones.”

**Комментарий. Автор Vamsidhara Pandita:**

*pravaho nivahas caiva vivaha udvahas tatha \|*  
*samvahavaha-paravaha ity ete marutam ganah \|\|*

**“The groups of winds are these: Pravaha, Nivaha, Vivaha, Udvaha, Samvaha, Avaha, and Paravaha.”**

**Annotation**

In Siddhanta-siromani, the following seven winds are listed:

*bhu-vayur avaha iha pravahas tad-urdhvah*  
*syad udvahas tad anu samvaha-samjnakas ca \|*  
*anyas tato ’pi suvahah paripurvako ’smat*  
*vahah paravaha ime pavanah prasiddhah*

**"The winds of Bhu are: Avaha, Pravaha, which is above it, Udvaha, after that Samvaha, then Suvaha, Parivaha, and Paravaha. These are the well-known winds” (quoted in Sabda-kalpa-druma).**

According to Puranic Encyclopedia, the wind called Pravaha moves clouds. Avaha causes thunder. Udvaha converts seawater into vapor and causes rain. Samvaha moves clouds in the sky: The clouds are the airplanes of the gods. Vivaha gives form and shape to clouds. Parivaha, keeps Akasa-Ganga motionless. The soul travels with the seventh wind, Paravaha (Puranic Encyclopedia). Moreover, the Pravaha wind is said to move all the stars and the planets (Surya-siddhanta 12.73). According to Apte’s Sanskrit-English Dictionary, Parivaha bears the seven Rsis and the celestial Ganges.

### 10.25.10

*sthuna-sthula varsa-dhara muncatsv abhresv abhiksnasah \|*  
*jalaughaih plavyamana bhur nadrsyata natonnatam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sthuna—like pillars; sthulah—huge; varsa-dharah—streams of rain; muncatsu abhresu—given the fact that the clouds were releasing; abhiksnasah—repeatedly; jala-oghaih—by the multitude of water; plavyamana—being submerged; bhuh—the Earth; na adrsyata—was not seen; nata-unnatam—low or high.

*abhresu sthuna-sthulah varsa-dharah abhiksnasah muncatsu (satsu), bhuh jalaughaih plavyamana (abhut, atah) natonnatam (ca sthalam) na adrsyata.*

**Перевод:**

**When the clouds were relentlessly releasing streams of rain that were huge like columns, the Earth became submerged by water. There was no such thing as a high place or a low place.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

"While the clouds were releasing streams of rain that were vast like columns (sthuna-sthulah = sthuna-vat-sthulah), the Earth was not seen in such a way that the high was the low.” (natonnatam = nimnam unnatam tad-viparitam yatha bhavati tatha)

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The streams of water were huge like house pillars. "The Earth became submerged (plavyamana =plavyamana abhut)—or: plavyamana sati bhur nadrsyata (being submerged, the Earth was not seen)—therefore: natonnatam ca sthalam nadrsyata, “Neither high places nor low places were seen.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Amara states: sthuna stambhe ’pi vesmanah, “Sthuna also means the pillar of a house” (Amara-kosa 3.3.50). “While the clouds were raining streams of rain that were huge like pillars, the Earth became immersed, and after that, high places and low places were not seen (nadrsyata natonnatam – tatah ca natonnatam sthalam na adrsyata).”

### 10.25.11

*atyasarativatena pasavo jata-vepanah \|*  
*gopa gopyas ca sitarta govindam saranam yayuh \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

atyasara—due to the excessive downpour; ativatena—and due to the intense wind; pasavah—the animals; jata-vepanah—whose trembling occurred; gopah—the cowherd men; gopyah ca—and the cowherd women; sita—by the cold; artah—pained; govindam—to Govinda; saranam—for shelter; yayuh—they went.

*pasavah gopah gopyah ca atyasarativatena sitartah jata-vepanah (santah) govindam saranam yayuh.*

**Перевод:**

**Trembling, and afflicted by the cold due to the excessive downpour and the intense wind, the animals and the cowherd men and women went to Govinda for shelter.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

They were trembling (jata-vepanah = jata-kampah).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Jata-vepanah and sitartah are adjectives of the animals, of the men and of the women. Of those, the mention of the animals at the outset is with regard to the increase of cold, and for that reason at first he will give the details of the manner they went for shelter, in the next verse. This and everything else took place only due to the Lord’s desire for the fun of lifting Govardhana, or else for the sake of demonstrating the fact that the false pride of wealth is the topmost cause of anarthas, insofar as otherwise those occurrences would be impossible in their case: They are dear to the Lord.

Govindam means: gavam indram svami-pravaram, “Him, the best master of cows.” Alternatively: gah svamitvena palyatvena ca vindati iti tatha tam, “He gets cows as the master,” and so they went to Him for shelter.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) Jata-vepanah and sitartah are adjectives of pasavah, gopah, and gopyah. Of those, the mention of the animals at the outset is because they were outside. The mention after them of the cowherd men is because most of them were outside. The mention of the cowherd ladies is because most of them were inside. It should be discerned in this manner. This and everything else took place only due to the Lord’s desire for the fun of lifting Govardhana, which increases the prema of the people of Vraja, and with the desire to demonstrate the fact that the false pride of wealth, of Sakra and of others, is the topmost cause of anarthas, insofar as otherwise those occurrences would be impossible in their case: They are dear to the Lord.

### 10.25.12

*sirah sutams ca kayena pracchadyasara-piditah \|*  
*vepamana bhagavatah pada-mulam upayayuh \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sirah—the head (their heads); sutan ca—and the children; kdyena—with their bodies; pracchadya—after covering; asara-piditah— afflicted by the downpour; vepamanah—trembling; bhagavatah—of the Lord; pada-mulam—the base of the feet; upayayuh—they came near.

*(te) asara-piditah vepamanah sirah sutan ca kayena pracchadya bhagavatah pada-mulam upayayuh.*

**Перевод:**

**Afflicted by the downpour, and trembling, they covered their children with their torsos, covered their own heads, and approached the Lord’s feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

They covered them with effort, or with garments that cover (pracchadya = prayasena pracchada-pata-rupena va acchadya). The sense of bhagavatah (of the Lord) is He is manifesting His unlimited aisvarya by saving them, or He is manifesting His personal qualities such as caring for those who are miserable (dina-vatsalya). Therefore they went very close to Him (pada-mulam upayayuh = atyanta-nikatam praptah). And in that way bhagavatah means He has the topmost special affection.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

They covered them with effort (pracchadya = prayasena chadayitva). How is it that they had such knowledge? In that regard he says: bhagavatah. The idea is: Since His qualities are otherworldly, in their minds He came across as one whose qualities, such as compassion, have that sort of power. Therefore they went very close to Him (pada-mulam upayayuh = atyanta-nikatam praptah).

### 10.25.13

*krsna krsna maha-bhaga tvan-natham gokulam prabho \|*  
*tratum arhasi devan nah kupitad bhakta-vatsala \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

krsna—O Krsna; krsna—O Krsna; maha-bhaga—O You because of whom there is great good fortune; tvat-natham—whose master is You; go-kulam—the herd of cows; prabho—O Almighty; tratum—to protect; arhasi—You ought; devat—from the god; nah—us; kupitat—who is angry; bhakta-vatsala—O You who care for devotees.

*krsna! krsna! maha-bhaga! prabho! bhakta-vatsala'. (tvam) tvan-natham gokulam nah (ca) kupitat devat tratum arhasi (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Krsna, Krsna, our source of luck! Prabhu, save the cowherd community, whose master is You, and us from the angry god. You care for Your devotees.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He mentions the request of the cowherd men and women: "You ought to protect the race of cows (go-kulam = gavam kulam vamsam), for whom only You are the master, and us from Indra.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

The repetition krsna krsna is either due to the affliction of cold or because of the nature of His name, which attracts the tongue. In addition, ‘krsna’ itself is either with regard merely to the name or with the intent to express that He removes (karsana) all sorrow.

The vocative maha-bhaga has already been explained, in the context of the deliverance from a forest fire, at the end of the seventeenth chapter (“O you who have the multitude of bhagas, such as aisvarya," or “O You because of whom persons like us have considerable good fortune,” 10.17.23).

Or that word is part of the compound: maha-bhaga-tvan-natham, “the herd of cows, whose master is You, because of whom they have great good fortune,” therefore: “Please protect our herd of cows, because our protection will automatically be accomplished when they will be saved.” Or: “Save our entire village (nah gokulam - asmakam go-kulam vrajam eva va sarvam)." Alternatively: “the community and us” (nah = asman ca).

Devat means indrat (from Indra). Not mentioning his name is either on account of animosity or because he has the tendency to sin. Another explanation is: devat tatrapi kupitat (from the god, not to mention that he is angry). The sense is: “We ordinary humans cannot keep away from the calamity that he did here. Only You are qualified to save us (arhasi = yogyo ’si)."

“But then what power do I have in this matter?” In that regard they say: prabho, that is, “O You who have all powers!, given that we saw Your otherworldly powers when You thrashed Kaliya, and so on.” “But it would be wrong of Me to use My powers against the gods.” In that regard they say: he bhakta-vatsala! The drift is:

“For Your devotees’s sake, there is no wrong at all on Your part.” Before, out of fear of the conflagration the request was submited to the Lord and to Baladeva, and at this time it is only submited to the Lord, insasmuch as only He can extricate them from this very dangerous situation. Or it is because they have profuse and absolute affection only for Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) The repetition krsna krsna is either due to affliction or with the intent to express that He takes away (akarsana) all sorrow. “O You who are our topmost good fortune (maha-bhaga = asmakam parama-bhagya-rupa)! “Please protect our herd of cows.” Or: “Save our entire village.” Alternatively: “the community and us” (nah = asman ca).

Devat means indrat (from Indra). Not mentioning his name is either on account of animosity or because he has the tendency to sin. Another explanation is: devat tatrapi kupitat. The sense is: “Only You are qualified to save us, who are unable to counteract that.” “But then what power do I have in this matter?” In that regard they say: prabho, “O You who have all powers!, given that we saw Your otherworldly powers when You thrashed Kaliya, and so on.” “But it is not right to use My powers against the gods.” In that regard they say: he bhakta-vatsala! The drift is: “For Your devotees’s sake, there is no wrong on Your part.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Continuously recalling Garga’s statement: anena sarva-durgani yuyam anjas tarisyatha, “Because of Him, all of you will easily overcome all difficulties” (10.8.16), the cowherds request Him, being confident: “In such a great danger, only Sri Narayana, entering in Krsna, can save us.” Devat means indrat (from Indra).

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

They ask for the end of their pain. “The cows, the Brahmanas, and the mountain were revered only by Your order, after we disregarded Indra. Now he, angry due to being disrespected, is hurting the cows and others for whom You are the devata.” The cowherds, who had heard about and experienced His power, took shelter of Him, but did not voice this reproach to Krsna since He is the dearest: “Look at the trouble that You caused.”

### 10.25.14

*sila-varsa-nipatenahanyamanam acetanam \|*  
*niriksya bhagavan mene kupitendra-krtam harih \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sila—of stones; varsa—by the rain; nipatena—by the fall; hanyamanam—being stricken; acetanam—lifeless; niriksya— observing; bhagavan—the Lord; mene—thought; kupita—angry; indra—by Indra; krtam—done; harih—Hari.

*bhagavan harih (gokulam) sila-varsa-nipatena hanyamanam acetanam niriksya kupitendra-krtam (varsam) mene.*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing that the community, stricken by the fall of a rain of hailstones, was lifeless, Lord Hari thought it was the work of angry Indra.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Even before being informed He had thought about what angry Indra did: that rain.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Directly seeing (niriksya = saksad drstva) that they were being stricken in such a way that they had almost fainted (acetanam = murcchita-prayam yatha syat tatha), He understood (mene = jnatavan),” because: bhagavan—He is omniscient—and harih, He takes away everyone’s sorrow. Removing the sorrow of the cowherd community by lifting Govardhana, which is about to be mentioned, and removing Sakra’s pride are implied.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“Seeing that the community—gokula is understood from the context—was being stricken by a tempest endowed with a rain of hailstones (sila-varsativatena = sila-varsa-yuktena ativatena)—in the other reading: they were being stricken by the fall of a rain of hailstones (sila-varsa-nipatena = sila-varsasya nipatena); consequently—they had almost fainted (acetanam = murcchita- prayam)." Krtam means krtim (the deed).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Those various hardships of theirs, though they are the Lord’s eternal parsadas, was put in place only by thelila-sakti for the sake of supereminently relishing the Rasa (pleasure) of the bliss of love (premananda). It should be understood that those troubles only consisted of happiness because the ultimate consequence was happiness, like the trouble of the hunger of those who are hungry and greedy enhances pleasure when they get to eat.

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

This pain of Hari’s parsadas was created only by His lila-sakti for the sake of relishing the upcoming pastime, like the pain of hunger that people feel is for the purpose of giving an appetite.

### 10.25.15

*apartv atyulbanam varsam ativatam sila-mayam \|*  
*sva-yage vihate ’smabhir indro nasaya varsati \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

apa-rtu—out of season; atyulbanam—vehement; varsam—rain; ativatam—in which the wind is excessive; sila-mayam—abounding in stones; sva-yage vihate—given the fact that his fire sacrifice was discontinued; asmabhih—by us; indrah—Indra; nasaya—for destruction; varsati—is showering.

*asmabhih sva-yage vihate (sati), indrah apartu atyulbanam ativatam sila-mayam varsam nasaya varsati.*

**Перевод:**

**“Now that we stopped his fire sacrifice, for the purpose of destruction Indra is showering a rain that is out of season, vehement, tempestuous, and abounding in hailstones.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

What did He think? Suka describes His thoughts, in four verses. The rain, whose season had passed (apartu - apagatah rtuh yasya tat) and in which the wind was intense (ativarsam =atisayitah vatah yasmin tat), abounded in hailstones (sila-mayam =sila-pracuram).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Afterward, due to an absorption in anger, He talks to Himself, in four verses: This is to be understood, since ahead it is going to be stated: ity uktva (‘having said this’, 10.25.19). Or He talks to the cowherds to pacify them.

The plural in asmabhih (by us) is either due to the manifestation of His boldness, to break Sakra’s false pride, or in consideration of Nanda and others. “Indra showered that rain for the sake of destroying” ... the cowherd village, but in truth it was just to destroy his arrogance.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Afterward, due to an absorption in anger, He talks to Himself, in five verses, since the syntactical connection is with the next one: ity uktva (10.25.19). However, henceforth each verse is explained separately. Varsam varsati means: varsam karoti (he did a rain), much like: tapas tapyate (he does austerities). (The rest of the commentary is the same as the second paragraph in Brhad-vaisnava- tosani.)

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Thinking about what angry Indra had done, He talks to Himself, in five verses. The rain was out of season (apartu = apagatah rtuh yasya tat) and abounded in hailstones (sila-mayam = sila-pracuram).

### 10.25.16

*tatra pratividhim samyag atma-yogena sadhaye \|*  
*lokesa-maninam maudhyad dharisyesri-madam tamah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatra—in that regard; pratividhim—the counteraction; samyak—fully (or properly); atma-yogena—by My mystic might; sadhaye—I accomplish; loka-isa-maninam—of those who think themselves the controllers of the world; maudhyat—out of foolishness; harisye—I dispel; sri-madam—the false pride due to wealth; tamah—the ignorance.

*(aham) tatra pratividhim atma-yogena samyak sadhaye. (aham) maudhyat lokesa-maninam sri-madam tamah harisye.*

**Перевод:**

**“By My mystic might I am fully effecting the counteraction of it. I remove the ignorance, the false pride due to wealth, of those who out of foolishness consider themselves the controllers of the world.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

In this verse He says His lifting Govardhana involves a statement of purpose. “By My ability (atma-yogena = sva-samarthyena), I will bring about a counteraction in that regard, and by doing so I will dispel the ignorance, the false pride of wealth, of those who, due to foolishness, consider themselves the controllers of the world.” With the plural, in lokesa-maninam, He means to signify Varuna and others.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“I am properly (samyak)—by way of demon¬strating the glory of My best servant and thereby making everyone happy—effecting (sadhaye = sadhayami) the counteraction.” The present tense is used with the intent to express the occurrence right at that time; the same applies ahead, with gopaye (10.25.18).

“I will remove the ignorance of those who out of foolishness consider themselves, one by one, the controller of the world.” The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami. Another interpretation of atma-yogena is: atmano yogena upayena lilaya sri-govardhana-dharanadina, “by a means, a pastime, of Mine such as holding Govardhana.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“By My yoga, My inherent potency known as Yogamaya, I am properly—by way of demonstrating the glory of My best servant and thereby making everyone happy—effecting (sadhaye = sadhayami) the counteraction.” The present tense is used by the rule: vartamana-samipye, “When the sense is nearness to the present, the present tense is optionally used to indicate the near past or the near future” (Astadhyayi 3.3.131). The plural in lokesa-maninam is used with the intent to signify that He will give a lesson to others too by that punishment.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Pratividhim means pratikaram (counteraction). “By My Yogamaya I will dispel (harisye = harisyami) the ignorance, the false pride of wealth, of those who consider themselves the controllers of the world.”

**Комментарий. Автор Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa:**

Atma-yogena means: atmanah yogena acintyena prabhavena (by My inconceivable might).

### 10.25.17

*na hi sad-bhava-yuktanam suranam isa-vismayah \|*  
*matto ’satam mana-bhahgah prasamayopakalpate \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—not; hi—because; sat-bhava-yuktanam—who are endowed with a good mode of being; suranam—of the gods; isa-vismayah—the specific arrogance regarding God; mattah—from Me; asatam—of those who are not good; mana-bhahgah—breaking the conceit; prasamaya—for the abatement; upakalpate—is fit.

*Sanatana Gosvami / Jiva Gosvami*

*hi sad-bhava-yuktanam suranam isa-vismayah na upakalpate, mattah asatam (tesam) mana-bhahgah prasamaya (bhavati).*

**Перевод:**

**“Since it is improper that the gods, who are endowed with a good mode of being, have the overweening pride: “I am God,” My crushing of that conceit of them who have turned out bad is for the sake of an eminent fixity of their intelligence on Me.**

**Or: “The gods, who have a good mode of existence, find no amazement in the Lord? The discontinuation of the righteous’ respect for Me is fit for being abated nearby.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“But,” it might be objected, “the gods are in the mode of goodness and are Your devotees, so how can they possibly have ignorance?” In that regard He says: “Because the overweening pride: “We are the gods” (isa-vismayah = isah vayam iti vismayah garvah) of the gods, who are endowed with goodness, or else with bhakti to Me (sad-bhavah = sattvam mad-bhaktih va), does not occur, they are bad (na hi = vasman na ghatate 'to ’santas te)." Moreover, in the second half of the verse He says: “Breaking their conceit is just a favor.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

(Additions are underlined.) They are bad in the sense that their actions are bad, due to the false pride of wealth. The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami. Alternatively, in this verse He talks about the reason for this: sri-madam harisye, “I will dispel the false pride of wealth” (in the previous verse): hi yatah suranam iso ’ham iti visesena smayo garvah nopakalpate yogyo na bhavati, yatah sad-bhava-yuktanam, atah sri-madenasatam api tesam hitam eva karisyami, “Because the gods’ distinct overweening pride: “I am god” is improper, insofar as they have a good mode of being, I will only do what is beneficial for them although they are bad on account of the false pride of wealth.” That is what He is says with mattah (the breaking of their pride “by Me”), which denotes nanyatah (not by anyone else)... “on account of having a qualification for a glimpse of My aisvarya. ”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(In addition to the above:) Prasamaya means: prakrstah samah santih sukham va, kimva tan-nistha-buddhita tasmai bhavati, “for the sake of an eminent peacefulness, or an eminent happiness, or an eminent condition of having the intelligence fixed on Me,” by the Lord’s statement: samo man-nisthata buddheh, “Equanimity is the intelligence’s steadiness in Me” (Bhagavatam 11.19.36).”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In this verse He says: “I am not competing with Indra, who is extremely insignificant, rather out of mercy I am curing the vice in him, my devotee, that has arisen.”

“Because (hi = yasmat) the gods, who are endowed with goodness—or with bhakti to Me (sad-bhavah = sattvam mad-bhaktih va)—do not have the distinct overweening pride: “We are gods” (isa- vismayah = isah vayam iti visistah smayah garvah),191therefore the very fact of shattering the high respect (mana = manasya = adarasya) of them who are bad, due to being on a bad path at present, is for the sake of alleviating the disease of overweening pride (prasamaya = garva-rogasya upasantyai).”

**Комментарий. Автор Vijayadhvaja Tirtha:**

What is the purpose of removing the ignorance? In this verse He says: It is for the sake of destroying the ego, which is the ultimate cause of the bondage of samsara (material life, transmigration). With mattah and so on He says: The overweening pride (smayah = atyulbana-darpah): “I am god” is not the nature of the righteous. Prasamaya means prakrsta-man-nisthayai (for an eminent fixity in Me).

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

“The break of the conceit of unrighteous persons, done through one of them, is for the sake of everyone’s serenity and is appropriate nearby (prasamayopakalpate = sarvesam eva prasamaya bhavati upa samipe ca kalpate).”

### 10.25.18

*tasman mac-charanam gostham man-natham mat-parigraham \|*  
*gopaye svatma-yogena so ’yam me vrata ahitah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**
