tasmat—therefore; mat-saranam—whose shelter is I; gostham— the cowherd community; mat-natham—whose master is I; mat- parigraham—My family and entourage; gopaye—I protect; sva-atma-yogena—by My own mystic might; sah ayam—that well-known; me—by Me; vratah—vow; ahitah—was pledged.

*tasmad (aham) mac-charanam man-natham mat-parigraham gostham svatma-yogena gopaye. sah ayam vratah me ahitah (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Therefore, by My own mystic might I will save this cowherd community. I observe that well-known oath of Mine. I am their shelter and master, and they are My family and entourage.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“I will protect (gopaye - raksisyami).” Moreover: “That obligation—or that resolve (vratah = niyamah sahkalpo va)— is observed (ahitah = dhrtah) by Me (me = maya)."

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“Only I am its protector (mac-charanam - aham eva saranam raksita yasya tat) because only I am its Lord (man-natham = aham eva nathah isvarah yasya tat), otherwise there would be a diminution of the aisvarya of Mine alone. Additionally, it is My family (mat-parigraham = mama kutumbam)... so it must be saved, even with a wrongdoing.”

Or: “It is My shelter (mac-charanam = mama asrayam). It maintains Me (man-natham = mama paripalakam).” How? “Their sons, wives, and others are not their family; I am their family: to them I am the only dear one (mat-parigraham = aham eva parigraham na putra-daradi-sarvam yasya tat = mad-eka-priyam).”

“I protect (gopaye = raksami) with My yoga, a special power of Mine, for My own (sva = svesu nimittesu). Or I protect with a special power of Mine which is resplendent (su = susobhana), that is to say it consists of a worldly pastime accompanied with an extraordinary aisvarya" Someone might think: “That entails a clearly visible and extraordinary aisvarya here.” In that regard He says so ’yam and the rest (I observe that well-known oath of Mine), otherwise that would constitute a break in His vow: sakrd eva prapanno yah, and so on “I bestow constant fearlessness to one who, just once, surrenders, and beseeches Me by saying: “I am Yours.” This is My oath” (Ramayana, quoted in the Tosanis 10.2.26). Alternatively: vratah pratijna me maya ahito drdham dhrtah, “That oath is firmly observed by Me.” Exposing the arrogant pride of a maha-vira is for the sake of pacifying the cowherds.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

“Because Indra showers rain to destroy the residents of the village (gostha), such as My father, who consider Me as one of their own, therefore (tasmat) with My yoga, i.e. an uncommon, inherent force, right now I will protect (gopaye = samprati eva gopayisyami) this very cowherd community, that is to say: Not only right now: That was done time and time again previously. This very obligation of Mine, the form of saving the cowherd community, was sworn (so ’yam me vrata ahitah = ayam gosthasya palana-rupah mama niyamah eva vihitah). And as a concurrent occurrence I will dispel the ignorance of all the controllers of world.”

What is the cowherd community like? In that regard He says mac-charanam and so on: “Only I am its protector because only I am its master. Additionally, it is My family (mat-parigraham = mama kutumbam), hence it must be saved, even with a wrongdoing,” like in:

*vrddhau ca mata-pitarau sadhvi bharya sutah sisuh \|*  
*apy akarya-satam krtva bhartavya manur abravit \|\|*

**“Manu said: Old parents, a saintly woman, the wife, a son, and an infant should be supported even by doing hundreds of misdeeds” (marked in Manu-smrti as a spurious verse between 11.10 and 11.11).**

Alternatively: “It is My shelter (mac-charanam = mama asrayam). It maintains Me (man-natham = mama paripalakam).” How? “Their all in all is only 1.1 am the only dear one. Therefore I protect.” Being a natural thing to do is implied by the use of the present tense, and so it is said: atma-yogena. Consequently the words so ’yam (well-known) refer to this: Sah (that) means “My oath has been established from time immemorial,” and ayam (this) signifies “It and has come about now also.” The reason for that is: “That vow, the promise, is Mine (me = mama), who am the Lord and have pastimes as an eternal human form, and so it is observed in all its aspects (ahitah = sarvamsena dhrtah).

The following is meant: “I will break Indra’s arrogance to protect the community, given that Indra has the habit of opposing the cowherds, who take shelter of Me, and is not inclined to take shelter of Me.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Also because he did what he did, a critical situation is at hand, therefore I protect this cowherd community. It is a form of My home (mac-charanam = mama saranam grha-rupam). Anekartha-varga (the third chapter of Amara-kosa) states: saranam grha-raksitroh, “Saranam means home, and protector” (Amara-kosa 3.3.52).

With man-natham He says: “Only I am the master of this home.” Moreover: “In it is My entourage: My father, brother, beloveds, and others (mat-parigraham = mama parigrahah pitr-bhratr-preyasyadayo yatra tat). Next He says: “I do not only protect from this critical situation, I also protect from all critical situations, even from the time of the great pralaya.” “This well-known obligation was assumed by Me (so 'yam me vrata ahitah = prasiddho 'yam niyamo may a grhitah).”

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

The atmanepada in gopaye is poetic license.

### 10.25.19

*ity uktvaikena hastena krttvagovardhanacalam \|*  
*dadhara lilaya krsnaschatrakam iva balakah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

iti—in this way (or it marks the end of the quotation); uktva— having spoken; ekena hastena—with one hand; krttva—after cutting; govardhana-acalam—the hill named Govardhana194; dadhara—He held; lilaya—playfully; krsnah—Krsna; chatrakam—a mushroom; iva—like; balakah—a child.

*iti (sva-manasi) uktva krsnah govardhanacalam ekena hastena krttva, balakah iva chatrakam (dharati, enam) lilaya dadhara.*

**Перевод:**

**Having said this, Krsna cut off Govardhana Hill with one hand and playfully held it like a child tears off a mushroom and holds it.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Krttva means utkrttya (by cutting). Chatrakam means ucchilindhram (mushroom).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“With one hand” is said because of the statement of Hari-vamsa: savyena panina, “with the left hand” (2.18.31), and also because in that way Krsna showed off His body.

Govardhana is well known by that name in the groups of big mountains. Or it is so called in terms of being a benefiter of cows (gavam hita-krt): It is a mountain by the derivation: na katham api kadapi calati iti acalah, “It does not move in any way at any time, and so it is acala."

He easily (lilaya - anayasena) held it—or He held it with a special curvature such as the pose of His glorious right hand placed on His hip—because: He is Visnu, whose boyhood was accomplished. Or the sense is He is Nanda’s little boy (balakah = kalita-balyah sri-nanda-kumaro va). Thus, there was no transgression of balya-lila in holding it, and so only a special balya-lila is illustrated by that. The name Visnu is by the etymology: visvam vyapnoti iti visnuh, “He pervades the world, and so He is Visnu,” hence the idea that an effort was involved is automatically repudiated. Or balakah belongs to the example: “like some boy holds a mushroom.” In this way too, the sense is the same.

In addition, the word chatrakam (mushroom) suggests this: Krsna held all of Sri Govardhana only by holding its base like a person holds a whole mushroom by holding the bottom of its stem with one hand. This meaning was intended by Sri Vaisampayana: The hill was held by Him while He had a gigantic form unnoticed by people. For instance:

*sa dhrtah sangato meghair girih savyena panina \|*  
*grha-bhavam gatas tatra grhakarena varcasa \|\|*

**“That hill, conjoined with clouds, was held with the left hand. Because of a magnificence as the form of a home, at that time the mountain became as good as a home.” (Hari-vamsa 2.18.31)**

*apluto ’yam girih paksair iti vidyadharoragah \|*  
*gandharvapasarasas caiva vac ’muhcata sarvasah \|\|*

**“The Vidyadharas, the Nagas, the Gandharvas, and the Apsaras collectively exclaimed: “This hill jumped with wings.”” (Hari-vamsa 2.18.37)**

Otherwise, had He held the mountain with His very own hand, which is small, a very little height would have been obtained and as a result those statements would be incongruous. It is understood that holding it while being a gigantic form was just for the fun of dispersing the clouds with the peaks of Sri Govardhana, and so He held it as a pastime (lilaya), with the left hand. In truth, by letting them know that He had no fatigue, holding the hill was only for the purpose of enlivening those people of Vraja, whose sole concern is His happiness even by disregarding their own lives. Otherwise, had all of them perished, an immense grief would have ensued. Or He held it just the way He was, that is, His body was not colossal, in such a way that Govardhana was high.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

At first the verse states: ity uktva (having this said). This means: Afterward, at the outset of the arrival of huge clouds, He led everyone to a place near Govardhana. He held it with the left hand, on account of the statement of Hari-vamsa: savyena panina, “with the left hand” (2.18.31). “He cut it off” (krttva = chittva) from the base and lifted it up: This is understood, since it was disjoined from the north ofa, because of the renown even nowadays of that area, well known from Vardha Purana:

*tesam samraksanarthaya dhrto giri-varo maya \|*  
*so ’nnakuta iti khyatah sarvatah sakra-pujitah \|\|*

**“I held the best of hills to save them. It, well-known Annakuta, is always worshiped by Indra.”195**

As a pun, acala (mountain) means: na katham api kadacid pi calati, “It does not move in any way at any time.” He easily (lilaya = anayasena) held it—or He held it with a special curvature such as the pose of His glorious right hand on His hip, owing to a darsana of His same body in that way—because: balakas chatrakam iva (like a child picks up and holds a mushroom). The drift is He did not deviate from balya-lila. It is thus shown that there was no effort involved.

How did the body of a child lift the mountain? In that regard he says: visnuh, in other words: By the inconceivable potency, He is the pervader (visnuh = vibhuh) even in that form. In the reading krsnah, the sense is the same. It is stated in that way in Sahasra-nama Stotra: anirdesya-vapuh sriman ameyatma mahadri-dhrk, “His body cannot be defined. He has splendor. His Soul is immeasurable. He sustained the great mountain (Kurma sustained Mandara)” (Visnu-sahasra-nama Stotra 32). Therefore the gist is the mountain became as high as desired. Consequently there is a statement by Sri Vaisampayana: sa dhrtah sangato meghaih, “The hill was conjoined with clouds” (Hari-vamsa 2.18.31). Similarly: apluto ’yam girih... (see above). It is understood that this was just for the fun of dispersing the clouds with the peaks of Sri Govardhana.

In that regard, it’s inferred that He lifted Govardhana as follows: For the sake of being easily seen by the community, for the sake of a special resplendence and for the sake of holding it easily, upon disjoining the mountain from the portion of the mountain below ground, He ascended, in conformity with lila-sakti, one pile of rocks which looked like a paved mosaic and was located in a hollow in the middle. He sustained the middle part of the bottom of the mountain with one divine hand, and joyfully held it. Even hundreds of justifications regarding a refutation of the arrival of the outside water into the middle of the hollow are to be understood only in conformity with lila-sakti. For example, in Sri Hari-vamsa: sa dhrtah sangato... (see above).

Thus, He held it as a pastime, with the left hand. In truth, by letting them know that He had no fatigue, holding the hill was only for the purpose of gladdening the people of Vraja, whose sole concern is His happiness, even by disregarding their own lives. Otherwise, had all of them perished, an immense grief would have ensued. All the rest about it is to be inferred in that way.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“After talking to Himself in this way (ity uktva = iti sva-gatam uktva), He uprooted it with one hand, the left one.” That is said in Hari-vamsa: sa dhrtah sangato... (see above).

He held it as if it were a mushroom (chatrakam iva = silindhram iva). This is understood: When He wanted to lift it, the rain, though it was such, was moved in the sky by the Samhariki potency, an amsa of Yogamaya, so that the turban, the clothes, etc., of the Lord, who was running with great speed from the porch of His house to lift Govardhana, did not get too wet.

### 10.25.20

*athaha bhagavan gopan he ’mba tata vrajaukasah \|*  
*yathopajosam visata giri-gartam sa-go-dhanah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

atha—afterward; aha—spoke; bhagavan—the Lord; gopan—to the cowherds; he amba—O mother; tata—O father; vraja-okasah—O you whose abode is Vraja; yatha-upajosam—if it be your pleasure; visata—enter; giri-gartam—the hollow of the hill; sa-go-dhanah—you, with the cows.

*atha bhagavan gopan (prati) aha (sma): he amba! (he) tata! (he) vrajaukasah! (yuyam sarve) sa-go-dhanah giri-gartam yathopajosam visata.*

**Перевод:**

**Afterward, the Lord addressed the cowherds: “Dear mother and father! Hey all of you residents of Vraja! Enter the hollow of the mountain with the cows, if you please!**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Yathopajosam means yatha-sukham (as you please).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

He spoke afterward, that is, after He had lifted Govardhana. Only a complete lack of effort is implied, otherwise He would have been unable to speak.

The vocative for the mother: he amba, at first is due to a special affection. Or it was because of seeing the rain of angry Indra, which was caused by her son. Or it was for the purpose of consoling her on account of that rain; she was overwhelmed by the sorrow of anxiety by suspecting that her son was in trouble. And after that, he tata (O father), since she will enter only once he has entered. Or it was in order to make him breathe a little: he was alarmed by the distress of the whole cowherd community. Another explanation is the vocative for both of them separately at the outset is because everyone else will enter only once those two get in.

The gist of the vocative he vrajaukasah is: Residing in the village will happen in the same way here. “Enter in accordance with your respective joie de vivre (yathopajosam = sva-sva-prity-anusarena).” The fact that the hollow was not crowded, and so on, is made to be perceived. For instance, in Hari-vamsa, He said:

*sailotpatana-bhur esa mahati nirmita maya \|*  
*trailokyam apy utsahate raksitum kim punar vrajam \|\|*

**“This gigantic land where the mountain was uprooted was fashioned by Me. It can protect the three worlds, let alone Vraja.” (2.18.56-57)**

The hollow of the mountain denotes the part of the ground where the base of the mountain was uprooted (giri-gartam = gireh gartam = tan-mulotpatana-bhu-bhagam).

They were accompanied by the cows, which are the wealth (go-dhana = gavah eva dhanani tat-sahitah). Or they were with the cows and with other wealth, things such as jewels, gold, and silver. All the animals are indicated by the word go.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

How did all of Vraja fit in a hollow of Govardhana, given that the size of Vraja is described in Hari-vamsa as: madhye yojana-vistaram tavad-dvi-gunam ayatam, “In the hollow, it was eight miles in breadth and twice as much in length” (Hari-vamsa 2.9.21)? It is because it became very large by His inconceivable potency. For instance, in Sri Hari-vamsa, He said: sailotpatana-bhur esa... (see above).

(Additions are underlined.) The hollow of the mountain denotes the part of the ground where the base of the mountain was uprooted: There is a justification only in a hollow, in consideration of being surrounded by winds and so forth.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

How could all the inhabitants of Vraja fit at the base of Govardhana, which measures three krosasi In truth, even the strikes of hundreds of thunderbolts hurled by furious Indra were felt by Sri Govardhana, who had an inconceivable vitality only from the bliss of the touch of the Lord’s hand, as though flower garlands were being slammed on his back, so that all the people located in the town of Vraja (vraja-nagara), which measures four yojanas, and all the animals such as cows resided at the base of the hill in such a way that there was enough room. Therefore, in Hari- vamsa the Lord said: sailotpatana-bhur esa... (see above).

Moreover, this is understood: The animals, such as deer and hogs, and the birds, all of which were on top of Govardhana, noticed the clouds, which were raining and had reached the mountain slopes—according to Hari-vamsa: sa dhrtah sangato meghaih, “The hill was conjoined with clouds” (2.18.31)—ascended to high mountain peaks, and did not have any trouble, not even one bit.

### 10.25.21

*na trasa iha vah karyo mad-dhastadri-nipatena \|*  
*vata-varsa-bhayenalam tat-tranam vihitam hi vah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

na—not; trasah—fearing; iha—here; vah—by you; karyah—should be done; mat-hasta—from My hand; adri—of the mountain; nipatena—due to the fall; vata—of the wind; varsa—and of the rain; bhayena alam—enough of the fear; tat-tranam—deliverance from those two; vihitam—is arranged; hi—since; vah—your.

*iha (giri-garte sthitanam) vah mad-dhastadri-nipatena trasah karyah na (bhavati). vata-varsa-bhayena alam, hi vah tat-tranam (maya) vihitam (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Here, you should not fear that the hill will fall from My hand. Enough of being afraid of the wind and the rain: I have arranged for your deliverance from them.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“We fear that at some point in time it might fall from Your hand, since You’re a boy.” He responds to that here. “Fearing a continuous fall (nipatanat = nitaram patanat)—the suffix i\[n\] in patana is used without a change in meaning—of the mountain from My hand—or a fall because of someone, such as Indra—is not worthy of being done by you all (vah = yusmabhih yusmakam va) (karyah = kartum na yogyo bhavati). Therefore enough of the fear of the wind and the rain,” meaning there is no purpose in being afraid (alam = prayojanam na asti).

Alternatively, “You should not fear, because (hi = yatah) your deliverance from the wind and the rain has been arranged by Me due to your fear of those two (vata-varsa-bhayena = vata- varsa-bhayena hetuna)." Or, “Your deliverance has been effected by you (vah = yusmabhih), by your worship of Govardhana.” Or “Your deliverance from them has been arranged by Govardhana... otherwise how could I, a little boy, possibly hold this gigantic mountain?” The name Govardhana is not mentioned out of respect, in order to evoke their faith.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Nipatanat signifies nipatanat. The causative suffix nic is used without a change in meaning. “You should not fear that the mountain will slip (ni = nilaram) from My hand.” The pronoun vah stands for yusmakam. The genitive case is ordained by the rule: krtyanam kartari va (Astadhyayi 2.3.71) (visnukrtyanam kartari sasthi va, HNV 647). Or “Do not fear that the mountain will slip from My hand because of Indra or some other reason.” “Therefore enough of the fear of the wind and the rain—that is, there is no purpose in being afraid (alam = prayojanam na asti)—, because (hi = yasmat) your deliverance, by means of lifting the mountain, has been arranged by Me.” Or, “Your deliverance has been effected by you (vah = yusmabhih), by your worship of Govardhana.”

### 10.25.22

*tatha nirvivisur gartam krsnasvasita-manasah \|*  
*yathavakasam sa-dhanah sa-vrajah sopajivinah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatha—in that way; nirvivisuh—they entered; gartam—the hollow; krsna—by Krsna; asvasita—were reassured; manasah—they whose minds; yatha-avakasam—as much as there was room; sa-dhanah— accompanied by their wealth; sa-vrajah—accompanied by the village; sa-upajivinah—accompanied by the dependants.

*(te vrajaukasah) tatha krsnasvasita-manasah sa-dhanah sa-vrajah sopajivinah yathavakasam gartam nirvivisuh.*

**Перевод:**

**Thus reassured by Krsna, they entered the hollow beneath the mountain and were followed by their cattle, by their dependants and by the whole village, as much as the empty space allowed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Sa-vrajah means sakata-mandala-sahitah (accompanied by the bunch of carts). Sopajivinah means bhrtya-purohitadi-sahitah (accompanied by the servants, the priests, et al.).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

(The commentary is the same.)

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Their minds were pacified in this way, i.e. by such a clever discourse and by easily holding the mountain with His left hand, by Krsna, the Lord who attracts the hearts of all and whose pastimes are utterly amazing. The inhabitants of Vraja were accompanied by their wealth, that is, they were with their valuables and with their cows.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(In addition to the above:) “They entered in such a way that the place was not crowded (yathavakasam = asahkirnataya),” inasmuch as Govardhana is very expansive. Nowadays, however, in Kali yuga, most of Govardhana is covered. It is said in Hari-vamsa:

*ayam dhrto maya sailah prthvi-grha-nibhopamah \|*  
*trasyate sa-vraja ga vai mad-vasyas ca bhavisyati \|\|*  
*sa dhrtah sangato meghair girih savyena panina \|*  
*grha-bhavam gatas tatra grhakarena varcasa \|\|*

**‘“Once I lift the mountain, it will look like a mountain cave. In that way the cows and the rest of the village will be saved. I will keep them under My control.’ By His power, with His left hand Krsna lifted the mountain up into the clouds. The mountain became a home for everyone.” (Hari-vamsa 3.18.29 and 31)**

### 10.25.23

*ksut-trd-vyatham sukhapeksam hitva tair vraja-vasibhih \|*  
*viksyamano dadharadrim saptaham nacalat padat \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

ksut—of hunger; trt—and thirst; vvatham—the pain; sukha—of comfort; apeksam—expectation; hitva—rejecting; taih vraja- vasibhih—by those inhabitants of the village; viksyamanah—being gazed at; dadhara—He held; adrim—the mountain; sapta-aham—for seven days; na acalat—He did not move; padat—from the position.

*(sah krsnah) ksut-trd-vyatham sukhapeksam (ca) hitva taih vraja- vasibhih viksyamanah saptaham (vyapya) adrim dadhara. (sah krsnah) padat na acalat.*

**Перевод:**

**While the inhabitants of the village were gazing at Him by negating the pain of hunger and thirst and by forgoing any expectation of comfort, Krsna held the mountain for seven days and did not budge.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Krsna did not move from His position (padat = sthanat).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The inhabitants of Vraja, including the cowherds and the cattle, forgot all about their pain caused by hunger and thirst and about pleasures such as lying down. Krsna was observed by them in special ways (viksyamanah = visesena iksyamanah), that is, with great amazement and with much affection. The sense is He was their very life. Looking at Him was not only the reason they gave up their pain and their expectations of comfort, it was also the purpose of giving those up. That they gazed at Him helped Him hold the mountain, since they made Him joyful that way. It is said in Visnu Parana:

*krsno’ pi tam dadharaiva sailam atyanta-niscalam \|*  
*vrajauka-vasibhir harsa-vismitaksair niriksitah \|\|*  
*gopa-gopi-janair hrstaih priti-vistariteksanaih \|*  
*sarhstuyamana-caritah krsnah sailam adharayat \|\|*

**“Krsna held the mountain, which was completely stable. Gazed at by the general population of Vraja, whose joyful eyes were amazed, and His deeds extolled by the elated gopas and gopis, whose eyes were widened by love, Krsna upheld the mount.” (VP 5.11.20-21)**

Or the clause “ksut-trd-vyatham sukhapeksam hitva” modifies Krsna: He gave up pain and any expectation of comfort. Due to the Vrajavasis’ glancing, He had no desire to sleep. He did not budge from the place where He had planted His feet. It is thus said that holding the mountain was very easily done.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The Vrajavasis gave up their pain caused by hunger and thirst simply by gazing at Him. It is said that way in Visnu Purana: vrajauka-vasibhir harsa... (see above).

It’s understood that Krsna stood by facing everyone. By continuously drinking the nectar of the beauty and sweetness of Krsna, the Vrajavasis felt no hunger, thirst or fatigue. Krsna too, by seeing the beautiful forms of His beloved gopis, forgot about eating, drinking and sleeping. The seven days of continuous rain from the Samvartaka clouds failed to flood the district of Mathura because the Lord, simply by His iccha-sakti (desire potency), immediately dried up the water as it fell to the ground. To the Vrajavasis, the seven days seemed like half an hour.

### 10.25.24

*krsna-yoganubhavam tam nisamyendro ’tivismitah \|*  
*nistambhobhrasta-sahkalpah svan meghan sannyavarayat \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

krsna-yoga—of Krsna’s mystic power; anubhavam—the might; tam—that; nisamya—upon seeing; indrah—Indra; ad-vismitah— very amazed; nistambhah—he whose false pride is gone; bhrasta—is thwarted; sankalpah—he whose resolve; svan—own; meghan— clouds; samnyavarayat—held back.

*indrah krsna-yoganubhavam tam nisamya advismitah nistambhah bhrasta-sahkalpah svan meghan sannyavarayat.*

**Перевод:**

**When Indra beheld the might of Krsna’s mystic power, his amazement rose and his hubris was crushed. His desire thwarted, he called back his clouds.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“Indra saw (nisamya = drstva) the might (anubhavam = prabhavam) of Krsna’s special natural power (yoga = svabhavika-sakti-visesa)."" The Visva-kosa states: srutau drstau nisamanam, “The verbal base nisam means to hear or to see.”

Indra lost his arrogance (nistambhah = nasta-madah). Why? bhrasta-sankalpah, his desire to hurt the cowherd community was thwarted. He called back his clouds. The prefix sam signifies that the clouds were not even allowed to remain at some distance.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Indra called back his clouds, because he was afraid: “I don’t know what kind of punishment Krsna intends to give me.”

### 10.25.25

*kham vyabhram uditadityam vata-varsam ca darunam \|*  
*nisamyoparatamgopan govardhana-dharo ’bravit \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

kham—the sky; vi-abhram—in which the clouds are gone; udita-adityam—in which the sun has arisen; vata-varsam—the tempest (“wind and rain”); ca—and; darunam—fierce; nisamya—upon seeing; uparatam—had stopped; gopan—to the cowherds; govardhana-dharah—the holder of Govardhana; abravit—spoke.

*kham vyabhram uditadityam vata-varsam ca darunam uparatam nisamya govardhana-dharah gopan (prati) abravit.*

**Перевод:**

**Seeing that the fierce tempest had ceased, the sky was cloudless and the sun had reappeared, the holder of Govardhana spoke to the cowherds.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Krsna looked sideways. The sentence with the epithet “Govardhana-dhara” is Sukadeva’s statement consisting of his enthusiastic inner vision.

### 10.25.26

*niryata tyajata trasam gopah sa-stri-dhanarbhakah \|*  
*uparatam vata-varsam vyuda-prayas ca nimnagah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

niryata—get out; tyajata—give up; trasam—fear; gopah—hey cowherd men; sa—along with; stri—the women; dhana—the wealth; arbhakah—and children; uparatam—has ceased; vata-varsam— the tempest; vi-uda—devoid of water; prayah—almost; ca—and; nimnagah—the rivers (“they go down”).

*gopah! (yuyam) sa-stri-dhanarbhakah niryata. (yuyam) trasam tyajata. vata-varsam uparatam (asti). nimnagah ca vyuda-prayah (santi iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Cowherd men! You, along with your women, children and belongings, may go. Give up all fear. The tempest is over, and the rivers are almost dry.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Vyuda-prayah means the rivers are no longer overflowing.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Their wealth (dhana) refers to their cattle, or else to their cattle and belongings.

### 10.25.27

*tatas te niryayur gopah svam svam adaya go-dhanam \|*  
*sakatodhopakaranam stri-bala-sthavirah sanaih \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatah—afterward; te—they; niryayuh—departed; gopah—the cowherd men; svam svam—respective; adaya—after taking; go-dhanam—the wealth of cows; sakata—on the wagons; udha— loaded; upakaranam—\[in such a way that\] the implements; stri— women; bala—children; sthavirah—elderly; sanaih—slowly.

*tatah te gopah stri-bala-sthavirah (ca) sakatodhopakaranam (yatha bhavati tatha) svam svam go-dhanam adaya sanaih niryayuh.*

**Перевод:**

**Thereafter the cowherd men assembled their respective wealth of cows in the manner of loading the wagons and slowly departed along with the women, the children and the elderly.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

They loaded their belongings (upakaranam = dhanadikam). The cowherds’ women and others too slowly departed, otherwise everyone would have collided.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

They departed in such a way that their belongings were mounted on wagons (sakatodhopakaranam = sakatesv arudhany upakaranani yatra tad yatha syat tatha).

### 10.25.28

*bhagavan api tam sailam sva-sthane purva-vat prabhuh \|*  
*pasyatam sarva-bhutanam sthapayamasa lilaya \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

bhagavan—the Lord; api—too; tam—that; sailam—mountain; sva-sthane—in its place; purva-vat—as before; prabhuh—the Almighty; pasyatam sarva-bhutanam—while everyone was looking; sthapayamasa—He put; lilaya—playfully.

*pasyatam sarva-bhutanam bhagavan api prabhuh tam sailam sva- sthane purva-vat lilaya sthapayamasa.*

**Перевод:**

**While everyone was looking on, the almighty Lord playfully put the mountain back in place as before.**

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The genitive case in “pasyatam sarva-bhutanam” has the sense of the locative absolute.

### 10.25.29

*tam prema-vegan nibhrtavrajaukaso*  
*yatha samiyuh parirambhanadibhih \|*  
*gopyas ca sa-sneham apujayan muda*  
*dadhy-aksatadbhir yuyujuh sad-asisah \|\|*  
*(upajati 12)*

**Пословный перевод:**

tam—Him; prema—of love; vegat—by a rush; nibhrtah—happy; vraja-okasah—they whose dwelling is the cowherd village; yatha—suitably; samiyuh—they met; parirambhana-adibhih—by hugging etc.; gopyah—the cowherd ladies; ca—and; sa-sneham— affectionately; apujayan—honored; muda—with joy (or due to excitement); dadhi—with yogurt; aksata—with unbroken grains; adbhih—and with water; yuyujuh—they pronounced; sat—eminent; asisah—benedictions.

*vrajaukasah (gopah) tam (krta-raksam krsnam) prcma-vegat nibhrtah (santah) yatha parirambhanadibhih samiyuh. gopyah ca sa-sneham muda dadhy-aksatadbhih (tam) apujayan, sad-asisah yuyujuh (ca).*

**Перевод:**

**Joyful because of a rush of love, the inhabitants of Vraja met Him in suitable ways by hugging Him and so forth, and the cowherd ladies affectionately honored Him with yogurt, unbroken grains, and water, because of their excitement, and pronounced eminent blessings.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The cowherd men, feeling content (nibhrtah = purnah), approached Him (samiyuh = upajagmuh) by suitably (yatha = yathocitam) hugging Him and so forth. Sad-asisah means sresthan asirvadan (best blessings).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

To describe their joyful reunion, Suka speaks as though he is singing due to an upsurge of love. They approached Him (tam). The sense is: “Him who had held Govardhana to save the cowherd community.” Or else, “The Vrajavasis met Him (samiyuh = militavantah) and hugged Him, etc., although He had shown such godly might.” The reason for that is: prema-vegat, “because of a quickness, an upsurge, of love”; their zeal was caused by Him. The sense is: “with an upsurge of love.” The word adi (etc.) in parirambhanadibhih means they also gave blessings, smelled and kissed His head, took hold of His left arm, and asked Him questions about whether He was tired and the like. They did so suitably (yatha = yathocitam), according to their status either as an elder, an equal or a junior. Sa-sneham is an adverb (affectionately), or it modifies tam (Him). The blessings were like: “Defeat the wicked,” “Protect the righteous,” “Be rich,” “Be powerful,” and “Delight Your kin.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Here the cowherd ladies are those who have vatsala. By the word ca (and), the priests and others are meant. The cowherds honored (a?ujayan = sammanayamasuh) Him with curds and so on and with auspicious words.

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

They became happy (nibhrtah = sukhitah). The cowherd ladies pronounced (yuyujuh = prayuyujuh) the best blessings.

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

The yogurt, the unbroken grains and the water are ingredients for the customary homage among people of a certain region: Yogurt is used to draw a tilaka, unbroken grains of rice are put above it, and water is sprinkled over the top of the head.

### 10.25.30

*yasoda rohini nando ramas ca balinam varah \|*  
*krsnam alihgya yuyujur asisah sneha-katarah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

yasoda—Yasoda; rohini—Rohini; nandah—Nanda; ramah— Balarama; ca—and; balinam—of the strong; varah—the best; krsnam—Krsna; alingya—afterhugging; yuyuyuh—they pronounced; asisah—blessings; sneha—because of affection; katarah—excited.

*yasoda rohini nandah ramah ca balinam varah krsnam alihgya sneha-katarah (santah) asisah yuyujuh.*

**Перевод:**

**Yasoda, Rohini, Nanda, and Rama, who is the best of the strong, embraced Krsna. Overwhelmed by affection, they gave blessings.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Yasoda and others mentioned here were highly affectionate and were behind the other cowherd men and ladies. Rohini’s name is stated before Nanda’s either because she is Yasoda’s assistant or because he gives her extra respect.

Baladeva is the best of the strong (balinam varah): Although he too had the ability to hold Govardhana inasmuch as in his form as Sesa, his amsa, he nonchalantly holds the Earth on one spot on his head, he did not want to interfere because he knew Krsna wanted to do this pastime. Or the sense of “balinam varah” is he gave Krsna a big hug.

Having lost their gravity because of their affection (sneha- katarah — snehena katarah adhirah santah), they gave blessings, which were of this nature: “Protect us for a long time,” “May You always be happy,” and “May all Your desires be fulfilled.”

In ancient images of the holding of Govardhana, this is sometimes seen: The two mothers offer fresh butter to eat, and so on, and the father and the brother lean on Govardhana with their heads. All this is implied by the mention that they were beside themselves (katarah = adhirah) with affection.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Suka points out that these ones, His mother and the others, are very special. The mention of Rama here, in the group of those who have vatsalya, is not inapplicable, simply because he is older than Him. Someone might think: “Balarama is very affectionate, so why did he not assume his form of Sesa and enact the great feat of holding up Govardhana on behalf of his younger brother?” The answer is that Krsna had already planned to do so: “Because I am the one who stopped Indra’s sacrifice and initiated the sacrifice for Govardhana, I Myself shall protect Vraja by lifting Govardhana.”

### 10.25.31

*divi deva-ganah siddhah sadhya gandharva-caranah \|*  
*tustuvur mumucus tustah puspa-varsani parihiva \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

divi—in the heavens; deva-ganah—the gods; siddhah—the perfected beings (yogis accomplished in the siddhis), sadhyah—the Sadhyas; gandharva-caranah—the Gandharvas (musicians) and the Caranas (singers); tustuvuh—praised; mumucuh—they released; tustah— satisfied; puspa-varsani—showers of flowers; parthiva—O king.

*parthiva! divi deva-ganah siddhah sadhyah gandharva-caranah (tam) tustuvuh. (te) tustah puspa-varsani mumucuh.*

**Перевод:**

**In the heavens, the gods, as well as the yogis accomplished in the mystical perfections, the Sadhyas, the celestial musicians and the celestial singers, praised Him to their hearts’ content, and released showers of flowers, O king.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The gods too, not only the Vrajavasis, felt rapture. This is expressed in two verses. Why did they praise Him despite the fact that Indra felt miserable because the sacrifice meant for him was canceled? In that regard Suka says: tustah (content). This means they were joyful, for two reasons: The arrogance of Indra, who was committing a crime, was broken and they witnessed Krsna’s very sweet fun.

With parthiva (O king), Suka addresses Pariksit out of astonishment: the gods were happy that the king of gods was unhappy. Or the idea is the gods favored the Lord over Indra like the citizens favor the king over a senator. It’s understood, however, that Indra was not angry that his arrogance had been crushed.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Here Suka mens to say: The celestial beings were as jubilant as the residents of Vraja.

### 10.25.32

*sankha-dundubhayo nedur divi deva-pracoditah \|*  
*jagur gandharva-patayas tumburu-pramukha nrpa \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sahkha—conches; dundubhayah—kettledrums; neduh—resounded; divi—in the heavens; deva-pracoditah—used by gods; jaguh—sang; gandharva-patayah—the chief Gandharvas; tumburu-pramukhah— among whom the best is Tumburu; nrpa—O king.

*nrpa! deva-pracoditah sankha-dundubhayah divi neduh. (divi) gandharva-patayah tumburu-pramukhah jaguh.*

**Перевод:**

**Conches and kettledrums used by gods resounded in the heavens, and the chief Gandharvas, led by Tumburu, sang, O king.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The instruments were amazingly played (pracoditah = prakarsena coditah = vicitrataya vaditah). Or the sense is the chief Gandharvas were inspired (pracoditah = preritah) by the godly musicians because of the dancing and so forth. “O king! You know what a big festival is like.”

### 10.25.33

*tato 'nuraktaih pasupaih parisrito*  
*rajan sa gosthamsa-balo 'vrajad dharih \|*  
*tatha-vidhany asya krtani gopika*  
*gayantya iyur mudita hrdi-sprsah \|\|*  
*(upajati 12)*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatah—afterward; anuraktaih—affectionate; pasu-paih—by the herdsmen; parisritah—encircled; rajan—O king; sah—He; gostham—to the cowherd village; sa-balah—accompanied by Bala; avrajat—went; harih—Hari; tatha-vidhani—\[deeds\] of this kind; asya—of Him; krtani—the deeds; gopikah—the cowherd women; gayantyah—while singing; iyuh—went; muditah—happy; hrdi- sprsah—of Him who touches the heart (or the gopis, who touch the heart).

*rajan! tatah sah harih sa-balah anuraktaih pasupaih parisritah gostham avrajat. gopikah tatha-vidhani asya hrdi-sprsah (sri-krsnasya) krtani gayantyah muditah (gostham) iyuh (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**Afterward Hari, accompanied by Bala and encircled by the loving herdsmen, went to the cowherd village. The cowherd women too went, joyfully singing such deeds of Him who touched their hearts.**

**Or: Powerful Hari, surrounded by the loving herdsmen, went from there to the village. The cowherd women, joyful while singing such deeds of His, touched the heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“From there” (tatah) means “from Govardhana.” “Such deeds” refers to deeds such as the holding of Govardhana.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

While as if singing in exultation as before, he narrates Krsna’s entrance in the village. “He was surrounded by them” (parisritah = paritah sritah vrtah) because: anuraktaih, they were affectionate. Sah (He) means “the one who held Govardhana to save Vraja.” Sometimes the reading is sva-gostham instead of sa gostham. Once in the village, He went home. Here the name Hari is used in the sense that He dispelled (harana) the Vrajavasis’ afflictions caused by Indra and because He is a charmer (mano-harana). The gopis became more happy than everyone else: they sang. It is thus shown that they had the ability to compose songs right then and there.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Suka means to say: Krsna and His beloveds had met only by exchanging sidelong glances from afar, unnoticed by all; at the time of departure, those girls sang with love.

The gopis sang about His feats from Govardhana (tatah) to the village. Hrdi-sprsah means the gopis touch the heart, that is, both the heart and the mind. Or hrdi-sprsah is an adjective of asya (of Him): Krsna, their lover, touched their hearts.

## Chapter 26 - Krsna’s Divinity is Revealed by Nanda to the Other Cowherds

### 10.26.1

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*evam-vidhani karmani gopah krsnasya viksya te \|*  
*atad-virya-vidah procuh samabhyetya suvismitah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah uvaca—Sri Suka said; evam-vidhani—of this kind; karmani—deeds; gopah—the cowherd men; krsnasya—of Krsna; viksya—beholding; te—they; atat-virya-vidah—not knowing His prowess; procuh—spoke; samabhyetya—having assembled; su¬vismitah—very astonished.

*sri-sukah uvaca—te gopah krsnasya evam-vidhani karmani viksya su-vismitah atad-virya-vidah (santah) samabhyetya procuh.*

**Перевод:**

**Sri Suka said: Beholding such exploits of Krsna, the cowherd men were very astonished. They could not understand His power, and so they held a meeting and spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*sadvise vismitan gopan krsnasyadbhuta-karmabhih \|*  
*nando gargoktim asravya tad aisvaryam avarnayat \|\|*

**“In the twenty-sixth chapter, Nanda relates to the cowherd men, who were amazed by Krsna’s wonderful deeds, the words of Garga Rsi, thus describing to them His godly might.”**

**10.26.1**

“They approached Nanda” (samabhetya = nandam abhigamya).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Sukadeva begins this narration for two reasons: to avert the possibility that the Vrajavasis’ love for Krsna might decrease as a result of knowing, after seeing the Lord’s power, that He has godly might and to increase their love for Him once Nanda clears their doubts.

They saw such deeds of Krsna; this means His deeds are extraordinary. The plural is used to include all the previous events. The cowherds did not care to know that Krsna is powerful; that is why they loved Him so much. Utterly amazed at the turn of events, they courteously approached Nanda and spoke eminently (procuh = prakarsena ucuh), that is, either by propounding a logical reasoning or in such a way that their discourse culminates in love.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*sadvimse tu tad-aisvaryanaisvaryeksana-sahkinah \|*  
*gopan prabodhayamasa nando gargokti-gauravaih \|\|*

**“In the twenty-sixth, this is described: The cowherd men were doubtful because Krsna seemed to be both godly and mortal, and so Nanda enlightened them by means of the authority of Garga’s statements.”**

During the lifting of Govardhana Hill, the cowherd men were completely submerged in relishing the nectar of the sweetness of Krsna, and so they had no occasion to analyze the situation. But afterward, once they returned home, they had doubts:

“Having witnessed the deed of lifting of Govardhana Hill, we recall His other deeds, such as the killing of Putana and other demons, extinguishing the forest fire, and so on. At those times, we thought that these things occurred either because of a benediction of the Brahmanas, because of Nanda’s great fortune or because of the boy, having achieved the mercy of Narayana, had become empowered

by the Lord. But all these presumptions were false. He is only seven years of age: For such a boy to hold up the king of mountains for seven days certainly negates any possibility that He is an ordinary human; rather it indicates that He must be God.

On the other hand, He is enlivened by our pampering, although we, including His father and uncles, are simple cowherds. Nor only that, He gets depressed when we don’t pamper Him: He also becomes hungry and thirsty, and goes to steal dairy goods. He also cheats, lies, chatters childishly and tends the calves. Why would He do those things if He is God? Rather they negate the possibility that He is God and seem to prove that He is human. We cannot tell whether one possibility makes more sense than the other, so let’s inquire from Nanda. He is very smart; he will dispel our confusion.” Making up their minds in this way, they entered Nanda’s assembly hall and questioned him, as stated in this verse.

### 10.26.2

*balakasya yad etani karmany atyadbhutani vai \|*  
*katham arhaty asau janma gramyesv atma-jugupsitam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

balakasya—of the boy; yat—because; etani—these; karmani— deeds; ati-adbhutani—very astonishing; vai—indeed; katham— why?; arhati—should; asau—He; janma—a birth; gramyesu—amidst worldly people; atma—to Him; jugupsitam—contemptible.

*yad balakasya etani karmani aty-adbhutani vai (bhavanti, tasmat) asau atma-jugupsitam gramyesu janma katham arhati.*

**Перевод:**

**“These deeds of the boy are utterly astonishing indeed, so why would He deserve a birth in the midst of rustics? It must be despicable to Him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Because (yat = yasmat) these amazing activities occurred, how is it proper for Him to have taken birth in the worldly homes of cowherd men?” Atma-jugupsitam means such a birth does not befit Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“Why would He take a birth which He finds contemptible?” The sense is He might be criticized for that. The pronoun asau (he) signifies that He was not present, since He was in the woods.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The gist of the term atma-jugupsitam is that He does not get involved in whatever is inferior to His status.

### 10.26.3

*yah sapta-hayano balah karenaikena lilaya \|*  
*katham bibhrad giri-varam puskaram gaja-rad iva \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

yah—who; sapta-hayanah—seven years old; balah—a boy; karena ekena—with one hand; lilaya—playfully; katham—how?; bibhrat— while holding; giri-varam—the best mountain; puskaram—a lotus; gaja-rat—the king of elephants; iva—like.

*yah sapta-hayanah balah (bhavati, sah) katham ekena karena, puskaram (bibharti) gaja-rad iva, lilaya giri-varam bibhrat (sthitah).*

**Перевод:**

**“The boy is only seven years of age. How could He playfully hold aloft the best mountain with one hand? He looked like a king of elephants that holds a lotus.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

They describe His amazing deeds. How did He stand while holding it? “Like a mighty elephant (gaja-rat = maha-gajah) holds a lotus (puskaram = padmam).”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

He playfully held Govardhana. An example of how easy this was is given: The example of an elephant holding a lotus implies that a special beauty was involved in the act. The sense is: Therefore He cannot be human.

The Visnu Purana states that He began herding the cows in His seventh year, after coming to Vrndavana in the summer:

*kalena gacchata tau tu sapta-varsau maha-vraje \|*  
*sarvasya jagatah palau vatsa-palau babhuvatuh \|\|*

**“When some time had passed there in great Vraja, those two herders of calves, the two guardians of the entire world, attained the age of seven.” (Visnu Parana 5.6.35)**

Sridhara Svami comments on this citation as follows: “They herded the calves in this way. When some time passed, in Their seventh year of age They became able to herd the cows.”

Afterward, either in that year or in the next, They played in the rainy season. After that, Kaliya was subdued. Thereafter Dhenuka and Pralamba were killed. In the fall, Krsna lifted Govardhana Hill. This is according to Visnu Purana, and so the sequence of events therein must relate to another kalpa. In that way, the contradiction with the text that begins: tatas ca pauganda-vayah-sritau, “Afterward, Krsna and Balarama attained the age of pauganda and were authorized to herd cows” (Bhagavatam 10.15.1) is removed.202

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In twelve verses starting from here, the cowherds say He could not possibly do such deeds if He is not the Lord. Krsna was holding the mountain while standing (bibhrat = bibhrat sthitah).

### 10.26.4

*tokenamilitaksena putanaya mahaujasah \|*  
*pitah stanah saha pranaih kaleneva vayas tanoh \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tokena—by Him, a toddler; a-milita—were completely closed; aksena—whose eyes; putanayah—of Putana; maha-ojasah—of her who had great power; pitah—was sucked; stanah—the breast; saha—with; pranaih—\[with\] her life airs; kalena—by Time; iva— like; vayah—the age; tanoh—of a body.

*(yena) tokena amilitaksena mahaujasah putanayah pranaih saha tanoh vayah iva kalena (piyate), stanah pitah.*

**Перевод:**

**“The toddler, whose eyes were closed, sucked the breast of powerful Putana and thereby sucked out her life force, like the longevity of a body is sucked by Time.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Mahaujasah is an adjective of Putana: she was powerful. This happened in the same way that a body’s lifespan, or else its youth, is sucked by Time. The word katham (how?), in the previous verse, is carried forward.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

When He killed her, His eyes were completely (a = samyak) closed. The word katham is carried forward to this verse and to the next ones. Because all His deeds are wonderful, a birth amidst rustics is not suitable for Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Putana’s breast was sucked by that toddler (tokena = yena balena), whose eyes were slightly (a = isat) closed.” An example of acting imperceivably is given: “like Time drinks away the youthfulness of the body.”

### 10.26.5

*hinvato ’dhah sayanasya masyasya caranav udak \|*  
*ano ’patad viparyastam rudatah prapadahatam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

hinvatah—of Him who was moving; adhah—below; sayanasya—of Him who was resting; masyasya—of Him who is one month old; caranau—both feet; udak—upward; anah—the cart; apatat—fell; viparyastam—upside down; rudatah—who was crying; prapada—by the tip of the foot; ahatam—was hit.

*anah (svasya) adhah sayanasya masyasya udak caranau hinvatah rudatah (yasya balasya) prapadahatam viparyastam (sat) apatat.*

**Перевод:**

**“At three months old, the boy was lying on His back, below a cart. While crying, He kicked His feet upward, and so the cart, hit by the front part of His foot, turned upside down.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Masyasya means “of Him who is three months old” (= masas trayah paricchedakd yasya). “How did the cart fall upside down when struck by the tip of the foot of Him who was waving (hinvatah = calayatah) His feet upward (udak = urdhvam)?”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The cart was lightly struck by the tip of His foot, yet it turned over. That is amazing. His crying is suggestive of His very young age.

The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami. Regarding his explanation of masya, the word literally means that Krsna was one month old, by the derivation: masyasya masa-mdtram vyapya jata-balyasya. The word is formed by the rules: tam adhisto bhrto bhuto bhavi vd (tam adhisto bhrto bhavi, Astadhydyi 5.1.80) and masad vayasi yat khanau (Astadhydyi 5.1.81). But the resultant meaning is “three months old,” by the derivation of masa (one month, i.e. three months) as an eka-sesa compound: masas ca masas ca masas ca masa iti, because of the text: trai-masikasya ca pada sakato ’pavrttah, “The cart was overturned by His foot when He was three months old” (Bhagavatam 2.7.27).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

(The commentary is the same as Bhavartha-dipika.)

### 10.26.6

*eka-hayana asino hriyamano vihayasa \|*  
*daityena yas trnavartam ahan kantha-grahaturam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

eka-hdyanah—one year old; asinah—while sitting; hriyamanah—being kidnapped; vihdyasa—via the sky; daityena—by the demon; yah—who; trndvartam—Trnavarta; ahan—He killed; kantha—on his neck; graha—by a grab; dturam—overwhelmed.

*yah (balah) eka-hayanah asinah daityena vihayasa hriyamanah trnavartam kantha-grahaturam (krtva) ahan.*

**Перевод:**

**“At one year of age, He was sitting. He was taken into the sky by Trnavarta, but the demon, distressed by being grabbed on the neck, was killed by Him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“How did Krsna, who was being kidnapped by a demon, kill that demon Trnavarta?”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The fact that He was merely sitting signifies that He could not walk. The demon was overwhelmed just by being grabbed on the neck (kantha-grahaturam = kantha-grahana-matrena eva aturam) (aturam = vihvalam).

### 10.26.7

*kvacid dhaiyangava-stainye matra baddha ulukhale\|*  
*gacchann arjunayor madhye bahubhyam tav apatayat \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

kvacit—once upon a time; haiyangava—of fresh butter; stainye—given that there was a theft; matra—by His mother; baddhah—tied; ulukhale—on a mortar; gacchan—going; arjunayoh madhye— between two Arjuna \[trees\]; bahubhyam—with both arms; tau apatayat—He made those two fall.

*kvacid dhaiyangava-stainye (sad, yah balah) matra ulukhale baddhah (san) bahubhyam arjunayoh (vrksayoh) madhye gacchan tau apatayat.*

**Перевод:**

**“One time, He was tied to a mortar by His mother because He stole fresh butter. On that occasion, while crawling between two Arjuna trees He made those two trees crash.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Haiyangava-stainye means navanita-caurye (given that there was a theft of fresh butter). Bahubhyam gacchan (going with both arms) means ringan (crawling).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Kvacit means kadacit (on one occasion). The same applies in the next verses. He made the trees fall by crawling with both hands. This shows His force.

### 10.26.8

*vane sancarayan vatsan sa-ramo balakair vrtah \|*  
*hantu-kamam bakam dorbhyam mukhato ‘rim apatayat \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

vane—in the woods; sahcarayan—while tending; vatsan—the calves; sa-ramah—accompanied by Rama; balakaih—by the cowherd boys; vrtah.—surrounded; hantu-kamam—\[Baka,\] desiring to kill; bakam—Baka; dorbhyam—with both arms; mukhatah—by the beak; arim—the enemy; apatayat—tore apart.

*(yah balah) vane vatsan sancarayan sa-ramah balakaih vrtah (atmanam) mukhatah hantu-kamam bakam arim dorbhyam (mukhatah) apatayat.*

**Перевод:**

**“Another time, the boy, accompanied by Rama and surrounded by young cowherds, was tending the calves in the woods. Baka sought to kill Him with its beak, and so with both hands He bifurcated that enemy from the beak.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“How did He tear apart the enemy, which had the guise of crane, by the beak with both arms? That enemy wanted to kill Him by the beak.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Baka wanted to kill Krsna, especially because He killed his sister Putana. In truth, Baka was killed after Vatsasura (10.11.43) (10.11.51). The sequence is out of order since the cowherds were under the spell of amazement.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Having caught Baka with both of His hands (dorbhyam = dorbhyam dhrtva), how did He rip him apart beginning from the mouth (mukhatah = mukham arabhya)?’’

### 10.26.9

*vatsesu vatsa-rupena pravisantam jighamsaya \|*  
*hatva nyapatayat tena kapitthani ca lilaya \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

vatsesu—among the calves; vatsa-rupena—as the form of a calf; pravisantam—who was entering (who had entered); jighamsaya— with the intent to kill; hatva—after killing \[the demon\]; nyapatayat— He made \[the fruits\] fall; tena—by means of that \[demon\]; kapitthani—kapittha fruits; ca—moreover; lilaya—playfully.

*(yah balah) jighamsaya vatsa-rupena vatsesu pravisantam (vatsasuram) lilaya hatva tena (mrta-daitya-sarirena) kapitthani nyapatayat.*

**Перевод:**

**“Upon killing the demon who had entered among the calves by disguising himself as a calf with the intent to kill, He playfully made kapittha fruits fall by using that dead demon.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Vatsasura wanted to kill Him and Rama. Krsna caught both hind legs, whirled him around and threw his body at the top of a big tree, like Rama did in his pastime with Dhenuka, and thus made the fruits fall.

### 10.26.10

*hatva rasabha-daiteyam tad-bandhums ca balanvitah \|*  
*cakre tala-vanam ksemam paripakva-phalanvitam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

hatva—after killing; rasabha—who was a jackass; daiteyam—the demon (“descendant of Diti”); tat-bandhun—his friends; ca— and; bala-anvitah—accompanied by Bala; cakre—He made; tala- vanam—Talavana; ksemam—safe; paripakva—very ripe; phala—fruits; anvitam—which had.

*(yah balah) balanvitah rasabha-daiteyam tad-bandhun ca hatva paripakva-phalanvitam tala-vanam ksemam cakre.*

**Перевод:**

**“By killing, in the company of Balarama, the jackass demon and its friends, He made the Tala forest safe. The fruits in that forest were fully ripe.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“Krsna was accompanied by Bala” (balanvitah). This shows that even though Bala killed Dhenuka, Krsna is predominant in that pastime because Bala’s upsurge of strength occurred only by His power. In that sense, both of Them killed Dhenuka.

Krsna made the forest safe: No one became afraid to go there. This means everyone could enjoy the fruits.

### 10.26.11

*pralambam ghatayitvogram balena bala-salina \|*  
*amocayad vraja-pasun gopams caranya-vahnitah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

pralambam ghayayitva—having caused Pralamba to die; ugram—fierce; balena—by the agency of Bala; bala-salina—who abounds in strength; amocayat—He delivered; vraja-pasun—the animals of the cowherd community; gopan ca—and the cowherd boys; aranya—of the forest; vahnitah—from the fire.

*(yah balah) balena bala-salina ugram pralambam ghatayitva aranya-vahnitah vraja-pasun gopan ca amocayat.*

**Перевод:**

**“The boy got dreadful Pralamba killed by mighty Balarama and then saved the herd and the herdsmen from a conflagration.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

In the killing of Pralamba too, it’s implied Krsna is more important than Balarama, whose special might was obtained by His influence.

### 10.26.12

*asi-visatamahindram damitva vimadam hradat \|*  
*prasahyodvasya yamunam cakre ’sau nirvisodakam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

asi—on the fangs; visa-tama—which has the worst poison; ahi— of snakes; indram—the king; damitva—after taming; vimadam— \[Kaliya,\] devoid of pride; hradat—from the lake; prasahya—by force; udvasya—after making him give up his residence; yamunam— the Yamuna; cakre—He made; asau—He; nirvisa—has no poison; udakam—one whose water.

*(yah) asau asi-visatamahindram prasahya damitva vimadam (tarn) hradat udvasya yamunam nirvisodakam cakre.*

**Перевод:**

**“The boy tamed the king of snakes, which had the most virulent poison on its fangs, made that snake lose its arrogance, expelled it from the lake by force and made the Yamuna poisonless.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Vimadam is an adverb: “Krsna tamed Kaliya in such a way that the snake lost its arrogance.” Or the connection is: vimadam santam hradad udvasya, “Once the snake lost its arrogance, Krsna expelled the snake from the lake.”

### 10.26.13

*dustyajas canurago ’smin sarvesam no vrajaukasam \|*  
*nanda te tanaye ’smasu tasyapy autpattikah katham \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

dustyajah—hard to give up; ca—moreover; anuragah—love; asmin—for Him; sarvesam—all; nah—our; vraja-okasam—us whose residence is the cowherd village; nanda—O Nanda; te— your; tanaye—for the son; asmasu—for us; tasya—His; api—too; autpattikah—natural; katham—how?

*nanda! sarvesam nah vrajaukasam asmin te tanaye anuragah dustyajah (bhavati). asmasu tasya api (anuragah) autpattikah (bhavati iti yat, tat) katham (jatam).*

**Перевод:**

**“Dear Nanda, we and all the other residents of Vraja cannot give up loving your son. And His love for us too is quite natural. How do you explain this?**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Autpattikah means natural. The word katham expresses their doubt: “Perhaps He is the Soul of all.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“Even when we consider the matter, we cannot stop loving Him.” This means their love for Him is natural. “In His case too. His love for us is natural, although we don’t deserve it.”

In Sridhara Svami’s explanation of katham, the sense is Krsna is the soul and they are the body.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In that way, the cowherds proved that Krsna is God, and here they say, “We should also consider one more sign, relative to ourselves and all other residents of Vraja.”

The mention of “your son” implies: “Even when we fully consider that He is your son, not ours.”

“His has affection not only for us cowherd men, who are in the mood of parental love, but also for everyone, even the children, who are in the mood of friendship; for those of other social classes, such as the forest dwellers; and even for the animals and birds.”

The loving attraction is increasing at every moment as though it is ever fresh. This affection is worded as anuraga to signify that it is such (increasing at every moment204), meaning it is not ordinary affection.

“Furthermore, we cannot give it up, because it is natural. Even though we see signs that He is God, we still cannot stop loving Him. Because we love Him more than we love our children, wealth, body, life and soul, such an object of love can only be Paramatma. We think this is who He is. If He were just a human being, this extraordinary affection would not be possible.” “Fine. So you say He is God?” “On second thought, He loves us, all of us, and the forest dwellers. As an atmarama, He should be detached from everything, so how is that kind of love possible in Him? It doesn’t make sense that He has such natural attachment to us, who are in material life.”

### 10.26.14

*kva sapta-hayano balah kva mahadri-vidharanam \|*  
*tato no jayate sanka vraja-natha tavatmaje \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

kva—where?; sapta-hayanah—seven years old; balah—the boy; kva—where?; maha-adri—of the great mountain; vidharanam—the special holding; tatah—therefore; nah—our; jayate—has occurred; sahka—doubt; vraja-natha—O chief of Vraja; tava—your; atmaje— about the son.

*vraja-natha! kva sapta-hayanah balah (bhavati), kva mahadri- vidharanam (bhavati). tatah nah tava atmaje sanka jayate (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Where on the one hand is this seven-year-old boy, and where on the other is His act of holding the great mountain? Therefore, chief of Vraja, we have a doubt about Your son.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Out of amazement, they speak while making dra¬matic gestures.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Here the word sahka is expressive of this doubt: “Is He a boy or some god?”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Given that they have already stated the pastime of lifting Govardhana, the reason they mention it again is that they are astonished.

### 10.26.15

*nanda uvaca*  
*sruyatam me vaco gopa vyetu sanka ca vo ’rbhake \|*  
*enam kumaram uddisya gargo me yad uvaca ha \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

nandah uvaca—Nanda said; sruyatam—should be heard; me— my; vacah—the discourse; gopah—hey cowherds; vyetu—let \[the doubt\] go away; sahka—the doubt; ca—and; vah—your; arbhake— about the boy; enam—to this; kumaram—young boy; uddisya—by referring; gargah—Garga; me—to me; yat—which; uvaca—spoke; ha—(used as a verse filler).

*nandah uvaca—gopah! enam kumaram uddisya gargah me yad (vacah) uvaca, (yusmabhih tad) vacah sruyatam. vah me arbhake sanka vyetu.*

**Перевод:**

**Nanda said: “Cowherds! Hear what Garga told me about the boy. Let your doubt about my son be dispelled.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Previously, Nanda could not stop imagining all sorts of possibilities while pondering over Krsna’s deeds, but when he heard the speech of Garga Acarya, he understood the truth about Him. At this time, Nanda gave the cowherds the same information that he heard from the acarya.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Suspecting that the cowherds would love Krsna less because of fear and reverence occasioned by realizing that He is God should he clearly say that He indeed is God who has descended on Earth to reveal His own unlimited godhood, Garga did not directly state His topmost godly might, but only hinted at it with special epithets and designations, which Nanda understood to mean that Krsna was a boy whose natural qualities are similar to those of God.

Nanda says arbhakam (the son) and repeats this with me kumaram, which means mama putram (my son), for the sake of making the cowherds think in that direction.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Listen: Desiring to eliminate my problems, my cherished deity, Sri Narayana, entered into my boy, who had great power in the past.” Hearing this, the cowherds doubted Nanda, and so he thought: “I will enlighten them by telling them Garga’s discourse.” With this intention, Nanda says sruyatam and so on.

### 10.26.16

*varnas trayah kilasyasangrhnato ’nu-yugam tanuh \|*  
*suklo raktas tatha pita idanim krsnatam gatah \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**“Your son assumes bodies in conformity with the yugas. White, red, and yellow were three colors of His. Now His color is dark blue.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Garga’s discourse begins here. The explanations can be looked into in the commentary in that chapter (10.8.13-18).

### 10.26.17

*prag ayam vasudevasya kvacij jatas tavatmajah \|*  
*vasudeva iti sriman abhijhah sampracaksate \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**“Previously this son of yours was born somewhere as Vasudeva’ child. Therefore the learned call Him ‘Vasudeva’. He is glorious.**

### 10.26.18

*bahuni sand namani rupani ca sutasya te \|*  
*guna-karmanurupani tany aham veda no janah \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**“Your son has many forms and names which are in conformity with His qualities and deeds. I know them, but people do not.**

### 10.26.19

*esa vah sreya adhasyad gopa-go-kula-nandanah \|*  
*anena sarva-durgani yuyam anjas tarisyatha \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**“He will occasion your topmost benefit. He delights the cowherds and the cows. Because of Him, all of you will easily overcome all difficulties.**

### 10.26.20

*puranena vraja-pate sadhavo dasyu-piditah \|*  
*arajake raksyamana jigyur dasyun samedhitah \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**“Previously, when there was anarchy, O chief of Vraja, the sadhus were pained by scoundrels, but He protected the sadhus and made them thrive, hence the sadhus vanquished those scoundrels.**

### 10.26.21

*ya etasmin maha-bhagah pritim kurvanti manavah \|*  
*narayo ’bhibhavanty etan visnu-paksan ivasurah \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**“Humans who are affectionate to Him are very fortunate. Enemies cannot subjugate them, just like asuras cannot defeat the gods, who have Visnu on their side.**

### 10.26.22

*tasman nanda-kumaro 'yam narayana-samo gunaih \|*  
*sriya kirtyanubhavena tat-karmasu na vismayah \|\|*

**Перевод:**

**“Therefore, Nanda, this son is similar to Narayana in terms of qualities, splendor, renown, and might. There is no reason to be amazed at His exploits.””**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Hence there is no reason to be amazed at His exploits.” These are the words of Nanda.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

In Garga’s discourse (10.8.19), the first line above, “tasman nanda-kumaro ’yam" reads: “tasman nandatmajo ’yam te", and the fourth line above, “tat-karmasu na vismayah”, reads: “gopayasva samahitah" (be alert and protect Him).

The same sense of Garga’s statement is obtained. Consequently, out of humility, in this verse Nanda implies that everyone together should protect his boy and should have feelings of possessiveness toward Him because He has such attributes, and reiterates the same in another way: “There is no reason to be amazed at His exploits” (na vismayah = na vismayah karyah). Here the word tat-karmasu (at His exploits) signifies more than what it says; Nanda’s intended meaning is: “Do not be amazed at the natural love that you and Him have for one another.” In truth, however, they did not know that the reason for that is an eternal inherent connection. Although they were aware that Garga had said something, in light of the text after the killing of Baka: aho brahma-vidam vacah, “How amazing! The words of those who have realized Brahman are never proven false. Now we realize that what Bhagavan Garga said is true” (10.11.57), nevertheless at this time those seven sentences taken together were something special.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nanda says, “Because of Garga’s statement, ‘Therefore, Nanda, this son...’, Krsna is not only mine. My son is your son too. Even by considering this aisvarya, do not cease your parental affection toward Him, and do not stop to bless

Him hundreds of times.” With this in mind, Nanda did not repeat Garga’s words: tasman nandatmajo ’yam te, ‘‘Therefore, Nanda, He is your son” (10.8.19).

Nanda continues: “The term narayana-samah is said only because He is an avesa of Narayana. The idea is not that He is Narayana, just like a suryakanta gem is said to be the same as the sun. Hence He is neither God nor a miserable jiva, but He performs superexcellent feats. Consequently He is only some ornament of our dynasty. For this reason, in the end Garga stated: tat-karmasu na vismayah, “There is no need to be amazed at His exploits.” By considering the astonishment in the fact that His deeds are out of this world, do not think that He is God. Since we were prevented by Garga to think that way, you all should be kind to Him and tell Him only this kind of blessing: “Live long.” Do not be indifferent to Him.”

In the end, the same words of Garga: gopayasva samahitah, “Be alert and protect Him” (10.8.19) are reiterated. And by removing the amazement of the cowherd men, Nanda has also eradicated their doubt.

### 10.26.23

*ity addha mam samadisya gorge ca sva-grham gate \|*  
*manye narayanasyamsam krsnam aklista-karinam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

iti—in this way (or end of quotation); addha—directly; mam—me; samadisya—having told; garge—once Garga; ca—too; sva-grham— to his home; gate—had gone; manye—I think; narayanasya—of Narayana; amsam—a part manifestation; krsnam—Krsna; aklista- karinam—who makes one distress-free.

*ity addha mam samadisya garge ca sva-grham gate, (aham) krsnam narayanasyamsam aklista-karinam manye (sma iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Having directly told me this, Garga went to his home. Afterward I thought that Krsna, who makes everyone distress-free, is a part manifestation of Narayana.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Having directly announced this to me, Garga went home. At that time I did not think so, but now I think that Krsna is a part manifestation of Narayana.” The reason for that is: aklista-karinam.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“Given that I am also his father, since that time I have considered Him to be similar to Narayana. I presume that He is a part manifestation, meaning He is empowered by Narayana (sakty-avesin).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“I suppose (manye = vitarkayami) that Krsna is a sakty-avesin expansion of Narayana. His habit is to make us free from distress (aklista-karinam = asman aklistan kartum silam yasya tam)."

### 10.26.24

*iti nanda-vacah srutva garga-gitam vrajaukasah \|*  
*drsta-srutanubhavas te krsnasyamita-tejasah \|*  
*mudita nandam anarcuh krsnam ca gata-vismayah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

iti—in this way (or marks the end of the quotation); nanda- vacah—Nanda’s discourse; srutva—after hearing; garga-gitam— sung by Garga; vraja-okasah—the residents of Vraja; drsta-sruta-anubhavah—they by whom the power \[of Krsna\] was seen and heard; te—they; krsnasya—of Krsna; amita-tejasah—whose fiery energy is unmeasured; muditah—joyful; nandam anarcuh—honored Nanda207; krsnam—Krsna; ca—and; gata-vismayah—they whose astonishment is gone.

*iti nanda-vacah garga-gitam (vakyam ca) srutva vrajaukasah muditah nandam anarcuh. amita-tejasah krsnasya drsta-srutanubhavah te gata-vismayah krsnam (anarcuh).*

**Перевод:**

**The residents of the village, joyful after listening to both Nanda’s discourse and Garga’s speech, had beheld and heard about the power of Krsna, whose fiery energy is immeasurable, and so they honored Nanda. Later, once their astonishment was gone, they also honored Krsna.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

They listened to Nanda’s discourse and, through it, the song of Garga. Or the sense is they heard Nanda’s discourse, in which was Garga’s song.

The verb anarcuh is expressive of arcanam. Thus, the cowherds worshiped Nanda with scents, sandalwood, clothes, ornaments, etc., brought from their homes. Then they worshiped Krsna, when He returned from the woods at dusk. In Visnu Purana, Parasara says the cowherds asked Krsna to solve their doubt:

*gate sakre tu gopalah krstiam aklista-karinam \|*  
*ucuh pritya dhrtam drstva tena govardhanacalam \|\|*  
*vayam asman maha-bhaga bhagavan mahato bhayat \|*  
*gavas ca bhavata trata giridharana-karmana \|\|*  
*balakrideyam atula gopalatvam jugupsitam \|*  
*divyam ca bhavatah karma kim etat tata kathyatam \|\|*  
*kaliyo damitas toye dhenuko vinipatitah \|*  
*dhrto govardhanas cayam sankitani manamsi nah \|\|*  
*satyam satyam hareh padau sapamo ’mita-vikrama \|*  
*yathavad viryam alokya na tvam manyamahe naram \|\|*  
*pritih sa-stri-kumarasya vrajasya tvayi kesava \|*  
*karma cedam asakyam yat samastais tridasair api \|\|*  
*balatvam cativiryatvam janma casmasu sobhanam \|*  
*cintyamanam ameyatman chankam krsna prayacchati \|\|*  
*devo va danavo va tvam yakso gandharva eva va \|*  
*kim asmakam vicarena bandhavo ’si namo ’stu te \|\|*

**“After Indra left, the cowherds, who had seen Krsna hold Govardhana Mountain, affectionately spoke to Him, whose deeds are unimpeded: “By your feat of holding the mountain, O supereminent personage, you saved both us and the cattle from this great peril. The fun you had as a child was incomparable. You don’t like to follow the customary festive sacrifice of the cowherds. And what about this divine deed of yours? Tell us exactly what is going on, dear boy. Kaliya was subdued in the water, Dhenuka was thrashed, and Govardhana was held aloft. We are in doubt. We swear oath after oath at Lord Hari’s feet: Upon seeing your might, O being of immeasurable prowess, we think you are not a man. Kesava, the love that the whole community, including the girls, has for you; this particular feat of yours that cannot be done by the gods, even if they were to try to do it together; your childhood, filled with heroism; and your birth among us, which seems out of place, make us wonder, O unfathomable soul. All this leads to a doubt, Krsna. Are you a god, a Danava, a Yaksa, a Gandharva or, upon due deliberation, our kinsman? Anyway, we salute you.” (Visnu Purana 5.13.1-8)**

*sri-parasara uvaca*  
*ksanam bhutva tvasau tusnim kincit-pranaya-kopavan \|*  
*ity evam uktas tair gopaih krsno ’py aha mahamatih \|\|*  
*mat-sambandhena vo gopa yadi lajja na jayate \|*  
*slaghyo vaham tatah kim vo vicarena prayojanam \|\|*  
*yadi vo ’sti mayi pritih slaghyo ’ham bhavatam yadi \|*  
*tadatma-bandhu-sadrsi buddhir vah kriyatam mayi \|\|*  
*naham devo na gandharvo na yakso na ca danavah \|*  
*aham vo bandhavo jato naitac cintyam ito ’nyatha \|\|*

**Sri Parasara continued: When they had ended, Krsna stayed silent for a moment and became somewhat affectionately angry. Then He, a very smart being, replied as follows: “Cowherds, if you are not ashamed of My relationship with you, or if you feel I am praiseworthy, what reason do you have to deliberate upon the matter? If you have affection for Me, if I deserve a praise from you, then think of Me as your friend and relative. I am neither a god, a Gandharva, a Yaksa or a Danava. I am your kinsman. Don’t think anything else.” (Visnu Purana 5.13.9-12)**

This was Krsna’s reply as told by Vaisampayana:

*manyante mam yatha sarve bhavanto bhima-vikramah \|*  
*tathaham navamantavyah sajatiyo ’smi bandhavah \|\|*

**“Do not think that My prowess is terrifying. Your reverence of Me is a form of disrespect. Stop doing that. I belong to your caste and am one of your relatives.” (Hari-vamsa 2.20.11)**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The verb anarcuh means they honored him with presentations of clothing, jewels and gold coins. Given that Krsna was in the forest at the time, later in the evening they gratified Him, decorating Him with yellow garments, necklaces, arm bracelets, earrings and crowns, and shouting “Glory, glory to the jewel of Vraja-bhumi. May You live long.”

### 10.26.25

*deve varsati yajha-viplava-rusa vajrasma-varsanilaih*  
*sidat-pala-pasu-stri atma-saranam drstvanukampy utsmayan \|*  
*utpatyaika-karena sailam abalo lilocchilindhram yatha*  
*bibhrad gostham apan mahendra-mada-bhitpriyan na indro gavam \|\|*  
*(sardula-vikriditam)*

**Пословный перевод:**
