deve varsati—when the god (Indra) rained; yajha—of the sacrifice; viplava—on account of the cancellation; rusa—because of anger; vajra—due to lightning; asma-varsa—due to hails of stones; anilaih—and due to tempests; sidat—who were distressed; pala-pasu-stri—\[the community,\] in which the herdsmen, the herd and the women; atma-saranam—\[the community,\] whose shelter is Himself; drstva—upon seeing; anukampi—He is compassionate by nature; utsmayan—while highly smiling; utpatya—after uprooting; eka-karena—with one hand; sailam—the mountain; abalah—a weak \[child\]; lila—for fun; ucchilindhram—a mushroom; yatha—like; bibhrat—while holding; gostham—the cowherd community; apat— He protected; maha-indra—of Indra (“the great king”); mada—of the arrogance; bhit—the destroyer; priyat—may He be pleased; nah—with us; indrah—the king; gavam—of cows.

*deve yajha-viplava-rusa varsati (sati, yah sri-krsnah) vajrasma- varsanilaih sidat-pala-pasu-stri atma-saranam gostham drstva anukampi utsmayan, abalah (balah) yatha lilocchilindhram (utpatya enam bibharti), sailam utpatya (enam) eka-karena bibhrat apat, (sah sri-krsnah) mahendra-mada-bhit gavam indrah nah priyat (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**The god of rain sent forth a deluge out of anger when the fire sacrifice dedicated to him was canceled. Beholding the cowherd community, which is under His protection and in which the herdsmen, the herd and the women were oppressed by thunderbolts, tempests and hails of stones, Krsna became compassionate and smiled. He saved the community by uprooting the mountain and holding it high with one hand like a little boy picks up a mushroom for fun. May He, the destroyer of Indra’s arrogance and the king of cows, be pleased with us.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Remembering the lifting of Govardhana Hill and all the aspects of its narrative, he prays for the affection of Krsna, who had manifested His godly might.

“Upon seeing the cowherd community in distress, Krsna, who is compassionate, smiled (utsmayan = hasan).” This means He showed maturity. “He lifted the mountain and held it with one hand like a child (abalah = balah) picks up a mushroom for fun (lila = lilartham).”

With the epithets mahendra-mada-bhit (destroyer of Indra’s arrogance) and gavam indrah (king of cows), he remembers the meanings of the next chapter. “May Sri Krsna be pleased (priyat = priyatam) with us.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

When Krsna saw the cowherds oppressed by Indra, He became compassionate (anukampi); this word ends in the suffix mat\[u\] which has the sense of bhuman (abundance). With utsmayan, he says: Although He was agitated with mercy, His bravery was not shaken. The drift is He smiled in the manner of deriding Indra.

Having lifted Govardhana, Krsna held the mountain with the left hand, like a child picks up a mushroom to play with (lila - lila-prayojanaka). He held the mountain aloft for seven days and nights.

With scorn, he says: Although Krsna is the king of cows, He shattered the arrogant pride of the great king.” In truth, however, the sense is: Being the great king is included in that kingship of cows, somewhat like rivers enter in the sea.

The verb priyat (May He be pleased) is the lin tense in the sense of asih (blessing). The gist is: “Once He is pleased, my being a follower of the people of the cowherd community will be accomplished.” With that mood of being part of the cowherd community, he says: indro gavam (He is the king of cows). In this way he shows that being such a follower is his own goal in life, much like Brahma did.

In this regard, the Sruti states: jajana eva vyavadhata sprdhah prapasyad viro ’bhipaumsyam ranam, avrscad adrim iva avasasyadah sprdhastabhnan nakam svavasyayaprthum.208The sense is as follows: “From the time that He took birth, the hero, Krsna, killed His rivals in special ways. He eminently saw that combat is a manly thing to do. This means He did many kinds of wars with the demons. Moreover: In the form of Govardhana Mountain, He easily consumed the food offered by the cowherds. He immobilized the heavens, the clouds, which were acting as rivals, because: He lifted the great mountain and held it, playfully.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“My dear king, protecting the cowherd community, who had taken shelter of Him, from the danger of lightning, hail and tempest which arose from the anger of Indra, by lifting Govardhana Hill, Krsna, who showed expertise in starting the sacrifice to Govardhana that way, dispelled the arrogant pride of the gods and felt pleased. In like manner, may He, having saved you from the lightning-bolt-words generated by the anger of a Brahmana, and showing His expertise in starting the sacrifice of the recitation of this scripture, Sri Bhagavatam, after raising it from the waters of the Vedas, be pleased to end the overweening pride of the Brahmana philosophers devoid of bhakti." With this in mind, here Sukadeva, considering King Pariksit as the central post of his own sacrifice, prays for the satisfaction of Krsna.

Krsna is the king of cows; this is said by the logic that only a king can shatter the overweening pride of a king.

“Let Krsna be pleased with us (priyat = prinatu) (nah = nah prati)—me, Pariksit, and all other listeners.”

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

The absence of the suffix ?a? at the end of the compound sidat-pala-pasu-stri is poetic license, and so is the parasmaipada in utsmayan.

## Chapter 27 - Indra Extols Krsna; He and Surabhi Give an Abhiseka to Krsna and Name Him Govinda

### 10.27.1

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*govardhane dhrte saile asarad raksite vraje \|*  
*go-lokad avrajat krsnam surabhih sakra eva ca \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah uvaca—Sri Suka said; govardhane dhrte saile—once Govardhana Mountain had been held; asarat—from the deluge; raksite vraje—once the cowherd community had been saved; golokat—from the planet of the cows; avrajat—came; krsnam—to Krsna; surabhih—the Surabhi cow; sakrah—Indra; eva—the same; ca—and.

*sri-sukah uvaca—govardhane saile dhrte, vraje (ca) asarat raksite (sati), surabhih sakrah eva ca go-lokat krsnam avrajat.*

**Перевод:**

**Sri Suka said: After the events of holding Govardhana Hill and saving the residents of Vraja from the deluge, Mother Surabhi and Indra came from the planet of the cows to meet Krsna.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*sapta-vimse tad alaksya krsnasya prabhavam param \|*  
*varnyate surabhindrabhyam abhiseka-mahotsavah \|\|*

**“In the twenty-seventh chapter, this is described: the great festival of ablution performed by Surabhi and Indra, after they had seen the transcendental power of Krsna.”**

**10.27.1**

The phrase govardhane dhrte saile (given that Govardhana Mountain was held) is the reason Indra fearfully arrived. And asarad raksite vraje (given that Vraja was saved from the deluge) is the reason Surabhi joyfully arrived.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Govardhana is so called because it increases, or fosters, the cows. On account of the assistance of Govardhana, the idea that the cows were in trouble due to that deluge is repudiated. On the contrary, the cattle fared well because of the abundant grass.

The term vraja refers to the humans, animals and birds that live there. Surabhi came from goloka, that is, the material Goloka, not the spiritual one which is a particular manifestation of Gokula, inasmuch as Indra could not possibly come in contact with the Surabhi of that kind. The spiritual Goloka will be shown at the end of the twenty-eighth chapter.

Indra arrived with mother Surabhi because he knew that Krsna is fond of cows. To bring her with him, he first went to her planet. They came to Vraja from there. Surabhi will say: brahmana codita vayam, “We were encouraged by Brahma” (10.27.21). Dispatched by Brahma, Indra came with him to Surabhi’s planet. From there, Indra, acknowledging the order of Brahma, came with Surabhi.

Ca has the sense of api (although). The drift is: Indra could not go on his own because he committed a big offense. Still (api = tathapi), he came, because he had no other refuge. The reason for that is: krsnam. Krsna is the Lord in person, and so Indra came to take shelter. As far as Surabhi is concerned, the name “Krsna” signifies that He attracts her heart with His quality of being affectionate to her offsprings. The word eva (only) signifies that Indra came without his retinue. Vaisampayana gives some more details:

*sa dadarsopavistam vai govardhana-sila-tale \|*  
*krsnam aklista-karmanam puruhutah purandarah \|\|*  
*tam viksya balam mahata tejasa diptam avyayam \|*  
*gopa-vesa-dharam visnum pritim lebhe purandarah \|\|*  
*tam sambu-jalada-cchayam krsnam srivatsa-laksanam \|*  
*paryapta-nayanah sakrah punah punar udaiksata \|\|*

**“Purandara, who has many names, saw Krsna sitting at the base of Govardhana Mountain. Beholding the boy, whose deeds are unimpeded, who had great radiance with His fiery energy, who had the attire of a cowherd and who is Visnu, Indra felt love. He continuously gazed at Krsna, whose luster resembled the sheen of a dark cloud and who had the characteristic of Srivatsa, and thus gratified his eyes.” (Hari-vamsa 2.19.3-5)**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*sapta-vimse bhayad indra-stutis tatra krpa hareh \|*  
*surabhya cabhiseko yad govindety abhidhabhavat \|\|*

**“In the twenty-seventh chapter, Indra offers a prayer out of fear, and Hari shows mercy. Mother Surabhi too performs the abhiseka ceremony, on which occasion Krsna received the name Govinda.”**

By Brahma’s order, Surabhi performed the abhiseka of the Lord; Indra was her assistant in that matter.

### 10.27.2

*vivikta upasangamya vriditah krta-helanah \|*  
*pasparsa padayor enam kiritenarka-varcasa \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

vivikte—in a lonely place; upasahgamya—after coming close; vriditah—embarrassed; krta-helanah—he by whom an offense was done; pasparsa—he touched; padayoh—at both feet; enam—Him; kiritena—with his crown; arka—\[was like the effulgence\] of the sun; varcasa—whose radiance.

*krta-helanah vriditah (indrah) vivikte (sthale enam) upasangamya aka-Barcas kiritena padayoh enam pasparsa.*

**Перевод:**

**Indra, who had committed an offense and was ashamed, approached Krsna in a solitary place and touched His feet with his crown, whose radiance resembled sunshine.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Vivikte means in a solitary place.”He touched His two feet,” means he offered obeisances.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

On Surabhi’s advice, Indra went alone to see Krsna. That way, it was easier for him to beg forgiveness.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Vivikte means “in a solitary place. ’’This location is specifically mentioned by Vaisampayana: sa dadarsopavistam vai govardhana-sila-tale... (see above). It’s understood that at first, Indra saw that the Lord had gone far away from His friends.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Krsna was thinking: “Alas, Govardhana suffered so much on its back by the striking of Indra on account of Me, his adversary.” Hence, early in the morning He went to see the status of the mountain. While Krsna was going to a secluded place, at that time Indra came there.

Indra was sent by Surabhi: “Listen, Indra. Depart without your retinue, become humble, and throw yourself like a rod at the lotus feet of the Lord in order to beg forgiveness of your offense.”

Simply with the eyes, Krsna communicated this to him: “My dear king of gods, what is this unfathomable fatherly mercy that you are bestowing to Me? I am just a child. I am ignorant, yet I am sinful because I stopped your sacrifice. Still you have come here to show your grace upon Me.” Understanding this, Indra became embarrassed.

### 10.27.3

*drsta-srutanubhavo ’sya krsnasyamita-tejasah \|*  
*nasta-tri-lokesa-mada idam aha krtanjalih \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

drsta-sruta—was seen and heard; anubhavah—\[Indra,\] by whom the power; asya—His; krsnasya—Krsna’s; amita—is not measured; tejasah—whose fiery energy; nasta—is lost; tri-loka-isa—“I am the king of the worlds”; madah—he whose overweening pride; idam— this (in the next verses); aha—speaks (spoke); krta-ahjalih—he by whom joining the palms was done.

*amita-tejasah asya krsnasya drsta-srutanubhavah (indrah) nasta-tri-lokesa-madah krtahjalih idam aha (sma).*

**Перевод:**

**Indra had seen and heard about the power of Krsna, whose fiery energy is immeasurable. Having cast away the false pride of thinking of himself as the king of the universe, Indra joined his palms and spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The adjective nasta-tri-lokesa-madah means: “Indra, whose overweening pride “I am the king of the worlds” was gone” (= nastas tri-lokeso ’ham iti mado yasya sah).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Indra saw Krsna’s power when He held Govardhana, and heard about His power from Brahma. Although his crown was shining, in Krsna’s presence Indra was like a firefly in daytime, and so he at once lost his false pride. Or the reason for that is: amita-tejasah, which ends in the ablative case: “because of Krsna’s immeasurable fiery energy.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

First he saw the Lord’s power with his own eyes. Later, when he understood his offense, he went to the top of Mount Meru to inquire about the means of his deliverance; there he heard Brahma talk about the might (anubhava = prabhava) of Krsna.

### 10.27.4

*indra uvaca*  
*visuddha-sattvam tava dhama santam*  
*tapo-mayam dhvasta-rajas-tamaskam \|*  
*maya-mayo ’yam guna-sampravaho*  
*na vidyate te ’grahananubandhah \|\|*  
*(upajati 11)*

**Пословный перевод:**

indrah uvaca—Indra said; visuddha-sattvam—is transcendental existence; tava—Your; dhama—abode (or status); santam— peaceful; tapah-mayam—made of effulgence; dhvasta-rajah-tamaskam—by which material passion and ignorance are destroyed; maya-mayah—consists of illusion; ayam—this; guna—of the modes of material nature; sampravahah—the great flow; na vidyate— does not exist; te—in Your case; agrahana—is wrong assumptions; anubandhah—whose cause.

*indrah uvaca—tava dhama visuddha-sattvam santam tapo-mayam dhvasta-rajas-tamaskam (bhavati). ayam (samsarah) maya-mayah guna-sampravahah agrahananubandhah te na vidyate.*

**Перевод:**

**Indra said: “Your abode is pure sattva, peaceful, effulgent, and devoid of rajas and tamas. You do not belong to this, the flow of the material modes, which consists of illusion and is caused by wrong assumptions.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

To express his wish: “Please forgive me,” in four verses Indra says, “You, obviously, did not commit an offense. Rather You only did me a favor.”

“Your identity (dhama = svarupam) is one form (santam = eka-rupam), hence it is full of awareness, meaning it knows everything (tapo-mayam = pracura-jnanam = sarva-jnam).” How so? dhvasta-rajas-tamaskam, “In it, rajas and tamas do not exist.”

Therefore: “This (ayam), meaning it is being seen by me and others, the flow of the gunas, that is, the material world, which is sprouted by the gunas (guna-sampravahah = gunaih samprohyate id tatha = samsarah), which is an effect of Maya (maya-mayah = maya-karya-rupah), does not relate to You, because: agrahananubandhah, “It is put together by means of ignorance” (= agrahanena ajnanena anubadhyate iti tatha).

The gist is: “You, who are omniscient, have nothing to do with it.” Alternatively, the idea is the material world is related to ignorance (agrahananubandhah = ajhana-sambandhah).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Although the form of Bhagavan is beyond the gunas and is dense sac-cid-ananda, still: visuddha-sattvam. This is stated merely by considering a similarity with the nature of sattva-guna, which is devoid of greed, anger, and so on. Although the gods are sattvika, they sometimes have greed and so forth. To make a distinction, here the adjective visuddha (pure) is used. The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami. Or visuddha-sattvam is the play of the transcendental potency.

Or: “O pure one (visuddha)! You body (dhama = sri-murtih) is sheer existence (sattvam = sattva-matram).” This means it is one in nature with Brahman. Or dhama means “Your abode, the cowherd village.” The gist is: “Out of ignorance of You, I offended You. That is also why I am in material life.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Here the term visuddha-sattva denotes a function of the transcendental potency which is closely woven with sattva-guna (= prakrta-sattvanusyuta-cic chakti-vrtti-visesa). For example, the Brahma-samhita states:

*sattvavalambi-para sattva-visuddha-sattvam*  
*govindam adi-purusam tam aham bhajami \|\|*

**“I worship Govinda, the primeval form of the personal aspect of the Absolute. His existence is pure: It is an existence beyond what rests on sattva-guna.”209 (Brahma-samhita 5.41)**

The rest was explained by Sridhara Svami. In his commentary, the sense is: visuddha-sattvatmakam svarupam (Your identity consists of pure sattva).

Or: “This manifestation of Yours” (dhama = prakaso ’yam). This means it is a self-manifestation, given that the word visuddha signifies the exclusion of everything material. It is santam, not agitated, and tapo-mayam, aware to a high degree (= jnanatisaya-rupam), in the light of the text of Visnu Purana

*jnana-sakti-balaisvarya-virya-tejamsy asesatah \|*  
*bhagavac-chabda-vacyani vina heyair gunadibhih \|\|*

**“Total cognizance, powers, strength, prowess, supremacy, and radiance, all of which are devoid of rejectable qualities and so on, are literally expressed by the word Bhagavan.” (Visnu Purana 6.5.79)**

There is no material sattva at all. The Visnu Purana states:

*sattvadayo na santise yatra ca prakrta gunah \|*  
*sa suddhah sarva-suddhebhyah puman adyah prasidatu \|\|*

**“May the primeval Purusa be pleased: The Lord is purer than all pure things combined. The material gunas, beginning from sattva, do not exist in Him.” (Visnu Purana 1.9.44)**

Therefore: “The flow of Your qualities, such as compassion, does not consist of Maya (maya-mayo na vidyate)." Why? grahananubandhah, “\[The flow of Your qualities\] is obtained only by Your acceptance” (= grahanena anubadhyate = tvat-svikarena eva prapyate). Or: agrahananubandhah, “The flow is obtained without the influence of material sensory perception” (= agrahana = agrahanena = indriya-karanaka-paricchedabhavena eva).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Out of false pride, I ruined your sacrifice. And out of greed, under the pretext of doing a sacrificial offering to Govardhana I ate all the food offerings meant for you. Everything is my fault. You know it.”

Anticipating such crooked words from the Lord, here Indra means to say:” My Lord, I have been bewildered by Your illusory energy, but because now I am receiving a drop of Your mercy, I can somehow understand the truth about You.”

“Your personality (dhama = svarupam), is santa, not fierce, and tapo-maya, the nature of awareness (= jhana-svarupam)." Then does it consist of sattva-guna? “No. It is visuddha-sattva, transcendental. Therefore rajas and tamas cannot possibly exist in You. Not only that, these two modes present in other personalities are destroyed because of You (dhvasta-rajas-tamaskam = dhvastam rajas tamas ca yasmat)... by remembering You. Hence the total flow of the material modes (sam = samyak), which is in me and in other personalities in this world, in other words: material life, which consists of Maya, has nothing to do with You.”

“Fine, I am not like a jiva, but sometimes I use Maya just for fun.” There is no fault in that either; thus Indra says: agrahana- anubandhah, which means: na vidyate grahanasyanubandha akanksapi yatra sah (the flow, in which there is no desire of taking).

**Комментарий. Автор Madhvācārya:**

Vi-suddha-sattvam means vigata-suddha-sattvam (devoid of pure sattva-guna). “Because of the connection with the three gunas, that flow does not exist in You” (tava = tvayi). Tapo-mayam means jhanatmakam (Your identity “consists of sheer awareness”).

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

“Your abode (dhama = sthanam) is visuddha- sattvam.” The word suddha (pure) means the sattva is untouched by either rajas or tamas. This sattva is especially pure (visuddha = visesena suddha), meaning it is not even touched by sattva-guna. Even His power (dhama = tejah) is like that.

“The material world (guna-sampravahah = prapahcah) does not have a motive which includes the knowledge of You” (na vidyate te grahananubandhah = te grahanasya jnanasya anubandha-rupah na bhavati).

**Комментарий. Автор Vira-Raghava Acarya:**

“Your abode, the ethereal sky (dhama = sthanam = parama-vyoma), is pure sattva, meaning it is devoid of rajas and tamas, therefore it is santa, devoid of craving and aversion.”

The word yatra (“in which” abode) needs to be added: “In it, neither the course of the gunas, which has come from Your Maya (te maya-mayah = tava mayayah agatah), or the bondage of karma, which is the cause of taking a body (grahananubandhah = sarira-grahana-karana-bhutah karmanubandhah ca), exists (na vidyate).”

In maya-mayah, the suffix maya\[t\], mentioned in the rule: mayat ca (Astadhyayi 4.3.82), has the sense described in the sutra: tata agatah (Astadhyayi 4.3.74).

**Комментарий. Автор Pandit Ganga Sahaya:**

“The course of the gunas is continuously put together because of the taking, that is, the wrongful superimposition of the sense of identity on the mind/ body complex (grahananubandhah = grahanena anubadhyate) (grahanena = dehadau atmadhyasena),” or else because of ignorance (agrahana = agrahanena - ajnanena).

### 10.27.5

*kuto nu tad-dhetava isa tat-krta*  
*lobhadayoye 'budha-linga-bhavah \|*  
*tathapi dandam bhagavan bibharti*  
*dharmasya guptyai khala-nigrahaya \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

kutah—how?; nu—at all; tat-hetavah—the causes of it (of material existence); isa—O Lord; tat-krtah—are made by it; lobha-adayah— greed and so on; ye—which; abudha—of an unintelligent person; linga—which are signs; bhavah—are modes; tatha api—nevertheless; dandam—rod \[ofpunishment\]; bhagavan—God in form; bibharti— holds; dharmasya—of righteousness; guptyai—for the protection; khala—of miscreants; nigrahaya—for the chastisement.

*isa! tad-dhetavah tat-krtah ye lobhadayah abudha-linga-bhavah (bhavanti, te tava) kutah nu (syuh). tathapi bhagavan dharmasya guptyai khala-nigrahaya dandam bibharti.*

**Перевод:**

**“My Lord! Greed, anger and other such mental states are the causes of material life and are created by it. They are signs of unintelligent people, so how could You possibly have any of those? Nevertheless, God wields the rod of punishment to protect dharma and to chastise miscreants.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Indra intends to say this: “When there is neither ignorance or the connection with the material body, which is made by ignorance, how could greed and the like possibly exist?”

Tat-krtah means they are produced by a connection with the body; tad-dhetavah means they are the causes of yet another body. “But,” it may be objected, “sometimes greed, anger and so on are seen in very learned scholars.” In response he says: abudha-lihga-bhavah, meaning those things make one recognize the fools. The drift is there is no absolute rule that someone who has no craving, aversion, etc., is a jnani. In the sentence beginning from tathapi he says: “Nevertheless, that is, even in the absence of greed and so forth, You shattered my false pride for the sake of punishment.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Indra describes the same idea, by the mode of kaimutika-nyaya (not to mention): “Because You have no fault, Your devotees too have none.” Isa is a vocative: “O controller of Maya!” Because of adi (etc.) in lobhadayah, anger is included. The reading isa manyu-lobhadayah is approved by Citsukha and others.

The honorific pronoun bhavan needs to be added: “You, sir, wield the rod of punishment,” because: bhagavan, that is, Paramesvara who has made His descent in person to benefit the world. Or bhavan is not implied, and so the wording “God wields the rod of punishment” is indirect, though direct, out of fear and reverence.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Indra describes the same idea, by the mode of kaimutika-nyaya: “If Your qualities are not made of Maya, how could You possibly have faults, which are caused by it (tad-dhetavah = maya-hetukah)?" The reason for that is: isa, “O controller of Maha-maya.”

“How can you say so? You know that I have faults, because I ate the food of Annakuta, did not tolerate your arrogance, and so forth. Why do you prattle out of fear?” Indra responds: tat-krta lobhadayo ye ’budha-linga-bhavah stands for: tvat-krta lobhadayo ye budha-linga-bhavah, “The greed and other things brought forth by You are signs of an intelligent person.” They are not made of Maya; rather they are only made of krpa. Chastising the miscreants too is a form of mercy.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Greed and other mental states are tad- dhetavah in the sense that they are the causes of the flow of the gunas, and are tat-krtah insofar as they are the effects of that flow.

“Indra, how can you say I don’t have material qualities? I ruined your sacrifice.” In response to that he says: “Nevertheless,” that is “even though You have no greed and the like...”

### 10.27.6

*pita gurus tvam jagatam adhiso*  
*duratyayah kala upatta-dandah \|*  
*hitaya ceccha-tanubhih samihase*  
*manam vidhunvan jagad-isa-maninam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

pita—the father; guruh—the teacher; tvam—You; jagatam—of the three worlds; adhisah—the overlord; duratyayah—insurmountable; kalah—Time; upatta-dandah—You by whom the rod is taken; hitaya—for the benefit; ca—and; iccha—at will; tanubhih—with bodies; samihase—You endeavor; manam—the false pride; vidhunvan—while shaking off; jagat-isa—of being lords of the world; maninam—of those who have the self-conceit.

*tvam jagatam pita guruh adhisah duratyayah kalah upatta-dandah, jagad-isa-maninam manam vidhunvan, hitaya ca iccha-tanubhih samihase.*

**Перевод:**

**“You are the father, the teacher and the overlord of the worlds. You are insurmountable Time. You endeavor to also benefit everyone by assuming forms at will and taking the rod of punishment, curbing the pride of those who fancy themselves the rulers of the world.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“But I am just the son of a cowherd. What power do I have to chastise you? Or, what might be the reason? Or else why would I punish anyone at all?” Indra responds here; he mentions three reasons: “You are the maker, the teacher and the controller of the worlds.” Krsna is able because He is Time. Therefore: “Having taken the rod of punishment, You endeavor, with bodies of Lila Avataras, to create well-being (hitaya = kalyanaya). Your endeavor is only Your pastime. You dispel the arrogance of people like me, who have the self-conceit of being a ruler of the world.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“What You did was for my benefit.” The sense of samihase (You endeavor) is: vicitra-lilam tanuse (You make an amazing pastime).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“But what personal gain do I have in safeguarding dharma and in subduing evil?” In reply to this possible objection, here Indra replies: “The auspiciousness of the world.” “To those who like You, out of mercy You act as a father to a child, as a guru to a disciple, and as the bestower of all good things. To the wicked, however, You are insurmountable (duratyayah = durvarah) Time: You purify them by punishing them. Therefore You endeavor (samihase = cestase), by the incarnations which You assume by Your free will (iccha-tanubhih = sveccha-mayavataraih), only for the benefit of both categories of people. Your endeavor, it is implied, is simply a pastime, such as the killing of Putana, which remove the wicked and protect the pious. But whatever punishment You exert against Brahma and others, who are Your empowered representatives, is for the purpose of removing their false pride. This too is Your pastime.” In this way, Indra offers homage.

### 10.27.7

*ye mad-vidhajna jagad-isa-maninas*  
*tvam viksya kale ’bhayam asu tan-madam \|*  
*hitvarya-margam prabhajanty apasmaya*  
*iha khalanam api te ’nusasanam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

ye—which (aforementioned ones); mat-vidha—of my kind; ajnah— ignorant people; jagat-isa—as king of the world; maninah—they who have the self-conceit; tvam—You; viksya—by seeing; kale—in time; abhayam—fearless; asu—quickly; tat-madam—that self-conceit; hitva—after giving up; arya—of high-minded people; margam—the path; prabhajanti—they follow; apa-smayah—they whose arrogance is gone; iha—the demeanor; khalanam—of the wicked; api—also; te—Your; anusasanam—the punishment.

*ye mad-vidhajnah jagad-isa-maninah kale abhayam tvam viksya tan-madam asu hitva apasmayah (santah) arya-margam prabhajanti. te iha khalanam api anusasanam (bhavati).*

**Перевод:**

**“Fools of my kind, who think they are the king of the world, quickly give up that self-conceit when they see You undaunted in times of danger. Devoid of hubris, they follow the noble path. Thus, Your demeanor also serves as a punishment for the wicked.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Indra expounds on the previous verse. “When ignorant people like me, those who think they are the king of the world, see that You are fearless even in time of fear (kale = bhaya-kale ’pi), such as recently during the deluge, they give up that self- conceit and, rendered void of haughtiness, practice bhakti. Hence Your very demeanor is the punishment (anusasanam = dandah) of miscreants.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Indra mentions their benefit: the noble path. “Although Your endeavor is only meant to delight the devotees, it is also the cause of instructing the wicked (anusasanam = siksa-karanam bhavati)."

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Once they give up their conceit, their hubris is gone (apasmayah = gata-smayah = nasta-garvah), and so they take to the path of noble persons, that is, the path of Your devotees. Hence this pastime of Yours of lifting Govardhana Hill was the punishment (anusasanam = dandah) of the wicked, me.”

### 10.27.8

*sa tvam mamaisvarya-mada-plutasya*  
*krtagasas te ’vidusah prabhavam \|*  
*ksantum prabho ’tharhasi mudha-cetaso*  
*maivam punar bhun matir isa me ’sad \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sah—that one; tvam—You; mama—my; aisvarya-mada-plutasya—of me who am plunged in the false pride of godly might; krta-agasah— of me by whom a sin was done; te—Your; avidusah—of me who did not know; prabhavam—power; ksantum—to forgive; prabho—O Almighty; atha—after this; arhasi—You should; mudha-cetasah— of me whose mind is foolish; ma—not; evam—such; punah—again; bhut—may it be; matih—mindset; isa—O Lord; me—my; asati—bad.

*prabho! isa! sah tvam mama aisvarya-mada-plutasya krtagasah te prabhavam avidusah mudha-cetasah ksantum arhasi. atha me matih evam asati ma punar bhut.*

**Перевод:**

**“O Lord Almighty, I was submerged in the false pride of my godly might, and so I committed an offense, not knowing Your power. I was foolish. Kindly forgive me. May such a bad mindset of mine not occur again.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Having described the Lord’s svarupa (essence of being) and mentioned his intention, he makes Him forgive. Then he says another request: evam-bhuta asati matir me punar ma bhut, “May such a bad mindset of mine not occur again.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“O Almighty!” (prabho). This means He is able to forgive. “You, that benefactor of the world (sah = jagad-dhitakari), are qualified (arhasi = yogyo ’si) to forgive me, though I committed a big offense. I was unaware of Your glory (prabhavam avidusah - mahatmyam ajanatah) because: mudha- cetasah, I wasn’t thinking, because: aisvarya-mada-plutasya, I was submerged in the false pride of godly might.”

Or: “I did an offense although I know Your power” (te ’vidusah prabhavam = te vidusah prabhavam). You are most compassionate, and so for You to forgive this one offense of mine is a trifle. Still, be pleased to forgive me so that I never offend You and Your devotees.”

It should be understood that he requests this with an impure heart, given that he is following what he said, as follows, in terms of being unable to be forgiven: tvam viksya kale bhayam, “People like me give up the false conceit upon seeing You afraid in time of danger” (kale ’bhayam = kale bhayam). For this reason, he will forget about it on the occasion of the theft of the Parijata flower tree, and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“By lifting Govardhana Hill, I have simply protected Vraja. I still did not punish you. Now I will effect your punishment properly by calling Yamaraja.” Fearing this, Indra speaks: “You are the well-known father and teacher, therefore, by Your mercy, kindly pardon me.”

Next, with maivam and the rest he says: “I cannot be purified by being punished. Rather, purify me by Your mercy so that this foolish mentality of mine ends.” But this, as stated in Vaisnava- tosani, he will forget.

### 10.27.9

*tavavataro ’yam adhoksajeha*  
*bhuvo bharanam uru-bhara-janmanam \|*  
*camu-patinam abhavaya deva*  
*bhavaya yusmac-carananuvartinam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tava—of Yours; avatarah—descent; ayam—this; adhoksaja—O Adhoksaja; iha—here (on Earth); bhuvah—of the Earth; bharanam—who are burdens; uru-bhara—of many burdens; janmanam—because of whom there is the origination; camii- patinam—of army leaders; abhavaya—for the destruction; deva—O God; bhavaya—for the prosperity; yusmat-carana—Your feet; anuvartinam—of those who follow.

*adhoksaja! deva! tava ayam iha avatarah bhuvah (svayam) bharanam uru-bhara-janmanam camu-patinam abhavaya yusmac- carananuvartinam (tu) bhavaya (bhavati).*

**Перевод:**

**“O Lord who are beyond sensory perception, Your descent here is conducive to the annihilation of army leaders, who are not only a burden to the Earth but also bring into existence many such problems, and to the prosperity of those devoted to Your feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The implication is: “Because I am Your servant, I should be forgiven even though I committed a great offense.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“O Adhoksaja, You who are out of the range of sensory perception! You are completely invisible, yet Your manifestation (avatarah - prakatyam) here, on Earth, is for the sake of the auspiciousness of those who serve Your feet, especially the residents of Vraja.”

“O Deva, You who are worthy of being worshiped (deva = pujya).” In this way he establishes that he is a servant. The drift is, “I know that You descended because of our request, for the benefit of the gods.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“I was foolish. I knew that after hearing the gods’ prayer You descended to this world for our benefit, but I became blinded by pride. Only now, having received punishment, have I regained my eyes. I know You. You descended for the destruction (abhavaya = nasaya) of military leaders and for the auspiciousness (bhavaya = mangalaya) of those who serve Your feet. I, on the other hand, do not belong to either of these categories, and so neither my destruction nor my well-being has come about. In this way You remain indifferent to me, so to hell with me.”

### 10.27.10

*namas tubhyam bhagavate purusaya mahatmane \|*  
*vasudevaya krsnaya satvatam pataye namah \|\|*

*tubhyam bhagavate namah (astu). purusaya mahatmane vasudevaya krsnaya satvatam pataye namah (astu).*

**Перевод:**

**“Obeisances to You, Bhagavan. I offer my profound respects to Krsna, who is the Purusa, the great Soul, Vasudeva, and the chief of the Yadus.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

While asking for forgiveness, he offers obeisances: “My profound respects to You, the Supreme Lord, Krsna.” He is the Purusa, the inner controller of all. He is the great Soul, meaning He cannot be delimited although He abides in the hearts of all. Why? He is Vasudeva, who resides everywhere (vasudevaya = sarva- nivasaya). He is the chief of the Yadavas (satvatam = yadavanam).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“My respects to You. who are God in person (bhagavate = saksat paramesvaraya)." Here the name Krsna means He attracts the hearts of all by manifesting unlimited godly might. Having expressed external aisvarya, with purusaya and so on he refers to the internal kind.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Thus, by way of offering evidence that “I too am a follower of Your lotus feet,” he hopefully offers obeisances, in this verse and in the next.

In consideration of Uddhava’s statement: paravareso mahad- amsa-yuktah, “Though unborn, the Lord, who is the master of the high and of the low and who has the mahats and the amsas, took birth like fire \[which, though present everywhere, manifests in wood\]” (3.2.15), first of all Indra offers obeisances to His part manifestations: Bhagavan is Maha-Vaikuntha-natha. The Purusa is the creator of mahat-tattva. The great Soul is Paramatma.

Next, Indra bows to Him, the amsi. The name “Vasudeva” obliquely refers to His father, “Krsna” is His own name, and “chief of the Yadus” also points to His associates.

### 10.27.11

*svacchandopatta-dehaya visuddha-jhana-murtaye \|*  
*sarvasmai sarva-bijaya sarva-bhutatmane namah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sva—own (or of His own devotees); chanda—by the desire; upatta—is taken; dehaya—whose body; visuddha—transcendental; jnana— awareness; murtaye—who is the form; sarvasmai—who is everything; sarva-bijaya—who is the cause of everything; sarva-bhuta-atmane—who is the Soul in all beings; namah—obeisance.

*svacchandopatta-dehaya visuddha-jhana-murtaye sarvasmai sarva- bijaya sarva-bhutatmane namah (astu).*

**Перевод:**

**“I salute the Lord. He assumes a body by His will, is the embodiment of sheer awareness, is everything, is the cause of all, and is the Soul in all beings.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Do you mean that I am a Yadava?” “No. My obeisance to You who take bodies by the desire (chandena = icchaya) of Your devotees (sva = svesam bhaktanam). In addition, Your body is transcendental awareness (visuddha-jhana-murtaye = visuddham jnanam eva murtir yasya tasmai). You are everything... by Maya. Why? You are the cause of all (sarva-bijaya = sarvasya karanaya). Therefore: sarva-bhutatmane namah.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“Obeisances to You, by whom divine bodies, such as Matsya and Kurma, are taken at will because of Your devotees.” Visuddha means “beyond Maya,” and so visuddha- jhana-murtaye means “You whose bodies are beyond Maya and are forms of spiritual awareness in terms of being self-manifestations.” The seed, or cause, of all is the Maha-Purusa.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Given that Krsna is the object of prema in many ways, the term svacchandopatta-dehaya means He assumes a body in conformity with the desire of each devotee to bestow bliss by dasya, by sakhya, by vatsalya, and by romance.

### 10.27.12

*mayedam bhagavan gostha-nasayasara-vayubhih \|*  
*cestitam vihate yajne manina tivra-manyuna \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

maya—by me; idam—this; bhagavan—O Lord; gostha-nasaya—for the destruction of the cowherd community; asara—by hard rain; vayubhih—and by winds; cestitam—was done; vihate yajhe—when the sacrifice was disrupted; manina—\[by me\] who had false pride; tivra—was fierce; manyuna—whose anger.

*bhagavan! yajhe vihate (sati) manina tivra-manyuna (ca) maya asara-vayubhih gostha-nasaya idam cestitam.*

**Перевод:**

**“O Lord, I did what I did to destroy the cowherd community with hard rain and with tempests when the sacrifice meant for me was annulled. I was conceited and very angry.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Indra tells his offense, mentioned with the word krtagasah (of me who did an offense) in text 8. “This improper deed (idam = idam akrtyam) was done (cestitam = krtam) by me.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The pronoun idam (this) signifies that the offense was done recently. The sense of Bhagavan is: “O You who are omniscient. You already know my wicked deed. What more can I say about my wickedness?”

Or the gist of Bhagavan is: “I did this to destroy Your community even though You, who are replete with all types of godly might, were directly present.” Indra thus implies that his offense is even more serious because of this.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“My dear Indra, you are My devotee, as proven by your prayer. But these wicked clouds, even without your order, greatly disturbed My Vraja. Therefore you should punish them.” Anticipating such a purifying chastisement, Indra thinks: “Alas, there is no scope for duplicity against Him, the indwelling Soul,” and frankly states what his deed was. He gives the reason: vihate yajne (when the sacrifice was annulled). “But,” Krsna might reply, “although I, Your master, cancelled it, I did not notice any faulty response by you, My servant. Indra answers to this with manina, implying the idea: “What is impossible for one who is falsely proud of having godly capabilities?” “Still, even if pride and other material emotions arise by the arrangement of Providence in My devotees, they eradicate those faults by mental control.” Indra replies with tivra-manyuna. The idea is anger is very fierce, and can even disrupt mental control by force.

### 10.27.13

*tvayesdnugrhito ’smi dhvasta-stambho vrthodyamah \|*  
*isvaram gurum atmanam tvam aham saranam gatah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tvaya—by You; isa—O Lord; anugrhitah—was shown mercy; asmi—I (or am); dhvasta—was destroyed; stambhah—I whose false pride; vrtha-udyamah—I whose undertaking was fruitless; isvaram— the Lord; gurum—the teacher; atmanam—the Soul (Paramatma, and Paramesvara); tvdm—to You; aham—I; saranam gatah—have taken shelter.

*isa! dhvasta-stambhah vrthodyamah (aham) tvaya anugrhitah asmi. aham tvam isvaram gurum atmanam saranam gatah (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“You did me a favor, Lord. My hubris is crushed. My undertaking was fruitless. I come to take shelter of You, God, the Guru, the Soul.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Nevertheless, my dear Lord, You did me a favor.” That favor is expounded with the words dhvasta-stambhah (my hubris is crushed) and vrthodyamah (my efforts were rendered useless).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“O Isa” means “O controller of all.” Indra implies: “Although You can punish me, You only did me a favor.” That favor was substantial; it was not done in vain. This is exactly what he says with dhvasta-stambhah, “I in whom the hubris is gone” (= nasta-madah yasmin), because: vrthodyamah, “My efforts were crushed” (= hatodyamah). In dhvasta (perished), the causative sense is meant (“was caused to perish”) (because the verbal root dhvans is intransitive).

“Therefore, the Guru is only You, and so I, an offender, take shelter of You.” Indra mentions two other reasons for taking shelter: Krsna is the controller (isvaram = niyantaram) and is the foundational essence of being (atmanam = mula-svarupam) of all, like the sun is of its rays.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Although a doctor has been reviled, if he is merciful he still cures the sick. My disease of false pride is now destroyed. This is because my endeavor is spoiled, that of trying to disrupt Vraja. In this way, You are the Lord in terms of being the controller, the spiritual master due to acting beneficially, and the Soul inasmuch as You are the ultimate abode of love.”

### 10.27.14

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*evam sahkirtitah krsno maghona bhagavan amum \|\|*  
*megha-gambhiraya vaca prahasann idam abravit \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah uvaca—Sri Suka said; evam—in this way; sahkirtitah— glorified; krsnah—Krsna; maghona—by Indra; bhagavan—the Lord; amum—to him; megha—\[like the rumble\] of a cloud; gambhiraya—deep; vaca—with a voice; prahasan—while laughing; idam—this; abravit—spoke.

*sri-sukah uvaca—bhagavan krsnah maghona evam sahkirtitah prahasan amum megha-gambhiraya vaca idam abravit.*

**Перевод:**

**Sri Suka said: Thus glorified by Indra, Lord Krsna laughed and spoke to him as follows in a voice deep as the rumbling of a cloud.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Krsna was praised (sahkirtitah = stutah) by Indra. With the word bhagavan, which signifies that He is almighty in the highest way, Suka implies that Krsna did not care too much for Indra, an insignificant offender, and therefore he describes His voice as the rumbling of a cloud (megha = megha-garjita); this means Krsna is prestigious. The word prahasan (laughing; eminently smiling) means He is high-minded. “Krsna spoke to him.” In point of amum (him): The pronoun adas (him), from which amum is made, is in the singular: By common usage, the sense is Indra is insignificant.

### 10.27.15

*sri-bhagavan uvaca*  
*maya te ’kari maghavan makha-bhango ’nugrhnata \|\|*  
*mad-anusmrtaye nityam mattasyendra-sriya bhrsam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-bhagavan uvdca—the Lord said; maya—by Me; te—your; akari—was done; maghavan—hey Indra; makha—of the sacrifice; bhangah—the disrupture; anugrhnata—\[by Me,\] who was doing a favor; mat-anusmrtaye—for the sake of remembering Me; nityam— always; mattasya—of you who were arrogantly proud; indra-sriya— because the opulence of a king; bhrsam—very.

*sri-bhagavan uvdca—maghavan! indra-sriya bhrsam mattasya (tava) nityam mad-anusmrtaye (tvayi) anugrhnata maya te makha-bhangah akari.*

**Перевод:**

**The Lord said: “Wanting to be merciful to you, Indra, I disrupted the sacrifice meant for you so that you always remember Me. You were very conceited because of your godly opulence.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Indra having offered his inner thought, the Supreme Lord does the same. Indra was very conceited because of his sovereignty over the gods (indra-sriya = deva-rajyena).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The Lord speaks in a manner suitable for being the Almighty: “By disrupting the sacrifice, I was only doing you a favor (anugrhnata = anugrhnata eva); I was not angry at you.”

### 10.27.16

*mam aisvarya-sri-madandho danda-panim na pasyati \|*  
*tam bhramsayami sampadbhyo yasya cecchamy anugraham \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

mam—Me; aisvarya—of kingly power; sri—and beauty (or opulence); mada—because of the false pride; andhah—blind; danda-panim—Me in whose hand is a rod; na pasyati—he does not see; tam—him; bhramsayami—I cause the fall; sampadbhyah—from his assets; yasya—to whom; ca—also; icchami—I desire; anugraham— favor.

*aisvarya-sri-madandhah (janah) mam danda-panim na pasyati. yasya ca anugraham icchami, (aham) tam sampadbhyah bhramsayami.*

**Перевод:**

**“Blinded by the false pride of power and wealth, one does not see that I hold the rod of punishment. If I want to do him a favor, I make him fall from his exalted position.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“I take away the wealth and other kinds of affluence which were the results of his great power and beauty of him to whom I want to show mercy. In your case, however, I saw that you would not be able to tolerate that, and so I only disrupted the sacrifice meant for you.”

### 10.27.17

*gamyatam sakra bhadram vah kriyatam me ’nusasanam \|*  
*sthiyatam svadhikaresu yuktair vah stambha-varjitaih \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

gamyatam—going should be done; sakra—hey Indra; bhadram— good fortune; vah—your; kriyatam—should be done; me—My; anusdsanam—teachings; sthiyatdm—staying in place should be done; sva-adhikaresu—in you own jurisdictions; yuktaih—qualified; vah—by all of you; stambha-varjitaih—devoid of false pride.

*sakra! (svarge) gamyatam. (gatva ca) me anusasanam kriyatam. (tena) vah bhadram (bhavisyati). yuktaih stambha-varjitaih vah svadhikaresu sthiyatam (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Indra, you may go. May good betide you. Practice My precepts. You gods should properly, without arrogance, remain in your official positions.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Vah signifies yusmabhih (by all of you): The plurality is meant to include Varuna and other gods. “But where should I go, since You are the Lord even in heaven?” To this possible objection the Lord says kriyatam and so on: “Remain in your duty as you were, but by following My order.” Yuktaih means not infatuated, and stambha-varjitaih means free from egoism.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

This favor was not the best possible blessing, only because he was not qualified for anything better, given that he had not evoked His full satisfaction. Therefore later, by not carrying out His precepts he will commit another offense. This will be clear in the episode of the theft of the Parijata tree.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

In this connection Krsna does not say “You will never have false pride in the future,” and so it should be understood that his false pride will reappear, in the incident of stealing the Parijata tree, for the purpose of perfecting the Lord’s pastime.

### 10.27.18

*athaha surabhih krsnam abhivandya manasvini \|*  
*sva-santanair upamantrya gopa-rupinam isvaram \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

atha—afterward; aha—speaks (spoke); surabhih—the Surabhi cow; krsnam—to Krsna; abhivandya—after offering signs of respect; manasvini—she was clever (cheerful); sva-santanaih—with her offsprings; upamantrya—after getting for His attention; gopa-rupinam—who had the form of a cowherd; isvaram—the Lord.

*atha surabhih gopa-rupinam isvaram krsnam abhivandya manasvini (sati) sva-santanaih upamantrya (enam prati) aha (sma).*

**Перевод:**

**Afterward, noble-minded Surabhi saluted Krsna, the Lord in the form of a cowherd, caught His attention with the cows, her offsprings, and spoke to Him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Surabhi’s offsprings are the cows. She called out to Him (upamantrya = sambodhya): “Krsna, Krsna!” and so on.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The cows are her progeny like Krsna is in Candra’s dynasty. Why did she not come first to plead on Indra’s behalf? The reason is: manasvini, she is clever (= dhira-citta).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“She was with her progeny,” the cows present in Vraja. Her conceit of considering them as her progeny, even though she is material and they, the associates of Krsna, are transcendental, is because they took birth in her lineage. In like manner, Candra, the moon, though material, identifies Krsna, who took birth in the lunar dynasty, as his descendant.

### 10.27.19

*surabhir uvaca*  
*krsna krsna maha-yogin visvatman visva-sambhava \|*  
*bhavata loka-nathena sa-natha vayam acyuta \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

surabhih uvaca—Surabhi said; krsna—O Krsna; krsna—O Krsna; maha-yogin—O You who have great mystical might; visva-atman—O Soul of the universe; visva-sambhava—O origin of the universe; bhavata—by You; loka-nathena—who are the master of the worlds; sa-nathah—with a master; vayam—we; acyuta—O Acyuta.

*surabhih uvaca—krsna! krsna! maha-yogin! visvatman! visva-sambhava! acyuta! bhavata loka-nathena vayam sa-nathah (bhavamah).*

**Перевод:**

**Surabhi said: “O Krsna, Krsna! O You who have great mytic might, O Soul of the universe, O source of the cosmos, O Acyuta! With You, the master of the world, we have a master.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Even though hurt by Indra, we were protected by You” (sa-nathah = sa-nathah krtah = raksitah).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Maha-yogin means “O You who always manifest the godly might of Yoga, such as anima (the power of becoming extremely small). The name “Krsna” refers to Him as a cowherd, and the other vovatives refer to Him as God. “With You, though You are the master of the worlds, we have a master.” The name “Acyuta” affirms that the Lord is eternally related as the master of cows.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The repetition in “Krsna, Krsna!” is due to joy. The gist of the vocative maha-yogin is: “By lifting Govardhana, only by the power of Yoga, You saved my offsprings.”

### 10.27.20

*tvam nah paramakam daivam tvam na indro jagat-pate \|*  
*bhavaya bhava go-vipra-devanam ye ca sadhavah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tvam—You; nah—our; paramakam—supreme; daivam—God; tvam—You; nah—our; indrah—Indra; jagat-pate—O master of the universe; bhavaya—for the well-being; bhava—be; go-vipra- devanam—of cows, of Brahmanas, and of gods; ye—who; ca—and; sadhavah—saintly persons.

*jagat-pate! tvam nah paramakam daivam (asi). tvam nah indrah (asi). ye sadhavah (bhavanti, tesam) go-vipra-devanam ca bhavaya (tvam indrah) bhava.*

**Перевод:**

**“You are our supreme Deity. You are our Indra, O ruler of the universe. Be our king for the well-being of bovine animals, of Brahmanas, of the gods and of the pious.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“You are our supreme Deity (paramakam = paramam) (daivam = devata). Therefore, O Lord of the universe, for the prosperity (bhavaya = abhvudaya) of cattle, of Brahmanas, et al., only You should be our Indra.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

In paramaka, the suffix ?an is used by the rule: nitau ca tad-yuktat, “Ka and kan are also used when niti (proper conduct) is understood” (Astadhyayi 5.3.77).

“O master of the universe, be our Indra.” The sense is: “You are our master although You are also the master of the universe.” Even by being the king of cows, the prosperity of Brahmanas and of others arise; this is from Go-sukta:

*gobhyo yajhah pravartante gobhyo devah samuthitah \|*  
*gobhir vedah samudgirnah sa-sadanga-pada-kramah \|\|*

**“Sacrifices take place because of cows. The devatas arise because of cows. The Vedas along with the pada-krama and the six auxiliary branches of learning were proclaimed because of cows.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“You are our Deity because of whom there is the highest joy” (parama-kam = paramam sukham yasmat tat). The vocative jagat-pate implies: “Although You are the master of the universe, now, because You are acting as a cowherd and because You defeated Indra, You should take the role of Indra.”

### 10.27.21

*indram nas tvabhiseksyamo brahmana noditavayam \|*  
*avatirno ’si visvatman bhumer bharapanuttaye \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

indram—as Indra (king); nah—our; tva—You; abhiseksyamah— we will consecrate; brahmana—by Brahma; noditah—encouraged; vayam—we; avatirnah asi—You have descended; visva-atman—O Soul of all; bhumeh—of the Earth; bhara—the burden; apanuttaye— to dispel.

*visvatman! brahmana noditah vavam tva nah indram abhiseksyamah. (tvam) bhumeh bharapanuttaye avatirnah asi (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Encouraged by Brahma, we will consecrate You as our Indra. O Soul of all, You have descended to remove the Earth’s burden.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“But,” Krsna might object, “you already have an Indra.” She replies here. The sense is: “We’ve had enough with Purandara being the Indra.” “But the chief god is Indra, so how can I possibly be Indra?” They answer with the words beginning avatirno’si.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“You are our king; we will let everyone know this by doing an official ceremony.” “But Brahma gave Purandara the post of king, so he will disapprove.” They respond with brahmana and so on. The sense is: “No. We have his approval.” “Then why did Brahma not come?” “Only we have the right to do this. We are antaranga, as the mother of Your cows, whereas he is bahiranga because he only has jurisdiction over the material world.” This explains the plural in vayam (we), which she uses because she thinks highly of herself. Or the plural includes Indra, who was with her, and her retinue.

It’s understood that when Indra begged forgiveness, Brahma, who had already offended the Lord previously, did not come out of fear of committing another offense.

The drift of avatirno’si was explained by Sridhara Svami. There is another rendering: “I am just the son of Nanda the cowherd, so how can I possibly be your Deity? Neither you or Brahma have considered this.” “You do not take birth like a jiva does. You have descended from the topmost Goloka. You are the Soul of the universe. It is fitting that the world should continue because of You.

Everyone will be happy when Your abhiseka will take place. You already approve of this because You descended to make people joyful.” It is implied that everyone will be happy that way, by the logical reasoning expressed in this verse:

*yatha taror mula-nisecanena*  
*trpyanti tat-skandha-bhujopasakhah \|*  
*pranopaharac ca yathendriyanam*  
*tathaiva sarvarhanam acyutejya \|\|*

**“Like the boughs, branches and branchlets of a tree are nourished by watering the root and like the senses are nourished by sustaining the life force, by paying homage to Acyuta everyone is honored.” (4.31.14)**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“You are our Indra.” “But,” Krsna might ask, “on whose order are you acting like this? Or else, are you doing so independently?” She replies with the words beginning brahmana. The gist is: “When Indra, distraught out of extreme fear, went to submit his problem to Brahma to get assistance from him, at that time Brahma remembered his own offense, and after fearfully considering the matter, ordered me: “Oh Surabhi, you are the most special object of affection of that Lord who is the protector of your offsprings. Therefore you should go and beg that ocean of mercy to forgive Indra for his offense. Perform His ablution ceremony to coronate Him as the king of cows.”

“Furthermore, what is the special glorification involved in consecrating You as our Indra, given that You are the Indra of millions of universes and given that the service of Your lotus feet is difficult to achieve even by Brahma, Rudra and other great gods? Nevertheless, let this bathing ceremony be performed simply for the sake of our elevation.” This is the substance of avatirno ’si.

### 10.27.22-23

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*evam krsnam upamantrya surabhih pavasatmanah \|*  
*jalair akasa-gangaya airavata-karoddhrtaih \|\|*  
*indrah surarsibhih sakam codito deva-matrbhih \|*  
*abhyasincata dasarham govinda iti cabhyadhat \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah uvaca—Sri Suka said; evam—in this way; krsnam—Krsna; upamantrya—having summoned; surabhih—Surabhi; payasa—with milk; atmanah—her own; jalaih—with the honorable water; akasa- gangayah—of the heavenly Ganges; airavata-kara—by Airavata’s trunk; uddhrtaih—\[water,\] extracted; indrah—Indra; sura-rsibhih sakam—with the Rsis who are gods; coditah—encouraged; deva- matrbhih—by the mothers of the gods; abhyasihcata—he/ she bathed; dasarham—Krsna (“descendant of King Dasarha”); govindah— Govinda; iti—this (or end of quotation); ca—and; abhyadhat—he/ she named.

*sri-sukah uvaca—surabhih krsnam evam upamantrya atmanah payasa indrah (ca) surarsibhih sakam (agatabhih) deva-matrbhih coditah airavata-karoddhrtaih akasa-gahgayah jalaih dasarham abhyasincata, govindah iti abhyadhat ca.*

**Перевод:**

**Suka said: Surabhi asked Krsna to come forth in this way and gave Him an ablution with her milk. Indra, encouraged by the divine mothers and accompanied by godly Rsis, did so with the water of the heavenly Ganges collected by Airavata’s trunk. Krsna, the descendant of Dasarha, received the name Govinda.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Surabhi bathed Him with her own milk, and Indra also bathed Him, with the water of the heavenly Ganges.

”By the mothers of the gods” (deva-matrbhih) means by Aditi and others, or else by the gods and by the mothers.

They named Him “Govinda” (abhyadhat = nama krtavan), by the derivation: gah pasun, gam svargam va indratvena vindatiti krtva govindah, “He obtains the cows, or else heaven, as the king.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Upamantrya means Surabhi first requested Him to accept to become her Indra. Out of shyness, Krsna did not verbally accept, yet He implicitly did so, by the maxim: “Silence is a sign of consent.”

Indra did not come forward of his own accord, but was sent (coditah = presitah) by the divine mothers, who had come from heaven with the godly Rsis (surarsibhih sakam = surarsibhih sakam tatra saksad agatabhih), as follows: “Krsna is Bhagavan. He is merciful and cares for those who surrender to Him. Go ahead and perform a great festival with devotion.” Thus Indra, accompanied by those sages, performed the sacred ablution with waters, by means of jewel-studded pitchers brought by Airavata, according to Visnu Purana (5.12.13). The waters of holy places had initially been collected by Airavata.

The name “Govinda” means gavam indrah (king of cows), because the intended meaning is gavendra and because that name was implied by the mention: privan na indro gavam, “May He, the king of cows, be pleased with us” (10.26.25). Another reason is this upcoming text: iti go-gokula-patim govindam abhisicya, “Having thus performed the sacred ablution of Govinda as the king of cows and of the cowherd community” (verse 28). The derivation of that name is irregular, and so the name is classed in the list of prsodaradis (list of words irregularly formed, beginning from prsodara).

Krsna’s name “Dasarha” is mentioned to signify that being Govinda is more eminent than being the descendant of Dasarha.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The name Govinda means either “He obtains the cows as the king”, “He obtains heaven as the king” or “He obtains the senses (go = indriya) of His devotees, due to being attractive.”

### 10.27.24

*tatragatas tumburu-naradadayo*  
*gandharva-vidyadhara-siddha-caranah \|*  
*jagur yaso loka-malapaham hareh*  
*surahganah sannanrtur mudanvitah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tatra—there; agatah—who had arrived; tumburu—Tumburu (a chief Gandharva); narada—Narada; adayah—of whom the foremost were; gandharva-vidyadhara-siddha-caranah—the Gandharvas, the Vidyadharas, the Siddhas and the Caranas; jaguh—sang; yasah—the glory; loka-mala-apaham—which dispels the impurity of the world; hareh—of Hari; sura-anganah—the wives of gods; sannanrtuh— danced; muda anvitah—endowed with joy.

*tatra agatah tumburu-naradadayah gandharva-vidvadhara- siddha-caranah loka-malapaham hareh vasah jaguh. suranganah mudanvitah sannanrtuh.*

**Перевод:**

**The celestial beings, headed by Tumburu and Narada, who had come there sang Hari’s glory, the purifier of the world. The goddesses joyfully danced.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Then a great festival which delighted the world occurred. This is mentioned in three verses. “They had arrived there.” That place, according to Varaha Purana, was Sakra-kunda, or else, according to Skanda Purana, Govinda-kunda. Those two places are near Govardhana and are well-known.

Mudanvitah (joyful) is an adjective that modifies everyone; this is the reason the abhiseka turned out as a great festival. Tumburu is mentioned first due to being better than Narada in singing. This is clear in Linga Purana. Narada is an eternal associate of the Lord; he is the best of all associates, including Garuda, of the Lord’s Avataras. The word adi signifies Citraratha and others. Or the sense of tumburu-naradadayah is Tumburu and Narada were at the front of the celestial beings (= tumburu-naradau adau agratah yesam te gandharvadayah). Hari’s glory cleanses the faults of everyone, that is, the faults in bhakti, such as the desire for impersonal liberation.

### 10.27.25

*tam tustuvur deva-nikaya-ketavo*  
*hy avakirams cadbhuta-puspa-vrstibhih \|*  
*lokah param nirvrtim apnuvams trayo*  
*gavas tada gam anayan payo-drutam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tam—Him; tustuvuh—praised; deva—of gods; nikava—of the multitude; ketavah—the most eminent; hi—only (the same ones); avakiran—they covered; ca—and; adbhuta—amazing; puspa—of flowers; vrstibhih—with showers; lokah—the worlds; param—high; nirvrtim—joy; apnuvan—got; trayah—three; gavah—the cows; tada—at that time; gam—the Earth; anayan—brought; payah—with their milk; drutam—to a fluid state.

*deva-nikava-ketavah hi tam tustuvuh adbhuta-puspa-vrstibhih (enam) avakiran ca. travah lokah param nirvrtim apnuvan. tada gavah gam payo-drutam anayan.*

**Перевод:**

**The most eminent gods eulogized Him and covered Him by raining amazing flowers on Him. The three worlds highly rejoiced. At that time, the cows made the Earth wet with their milk.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The word ketu means mukhya (best), in the sense of being worthy of being seen like a flag (ketu). “The cows made the Earth wet (drutam = ardram) (anayan = akurvan) with their milk.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The best gods were Varuna and other such gods.

### 10.27.26

*nana-rasaughah sarito vrksa asan madhu-sravah \|*  
*akrsta-pacyausadhayo girayo ’bibhrad unmanin \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

nana—various; rasa—because of liquids; oghah—in which are streams; saritah—the rivers; vrksah—the trees; asan—became; madhu—sweet sap; sravah—exuded; akrsta—without being cultivated; pacya—were ripe; osadhayah—the plants; girayah—the hills; abibhrat—had; ut—above; manin—gems.

*saritah nana-rasaughah asan. vrksah madhu-sravah (asan). akrsta-pacyausadhayah girayah unmanin abibhran.*

**Перевод:**

**The rivers contained streams of various liquids, the trees exuded sweet sap, the fruits and vegetables came to maturity without cultivation, and the hills held gems above ground.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

The rivers carried streams of milk and so on. Akrsta-pacyausadhavah should read: akrsta-pacya ausadhayah, meaning rice and other plants became ripe without farming (akrsta-pacyah = karsana vina eva pakvah). Or akrsta-pacyausadhavah is an adjective of girayah, “the hills, on which the plants became ripe without farming.” “The hills had outwardly manifest gems that were in the ground (unmanin - garbha-gatan manin ut udgatan bahih prakatan)." The verb abibhrat should read: abibharuh.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The drift is this: Whatever was special in Vrndavana before this occurred all over the world at that time. In akrsta-pacyausadhayah, the absence of a case ending after pacya is poetic license, or else the phonetic combination is.

### 10.27.27

*krsne ’bhisikta etani sarvani kuru-nandana \|*  
*nirvairany abhavams tata krurany api nisargatah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

krsne abhisikte—when Krsna was consecrated; etani—these; sarvani—all; kuru-nandana—O son of the Kurus; nirvairani— devoid of enmity; abhavan—became; tata—hey dear boy; krurani— angry; api—even; nisargatah—by nature.

*kuru-nandana! tata! krsne abhisikte (sati) etani sarvani nisargatah krurani api (jantuni) nirvairani abhavan.*

**Перевод:**

**Dear son of the Kurus, when Krsna was given the sacred ablution, all living beings, including those angry by nature, became devoid of animosity.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Not only were qualities enhanced, but natural faults such as an inherent mutual enmity ceased to exist. Mutual enemies such as snakes and mongooses became friends like when Krsna took birth: jayamane janardane (10.3.8). Still, Vrndavana was always like that; this completes the idea.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The word bhutani (beings) needs to be added to the sentence.

### 10.27.28

*iti go-gokula-patim govindam abhisicya sah \|*  
*anujnato yayau sakro vrto devadibhir divam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

iti—in that way; go—of the cows; go-kula—and of the community of cowherds; patim—the master; govindam—Govinda; abhisicya— having consecrated sah—he; anujhatah—given permission; yayau— went; sakrah—Indra; vrtah—surrounded; deva-adibhih—by gods and others; divam—to heaven.

*sah sakrah iti go-gokula-patim govindam abhisicya anujhatah (san) devadibhih vrtah divam yayau (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**Having thus performed the sacred ablution of Govinda as the king of cows and of the cowherd community, Indra, having received permission to leave, departed for heaven while being escorted by the gods and others.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The pronoun sah (he) means both “although he was a big offender” and “his polite behavior was accepted by the Lord.” Indra consecrated Him who was naturally Govinda as the king of cows and of the cowherd community (go- gokula-patim = go-gokula-patitvena).

In the uttara-khanda of Padma Purana, it is said that Nanda, Yasoda and others arrived at that place:

*gopa-vrddhas ca gopyas ca drstva tatra satakratum \|*  
*tena sampujitas caiva praharsam atulam vayuh \|\|*

**“There the elderly cowherd men and the cowherd ladies saw Indra, who then honored them, and so they felt an incomparable rapture.”**

However, it’s understood that the above description occurred in another kalpa because it contradicts the previous text: vivikta upasangamya, “Indra approached Krsna in a solitary place” (10.27.2).

## Chapter 28 - Krsna Rescues Nanda From the Realm of Varuna and Shows His Own Abode to the Cowherds

### 10.28.1

*sri-suka uvaca,*  
*ekadasyam niraharah samabhyarcya janardanam \|*  
*snatum nandas tu kalindyam dvadasyam jalam avisat \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah uvaca—Sri Suka said; ekadasyam—on the eleventh day of the fortnight; niraharah—he who is fasting; samabhyarcya—having properly worshiped; janardanam—Janardana; snatum—to bathe; nandah—Nanda; tu—only; kalindyam—in the Kalindi (Yamuna); dvadasyam—on the twelfth day; jalam—the water; avisat—he entered.

*sri-badarayanih uvaca—nandah tu ekadasyam niraharah (san) janardanam samabhyarcya dvadasyam kalindyam snatum jalam avisat.*

**Перевод:**

**Suka said: On ekadasi, Nanda held a fast and worshiped Janardana. On dvadasi, he entered the water of the Kalindi to bathe.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*astavimse tato nandanayanam varunalayat \|*  
*vaikuntha-darsanam catha gopanam anuvarnyate \|\|*  
*govardhanam samuddhrtya vase krtvamaresvaram \|*  
*nandanayanatah krsno varunam ca vase ’nayat \|\|*

**“In the twenty-eighth chapter, this is described: Nanda was brought back from Varuna’s abode, and the cowherd men saw the transcendental world. After lifting Govardhana and subduing the king of gods, Krsna also subdued Varuna by bringing back Nanda.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Because of the context, Sukadeva narrates the same kind of deed: Varuna’s offense was similar to Indra’s, and in both cases Krsna diminished their aisvarya.

Nanda needed to take a bath as part of the procedure before breaking the fast. Dvadasi was the time for breaking the fast, but was almost finished.

The name Janardana is derived as: janair bhaktair ardyate 'trptataya nityam bhakty-artham yacyate in tatha, “He is requested by people, meaning He is always begged for the sake of bhakti by devotees due to being unsatisfied.” Nanda fasted to worship Him. For this reason, he entered the water to bathe in the Kalindi, which is known to increase bhakti to the Lord. The word tu (only) means Nanda entered alone. This shows how eager he was to do so.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The ekadasi had been unusually short: only six praharas (eighteen hours). The dvadasi, during which the fast had to be broken, was going to come to an end just before the sunrise of the next day.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*astavimso ’bhavan nanda-haranam varuna-stutih \|*  
*gopanam vismayautsukyad brahma-vaikuntha-darsanam \|\|*  
*indrasyagas ca tat-ksantim uktva sva-smrtim agate \|*  
*varunasyapi te vaktum aha lilantaram munih \|\|*

**“In the twenty-eighth chapter, the abduction of Nanda, Varuna’s praise, and the vision of Brahman and of Vaikuntha by the cowherds because of their eagerness for wonderment are told. Suka mentions another pastime in order to narrate Varuna’s offense and its absolution, which he remembered by describing Indra’s offense and its absolution.”**

### 10.28.2

*tam grhitvanayad bhrtyo varunasyasuro 'ntikam \|*  
*avijnayasurimvelam pravistam udakam nisi \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

tam—him; grhitva—after kidnapping; anayat—brought; bhrtyah—a servant; varunasya—of Varuna; asurah—a demon; antikam—near; avijhaya—not knowing; asurim—bad; velam—time; pravistam— who had entered; udakam—the water; nisi—at night.

*asurim velam avijnaya nisi udakam pravistam tam bhrtyah asurah grhitva varunasya antikam anayat.*

**Перевод:**

**Not knowing that the time was bad, Nanda entered the water at night. A demoniac servant of Varuna abducted him and brought him to Varuna.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Because he was intent on properly breaking the fast during dvadasi, of which there only remained a few minutes, Nanda did not consider that it was a bad time, and so even before dawn he proceeded to bathe on the strength of the scriptural injunction to enter the water in the dark of night. This statement of sastra is a reference:

*kalardham dvadasim drstva nisithad urdhvam eva hi \|*  
*amadhyahnah kriyah sarvah kartavyah sambhu-sasanat \|\|*

**“If one sees that the dvadasi will end a few minutes after the middle of the night, one should then perform all the duties usually prescribed in the forenoon of dvadasi, in accordance with the order of Lord Sambhu.”**

But a servant of Varuna, here called an asura in the sense that he was not too knowledgeable, kidnapped him. Ahead, Varuna will say: ajanata mamakena, “by my servant, who did not know” (10.28.7). The sense is he did not know bhagavad-dharma (bhakti).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The servant is called an asura because, due to his caste, he did not know vaisnava-dharma. The term asura is fitting here since it also shows that he was qualified, because of his brute force, to protect the waters at that bad time (asurim).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Avajnaya means Nanda disregarded the time.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Varuna’s servant was an asura. He brought Nanda to Varuna. The reason for that is: “Disregarding the bad time, Nanda entered the water.” Only out of ignorance, a fault was attributed to him. In truth, Nanda entered the water on the strength of scriptural injunction.

### 10.28.3

*cukrusus tam apasyantah krsna rameti gopakah \|*  
*bhagavams tad upasrutya pitaram varunahrtam \|*  
*tad-antikam gato rajan svanam abhaya-do vibhuh \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

cukrusuh—they shouted; tam—him; apasyantah—not seeing; krsna—O Krsna; rama—O Rama; in—(end of citation); gopakah— the cowherds; bhagavan—the Lord; tat upasrutya—hearing that; pitaram—His father; varuna-ahrtam—abducted by Varuna; tat- antikam—to his side (Varuna’s); gatah—went; rajan—O king; svanam—to His own; abhaya—of fearlessness; dah—the giver; vibhuh—Vibhu (“all-pervasive”).

*rajan! gopakah tam apasyantah krsna rama iti cukrusuh. tad (akrosanam) upasrutya bhagavan svanam abhaya-dah vibhuh pitaram varunahrtam (jhatva) tad-antikam gatah.*

**Перевод:**

**Not seeing him, the cowherds shouted: “Krsna! Rama!” Hearing this, the Lord, Vibhu, who gives fearlessness to His own, O king, went to Varuna, knowing that he had abducted His father.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Krsna gives fearlessness to His own” means He made them, who were dedicated to performing bhagavad-dharma, fearless: “Don’t be afraid.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The words from cukrusus tam form one half verse.215Those cowherds were the bodyguards of Nanda Maharaja and were appointed in the four directions. Although they yelled from a distance, Krsna heard the shouts as if they were nearby (upasrutya) (upa = samipe era). The word jhatva (upon understanding) needs to be added: “Krsna, understanding that His father had been taken by Varuna, went to meet Varuna.” The reason He was able to do so is pointed out in the matter of kaimutya (implied consequence): He is Vibhu, meaning He pervades. Krsna bestows fearlessness to His own, those born in the caste of cowherd—not to mention that He made His father fearless.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“The cowherd men” means those guarding Nanda when he went out during the night to take bath. Hearing them yelling, Krsna, who at that time was far away, heard the shouts as if they were near, because He is present everywhere. Understanding that His father had been abducted by Varuna, He came into the presence of the cowherd men who had been guarding Nanda Maharaja. He asked “where did My father go?” and beheld what happened, and so He jumped in the water and went to the place of Varuna. Krsna bestows fearlessness to His own in the sense that He was going to give fearlessness to His relatives by bringing back Nanda.

### 10.28.4

*praptam viksya hrsikesam loka-palah saparyaya \|*  
*mahatya pujayitvaha tad-darsana-mahotsavah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

praptam—who had arrived; viksya—upon seeing; hrsikesam— Hrsikesa; loka-palah—guardian of the world216; saparyaya— with homage (with paraphernalia for homage); mahatya—great; pujayitva—after worshiping; aha—spoke; tat-darsana—by seeinf Him; maha-utsavah—he has a great festival.

*loka-palah praptam hrsikesam viksya tad-darsana-mahotsavah (san) saparyaya mahatya pujayitva aha (sma).*

**Перевод:**

**When Varuna, a regent of the quarters, saw that Hrsikesa had arrived, he paid homage to Him with elaborate paraphernalia for worship. In a festive mood because of seeing Him, Varuna spoke as follows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Saparyaya means arhanena (by offering homage).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The name Hrsikesa means He sets in motion all sensory activity. The drift of “Varuna saw that Hrsikesa was obtained” is Varuna understood that Krsna had arrived although He is normally out of the range of sensory perception.
