Varuna’s epithet as loka-pala (regent of the quarters) hints at his ability to do a fantastic formal worship of the Lord. By seeing Him, he had great bliss (mahotsavah = mahan utsavah anandah yasya): This is the reason for doing that sort of homage.

The following is being said: At first Krsna was angry at his bad servant.Upon arriving, however, He noticed that the servant was not too agitated even though he was afraid and that he had approached Him respectfully by offering dandavat pranama, and so Krsna’s outlook bore signs of forgiveness given that He thought His objective would be fulfilled. Afterward Varuna had great bliss by seeing Him and began to offer a praise and to pay homage to Him.

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

The word saparya means puja-samagri (parapher¬nalia for formal worship).

### 10.28.5

*varuna uvaca*  
*adya me nibhrto deho ’dyaivartho ’dhigatah prabho \|*  
*tvat-pada-bhajo bhagavann avapuh param adhvanah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

varunah uvaca—Varuna said; adya—today; me—my; nibhrtah— is fulfilled; dehah—body; adya eva—right now; arthah—the goal; adhigatah—is achieved; prabho—O Almighty; tvat-pada—Your feet; bhajah—those who serve; bhagavan—O Lord; avapuh— reached; param—the other side; adhvanah—of the path.

*varunah uvaca—prabho! bhagavan! adya me dehah nibhrtah. adya eva (mama) arthah adhigatah. tvat-pada-bhajah adhvanah param avapuh.*

**Перевод:**

**Varuna said: “Almighty Lord, today my having a body has become a success. Today my goal has been reached. Those who serve Your feet reach the end of the path.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Now the body is being held by me (me = maya) (nibhrtah = dhrtah).” The sense is: “When I first caught sight of You, I achieved the success of having a body.” Or nibhrtah means purna-manorathah, “My body has fulfilled its purpose.”

“Right now, real wealth (arthah) is obtained.” Varuna, the master of scores of great jewels, never came across such wealth. Moreover: “Those who serve Your feet obtain liberation.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

“The goal (arthah), liberation, has just been attained to a high degree (adhigatah = adhikam prapatah)." The reason for that is tvat-pada and the rest. Or the goal is bhakti: “It has been attained due to my being qualified (adhigatah = adhikaritaya praptah). Those who serve Your feet go to the transcendental world.” That is fitting; this is the sense of bhagavan, “O Bhagavan, You who expand Your glory.”

Or the gist is: “Your devotees attain Vaikuntha, but now I am seeing You, Nanda-nandana, in person in my home!”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

The verse was explained by Sridhara Svami. In his commentary, his gloss purna-manorathah should be taken as a bahuvrihi compound: me mama ?urnO manoratho yatra (my body, regarding which the desire has been fulfilled).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Your devotees go beyond the path... of material life.”

### 10.28.6

*namas tubhyam bhagavate brahmane paramatmane \|*  
*na yatra sruvate maya loka-srsti-vikalpana \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

namah—obeisance; tubhyam—to You; bhagavate—who are God in form; brahmane—who are Brahman; parama-atmane—the Soul; na—not; yatra—in whom; sriiyate—is heard of; maya—Maya; ioka- srsti—the creation of the world; vikalpana—which arranges.

*tubhyam bhagavate brahmane paramatmane namah (astu), yatra maya loka-srsti-vikalpana na sruyate.*

**Перевод:**

**“My profound respects to You, Lord. You are Brahman and Paramatma. No one has ever heard that Maya, which fancifies the creation of the world, has anything to do with You.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Bhagavate means: niratisayaisvaryaya (to You whose godly might is unexcelled); brahmane means: purnaya (You who are complete); and paramatmane means: sarva-jiva-niyantre (You who control all souls). The reason for all of the above is: na yatra and the rest: “In You, Maya, which diversifies the creation of the universe (loka-srsti-vikalpana = loka-srstim vikalpayati), is unheard of.” The sense is: “You do not have ignorance.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

While describing His glory, he bows with bhakti. Given that the sequence is: Bhagavan, Brahman, and Paramatma, the sense of the term Brahman should be explained in terms of being the consequence of being Bhagavan, and the sense of Paramatma as being the consequence of being Brahman.217The rest was revealed by the venerable one.

There is another rendering. Krsna might say, “What are you talking about? I m just the son of a cowherd.” Varuna counters that here. The sequence “Bhagavan, Brahman, Paramatma” breaks the order stated earlier: brahmeti paramatmeti bhagavan iti sabdyate (1.2.11).

With na yatra and so on, he says He is not a form of Maya. Varuna says Maya is loka-srsti-vikalpana in the sense that she has the power to diversify the creation of people, that is, of the souls (= lokanam jivanam eva srstim sa vitatataya kalpayitum saknoti), and so she has no power over Him, Isvara. The drift is: Although He is Paramatma and although He is Paramesvara, by virtue of having no connection with Maya His status as Para-Brahman is substantiated. The purport here is: “Now that You have come here, by seeing You I am fully successful.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

While describing His glory, he bows with bhakti. Bhagavan is He who is replete with the six kinds of aisvarya. Paramatma is the inner controller of all. Brahman is He by whom those powers are not revealed to some qualified person.

(Additions are underlined.) Maya has the power to diversify the creation of the souls, and so she has no power over Him, Isvara. It is thus shown that another kind of Maya. the svarupa-sakti. fashions the respective varieties of His aisvarya. forms and qualities. The purport here is: “Now that You have come here, by seeing You I am fully successful.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

The gist is: “You are to be worshipped by means of bhakti, jnana and yoga.” With na yatra he means to say: “Those who think that Your status of Godhead, being the impersonal Absolute and being the personal Absolute are based on the material varieties of illusion are deluded.” Maya is the energy from which comes the variegated arrangement of the creation of the world (= loka-srster vividha-kalpanam yatah sa).

### 10.28.7

*ajanata mamakena mudhenakarya-vedina \|*  
*anito ’yam tava pita tad bhavan ksantum arhati \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

ajanata—who did not know; mamakena—by my servant; mudhena—who is an idiot; akarya-vedina—who knows what not to do (or who does not know what needs to be done); anitah—was brought; ayam— he (well-known); tava—Your; pita—father; tat—that (or therefore); bhavan—You (honorific); ksantum arhati—are qualified to forgive.

*ayam tava pita ajanata mamakena mudhena akarya-vedina anitah (iti yat), bhavan tat ksantum arhati.*

**Перевод:**

**“He, Your father, was brought here by my servant, an ignorant idiot who knows what not to do. Therefore may You, sir, be pleased to forgive this.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Be pleased to forgive what was done, the abduc¬tion of Your father.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“Please forgive my big offense, because my servant is ignorant.” This means the servant did not know that Nanda was Krsna’s father. The reason for that is the servant is a fool (mudhena = murkhena); his habit is to know what not to do (akarya-vedina = akaryam kartum silam asya).

Ayam (he, or this) signifies that Varuna, joining his palms, points to Nanda, who had been kept close-by in his home. Regarding the text in the second canto: nandam ca moksyati bhayad varunasya pasad, “He will save Nanda from the fear of Varuna’s noose” (2.7.31), the sense is He will free Nanda from the fear of the noose, not that He will save Nanda from the noose.

“Forgive that,” i.e. the offense of kidnapping. To dispel the idea that he is a big offender, he says: prabho, “O Almighty” (= parama-samartha). The sense is: “You can forgive this too.” Or the idea is: “You are my master, and so it is fitting that You should forgive Your servant.” Another reading is bhavan.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Your father was kidnapped by my servant who did not know (ajanata) the statement of bhakti-sastra that when the dvadasi is about to end, one can enter the water before sunrise. That explains why he is an idiot (mudhena): although he is my servant, he does not know what I stand for (akarya-vedin = mama bhrtyo ’pi mat-karyam na janati). Please forgive, because You are an ocean of forgiveness.”

### 10.28.8

*mamapy anugraham krsna kartum arhasy asesa-drk \|*  
*govinda niyatam esa pita te pitr-vatsala \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

mama—to me; api—also; anugraham—a favor; krsna—O Krsna; kartum arhasi—please do; asesa—everything; drk—You see; govinda—O Govinda; niyatam—may be led away; esah—he; pita— father; te—Your; pitr-vatsala—O You who greatly care for Your parents.

*krsna! govinda! (bhavan) asesa-drk mama api anugraham kartum arhasi. pitr-vatsala! esah te pita niyatam (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Krsna, kindly favor me too. You see everything, Govinda. O You who greatly care for Your parents, You may bring back Your father.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Varuna took Krsna to his inner apartments and showed him His father. Then he spoke the above. Varuna calls Him Govinda in reference to the abhiseka done by Indra though the latter offended Him, implying that Krsna was very merciful in accepting this from Indra. In point of pitr-vatsala: “O You who are affectionate to Your father,” with this vocative Varuna implies: “For all this time, I kept Nanda in my home with the hope of having that kind of good fortune.”

### 10.28.9

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*evam prasaditah krsno bhagavan isvaresvarah \|*  
*adayagat sva-pitaram bandhunam cavahan mudam \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah uvaca—Sri Suka said; evam—in this way; prasaditah— propitiated; krsnah—Krsna; bhagavan—the Lord; isvara-isvarah— the master of controllers; adaya—after taking; agat—went; sva- pitaram—His father; bandhiinam—of His relatives; ca—too; avahan—while evoking; mudam—the joy.

*sri-sukah uvaca—krsnah bhagavan isvaresvarah evam prasaditah sva-pitaram adaya bandhunam mudam ca avahan agat.*

**Перевод:**

**Suka said: Thus propitiated, Lord Krsna, the master of overlords, took His father and left, thereby also delighting His relatives.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Why was Krsna satisfied? The reason is: bhagavan: He knows everything, including the fact that Varuna was not at fault.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

It’s understood that He took Nanda Maharaja back home before sunrise.

### 10.28.10

*nandas tv atindriyam drstva loka-pala-mahodayam \|*  
*krsne ca sannatim tesam jnatibhyo vismito ’bravit \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

nandah—Nanda; tu—however; ati-indriyam—beyond the senses; drstva—upon seeing; loka-pala—of Varuna; maha-udayam—the great opulence; krsne—to Krsna; ca—and; sannatim—the docility; tesam—their; jhatibhyah—unto the family members; vismitah— astonished; abravit—told.

*nandah tu atindriyam loka-pala-mahodayam krsne tesam (varunadinam) sannatim ca drstva vismitah (san asthanyam upavisya) jnatibhyah abravit.*

**Перевод:**

**Nanda, however, was astonished to see both Varuna’s opulence, which he had never heard of, and their profound respect for Krsna, and so he told his family members.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Nanda had never before seen such opulence (mahodayam = aisvaryam) (atindriyam = adrsta-purvam).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

The word tu introduces a new topic. Tesam (their) refers to Varuna and to those who live in his abode. Nanda was astonished only because of his absorption in sweet human pastimes. This is turned into a philosophical conclusion here. Only love for Krsna, not the luxury, was the cause, a supereminent one. The sense is: If luxury is required, it will be shown.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

Nanda was astonished at Varuna’s great opulence, an opulence because of which his senses were very amazed (atindriyam = aticamatkaravanti indriyani yatas tam).218It’s understood that he broke his fast in this dvadasi, sat in an assembly and gave the news to his kin.

### 10.28.11

*te cautsukya-dhiyo rajan matva gopas tam isvaram \|*  
*api nah sva-gatim suksmam upadhasyad adhisvarah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

te—they; ca—and; autsukya-dhiyah—they whose thoughts \[are filled with\] eagerness; rajan—O king; matva—by thinking; gopah—the cowherds; tam—Him; isvaram—as God; api—perhaps (or a question marker219); nah—to us; sva-gatim—His own abode; suksmam— transcendental; upadhasyat—would bestow; adhisvarah—the overlord.

*rajan! te ca gopah tam isvaram matva autsukya-dhiyah (santah) “api adhisvarah nah sva-gatim suksmam upadhasyat” (iti manoratham krtavantah).*

**Перевод:**

**Filled with eagerness by thinking of Him as God, the cowherds, O king, thought: “Maybe He, the Almighty, would bestow His subtle abode upon us.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“Their minds had eagerness” (autsukya-dhiyah = autsukya-yukta dhir yesam te). The cowherds fancied this: “Will He make us reach His subtle abode, Brahman?” (api = kim) (sva-gatim = sva-sthanam) (suksmam = brahmakhyam) (upadhasyat = upadhasyad = prapayisyati iti sankalpitavantah).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Here sva-gatim only means sva- sthanam (His abode), nor Brahman, because Brahman cannot be described as suksma (subtle). Besides, given that sva-gatim has one meaning, another literal meaning, Brahman, cannot be construed out of it, because using the word sva-gatim twice would contradict the rule: sabda-buddhi-karmanam viramya vyaparabhavah, “A word, or a means of knowing, or an action has no more rhetorical function after it has been used one time” (Sahitya-darpana 2.13). Krsna’s abode is hard to fathom (suksmam = durjheyam).

Their desire to see His abode happened only because of love for Him, since even though they knew He is the Almighty their natural perception of Him as a son, nephew and so on was not compromised.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“Will He bestow the transcendental (suksmam = mayatitam) abode of His worshipers (sva-gatim = svopasakanam gatim), meaning the brahmananda and Vaikuntha, upon us or not?” (upadhasyat - upadhasyati na upadhasyati).

The cowherds said: “Dear chief of Vraja, earlier you told us, by relating the speech of Garga Muni, that Krsna is like Narayana, but now, from the prayers offered by Varuna, it seems that you conclude that He is Narayana . If so, certainly this ardent desire of us, your family members, will be fulfilled, although we are in material life. Hey cowherds, make your wish; He, Paramesvara, will fulfill it.” Some said, “We want to be liberated.” Others said, “We want to live in the transcendental world.”

However, the cowherds did not behave like Vasudeva, who said: (1) yuvam na nah sutau saksat pradhana-purusesvarau, “You two are not our sons. You are the Purusa and the Isvara of Material Nature” (10.85.18) and (2) tat te gato ’smy aranam adya padaravindam, “Therefore, O friend of the distressed, I now approach Your lotus feet for shelter” (10.85.19), nor like Arjuna, who said: sakheti matva prasabham yad uktam, “I said many disrespectful things to You while considering You my buddy” (Bhagavad-gita 11.41). Thus, Vasudeva and Arjuna experienced a slackening of their natural relationship with the Lord because of becoming affected by being aware of His godly supremacy.

### 10.28.12

*iti svanam sa bhagavan vijnayakhila-drk svayam \|*  
*sankalpa-siddhaye tesam krpayaitad acintayat \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

iti—this; svanam—of His kin; sah—He; bhagavan—the Lord; vijhaya—having understood; akhila-drk—who sees everything; svayam—automatically; sankalpa—of the resolve (desire); siddhaye—for the accomplishment; tesam—their; krpaya— mercifully; etat—this; acintayat—pondered.

*iti svanam (sankalpam) svayam vijnaya sah bhagavan akhila-drk tesam sankalpa-siddhaye krpaya etad (vaksyamanam) acintayat.*

**Перевод:**

**Automatically understanding this desire of His kin, the Lord, who sees everything, mercifully pondered as follows to fulfill their wish.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

“He, who is omniscient (akhila-drk = sarva-jnah), understood by Himself (svayam = svayam eva) this desire of them, His kin. Thereafter, to fulfill that desire of theirs, He thought as follows (etad = vaksyamanam)."

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Svanam means jhatinam (of His relatives), from the definition in Sabda-smrti: svam ajnati-dhanakhyayam.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

He understood the desire of His relatives, which was such (iti = evam-bhutam). As far as He was concerned, however (svayam = svayam tu), He saw, knew, as the omniscient Lord, everything (akhila-drk), that is, everything about the pleasure of experiencing Brahman, the pleasure of residing in Vaikuntha and the pleasure of pure love of God found in Vraja.

Although the Lord covers His opulence in the presence of His personal associates in a manner relative to their level of pure love for Him, nevertheless at that particular time, being inspired by His pastime potency, His total omniscience became manifest.

The Lord thought as follows, what will be stated in the next verse, with this intention: “Even though in comparison to even the smallest fraction of the sweet love that those cowherd men have for Me the joy of Brahman and the joy of Vaikuntha are quite insignificant, still, to fulfill the desire of the cowherds, who are being foolish in terms of being part of My human-like pastimes, I will make them realize the joy of Brahman and the joy of Vaikuntha, both of which they desire.”

### 10.28.13

*jano vai loka etasminn avidya-kama-karmabhih \|*  
*uccavacasu gatisu na veda svam gatim bhraman \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

janah—a person; vai—indeed; lake etasmin—in this world; avidya- kama-karmabhih—because of ignorance, desires and karma; ucca— high; avacasu—low; gatisu—destinations; na veda—does not know; svam—own; gatim—destination; bhraman—while wandering.

*janah vai avidya-kama-karmabhih etasmin loke uccavacasu gatisu bhraman svam gatim na veda (iti).*

**Перевод:**

**“Indeed, revolving in diverse states of existence, whether high or low, in this world because of ignorance, material desire, and karma, people do not know their destination.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Avidya, ignorance, refers to the notion of thinking of oneself as the mind-body complex. Thereafter: kama, desire. Consequently: karma (action). People, wandering in high species and low species, such as the gods and the animals respectively, do not know where they are headed.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

Krsna is about to give a boon, and so this verse cannot possibly refer to materialistic people. Therefore here the word jana (person, people) denotes the Vrajavasis. This usage is also found in this text: salokya-sarsti-samipya- sarupyaikatvam apy uta, diyamanam na grhnanti vina mat-sevanam janah, “Persons (pure devotees) do not accept any kind of liberation, whether salokya, sarsti, samipya, sarupya, or ekatva, even though it is offered, without the prospect of serving Me” (3.29.13).

Thus the sense is: “My people, wandering in their abode (bhraman = svam gatim bhraman) in terms of being manifest in the midst of gods, animals and so on (uccavacasu gatisu = deva-tiryag-adisu gatisu abhivyaktatvena), do not know their abode,” because the aspect of their awareness of His aisvarya is covered by their absorption in sweetness; this is exactly what is being said with: avidya-kama-karmabhih, “because of ignorance, not being interested in anything other than being absorbed in My pastimes; because of desire, many desires related to Me; and because of actions (karma = kriya) favorable to Me.”

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

From the context, here jana refers to a resident of Vraja such as Krsna’s father: “Because of ignorance in this world, that is, the ignorance of the nature of the soul, and, consequently, because of having a desire, and, consequently, because of doing a deed, Nanda wandered to Varuna’s abode, which is among the high destinations and low destinations, and does not know his own status.

“Now Nanda, having seen the opulence in Varuna’s kingdom, an opulence which is only Mine, thinks that Vrndavana, the very essence of the transcendental world, is less than that.”

The verse should not be explained like this: “While wandering among species of gods, animals, etc., because of ignorance, material desire and material deeds, these people, the residents of Vraja, do not know their destination: liberation, bestowed by Me, and a position in Vaikuntha.”

Nanda and other residents of Vraja cannot possibly be in material life, especially not because of ignorance, material desire and material deeds, given that they are nitya-siddhas in terms of viewing Krsna as a son, and so forth. This is a text in that regard: tasam aviratam krsne kurvatinam suteksanam, na punah kalpate rajan samsaro ’jnana-sambhavah, “In the case of those females who always thought of Krsna as their son, material life, born of ignorance, is not fitting, O king” (10.6.40).

Moreover, the explanation is not that liberation and a position in Vaikuntha will be bestowed, in consideration of Brahma’s words: esam ghosa-nivasinam uta bhavan kim deva rata, “When and what prize other than You, the entire prize, will You give to these village residents” (10.14.35). All this has been logically expounded at the end of the narration of the killing of Putana. This should be looked into.

**Комментарий. Автор Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakur:**

Sripada Jiva Gosvami Prabhu has given explanations on this verse in his Krsna-sandarbha (116) as follows:

Janah means resident of Vraja, “My kin,” and etasmin means in this material world.

Avidya-kama-karmabhir uccavacasu gatisu means among the higher species and lower species, such as those of gods and animals, which were occasioned by material activities based on material desire and ignorance.

Svam gatim bhraman means thinking that one’s destination is the same as or is not too different from the destination of the aforesaid material species.

Then he gives the meaning of the whole verse: “My own men, these cowherds, think themselves nondifferent from persons who take birth in higher species and lower species, such as those of gods and animals, within this world, such forms of life being products of material activities, which are born out of ignorance. Thus, they do not understand their own true position. Although this delusion has been arranged by My potency known as Nila220for the purpose of nourishing the sweet pastimes of Vrindavan, nevertheless in accordance with the desires of the residents of Vrindavan I will reveal to them for a few moments their extraordinary future destination, and thus dispel their delusion.” This is the purport of the verse.

### 10.28.14

*iti sancintya bhagavan maha-karuniko harih\|*  
*darsayamasa lokam svam gopanam tamasah param \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

id—(end of citation); sahcintya—after fully pondering; bhagavan— Lord; maha-karunikah—very compassionate; harih—Hari; darsayamasa—showed; lokam—the world; svam—His own; gopanam—to the cowherds; tamasah param—which is beyond Prakrti.

*iti sancintya bhagavan maha-karuniko harih svam lokam tamasah param gopanam darsayamasa.*

**Перевод:**

**Having fully pondered in this way, Lord Hari, who is very kind, showed His own abode to the cowherds. That abode is beyond material nature.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He showed Brahman (svam = brahma-svarupam) and Vaikuntha (lokam = vaikunthakhyam ca), both of which are beyond material nature (tamasah = prakrteh).

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

“He showed Goloka, which is related to the cowherds (gopanam = gopanam sambandhi)." The word tamas denotes prakrti, as in the text: tamo-mahad-aham-kha-caragni-var-bhu samvestitanda-ghata-sapta-vitasti-kayah (10.14.11).

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“He showed them Brahman and Vaikuntha” because: maha-karunikah, “He is very kind.” The sense is He thought: “I will let them know by contrast how the sweetness of Vrndavana is much better than the joy of any of those two.”

But, it may be objected, the vision of Brahman leads to the attainment of Brahman, which amounts to the type of liberation called sayujya, and thereafter it is impossible to get out of it, so how did they get back to relishing the sweetness of Vrndavana? In that regard, it is said: vibhuh (He is all-pervasive). This means He was able to take them out of impersonal liberation and out of Vaikuntha.

### 10.28.15

*satyam jnanam anantam yad brahma jyotih sanatanam \|*  
*yad dhi pasyanti munayo gunapave samahitah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

satyam—real; jhanam—awareness; anantam—infinite; yat—which; brahma—Brahman; jyotih—effulgence (self-manifest); sanatanam—eternal; yat—which; hi—the same one; pasyanti—see; munayah—the sages; guna-apaye—when there is the removal of the modes of material nature; samahitah—in trance.

*yad brahma satyam jnanam anantam jyotih sanatanam (bhavati), yad hi (brahma) munayah gunapaye (sati) samahitah (santah) pasyanti, (sah tad darsayamasa).*

**Перевод:**

**That abode is Brahman, which is real, sheer awareness, infinite, selfmanifest and eternal. The sages see it when they are in trance, after the gunas have gone away.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

Because it is impossible for those who are covered by a body and a subtle body to see, first of all He revealed to them the essence of being of Brahman, which is distinct from the material body and so forth. This is described here.

Brahman is unbounded (satyam = abadhyam), alive (jnanam = ajadam), infinite (anantam = aparicchinnam), self-manifest (jyotih = sva-prakasam), and eternally existing (sanatanam = sasvat siddham). “Out of mercy, He showed it, which the jnanis see when the modes of material nature have been eliminated.”

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

Some listeners in the assembly were regular people, and so Suka gives details to explain what transcendence is. Hi means eva (the same one). “Once in trance (samahitah = samadhi-rupah santah) when they go beyond Maya (gunapohe = maya-gunatikrame sati eva), the masters of yoga see that Brahman.”

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

What does tamasah param mean? (beyond darkness; beyond Prakrti). With this in mind, he gives a general description.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

“The sages, the jhanis, see it when they are beyond the gunas.” Because Vrndavana too is like this, in terms of having the same nature as the bliss of Brahman, it is sweeter simply due to being in the midst of the opulences of Maya, like the light of a ghee wick in the middle of darkness is sweeter than normal. Therefore He showed them the effulgence (jyotih) which was beyond darkness, rather than the light which is satya and jnana present in the midst of darkness.

Moreover, because it consists of various pastimes the Lord’s essence of being too is sweeter than the essence of being of Brahman.

### 10.28.16

*te tu brahma-hradam nita magnah krsnena coddhrtah \|*  
*dadrsur brahmano lokam yatrakruro ’dhyagat pura \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

te—they; tu—only (the same ones); brahma-hradam—to Brahma-hrada (the lake so called) (“Brahman in the form of a lake”); nitah—were brought (led); magnah—plunged; krsnena—by Krsna; ca—and; uddhrtah—taken out; dadrsuh—they saw; brahmanah— of Brahman (of transcendence); lokam—the world; yatra—where; akrurah—Akrura; adhyagat—went; pura—in the past.

*te tu brahma-hradam krsnena nitah (tasmin) magnah (santah) brahmanah lokam dadrsuh, (tasmat tena) uddhrtah ca (abhavan), yatra (hrade) pura akrurah adhyagat.*

**Перевод:**

**The cowherds were brought to Brahma-hrada by Krsna and plunged in it. They were taken out of it by Him and saw the world of transcendence. This lake is the place where Akrura once went.**

**Or: The cowherds, led to Brahma-hrada by Krsna, plunged in it and saw the world of transcendence. He then took them out of the lake, where some time ago Akrura understood.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

He brought them to the lake which is Brahman, in the sense that Brahman is like a lake because when submerged in it a person has no knowledge of anything specific.

They were brought to Brahma-hrada and plunged in it. Next Suka talks about the detail expressed by the word tu (but): Then they were taken out (uddhrtah = utthapitah) by Krsna, as though they were being taken out of samadhi. Once taken out, they saw the world of that Brahman. That world is called Vaikuntha.

“But,” it may be questioned, “it doesn’t make sense that they were immersed in Brahman and saw a world.” Anticipating this objection, he says yatra and so on: “Akrura had a vision there in the past (adhyagat = drstavan)222when Krsna was present,” that is, when He was the cause (yatra = yasmin krsne nimitte sati) (10.39.41- 45). Suka said it happened in the past insofar as it occurred prior to the conversation between himself and Pariksit. The drift is that nothing is impossible for Bhagavan, whose godly might cannot even be conjectured.

Or the sense is: “Where Akrura had a vision, the name of that lake of the Yamuna is Brahma-hrada (yatrakruro ’dhyagat = akruro yatra drstavams tasya yamuna-hradasya brahma-hrada iti nama). Once brought to that lake, they saw the world of Brahman. Afterward they were taken out by Krsna, seeing whom the cowherds became astonished.” The lack of order of the words combined with an idea which is not well-known should be tolerated.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

(Jiva Gosvami had provided the same comment)

They were brought to the lake, which is like a lake of Brahman because of plunging deep into it and so on. They plunged in it and thereby immediately reached the state of realizing it. Then they were taken out of it by Him. Going beyond the state of realization of Brahman as it is generally known, they were elevated to the state of a transcendental contemplation of a specific form revealed by the svarupa-sakti and saw, with their own eyes, the abode of Brahman, that is, the abode of the Para- Brahman who has a human form. This means they saw Vaikuntha, as mentioned in the second canto:

*tasmai sva-lokam bhagavan sabhajitah*  
*sandarsayamasa param na yat-param \|*  
*vyapeta-sanklesa-vimoha-sadhvasam*  
*sv-adrstavadbhir vibudhair abhistutam \|\|*  
*pravartate yatra rajas tamas tayoh*  
*sattvam ca misram na ca kala-vikramah \|*  
*na yatra maya kim utapare harer*  
*anuvrata yatra surasurarcitah \|\|*

**“Thus honored by Brahma, the Lord showed him His abode, the highest realm, where affliction, confusion and fear do not exist and which was glorified by liberated souls who had superb spiritual merit. There, neither tamas, rajas, or sattva mixed with those two exists, nor does the course of time take place. Maya does not exist there, much less her offshoots. Hari’s followers in that realm are revered by gods and by asuras.” (2.9.9-10)**

This is in Jitanta-stotra in Narmada-pancratia:

*lokam vaikuntha-namanam divyam sad-guna-samyutam \|*  
*avaisnavanam aprapyam guna-traya-vivarjitam \|\|*

**“The realm called Vaikuntha is divine, is endowed with the six qualities, cannot be reached by nondevotees, and is devoid of the three modes of material nature.”**

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

They were brought to Brahma-hrada, a lake which is like a lake of Brahman, because someone immersed in it has no awareness of anything specific. Once brought there, the Vrajavasis plunged in it and were taken out of it by Krsna; by His inconceivable power, they were even taken out of impersonal liberation, that is, they were pulled out of it. In that condition, they saw Vaikuntha, the world of that same Brahman, because of the text in the second canto: lokam vikuntham upanesyati gokulam sma, “Krsna will take the cowherd community to the Vikuntha world” (2.7.31).

Regarding uddhrtah (taken out of), the implied analogy is this: As other people, when lifted from the lake of material life, realize Brahman, the Absolute Truth, so the cowherds endowed with pure love, when lifted from the lake of Brahman, saw Vaikuntha-loka. In other words, Vaikuntha affords more joy than the calamity of merging in Brahman.

This philosophical conclusion is subtly revealed in the verse: Although the experience of joy, which involves pure love, in Vaikuntha is superior to the realization of the bliss of Brahman, which is void of love, the experience of the love-filled joy in the cowherd community is the best of all.

The last clause means: “... in which place, Vaikuntha, Akrura went” (adhyagat = gatavan). Or “where Akrura saw his cherished Deity.”

### 10.28.17

*nandadayas tu tam drstva paramananda-nirvrtah\|*  
*krsnam ca tatra cchandobhih stuyamanam suvismitah \|\|*

**Пословный перевод:**

nanda-adayah—of whom Nanda is foremost; tu—but; tam—that; drstva—seeing; parama-ananda—due to the topmost bliss; nirvrtah— happy; krsnam—Krsna; ca—and; tatra—there; chandobhih—with Vedic hymns; stuyamanam—being praised; su-vismitah—veru amazed.

*nandadayah tu (gopah) tam (lokam) drstva paramananda-nirvrtah (babhuvuh. te) krsnam ca tatra chandobhih stuyamanam (drstva) suvismitah (abhavan).*

**Перевод:**

**Nanda and the other cowherds became joyful with the topmost bliss when they saw that realm, and by beholding Krsna being praised there with Vedic hymns they were flabbergasted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

They saw either Vaikuntha or Goloka. The cowherds were completely filled with the highest bliss (paramananda- nirvrtah = paramanandena nihsesena vyaptah babhuvuh), because of gazing at His special place which they were eager to see. Or they became overjoyed by seeing that Goloka is very much the same as Gokula, which is on Earth.

Beholding Krsna praised by Vedic hymns, the cowherds very very amazed. Or the sense is their special smiles were splendid (su-vismitah = susobhanam visesatah smitam yesam tatha-bhutah babhuvuh).

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

Just like the cowherds’ vision was more special than Akrura’s, their bliss was higher than his. The word tam denotes Sri Krsna’s abode, which is directly related to them. Hence, naturally they became paramananda-nirvrta (joyful with the topmost bliss). They also became astonished, because they saw that Krsna had not given up His mindset of being Nanda’s son. He was praised by Vedic hymns, or by means of Vedic hymns, or else both by those hymns and by means of those hymns, such as Gopala-tapani.

The realm that they saw was the topmost Goloka, which is different from other Vaikunthas. In this regard, the word sva in sva-gatim (verse 11) means Sri Krsna’s. Moreover Sukadeva said: lokam svam gopanam (verse 14), where the genitive case in gopanam is clearly indicative of a direct connection with the cowherds. Moreover here Krsna is mentioned by this very name. It is thus proven that the realm was Goloka.

Brahma said: ahny aprtam nisi sayanam atisramena, lokam vikuntham upanesyati gokulam sma, “Krsna will take the cowherds, who are busy in daytime and who sleep at night because of fatigue, to the Vikuntha world” (2.7.31). The sense of this citation is as follows. The term Brahma-hrada in the current verse denotes two things: the actual place, called Akrura-tirtha, and the realization of Brahman. Regarding the first one, the sense is: In daytime the cowherds will be busy serving Him, as described in texts such as: esam ghosa-nivasinam (10.14.35), and at night they will sleep; their sleep is a form of samadhi on that. In the second alternative, the sense is: In daytime the cowherds will be busy looking for Nanda, detained in the realm of Varuna, and at night they will sleep because of fatigue; in their sleep, Krsna will show them, the residents of the cowherd village (gokulam = gokula-vasi-janam), Goloka in a close way (lokam vikuntham = lokam golokakhyam) (upanesyati = darsayisyati) (upa = samipe). Goloka is described in many texts. For example:

*svargad urdhvam brahma-loko brahmarsi-gatia-sevitah \|*  
*tatra soma-gads caiva jyotisam ca mahatmanam \|\|*  
*tasyopari gavam lokah sadhyas tam palayanti hi \|*  
*sa hi sarva-gatah krsna mahakasa-gato mahan \|\|*  
*upary upari tatrapi gatis tava tapomayi \|*  
*yam na vidmo vayam sarve prcchanto ’pi pitamaham \|*

**“Above the heavenly planets is Vaikuntha, served by the Brahma Rsis. It is the goal of Siva and of the greats who are enlightened souls. Above it is the planet of cows, which perfect beings protect. Krsna, it is all-pervasive and majestic. Above everything is Your abode consisting of tapas: We do not understand this abode, even though we inquired about it from the Grandfather, Brahma.” (Hari-vamsa 2.19.29-31)**

In this quotation, “Svarga” denotes all the planets above and including Svarga. “Brahmaloka” (transctndental world) Vaikuntha; for example, Sridhara Svami explains brahmalokah in Bhagavatam 2.5.38 as vaikunthakhyah (the realm known as Vaikuntha). And “Soma” is Siva, who is with Uma (soma = sa-uma = uma-sahita). “Tapomayi” means anavacchinaisvarya-mayi (the realm has unlimited opulence).

Krsna eternally has fun with His entourage in Goloka, which is a special manifestation of Vrndavana. Goloka is not manifest in Prakrti. Sometimes He, accompanied by the same entourage, becomes visible in that special manifestation which is manifest in Prakrti. The general rule that He always has associates is seen in scriptures on upasana (meditational worship), etc. At that time, His associates appear in many forms, given that there are many universes; to enhance the pleasure of the pastimes (lila-rasa), the lila-sakti, like it did to Vasudeva and others on the occasion of the sixteen thousand weddings, gives each of those same forms a separate identity and ensures that they don’t know that their own character also exists elsewhere.

Thus, it is proven here that Krsna showed them Goloka, a special manifestation of the same Vrndavana. Because of the nondifference of the two manifestations even though they were different, He did not show the cowherds their doubles there nor did He show them the doubles of other associates in His entourage. The Vedic hymns mentioned here are extrinsic, on account of being similar to traveling bards. This showing of Him being praised by Vedic hymns was only for the purpose of proof.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

"Beholding it, the realm called Vaikuntha, they became overjoyed with the highest bliss," because they saw that the Vrndavana situated in the spiritual Goloka had the same attributes as those of Vrndavana. They became extremely joyful, like a millionaire who loses all his wealth and then by chance sees a sign that his wealth has been recovered.

Then they looked for Krsna. When they saw Him being praised there by the personified Vedic hymns, they became utterly astonished: “Where have we arrived? These praisers are forms of light. We have never seen anything like them in Vrndavana. Who are they? We cannot even ask them anything. Krsna is in their midst. Although He sees us, His father and other relatives, He is not acting out His childish swagger. He does not put His arms around our necks. We are too shy to approach Him, let alone hug Him. We are not thirsty and feel no hunger. How strange! How is it that His mother, unable to feed Him, is willing to keep on living?”

They were astonished in such ways. This sentence should be added to the text: “They were sent back to Vrndavana by Yogamaya who was sent by the lila-sakti."

The gist of this section was rendered in verse by the venerable Sri Rupa Gosvami in his Stava-mala:

*loko ramyah ko ’pi vrndatavito*  
*nasti kvapity anjasa bandhu-vargam \|*  
*vaikuntham yah susthu sandarsya bhuyo*  
*gostham ninye patu sa tvam mukundah \|\|*

**“No realm is as lovely as the forest of Vrindavan. Having nicely showed the transcendental world to His relatives, Mukunda brought them back to the cowherd village. May He protect you.” (Astadasa-cchanda-stava 29)**

## Introduction (29-33)

This set of five chapters from the tenth canto of Bhagavata Purana is called the Pancadhyayi. It is an epic poem celebrated as the most romantic text of Sanskrit literature. The Pancadhyayi illustrates the apex of Love of God in the two aspects of srngara-rasa (romantic love): separation and meeting. In short, this sublime text showcases the Sanskrit language in its finest form and hints at the nature of real love.

Sanskrit is the language of a culture that teaches how to be rasika. The Pancadhyayi is the cream of Sanskrit literature because it occasions the direct realization of Rasa in literature (aesthetic delight) and because it sheds light on the path of Rasa (mojo, magical vibe). The commentators selected here are skilled in frothing up the meanings and in bringing out the sweetness. In life, practicing bhakti is not always possible, whereas Rasa is already happening everywhere: It is a question of raising the standards. Sanskrit culture provides a framework for that, by classing the modes of existence in four categories: tamasika (ignorance and lethargy), rajasika (the mode of action / passion), sattvika (peacefulness and goodness), and paramarthika (mode of transcendence).

In that regard, relations between human beings take place either from the outlook of the ego or from the perspective of the soul. The nature of the soul is Rasa in the highest sense (bliss mixed with astonishment). The consciousness of the ego comprises the first three modes and is infused by the consciousness of the soul.Therefore, Rasa is reflected to some degree on the screen of the mind and thus becomes degraded in nature, until we desire to experience Rasa in its pure form. Raising the standards of Rasa in day-to-day life means increasing the level of appropriateness, because Rasa depends on it, says Ananda-vardhana: anaucityad rte nanyad rasa-bhangasya karanam (Dhvany-aloka 3.14 Vrtti). Reading first-class poetry is one of the best methods to realize the true nature of the soul. And the highest level of Rasa is bhakti-rasa, because God is Rasa: raso vai sah (Taittiriya Upanisad 2.7).

In Sanskrit texts prior to the Bhagavatam, the Play of the Rasa is briefly described in Hari-vamsa (2.20.18-35) and in Visnu Purana (5.13.14-62). In the Pancadhyayi, the Rasa dance is depicted in the fifth chapter (10.33). The first four chapters are the buildup to it. Thus, the Pancadhyayi contains both the apex of the vipralambha aspect (separation) of srngara-rasa and the climax of its other aspect, sambhoga (meeting). Not only that, the vipralambha and the sambhoga are eminently described in alternate sequence.

In the heart of the five chapters of the Pancadhyayi is Gopi- gitam (the gopis’ song), the nineteen verses sung by the cowherd girls of Vrindavan who felt the pang of separation from Krsna. Most scholars opine that this chapter (10.31) is the sweetest chapter of the Bhagavatam, by even exceeding Venu-gitam (10.21) because of embellishments in terms of alliteration, meter, and double if not triple or quadruple meanings. The gopis’ mood in Venu-gitam (the song of the flute) was purva-raga (love before ever meeting the lover), whereas in Gopi-gitam the mood is pravasa-vipralambha (separation after meeting). In the Pancadhyayi too, Krsna played the flute to attract the gopis. In that way, He lived up to His name: The verbal root krs means ‘to attract’.

In addition, the Bhagavatam cleverly glorifies Sri Radha with these words, without ever naming Her: anayaradhito nunam bhagavan harih, “For sure, Lord Hari was worshipped (aradhitah) by Her” (10.30.28), whereas the Visnu Purana expresses the same literal meaning, but without an implied sense: visnur abhyarcitas taya (5.13.35).

Sanskrit commentators use the term Rasa-lila (the entertainment called Rasa), but in the Bhagavatam, the words in this regard are rasa-krida (the Play of the Rasa) and rasotsava (the Rasa festival) (10.33.2-3).

Visvanatha Cakravarti derives the word rasa as follows: nrtya-gita-cumbanadinam rasanam samuho rasah, “The term rasa signifies a multitude of rasas such as dancing, singing, kissing, and embracing” (Sarartha-darsini 10.33.2). Usually the term rasa denotes the well- known rasas of poetry, such as srngara-rasa, but Visvanatha Kaviraja says that by the derivation rasyate iti rasah (what is relished is called rasa), a vyabhicari-bhava too, or an anubhava, etc., can be called rasa (aesthetic delight) if it is relished: rasyate iti rasa iti vyutpatti-yogad bhava-tad-abhasadayo ’pi grhyante (Sahitya-darpana 1.3). Kissing, dancing, and so on are anubhavas of srngara-rasa. Thus the Rasa is a multitude of rasas in that sense. Still, transient emotions (vyabhicari-bhavas) also occur.

The word rasa is found neither in Hari-vamsa nor in Visnu Purana. Often times the word hallisaka is used as a synonym of the Rasa dance. Bhakti-siddhanta Sarasvati wrote:

In the book named Sangita-sara it is stated: “When a male dancer performs, being surrounded by a circle of many women dancers moving about, it is called a hallisaka. When a hallisaka dance is accompanied by various refined talas (tunes), dance steps, and gestures, it is called a rasa dance.”

In usage, the terms hallisaka, hallisaka and hallisaka are synonymous. The suffix ka was added after the original word without changing the meaning. The definition is: strinam hallisam saha-nartanam, “The hallisa is a dance with women” (Trikanda-sesa 1.7.2). Thus, Rupa Gosvami (Astadasa-cchandah-stava 32, Govinda-virudavali 32, Hamsa-duta 18, etc.), Kavi Karnapura (Ananda-vrndavana-campu) and Krsnadasa Kaviraja (Govinda-lilamrta 12.77; 22.59) used the term hallisaka to denote the Rasa dance. Krsnadasa Kaviraja used the terms hallisaka (Govinda-lilamrta 22.6) and hallisa (Govinda- lilamrta 12.87).

Visvanatha Kaviraja includes the hallisa in his dramaturgic theory as one of the eighteen forms of small drama.He defines it as a theatrical performance in one act where one male is accompanied by seven, eight or ten female dancers.

The Hari-vamsa mentions the term hallisaka (2.89.68), but in that context it is used as the name of a musical style.Most likely, the usage of the term evolved to signify the aforesaid dance style. Perhaps the term hallisaka is derived from the word jhalli, a type of drum.

Not all the commentaries included in the previous volumes of this series are found here. First of all, as usual I translated in full the commentaries of Sridhara Svami (Bhavartha-dipika), Visvanatha Cakravarti (Sarartha-darsini), Sanatana Gosvami (Brhad-vaisnava- tosani), and Jiva Gosvami (Laghu-vaisnava-tosani). For the most part, Sridhara Svami gives glosses, and his elucidations are concise. Visvanatha Cakravarti’s commentary is so called because it shows the essential meanings, especially those in the other commentaries; it is outstanding. Sanatana Gosvami likes to brainstorm ideas, so much so that sometimes his explanations contradict one another. At his request, Jiva Gosvami edited his commentary, originally called Vaisnava-tosani, and thus composed his own commentary, Laghu-vaisnava-tosani. But quite often he left out good elements of Sanatana Gosvami’s commentary. Those elements are rendered here. As regards the tenth canto, Jiva Gosvami’s other commentary, Krama-sandarbha, is extremely brief. On occasion, the comments that he made in Sat-sandarbha, especially in Krsna-sandarbha and in Priti-sandarbha, about a verse of Pancadhyayi are shown. The Brhat-krama-sandarbha is a commentary by an unknown Vaisnava pandit.

Moreover, I translated excerpts of Baladeva Vidyabhusana’s commentary, called Vaisnavanandini. For the most part, Baladeva Vidyabhusana paraphrased Visvanatha Cakravarti and Jiva Gosvami. In addition, I related Ganga Sahaya’s comments about grammatical irregularities in the text of Bhagavatam. His commentary, called Anvitartha-prakasika, and the other commentaries are the source references for the syntactical connection of the words below each verse: The words of the verse are placed in proper order in prose and the missing words are added in parentheses to complete the sentences. The translation of a verse follows the syntactical connection (prose order).

Srinatha Pandita’s commentary, Caitanya-mata-manjusa, is also shown. Some scholars call him Srinatha Cakravarti. Based on Visvanatha Cakravarti’s commentary on text 10.29.9, it seems that Visvanatha Cakravarti took inspiration from Srinatha’s commentary. More details are provided in the footnote there. Another possible proof of this is in Visvanatha Cakravarti’s commentary on verse 10.30.14, where his idea about Yogamaya is taken from Caitanya- mata-manjusa 10.30.15.

I included Vallabhacarya’s commentary on Gopi-gitam and so on. The abovementioned commentaries on the previous chapters were translated in the previous volumes. For the details about the commentators, consult my introduction in the first volume of this series.

Narayana Bhatta’s commentary, Rasikahladini, is translated here on special occasions. He was born in 1532 CE (samvat 1588) in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, but came to live in Vraja in 1546. On the recommendation of Sanatana Gosvami and Rupa Gosvami,he was initiated by Krishna Das Brahmachari, who was a disciple of Gadadhar Pandit and was serving at the Madan Mohan temple in Vrindavan. Narayana Bhatta lived in Radha Kund up to at least 1552 CE, and then moved to Unchagaon (Uccagrama, near Varsana, Vraja) for the rest of his life.

Narayana Bhatta discovered all the tirthas and the lila-sthalis of Vraja mentioned in the Varaha Purana which were not yet found. He would call the villagers and ask them to excavate those places. He discovered the various locations connected with Sri Krsna’s Rasa-lila and mentioned them in his Vraja-bhakti-vilasa. He constructed Rasa-mandalas in those places, revamped the old ponds, rebuilt the temples and installed deities therein. He was able to do all this with the financial help of Raja Todaramala, the treasurer of Emperor Akbar. Narayana Bhatta determined the boundary of Vraja. He also started the practice of Vraja-mandala-parikrama (circumambulating the twelve forests of Vraja). He gave every lake, pond, village and grove in the circuit of Vraja a distinct name. In Braj, Narayana Bhatta also had great influence in establishing the tradition of the theatrical representation of Rasa-lila.

In addition to Rasikahladini, Narayana Bhatta wrote many works. Of those, Vraja-bhakti-vilasa and Vraja-pradipika are the most exhaustive early descriptions of the Braja Dham parikrama. His Bhakti-rasa-tarangini is mentioned with high regard by Visvanatha Cakravarti in his commentary on Ujjvala-nilamani in order to disprove Jiva Gosvami’s opinion that Krsna and the gopis have a relationship of svakiya-bhava (matrimony), not of parakiya-bhava (paramourship).In Vraja-bhakti-vilasa, Narayana Bhatta mentions Brhat-vraja-gunotsava, a huge work of twenty- six thousand verses composed by him. He says that just as Vraja-bhakti-vilasa describes the different forests of Vraja with their presiding deities and their tirthas, so this work describes the different villages, their presiding deities, the tirthas and the corresponding pastimes of Krsna’s. That book has not been found.

The edition of Rasikahladini consulted for this translation was published in the 1950s by Krishna Das, a resident of Kusuma- sarovara (Govardhana, U.P.). The editor is Prabhu Dayal Mittal, a very highly reputed scholar of the Radha-vallabha Sampradaya. Another edition consulted is the text published by Krsna-Sankara Sastri among other commentaries (Srimad-Bhagavatam aneka- vyakhya-samalankrtam). Narayana Bhatta took elements from Sanatana Gosvami and sometimes from Vallabhacarya and from Jiva Gosvami. For the most part, Narayana Bhatta quoted Rasarnava- sudhakara instead of Ujjvala-nilamani. Narayana Bhatta is, of course, different from Bhatta Narayana, the author of the famous play Veni-samhara (c. 700 CE).

Further, Sanatana Gosvami took most of Vallabhacarya’s excellent explanations (ref. 10.29.8; 10.29.12, 10.29.19, etc.). Sometimes those ideas are also seen in Jiva Gosvami’s commentary.

Here the text of Bhagavatam is sourced in Sridhara Svami’s edition, which includes his commentary. The variant readings in the Bhaktivedanta Book Trust (BBT) edition are shown in the footnotes, but not the abundant typographical mistakes in that edition. I also showed the variant readings in Vallabhacarya’s edition, which accompanies his commentary.

Sanatana Gosvami, Jiva Gosvami and Visvanatha Cakravarti used a version of the text of Bhagavatam which is no longer available. In verse 10.29.45, for instance, their reading kamalamoda instead of kumudamoda cannot be sourced in the abovementioned editions, nor in Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati’s Gaudiya Matha edition, which is the source of the BBT edition (barring the typos), nor in Krsna- Sankara Sastri’s edition of Bhagavatam, which includes the readings followed by Vijayadhvaja Tirtha in Madhvacarya’s edition, and so on, nor in Rama-Narayana’s edition.

The Pancadhyayi eminently sheds light on the quality of being rasika. To let the readers better understand the double meanings and so on, in the translation of the commentaries I took the extra step to show the commentators’ glosses. A gloss is a synonym of a word in the root text. In the translation, when words are in parentheses with an equal sign (=) in the middle, the word on the left side of the equal sign is the word in the text of Bhagavatam and the word on the right side is the commentator’s gloss. Words between em dashes (—) are part of the text: They are not my addition. Moreover, if the meter of a verse is not anustup, I write the name of the meter just below the verse, unless the meter is the same as the one used in the previous verse.

The numbers of the verses here are the numbers used in every major edition of Bhagavatam except the BBT edition. In other words, the numbers here are the same as those in the BBT edition, except in chapter 30, starting from verse 10.30.31, where the BBT counts two verses as one (10.30.30) and in chapter 33, where the BBT version again follows the Gaudiya Matha edition, which combines verses 3 and 4 in almost every other edition to make a verse number 3. Still, the text in all the editions is the same. The text of Bhagavatam in the Gaudiya Matha edition is taken from Rama-Narayana’s edition; Rama-Narayana grouped verses at his own discretion, throughout the Bhagavatam, and numbered them as he wished.

Further, the late Gopi-parana-dhana Prabhu, the former director of the BBT and director of the first Sanskrit school from which I graduated, in Govardhana, translated the tenth canto (starting from chapter fourteen), eleventh canto and twelfth canto for the BBT and wrote the purports for the BBT based on the acaryas’ commentaries.

Gopi Prabhu taught me how to translate properly and encouraged me in my task of translating the commentaries on the Bhagavatam. He was a pioneer, and I offer my profound respects to him.

My heartfelt thanks also go to Gopala Bhatta Dasa, the American businessman who covered all the costs related to Gopi Prabhu’s Sanskrit school for the ten years of its existence (2005- 2014) and who thus provided free tuition to every student. God bless.

Gaurapada Dasa,  
M.A. Vrindavan, India  
Autumn 2016

## Chapter 29 - The fore play of the Rasa

### 10.29.1

*sri-suka uvaca*  
*bhagavan api ta ratrih saradotphulla-mallikah* ***\[12\]****I*  
*viksya rantum manas cakre yoga-mayam upasritah II*

**Пословный перевод:**

sri-sukah—the venerable Suka; uvaca—said; bhagavan—the Lord; api—also (or although); tah—those; ratrih—nights; sarada— because of autumn: utphulla—in bloom; mallikah—jasmine flowers; viksya—upon seeing; rantum—to enjoy amorous pleasure; manah cakre—He made up His mind; yogamayam—Yogamaya (the transcendental energy); upasritah—relying on.

*sri-sulcah uvaca—(sah) bhagavan api tah ratrih sarada utphulla- mallikah viksya yoga-may dm upasritah (san) rantum manah cakre.*

**Перевод:**

**Sri Suka said: Seeing those nights, during which the jasmines were in bloom because of autumn, Krsna, relying on Yogamaya, made up His mind to enjoy amorous pleasure even though He is God.**

**Комментарий. Автор Sridhara Swami:**

*unatrmise tu rasartham ukti-pratyuktayo hareh \|*  
*gopibhi rasa-samrambhe tasya cantardhi-kautukam \|\|*  
*brahmadi-jaya-samrudha-darpa-kandarpa-darpa-ha \|*  
*jayati sri-patir gopi-rasa-mandala-mandanah \|\|*

**In the twenty-ninth chapter, Hari’s arguments in the scope of Rasa and the gopis’ counter-arguments are described, and His jovial act of disappearing, given that the gopis felt too proud of themselves at the outset of the Rasa, is depicted.**  
**Laksmi’s husband who has become the gopis’ ornament in the circle of the Rasa dance is super eminent. He thus defeats the vanity of Cupid, whose pride was accentuated by his victories over Brahma, Siva and others.**

Regarding the verse, someone might argue: “This is the opposite of what is expected because it looks like He is the vanquisher of Cupid by having fun with the wives of other men.” That is wrong because many scriptural texts state that He is completely independent from an ontological perspective: yoga-mayam upasritah, “relying on Yogamaya” (10.29.1), atmaramo ’py ariramat, “Although He revels in Himself, He gave them amorous pleasure” (10.29.42), saksan manmatha-manmathah, “He is exactly the Cupid of Cupids” (10.32.2), atmany avaruddha-sauratah, “He whose amorous feelings are confined to Himself” (10.33.26), and so on.

Therefore the truth of the matter is that this false appearance (since He looks human although He is God) of taking pleasure in a Rasa dance is meant to signify the victory over Cupid. And moreover, under the pretext of describing topics of love, the Pancadhyayi (‘set of five chapters’)is specifically meant to foster renunciation. We shall make this clear later on.

The words “those nights” refer to the nights he promised to enjoy with the gopis, in the text: yatabala vrajam siddha mayema ramsyatha ksapah, “Girls, return to the village. You are successful. You will enjoy these nights with Me.” (10.22.27)

**Комментарий. Автор Vallabhacarya:**

*brahmanandat samuddhrtya bhajanananda-yojane \|*  
*lila ya yujyate samyak sa turye vinirupyate \|\|*  
*laukika-strisu sarhsiddhis tad-dvara puruse bhavet \|*  
*svanandanubhavartharh hi yogyatapi nirupita \|\|*  
*tato hi bhajananandah strisu samyag vidharyate \|*  
*tad-dvara purusanam ca bhavisyati na canyatha \|\|*  
*striya eva hi tam patum saktas tasu tatah puman \|*  
*ato hi bhagavan krsnah strisu reme hy ahar-nisam \|\|*

**In keeping with the theme of indicating what is superior to the bliss of Brahman (in the previous chapter, Krsna immersed the gopas in Brahma-hrada, took them out of it and showed them the spiritual world), to establish a connection with bhajanananda (the bliss of spiritual practice) the pastime which is most fit in this matter is expounded in the fourth section.**

**The acme of bhajanananda (Rasa in the form of Love of God) took place in ordinary women. By means of their example, a man can achieve the full-fledged perfection of bhajanananda. The suitability for realizing this bliss of the soul is also described.**

**In its highest form, the bliss of spiritual practice is the lot of women. By means of their example, the same can happen to men. It is not the other way round.**

**Only women are able to taste that bhajanananda. After that, the Purusa can taste it in them. Hence Lord Krsna enjoyed being with those women day and night.**

Someone might think, “It is said here that the Lord made up His mind to enjoy amorous pleasure. This means He fell from His position.” Suspecting this, he says: yoga-mayam upasritah. Yogamaya establishes an already established situation elsewhere, as in the case of Sankarsana.

**Комментарий. Автор Srinatha Pandita:**

Yogamaya is the potency that is very clever in making the impossible possible. All this was the work of Yogamaya, as pointed out in the text: karyarthe sambhavisyati (10.1.25). When the gopis will set out to meet Krsna, Yogamaya will put them out of the range of their husbands and others. Upon their return, she will keep their husbands bewildered, as shown in the text: manyamanah sva-parsva-sthan svan svan daran vrajaukasah, “Bewildered by His power of illusion, they thought that their respective wives were at their sides” (10.33.38). During the Rasa dance, she will bring about attires, ornaments and other things suitable for that. When the gopis, in separation from Krsna, will feel one with Him (10.30.15), she will assume the role of Putana and others who are adverse to Him. The rest may be inferred in like manner.

The sense of the plural in ratrih is this: The Rasa-lila required many nights. When the Lord willed that many nights should come together to form one long night, right then He saw many nights nearby in embodied form with folded hands.

**Комментарий. Автор Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura:**

*sri-rama-krsna-ganga-caranan natva gurun uru-premnah \|*  
*srila-narottama-natha-sri-gauranga-prabhum naumi \|\|*  
*pranamya sri-gururh bhuyah sri-krsnam karunarnavam \|*  
*lokanatham jagac-caksuh sri-sukam tarn upasraye \|\|*  
*gopa-rama-jana-prana-preyase ’tiprabhusnave \|*  
*tadiya-priya-dasyaya mam madiyam aham dade \|\|*  
*atha pancabhir adhyayaih panca-prana-samair munih \|*  
*rasam praha hareh sarva-lila-sampac-chiromanim \|\|*  
*raso jayati yad datta-saubhagya gopa-yositah \|*  
*dhara-stha adhari-cakruh sarvordhva-stham ramam api \|\|*  
*unatrimse venu-nada-parusya-visa-varsanam \|*  
*gopika-catakisv abhih kridantardhis ca varnyate \|\|*  
*unatrimse venu-nada-parusya-visa-varsanam \|*  
*gopika-catakisv abhih kridantardhis ca varnyate \|\|*

**From my heart filled with love, I first offer my respects to the feet of Srirama (Radha-ramana Cakravarti), of Sri Krsna (Krsna-carana Cakravarti), and of Sri Ganga (Ganga-Narayana Cakravarti) and then bow to Srila Narottama, Srila Lokanatha, and Sri Gauranga Prabhu.**

**Upon again bowing to Sri Guru, I seek the shelter of Sri Krsna, who is an ocean of mercy and the master of the universe, and rely upon Sri Suka, the eye for the world.**

**I offer myself and everything I possess to the Almighty who is dearest to the life force of the young cowherd women, with the hope of serving Him.**

**Now, in five chapters which are equal to the five life airs, the sage narrates the Rasa: This pastime is the prize jewel in the treasury of all His pastimes.**

**The Rasa is glorious because the cowherd women, who acquired good fortune and who lived on Earth, diminished Laksmi’s status of being the highest.**

**In the twenty-ninth chapter, the raining of the harsh poison of the sound of Krsna’s flute on the cataki birds that were the gopis, His games with these girls and His disappearance are described.**

At seven years of age, on the new moon (amavasya) in the month of Kartika (October-November) the Lord stopped a sacrifice to Indra by proposing the philosophy of Karma-vada. On the first day (pratipad) of the bright fortnight of that month (i.e. the next day), the festival of the sacrifice to Govardhana occurred. On the second day, the festival of having lunch on bhratr-dvitiya (sisters traditionally show honor to their brothers)on the shore of the Yamuna took place; It is understood that it happened even though Sukadeva did not mention it. On the same day, Indra spoke in anger; this was described. Then, from the third day to the ninth, the Lord held up Govardhana Hill. On the tenth day, the cowherd men expressed their wonderment. On the eleventh, Govinda was given an ablution (abhiseka). On the twelfth He traveled to Varuna’s planet. And on the full-moon day (purnima), He went to Brahmaloka (the transcendental world).

After that, in the same year, when He was eight years of age,the Rasa festival, the crest jewel of all the festivals which are His pastimes, occurred on the full-moon night of the month of Asvina (September-October). He was one year older because it was the end of autumn (His birthday is in Bhadra, August-September).

Now Sukadeva begins to describe the Rasa festival: Although He is the Lord, meaning although He has the six kinds of opulence to the fullest extent, He made up His mind to enjoy amorous pleasure—because He was attracted by the utmost sweetness of a night of autumn, of Vrindavan and of the young women of Vraja. These three represent the time, the place, and the persons and are the stimuli (uddipana) and the subjects or objects (alambana) of amorous pleasure.

Under the sway of love, He not only became desirous of taking with His own senses the manifold, utter exquisiteness of billions of sexy women who are the wish-fulfilling gems of ujjvala- rasa (srngara-rasa) (romance), an exquisiteness which consists of their beauty, youthfulness, fragrance, sweetness, wittiness, refined sounds, and skill in the performing arts (singing, dancing, and playing instruments), He also wanted those women to take with their senses His own beauty and so on. The moment He so desired all this to occur uninterruptedly in only one night, then Yogamaya, which is the potency that is very clever in making the impossible possible, was impelled by His potency called Satya-sankalpata (it fulfils desires). Yogamaya brought billions of nights that could facilitate such enjoyments, compressed them into that single night of twelve hours and thus put on a show. And therefore the plural is used: ta ratrih (those nights). In that line of thought, it is said ahead: brahma- ratra upavrtte, “when a night of Brahma had passed” (10.33.39). The word tah (those), from the pronominal base tat, is used in the sense of prasiddha (the famous ones): In connection with ratrih (nights), the idea is that the nights had many qualities. In other words, the nights were eminent.

In the reading saradotphulla-mallikah, the word ends in the suffix \[t\]a\[p\].The sense is “The nights, in which the jasmines were blooming even though it was autumn” (saradotphulla-mallikah = saradayam api utphulla mallika yasu tah). The term mallika means kunda (jasmine): They were in bloom even in autumn, as per the text: kunda-srajah kula-pater iha vati gandhah (10.30.11). And even daytime lotuses were in bloom at night, so says the text: reme tat-taralanandi kamalamoda-vayuna (10.29.45).Such was the eminence of Vrindavan.

In the reading saradotphulla-mallikah, the compound is analyzed as: saradyas ca ta utphulla-mallikas ca, “They are autumnal flowers and are open jasmines.” (Thus this reading makes no sense.)

He began to enjoy those. Had the verb reme (he took amorous pleasure) been used, someone could have argued that the Lord is only pretending to be a man, and that He, who revels in Himself (atmarama) and whose desires are automatically fulfilled, is externally, not really, taking pleasure in the company of the women of Vraja. To refute this, it is said here: rantum manas cakre, “He made up His mind to enjoy amorous pleasure.” This suggests that the amorous enjoyment does indeed relate to the heart. It is not external (ungenuine). Then someone might argue, “All right, the amorous enjoyment relates to the heart, but since the beautiful girls of Vraja are devotees of the Lord, He takes pleasure in being with them only in conformity with that.” To repudiate this, the atmanepada is used in the verb cakre (he made), which implies that the purpose of the amorous enjoyment was the doer’s own happiness.

In addition, the damsels of Vraja had so much love that the Lord, though He is automatically replete with all types of happiness, made up His mind to enjoy their company. The same general idea is expressed by the words itthambhuta-guno harih in the verse that begins atmaramas ca munayah.Thus, there was a supereminence of the damsels too. For example:

*so ’pi kaisoraka-vayo manayan madhusudanah \|*  
*reme tabhir ameyatma ksapasu ksapitahitah \|\|*

**“Though He is Madhusudana, the inconceivable Soul, whose enemies become ruined, He, thinking highly of the age of youth, enjoyed being with those women during the nights.” (Visnu Purana 5.13.60)**

*yuvatir gopa-kanyas ca ratrau sankalya kala-vit \|*  
*kaisorakam manayanahsaha tabhir mumoda ha \|\|*

**“Thinking highly of His fresh youth, He who knows when it’s time invited both the young women and the virgin girls and took pleasure in being with them.” (Hari-vamsa 2.20.18)**

The word manayan in these two citations from Visnu Purana and Hari-vamsa means adrtam kurvan (while making honorable). Had there been no play between Krsna and those women, His age of kaisora (adolescence) would have been disrespected. For this reason, a highly experienced connoisseur has stated: kaisoram saphali-karoti kalayan kunje viharam harih, “While having fun in the pleasure grove, Flari renders His adolescence successful” (Bhakti-rasamrta-sindhu 2.1.231). Thus in every way the eminence of the damsels too is implied.

On top of that, everything contradictory is reconciled and everything left unsaid is made explicit, by the word yogamayam. “He relied upon her to a high degree” (upasritah = upa asritah = adhikyena asritah). Yogamaya is a function of His inconceivable transcendental potency. The fact that He relied on her out of all the potencies that lie at His disposal shows that in this pastime she too is very fortunate.

**Комментарий. Автор Sanātana Gosvāmī:**

*namah krsnaya rasa-rasikaya*

**“I offer my respects to Krsna, the witty enjoyer of the Rasa.”**

Badarayani, who has splendor, spoke (sri-badarayanir uvaca = sri- yukta-badarayanir uvaca). In this regard, the venerable Sri Vyasa is called Badarayana because he performed great austerities in Badarikasrama. His son, Badarayani, is the form of the result of his austerities. This implies that Sukadeva knows everything, is filled with prema-rasa for the Lord, and so on. Since the story is told by him, the drift is that this story is filled with prema-rasa in every way just like it is both the sadhana (the means to achieve) and the sadhya (the goal). Hence the gist is: It should be heard with bhakti.

Now, to illustrate the highest purpose of ,His descent, a purpose which is the expansion of a special kind of love by means of completely fulfilling the innermost desires of the divine gopis; to reveal that He flirts with those girls and that His happiness is the best of all; to narrate, in a set of five chapters which are akin to the five life airs, the fun of the divine Rasa with girls who are suitable for Him due to the easy accomplishment of the expansion of a special love owing to the realization of an extraordinary sweetness of the Lord’s form and so on by them who are like ordinary women in activities like drinking the nectar of the lips; to bring to light the requisites of the

Rasa; and to describe the attraction felt by the divine gopis; in this verse which begins bhagavan api he talks about the manifestation of the Lord’s special mood in terms of being the reason for those.

It is understood that this fun took place in kaisora, the suitable age for that. For instance, in Sri Visnu Parana (see above) and in Sri Hari-vamsa (see above). This fun pervaded the whole duration of His age of kaisora. All this and the rest should be explainable ahead in appropriate places. As a partial indication of the above, it is said that this first pastime lasted one night, at the outset of kaisora.

The term bhagavan is used with the intent to express the manifestation of the very essence of His unlimited godhood during the play of Rasa. Nanda and others became wholly satisfied in a state of the highest bliss. To become wholly satisfied in a state of the highest bliss, the Lord too (bhagavan api) desired (manas cakre - aicchat) to create a special pastime (rantum = krida-visesam kartum). Such is the sense of the word api (also, although).

The gist of the words “those nights” was revealed by Sridhara Svami. There is another explanation: “The indescribable nights” (tah = anirvacaniyah), meaning those nights were the best of all forms of time and were imbued with the Rasa of the highest bliss. In short, those nights were suitable for the play of Rasa. Owing to the plural, it is understood that the good fun of Rasa occurred during many nights. That will become clear in the end (10.33.39).

The words saradotphulla-mallikah mean: “The nights, in which the jasmines were in full bloom because of autumn” (saradotphulla- mallikah = sarada krtva uccaih phulla vikasita mallika yasu tah). Even though all kinds of flowers bloom in divine Vrindavan, which has all the seasons, and moreover even the jati (jasmine), the kumuda (night-blooming lotus), the kamala (day-blooming lotus) and so on bloom in autumn, still “utphulla-mallikah” is said with the intent to express the special blooming during the night. In the same way, ahead the word kumudvantam is used (10.29.3).

Thus, “seeing the stimuli,” in other words, “perceiving that the nights were suitable for amorous love,” He made up His mind, etc., while manifesting Yogamaya, a special type of potency of sat-cid- ananda known as Para (transcendental), as a means (upasritah = upa dsritah) (upa = upakaranatvena) (asritah = prakatitavan san). The extraordinariness of the highest bliss of the entertainment of Rasa as compared to the bliss in all other pastimes is meant to be stated that way. In the eighth chapter, in the context of balya-lila, it was explained that all the pastimes are forms of sat-cid-ananda (transcendence, lit. “real awareness and bliss”).

Alternatively, “as a certain characteristic He had mercy endowed with godly might” (yogamayam = yogah aisvaryam tad- yukta maya daya tam) (upasritah = upadhitvena praptah san), that is, by the fun of Rasa He expanded both His godly might and His mercy. The Visva states: maya dambhe krpayam ca, “Maya means dambha (deceit) and krpa (mercy)” (Visva-kosa).

Or the word api is syntactically connected right here. “Although He relies on yogamaya due to proximity,” meaning “although He always relies on yogamaya” (upasrito ’pi = samipyena nityam asrito ’pi).” Here yogamaya means the Maya—either the covering potency of the material Maya or deceit—endowed with atmaramata (the state of mind of taking delight in oneself) (yogamayam = yogah atmaramata maya avaranatmika va kapatyam va, yoga-yuktam mayam). The gist is: At that time there was neither yoga nor maya, rather the real nature of the expansion of the wealth of love for His lotus-like feet became obvious.

There is another interpretation: “Although He relies on deception in a meeting,” like He used deception in dealing with the wives of sacrificial Brahmanas (yogamayam upasrito ’pi = yoge samyoge ya maya yajha-patnisv iva vancana tarn upasrito ’pi). This means: On that occasion, the deception in meeting Him did not return, because a special meeting with the gopis occurred (even though there was deception at first).

Or, “Although He always abides in Laksmi,” who is yoga in the sense that she unites, meaning she is always on His chest. In other words, “although He is always served by her” (yogamayam upasrito ’pi = yoge samyoge ya maya yajna-patnisv iva vancana tarn upasrito ’pi).Laksmi has nothing to do with the play of Rasa, and moreover she cannot achieve it.

Or else, “He relied on the flute,” which is yoga-maya in the sense that its sound is for the purpose of union (yoga-maya = yogaya samyogaya mayah sabdo yasyah sa yogamaya vamsi). The verbal root is ma\[h\] mane sabde ca (to measure; to sound). The word may a is made with the suffix \[gh\]a\[h\].

Or, “He mentally relied (upasritah = manasa upasritah) on Sri Radha,” who is yoga-maya either because in Her is a measure, i.e. the limit, of union or because She gets the splendor, or the excellence, of union (yoga-mayam = yogasya samyogasya mayo manam paryaptir yasyam sa yogamaya sri-radha, athava yogasya samyogasya ma laksmih sampattir iti yavat tam yati prapnotiti yogamaya sri-radhaiva tam). The reason is that She is the ultimate cause of the play of Rasa. That is well known in Padma Purana.

**Комментарий. Автор Jīva Gosvāmī:**

*namah sri-rasa-rasikebhyah*

**“I offer my respects to the venerable Sri Rasa-rasika.”**

In Sridhara Svami’s commentary, the word rasa-samrambhe \[in the first invocatory verse\] has the sense of tasmin nimitte (when there was that reason). The sense is: rasarambha-sambandhinam manam viksya, “Upon observing overweening pride related to the beginning of the Rasa, \[He disappeared\].” (ref. 10.29.47-48). In addition, the meaning of kandarpa-jetrtva-pratiteh and so on is: “This is the opposite of what is expected because by enjoying the wives of other men it looks like Cupid is the victor.”

Now, regarding sri-badarayanir uvaca in the text: The whole thing rests on this preliminary by the force of this context (the Pancadhyayi), whose great glory is going to be described (just ahead in the commentary). The venerable Vedavyasa is called Sri Badarayana because he performed great austerities in Badarikasrama. Those austerities were only characterized by his mental reverence of Sri Krsna, because it is fitting for him, who knows everything, to be completely engaged in that, the highest thing. His son is the form of the result of such austerities. Thus he has qualities such as omniscience and having prema-rasa for the Lord. Although his other qualities might come to mind, only the culmination of the greatness of the etymology of his name takes place here, and so it is implied that the text should be heard only with bhakti.

In the reading sri-suka uvaca, however, the quality of speaking in a very gentle way is shown by his quality of being a natural at having the highest ujjvala-rasa, hence it is implied that the text should be heard only by those who have that sort of heart.

To show that fulfilling the innermost desires of the beautiful girls of Vraja, who have the highest possible love, is the very best purpose of the Lord, who is doing everything only for the happiness of the priya (the dear one, Himself); and to bring to light that He has the highest possible happiness; in five chapters which are as dear as the five aspects of one’s life force he narrates the good fun of Rasa He had with those girls, who were suitable for Him because of the easy accomplishment of the expansion of a distinct type of love. And that is because the nectar of His lips which is His own rasa cannot possibly be obtained anywhere else, given that not even the atmaramas can achieve the extraordinary realization of the Lord’s form, fluids, aromas, touch and sounds (the objects of the five senses).
